name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person who acts to leave behind the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the entity that is relinguished to no one from the Agent's possession.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent gives up the Theme.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Agent gives up the Theme.

name: Manner
definition_en: The style in which the Agent gives up the Theme.

name: Duration
definition_en: For what expanse of time the Agent has given up the Theme.

name: Explanation
definition_en: Explanation denotes a proposition from which the act of abandonment logically follows.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The FE Depictive describes the Agent during the abandoning event.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Agent leaves the Theme behind.

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Agent abandons the Theme.

name: Event_description
definition_en: A description of the event as a whole.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme covers or fills the Location.  This FE most frequently occurs in a PP Complement headed by with or in.  'The waters of the bay teemed with fish.'

name: Location
definition_en: Location is the object or area that the Theme fills or covers.  This frame element generally occurs as the External Argument.'The walls crawled with nanite surveillance probes.' 'The picture frame was thickly coated with dust.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree of abundance with which the Theme covers or fills the Location.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive describes the state of the Location.' She had a closet crammed full of clothes.'

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the the Abounding_with event occurs.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity (often a food item)  that absorbs heat.  'Bacon frying in the pan and scenting the air '

name: Container
definition_en: The Container that holds the Entity that absorbs the heat.  'Five fat sausages were frying in the pan '

name: Heat_source
definition_en: This FE identifies the object that directly supplies heat to the Entity.  'Food was placed to sizzle on the barbecue .'</def-root >

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the heat application occurs.  ' In the kitchen the meat sizzled in the oven and a big pan of potatoes stood on the hob '

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is a substance through which heat is absorbed by the Entity.  'The golden meat was simmering in a sauce that seemed lifted straight out of a French coq au vin rouge'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the cooking event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  'Get them frying slowly, iin a spoonful of olive oil.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the heat absorption takes place.  'Five minutes agothe eggs weren't boiling yet.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The thing or state-of-affairs that leads to the Entity being heated and undergoing change.  'The liquid nitrogen was simmering from the heat.'

name: Temperature
definition_en: The temperature that the Entity stays at, resulting in change.  'No, that kind of batter should bake at a lower temperature.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Entity is exposed to heat.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason why a state of affairs is caused or maintained by an (implicit) agent.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes the Entity as being in some state during the action.

name: Result
definition_en: The final state of affairs after the absorbing heat event has finished.   'The lobster boiled to death.'

name: Collection
definition_en: The Collection whose Quantity is under consideration.  'Extension brings projects galore.'

name: Quantity
definition_en: The feature of an Collection which is under discussion. This FE is incorporated by all the lexical units in this frame.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Measure from the norm or from the value for another Collection.  'For those who manage to make their way onto the lakes, waterfowl is very abundant.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Collection is in the state of having  a particular Measure for the Quantity.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Measure
definition_en: The measure of the Quantity, which is incorporated by the lexical units.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Collection occurs.  'Maggots began to teem in his black fur.'

name: Abuser
definition_en: The Abuser subjects the Victim to repeated verbal, physical, emotional or sexual attacks. 'Fred abused Martha by locking her into a closet .'

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is the recipient of the Abuser's actions. 'Fred abused Martha by locking her into a closet .'

name: Type
definition_en: Type is used for the domain in which the Abuser mistreats the Victim. 'Fred is known for his emotional abuse of women.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree is the extent to which the abuse occurs.  'Fred abused Martha alot.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the abuse occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the abuse occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner is used for any description of the abuse event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Abuser that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'It is fair to say that it was malicious abuse.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Abuser accomplishes the abuse.  'Fred abused Martha by locking her into a closet.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity used by the Abuser to accomplish the abuse.  'Look, being battered with a mallet is no one's idea of a good time.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Abuser intends to accomplish by performing the abuse.   'They are abusive in order to get back at those who abused them.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that abuse occurs.  'She had been battered for years before she even knew there was anything serious wrong.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often abuse occurs.  'She had been abused too much as a child to let it happen again.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the Abusing event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme whose motion is blocked or free.

name: Useful_location
definition_en: The place or thing that the Theme is headed towards, despite a potential or actual Barrier.

name: Barrier
definition_en: An entity that (at least potentially) prevents the Theme from getting to the Useful_location.

name: Participant
definition_en: In this frame, Participant is the accompanied entity (person or object).'Charlie played the piano with Lily.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: In this frame, Co-participant is the accompanying entity (person or object).'Charlie played the piano with Lily.'

name: Participants
definition_en: Two or more entities construed as symmetrically and usually equally participating in an event or relation.  'Lao Tzu and Confucious built the house together.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that lets them accomplish their Goal.   'Can you , too , achieve omniscience by calling on the power of God ?'

name: Agent
definition_en: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional act that fulfills the Goal.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Agent that allows them to achieve their Goal.  'With a simple hammer and saw , you can accomplish almost anything !'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Agent achieves their Goal.  'She had already achieved that feat in Burma .'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent achieves their Goal.  'By 1700 , our forces will have achieved total victory .'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Perhaps you achieved perfection too quickly .'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state-of-affairs from which the accomplishment would be predicted.  'Yes, he was humble, but he achieved enlightenment only because he came from the upper class.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Agent achieves the Goal.   'He has only partially achieved his objective .'

name: Goal
definition_en: The state or action that the Agent has wished to participate in.  'Iraq had achieved its programme objective of producing nuclear weapons . '

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of accomplishing  a Goal.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which Goal is accomplished.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that it takes for Goal to be accomplished.

name: Domain
definition_en: The particular aspect or domain of the Goal that is achieved.  'No one can surpass his economic and financial achievements.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Wearer
definition_en: The Wearer wears the Accoutrement. 'Why must you always wear your helmet when I'm driving?'

name: Style
definition_en: This FE identifies  the Style of the Accoutrement. 'He wore a Jacobean wig.'

name: Material
definition_en: This FE identifies the Material from which the Accoutrement is made.'He wore a gold watch.'

name: Accoutrement
definition_en: This FE identifies  the Accoutrement. 'She wore a tiara.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the Accoutrement. 'Kim wore an exquisite tiara.'

name: Use
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Accoutrement is worn or made.  'She was wearing reading glasses.'

name: Part
definition_en: This FE identifies a part of the Accoutrement. 'He bought a leather cap with sheepskin flaps.'

name: Body_location
definition_en: This FE identifies the place on the body where a particular Accoutrement is located. 'Tess wore a single ring in her left nostril.'

name: Creator
definition_en: The individual or group who created the Accoutrement.  'We found this Chinese anklet two layers below Tel-Wilaya 3.' 'De Beers jewelry is justly famous.'

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which the Accoutrement was created.  'What was a 17th century brooch doing in her attic?'

name: Name
definition_en: A name given to an individual Accoutrement to distinguish it from all other objects.  'The ring Narya was passed to Gandalf.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual who tries to interact with the Target.  'The mailman is very exact about addresses -- he has to be .'

name: Target
definition_en: The Target is the entity whose attributes (esp. position) the Agent is attempting to match in an action.

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt at interaction, incorporated in the LUs of the frame.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent attempts to hit a Target_value.

name: Degree
definition_en: How closely the expected or actual location that the Instrument interacts with corresponds to the Target_value.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when something hits or misses.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Agent manages or fails to interact with the Target.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The object manipulated by the Agent in order to interact with the Target.

name: Target_value
definition_en: The value or values for a parameter that match the Agent's intent.

name: Deviation
definition_en: Expected or actual deviation from the Target_value.  'For this they would need a thermometer accurate to within a microkelvin. '

name: Domain
definition_en: The particular aspect or domain in which something is accurate.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Agent, Means, or Instrument is accurate.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer comes up with or conceptualizes the New_idea. It is normally expressed as an External Argument:  'Kim Sung invented cinnamon cheez fries in 1988.'

name: New_idea
definition_en: The New_idea is a concept not previously present in society which the Cognizer introduces.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Cognizer comes up with the New_idea. 'The strong gravitic shield was discovered in 2162.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Cognizer comes up with the New_idea. 'Was the light bulb invented in Austria?'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Cognizer accomplishes the innovative achievement. 'Jo invented 550 different electronic devices by tinkering with old cables.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Cognizer creates the New_idea . 'He invented the holographic charge-distributor to protect office buildings.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which the Cognizer created the New_idea.  'Wildcom pioneered the use of short wire segments because of rising wire costs.'

name: Field
definition_en: The Field is the general domain of endeavor to which the Cognizer is contributing and of which the New_idea is a part. 'These photochemical techniques were pioneered in broadcasting.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity used by the Cognizer to achieve the introduction of the New_idea into society.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the creative event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Cognizer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Basis
definition_en: The conceptual material from which the Cognizer invents the New_idea.  'Galen invented the term 'gonorrhea' from the words for genital and flow.'

name: Location_of_appearance
definition_en: The Location_of_appearance is where the Invention is first discovered by others.  'This term was coined by James Joyce in his second novel.'

name: Effect
definition_en: The change brought about by the Substance.  'There is a clear co-variation between allergic symptoms in children and the concentration of softening agents in their homes.'

name: Substance
definition_en: The internally undifferentiated physical entity that has an Effect.  'While marijuana?s advocates say the drug is a mellowing agent that can be used for medicinal purposes, some police will say marijuana is a gateway drug.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Substance.  'This transmissible agent is a virus containing DNA.'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Substance belongs to.   'Pharmacological agents could then be selected to modify these cascades.'

name: Name
definition_en: The name of the material that makes up the active Substance.  'Anthrax agent in this form is particularly mobile.'

definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Instance
definition_en: The real-world individual--a concrete or abstract thing or an event--which differs from its counterpart in a discourse-salient non-real world.  'In May of 1994, FBI agents working for Mr. Fiske interviewed Mrs. Foster, showed her an ACTUAL  gun, not a photo, and asked her if she could identify the gun.'

name: Type
definition_en: A kind of entity, instances of which are expected to occur in both the real and the non-real world.   'His actual name was Nabu-Kudurri-Usur.'

name: Addict
definition_en: The Addict is physiologically or psychologically dependent on a substance or a behavior.

name: Addictant
definition_en: Addictant is the substance or behavior to which the Addict is dependent.'Pat defeated her heroin addiction.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an Addict is addicted to the Addictant.

name: Compeller
definition_en: Compeller is the part of a human's body or psyche that compels the Addict to seek out the Addictant. 'Pat <m name="Supp">is emotionally addicted to Kim.' 'Cyril <m name="Supp">is physically addicted to nicotine.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The person doing the calculation.

name: Numbers
definition_en: The Numbers that are used in the calculation.

name: Result
definition_en: The outcome of the Cognizer's calculcations.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Cognizer operates on the Numbers.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Cognizer performs their calculation

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by calculating.

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by the Cognizer that brings about their calculation of the Result.

name: Manner
definition_en: A holistic description of the event (e.g. "the same way"), including depictions of the Cognizer in terms of how the Cognizer's state affects the entire action.  'This week the top brass again grimly tallied the number of dead .'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the person who specifies the Role to be filled by the Specified_entity.  'ButArturo Boncato Jr., marketing manager of the Marco Polo Hotel, cited the high occupancy rates in the hotels as proof of increasing visitors' confidence.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the person to whom the Speaker identifies the filler of a Role.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs,  including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In agentive frames, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'Greedy Englishmen eagerly cited Spanish brutality as an excuse to seek control of their opponent?s holdings.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Speaker makes a statement.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement.  'In a subsequent paper he adduced further evidence.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Speaker during the statement.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the statement is made.  'Persistent, heavy rainfall and poorly maintained drainage systems were cited yesterday as the prime causes for the rising floodwaters'

name: Place
definition_en: The FE specifies the place where the statement takes place.  'In Kuala Lumpur, he also pointed to the accountability/assessment arena as a place for new businesses to investigate.'

name: Specified_entity
definition_en: The entity that the Speaker identifies as filling a particular Role.  'Reilly pointed to the high labor costs as the main reason for the decision to close down the New Orleans facility.'

name: Role
definition_en: A slot in a particular or generic event or relation whose filler the Speaker identifies.  'TCI named the overly expensive bid price as the main reason for their strict opposition against a merger.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by performing the action indicated by adducing the Specified_entity.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Speaker (or Medium) comes to said conclusions about the Specified_entity.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: The event of which the adducing is a part.

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times an event is occuring (within a period of time).

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The circumstances under which the adducing takes place.  'With that audience, you might have to adduce some rather different facts in order to support your argument.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure.  'The cat is adjacent to the mat.'

name: Figure
definition_en: The Figure is perceived as located relative to a certain Ground location. The figure can be an entity or an event.  'The cat is adjacent to the mat.'

name: Distance
definition_en: This  FE identifies the  Distance between the Figure and the Ground.  This FE requires an image schema with a vector that extends from the Ground, or a subpart of the Ground, in some direction, and the Distance is measured along this vector from the Ground to the profiled region.    'The cat is immediately adjacent to the mat.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure. This FE is filled by one of a closed class of adverbs:  up, down, out (meaning 'beyond the boundary around the viewpoint'), off (meaning 'disconnect between landmark and figure'), back (meaning 'along a line from front to back of landmark, and relatively inaccessible'), and, more rarely, away, along, and dialectally, back down (meaning 'down and behind').

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the locative relation between Figure and Ground obtains.

name: Figures
definition_en: The Figures are items which mutually serve to identify the location of the other items.

name: Deixis
definition_en: An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder), or specifically separated from the speech context by distance or a barrier (over).  Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.  'It is lying here next to my desk.'

name: Accessibility
definition_en: An indication of how accessible the Figure is to some participant in the speech context (either the speaker or the addressee, or some other highly salient viewpoint in a narrative).  This FE normally describes availability for manipulation and use, but may simply describe how easily seen or difficult to see the Figure is. There is a closed class of items that can fill this slot, including only 'just' and 'right' indicating ease of access, and 'way', 'all the way', or (dialectally) 'clear' indicating distance and difficulty of access.    'The flashlight 's right next to my handbag.'

name: Directness
definition_en: An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target.  This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, directly, and due (and some combinations of these), but also occurs with rarer items like 'smack dab'.   'The houses are directly adjacent to each other.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that controls the value of a Feature.

name: Part
definition_en: The part of the complex entity which is changed in the process of adjusting. 'She adjusted the injectors to make the mixture leaner.'

name: Feature
definition_en: The Feature with respect to which the Part is adjusted. 'She adjusted the temperature of the oven so that the pie crust would brown a little.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The state of the Part with respect to the Feature that the Agent brings about by making the adjustment.  'You should adjust the antenna to poke outside the bag.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by the Agent which affects the Part.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the adjusting takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the adjusting occurs.

name: Final_value
definition_en: The value associated with the Feature that the system ends up in.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity manipulated by the Agent to adjust the Part and Feature.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Agent hopes to bring about by adjusting.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the adjustment act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Degree
definition_en: A characterization of the amount that the Final_value and Initial_value differ.  'Do n't adjust the pressure by more than two PSI .'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent selects a Value for his/her Attribute and begins to use it.  'Some organizations, like the Sierra Club, have adopted a position of neutrality on US immigration policies.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The Attribute of the Agent can take on several Values, selected by the Agent .  'The Council of Constance (1414-18) adopted conciliarism as a stance, hoping that it would permit the election of a pope acceptable to both Catholic factions.'

name: Value
definition_en: The Value, chosen and made effective by the Agent, specifies the Attribute.  'He crammed his cap back again into his pocket and re-entered the office, assuming an air of absentmindedness.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period when the Agent selects and begins to put into effect the Value.  'On January 1, 2001, our nation will adopt the US dollar as our official currency.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the adoption of a position which is not classified under more specific descriptions, including comparisons to other events (similarly), rates of adoption (slowly), and descriptions of the Agent which also influence the action (eagerly).  'Israel has reluctantly adopted a non-violent defensive measure to protect its citizens from death.'

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent adopts the Value of the Attribute.

name: Role
definition_en: This FE identifies the role filled by a particular participant of the clause headed by the target. In so doing, it relates the state of affairs evoked by the target to another background state of affairs by indicating that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills a second kind of role in the background, either generically or in some specific instance.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent has the Attribute which can take different Value.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which an Agent adopts a Value for an Attribute.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The instument through which an Agent adopts a Value for an Attribute.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.). This may or may not reflect the actual reality of the state of affairs.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which a particular gradable Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing    the deviation of the implicit value either from the norm or from the value for another Entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having a particular implicit value for the Attribute.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular implicit value for the Attribute.

name: Viewpoint
definition_en: The individual who judges the Entity's aesthetics.   'She has always been beautiful to me.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity is in the state of having a particular implicit value for the Attribute.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the sentient entity affirming or denying the truth of the Message (this can be spoken or written). It is normally expressed as the External Argument of the predicative uses of the target word, or as the Genitive modifier of the noun.   'No one believed Evelyn's affirmation that she could speak to ghosts.'  'Evelyn conceded that the ghosts were actually just imaginary friends.'

name: Message
definition_en: The Message identifies the content whose truth the Speaker is affirming or denying. It can be expressed as a clause or as a noun phrase.   'They refute the criticisms that they are only interested in power and money.'  'On Monday my boss confirmed that I was indeed promoted.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the person to whom the truth of the Message is affirmed or denied.

name: Place
definition_en: Place specifies the location where the Message is affirmed or denied.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Message is affirmed or denied.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner describes the way in which the Speaker affirms or denies a Message.

name: Iterations
definition_en: Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Means
definition_en: Means expresses the act whereby the Speaker affirms or denies a Message.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Speaker while he/she affirms or denies the Message.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE identifies an event during which the Speaker affirms or denies the truth of the Message.

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, Event_description is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole - here, the Message event.

name: Frequency
definition_en: Frequency is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to their affirmation or denial of the Message.

name: Medium
definition_en: The Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the Message.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It is rarely mentioned in constructions with verbal targets, and is much more common with nominal targets, where it is usually expressed as a PP Complement headed by "of" or about".

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which a particular age is under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is a function of the amount of time that the Entity has existed.

name: Age
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's age.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Age from the norm.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is at a particular Age.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Age.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The Frame Element Expressor marks expressions that indicate a body part, gesture or other expression of the Entity that reflect its age.    '"Who's there?" she barked. "Ensign Kim, ma'me," the youngish voice of Voyager's young Harry Kim came over the comm line. "'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Entity.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Individuals
definition_en: This FE identifies the people or things that form  the Aggregate. 'A crowd of hoodlums filled the plaza.'

name: Aggregate
definition_en: This FE identifies the collection of entities that are the Aggregate. 'A crowd of hoodlums filled the plaza.'

name: Aggregate_property
definition_en: This FE describes a property of the Aggregate rather than the Individuals and is used to tag the adjective that modifies the aggregate noun when it is unambiguous.'A large crowd of hoodlums filled the plaza.'

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to the Aggregate.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location or political locale that the Organization is contained within.

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant Domain as it pertains to the Aggregate.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity which is undergoing aging.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity ages.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity undergoes the aging event.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In agentive frames, it may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Theme that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'These kinds of condoms aged quickly.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE indicates where the Entity is located.

name: Result
definition_en: The end Result of the Entity aging.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the person to whom a particular action has been proposed and who responds to the request or offer made.

name: Interlocutor
definition_en: This is the person who proposed the Proposed_action  to the Speaker and to whom the Speaker communicates  their response.

name: Medium
definition_en: As with Medium in other communication frames, the physical entity or channel used to communicate can be expressed.

name: Proposed_action
definition_en: The Proposed_action is an action that the Speaker would perform if they were to accept or refuse the request or offer.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including  secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly).

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Speaker.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Speaker responds to the request or offer made.

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The response may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Speaker mental or emotional state.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Speaker  gives their verbal response to the proposed action.

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which the Speaker makes their verbal response concerning the proposed action.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by agreeing or refusing to perform the Proposed_action that is requested of, or suggested to  them.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of response events.

name: Role
definition_en: Role denotes the status that the Interlocutor requested to be granted.   'A serious injustice was committed by Citizenship and Immigration Canada (CIC) when it refused her as a political refugee.'

name: Co-timed_event
definition_en: This FE identifies the subevent of the agreeing/refusing to act.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times (within a given period) that the agreeing/refusing to act occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness, and consists of any descriptions of the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames. The state of affairs reported by the target is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier.

name: Agriculturist
definition_en: The Agriculturist is the agent cultivating Food.

name: Food
definition_en: Food is the item cultivated by the Agriculturist.  'They cultivate fungi.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument is used by the Agriculturist as a tool to help obtain Food. (This tool is not limited to typical artifacts and can be hands, arms, and other atypical hunting and fishing instruments.)

name: Duration
definition_en: For what length of time the Agriculturist attempted to obtain Food.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Agriculturist cultivates Food.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agriculturist cultivates Food.

name: Outcome
definition_en: The failure or success of an attempt.

name: Place
definition_en: The greater geographic location where the Agriculturist cultivates Food.

name: Time
definition_en: When the agricultural event occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agriculturist intends to accomplish by cultivating Food.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Agriculturist cultivates Food.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.  'Most of lowland Britain is intensively cultivated.'

name: Ground
definition_en: This is the the background or context for the Food to which the Agriculturist pays attention in his agricultural efforts.  'Romans were cultivating the land in Northern Gaul.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates the subtype of agriculture that the Agriculturist is engaging in.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE appraises the event.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the agricultural event itself and any of its participants.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that manipulates the Instrument to enable interaction with the Targeted.

name: Targeted
definition_en: The Targeted is the entity located in an indirectly accessible location relative to the Agent.  'I tried to target his left thigh .'

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the aiming is achieved.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent takes aim.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent during the event.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Agent aims at the Targeted.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any generalized description of the details of the event in terms of comparison to another event or what would be expected of the details given some state of the Agent.  'She took careful aim before shooting .'

name: Duration
definition_en: The time peiod over which the adjustment of the Instrument takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason for which the Agent attempts to interact with the Targeted

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is independent of the the aiming of the Agent, but contextualizes it.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The object manipulated by the Agent in order to interact with the Targeted.

name: Target_location
definition_en: The location that the Agent wishes to ready the Instrument to access.  'If you target towards the bridge , make sure to avoid the church .'

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: The location from which the proto-agent acts or perceives.  This does not include the location of a thing which is affected or perceived in the event.  'With remote drones , you can target Moscow <fex name="">from your own living room .'

name: Activity
definition_en: The Activity is undertaken by the Agent and is directed towards the Targeted or Target_location.  'The attack targeted a village south of here.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: A larger event during which an aiming event takes place.  'Milatary convoys were targeted by rebels in several attacks over the past week.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that provides an explanation for the Aiming event.  'They were targeted because they were the most prominent supporters of the establishment.'

name: Alignment_match
definition_en: A region of space oriented the same as the Ground.

name: Ground
definition_en: An entity whose location and orientation is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Alignment_match and Alignment_mismatch regions.

name: Alignment_mismatch
definition_en: A region oriented approximately perpendicular to the Ground

name: Alliance
definition_en: The entity of which the individuals are Members.

name: Members
definition_en: The persons or groups belonging to the Alliance.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason for which an Alliance is formed.

name: Period_of_existence
definition_en: The interval during which the Alliance exists.  'Hezbollah was founded in 1982 in response to the Israeli invasion of Lebanon, and subsumed members of the 1980s coalition of groups known as Islamic Jihad.'

name: Member_1
definition_en: That group or individual which has joined the Alliance which is grammatically more prominent when the Members are presented separately.  'Our alliance with Japan is the cornerstone of Asia-Pacific security strategy.'

name: Member_2
definition_en: That group or individual which has joined the Alliance which is grammatically less  prominent when the Members are presented separately.  'Thanks in part to their coalition with McCoy, but thanks also to their seniority and the knowledge of some of their leaders, they hold considerable influence '

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of some property of the Alliance.  'The two leaders enjoy an uneasy alliance.'

name: Situation
definition_en: Something that may happen in the future, or at least whose factual status is unresolved. This is often tagged in a second FE layer and generally contains the target.  'You have a chance at life.'

name: Agent
definition_en: An individual involved in the Event.  "You have a choice."

name: Number_of_possibilities
definition_en: The number of different future Events under consideration.  'There are two possibilities.'

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: An entity intimately involved in the Event.  'You have one choice to make for him.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Agent hopes to bring about which is associated with some of the possible Events but not others.  'There 's only one choice to get what you want .'

name: Profiled_alternative
definition_en: A situation that cannot be true at the same time as the Contrasting_alternative.

name: Contrasting_alternative
definition_en: A situation that cannot be true at the same time as the Profiled_alternative.

name: Parts
definition_en: The entities that merge to form a single Whole.

name: Whole
definition_en: The single, undifferentiated entity that is the result of the amalgamation.  'They had all just merged into one big file.'

name: Part_1
definition_en: The prominent entity that combines with Part_2 to form a Whole.  'The single smaller soul merges with the Ur-soul.'</def-root >

name: Part_2
definition_en: The less focussed-upon entity that the Part_1 merges with.  'The single smaller soul merges with the Ur-soul.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the thoroughness of the mixing job, i.e. to what degree the resulting Whole is undifferentiated.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  In this frame, it is also deemed to include modification indicating the speed of the event.

name: Result
definition_en: The state of the Parts after the amalgamation.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Parts become amalgamated into a Whole

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the amalgamation occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of Part_1 or Parts.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A Descriptor describes the target. Usually adjectives, used with noun LUs.  'This beautiful combination is only available for a limited time.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: The Recipient indicates the entity that ends up in possession of the Mass_theme.

name: Mass_theme
definition_en: The collection of objects that ends up in the Recipient's possession.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location that the Mass_theme formerly occupied.  Persons that begin in possession of the Mass_theme may metonymically stand in for the Source.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place denotes where the Mass_theme is acquired.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional amassment is performed.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation refers to the existing eventuality that the Recipient is responding to.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is the action of the Recipient which results in their possession of the Mass_theme.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the Amassing which is not covered by more specific FEs.  It includes such specifications as comparisons to other events (similarly), rates of acquisition (slowly), and descriptions of the Recipient which also influence the action (eagerly).  'If you press the show duplicates button, then all the redundant bookmarks that you have haphazardly accumulated will be neatly displayed in alphabetical order .'

name: Result
definition_en: The state that either the Recipient or the Mass_theme end up in after the acquisition.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE describes the length of time over which amassing occurs.  'Bogs accumulate carbon for thousands of years .'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which amassing occurs.

name: Role
definition_en: Role is used for the capacity in which the Recipient  amasses stuff, and is expressed in as-PPs.  'By the time I was 16 , I was winning major contests , amassing a few quid in the bank as a part-time model and walking as though I had a brush handle up my arse .'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where  it is a certain Temperature .   'Chicago is  hot today .'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The temperature feature of the weather.

name: Temperature
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the Temperature of the environment.  'The temperature  was 85 F in the shade today'

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Temperature from the norm.  'It's like totally chilly, dude, like, totally.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which an ambient environment has a particular Temperature.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the ambient Temperature is as specified.   'It's plenty cool in the shade'

name: Weather
definition_en: The meteorological conditions which determine the ambient temperature of a locale.  'We get warmer weather this time of year.'

name: Ammunition
definition_en: This FE identifies the Ammunition that is designed to have a particular Use.

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which a piece of ammunition is intended.

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Ammunition into existence.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which an Ammunition comes into existence.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to an Ammunition.

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Ammunition.

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Ammunition, including components, ingredients, etc.

name: Weapon
definition_en: The weapon that the Ammunition is used in.  'Ammo for an AK-47 was found in the bedroom .' 'Shotgun shells, unlike simple balls, cannot be reused .'

name: Value
definition_en: The value of an attribute.  'The final tally for 1990 was <fex name="Value">199,000 . '

name: Attribute
definition_en: The scalar property of a concrete or abstract entity.  'During the first three years of drug squad work, arrests totaled some sixty-four persons. '

name: Time_span
definition_en: The span of time when the Attribute has the Value. 'The total for last month far exceeded expectations.' 'The April total is 20,000.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE indicates the time span during which the total of the Attribute is the Value, with the added information that it is (somehow) calculated at a regular interval coinciding with the transition between spans of time.

name: Numbers
definition_en: A set of numbers that add up to the Value.  'Look, you turn those into numbers, and then 592 and 74 total 666, right?'

name: Animal
definition_en: The living organism belonging to the kingdom Animalia.  'Did you see that bird in the tree?'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Animal not covered by another frame element.  'The dogs that live next door are so well-behaved.'

name: Origin
definition_en: The location from which the Animal originated.

name: Characteristic
definition_en: A quality of the Animal.  'Foxes are sly.'

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs.  It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.

name: Stimulus
definition_en: The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.

name: Empathy_target
definition_en: The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The body part, gesture, or other expression of the Experiencer that reflects his or her emotional state.  They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response.  In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus.  Quite often in such cases, the Stimulus can be inferred from the Circumstances

name: State
definition_en: The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Experiencer, Expressor, or State can be described as having said emotion.

name: Convict
definition_en: The Convict is the individual convicted of the crime who may make an appeal on her or his behalf.

name: Representative
definition_en: The Representative applies to a higher court on behalf of the Convict.

name: Decision
definition_en: The Decision is the ruling handed down by the first court.

name: Grounds
definition_en: The Grounds is the legal basis on which the appeal rests.

name: Court
definition_en: The Court is the judicial establishment to which the Convict appeals.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which a Convict or Representative appeals.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Name
definition_en: The name of the person referred to by a Title.  'Reverend Roberts wears wrinkled robes.'

name: Title
definition_en: How a person is referred to within an Institution, often denoting their rank or status. Title is always marked on the target.  'Judge Judy has made her decision.'

name: Context
definition_en: The language, region, or domain in which the Title applies.  'Judge Noonan of the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit will cast his vote today.'

name: Type
definition_en: The sub-type of the Title.  'High King Brian shook his head sadly .'

name: Cook
definition_en: The Cook applies heat to the Food.'Drew sauteed the garlic in butter.'

name: Heating_instrument
definition_en: This FE identifes the entity that  directly supplies heat to the Food.  'Jim browned the roast in the oven.'  This FE will take precedence over Container when both are expressed in the same constituent.  For example:  'Kate cooked the rice in a rice-cooker.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the heat application  occurs. 'We baked the cake in the kitchen.'

name: Food
definition_en: Food is the entity to which heat is applied by the Cook.'Suzy usually steams the broccoli.'In instructional imperatives, this FE, which would be used for the (missing) object, is tagged CNI:'Cook on low heat for two hours.CNI'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time at which the heat application occurs. 'Jim roasted the chestnuts in the evening.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which heat is applied to Food. 'Kate blanchedthe broccoli by throwing it into a pot of boiling water.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.'John baked cookies to show Patti that he was sorry.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration is the amount of Time heat is applied to the Food.'Jim boiled the egg for three minutes.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the substance through which heat is applied to the Food. 'Bobby fried the potatoes in oil.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: Co-participant is the gramatically less prominent of two foods to which heat is applied by the Cook.' Kate baked the apples with cinnamon.''Joe roasted potatoes with the chicken.'

name: Temperature_setting
definition_en: This FE identifies the Temperature_setting of the Heating_instrument for the Food.  'He baked the cookies at 350 degrees for 11 minutes.' 'She microwaved the popcorn on high.' 'You can't cook popcorn on low heat!'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which heat application occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the cooking event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Cook that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'Saute the onions gently.'

name: Container
definition_en: The Container holds the Food to which heat is applied.'Boil the potatoes in a medium-sized pan.'Things that apply the heat directly are Heating_Instruments, e.g. crock-pot, electric skillet.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: THe person for whose benefit the food is cooked.

name: Selector
definition_en: The Selector is responsible for the appointment of the new official.  Typically, it occurs as the External Argument of verbs.

name: Official
definition_en: The Official is a person appointed to a recognized position.

name: Role
definition_en: Frequently, the Official is referred to only by his/her role. However, the Role can be expressed separately from the leader, usually as either a secondary predicate or in a PP Complement (headed by as).

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE indicates the Degree to which an event occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive indicates the state of one of the participants during the action.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE is used for the Manner of performing an action.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which  the Selector accomplishes the designation of the Official.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE  is used for indicating the Result of an event.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This frame element describes the situation that brought about the new appointment.

name: Function
definition_en: The Function is the purpose the Official will fufill.  'Under the new program, SCC will accredit organizations to assess wood flow from certified forests to workshops or factories.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the designation of the official takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the appointment takes place.

name: Body
definition_en: A group of individuals who are elected or appointed to perform some function, and to which the Official is assigned.

name: Part
definition_en: A  Part of a larger architectural unit, the  Whole.  'Marty leaned against the  fireplace.'

name: Whole
definition_en: An architectural unit which includes the Part.   'The living-room fireplace  is just for show.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A property relating to the  Part.  'The building had a dilapidated facade. '

name: Orientation
definition_en: This is a property of the  Part that situates  the  Part within the Whole.  'Looks like he fell through the side wall, innit?'

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Part, including components, ingredients, etc.  'The house has a marble floor'

name: Creator
definition_en: The Individual  who creates the Part.   'If a mason's wall collapses, is it always his fault?'

name: Term1
definition_en: The grammatically more prominent number in an arithmetic operation.

name: Term2
definition_en: The grammatically less prominent number in an arithmetic operation.

name: Terms
definition_en: Two more or elements of a commutative arithmetic operation. This frame element may be represented as Term1 and Term2.

name: Terms
definition_en: Two more or elements of a commutative arithmetic operation. This frame element may be represented as Term1 and Term2.

name: Term1
definition_en: The grammatically more prominent number involved in a commutative operation.

name: Term2
definition_en: The grammatically less prominent number involved in commutative operation.

name: Term_1
definition_en: Term_1 is the first operand in the non-commutative arithmetic that is modified by Term_2 (e.g. subtracted or divided by Term_2).

name: Term_2
definition_en: Term_2 is the second operand of the non-commutative arithmetic which modifies Term_1 (e.g. subtracts from or divides Term_1).

name: Armor
definition_en: The Armor prevents the Asset from coming to harm.  'Metal armor was so heavy that sometimes knights found it difficult to move.'

name: Danger
definition_en: An object or situation that could damage the Asset.  'The anti-mine armor being developed by the army is still months from completion.'

name: Asset
definition_en: Something desirable which might be lost or damaged and which is protected by Armor.  'Our company's tank armor provides an unprecedented about of protection.'  'The bullet was stopped by her bullet-proof vest.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description or characteristic of the Armor.  'The rusted mail provided little protection against his foe's broadsword.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Armor protects the Asset, e.g., how resilient it is.

name: Material
definition_en: The Material which the Armor is primarily made of.  'It is now common for officers to wear kevlar bullet-proof vests.'</def-root >

name: Subregion
definition_en: The place on the Asset covered by the Armor.  'Tanks will now be fitted with underbelly armor to protect against roadside bombs.'  'This style of chest armor was used in Japan during the 11th century.'

name: Type
definition_en: A description of the subtype of Armor.

name: Defendant
definition_en: The Defendant is charged with a crime by a Judge. ' Jan was arraigned on eight counts of treason.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the arraignment occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the arraignment occurs.

name: Judge
definition_en: The Judge is the head of the court where the arraignment occurs. ' Jan was arraigned on eight counts of treason before Duncan Smith.'

name: Charges
definition_en: Charges is the crime with which the Defendant is charged. 'Jan was arraigned on eight counts of treason.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the arraignment takes.  'Just a short little arraignment, and then you'll walk, alright?'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the arraignment which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (openly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Judge that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'Everyone 's always very carefully arraigned before they meet trial, don't you worry none.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who causes the Theme to be in a particular Configuration.

name: Theme
definition_en: An entity that consists of  parts which can be put into a configuration relative to each other and/or relative to their environment.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the arranging takes place.

name: Configuration
definition_en: A state that holds of the Theme or a relation that holds among the constituent parts of the Theme as a result of the arranging action.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the arranging action which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). With agentive use, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent  that also affect the action ( eagerly, carefully). </def-root >

name: Location
definition_en: The place in which the Theme is put into a Configuration.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances identifies the situation in which an Agent arranges a Theme.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent is trying to bring about by changing the Configuration of the Theme.  'Arrange the stones in a circle to acheive maximal effect.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity used by the Agent to change the Theme's Configuration.  'Arrange the floats into a line with your oar.'

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Agent in order to arrange the Theme.  'You must array them in a circle by concentration alone.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Arranging act has occured.

name: Charges
definition_en: Charges identifies a category within the legal system; it is the crime with which the Suspect is charged.'The police arrested Harry on charges of manslaughter.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the arrest occurs.'The police arrested Harry in front of his house.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the arrest occurs. 'The police arrested Harry on Wednesday afternoon.'

name: Authorities
definition_en: The Authorities charge the Suspect with commiting a crime, and take him/her into custody.'The police arrested Harry on charges of manslaughter.'

name: Suspect
definition_en: The Suspect is taken into custody, under suspicion of having committed a crime.'The police arrested Harry on charges of manslaughter.'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates the subtype of arrest under which the Suspect is placed. 'The police placed Harry under house arrest.'

name: Offense
definition_en: Offense identifies the ordinary language use of the reason for which a Suspect is arrested.  'They arrested Harry for shoplifting.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the arresting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Authorities that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which Authorities arrest a Suspect.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which Authorities arrest a Suspect. 'The police arrested Harry to get him off the street.'

name: Source_of_legal_authority
definition_en: The Source_of_legal_authority describe the law which grants the power of arrest to the Authorities. 'The policeman arrested him under the "suspected loitering with intent" power.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: A person that participates in the event along with the Authorities or the Suspect.  'She was arrested with the Minister of Finance, Javier Soledad .'

name: Theme
definition_en: Theme is the object that moves. It may be an entity that moves under its own power, but it need not be. 'The officer approached the house.''I ducked as the baseball approached my head.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Source expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent.  If present, they often express a general direction from which a Theme moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.'The cat approached the bird from behind.''She arrived from New York yesterday.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.  In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.'The officer approached the house through the bushes.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is any expression that tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. 'We arrived in Paris before midnight.' Although always conceptually present and specific, Goal may sometimes be understood from context, rather than expressed by any separate constituent. 'Our visitors arrived yesterday.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A Manner expression  describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion.  Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.'The messenger entered the room clumsily.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a Theme arrives.

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Theme is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Theme.   Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.  'I reached Canada by car.'  'I reached Mexico on foot.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique. 'Pat came  with me down the street.' 'The squirrel  returned with the nut.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when arriving occurs.

name: New_situation
definition_en: The New_situation are the state of the Goal when the Theme arrives.  'The senator arrived to a standing ovation.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the state of the Theme upon arrival. 'The Princess of Wales arrived smiling.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The time period within which the arrival repeats multiple times.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Theme arrives to the Goal.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE marks the state of affairs reported by the Arriving Event as understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Theme arrives at the Goal.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the arriving event occurs.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies a phrase that describes the actor of an action.

name: Offense
definition_en: The illegal setting of fire to destroy something.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an action is performed.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which arson is committed.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The action that the Perpetrator is trying to accomplish with the arson Event.  'Arson for insurance fraud is quite common.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time that a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the arson occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the arson occurs.

name: Perpetrator
definition_en: The Perpetrator sets fire to a building in order to gain some benefit from so doing. 'The two men were charged with arson when found running from the burning factory.'

name: Victim
definition_en: Victim identifies the enity that is negatively effected by the arson. 'There has been an increase in the number of  arson attacks on local schools.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The frequency with which an act of arson is committed.   'The churches were plagued with frequent arson.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Artifact
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity or substance that is designed to have a particular Use. This can refer to physical artifacts, like a mug or computer monitor, or a digital artifact, such as a website or document.

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which an artifact is intended.

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Artifact into existence.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which an Artifact comes into existence.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to an Artifact.

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Artifact.

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Artifact, including components, ingredients, etc.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describes either a state or characteristic of the artifact which is not subsumed by the core FEs.

name: Component
definition_en: An entity that is a part of an Artifact and serves a distinct Function.

name: Artifact
definition_en: A deliberately made entity which fulfilling a purpose, whose complete form is composed of more than one Component.

name: Function
definition_en: The role or purpose of the Component as it pertains to the Artifact.

name: Material
definition_en: The type of matter that the Component comprises.

name: Creator
definition_en: The entity who creates the Component.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: When the Component was created.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity that is being evaluated in terms of whether it is an instance of the Reference_category.  'The bomb found at the US Embassy in Berlin was fake.'

name: Reference_category
definition_en: The type relative to which the Entity is evaluated.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Entity seems to belong (or not, if so specified by the lexical unit) to the category of the Reference_category is clear. Typically, this frame element is realized as an end-of-scale expression.  'Of course, the picture was completely fake, as could be seen by a number of clues.'

name: Artist
definition_en: A person who creates an Artwork with a particular recognizable Form.

name: Artwork
definition_en: A created artifact that is created by an Artist and has a unique Form as perceived by some judge.

name: Form
definition_en: The Form is a style that characterizes an Artwork (or an Artist, metonymically) and can be recognized by a judge. This FE is usually incorporated into the target for nouns in this frame.

name: Time
definition_en: A description of when the Artwork was created.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Form that the Artwork resembles.

name: Individuals
definition_en: The Individuals are self-movers who intentionally assemble together.

name: Group
definition_en: The Group describes the resulting formation of the Individuals.

name: Party_1
definition_en: Party_1 is the grammatically more prominent participant in the assembling event.  It can refer to either a single individual or a larger party separate from Party_2 previous to the assembling.

name: Party_2
definition_en: A grammatically less prominent participant in the assembling event.  It can refer to either a single individual or a larger party separate from Party_1 previous to the assembling.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the assembling which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Individuals or Group that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, eagerly, carefully).

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the assembling occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means descibes the way in which the Individuals accomplish the assembling.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the assembling occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Group plans to engage in upon assembly.

name: Assessor
