definition_en: The sentient entity that evaluates the Phenomenon.

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The entity whose Value according to a Feature is being measured.

name: Value
definition_en: The value (according to some scale) that the Phenomenon is deemed to have.  The Value is taken to indicate the Phenomenon's acceptability.

name: Feature
definition_en: The type of property or feature that the Phenomenon is being judged on.  'You will also be graded on your speed of response . '

name: Evidence
definition_en: Some fact perceived by the Assessor which leads to their evaluation of the Phenomenon.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any secondary effect of the action or characterization of the Assessor which saliently affects the character of the assessment.  'He quietly graded the papers.'

name: Method
definition_en: An event or procedure that allows the Assessor to evaluate the Phenomenon.  'The study evaluated the risk of a major quake.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which assessment occurs

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Assessor makes the assessment.  'The committee rated Smithers " most loyal servant " about a week ago .'

name: Standard
definition_en: An entity that the Phenomenon is compared to in the assessment.  'Smiter weighed his chances in the snow against the danger posed by the troop of sycophants hurtling towards him. '

name: Purpose
definition_en: The goal that the Assessor hopes to accomplish by assessing the Phenomenon.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the assessing takes place.  'They 'll evaluate you in that room over there , and then you 're free to go .'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Assessor to make the assessment.  'This chapter evaluates the far-left's contribution to the environmentalism debate since the '70's .'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: A person who participates along with the Assessor in the assessing event.  'In order to find the best suited, targeted form of activity, the prisoner?s work and functioning capability is assessed together with him/her.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times assessing occurs per some unit of time.   'Brown 's chapter on geodemographics discusses an application field where primary data collected for operational purposes are typically evaluated in relation to secondary data derived from sources such as the Census of Population .'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: This extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world at a partiicular time and place.

name: Result
definition_en: The result of the assessing.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE denotes the length of time during which a continuous event occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Station
definition_en: The locale where the Entity is supposed to be.  It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.  'Get back to your station, soldier!.'

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Salient parts that make up a Station.

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that the Station is located with respect to.  'The post by the main entrance was the least desirable assignment.'

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Station about.  This FE also covers expressions that indicate that there was no salient formation.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location that the Station is a part of.   'Most of the fort's stations are manned by two individuals ata  time.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Station.  'Why did she always get assigned to the dirtiest post in the park?'

name: Related_event
definition_en: An event related to the Station in some way other than (1) Formational_cause (which is a separate FE) or an intended use (which would place the instance in Locale_by_use), or (3) a defining event (which would place the instance in Locale_by_event).

name: Task
definition_en: The activity that is carried out at the Station.  'This will be your firing station.'

name: Responsible_party
definition_en: The Responsible_party is tasked with remaining at the Station to perform a Task.

name: Benefited_party
definition_en: The Benefited_party receives a benefit from the action of the Helper.

name: Helper
definition_en: The Helper performs some action that benefits the Benefited_party.

name: Goal
definition_en: The desirable state of affairs that the Benefited_party is involved in and which is enabled by the Helper.  'Jack helped Jill climb Mt. Everest.'

name: Focal_entity
definition_en: This FE identifies a Focal_entity involved in achieving the Goal. 'Whoever didn't cook has to help with the dishes.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Assistance occurs. 'The police assisted Harry in finding his cat on Wednesday afternoon.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Assistance occurs. 'The police assisted Harry in finding his cat in front of his house.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which a Helper assists a Benefited_party.   'The doorman assisted Harry into the car with enthusiasm.'

name: Means
definition_en: An action that the Helper undertakes in service of the Benefited_party's Goal.  ' Her teachers and her parents helped her by reading sections to her and by outlining some of the chapters.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity used by the Helper in service of the Benefited_party's accomplishing their Goal.  'Actually, he was born in his parents' Dodge Durango, with Sheree Benefield beginning to give birth as his dad, Jon Benefield, held the wheel with his left hand, helped her with his right and maneuvered the sport utility vehicle up the I-65 exit ramp at Warrior.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The aspect of accomplishing the Goal to which the Helper's assistance is relevant.  'How can you be helped spiritually by his music, when he is defying God?s Word with his very appearance?'

name: Degree
definition_en: The measure to which the Helper's assistance brings the Benefited_party closer to accomplishing their Goal.  'The Algebra Buster software helped my daughter very much. '

name: Duration
definition_en: The time period during which the Helper gives assistence to the Benefited_party.  'Several nations helped ours during our most difficult years.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The situation that the Helper wishes to bring about by helping the Benefited_party to acheive the Goal.  Note that this FE should normally be used only when this situation is separate from the Goal.  'I helped her with the problem just to show her that it could be done.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the questions how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs; Iteration expressions answer the question how many times.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.  'Since the earthquake did so much damage, even the federal government aided in the recovery process.'

name: Protagonist_1
definition_en: The profiled participant in a reciprocal event, encoded as the subject of an active-form sentence or as a by-PP in a passive.  '"You can't argue politics with foreigners," sighed the policeman.'

name: Protagonist_2
definition_en: The participant involved (subordinately) with Protagonist_1 in a reciprocal event.  It is generally coded in a with-PP.  'We have been arguing the point with the inspector at claims branch for many many months and we just seem to go round in circles.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent has committed a Wrong and is making Amends.  'Syria has atoned for its support of Iraq.'

name: Wrong
definition_en: Wrong identifies the act committed by the Agent for which Amends are made.  'Smithers is atoning for his misspent youth.'

name: Amends
definition_en: Amends marks expressions that indicate what the Agent does to compensate for the Wrong that was committed.  'He atoned for his sin with good works. '

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate the Degree to which Amends made are adequate for atoning the Wrong.  'The sacrifice fully atoned for his sin.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The situation that the Agent hopes to bring about by atoning.  'He atoned for his sins so that he could be inducted into the society.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the atonement which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Agent atones for the Wrong.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Agent expiates the Wrong.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent manipulates an object. Agent typically refers to animate beings, but is also extended to mechanical and other inanimate objects.  It is most frequently expressed as the external argument of verbs. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair.'

name: Item
definition_en: This FE identifies the Item that the Agent attaches to the Goal. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an attaching event. 'The robber tied his ankles together.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal identifies the location to which an Item is attached. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair.'

name: Connector
definition_en: The Connector forms the bond that maintains the Item or Items in a fixed position; it is usually expressed in a with-PP. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair  with a rope.'

name: Items
definition_en: This FE identifies the plural Items that are tied together, resulting in their mutual attachment. 'The robber tied Harry's ankles together.'  Notice that when the FE Items occurs, neither Item nor Goal can occur.

name: Handle
definition_en: Thie Handle is the point of attachment on the Item to which the Agent attaches. 'The robbers tied Harry to the chair by his ankle.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects an Item or Items. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair by wrapping the rope around his chest.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent intentionally affects an Item or Items. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair with enthusiasm.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent intentionally affects an Item or Items. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair in the basement.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent intentionally affects an Item or Items. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair to stop him from leaving.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent intentionally affects the Item or Items. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair at midnight.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent attaches an Item or Items.  Typically, it transmits the force applied by the Agent, and is not left behind as a participant in the resultant Being_attached frame. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair  with his left hand.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item ends up attached.  'You only partially anchored it, and now it's torn off.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times the Attaching event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the Attaching event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Duration
definition_en: The time when the Attaching occurs.

name: Victim
definition_en: This FE is the being or entity that is injured by the Assailant's attack. 'The mysterious fighter attacked the guardsmen with a sabre.'

name: Weapon
definition_en: An entity used by the Assailant to cause damage to the Victim. 'The mysterious fighter attacked the guardsmen with a sabre.'

name: Assailant
definition_en: The person (or other self-directed entity) that is attempting physical harm to the Victim. 'The mysterious fighter attacked the guardsmen with a sabre.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Assailant that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Assailant that accomplishes the assault.  'Japanese ambushed Americans by bombing Pearl Harbor.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Assailant makes an assault on the Victim. 'Then Jon-O's forces ambushed them on the left flank from a line of low hills.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Assailant attacks the Victim. 'John assaulted Thibault to prove his manhood.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Assailant is responding to that leads them to make an assault on the Victim. 'Gloria attacked Michael for the cause of Justice.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Assailant attacks the Victim. 'As soon as he stepped out of the bar he was set upon by four men in ski-masks.'

name: Source
definition_en: The starting-point of the motion of the Assailant or projectiles of the Assailant as they move toward the the Place that the Victim is occupying in the attack.  In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion.  With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Assailant or Victim while the attack occurs. 'They attacked us in large numbers.'

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re-encoding, but not necessarily.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the attack on the Victim by the Assailant.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held. Form: once, twice, Cardinal expression + /it times, /it lots/a lot

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Assailant travels.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number (or description of the number) of times an attack takes place over a period of time.  'They attack daily.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that the attack lasts.  'The day-long attack crushed our morale.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE is used for expressions that indicate motion along a line from the deitic center towards a reference point (which may be implicit) that is neither the goal of motion nor a landmark along the way.  'They will no doubt launch an attack towards the weakest area of our territory.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a Goal. 'John attempted to climb Mt. Everest.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is what the Agent attempts to achieve.  'John attempted to climb Mt. Everest.'

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt to achieve a Goal. 'John's third failed attempt began propitiously.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an attempt occurs.

name: Effort
definition_en: This FE identifies the effort expended in an attempt.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent.

name: Place

name: Manner

name: Duration

name: Purpose

In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Domain

name: Condition

name: Target

name: Degree

name: Instrument

name: Target_location
definition_en: The location that the Agent is attempting to access using the Instrument.

name: Outcome

name: Seeker
definition_en: The Seeker is the agent hoping to obtain Food.

name: Food
definition_en: Food is the sought-out item by the Seeker.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument is used by the Seeker as a tool to help obtain Food. (This tool is not limited to typical artifacts and can be hands, arms, and other atypical hunting and fishing instruments.)

name: Duration
definition_en: For what length of time the Seeker attempted to obtain Food.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Seeker makes the attempt for Food.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an attempt at achieving a Food obtainment.

name: Outcome
definition_en: The failure or success of an attempt.

name: Place
definition_en: The greater geographic location where the Seeker attempts to obtain Food.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Food seeking action occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Seeker intends to accomplish by seeking Food.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Seeker attempts to obtain Food.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the amount of effort the Seeker puts into an attempt to obtain Food.

name: Ground
definition_en: This is the entity to which the Seeker pays attention. It is referred to as Ground because it serves as the background or context for the Food.

name: Addressee

name: Speaker

name: Topic

name: Medium

name: Depictive

name: Means

name: Period_of_iterations

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world (independent of the event).

name: Group

name: Frequency

name: Re-encoding

name: Place

name: Purpose

name: Salient_entity

name: Role

name: Agent

name: Goal

name: Outcome

name: Agent

name: Event
definition_en: The Event is the deliberate set of happenings given at a particular time and place.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Agent went about going to the Event.

name: Means
definition_en: Through what strategies and efforts the Agent made possible his attendance at the Event.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent attends the Event.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Agent attends the Event.

name: Circumstances

name: Purpose

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE describes the event as a whole.

name: Perceiver
definition_en: The individual that pays attention to the Ground.

name: Ground
definition_en: The sensory field or subset of a sensory field that the Perceiver is attending to.

name: Figure
definition_en: The entity that the Perceiver is specifically focussing on within the Ground.

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount of attention that the Perceiver is paying to the Figure or Ground.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The situation within which the Perceiver is alert.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Perceiver that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Expressor
definition_en: An entity (or event) associated with a Perceiver that gives evidence for a Perceiver's attentiveness.

name: Address_term
definition_en: This FE identifies the Address_term as used to get someone's attention, and may be a proper name. 'Boy, come over here right now!' 'Billy, come over here right now!'  Tag this constiuent with the FE Interjection on a secondary FE layer.

name: Interjection
definition_en: Interjection identifies the attention getting element. 'Hey, boy, come over here now!'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The person whose Attitude about a State_of_affairs is being expressed.  'Americans are optimistic despite the climbing unemployment rate.'

name: Attitude
definition_en: The outlook or viewpoint expressed by the Cognizer.  'Michelle had a somewhat negative outlook on the direction her life was heading.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: An event, topic, or situation about which the Cognizer has an Attitude.  'The economy looks quite grim at this moment.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree of the Attitude description.    'The team was very hopeful about the prospective victory. '

name: Time
definition_en: The Time interval during which the Cognizer has the Attitude about the State_of_affairs.

name: Proposition
definition_en: The information attributed to the Speaker or Text.  'Parents are present at and involved in the purchase or rental of games 83 percent of the time, according to a September 2000 Federal Trade Commission report '

name: Speaker
definition_en: A sentient entity that has communicated the information encoded by the Proposition.   'With the first big batch of music now blocked from Napster's file-swapping network, the average number of songs available on the service has dropped precipitously, according to at least one research company.'

name: Text
definition_en: A written or verbal collection of statements, which imparts the information of the Proposition.  'The son of the Syrian defense minister received 6 million barrels, according to the document, worth about $3 million. '

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which a particular Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

name: Value

name: Theme

name: Domain

name: Source

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Describes the Agent 's influence or power in some way. Descriptors are typically adjectives modifying nominal targets.

definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which avoiding occurs.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the Undesirable_situation is avoided. 'Mike avoided his supervisor at all costs.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which avoiding occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which avoiding occurs.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person whose awareness of phenomena is at question. With a target verb or adjective the Cognizer is generally expressed as an External Argument with the Content expressed as an Object or Complement. 'Your boss is aware of your commitment.' 'The students do not know the answer.'  Examples like the following belong in Opinion: 'Pat believes that things will change for the better.'

name: Content
definition_en: The Content is the object of the Cognizer's awareness. Content can be expressed as a direct object or in a PP Complement.  'Your boss is aware of your commitment.' 'The students do not know of your commitment.' 'The students do not know how committed you are.' 'The students did not know that you were so committed.' Examples like the following belong in Opinion: 'Pat believes that things will change for the better.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: The source of awareness or knowledge which can be expressed in a PP Complement: 'The sailors knew from the look of the sky that a storm was coming.' 'I knew from experience that Jo would be late.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Some verbs in this frame allow a Topic to be expressed in about-PPs. 'Kim knows about first aid.'  However, a number of nouns and adjectives in this frame which cannot take about-phrases allow Topic to be expressed as an adjectival or adverbial modifier. 'Kim is politically aware. ' ' Environmental consciousness is increasing.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer knows or thinks something.

name: Expressor
definition_en: Expressor is the body part that reveals the Cognizer's state to the observer. 'Bob's eyes were overly aware'

name: Role
definition_en: Role is the category within which an element of the Content is considered. 'He understood her remark as an insult.'

name: Paradigm
definition_en: This frame element identifies the Paradigm  which serves as the basis for the Cognizer's awareness. 'The formation of black holes should be understood in astrophysic terms.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which the Cognizer is aware of the Content.  'Yet there is no evidence that Mr. Parrish was cognizant at the time of the signing of the notes that the clauses in issue were present.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason why or how it came to be that the Cognizer has awareness of the Topic or Content.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person whose awareness of the Content is at issue.

name: Content
definition_en: The object of the Cognizer's awareness.

name: Expressor
definition_en: A body part that reveals the Cognizer's relation to the Content.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Content may be understood as pertaining to a Topic.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the state of awareness holds.

name: Evidence
definition_en: The Cognizer's source of awareness about the Content.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer knows or thinks something.

name: Role
definition_en: The category within which the Content is known.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Cognizer has awareness (or lack thereof) of the Content.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person who has (or lacks) awareness of the Content.  'That this chemical is dangerous to consume has been known to us for a long time now.'

name: Content
definition_en: The fact or idea which the Cognizer is aware of.  'That most of them are dangerous is not yet known.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the state of awareness holds.  'That is well known.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: The Cognizer's source of awareness about the Content.

name: Role
definition_en: The category whose applicability to the Content is known.  'The patient arrived with a suspected broken leg.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Cognizer has awareness (or lack thereof) of the Content.  'The long suspected killer has now released a statement outlining his thoughts on the criminal case.'

name: Accused
definition_en: At the time of bail setting, the Accused is held without bail/bond, released on his/her own recognizance, or required to give the Court  a specific amount of money for bail. 'Judge Duncan fixed the doctor's bail at one million dollars.'

name: Judge
definition_en: The Judge, as head of  the Court, determines the Accused's bail. 'Judge Duncan fixed the doctor's bail at one million dollars.'

name: Status
definition_en: Status idenitifies the decision made with regard to bail.  The possible statuses are "without bail/bond", "on one's own recognizance", or a specific amount of money required for bail. 'Judge Duncan fixed the doctor's bail at one million dollars.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the bail setting occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the bail setting occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the bail setting which is not covered by more specific FEs, including, secondary effects (openly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Judge that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: The method used by the Judge to set the bail.  'It used to be that a judge would set bail purely by guesswork.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Judge sets bail.

name: Trajector
definition_en: The entity whose status or location is (generally) unknown, and whose status or location is established by examining the Profiled_region.

name: Landmark
definition_en: The entity, generally presupposed, whose status or location is known or knowable and which thus serves as a basis for understanding the status or location of the Trajector by locating it in a Profiled_region which has a particular relation to the Landmark.

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: The region which has a particular shape, orientation, size, and location (literal or metaphorical) with respect to the Landmark.  The shape of the Profiled_region is virtually always incorporated in the target.  This shaped region usually includes the location of the Landmark, as seen with in.prep, at.prep, on.prep, but may also do exactly the opposite, as with away from.prep.

name: Party_1
definition_en: The individual or individuals that form the more prominent (i.e. agentive) party of the agreement, as compared with Party_2. That is, Party_1 is generally encoded as the External Argument of verbs, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Party_1. Thus Manner is construed to be that of Party_1, not necessarily that of Party_2 or the group of Parties as a whole.  'AOL 's agreement with the ACLU will soon expire , and renogotiation is not a real possibility .'

name: Party_2
definition_en: The semantically (and grammatically) less prominent participant (or group of participants) in the agreement. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with).  'Mozilla Foundation now has a bindingagreement with America Online.'

name: Obligation
definition_en: An expression of the commitment of the Parties .  'The US and Russia have an agreement to share early warning data on missile launches.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic is a description of the domain covered by the agreement.  'Some types of alloy steel have been covered in the expiring trade agreement.'

name: Medium
definition_en: As with other frames in the Communication domain, the Medium of communication may be expressed. Medium is the physical entity or channel used to record or negotiate the Obligation.    'The parties have a written agreement to arbitrate disputes arising in connection with the contract.'

name: Parties
definition_en: The group of individuals portrayed as equally involved in having an agreement.  'The US and Russia have an agreement to cooperate in destroying surplus portable anti-aircraft missiles.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where an agreement was made.  'The Kyoto treaty has so far been relatively ineffectual.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the agreement was made.  'The missile agreement of 1952 was still in force, however.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the agreement not specified by the other FEs, including particularly salient characteristics of the parties.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describes a characteristic or description of the agreement_on_action.

name: Cognizers
definition_en: This FE marks constituents that express the set of Cognizers whose similarity of opinion is at issue.

name: Cognizer_1
definition_en: When there is an asymmetry, Cognizer_1 is the individual characterized by their similarity in opinion to Cognizer_2, whose opinion is assumed to be known.  Cognizer_1 is often an external argument.

name: Cognizer_2
definition_en: When the Cognizers are expressed separately, Cognizer_2 is the one whose opinion is assumed to be known; it serves as a basis for establishing the opinion of Cognizer_1.

name: Question
definition_en: This FE denotes an implicit question in response to which the Cognizers give their Opinions, which are then assessed for their similarity.  The Question may concern the identitiy of a particular entity, as in the first example below, or it may be of the yes/no-type, as in the second example below.   'I think we see eye to eye in our ultimate goal, which is that we want to see a democratic Serbia.'   'Almost all anarchists, in contrast, would agree in their condemnation of warfare, ie, violent conflict between governments.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Cognizers are similar in their Opinions.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Cognizers are in agreement or disagreement.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the general area in which the Cognizers are in agreement or disagreement.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE is for descriptions of the agreement state not covered by more specific FEs, especially characterizations of the state as a whole or of one of the Cognizers or Cognizer_1.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the agreement or disagreement logically follows.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Cognizers

name: Opinion
definition_en: A state of affairs believed by the Cognizers.  'We agree that babies should not be dropped from helicopters.'

name: Topic
definition_en: A phenomenon that the Cognizers are considering with respect to their Opinion.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state-of-affiars under which aggreement occurs (as independent of the act of agreement).

name: Protagonist
definition_en: This FE identifies the Protagonist who is prepared to undertake some action in response to a Danger.  'Troops are on high alert following a string of bombings downtown.'

name: Activity
definition_en: The action that the Protagonist is prepared to do.  'You should be on alert to evacuate within 30 minutes of hearing the siren .'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Protagonist is on alert to the potential Danger.  'They're on alert now .'

name: Result
definition_en: The state or event that follows due to the ready state.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Protagonist remains ready to perform the Activity.  'We have been on guard for a long time.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Protagonist is wary of the possible Danger and ready to perform an Activity.  'All our soldiers are now on high alert.'

name: Danger
definition_en: A dangerous event or situation which teh Protagonist is aware of and is ready to respond to.  'We were all on guard for possible attempts to sabotage the operation.'

name: Dangerous_entity
definition_en: An entity of which the Protagonist is aware and which poses a danger.  'Be on alert for tigers.'

name: Total
definition_en: The complex multi-part entity of which a constituent Part is specified.  'As a representative in Congress in the years 1783-85, Gerry numbered among those who had possessed talent as Revolutionary agitators and wartime leaders.'

name: Part
definition_en: A subset of the Total.  'Just be glad that you number among the living.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE identifies the frequency with which the Part is included in the Total.  'The sort of equipment that astronomers use to detect extrasolar objects often counts among the equipment found in any radio enthusiast's workshop.'

name: Contrast_set
definition_en: This FE indicates other totalities that the Part may also be a subset of.

name: Subregion
definition_en: This FE indicates the sub-location of the Total in which the Part is included. [MAY BE UNNECESSARY]

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the subset relation holds.  'At that time, the factory numbered among the largest in the western half of North America.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place at which the subset relation holds.  'In Europe, the sport counts among the economic branches of industry which generate employment among the young people.'

name: Source_symbol
definition_en: A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Source_representation format.  'This expression translates the Greek word Hades.'

name: Source_representation
definition_en: The representation system in which the Content pre-exists.

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the translation equivalence holds.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the translation is made.

name: Target_symbol
definition_en: A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Target_representation format.   'The Tibetan sequence of words translates the Chinese Ti- shih.'

name: Target_representation
definition_en: The representation system within which the Target_symbol is equivalent in its signification to the Source_symbol within the Source_representation system .

name: Content
definition_en: The information that is meant to be represented by the Source_symbol and Target_symbol.

name: Equivalence
definition_en: An assessment of how equivalent the Source_representation and the Target_representation are.  'Choose the Russian expression that correctly translates the English word or phrase.'

name: Medium
definition_en: A text in which the Target_symbol is used to render the Content of a Source_symbol.  'In the Greek Scriptures the word translates the Greek word "theos".'

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount of Weapons that the Protagonist has (relative to some standard). 'He is very well armed.'

name: Weapon
definition_en: The destructive device that the Protagonist has with them.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The individual that possesses a Weapon.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where a Protagonist carries a Weapon.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Protagonist carries a Weapon.

name: Winner
definition_en: The individual or individuals who beat the Loser.

name: Score
definition_en: A quantity whereby progress is measured during the game, and Rank and Prizes are awarded to the Winner afterward.

name: Margin
definition_en: The amount by which the Winner 's and Loser 's Scores differ.

name: Rank
definition_en: The rank (according to Score) that a Winner acheives.

name: Prize
definition_en: A socially and/or monetarily significant entity which is given to a Winner according to Score or Rank.

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Winner or Loser that makes the beating event possible.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Winner or Loser which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Winner or Loser that also affect their action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Time
definition_en: When the Winner has victory over the Loser.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Winner has victory Loser.

name: Venue
definition_en: This FE is for the named venue of a competition, particularly when the place has been built for the purpose of a competition.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason why the Winner has victory over the Loser.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when winning events began to be repeated to when they stopped.

name: Loser
definition_en: The individual or individuals that get beat by the Winner.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world when the Winner beats the Loser.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re-encoding, but not necessarily.

name: Result
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that prevails as a result of the Winner beating the Loser.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times the Winner beats the Loser.

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the winning event operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness, or a description of the state-of-affairs introduced by the winning event.

name: Degree
definition_en: A qualitative measure of how much the Winner beat the Loser.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Competition
definition_en: The event in which the  Competition competes.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Winner beats the Loser.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the change takes place.  'He always became uncomforatable in bars .'

name: Time
definition_en: >When the change occurs.  'By 1945 he had become uncertain of the advisability of anyone having such a weapon.'

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: How long the Entity remains in the Final_category, Final_situation, or Final_quality.   'He became for the next three years the prophetic voice of the Salvadoran people until his assassination on March 24, 1980'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In cases where the Entity is intentional, Manner may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Entity that also affect the event (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'The majority slowly became more and more disenchanted with him.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity which undergoes a change, newly ending up in the Final_category or taking on a new Final_quality.  'I grow impatient with your insolence.'

name: Final_quality
definition_en: A description of a characteristic of the Entity after the change.  'Suddenly , she became impatient .'

name: Final_category
definition_en: The category that the Entity ends up in after the change.  Typically, this entails taking on a number of new characteristics.  'He never could understand how she ended up an evangelist.'

name: Transitional_period
definition_en: The period during which the Entity is in transition.  'Over the last 5 years, I've become sick and tired of your tomfoolery.'

name: Initial_state
definition_en: This FE describes the state of the Entity before change occurs.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE marks the set of conditions under which the Entity enters the Final_category or takes on the characteristic of the Final_quality.

name: Initial_category
definition_en: This FE describes the category of the Entity before a change.

name: Group
definition_en: A description of the kind of entities associated with instances of the Entity and saliently affected by its change.

name: Explanation
definition_en: Any eventuality or entity which brings about the change of the Entity.  'Smithers became tired from all the work he'd been doing.'

name: New_member
definition_en: The New_member becomes a member of a (socially-defined) Group.  'Have you signed up for the new Medicare Prescription program?'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the joining occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the New_member joins the Group.  'In 1714 he enlisted in the Venetian army to fight against the Moslem Turks.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the New_member joins the Group.  'An avid skier myself, I ventured to Aspen and enrolled in Nevin's school last winter to see what all the fuss was about.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the New_member becomes part of the group.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a New_member that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency with which the New_member becomes a member of a Group.

name: Group
definition_en: The Group is a socially-constructed entity composed of members. 'Please join our club! CNI'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A factor that explains why the New_member joins the Group.  ' I enlisted in the Navy because no one else in my family had ever been in it before.'

name: Role
definition_en: The capacity or role in which the New_member is placed upon joining the Group.  'Rogers joined our company last year as Vice President.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the New_member when they join.

name: Reciprocation
definition_en: This FE denotes an event paired with that of the main clause, which explains why the event of the main clause is expected. In particular, reciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished in the main clause, or an action that is paired with the action in the main clause as the other side of an agreement.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action.

name: Connector
definition_en: Connector identifies the  instrument used to attach, usually in a with-PP.  'The remoras attach to the whale with their strong jaws.'

name: Handle
definition_en: Handle identifies the point of attachment on the Goal to which the Item attaches.  'The remoras attach by the mouth.'

name: Item
definition_en: Item identifies the entity that comes to be attached to the Goal.  'Remoras attached to the dolphins.'

name: Items
definition_en: Items identifies the plural items that are tied together, resulting in their mutual attachment.  'The cells bind together.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal identifies the location to which the first Item is attached.  'The remoras attach to the underside of the whale.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an attaching event.  'The cells bind together.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Item comes to be attached to a Goal.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the attaching event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the attaching event takes place.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person who becomes aware of a Phenomenon. It is normally expressed as an External Argument.  'Pat discovered a great little restaurant in Soho.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: Thm Phenomenon is the entity or situation in the world of which a Cognizer becomes aware. It is normally expressed as an Object:  'Pat discovered a great little restaurant in Soho.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground is the background or context against which a Cognizer becomes aware of a Phenomenon. It is normally expressed by a locative PP:  'Pat discovered a great little restaurant in Soho.' 'I noticed a hint of sarcasm in her voice. '

name: State
definition_en: The State indicates the state or situation of the Phenomenon at the time when the Cognizer becomes aware of it.  It is normally expressed by a Predicate expression (e.g. a PP or a participial VP):  'We discovered the children playing in the pantry.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: The Evidence is some fact that allows the Cognizer to become aware of something. It is normally expressed with PP-from:  'We discovered from their job performance that they were well-trained.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which becoming aware is occurring.  'Sue could faintly discern the shape of a skull under Cheeks ' plump face.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifes the Manner in which becoming aware occurs.  'Pupils quickly discern what is acceptable to the teacher and merely aim to fulfil those expectations.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifes the Means by which the Cognizer becomes aware of the Phenomenon.  'By opening the book to page 10, you will find the Van Eerdens' number.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic indicates the general field within which the Phenomenon is found.  'Scientists attempt to make discoveries about the laws of nature.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Cognizer becomes aware of the Phenomenon.  'Robbie had wondered if they would be able to find the path at night.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The goal that the Cognizer has in mind, which they believe to be accomplishable by finding the Phenomenon.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Cognizer uses an Instrument to (enable themselves to) become aware of the Phenomenon.  In some cases, the Instrument may appear in subject position.  'Olson says the deputy came out to the farm and detected a radioactive substance with his Geiger counter.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: his frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE is minimally distinct from Duration and Duration_of final_state in that the clause described is conveyed to be iterative.

name: Item
definition_en: This FE identifies the Item that detaches from the Source.

name: Source
definition_en: Source identifies the location to which an Item was attached before getting detached.

name: Items
definition_en: This FE identifies the plural Items that are becoming detached from each other, resulting in their separation.   Notice that when the FE Items occurs, neither Item nor Source can occur.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the detaching event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously),  secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Item  becomes detached.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Item becomes detached from the Source.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item ends up detached.

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity is the thing that loses moisture and becomes dry.

name: Degree
definition_en: The intensity with which the Entity becomes dry.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Entity becomes dry.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity becomes dry.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Entity becomes dry.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The situation in which the Entity is becoming dry.

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: This FE indicates that the visiting is a particular instance in a series of repeated visiting events.

name: Whole
definition_en: The Whole is a single entity or an aggregate of entities which separates into Parts.  'Metalworkers' union to split into regional divisions'

name: Parts
definition_en: This refers collectively to the Parts resulting from separation of a Whole:  'These daughter chromosomes then begin to separate from each other, each moving away from the metaphase plate and toward one of the two spindle pole regions.' 'Watch as they split into many differently-shaped bits.'

name: Part_1
definition_en: Part-1 is the first of two Parts mentioned.  'Initially, the front part separated from the rest of the body.'

name: Part_2
definition_en: Part_2 is the second of two Parts mentioned. This is usually a PP Complement.   'Initially the front split from the rest of the body'

name: Criterion
definition_en: This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the separation. Criterion is typically expressed as a PP headed by by, or as a complex PP of the form on the basis of....  'Particles will therefore only separate on the basis of contact angle as long as their mass is between an upper and lower critical value.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the undergoers of the separation.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Means
definition_en: An intermediate action or event that enables the separation.  'Explore how cells divide by undergoing mitosis.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the separation occurs.  'However it is believed they separated at least 2 if not 3 million years ago.'.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the separation occurs.  'The two parts likely separated above the Atlantic.'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker has previously been speaking but has now stopped. 'The children finally quieted down.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject which the Speaker had been speaking about. 'Mark shut up about the book.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location where the becoming silent occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the becoming silent occurs.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The Expressor is the Speaker's voice or other communicative noise emitted by the Speaker. 'The excited chatter hushed.'</def-root >

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner in which the quietening occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Entity
definition_en: The thing that the Perceiver is able to see or recognize.

name: Perceiver
definition_en: The person who is able to see the Entity. This FE is often null-instantiated as it is deprofiled in this scene.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of how the Entity becomes visible that is not covered by more specific FEs.

name: Place
definition_en: The physical location in which the Entity becomes visible.

name: Time
definition_en: A temporal description of the event of the Entity becoming visible.

name: Artist
definition_en: The Artist works off-stage to help make the Production. 'John Williams composed the soundtrack to Star Wars.'

name: Production
definition_en: The Production is the final product put out by the off-stage (and on-stage) participants. 'Ralph Smith produced the off-Broadway hit "Why Is My Name Ralph?".'

name: Type
definition_en: An Artist may be categorizedy by Type. 'Hollywood director' 'independent film-maker'

name: Distributor
definition_en: Often (especially with film or television) the Production is advertised and transmitted to the audience by the Distributor. 'Even desperate producers would never produce a film for that television station.'

name: Studio
definition_en: This FE indicates the particular orgainzaion that makes the Production. 'The latest performance produced by The Umbrella Thesbians was a major hit in France.' 'First layer: New Line Cinema produces several films each year.' 'Second layer: New Line Cinema produces several films each year.'

name: Medium
definition_en: This FE indicates the Medium in which a particular Artist works or a Production is made. 'He produces for television' 'She is a theatre director.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the time when the Production is made. 'Silence of the Lambs was filmed in 1991.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE indicates the location of production. 'The documentary was shot on location.'

name: Nationality
definition_en: This FE indicates the Nationality, ethnicity, or primary working location of the Artist. 'Several Canadian directors have received attention from critics in recent years.' 'Local film-makers often collaborate for larger efforts.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which an Artist works on a Production. 'I produced this film to let people know what I went through as a child.'

name: Performer
definition_en: In screen performances, the Performer is filmed as he or she acts out a role with respect to the larger Production 'This particular scene was shot with a local choir and dancers.'

name: Score
definition_en: The music which may be performed in the performance of the Production, either in isolation or accompanying actions and speech.

name: Scene
definition_en: A Scene is a sub-part of a larger production.  In film, scenes are sometimes recorded independently, and later edited into the final movie.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Artist creates the Production.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the amount of Time for which an Activity is ongoing.  'Upon his release from federal detention in 1947 he joined the IWW and has remained active for five decades as a graphic artist, poet, and advisor.'

name: Activity
definition_en: This FE identifies the name of the ongoing Activity in which an Agent engages.  'He is always active demolishing the painted figures of men's faith and then is astonished to find the faith still there clothed in new figure.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the  Activity is pursued.  'He is retired from Whirlpool Corp. in Clyde and is active at the YMCA. '

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent is engaged in an ongoing Activity.  'Throughout her life, Bertha was active in civic organizations in order to establish chiropractics in the public eye.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Activity is pursued.  'Commercial selling was active yesterday but a lack of interest allowed the market to push sharply higher into the mid-session.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Activity which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that  affect the action (presumptuously, deliberately).   'The Government was deliberately inactive in respect of Maori. language teacher training and teaching.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent engages in an ongoing Activity.   'He was active for six decades as a painter, graphic designer and theorist of art and design.'

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: An entity acted upon by the Agent.  'As many as 324 companies' stocks were active across the board.'

name: Role
definition_en: This FE identifies the role filled by the Agent which is saliently associated with an Activity.  'Jacques Fuller has been active as a sculptor in Bloemfontein for almost two decades.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Agent or Salient_entity is active.  'Mick was an extremely active volunteer for the Air Force IT Day committee.'

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iterations, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs-Iteration expressions answer the question how many times.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Asset
definition_en: Something judged to be desirable or valuable which might be lost or damaged.  'There is a locked padlock that guarantees the information is secure. '

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of security from the expected value given the Asset and the state indicated by the target itself.  'My mail is totally secure in this box.'

name: Harmful_event
definition_en: An action that may occur or a state which may hold which could result in the loss of or damage to the Asset.  'Our system ensures that information stored within hardware is secure from external software attack and physical theft. '

name: Dangerous_entity
definition_en: A concrete or abstract entity which may come to cause the loss of, or damage to the Asset either due to its participation in a Harmful_event.  'We make sure your BMW is secure against intruders.'

name: Place
definition_en: A particular location in which the Asset is secure. Frequently, it is to be inferred that the characteristics of the location protect the Asset from a potential Harmful_event.  'Workers need to make sure their property is secure at work.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Asset enjoys  the specified level of security from a Harmful_event.  ' Israel is insecure today not because it does not have enough military power.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the state of security or insecurity of the Asset logically follows.

name: Situation
definition_en: The Situation under which the Asset is safe or unsafe.  'Our children are safe with that criminal behind bars.'  Most expressions of Time and Place also express the Situation and should be labeled as such on the 2nd FE layer.

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain in which the Asset has a degree of safety.  'Students with Asthma need to be medically safe at school.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Connector
definition_en: Connector identifies the instrument used to attach and is usually expressed in a with-PP.  'The tarp is  tied down with a rope.'

name: Handle
definition_en: Handle identifies the point of attachment on the Item.  'Harry was tied by the neck to the tree.'

name: Item
definition_en: Item identifies the entity that comes to be attached to the Goal.  'A handle  was affixed to the door.'

name: Items
definition_en: Items identifies the plural items that are tied together, resulting in their mutual attachment.  'The boats remained tied together.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal identifies the location to which the Item(s) is attached.  'The boat remained anchored to the coastline.'

name: Dependent_state
definition_en: Dependent_state identifies the state of the Item or Items which depends on the existence of the attachment.  'The tarp is tied down with a cord.' 'Harry's hands are tied downwith cords.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Item is in an attached state to a Goal, or two Items are attached to each other.  'The tiny stick  was fastened tightly to his wrist.'

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The entity that is not sleeping.  'She was awake through the whole football game.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Protagonist is awake.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Protagonist is awake.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Protagonist is awake.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Protagonist being awake which is not covered by more specific FEs including secondary effects (quietly, noisily), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Child
definition_en: Child identifies the new self-motile creature.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the birth occurs, generally expressed as a date or a year.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Child enters the world.

name: Relatives
definition_en: The individuals that the Child is related to, including the male and female individuals that come together to produce a Child (the parents), as well those who are related to them by birth or marriage.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Child as it enters the world.

name: Means
definition_en: The way in which the Child leaves the womb; this FE is typically only filled by phrases such as by natural birth or by Caesarian.

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: The interior region of the Landmark, within which the Trajector is to be found.

name: Landmark
definition_en: The container which serves as a reference point for the Trajector which is surrounded by it.

name: Trajector
definition_en: The entity which is to be located with respect to the Landmark.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Trajector is contained within the Landmark.

name: Item
definition_en: Item identifies the entity that is detached from a Source.   'I feel like my head is detached from the rest of my body.'

name: Items
definition_en: Items identifies the plural items that are detached from each other.  'The neck vertebrae are unfused in rorquals and gray whales, which allows for some flexibility at the head and neck.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source identifies the location from which the Item(s) is detached.   'The toilet is loose from the floor and must be repaired.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Item is in an detached state relative to a Source, or two Items are detached from each other.

name: Item
definition_en: The Item exists in a state of dryness. ' <fex name = "Item" >The mop is dry.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item is dry.

name: Subregion
definition_en: Subregion identifies the affected part of the larger whole. 'The cloth was <t >dry around the edges.'

name: Compensation
definition_en: The Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.  'Louise works as an engineer for $1,000'

name: Employee
definition_en: The Employee is obligated to perform a Task in order to receive Compensation.  'My Mom works for the Michigan Department of Agriculture.'

name: Employer
definition_en: The Employer gives Compensation to an Employee.  'My mom works for an Eye Doctor.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employee works for an Employer.  ' Last weekend, the commercial TV station Nova broadcast testimonies of young Czechs who have worked illegally for America's largest retailer, Wal-Mart.'

name: Place_of_employment
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place_of_employment of the Employee.  'The undocumented foreigners were working at the organic farm.'

name: Position
definition_en: The label given to a particular type of employment.   'Louise works as an engineer.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Employee  is in employment.  'He waited tables to finance his education at St. Lawrence University, where he was a top-notch wrestler.'

name: Task
definition_en: The Employee is obligated to perform the Task to recieve Compensation from the Employer .  'My dad works building houses.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time period during which an Employee  works for an Employer.  'From 2000-2001, Mr. Eckhardt clerked for The Honorable Jerry A. Funk, United States Bankruptcy Judge, Middle District of Florida.'

name: Field
definition_en: This FE identifies the Field in which one works.  'Undocumented foreigners work in construction for years.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the amount of Time for which the Employee continues being employed.  'She worked for 10 years in private and hospital practice and 19 years in teaching and administration.'

name: Rank
definition_en: Rank is the position in a hierarchy that an Employee occupies within the organization of the Employer.   'Sue has the  top job in the company.'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE identifies the Type of the profession.  'He's harkening back to a time before Bush became president and he had a white collar job and wore a suit.'

name: Contract_basis
definition_en: The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.  'As much as possible, however, do not attempt to run a full-time business in addition to holding a full-time job .'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Employee works.  'Most people work in the city.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Employee works.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE gives a description of the Being_employed event.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity which is confined.  'He was in captivity for six days.'

name: Holding_location
definition_en: The area within which the Theme is confined.  'The captives in the next room were fed well but otherwise ignored.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent prevents the Theme from moving.  'I would rather not remember being their captive.'

name: Reciprocation
definition_en: The reason for the confinement.  'He was our prisoner for betraying his superiors.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the general Place where the Theme is held captive.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Theme is held captive.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the state of being captive which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Theme.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Theme is held captive.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Theme remains in captivity.

name: Cause
definition_en: An inanimate force which causes the Theme in be unable to move.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: This is the person who performs an act of categorization. Typically, this frame element is expressed as an oblique.  'But to me, a bad thought constitutes a sin just as well. '

name: Item
definition_en: This is the entity which is is an instance of a particular Category. Typically, the Item is expressed as the external argument.  'To me, finding this is tantamount to finding the fabeled El Dorado.'

name: Category
definition_en: This frame element expresses a general type or class of which the Item is considered an instance. Typically, it is expressed in a prepositional phrase headed by as or under.  'I'd say that this book counts as fiction.'

name: Criteria
definition_en: This frame element expresses properties of the Item which is used as a basis for categorization. Criteria are the general dimensions along which Items can potentially differ from one another and hence, fall into different Categorys. For example, a paint sample can be classified by color or by finish (matte or gloss); if they are classified by color, one can be classified as orange and another as red. The Criteria FE is typically expressed as a PP headed by by, or as a complex PP of the form on the basis of...:  'If it counts as knowledge in part on the basis of justification from another source, it must be in part based on that source '

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which an Item (metaphorically) is construed as being in a Category.

name: Means
definition_en: An act or state of affairs by which the Item (perhaps metaphorically) is interpreted as being in a Category.

name: Time
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate when a certain Categorization holds.  'Fold in inflation and what counted as shameful gouging 20 years ago is today called charging what the market will bear.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the categorization holds. 'Material posessions count as valuable in a particular society.'

name: Controlling_entity
definition_en: A thing or person whose behavior controls a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.

name: Dependent_entity
definition_en: An entity, usually a thing, that is influenced in its behavior by a Controlling_entity.

name: Dependent_situation
definition_en: A situation whose temporal or other characteristics are influenced by a Controlling_entity.

name: Dependent_variable
definition_en: A scalar variable, whose value depends on the behavior of a Controlling_entity.  'Move the slider on the SpeedBar while playing audio or video material to control playback speed.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Controlling_entity effects the Dependent_entity.

name: Time
