definition_en: The Time at which the controlling occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the controlling occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Controlling_entity that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Binding_principle
definition_en: The Binding_principle is the law, contract, principle, or other (set of) obligations that is (or is not) operational.  'Once the treaty is in effect, US port authorities and the Coast Guard will monitor compliance by checking any yacht 79 feet or longer.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time for which the Binding_principle is or is not in effect.  'The contract will be effectivefor three fiscal years.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Binding_principle is in effect.  'All patent applicants and owners should be aware of the current uncertainty as to what patent fees will be in effect on October 1, 1998'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place at which the Binding_principle is or is not operational.  'This promotion is void in the state of Florida.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state-of-affairs under which the Binding_principle is/isn't operational.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A cause, reason, or other Explanation for the status of the Binding_principle  'Your contract is null because you left the county.'

name: Obligated_party
definition_en: The individual or group who is obligated to follow the Binding_principle.  'This statute is in effect for holders of H-1 visas until January.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Device
definition_en: The Device or machine that is in or out of operation.  'Lights were on in the primary school '

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when a Device is in or out of operation.  'I do n't want to turn round cos the lights are on at the moment '

name: Place
definition_en: The Place in which the Device is or is not operating.  ' Lights were on on the Kingston road bridge.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

name: Prisoner
definition_en: The Prisoner is held in custody as a punishment for having committed a crime.

name: Prison
definition_en: The facility where the Prisoner is held.

name: Authorities
definition_en: The Authorities hold the Prisoner in custody.

name: Crime
definition_en: The crime of which the Prisoner is guilty, resulting in imprisonment.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the general Place where the Prisoner is held captive.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Prisoner is in prison.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the state of being imprisoned which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Prisoner is in custody.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Prisoner remains in jail.

name: Whole
definition_en: The Whole is the larger entity that includes the Part.

name: Part
definition_en: The Part is either a subset or a constituent part of the Whole.

name: Theme
definition_en: An entity which is at a particular Location

name: Place
definition_en: The location (generally presumed to be known to the interlocutor) with respect to which the location of the Theme can be understood.

name: Dependent_state
definition_en: A state (of the Theme) that results as a consequence of the Theme being situated at the Location.  'The inn was well situated to take advantage of the visiting tourists.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Theme is at the Location.

name: Location
definition_en: A salient entity that the Theme is located with respect to.

name: Cotheme
definition_en: This frame element is used to denote phrases that specifically entail an entity which is conceived as moving relative to another entity.

name: Depictive
definition_en: A Depictive expression describes a state or condition of the Theme independent of its location.  'The rubble of the buildings lies in a heap just outside the city.'

name: Name
definition_en: Name identifies the linguistic expression used to refer to Entities.  'My name is Bond.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity is the person the speaker intends to refer to by using a particular name.  'You have an unusual surname.'

name: Language
definition_en: Language is used for a person or thing to whose name the Name of the Entity is taken or in honor of.  'Spanish and Indian names were precedents to other non-English-sounding names.'

name: Type
definition_en: The FE Type denotes sub-type of names.  'My given name used to be John.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Describes the Name in some manner.  'His favorite nickname is 'The Dark Knight'.'

name: Context
definition_en: The context is the region or domain in which the name applies.  'The Spanish name 'Juan' begins with an English 'w'.'

name: Etymological_root
definition_en: The source language or inspiration for the Name.  'His name in Spanish is 'Santiago', from the Latin.'

name: Dependent
definition_en: The state-of-affairs which cannot hold without the Requirement.

name: Requirement
definition_en: The entity or state-of-affairs that must be present or obtain in order for the Dependent to obtain.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Dependent depends on the presence of the Requirement.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent.

name: Condition
definition_en: The conditions under which the the Requirement is necessary.  'Such care is necessary if you operate under martial law.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The field of endeavor whose nature imposes the Requirement.  'Unfortunately, such tactics appear to be politically necessary nowadays.'

name: Place
definition_en: Place denotes a location in which the specified relation between Requirement and Dependent holds.  'In the US, the political clout of big city mayors is necessary to put this on the national agenda.'

name: Dependent_individual
definition_en: The individual who needs to have the Required_entity or for the Requirement state of affairs to obtain.  ' We ask you to obtain for us all that is necessary for us.'

name: Required_entity
definition_en: An entity that has to be present for the Dependent state of affairs to obtain.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: An characteristic or feature of the Requirement or Required_entity.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Responsible_party
definition_en: The person who must perform the Duty. 'Everyone has the obligation to vote.'

name: Duty
definition_en: The action that the Responsible_party is obligated to perform. 'My job is to get to the other side of the bridge.'

name: Condition
definition_en: This FE indicates the Conditions under which the Responsible_party is obligated to perform the Duty.  'As a conscientious citizen, it is your duty to report any suspicious behavior.'

name: Consequence
definition_en: The Consequence will result if the Duty is not performed.

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which the Responsibly_party is obligated to fulfill the Duty.   'At that time men were obligated to marry women from their own community.'

name: Place
definition_en: A location in which the Responsible_party has a specified Duty .  'I almost forgot to tell you that in Sweden we are obligated to spend atleast 7.5 months in the army for training.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Condition
definition_en: This FE indicates the Condition under which the  Duty is required of the Responsible_party.  'The use of a spirometer is mandatory if early stages of chronic obstructive lung disease are to be detected.'

name: Consequence
definition_en: The Consequence will result if the Duty is not performed.  'Attendance of the 341 meeting of creditors is mandatory or you will not receive your discharge.'

name: Duty
definition_en: The action that the Responsible_party is obligated to perform.   'Getting a shot against yellow fever is obligatory for travellers to Benin. '

name: Responsible_party
definition_en: The person who must perform the Duty.  'The use of TM software is obligatory for every freelance translator working on projects for our company.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which the Duty is mandatory.  'These days, wearing a seat-belt is mandatory.'

name: Place
definition_en: A location in which the Duty  obtains.  'Gymnasium is not obligatory in Sweden, but nearly everyone attends gymnasium'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The positive consequence of the Duty being fulfilled.  'Not acting as a savior is compulsory to avoid misunderstanding and loss of confidence in partnership, which many American investors, particularly African Americans, may experience.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason why the Duty is necessary for the Responsible_party.   'Rigorous posttreatment follow-up is mandatory, because long-term recurrence rates after treatment of melanoma in situ with imiquimod are yet unknown. '

name: Object
definition_en: The entity with an understood purpose.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Artifact exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for being operational.

name: Mother
definition_en: This frame element refers to the parent who is physically pregnant.

name: Father
definition_en: This frame element refers to a parent who contributed to the conception of a child but is not physically carrying a child.

name: Parents
definition_en: This frame element refers to the collective body expecting or carrying a child.

name: Offspring
definition_en: This frame refers to the conceived offspring borne by the Parents.

name: Duration
definition_en: This frame element refers to the length of time the Parents have been pregnant.

name: Behavior
definition_en: The Behavior is the state of affairs or action of the social actor that is regarded as susipcious.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Behavior is suspicious. 'That looks like very suspicious activity.'

name: Social_actor
definition_en: An individual that is suspected of wrongdoing because of the Behavior.

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity metonymically stands in for a Behavior that saliently involves the Entity.

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: Something that is profiled in the mind of the Cognizer as being related to mental Endeavors.

name: Endeavor
definition_en: A cognitive action (eg discussion, decision) performed by the Cognizer to which the Phenomenon is connected in some way.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: A participant in the mental Endeavor to which the Phenomenon is related. This frame element is often null-instantiated and may be inferred from the Endeavor.

name: Degree
definition_en: A description of how related the Phenomenon is to the Endeavor.

name: Specification
definition_en: The knowledge or situation that mediates the relevance of the Phenomenon to the Endeavor.  'How does Assad 's family dynamic play into his intransigence ?'

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is the organic matter that has decayed. 'The coconut milk became rancid.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which rotting has occurred. 'The coconut milk was so rancid.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity whose meeting or falling short of pre-conditions is assessed.  'Little Tommy was not up to getting out of bed.'

name: Activity
definition_en: The Activity that the Entity may participate in.  'He was a very meek and shy person, and always felt that he was not equal to the task set before him.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for participating in the Activity.  'Blind parents are very much up to driving their kids to soccer practice.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions.  'Bill was not equal to the task with the distraction of the alien landing.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to  meet or fail to meet the pre-conditions for participating in an Activity.   'Because of his mother's death, Smithers was not up to taking the final exam.'

name: Relevant_feature
definition_en: A characteristic or behavior of the Entity that is considered when judging whether the Entity might participate in the Activity.  'The robot is up to the task in intelligence but completely socially inept.'

name: Item
definition_en: The Item takes up the Liquid through its pores. ' <fex name = "Item" >The mop is drenched with water.'

name: Liquid
definition_en: The Liquid is a fluid or gas that permeates the Item.  It most frequently occurs in a PP Complement headed by with. 'The mop was drenched  with water.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item is wet. 'The mop is absolutely drenched.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation brings about the state of wetness, and is usually expressed in a from-prepositional phrase. 'The mop is drenched from the rain.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected. 'The mop was drenched on  the fringes.'

name: Assailant
definition_en: The Assailant is a group of armed forces (or, metonymically, their commander or the organization they represent) that encircles, surrounds, or otherwise cuts off the Beseiged in an attempt to force surrender.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is the fortification or geopolitical entity that is being attacked.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Assailant that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Assailant that accomplishes the assault.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Assailant makes an assault on the Victim.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Assailant attacks the Victim.

name: Source
definition_en: The starting-point of the motion of the Assailant or projectiles of the Assailant as they move toward the the Place that the Victim is occupying in the attack.  In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion.  With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Assailant attacks the Victim.

name: Weapon
definition_en: An entity used by the Assailant to cause damage to the Victim.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Assailant travels.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Victim is under attack from the Assailant

name: Standard
definition_en: The Standard is the entity that is located closest to the end of the scale evoked by some Variable. 'Hilary was unmatched by any politician in the country.'

name: Variable
definition_en: The Variable is a property that evokes a scale along which the Standard is located closest to one extreme in  comparison to its Competitors.  'Hilary possessed matchless integrity.'

name: Competitors
definition_en: The FE Competitors denotes the entities that are exceeded by the Standard with regard to the Variable.  'Hilary was unmatched by any politician in the country.' 'He is unrivalled even among tennis players for his temper.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The spatial or temporal context in which the Standard is not matched by any Competitors.  'Our commitment to service and quality is legendary and unmatched in Pakistan.'

name: Debtor
definition_en: The person (or organization) that owes the Owed_party. 'The pizza man billed Lee $35 for his order.'

name: Goods
definition_en: The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction.  'The man at the counter billed Lee for his dry-cleaning.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the billing occurs. 'The money was billed through a credit card transaction.'

name: Money
definition_en: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction, or as recompense for the Bad_action. 'The clerk invoiced the little old lady $49.95 for what she called "a little hand-holding . "'

name: Rate
definition_en: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. 'The cleaner bills at forty dollars per hour for his services.'

name: Owed_party
definition_en: The Owed_party expects a specific amount of Money from the Debtor, either because the Debtor received Goods or because the Debtor performed a Bad_action against the Owed_party. 'The salesman never billed me , so I did n't pay .'

name: Unit
definition_en: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by or per-PP.   'I need a per-item invoice !'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which an event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the billing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Seller that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully). 'He carefully collected all his debts.'

name: Billing_authority
definition_en: The individual who communicates to the Debtor the Money that they owe.

name: Payment_status
definition_en: Describes the relation between the invoice and the associated payment: unpaid, paid, overdue, etc.

name: Bad_action
definition_en: An earlier action by the Debtor causing harm (directly or indirectly) to the Owed_party, for which the Owed_party expects compensation, and therefore bills the Debtor.

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Constituent_parts make up a Locale.  'This is the  oldest  oak forest in California.'

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: Container_possessor is the location of which the Locale is a part.  'Jon explored the forests of California.'

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: Formational_cause brings about the features of the Locale. 'Jon explored the sun-scorched savanna.' This FE is also used for words  that indicate no salient formation. 'Jon explored the virgin woodland.'

name: Locale
definition_en: This FE identifies a stable bounded area, and is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames. 'There used to be a forest in that valley.'

name: Name
definition_en: This FE indicates the Names of Locales. 'Jon explored the forests of California.' 'Jon hiked around Muir Woods. '

name: Relative_location
definition_en: Relative_location identifies a place in respect to which a Locale is located.  'All the swamps outside of Georgia are dry.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description, characteristic, or property of the Locale which is not covered by more specific FEs.  'Apparently they found him at the bottom of a really deep bog.'

name: Rank
definition_en: The Rank is the taxonomic category to which the Member belongs.  It is also always the target-denoting noun.  'Molds and mushrooms belong to the kingdom Fungi.'

name: Member
definition_en: The living organism which belongs to the expressed Rank.  'The genus Homo includes modern humans.'

name: Subtype
definition_en: The subtype of the Rank.  'Do humans belong to the order Primate?'

name: Property
definition_en: A property of the Member of the Rank.  'Members of the phylum Cycliophora have a circular mouth.'

name: Organism
definition_en: An organic that has naturally occuring bioligical processes and functions.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any characterization of the Organism not covered by other FEs.

name: Origin
definition_en: The location from which the Organism originated.

name: Trigger
definition_en: The force that brings about the change in the Systemic_effect.

name: Systemic_effect
definition_en: The biological entity that is affected by the Trigger.

name: Place
definition_en: Location where the Systemic_effect takes place.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree identifies the extent to which the Experiencer receives the biological signal.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer receives the biological signal and possesses the internal experience which is a reaction to the phsyical signal. 'Mr. Burns was sexually aroused.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Experiencer feels the biological signal. Time may also allow inference about the Reason for the biological urge.  'I am exhausted when I babysit.' In such cases, we tag Reason on the second layer.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the  Place is where the Experiencer feels the biological signal.

name: Expressor
definition_en: Expressor is used for a gesture, expression, or body part indicating that the Experiencer is feeling a certain urge.  'He gave me a tired shrug and then looked down again.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration identifies the amount of time for which the Experiencer feels the urge.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which the Experiencer has the biological urge.  'Jen is tired because she gave birth last night..'

name: State
definition_en: State identifies the Experiencer's state of being.  'She was alarmed by John's hungry <fex  name = "State">state.'

name: Parameter
definition_en: Parameter is the particular biological realm in which the Experiencer feels the urge. 'Mr. Burns was <fex name = "Parameter">sexually aroused.'

name: Offspring
definition_en: The living being that is produced by the Parents.

name: Mother
definition_en: The female being that produces the Offspring.

name: Father
definition_en: The male being that aids in the production of the Offspring.

name: Parents
definition_en: The Mother and Father collectively.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the birth of the Offspring takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Offspring is born.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the birthing event takes place.

name: Traveller
definition_en: The Traveller is the entity which boards the Vehicle.  'At approximately 07:30 hours we emplaned in England and after circling to gather other units that made up the 1st Airborne Army, we headed for the Rhine.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The Vehicle is the intended means of conveyance of the Traveller.   'When he had mounted the horse, his armour glittered in the sun, and he looked so brave and handsome.'

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion outside of or off the Vehicle expresses the frame element Source.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path describes the trajectory of the Traveller's motion onto the Vehicle.

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The amount of time the Traveller spends on the Vehicle after boarding it.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Traveller or Vehicle during the boarding.  'Kate Lawler (no relation) reportedly boarded a plane drunk after hitting the bar when her flight was delayed for five hours. '

name: Time
definition_en: When the boarding of the Vehicle takes place.  'Therese entrained at 9am on 4 October for the Brandhoek area. .'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: A theme that rides in the same Vehicle as the main Traveller. This may be an entity the Traveller transports or a co-traveller moving under their own power.  'This woman got on the bus with a whole gaggle of little children.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Traveller boards the vehicle.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Traveller boards the Vehicle.  'You can get on the shuttle bus at the Bank of America across from the BART station.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Body_location
definition_en: This FE identifies the location on the body where the decoration takes place. 'Abby has a tattoo on her lower-back.'

name: Decorated_individual
definition_en: This is the individual whose body is decorated. 'Abby rarely wears lipstick.'

name: Decoration
definition_en: Decoration is the decorative item that adorns the body. 'Abby has a tattoo on her thigh.'

name: Decoration_descriptor
definition_en: Dec_desc identifies a descriptor of the Decoration. 'Abby wears red lipstick.'

name: Picture
definition_en: This is the frame element that describes what shape the Decoration represents. 'Abby has a tattoo of a rose on her thigh.'

name: Use
definition_en: This FE identifies the Use to which a body decoration is put. 'Abby is wearing stage make-up.'

name: Type
definition_en: Type designates different kinds of body decorations.  Often this FE will label part of a multi-word or compound word target.  'Abby wore SPF 15 make-up to work, everyday.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which a body has a particular characteristic. 'Chuck is rather muscular.'

name: Individual
definition_en: This FE identifies the individual (or individuals) being described. 'Chuck is muscular.' 'Chuck has a muscular body.'

name: Figure
definition_en: This FE identifies the Figure or form being described by the target. 'Chuck has a muscular body.'

name: Individual
definition_en: This FE identifies the Individual (or individuals) being described.  'Chuck is a redhead.'</def-root >

name: Figure
definition_en: This FE identifies the Figure or form being described by the target. 'The red-haired figure stood in the doorway.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the body description applies.  'Mort is extremely flat-footed.'

name: Attachment
definition_en: The Attachment is the larger body part to which the Body_mark is attached, or of which it is a part. 'Mark has a cancerous mole on his back.' 'The warts of her left hand shocked everyone.'

name: Body_mark
definition_en: This FE identifies  the Body_mark.  'Mark has a cancerous mole on his back.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This Frame Element is used for a characteristic or description of the Body_mark. it identifies a modifier of its head noun.   'Mark has a cancerous mole on his back.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: This Frame Element denotes the Possessor of the Body_mark.  'Mark has a cancerous mole on his back.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is the event that brings about the presence of the Body_mark.

name: Type
definition_en: A specific kind of the particular Body_mark.  'Well, looks like you got a plantar wart on your palm there.'

name: Constituents
definition_en: Salient constituents that make up the Body_mark.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent uses some part of his/her body to perform the action. Agent occurs as the External Argument. 'The boy swung his legs.'

name: Body_part
definition_en: With some verbs in this frame, the Body_part involved in the action is specified by the meaning of the verb and cannot be expressed separately.  For example,  'Pat yawned (*his mouth).'  With others, the Body_part is specified by the verb but can optionally be expressed separately, although its presence is generally redundant, as in 'Pat nodded (his head).'  A few verbs have a default Body_part which need not be expressed, but can be overridden by the expression of some other Body_part. 'Pat waved (his arms).' (The objectless version of the sentence, Pat waved, is a blend with communication.) The remainder of the verbs require a Body_part to be expressed in a separate constituent:  'Pat rolled his eyes.' Body_part generally occurs as the direct object.

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: Body movement may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state. Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement. 'Kim  bent her head in concentration.' 'Kim threw her hands up in despair.'

name: External_cause
definition_en: Cause is something in the external environment that causes the Agent to move part of his/her body.  Cause is usually expressed in a PP Complement:. 'Pat jerked her head at the sudden noise.' 'Kim's nose wrinkled at the smell.' '' Cause does not include any physical force moving the Agent's Body_part.  This type of situation is described by the frame Motion.Cause-to-move.

name: Addressee
definition_en: Addressee only occurs in the Body-movement frame in sentences which are blends with Communication.  Where it occurs, it is typically a PP Complement:  'Pat fluttered his eyelashes at me.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source is the place from which the Body_part is moved. 'The boy swung his legs from under the table.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path identifies the trajectory of motion of the Body_part without specifying a start or end point. 'Pat flung his arms up. '

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is any expression that identifies the endpoint of movement.   'Pat dropped her hands to her lap.'

name: Area
definition_en: Area identifies any expression describing a region in which the motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path.  (This FE should be contrasted with Place.)  'Pat waved her arms about her head.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the event occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the body movement occurs.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

name: Message
definition_en: This FE identifies the Message that the body movement conveys.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the body movement occurs.

name: Subregion
definition_en: This FE specifies the subregion of the body that is involved with movement. 'He bent his legs at his knees'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose of the body movement. 'He winked his eye to give her a hint'

name: Cognate_event
definition_en: This FE identifies the event noun of the verb. 'He clapped his loudest clap'

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time during which the movement of a Body_part occurs.  'It seemed like we were clapping our hands for hours.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location within which the movement of a Body_part takes place.  'There was singing for joy in the streets, and everywhere people lifting their arms into the air. '

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: An alternative description of the Body_movement.  'In a bid to reenter the conversation , he kept waving his hand towards the rest of them.'

name: Coordinated_event
definition_en: An event that the Agent perceives and responds to by moving in coordination with it.  'They bobbed their heads to the beat.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: This Frame Element denotes the Possessor of the Body_part.  'Kim's arm is broken.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This Frame Element is used for a characteristic or description of the Body_part. Note that Descriptor is not an FE of the same character as other FEs.  Specifically, rather than filling a slot, it identifies a modifier of its head noun.   'Kim has beautiful eyes.' 'His trembling hands....'

name: Body_part
definition_en: This Frame Element  is the Body_part. 'Kim's arm is broken.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: This FEidentifies  the Subregion of the Body_part referred to by the target.  'upper arm' 'lower back'

name: Orientational_location
definition_en: This Frame Element describes the location of the Body_part with respect to the inherent orientation of the body (or the larger body part) the Body_part is attached to.  'left leg' 'hind foot' 'second finger' 'front wings'  NB:  All of these (other than very productive types such as "left", "right", "front", "back", and "second") should be tagged as secondary targets.

name: Attachment
definition_en: The Attachment is the larger body part  to which the BP is attached. 'the fingers of her left hand' 'the fin on its back' 'the dorsal fin'

name: Financial_instrument
definition_en: The bond, insurance, or debt security which a Holder buys from an Issuer.  'West Shore Railroad bonds never mature.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the Financial_instrument reaches maturity.  'Treasury bonds mature after 30 years.'

name: Issuer
definition_en: The entity which is obligated to pay the Holder after the Financial_instrument matures.

name: Holder
definition_en: The entity which owns the Financial_instrument and is owed money from the Issuer.

name: Value
definition_en: What the Financial_instrument is worth after maturity.  'The bond maturedto the full amount in 2009.'

name: Principle
definition_en: The amount that the Holder originally paid to own the Financial_instrument.

name: Interest
definition_en: The growth rate on the Principle that results in the final Value of the Financial_instrument.

name: Borrower
definition_en: The person who receives the Theme from the Lender for a Duration.  'Tracy borrowed that book from Leonard last week.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the Borrower has possession of the Theme.

name: Lender
definition_en: The person or institution who gives the Theme to the Borrower for a Duration. 'Tracy borrowed that book from Leonard last week.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The object that the Borrower receives from the Lender for a Duration.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The aim of the Borrower which they believe will be accomplished by possessing the Theme.

name: Time
definition_en: When the borrowing even occurs.

name: Means_of_transfer
definition_en: The means by which the transfer of the Theme took place.  'I borrowed money from my dad via Western Union.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Borrower gets the Theme from the Lender.  'I am borrowing his car at the airport.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Borrower gains possession of the Theme from the Lender.  'I hastily borrowed the keys from his belt.'

name: Boundary
definition_en: The region which is between the Entities or between the Entity and empty space.

name: Entity
definition_en: The entity that has a Boundary.

name: Entities
definition_en: The joint construal of both Entities next to the Boundary.

name: Relative_location
definition_en: The relative location of the boundary in respect to the Entity or Entities.

name: Bounded_area
definition_en: This FE identifies a stable Bounded_area.  It typically serves as the denotation of nouns.

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: This FE identifies the salient Constituent_parts that make up a bounded area.

name: Relative_location
definition_en: Relative_location identifies the place in respect to which a bounded area is located.

name: Name
definition_en: This FE is used for the Name of a bounded area.

name: Owner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Owner, generally a person, of the bounded area.</def-root >

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: This FE identifies the Formational_cause (action or agent) that brings about the features of the bounded area.

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of which kind of Bounded_area the entity is.

name: Interior
definition_en: A region of space located inside a Ground.

name: Ground
definition_en: An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Interior, Surface, Boundary, or Exterior regions.

name: Surface
definition_en: The region located outside of, but in contact with, the Ground.

name: Boundary
definition_en: The region associated with the boundary of the Ground.

name: Exterior
definition_en: The region which is not located inside or in contact with the Ground.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the person who produces a message about a Topic.  'During the 1990s Rio Grande Do Sul's governor, Olivio Dutra of the PT, PREENED about the province's GE-free status.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the person to whom the Speaker communicated a message.   'Sheppard said Turner apparently was backing up his boast to a bystander when a patrol officer saw him writing on the sign and arrested him.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is a positively judged entity or state of affairs with which the Speaker is associated and about which they talk.   'Mike Wallace was told that Canseco had bragged about steroids.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).   'She insulted everyone she spoke to, and boasted loudly about a salary that no one else in the office could ever hope to make.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Speaker makes a boastful statement.  'He bragged about himself by saying: 'I understand the language of the birds.''

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement.  'CNN's Jeff Greenfield bragged on the air recently that ratings are high. '

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Speaker during the statement.  'His drunken boast, however, cost him his life.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the statement is made.  'The public does not care, but the media definitely do as Haddock herself boasted the next morning on Good Morning America.'

name: Place
definition_en: The FE specifies the place where the statement takes place.  ''I'm Pat Crowe,' he boasted at the police station.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A characteristic of the entity or state of affairs denoted by the Topic which explains why the Speaker is proud of the association with the Topic referent.  'He's not a particularly great one, but he's vaunted by the Democrats as the greatest threat to their party, so who are we to argue?'

name: Message
definition_en: A description of the state of affairs that redounds to the Speaker's credit  'Cosmai BRAGGED that Hyundai's latest quality rankings place the automaker on par with Honda and Toyota.'

name: Role
definition_en: Role is used for the capacity in which the Topic entity or state of affairs is judged, and is expressed in as-PPs.  'Ricky constantly bragged about his father as a musician but he never had much to say about him as a parent.'

name: Expressor
definition_en: Expressor is the body part or action that conveys the feeling of pride of the Speaker.  'The senator's boastful exaggerations of her academic record at a New Hampshire campaign event also contributed to her withdrawal.'

name: Occasion
definition_en: The Occasion is the reason a public statement is given.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular Statement event referred to is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to their speaking.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs.

name: Whole
definition_en: The Whole goes into Pieces which were not (necessarily) definable subparts prior to breaking.

name: Pieces
definition_en: The Pieces result from the breaking apart of the Whole.

name: Criterion
definition_en: This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event or participants not covered by more specific Frame Elements.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the breaking apart takes place.w

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the breaking apart takes place.

name: Means
definition_en: An action, event, or state that enables the event of breaking apart.  'The crew donned immersion suits and abandoned ship into a life raft as their vessel broke apart by wave action. '

name: Subpart
definition_en: The part of the Whole that is conceived as being broken or taken off from the remaining part of the whole.  'The handle broke off of the pot.'

name: Whole
definition_en: The piece that is presented in a less prominent position, and which is the landmark or remaining whole from which Sub_part breaks off. 'The handle broke off of the pot.'

name: Criterion
definition_en: This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the breaking off of the Sub_part happens.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the breaking off occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event or participants not covered by more specific Frame Elements.

name: Means
definition_en: An action, event, or state that enables the event of breaking off.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the individual who ends the confinement or captivity of the Theme.  'The police freed the suspect.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the person or object in motion released by the Agent.  'The police freed the suspect.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the release which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'The police freed the suspect carefully.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Agent which brings about the release.  'He set the entire convoy of prisoners free by bribing the guards.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation identifies the reason for which the Agent releases the Theme.  'The police set the suspect free  because he had a good alibi.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose identifies the purpose for which the Agent release the Theme.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Theme ceases to be confined.  '"Aren't you going to free us here?" she asked.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time identifies when the Agent release the Theme .

name: Location_of_confinement
definition_en: The location to which the Theme's motion was formerly inhibited.  'Rebels set three prisoners free from holding cells.'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world when the Releasing event occurs.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent's breathing causes the motion of the Air.  Agent is generally the External Argument. 'Lee breathed the hot desert air.'

name: Air
definition_en: Air is the substance that the Agent causes to move. 'Lee breathed the hot desert air.'

name: Goal
definition_en: This FE identifies the point at which the Air ends up as a result of the motion. 'Lee breathed into Ann's mouth.' </def-root >

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent breathes. 'Lee breathed deeply.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means of breathing. 'Lee breathes  with a respirator.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source identifies the starting point of the Air.  'Lee exhaled from the bottom of his lungs.'

name: Path
definition_en: This FE identifies the Path of the motion through locations after leaving the Source and before reaching the Goal.  'Lee breathed through his mouth.'</def-root >

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the degree to which an Agent is breathing.  'Lee was breathing too hard.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies a  phrase describing a participant in a breathing event. 'Lee was breathing calmly, naked on the floor.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the breathing occurs. 'Lee breathed with difficulty on the track.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE idenitfies the Duration of time that an Agent breathes. 'Lee breathed deeply for thirty seconds.'

name: Distance
definition_en: The distance that the Air travels.  'He exhaled the poison gas from the tooth a full three feet.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity that allows the Agent to breathe, either a natural part (the lungs, say) or a device (like a respirator).  'He has to breathe with an oxygen mask.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which breathing occurs.  'All I know is that he was still breathing at 2AM.'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: This FE designates internal events/states that cause the Agent to exhibit the specified type of breathing. Further, the internal state of the Agent is perceivable to others because of the breathing event.   'He gasped in horror .'

name: External_cause
definition_en: This FE denotes an event or state external to the Agent that causes them exhibit the specified manner of breathing but not as a conscious response to the External_cause.  'Isabel gasped at the strength of his grip.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances are expressions indicating prevailing physical conditions or states of affairs concurrent  to the breathing event.  'They respire at lower levels of light, temperature, and tissue moisture than bryophytes.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by breathing in the specified manner.  'Blanche respired steadily to allow the tension to subside.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is a sentient being who physically controls the movement of the Theme via the carrier, accompanying the Theme. 'Karl carried the books across the campus to the library.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal identifies the endpoint of the path.    'Karl carried the books to the library.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source indicates the beginning of the path along which the Theme travels.    'Karl hauled the books from the library  to the office.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path along which carrying occurs. 'Karl carried the books across the campus.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The objects being carried. 'Karl toted the books to the car.'

name: Constant_location
definition_en: The Constant_location expresses the location of the Theme relative to the Carrier.  This relationship holds for the entire length of the carrying event.  'Karl took the books to the library in his car.' 'Karl carried the books to the library in his arms.'

name: Area
definition_en: Area is used for descriprion of a general area in which the carrying action takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies a phrase describing the Carrier, Agent or Theme.

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE identifies the Distance the Theme is carried.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner  in which the Carrier or Agent carries the Theme .

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the carrying or transporting occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Carrier or Agent carries the Theme . 'We had to carry the heavy weights all the way to the top of the hillto show our strength.'

name: Carrier
definition_en: The Carrier provides support for the Theme.  Movement of the Carrier results in movement of the Theme. 'The boat ferried the troops across the river.'

name: Means
definition_en: The actions the Agent takes to move the Theme. 'The books were taken to the library by helicopter deliveries.' 'I haul books by putting them on top of my head.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the general area that serves as a setting for the specific motion of the Agent and Theme (with Source, Path, or Goal).   'Even in such a small port, these boats would transport many tons of trade-goods in to shore annually.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time in which the carrying event takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: This FE describes the particpant for whom the bringing is beneficial.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is used to indicate the location of a participant in cases where the multiple participants of an event are not co-located in the typical fashion.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist, regardless of whether the protagonist, and hence the Co-participant, is more agent- or more undergoer-like.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE is minimally distinct from Duration and Duration_of final_state in that the clause described is conveyed to be iterative.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent builds a Created_entity. 'Jack built a new house.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument(s) with which an Agent builds a Created_entity. 'Jack built a new house with hammer and nails.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the building occurs.  'Jack built a new house in a glade.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an intentional act is performed. 'Jack built a new house  to have more living space.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the building occurs.  'Jack built a new house early in the morning.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent builds a Created_entity. 'Jack built a new house by enlisting the help of his friends.'

name: Components
definition_en: This FE identifies the Components that form the Created_entity. 'Jack built  a new house out of old bricks.'

name: Created_entity
definition_en: Created_entity identifies the entity that is created in the act of building. 'Jack built a new house.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the act of building. 'We glued the airplanes together.'</def-root >

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifes the phrase describing the participant in the act of building. 'Jack built the new house naked.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE idenitifies the Manner in which an Agent builds a Created_entity.  'Jack built a new house lovingly.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: This extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Created_entity.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Building_part
definition_en: The place or area specified inside a structure.  The Building_part of the Whole. 'She works in the cancer ward of the local hospital.'

name: Whole
definition_en: The entirety of a building whose Building_part is discussed. 'I live on the sixth floor of the building.'

name: Use
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Building_part was constructed.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE designates the kind or Type of Building_part. 'She works in the cancer ward of the local hospital.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE describes where the Building_part is located. 'The laundry room is located on the lower level of this building.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of some property of the Building_part. 'The enormous room was filled with light from a number of large windows that overlooked the bay.'

name: Creator
definition_en: The Individual that created the Building.

name: Building
definition_en: The entity built by the Builder which has some Function.

name: Function
definition_en: The use for which the Building is intended.

name: Name
definition_en: The Name used to refer to the Building.

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Building, including components, ingredients, etc

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which the Building comes into existence.

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Building, including architectural style.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of some property of the Building.

name: Place
definition_en: The building's location.

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Building is located with respect to.

name: Possessor
definition_en: The person or other legal entity that owns or has possession of the Building.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which a bungling event occurs.  'Mickey really botched that swing.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifes a  phrase describing a particpant in an action.  'Mickey botched that swing without his cap.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Agent bungles.  'Mickey botched that swing deliberately.'</def-root >

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent bungles.  'Mickey botched that swing by leaning forward.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent performs an action incorrectly. 'Mickey botched that swing.'

name: Patient
definition_en: Patient is the entity affected by the Agent's bungling of an Action. 'Mickey fumbled the ball.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the bungling occurs.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent bungles.  'Mickey botched that swing with a heavy bat.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the bungling occurs.

name: Action
definition_en: This FE identifies the Action that the Agent performs incorrectly. 'Mickey botched that swing.'

name: Area
definition_en: The type of action that the Agent habitually bungles. 'The Austro-Hungarian Empire had a long history of military screw-ups.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent intentionally buries the Theme.  'The pirate placed the treasure on the island.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the object that is buried.  'The pirate buried the gold under the tree.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the initial location of the Theme, before it is buried.  'Her mother buried the seedlings from the smaller pot.'

name: Path
definition_en: Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path.  'The roots should be buried through the provided grate in order to provide support as the plant grows.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The FE Goal is the location where the Theme ends up.  'The suspect buried the gun in the ground.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of the placing action which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Theme's motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.  'The suspect buried the gun hastily behind the fence.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree indicates the degree to which the burying occurs.  'Make sure you completely bury it, otherwise it will be found eventually.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Theme.  'I buried the money uncounted.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is an act whereby the Agent achieves the burying of the Theme.  'I finally buried it by slowly pushing it into the top layer of soil.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the burying.  'The cables are buried invisibly under the soil.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration is the amount of time for which the Theme stays in the Goal location.  'If you bury it there for extended periods, it may begin to degrade.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place indicates where the burying occurs.  'It must have been buried south of this location, according to the map.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation that the Theme is buried.  'She buried the book because she feared others would read it.'

name: Time
definition_en: Time is when the burying occurs  'Smithers had buried the treasure there the night before.'

name: Area
definition_en: The Area is the general area where the Theme is buried.  'They probably buried them around the property.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: The Cotheme is buried along with the Theme  'The treasure was buried along with a parchment describing where it came from. '

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE is any expression which characterizes the extent of motion of the theme into the ground.  'I buried the seedseveral feet deep.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which buring occurs.  'Smithers buried the bone quickly and went to look for his dog.'

name: Cause
definition_en: A non-animate force which buries the Theme.  'The tornado buried most of the structures in this area.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the burying action.  'They buried the vase in the ground to protect it from looters.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The Beneficiary derives a benefit from the occurrence of the burying event.  'Bury the gold for me and when we dig it up, you can have half.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity is rendered unable to continue its regular operations.  'The local McDonalds shut down in 2008 because the owner passed away and no one would set up to the plate.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is named as one of the causes of failure.  'The local McDonalds shut down in 2008 because the owner died.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time of the failure.  'The local McDonalds shut down in 2008  because the owner died.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place of the failing entity.  'Every Ikea shut down in Ohio last week.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances that caused failure. Compared to Explanation, this describes situations or environments that lead to failure, not a specific reason for failure.  'Shops often close down amid political or economic turmoil.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes the way in which the Entity failed.  'When the housing bubble burst, his real estate chain abruptly closed down.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: The Containing_event is an event within which the failure occurs.  'Businesses in the Congo failed during their civil war.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A Depictive describes something about the Entity.  'The business, unable to maintain appeal in the E.U., closed its doors in 2003.'

name: Product
definition_en: Product identifies the product or service provided by the business.   'Josh runs a copier toner business.'

name: Proprietor
definition_en: Proprietor is the owner or chief participant in the business.  'I worked in Goldberg's legal practice .' 'I didn't want to go into the family business.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Descriptor indicates other characteristics of the business besides its Product and Proprietor. 'Chris runs a small company in Idaho.' 'I work for a non-profit arts company.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place in which the business is located. 'Chris's business in Idaho is thriving.' 'Local companies are looking for more and more Spanish-speaking employees.'

name: Business
definition_en: Business identifies the company or establishment. This may be the target itself or the Business_Name if it is an appositive not set off with commas (i.e. restrictive): 'The electronics firm went bankrupt.' In the appositive case, the name may also be tagged Business_Name on a second annotation layer. '1st Layer: The Japanese electronics firm Sony is growing rapidly.' '2nd Layer: The Japanese electronics firm Sony is growing rapidly.'

name: Business_name
definition_en: The name of the Business when it appears in an appositive set off by commas (non-restrictive): 'My clothing company, Togs, is doing well.'

name: Service_provider
definition_en: When a Business is described in terms of the professionals who work to produce the product or service, use Service_provider. ' John works as an office assistant for a firm of accountants.'

name: Cache
definition_en: This FE denotes the Cache of Resources.  'She concealed her cache of sweets under her sweater.'

name: Resource
definition_en: The goods or commodity that is being stored in a Cache.  'This is by far the largest cache of Roman coins to be uncovered in Britain since the eighteenth century.'

name: Use
definition_en: The future Use for the Resource.  'Police discover arms cache for school attack.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: The entity that possesses the Cache.  'Eventually our stash ran out and we had to get more.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Cache itself, rather than the Resource.  'Police are questioning at least three people after discovering a huge cache of semtex in a tea chest in East London.'

name: Relative_time
definition_en: Relative_time is used for the word or words that locate the time with respect to an identifiable reference point.  'Jo's mother will visit  this coming Tuesday.'

name: Name
definition_en: Name is used for the name of a day (month, etc.).   Note that only the word (or words) that is the name is (are) tagged, not the target word.  'Labor Day is just around the corner.' 'January is Black History Month.'

name: Whole
definition_en: Whole is used for the larger unit of which the target word names a part.  'Jo fled in the early morning of  Sunday December 15.'

name: Count
definition_en: The number of intervals of the specified type.  'These last two weeks,  I just keep getting myself into trouble .'

name: Unit
definition_en: The calendric unit that is denoted. LUs in this frame all denote the Unit.

name: Salient_event
definition_en: An event saliently associated with a particular calendric unit.  'Today was my school's cut day.'  'Republicans have indicated they plan to make Kerry's positions an election year issue.'

name: Landmark_period
definition_en: The time-expression that is used to establish when the Trajector_event occurred.  This FE, when present, always occurs on the second layer.  'Turn in your expense reports next April .'  This FE is not to be used when the relationship between a time expression and an event is overtly expressed by a target of the Temporal_collocation frame, as in the following, which differs from the preceding sentence only in the use of by:  'Turn in your expense reports by next April .'

name: Trajector_event
definition_en: An event that is located by the Calendric_unit expression.  'Last November , they selected a new president .'  This FE is not to be used when a target of the Temporal_collocation frame explicitly introduces the temporal relationship between the Landmark_period and the Trajector_event, as in the following, which differs from the above only in the additional word over:  'Over last November , they selected a new president .'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker produces the Message, the truth or sincerity of which is at issue. It is normally expressed as the External Argument of predicative uses of the target word, or as the Nominal Head of prenominal uses. 'Evelyn was candid about the party. ''Evelyn is a candid person.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the person to whom the Message is communicated. This FE often remains unexpressed. When expressed, it normally takes the form of a PP Complement headed by with. 'Evelyn was candid with me about the party.'

name: Message
definition_en: Message is the communicative content whose truth or sincerity is at issue. This FE does not normally co-occur with the other FEs in this frame. When it does occur, it is normally the External Argument of a predicative use of the Target word, or the modified Nominal Head in a prenominal use. 'Evelyn made some candid remarks. ''Evelyn's remarks were candid.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It often occurs without the Message FE in predicative uses of the target word. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by "about". 'Evelyn was candid about the party.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed. 'Evelyn made some candid remarks in French.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which a communication is candid--some are more candid than others.  'Evelyn's remarks were very candid.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE indicates the manner of candidness. '"He was a fool," John pointed out with ruthless candour.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity whose meeting or falling short of pre-conditions is assessed.  'Little Tommy ca n't read'

name: Event
definition_en: The Event that the Entity may participate in.  'White House voices doubts about Aristide's ability to govern'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for participating in the Event.  'Blind parents are very capable of raising children'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions.  'In this weather, an experienced pilot can still manage to fly 500 miles.'  'The new car has a cruising capacity in excess of 150 kph.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to be meet or fail to meet the pre-conditions for participating in an Event.   'They were not able to go outside because of the rain.'

name: Relevant_feature
definition_en: The characteristic or behavior of the Entity that is considered when judging whether the Entity might participate in the Event.  'These computers have the processing capacity to compute the precise date of the end of the world.'

name: Status
definition_en: The status of the capability.  'This machine has many new capabilities.'  'He has an innate potential.'

name: Role
definition_en: The particular role that the Entity plays in the Event.  'His ability as a leader to get things done is unparalleled.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Entity is capable of the Event.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE expresses how often the Entity is able to do the Event.  'Hong Kong's stores are usually able to arrange shipment.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity whose ability to contain items is assessed.   'Our facility seats up to 500 people.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Entity exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for holding the items.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the Entity meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions for containing.

name: Explanation
definition_en: An entity, event, or state that causes the Entity to be able or unable to hold the items.

name: Status
definition_en: The status of the capability (e.g., innately, with modifications).

name: Theme
definition_en: The Entity has the ability to contain the Theme, often expressed with a quantity.  'Our facility seats up to 500 people.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of one of the participants, typically the Theme but possibly the Entity.  'Our facilities seat 500 people seated.'</def-root >

name: Subregion
definition_en: This FE denotes a sub-part of the Entity which has a particular capacity. 'The two small cars seated only 32 inside.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose of the Entity's specified capacity. 'It seats approximately 180 persons for full silver service.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Entity has or had a certain capacity.

name: Stock
definition_en: The investment that a Shareholder makes into a business, differing from property and assets.

name: Type
definition_en: The the kind of Stock, of which there are two: preferred or common.  Holders of preferred stock are entitled to the first dividend that a company pays out, while holders of common stock are granted voting rights in corporate decisions.

name: Shareholder
definition_en: The creditor that has invested into a business by purchasing some Type of its Stock.

name: Issuer
definition_en: The entity that issues its Stock to the Shareholder.

name: Amount
definition_en: The Amount is the number of shares, though any measure prase will suffice.  'I have ten shares in Google.' 'Berkshire Hathaway bought majority shares in IBM today.'

name: Number
definition_en: This FE identifies the Number. 'JP has almost one million dollars.'

name: Entity
definition_en: This FE identifies the Entity enumerated by the Number. 'JP has almost one million dollars.'  In many cases, the Target is used to multiply another number.  In this case, the second number is labeled as "Unit":

name: Precision
definition_en: This FE identifies the Precision to which an Entity approximates a Number. 'About thirty cases are known.' In the case where a number is modified by a Multiplier, we have found it more plausible that phrases expressing Precision modify the main number (thus "million" in the first example, not "two"): 'JP has almost two million dollars.' 'There are just over six billion people in the world today.'

name: Multiplier
definition_en: How many times larger the group of Entitys is than the base Number. 'Four score and seven years ago, our forefathers set forth blah blah blah.'

name: Composite_number
definition_en: The total number of instances of the Entity.  This FE should be used when more basic number expressions are used together to form a Composite_number whose value is the sum of the constituent numbers. It is annotated on a second FE layer. For cases where a number is used to multiply another number, use Multiplier.  'She found six hundred and twelve errors in the manuscript.' 'Four score and seven years ago , I wasn't even born.' 'Thirty seven senators refused to vote.'

name: Unit
definition_en: A Unit expresses some quantification of some property of an entity, event, or situation by providing a base value of the property combined with a Number expressing how the current value for the property relates to the Unit.    'She's not even six years old yet!'  As units that specify a quantity property, numbers themselves can be used as Units.  'Three dozen eggs makes eighteen standard omelettes .'

name: Distributor
definition_en: The Distributor maintains a store of Goods for the purpose of selling or otherwise distributing them.

name: Goods
definition_en: The Goods are kept on hand and distributed by the Distributor.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Distributor carries the Goods.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place indicates where the carrying of Goods occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the storing of goods which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of a Distributor that also affect the action (deliberately, carefully).

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE indicates the length of time that the Distributor carries the Goods.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Undesirable_event
definition_en: The undesirable event which occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the Undesirable_Event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Undesirable_Event occurs.

name: Patient
definition_en: The entity that experiences the Undesirable_Event.  'An environmental disaster is just what we need.' 'Should hair loss befall you...'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE indicates the Circumstances under which a warning applies. (Proper only to betide.)

name: Cause
definition_en: The cause of the Undesirable_Event.  'Most counties are prepared for some level of natural disaster.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Fire begins to burn.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Fire begins to burn.

name: Fire
definition_en: The total material currently involved in combustion, including both the parts of the Fuel currently undergoing chemical alteration and the partially ionized gas that results from this process.

name: Fuel
definition_en: The entity that is begins to undergo rapid chemical alteration leading to damage or destruction.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Fire event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Explanation
definition_en: A description of why the event happened.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: This is the person who performs an act of categorization. Typically, this frame element is expressed as an External Argument.  'Kim categorized the books under fiction. Kim categorized them on the basis of genre.'

name: Item
definition_en: This is the entity which is construed or treated by the Cognizer as being an instance of a particular Category. Typically, the Item is expressed as an Object.   'Kim categorized the books under fiction.'

name: Category
definition_en: This frame element expresses a general type or class of which the Item is considered an instance. Typically, it is expressed in a prepositional phrase headed by as or under.  'Kim categorized the book as/under fiction.'

name: Criteria
definition_en: This frame element expresses properties of the Item which is used as a basis for categorization. Criteria are the general dimensions along which Items can potentially differ from one another and hence, fall into different Categorys. For example, a paint sample can be classified by color or by finish (matte or gloss); if they are classified by color, one can be classified as orange and another as red. The Criteria FE is typically expressed as a PP headed by by, or as a complex PP of the form on the basis of...:  'The students were categorized on the basis of their test scores.' 'The librarian classified the books by subject.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Cognizer categorizes.

name: Time
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate when a certain Categorization was made.  ' 20 years ago people would consider this as nothing unusual'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the categorization holds. 'Material posessions are defined as valuable in a particular society.'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Cognizer categorizes the Item in the given way.

name: Cause
definition_en: A force, process, or event that produces an effect.  'The wind made the door rattle.' 'The accident caused them to be more careful the next time.'

name: Affected
definition_en: Agents in a joint or reciprocal action (e.g. exchange)

name: Effect
definition_en: A positive or negative evaluation of the Phenomenon.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

name: Actor
