definition_en: An entity which participates in a Cause, perhaps volitionally and perhaps not.  'That one stone, apparently, caused the avalanche that engulfed square miles of forest.' 'Stephen Hawking caused an uproar when the results were published.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any holistic description of the event, including overall depictions (the same way) and descriptions pertaining to the Actor's influence on the character of the event (eagerly, quietly).

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Means
definition_en: An action through which the Actor or Cause accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the action denoted by the target occurs.

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.  'John made me give up smoking.' 'The wind made the door rattle.' 'The accident caused them to be more careful the next time.'

name: Effect
definition_en: The Effect is the event which results from the Cause. 'The eruption led to the extinction of thirty separate species.'

name: Averted_situation
definition_en: The situation that would be the case if the Cause event did not occur or the Cause state were not the case.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Cause occurs and Effect takes place or the Averted_situation does not occur as expected.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which at which the Cause occurs and Effect takes place or the Averted_situation does not occur as expected.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person causing a bodily experience in the Experiencer.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the being or entity whose experience changes.    'Do n't tickle me !'  If the Experiencer is included in the phrase indicating Body_part, the Experiencer FE is tagged on a second FE layer.  'Jolosa scratched her back .'

name: Result
definition_en: Result identifies the result of the Agent's action.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree is the degree to which the Experiencer's bodily experience is affected.  'The wool itched too much to wear it all the time .'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

name: Place
definition_en: Place identifies the place where the bodily experience is caused.

name: Time
definition_en: Time identifies the time when the experience-causing event occurs.

name: Body_part
definition_en: >The Body_part identifies the location on the Experiencer's body where the bodily experience takes place.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE is any object manipulated by the Agent to cause the experience.  'Rub the sore muscles down with the oil provided .'

name: Purpose
definition_en: Purpose identifies the state-of-affairs that an Agent hopes to bring about by causing an experience in the Experiencer.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies any Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action or the affected entity.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE identifies the event within which the bodily experience is caused.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A fact or action somehow related to the Experiencer that the Agent responds to by causing an experience in the Experiencer.

name: Iterations
definition_en: Iterations refers to the number of times the Agent or Cause causes an experience.

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that affects the Experiencer's Body_part.  'The coat chafed a bit .'

name: Subregion_bodypart
definition_en: The Subregion_bodypart defines the precise location on the Body_part in which the experience occurs.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the causal event and any of its participants.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Cause_bodily_experience event occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Cause_bodily_experience event to its end.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: This FE indicates that the Cause_bodily_experience event is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.  'Her sweater was itching her again .'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the Cause_bodily_experience event) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: A description presenting a separate aspect of the experience-causing event.  'In a serious breach of decorum , he rubbed Merkel 's shoulders .'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the Cause_bodily_experience event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Agent
definition_en: The sentient entity that effects a change in the Entity.  'The system administrator changed the value from 'KDE' to 'GNOME', and then restarted the system.'

name: Initial_category
definition_en: The category of which the Entity is a member before the Agent causes a change.  'Her time with the Healer Craft has changed her from a shy, nervous young girl into a confident (almost) young woman'

name: Final_category
definition_en: The category that the Entity belongs to after it has undergone the change.  'The radical message of the cross transformed Saul of Tarsus and changed him from a persecutor of Christians to a tender believer.'

name: Final_value
definition_en: The value that the Attribute assumes as a result of the change that the Entity is caused to undergo.  'We changed the size from 8 1/2x11 to a larger 11 x 17 and gave it a complete graphical makeover. '

name: Initial_value
definition_en: The value that the Attribute has before the change takes place.  'My dad changed his hair color from red  to blue today.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the change of the Entity is caused.  'He changed it after David Bowie told him that only twerps have the same first and last name.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the initial and final categories or values differ from each other.  'We significantly changed its appearance during this time. '

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the  event causing the change of the Entity which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Taking out his Driver's Ed pass certificate, Blair carefully changed the '6' of 1969 to an '8' making it read 23rd February 1989.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in bringing about the change in the Entity.   'I didn't change its name because I think it has already got used to it.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: A characteristic of the Entity for which a value can be assigned or determined by calculation, measurement , or observation.   'We changed the price from $1.26 to $1.27 per pint.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The abstract or concrete thing or situation that the Agent causes to change.  'The recent terrorist attacks had changed the political climate.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event that causes a change in the Entity.  'Major technological innovations changed the social and economic conditions.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by effecting a change in the Entity.  'His real name is Jerry Rivers, but he changed it in order to sound more ethnic and appealing'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent (or event resulting from the Cause) that produces a change in the Entity.   'Ling said he had transformed the car by putting slicks on.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the change of the Entity is caused.  'In his own room he had modified nothing.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Role
definition_en: The particular role that the Agent plays in the Cause_change event.

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

name: Manner

name: Speed

name: Subregion

name: Time

name: Patient

name: Agent

name: Container

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who causes an entity (Item) to change its positon on a scale with respect to some property (Variable).

name: Difference
definition_en: The distance between the orginial value (Value-1) and the final value (Value-2) of the entity on the scale (Variable).  'Coke raised the price of their soda by 2%.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The scale along which the Item ranges in value. 'They increased the price of oil.'

name: Value_1

name: Value_2

name: Co-variable

name: Path

name: Speed
definition_en: The rate at which the entity's positon on the scale changes.  'Ford slowly raised the price of their best-selling model.'

name: Item

name: Means

name: Event

name: Type

name: Medium

name: Place

name: Agent
definition_en: With some words in this frame, an Agent who causes the change in size of the Item may be present. The Agent typically occurs as the External Argument of a verb.  'Management expanded the company.'

name: Item
definition_en: The Item is frequently the External Argument of verbs or the NP Object if an Agent is expressed.  'The company expanded.' 'Management expanded the company.'

name: Initial_size
definition_en: Initial_size is rarely expressed without Result_size also being explicit.  Initial_size generally occurs in a PP-from Complement.  'The glacier shrank from 1km square to 400 square meters.'

name: Result_size

name: Size_change
definition_en: Size_change identifies the amount by which the size of an Item changes.  'A 2-3cm expansion in width is required.'

name: Dimension
definition_en: Change of size may be limited to or described in terms of a single Dimension.   'The image was enlarged in height.' 'The machinist narrowed the tube by 6 inches in diameter.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent brings about the expansion of the Item.

name: Manner

name: Co-variable
definition_en: The feature that the size of the Item is varied in step with.  'I narrowed the viewport with the increasing glare.'

name: Group

name: Rate

name: Instrument

name: Source

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is the location the Fluid ends up in as a result  of the motion  'Why did  you squirt juice onto my chair?'

name: Path
definition_en: The trajectory along which the Fluid moves, exclusive of the Source and Goal.

name: Area

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is the being or entity that is injured.  If the Victim is included in the phrase indicating Body_part, the Victim FE is tagged on a second FE layer (see 3rd example).  'Someone bashed him on the back of the head with a heavy smooth object.' 'The farmer tied him to the fence to stop him butting the sheep.' 'Jolosa, who broke a rival player 's jaw, was told to model his play on the England striker.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result identifies the result of the Agent's action.  'Riot police in Nairobi clubbed four women unconscious on March 3.' 'A battered wife who burned her brutal husband to death was freed from jail yesterday.' 'Claire McLaren, 16, was punched and kicked senseless by a thug.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree is the degree to which the Agent causes harm to the Victim.  'She wanted to slap him hard for his change of mood.' 'Fox spun around and slapped him, harder than necessary.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Agent acts upon the Victim.  'He violently slapped his assailant.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.   'Rachael injured her friend by closing the car door on his left hand.'

name: Place

name: Time
definition_en: Time identifies the time when the harm-causing event occurs.  'Riot police in Nairobi clubbed four women unconscious on March 3.'

name: Body_part

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE is any object used to cause the injury.  'Someone bashed him on the back of the head with a heavy smooth object.' 'John butted her in the chest with his head.'

name: Purpose

name: Depictive

name: Containing_event

name: Cause

name: Subregion_bodypart

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Cause_harm event and any of its participants.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Cause_harm event occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Cause_harm event to its end.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: This FE indicates that the Cause_harm event is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the Cause_harm event) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: A description of the harm event which significantly displays a different aspect.  'Then she elbowed me -- a serious affront to my sensibilities !'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the Cause_harm event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Force
definition_en: The Force is the amount of force in the course of the impact.  'He smacked the bat hard against the wall.'

name: Impactee
definition_en: The Impactee is the entity which is hit by the Impactor.  'What I want to know is who smacked my head with a 10-ton truck?' 'He slammed the lid down on the top of the jar so hard that it broke.'

name: Impactor
definition_en: The Impactor is the entity that hits the Impactee because of the Agent's efforts.  'Those hoodlums strike my car with water balloons every day!' 'Well, then he just ran the car right into the wall.'

name: Impactors
definition_en: The Impactors are the multiple entities that collide.  'Mr. Addams likes to collide toy trains at high speed.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The FE Manner identifies the manner in which an Agent intentionally affects a Impactee.  'They ` hot-wired " a prison van and repeatedly rammed it into a security gate.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.  'Father Shanahan , of Rushey Mead , Leicester , rammed his Datsun into another car on the way to the city 's Gilroes cemetery.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the impact.  'I slammed the door shut.'

name: Speed
definition_en: This FE indicates the Speed of the Impactor (or Impactors at impact.  'The statue was rammed into the wall at 30 mph--a bit faster than John could have hurled it.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: Subregion identifies the part of the larger whole which was hit.  'The gunman grazed him on his left temple.' 'She struck him hard across the left cheek with the flat of her hand.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time  when the impact occurs.  'A postman rammed his Fiat Panda into a getaway car after spotting the burglars  .'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent  causes an impact.  'One juggler was hitting the ceiling with every other ball.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects an Impactee.

name: Means
definition_en: The FE Means identifies the means by which an Agent intentionally affects a Impactee.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The FE Purpose identifies the purpose for which an Agent intentionally affects the Impactee.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE identifies the  Period_of_iterations during which the Agent repeatedly causes impacts.

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional,  typically non-human, force that causes an Impactor to make sudden,  forcible contact with an Impactee.  'A violent explosionrattled the windows.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the one whose action causes the motion of a Theme.  The Agent is generally realized as the External Argument.  'Pat threw the china at the wall.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The FE Theme is generally an NP Object.  'Pat threw the china at the wall.'

name: Source
definition_en: The FE Source is the starting point of motion.  'Pat dragged the box out of the cupboard.'</def-root >

name: Path
definition_en: The FE Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal.  'I pushed the trolley along the street.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The FE Goal is the point at which the Theme ends up as a result of the motion.  'Kim threw the cat into the garden.'

name: Distance
definition_en: The FE Distance is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme.  'Pat threw the Javelin 50 meters.'

name: Area
definition_en: The FE Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element.  'Kim pushed the lawnmower around the garden.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of a participant during the action 'We pushed the cart around, gleeful.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Means
definition_en: The FE Means indicates the action that is taken that results in the motion of the Theme

name: Manner
definition_en: The FE Manner is any expression which describes a property of the motion of the Theme which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.

name: Subregion
definition_en: Subregion identifies the part of the Theme that makes contact with the resulting location. When Subregion is expressed, there usually is no Goal expressed.  'The horse pitched the rider on his head'

name: Cause
definition_en: Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that causes the Theme to be set in motion.  'The storm tossed the sailor from the boat'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity saliently involved in the transmission of force from an Agent to a Theme.  It may be the Agent's bodypart, or some kind of device.  'When passing a basketball, you should throw with bath hands.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the general area that provides a setting for a specific motion (with Source, Path, or Goal).

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the motion of the Theme occurs.  'We shoved half of the cargo overboard on the 29th.'

name: Result
definition_en: A resultant state that the Theme is in at the end of its motion.  'The fireman dragged the injured driver clear'

name: Handle
definition_en: The Agent's manipulation of the Theme may be further specified as being localized to some part of the Theme, a Handle. The Handle is usually expressed as a PP

name: Initial_state
definition_en: A previous state that the Theme was in before the beginning of its motion.  'Paul pulled Fran upright from her sitting position.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that the action requires.

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who causes the Set to increase in number.

name: Difference
definition_en: The distance between the orginal value (Initial_number) and the final value (Final_number) of the Set.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The scale along which the Set ranges in, i.e., number.

name: Initial_number
definition_en: The initial number of entities in the Set.

name: Final_number
definition_en: The final number of entities in the Set.

name: Co-variable
definition_en: The Co-Variable is the scale that the amount of the Set is measured against.

name: Path
definition_en: Any expression that says something about the movement of the entity (Set) along the scale between its Initial_number and its Final_number.

name: Speed
definition_en: The rate at which the entity's positon on the scale changes.

name: Set
definition_en: The entity whose amount is being changed.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Agent that brings about the change in the number of the Set.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the proliferating of the number of a Set is performed.

name: Time
definition_en: When the proliferating occurs.

name: Cause
definition_en: The force that causes the change.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Agent changing the number of the Set which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent changes the number of the Set.

name: Initial_state
definition_en: The state of the Set before it is affected by an outside Agent or Cause.

name: Final_state
definition_en: The state of the Set after it is affected by an outside Agent or Cause.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent performs the intentional act which changes the temperature of the Item.  'Ryan reheated the pasta in the microwave.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which  the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

name: Item
definition_en: The Item undergoes the temperature change.  'Ryan reheated the pasta in the microwave.'

name: Temperature_goal
definition_en: The Temperature_goal is the temperature to which the Agent is heating or cooling the Item.  'Heat the syrup to 180 degrees.'

name: Temperature_change
definition_en: The Temperature_change is the amount of difference between the intial and goal temperatures.

name: Temperature_start
definition_en: Temperature_start is the initial temperature of the Item.  'Heat the sugar water mixture from room temperature until it reaches 180 degrees.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which  the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where  the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which  the Agent changes the temperature of the Item and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when  the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.

name: Result
definition_en: Result is the resultant state of  the Agent changing the temperature of the Item.

name: Cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that changes the temperature. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.  'The sun warmed the house.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time for which the Agent changes the temperature of the Item.  'Refrigerate the cookie dough for an hour before baking.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.  'The mousse was chilled around the edges.'

name: Container
definition_en: This FE identifies the Container that holds the Item whose temperature is being changed.  'Heat the potatoes in a medium-sized pan.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Item.

name: Hot_Cold_source
definition_en: The Hot_Cold_source is the source of the heat or coolness.  'We chilled the drinks on ice.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the temperature change occurs.  'Bill cooled the jello at room temperature.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Item approaches (an implicit) Temperature_goal, which is often construed to be the ambient temperature.  'You'll probably have to wait a while to warm your legs up completely.'

name: Agent
definition_en: In causative uses of these verbs there is an Agent responsible for amalgamating the Parts. The Agent is generally the External Argument (or the object of a PP-by in passives).'The chef combined the ingredients.''The ingredients were combined by the chef.'

name: Whole
definition_en: This  FE identifies Whole as the entity resulting from combination of Parts.  When overtly expressed, it is usually a PP Complement (often headed by into).'Chuck merged the corpora into a database.' 'The directors merged the two companies into a conglomorate.'

name: Parts
definition_en: This FE identifies the Parts entities being combined, and is often expressed in a single plural NP, usually the direct object of a verb. 'Chuck merged the corpora into a database.''The directors merged the two companies into a conglomerate.'

name: Part_1
definition_en: This FE identifies the first of two Parts mentioned. It  is most often the NP-Object of a verb.  'The workmen joined the annex to the main building.'

name: Part_2
definition_en: This FE identifies the second of two Parts mentioned. It is usually a PP Complement.  'The workkmen joined the annex to the main building.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the amalgamating occurs.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the thoroughness of the mixing job, i.e. to what degree the resulting Whole is undifferentiated.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the amalgamating occurs.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE  is used for indicating the Result of amalgamating. 'Chuck merged the corpora together.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Parts during the amalgamation.  Often it refers to the proportion of the Parts to one another.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state of affairs that the Agent seeks to bring about by the Amalgamation.

name: Place
definition_en: The location that the event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the amalgamation occurs.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act causing the Dryee to become dry. ' Michael dehydrated the apples.' 'Abby dried out the room <fex name ="Instrument">with a dehumidifier.'

name: Dryee
definition_en: The Dryee is the entity which has the water removed from it. 'Michael dehydrated the apples.' 'Abby dried out the room with a dehumidifier.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.  'Abby dried out the room with a dehumidifier.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an the Agent dries the Dryee.</def-root >

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which Agent intentionally affects the Dryee and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent intentionally affects the Dryee.

name: Cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of dryness. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.  '<fex name ="Cause">The wind dried <fex name = "Dryee">the porch.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.  'The cloth was dried around the edges.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the length of Time that the drying takes.

name: Temperature
definition_en: This FE identifies the Temperature at which heat is applied to the Dryee.  'He dried the apples in the oven for a day at 350 degrees.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Dryee ends up dry.  'First, the remains should be completely desiccated before you begin the extraction.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is a volitional animate being who causes the New_member to become part of the Group.  'Matt seems to add new work to his flickr most days.'

name: Existing_member
definition_en: Something that is already a member of the Group and represents the Group as a whole.

name: New_member
definition_en: An item that becomes a part of the Group.

name: Group
definition_en: The Group is anything that can be conceptualized as a complex collection of parts or ingredients, including through metonymy like containers or locations, which New_members can join.  'The companyincludes philanthropic endeavors in their accomplishments'

name: Cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that is responsible for causing a New_member to enter a Group.  'The calls of crows added an eerie aspect to the atmosphere of our date.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the inclusion of a New_member.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies when the inclusion of the New_member to the Group occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner in which the Agent acts.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies what the Agent hopes to accomplish by including a New_member to a Group.  'Add a few pinches of pepper to the mixture to get the best flavor.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which a New_member is entered into a pre-existing Group.

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the sharpening (or dulling) action.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent causes the Patient to become more or less sharp. 'The smith sharpened many knives in the days before the war.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with an Patient, causing it to change in sharpness. 'Never sharpen your knives with my whetstone.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Agent sharpens the Patient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent sharpens the Patient. 'George sharpened the bayonet to please the sergeant.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent sharpens Patient.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is the entity that is sharpened. 'Several cuts into the log had dulled the blade.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner in which the Agent changes the sharpness of the Patient. 'He sharpened the knife silently.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The state of affairs that the Agent is responding to by executing the sharpening act.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Patient's sharpness is affected by the Agent.

name: Cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of sharpness.  Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes. 'The relentless impacts against the wood gradually blunted the edge of this axe.'

name: Result
definition_en: The resulting configuration of the Patient.  'Sharpen this knife to a nice point.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is a volitional animate being who causes the Patient to become wet.  'Hannah drenched the cat with anti-flea ointment.'

name: Liquid
definition_en: The Liquid is a fluid or gas that permeates or covers the Patient.  It most frequently occurs in a PP Complement headed by with.  'Jo soaked the dog with water.'

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient takes up the Liquid through its pores or has the Liquid covering its surface.  'Ellen wet  the sponge with water.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner or way in which the Agent wets the Patient.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an the Agent wets the Patient

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent wets the Patient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent wets the Patient and what the Agent hopes to accomplish.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent wets the Patient.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally wets the Patient.  'Colin doused the burning pot with a fire extinguisher.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces the state of wetness.  'The sprinklers drenched me.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the Agent wets the Patient.  'Ryan doused the fire with water until it stopped smoldering.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.  'The cloth was wetted around the edges.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE describes the reason for the state of the Cause_to_be_wet event.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that intends a fire to burn and brings it about.

name: Flammables
definition_en: The Flamables is the the object that burns as a result of the Cause, Agent, or Actor.

name: Cause
definition_en: The cause of the fire.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the event takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Kindler that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An event brought about by the Cause or the Kindler that actually makes the Flammables catch fire.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes the Kindler as being in some state during the action.

name: Actor
definition_en: The individual who, while actively performing an action, unintentionally causes the Flammables to burn.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual who causes the Process to continue or the State to be maintained.  'Smithers kept the food warm'

name: Process
definition_en: A Process that is maintained by the Agent or Cause.  'The soot in the air  kept it raining for weeks'

name: State
definition_en: The State that is maintained by the Agent or Cause.  'We need to keep China British.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time for which the Agent maintain the State or Process.   ' I responded quickly to the relaxed, calm atmosphere and found answers to questions that had kept me on edge for years.'

name: Means
definition_en: The event by which an Agent or Cause maintains the State or Process.  'The car did not break down, though it kept me on edge by making a funny noise all the way'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event that causes the Process or State to be maintained.   'The storm kept us in all the next day.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by maintaining the State or Process.  'On my Toshiba I had shrunk the Windows partition and kept it there for use via the dual boot.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Agent that maintain the State or Process.  'The third time I kept the engine going with the accelerator pedal'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Process continues.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Process continues.

name: Process
definition_en: A Process which is ended by the Agent or Cause.

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Agent that causes the Process or State to end.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Process or State is caused to end.   'They ended their relationship in the same coffeehouse where it started.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for why the Process or State is ended.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Process or State is ended.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Process or State is brought to an end.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of the event that causes the Process or State to end.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner of causing the Process or State to end.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual who causes the Process or State to end.

name: Cause
definition_en: An event that causes the Process or State to end.  'That move ended her political career, she said in a 1994 Times Union interview.'

name: State
definition_en: A State which is ended by the Agent or Cause.  'We should end poverty.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent intentionally tries to bring about an internal mental or emotional state.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is an External Argument of the target word and purposefully arouses an emotional state.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the person the Agent causes to have a particular emotional state.

name: Manner
definition_en: This Frame Element is for expressions that elaborate the manner in which the Agent affects the Experiencer.

name: Resulting_action
definition_en: What the Agent intends to make the Experiencer do by causing a certain experience and the Experiencer actually does.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent affects the Experiencer.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent affects the Experiencer </def-root >

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Agent brings about the emotional state.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent brings about the emotional state in the Experiencer.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the Experiencer ends up feeling an emotion.  'He completely terrorized her.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the Whole_patient being broken into Pieces. 'I and I alone can shatter the gem and break the curse.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with a Whole_patient to accomplish its fracture.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the fracturing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the breakage.

name: Whole_patient
definition_en: The entity which is destroyed by the Agent and that ends up broken into Pieces. 'Shattering someone's confidence is a little different than shattering a dish.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Agent breaks the Whole_patient into pieces.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent causes the break-up of the Whole_patient. 'The window cleaners shattered every other pane to protest their working conditions.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action. 'He tore the treaty up out of frustration.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent breaks up the Whole_patient.

name: Pieces
definition_en: The fragments of the Whole_patient that result from the Agent's action. 'I smashed the toy boat to flinders.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the fracturing is completed. 'I shattered the vase completely.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the Whole_patient which is directly affected by the breakage. 'With a swing of his broadsword, he shattered the gobletall the way to the stem.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an event. ' I broke it open.'

name: Resistant_surface
definition_en: The Resistant_surface is the surface against which a Agent presses the Whole_patient.  'Michael broke the bottle against his head . ' 'She did her best to rip her shirt on the fence.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event which leads to the fragmentation of the Whole_patient.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The Vehicle ends up stationary on land.  'She landed the plane on an unoccupied airstrip.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Source expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent.  'We tried to land the helicopter from the east to avoid detection.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.  In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.  'He wasn't willing to land the plane through lightning and rain.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is any expression that tells where the Vehicle ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.   'They set planes down on the strip before midnight.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A Manner expression describes a property of landing which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion.  Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.  'The pilot carefully put down the plane and let the police approach.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a Operator lands a Vehicle.

name: Cotheme
definition_en: Cotheme is a second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.   'Jones landed the with three planes which were flying in close formation.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Operator lands teh Vehicle.

name: New_situation
definition_en: The New_situation are the state of the Goal when the Vehicle arrives.   'I dream of landing a troop carrier to a standing ovation.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the state of the Operator or Vehicle upon arrival.   'We were forced to land the small passender plane unaware of the conditions on the ground.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The time period within which the landing event repeats multiple times.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the landing event itself and any of its participants.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Operator lands the Vehicle at the Goal.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE marks the state of affairs reported by the landing event as understood to play a role in the state of affairs of Event_description

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Operator lands the Vehicle at the Goal.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the landing occurs.

name: Operator
definition_en: The Operator maneuvers the vehicle onto land.  A skilled pilot would never set a plane down in weather like this.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that manipulates a Sound_maker so that it makes Noise.  'You can ring the bell as often as you'd like.  '

name: Sound_maker
definition_en: The entity that produces the Noise, as a result of the action of the Agent.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion is the sublocation of the Sound_maker from which the sound is emitting.

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: The location from which an Agent or Cause acts to project sound from a Sound_maker toward an (implicit) perceiver.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of one of the primary participants (either Agent or Sound_maker) during the course of the sound-making event.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An action directly due to the Agent or Cause that results in the Sound_maker emitting noise..

name: Cause
definition_en: The inanimate force of nature that causes the Sound_maker to produce noise.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs or action that the Agent wishes to bring about by performing the action.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the noise is produced.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the sound is produced.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times the Sound_maker makes noise per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Iterations
definition_en: Used for expressions that indicate the number of times Sound_maker makes noise.

name: Project
definition_en: The object or idea that undergoes change due to the efforts of the Agent.

name: Prior_state
definition_en: The former state of the Project.

name: Post_state
definition_en: The state of the Project following an advance.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the progress occurs.

name: Rate
definition_en: The rate at which the change happens.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the progress, generally a description comparing events (the same way); in addition, it may describe characteristics and states of the Agent that also affect the development.

name: Duration
definition_en: The period over which the Agent develops the Project.

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount of advancement that the Project has attained.

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant dimension of development.  'We have developed our community economically in these last few years.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that brings about the development of the Project.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the the Project progresses.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent progresses the Project.

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Agent which enables the advancement.

name: Theme
definition_en: Theme identifies the object involved in motion.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE  identifies the Place where the event occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which an event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is the way in which the motion in place is instigated.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Periodicity
definition_en: The number of times the Theme returns to a state in a given duration. 'It turns at 1000 rpms.'

name: Fixed_location
definition_en: The point or set of points that define the limits of motion for the Theme.  For spinning motions, it is the axis, for vibrating it is a boundary, for swinging it is a point. 'She twirled around him several times.' 'Balls spin on their axes .' 'The window vibrated in the frame.' 'He swung by a single handhold.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent performs the intentional act.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

name: Angle
definition_en: Angle identifies the amount that the Theme turns. 'Spin the dial a quarter turn.'

name: Locus
definition_en: The Agent's manipulation of an Theme may be further specified as being localized to some part of the Theme, a Locus.  This FE is usually expressed as a PP Complement.  'Pat squeezed Jo by the hand.'

name: Bodypart_of_agent
definition_en: This FE identifies the part of the Agent's body being used to manipulate the Theme.   'Kim twirled the glass in his fingers.'

name: Cause
definition_en: Cause identifies the non-agentive force that causes the motion in place. 'The wind vibrated the string.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, that express the Direction of the swinging, vibrating or rotating.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent intentionally creates a situation in which the Perceiver observes or experiences the Phenomenon.

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The Phenomenon is an entity or idea that is perceived by the Perceiver.

name: Perceiver
definition_en: The Perceiver is made to have a perceptual experience by the Agent.

name: Means
definition_en: The instrument or method by which the Perceiver was shown the Phenomenon.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the way in which the Agent presents the Phenomenon.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Frequency
definition_en: Frequency describes how often the Agent presents the Phenomenon.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent causes the perception of the Perceiver.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose of the Agent in creating the perception of the Perceiver.

name: Actor
definition_en: An Actor is a sentient being who is exhibiting, possibly uninintentionally, some Phenomenon.

name: Entity
definition_en: An object that has some association with a Phenomenon.

name: Medium
definition_en: The Medium through which a Phenomenon is expressed.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: A Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the Actor or Co-participant Agent.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Agent
definition_en: A sentient being acts with the intention of causing a process to begin again. 'The driver restarted the truck after it stalled.'

name: Process
definition_en: The process which begins again after a suspension.

name: Hiatus
definition_en: The period of time during which the process is suspended. 'The two countries revived diplomatic relations after a lull of five years.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the process is restarted. 'This state reinstated the death penalty in 1975.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that causes the process to resume. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.  'The spring rains restarted the flow of the stream.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent causes the Process to resume.  'The two nations revived relations in Geneva during the latest round of talks.'

name: Means
definition_en: The intentional act performed by the Agent that results in the resumption of the Process.  'He managed to revive the controversy by leaking the story to several tabloid magazines.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the manner in which the Agent causes the resumption of the Process.  'Japanese banks have been rapidly reviving business activity.'

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The length of time for which the Process continues after being started by the Agent.  'The project was restarted for several weeks before it was permanently abandoned.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent intentionally brings about the decay of the Patient.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient undergoes decay.

name: Depictive
definition_en: A depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of causing the Patient to rot.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by an Agent, or a sub-event centered around a Cause that leads it to cause the Patient to rot.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Cause causes the Patient to rot.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Cause acts upon the Patient.

name: Cause
definition_en: An event which causes the Patient to rot.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Agent may use an instrument to bring about the rotting.

name: Cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.   'The programme sparked a public outcry.'

name: Effect
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the process that the Cause initiates.  'Few things spark the wrath of the British like food additives.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Effect occurs.  'In Obscurania, the release of the movie sparked protests.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is the way in which the Cause causes the process to begin.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE is for the Time  when causing to start occurs

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Cause results in the Effect.

name: Purpose
definition_en: To what end the Cause caused the Effect.

name: Co-timed_event
definition_en: This FE identifies the first Co-timed_event of the started Effect.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Cause causes the Effect.

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason why or the way in which the Cause causes the Effect.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world at the time when the Cause produces the Effect.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: New_situation
definition_en: A consecutive event to the starting of the Effect.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies the  Depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Sleeper
definition_en: The person or being that is sleeping.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent intentionally affects a Patient.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent intentionally affects a Patient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent wakes the Sleeper. 'John roused her to irritate her.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which an intentional act is performed. Mary woke him because he looked troubled.

name: Cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.  'The rain woke me.' 'The smell of cooking woke the children.'

name: Sleep_state
definition_en: This describes the state out of which the Sleeper is awakened.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Sleeper ends up awake.  'I couldn't manage to rouse him completely, he could only mumble.'

name: Entity
definition_en: Concrete or abstract entity that does not exist after the event.

name: Place
definition_en: This is the Place where the new Entity ceases to exist.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifes the Time when a new Entity ceases to be.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE labels the Explanation of the destruction or disappearance of the Entity.

name: Components
definition_en: This FE identifies the components into which the Entity dissipates.

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: This FE identifies the length of time before the Entity comes into existence again.

name: Role
definition_en: The aspect of the Entity which no longer exists.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE identifies the Period_of_iterations during which habitual or iterative actions are performed.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Entity disappears.

name: Degree
definition_en: The completeness of the disappearance of the Entity

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person whose certainty or uncertainty is at issue.  'Marcel was sure that she had seen Eldridge on the balcony.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the entity that a Cognizer has a certain/uncertain belief about.  'She talked of quests , of finding this absurd religious character , but he was unsure of her conviction.' 'I 'm dubious about this Mafia story.'

name: Content
definition_en: The Content denotes the mental content that the Cognizer is certain or uncertain about.   'I am sure that we'll arrive on time.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE indicates the Degree to which the Cognizer is certain or uncertain.  'Charles felt fairly confident of her safety for the time being.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The FE Manner denotes the manner of the certainty or uncertainty.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part that conveys the mental state of  the Cognizer.  'She caught sight of her mother's dubious expression.'  Notice that we do NOT tag possessives such as 'her mother's' or 'on her face' that occur within the noun phrase of which the target adjective is a part. In sentences such as   'She had a dubious look on her face.'  NOTE: We do NOT tag 'have' and its subject since the governor relationship is between the verb 'have' and the noun that the target adjective modifies rather than between the target adjective and the verb 'have'.

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Cognizer is certain.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent blocks access to the Useful_location.  'Police have cordoned off the area where the crime took place.'

name: Useful_location
definition_en: The Useful_location is the place the Theme is headed towards and the Agent has changed the accessibility of.  'Protestors barricaded a highway that connects the industrial sectors to the ports.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is headed towards, or has an intention or tendency to head towards, the Useful_location, but is potentially blocked due to actions of the Agent.  'Authorities barricaded the road to all traffic.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Useful_location is or is not accessible.

name: Portal
definition_en: The Agent may regulate access to the Useful_location by regulating access to a Portal, including a part of the portal that could block potential Themes, such as doors or gates.  'They've blockaded the entrance -- no one can get in or out.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'The debate is on regarding the trial of individuals accused of non-violently barricading downtown pet stores.'

name: Means
definition_en: An action carried out by the Agent to bring about the change in accessibility.  'The students barricaded the doorways by lining up in two rows surrounding the building.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Agent changes the accessibility of the Useful_location.  'A rebel group blockaded the roadways late last night.'

name: Place
definition_en: The general Place where the blocking or allowing of access occurs.  'Many roads were cordorned off in the central district right after the incident.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Agent changes the accessibility of the Useful_location.  'They clearly blockaded this route to prevent anyone from sneaking past their surveillance technology.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: A portion of the Useful_location, usually its edge, where accessibility is blocked.  'Police cordoned off the park along its southern edge.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Agent uses the Instrument to block access, often by placing the Instrument such that it cannot be traversed.  'They barricaded the doors with heavy crates and rusted machinery.'

name: Theme
definition_en: This is the object which moves. In many sentences this FE will be expressed as something which moves under its own power. However, this FE is not required to be an animate mover, so it is different from a self-mover.  'At that point the truck in front of me turned right into the huge ditch/field that separates the interstate from the access road.'

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source.   'One of those ugly landcuisers cut left from the opposite lane in moving traffic.'

name: Path
definition_en: Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal (see below) expresses the frame element Path, excluding directional expressions.  'They turned right through another gate into a courtyard opening.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Any expression which indicates where the Theme ends up as a result of the change of direction.   'Finally, where the road begins to climb steeply, cut right onto a small trail near a sign in a tree, and go downhill to the stream.'.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In agentive frames, it may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Theme that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'I carefully turned left onto Narragansett and worked my way through the debris.'

name: Means
definition_en: An event involving the Theme that results in the Theme moving in the specified way.   'Participants drove a vehicle model that rolled on flat ground and turned right or left by steering front wheels as in a typical car.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the Theme changes direction.  'Suddenly, the jeep quickly turned left down a side road.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: This is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique:    'I turned right after them, closed in on the rear plane but then discovered another plane from the formation nearing me from the right side.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A phrase describing the state of the Theme during the act of changing direction.   'The big forward picked up speed entering Edmonton's end, cut to the right with Charlie Huddy draped over him and left a pass for Lemieux as Stevens battled Kevin Lowe into a screen in front of Fuhr.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the setting where the change of direction during the Theme's motion occurs.  'Turn right at the stop light and follow Park Avenue.'

name: Path_shape
definition_en: The configuration formed by the Path that the Theme traverses during the change of direction.  'The tank rumbled, backed quickly, turned left and right in a sine curve.'

name: Direction
definition_en: The new direction in which the Theme continues its motion.  'Eventually, though, I backtracked to Kel Tole and hung a left toward Kilgal Tole.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the change of direction takes place.   'Then I turned left onto 220th Street.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Theme wishes to bring about.   'That car was attempting to back in, and had to cut to the left in order to back up the vehicle.'

name: Means_of_motion
definition_en: The device or bodypart that serves to move the Theme.  'Go back to where you turned left in your car to reach the trailhead.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A factor which explains the change of direction of the Theme.    'We've turned north because we've struck desert heading south.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time the change of direction occurs and which the change of direction is taken to be a part of.  'Anyway, on my first trip to Wakefield, I turned right off Falls of Neuse Road, which is generally where the middle-class and upper middle-class houses and apartments are going.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that a change of direction occurs.  'They turned right three times and approached the sea lions from behind.'

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: A larger conceptualization that includes the change of direction as an integral part. The change of direction expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.   'The pilot of N3602D turned left in an attempt to avoid a collision.'

name: New_situation
definition_en: An unexpected event that affects the Theme, which is enabled by, and occurs after, the change of direction.  'I have a tendency to shoot straight forward after the initial drop and then cut to the left only to meet a knee-high rush of white water.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the change of direction event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.

name: Angle
definition_en: The angle between the old and the new Direction in which the Theme moves.  'There we turned right by almost 180 degrees and by a winding road, going steeply up we went to And?lka.'

name: Result
definition_en: The situation that results from the change of direction

name: Agent
definition_en: The sentient entity that changes the duration of the Event.  'Don't let him prolong the discussion to an absurd length.'

name: New_duration
definition_en: The new duration of the Event.  'Don't let him prolong the discussion to an absurd length.'

name: Initial_duration
definition_en: The planned duration of the Event before the change takes place.  'Harsh weather combined made it necessary to cut the tour short from its original four months to three.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the change in duration of the Event is caused.  'Last week, he unnecessarily prolonged the agony, thinking that he could tough it out.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the initial and final durations differ from each other.  'Too bad we can't extend our vacation even more.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the  event causing the change of the Event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Rain so cruelly cut short the game against Bangladesh.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in bringing about the change of duration.  'Why would someone cut our time short like that?'

name: Event
definition_en: The Event's duration is changed.  'Don't let him prolong the discussion to an absurd length.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event that causes the change in Event duration.  'Rain so cruelly cut short the game against Bangladesh.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by  changing the duration of the Event.

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent (or event resulting from the Cause) that produces a change in the Event's duration.  'It seems they are bent on prolonging conflict by ignoring normal wartime conventions.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the animate entity which brings about the change in time of the Event. 'The umpire postponed the game.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is the non-sentient force which brings about the change of time for the Event. 'The rain delayed the baseball game.'

name: Event
definition_en: The Event is the occurrence which changes time. 'The opening of the musical was delayed.'</def-root >

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the way in which the time change takes place. 'My mother thoughtlessly delayed my salon appointment.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means describe the way in which the time change is accomplished. 'The mayor delayed the ribbon-cutting ceremony by pretending to be ill.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree is the extent to which the time change takes place.

name: Destination_event
definition_en: The Destination_event is the occasion which the timing of the Event occurs with respect to.  'Consumers should postpone purchasing a new car until their credit rating is acceptable.'

name: Destination_time
definition_en: The Destination_time is the time at which the Event actually occurs. 'The king is postponing the festival until July.'

name: Interval
definition_en: The Interval between the Landmark_time and the Destination_time may be expressed. 'The lanch will be delayed for two months.'

name: Landmark_time
definition_en: The Landmark_time is when the Event was originally intended to take place. 'The driving test was postponed from July to September.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the reason or explanation for why the Event occurs at a different time.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Agent intends to bring about by changing the time the Event will take place.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the delay occurred.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the expected time of the Event changes.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE indicates the Result of the change of consistency of the Patient  'The liquid gelled into a semi-solid mass.'

name: Initial_state
definition_en: This is the original state of the Patient.  'The cheesecake finally hardened from its runny state.'

name: Patient
definition_en: Patient is the entity that undergoes a change.   'The blood congealed.' 'The liquid gelled into a semi-solid mass.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the the Patient changes consistency.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Patient changes consistency.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Patient changes consistency.

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed at which the change of consistency occurs.  'The jello set in 30 minutes.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the consistency change occurs.  'The jello sets at room temperature.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Patient changes consistency.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the Patient changes consistency.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.  'The jello set around the edges.'

name: Selector
definition_en: The Selector (most commonly a group of people) is responsible for a change in leadership.  Typically, it occurs as the External Argument of verbs.  'The voters elected Blair.' 'The president appoints the prime minister.'

name: Old_leader
definition_en: With words denoting removal (or attempted removal) from office of a leader, the Old_leader is typically the direct object of verbs, or occurs in a PP Complement with noun targets, frequently headed by the preposition against.  'The students overthrew the president.' 'The uprising against the king was quickly ended by the military.'

name: New_leader
definition_en: With words denoting appointment to a position, the New_leader is typically the object of verbs.  'The president appoints the prime minister.'

name: Role
definition_en: Frequently the Old_leader or New_leader is referred to only by his/her role. However, the Role can be expressed separately from the leader, usually as either a secondary predicate or in a PP Complement.  'The board of directors appointed Ashton Acting President.' 'The board of directors appointed Ashton as Acting President.' 'The voters elected Mitterand to the presidency.'

name: Old_order
definition_en: The FE Old_order identifies the political order that existed before the change of leadership occurs. 'The rebels overthrew the dictatorship.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE indicates the Degree to which an event occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive indicates the state of one of the participants during the action.  'We dethroned him, unaware of the evil we did.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE is used for the Manner of performing an action.  'The king was ousted violently.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which  the Selector accomplishes the change of leadership.  'The rebels overthrew the government by gaining the support of the military.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE  is used for indicating the Result of an event.

name: Circumstances
