definition_en: This frame element describes the situation that brought about the change of leadership.  'The king was deposed in a bloody coup.'

name: Function
definition_en: The Function is the purpose the New_leader will fufill.

name: Time
definition_en: When the change takes place. 'The 2000 coup against the dictator was led by former president Smith.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the change takes place. 'The crew mutinied out in the middle of the Atlantic, the scoundrels.'

name: Body
definition_en: A group of individuals who are elected or appointed to perform some function of governance.  'His district elected her  to Congress three times.'

name: Patient
definition_en: Patient is the entity that undergoes a change of phase.   'The water froze.'

name: Result
definition_en: The FE Result indicates the result of the change of phase.  'The lake froze solid.'

name: Initial_state
definition_en: This is the original state of the Patient.  'The rock solidified  from its molten state.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the Patient changes phase.  'The lake froze to depths of 30 feet.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed at which the change of phase occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Patient changes phase.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the Patient changes phase.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time at which the Patient changes phase.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the phase change occurs.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.  'The cloth froze around the edges.'

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is the entity that undergoes a change of phase.   'The water froze.'

name: Result
definition_en: The FE Result indicates the result of the change of phase.  'The lake froze solid.'

name: Initial_state
definition_en: This is the original state of the Patient.  'The rock solidified  from its molten state.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the Patient changes phase.  'The lake froze to depths of 30 feet.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed at which the change of phase occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Patient changes phase.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the Patient changes phase.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time at which the Patient changes phase.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances at which the phase change occurs.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.  'The cloth froze around the edges.'

name: Owner
definition_en: The Owner is the entity that contains within itself or controls the Possession.

name: Possession
definition_en: The Possession is the physical or metaphoric object that increases or decreases in quantity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Possession undergoes a change in quantity.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Possession undergoes a change in quantity.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree of the change in quantity.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE denotes a proposition from which the event of increasing or decreasing in quantity logically follows.

name: Item
definition_en: The entity whose temperature changes.

name: Initial_temperature
definition_en: The temperature that the Item has prior to the event.

name: Final_temperature
definition_en: The temperature of the Item after the event.

name: Temperature_change
definition_en: The amount of difference between the Initial_temperature and the Final_temperature of the Item.

name: Hot_cold_source
definition_en: The Hot_cold_source is the source of the heat or coolness

name: Cause
definition_en: An event or state-of-affairs that leads to the change in temperature of the Item.

name: Container
definition_en: This FE identifies the Container that holds the Item whose temperature is being changed.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Item during the temperature change.

name: Duration
definition_en: The span of time in which the Item is changing temperature.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the change in temperature occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Item changes temperature.

name: Subregion
definition_en: A portion of the Item which is affected by the temperature change.

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner in which the Item changes temperature.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the temperature change occurs

name: Result
definition_en: The state of the Item that results from the temperature change.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Temperature
definition_en: The scalar property that the Item possesses.  This FE is rarely expressed.  'The raw fish that is to be eaten as sushi has to be meticulously prepared and must first be chilled in temperature to exactly above freezing point.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the change in temperature takes place.

name: Device
definition_en: The Device or machine that is in or out of operation.  'The night lights were turned on in the secondary school.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when a Device is put into or out of operation.  'My dad turned the lights on for me at 10 o'clock '

name: Place
definition_en: The Place in which the Device is put into or out of operation.  'Suddenly, the lights got turned on on the Jamaica road bridge.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person who changes the operational state of the Device.   'Instantly Sue activated the commlink on the wall.'

name: Cause
definition_en: Cause identifies the non-agentive force that causes the Device to begin to operate.  'He was in his stocking feet while standing in the bayou that formed when the wind turned the shower on in that one upstairs bathroom.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The FE Purpose denotes a state of affairs that the Agent wants to bring about by putting the Device into operation.  'They then activated the beacon in order to inform the International coastguard of their position.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the event of the Device's being caused to operate or cease to operate logically follows.    'It works great for this price, I haven't activated the cable box because analog cable works like any TV tuner would. '

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In agentive uses, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'I carefully turned off the computers, turned off the lights, locked that back door, and went to my office to do the paper work.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Device is active after the action.

name: Means
definition_en: An action done by the Agent in order to cause the Device to being to operate.  'He activated the machine by pulling the lever.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The Attribute is a scalar property that the Item possesses.'Oil rose in price by 2%.'

name: Item
definition_en: The entity that has a position on the scale.   'I fear this service will diminish in quality.'

name: Difference
definition_en: The distance by which an Item changes its position on the scale.'Oil rose in price by 2%.'

name: Path
definition_en: Any expression that gives information about points on the scale that the Item traverses between the starting and ending point of its movement along the scale.'The price of oil moved up last month.'

name: Final_value
definition_en: The position on the scale where the Item ends up. 'Microsoft shares fell to 7 5/8.'

name: Initial_value
definition_en: The initial position on the scale from which the Item moves away. 'Microsoft shares fell from 12 3/8 to 7 5/8.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The rate of change of the Value.'Prices are rising by 2% a year.'

name: Correlated_variable
definition_en: The Correlated_variable is an ordered progression of positions or values (most often a sequence of spatial locations) that the (dependent) Attribute is measured against. The Correlated_variable is metaphorically mapped onto the progression of time, and in the absence of this FE, changes are simply measured against (forward-directional) time.  'The amount of power increases with the frequency of the laser.' 'As you travel along the Quan-duo road, the poverty level soars dramatically.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the change of position takes place. 'The eggs will only increase under pressure.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result. of an event

name: Group
definition_en: The Group in which an Item changes the value of a Attribute in a specified way.'Colon cancer incidence fell by 50 % among men over 30.''Net foreign debt has more than tripled in Africa over this decade.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is the time-frame in which the change of position occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time over which the change takes place. 'The amount of troops in the war will no doubt double over the next several years.'

name: Value_range
definition_en: A portion of the scale, typically identified by its end points, along which the values of the Attribute fluctuate.  'The patient's temperature fluctuated between 28.5 and 29.5.'

name: Initial_correlate
definition_en: The value, location, or state-of-affairs that corresponds to the Initial_value of the Attribute.  'From Monterrey to southern Oregon, tree height increases steadily in this species to a stunning 50 meters.'

name: Final_correlate
definition_en: The value, location, or state-of-affairs that corresponds to the Final_value of the Attribute.  'From Monterrey to southern Oregon, tree height increases steadily in this species to a stunning 50 meters.'

name: Place
definition_en: A location where Attribute is measured

name: Initial_state
definition_en: A description that presents the Item's state before the change in the Attribute's value as an independent predication.  'Diesels have increased from having a 20% market share in 1995 to just over 30% in 2004.'

name: Final_state
definition_en: A description that presents the Item's state after  the change in the Attribute's value as an independent predication.  'It was never bad (1 or 2 seizures a year), but this past decade, it has increased to having them 1 day a month and on that 1 day I have 6 or 7 seizures.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the quantity change takes place and of which it is taken to be a part.  'Hong Kong : Buying by London institutions helped the Hang Seng index to climb 39.95 points to 2,786.65 in moderate trade.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The situation or state-of-affairs that results in the change in quantity described in this instance of the frame.  'Her panic had declined because I spent two hours explaining what you did !'

name: Entity
definition_en: The entity which has undergone change.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the change in posture which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Protagonist that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The individual whose posture changes.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Protagonist's state throughout the time they are changing posture.

name: Location
definition_en: The place or  setting in which the Protagonist's change of posture takes place.   'The supplicant sat down outside the office and waited for the mayor.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Protagonist changes posture.

name: Result
definition_en: The final state of the Protagonist after the change of posture.

name: Path
definition_en: Path is used for expressions that indicate the trajectory of motion without referring to the Source or the Goal of motion.  'She leaned through the service door' 'Tim Thomas leaned forwards '

name: Goal
definition_en: This FE is used for any expressions that indicate the endpoint of the posture change. Often this is the place that provides support for the posture.  ' John leaned against the wall and closed his eyes'

name: Source
definition_en: Source is used for expressions that indicate the starting point of the change of posture.  'Charles stood up from his armchair'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE is used for expressions that indicate a line from the deitic center towards a reference point (which may be implicit) that is neither the Goal of the posture change nor a landmark along the way of the moving part of the body.  Often Direction is defined with reference to the canonical orientation of the Protagonist, or the orientation imposed by an implicit observer.  'Smithers leaned forward to grab the folder on the far side.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which a Protagonist assumes a posture.  'Sunil bent down to pick up the newspaper'

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE is used for expressions that indicate the extent to which the body (part) moves during the change of posture.  ' Bend back as far as you can'

name: Point_of_contact
definition_en: The part of the body that provides support to the Protagonist in holding the posture.  'Smithers crouched down on his haunces'

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Protagonist whereby they achieve the change of posture.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent makes the Patient more resistant to attack.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is the entity that is being made more resistant.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

name: Result
definition_en: The resultant state of the action.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by an Agent that enables them to act upon the Patient.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Agent makes the Patient more resistant.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Agent makes the Patient more resistant.

name: Cause
definition_en: An event which causes the Patient to become more resistant.

name: Attack
definition_en: This FE describes the literal or figurative Attack that the Agent is strengthening the Patient for.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that changes their situation.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Agent makes a change.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The aim of the Agent when they carry out the change.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Agent which brings about a change.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Agent's change which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Tools
definition_en: The entities controlled by an Agent to achieve some Purpose.

name: Old_tool
definition_en: The tool that the Agent had been using.

name: New_tool
definition_en: The tool that the Agent ends up using.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times that the action goes from start to finish.

name: Entity
definition_en: The object or phenomenon which exists in the State of disorder.  It is common for the Entity to be null instantiated in this frame.  'Subsequent bomb alerts caused travelchaos in the London Underground.'  'Get the treaty signed before there's time for any more chaos.INI'

name: State
definition_en: The State in which the Entity exists.  Usually the State will be the target-denoting noun.  'More chaos awaits the Soviet Union unless it ditches perestroika for a Thatcherite purge of its economy.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the State exists.  'Booking, reservations, staffing and just about everything was in a state of total chaos.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity exists in the State.  'Lying in bed listening to the chaos downstairs, he knew his conquest had only been temporary.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time in which the Entity exists in the State

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Entity exists in the State.  'Monica Lewinksy in 1998 gave him a rich new target, as did the electoral chaos of 2000.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any characterization of the State not covered by a more specific frame element.  'Let him picture her pottering in the improvised chaos of a damp, windowless room.'

name: Interlocutors
definition_en: The group of individuals involved in chatting.

name: Interlocutor_1
definition_en: The individual or individuals that form the more prominent (i.e. agentive) party of a conversation, as compared with Interlocutor_2. That is, Interlocutor_1 is generally encoded as the External Argument of verbs, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Interlocutor_1.  Thus a Purpose (or Means, Depictive, or Manner) is construed to be that of Interlocutor_1, not necessarily that of Interlocutor_2 or the group of Interlocutors as a whole.  'We chatted with the guards to distract them from the heist going on right behind them.'

name: Interlocutor_2
definition_en: The semantically (and grammatically) less prominent group of participants in a conversation.  It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with).    'I gossiped with the rest of the choir for a little while.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the chatting goes on.  'They yakked for hours!'

name: Topic
definition_en: The general subject that the statements of the Interlocutors in the conversation pertain to.  'Oh, we gossiped about the management shakedown a bit.'

name: Language
definition_en: The language(s) or dialect(s) that a conversation is conducted in.  'They exchanged gossip in French while I sat by, completely ignored.'

name: Means_of_communication
definition_en: The device used by the Interlocutors to communicate.  'Don't get excited--after a short telephone chat with a broker, you 'll have your money.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: What the Interlocutors (or Interlocutor_1) hope to accomplish by chatting.  'We shot the breeze for a couple of hours just to pass the time.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which a chat takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where a chat takes place.  'A bit of lunch-time conversation on the veranda would not be amiss, I hope?'

name: Means
definition_en: The way that the Interlocutors succeed in having a conversation.  'Though some of the fellas couldn't hear anymore, we chatted with them by sharing a typewriter.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the conversation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Interlocutors (or Interlocutor_1) that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the state of the Interlocutors (or Interlocutor_1) during the conversation.  'We talked for a few minutes, uncertain about why we were bothering.'

name: Perceptual_source
definition_en: Perceptual_source is used for the entity that is being described. A recipe can stand in for a Perceptual_source which is a kind of food.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which a chemical sense is described.  'The almonds are extremely bitter.'

name: Sensory_attribute
definition_en: Sensory_attribute is used for words that describe the perception itself. 	 'The almonds had a bitter  taste.' 'The coffee had a pungent smell.'

name: Chemical_entity
definition_en: The entity for which potency is being evaluated.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the potency from the norm expressed by the target LU.

name: Time
definition_en: The time during which the Chemical_entity is in the state of having  a particular potency.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Chemical_entity has the ascribed potency.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Chemical_entity has the ascribed potency.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive labels an independent descriptor of a Cognizer in a  choosing event.  'I could pick you out of a crowd blindfolded.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer chooses the Chosen out of the Possibilities. 'Wehave to pick a colour for the living room.'

name: Chosen
definition_en: Chosen identifies the entity or course of action which is selected from among the Possibilities. 'I decided to give it another try.' 'We have to pick a colour for the living room.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE  identifies the Explanation for which the Cognizer chooses the Chosen. 'He chose her for her beauty.'

name: Possibilities
definition_en: A Cognizer makes a choice from among a set of Possibilities. Possibilities are commonly expressed via an oblique phrase which indicates the alternative or alternatives, or by a subordinate clause (choosing to do it or choosing not to do it), typically headed by "whether or "if". 'They chose their new guitarist out of more than 300 auditioners.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which bthe Cognizer accomplishes the choosing. 'He picked a name by pointing to one in the phone book.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the choosing occurs.  'The winner was selected in the secret meeting room.'</def-root >

name: Larger_purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Larger_purpose for which the Cognizer chooses. It exemplifies what the Cognizer hopes to accomplish by choosing the particular Chosen. 'Mr. Smith chose Lord Rollins to be his running mate in order to further irritate all his critics.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Cognizer chooses the Chosen. 'I was n't chosen in the last round.' 'Select the jury by 3 PM.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the selecting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of a Cognizer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'She wisely chose the plain-looking cup.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic occurs quite rarely in this frame and usually only as a PP Complement of a noun target: 'There is no choice about the way through.' 'If there is any choice in hue at all, choose the darkest.'

name: Inherent_purpose
definition_en: The Cognizer intends the Chosen to fulfill an Inherent_purpose . 'Samsonchose  Delilahas a wife.'

name: Contrast
definition_en: The hypothetical Chosen that is less desirable for the Cognizer.

name: Entity
definition_en: An object or event that is described as being available under delimited Conditions.

name: Time
definition_en: A temporal characterization of the circumstances of the existence of an Entity.

name: Place
definition_en: A spacial characterization of the <fex name="">Circumstances of the existence of the <fex name="">Entity.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: A description of the state of the world in which the Entity can be experienced.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Properties of the Entity as it exists in the stated Circumstances.

name: Defendant
definition_en: The Defendant is the individual or entity summoned to appear in Court, or to pay a Fine instead.   'Mrs. Jones was summonsed for running a red light.'

name: Court
definition_en: The Court where the Defendant is summoned to appear.   'Police have summonsed Mr. Barnes to appear at the Manchester County Court.'

name: Authority
definition_en: The Authority serve a citation or summons to a Defendant, requiring that the latter appear in Court or pay a Fine.   'The cop cited Mrs. Jones for illegal parking.'

name: Charges
definition_en: Charges identifies the infraction or offense for which the Defendant is summoned.   'The cop served Mrs. Jones a citation for speeding.'

name: Fine
definition_en: Fine is the monetary amount that the Defendant may pay in certain citation cases, instead of him or her having to appear in Court.   'Jason refused to pay the $100 fine specified by his summons.'

name: Place
definition_en: Place is the location where the Defendant is issued the citation or summons.   'Police issued Owen a citation on the shoulder of the highway.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Defendant is issued the citation or summons.   'Molly was cited for driving over the speed limit on Friday.'

name: Claimant
definition_en: The Claimant asserts rights or priviliges, typically ownership, over some Property. 'The king ordered the envoy to claim the land accross the river.'

name: Property
definition_en: The Property is declared to be under the ownership of the Claimant. 'I claim this forest and environs in the name of the Queen.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The Beneficiary is declared the owner of the Property by the Claimant, or the person or group in whose name or favor the Claimant is acting. 'I claim this forest and environs in the name of the Queen.'

name: Role
definition_en: The Role of the land claimed. 'The French government claimed this string of islands as their own.' 'As of yet, no one has claimed this hill as belonging to anyone.'

name: Offender
definition_en: The individual who is accused or convicted of a Crime.  'Since 1976, 225 death row inmates have been granted clemency for humanitarian reasons. '

name: Crime
definition_en: An action deemed criminal by law.  'I never saw a legal case where a person was given clemency for murder.'

name: Executive_authority
definition_en: The constitutionally specified authority who has the power to grant clemency.  'Mr. Papa was granted clemency for a drug conviction by Mr. Pataki, and released in 1997'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Executive_authority  is responding to in granting clemency.   'Since 1976, 224 death row inmates have been granted clemency for humanitarian reasons. '

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which clemency is granted.  'In addition to Ms.  White, 55, Mr.  Pataki granted clemency yesterday to three men serving long prison terms for offenses under the stern Rockefeller-era drug laws that mandate long sentences for some relatively low-level drug crimes.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Executive_authority that accomplishes the granting of clemency.  'Write, call, e-mail, or fax Governor Frank O'Bannon as soon as possible and urge him to grant clemency by giving Gary Burris a sentence of life without parole'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the act of clemency which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Executive_authority that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Executive_authority intends to accomplish by granting clemency.  'And so he granted clemency so that all who surrendered would be received as freedmen into his own army.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Executive_authority grants clemency.  'Apparently, no woman has ever been granted clemency there.'

name: Containing_object
definition_en: This FE identifies the item that is closed by the agent with the fastener. Lee buttoned his coat.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent opens/closes the Containing-object. 'Harry uncorked the champagne.'

name: Fastener
definition_en: This FE identifies the fastener that the agent manipulates. 'Marcus tied his shoe with the neon-green shoelaces.'

name: Enclosed_region
definition_en: This FE identifies the region enclosed by the container-object that is closed. 'Harry buckled his belt around his ample waist.' 'Jeremy  buttoned the shirt around her hypothermic body.'

name: Manipulator
definition_en: This FE identifies the instrument or part of the body that manipulates  the Fastener. 'Lee unbuckled his belt  with one hand.' Note that this FE is syntactically omissible.

name: Container_portal
definition_en: This FE identifies the active zone of the container that may be expressed as the direct object of the target verb.   'We zipped the tent flap.' The sentence refers to the closure of the tent, hence is different from sentences where the action involves the manipulation of a fastener, e.g. We unscrewed the lid.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Container_portal/Containing_object ends up closed.  'Why did you only lace it up partway?'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity manipulated by the Agent that accomplishes the closure of the Containing_object or the Container_portal.  'He sealed the lid with wax.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the closing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Agent that accomplishes the closure of the Container_portal or Containing_object.  'He had to button his sleeve by holding the cuff in his mouth.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the closing event takes place.  'Shouldn't you have buttoned that in the bathroom?'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Agent closes the Container_portal or the Containing_object.  'They close the bank vault at precisely 5:35PM.'

name: Result
definition_en: The resultant state of the Closure action.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The person for whom the Closure event occurs.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE describes the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Closure event and any of its participants.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Garment
definition_en: This FE identifes the clothing worn.  'Mike wore a new leather jacket.'

name: Wearer
definition_en: The Wearer is the person wearing the clothes, or for whom the clothes are intended.  'Mike wore a new leather jacket.'

name: Style
definition_en: This FE identifes the design, or cut, of the clothing.  'Mike wore a tailored leather jacket.'

name: Material
definition_en: This FE identifes the material from which the clothing is made.  'Mike wore a new leather jacket.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE identifes any description of the clothing besides Style  and Material. 'Mike wore a new black leather jacket.' Note that each modifer of the target gets its own FE (and, hence, its own GF and PT).

name: Subregion
definition_en: This FE identifies a part of the clothing.  'Mike wore a leather jacket with fringes.'

name: Use
definition_en: This FE identifes the Use for which a Garment is worn or was made.    'Mike wore a new riding jacket.'

name: Body_location
definition_en: Body_location identifies the place on the body where the clothing is worn.  'Hannah draped a shawl elegantly over her shoulders.'

name: Creator
definition_en: The individual who created the Garment.  'She 's wearing a Ralph Lauren dress.'

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which the Creator makes the Garment.  'The bikinis of the 1940's are fairly similar.'

name: Name
definition_en: The name given to a specific Garment.  Note this is not the name of a general class of clothing items, but rather an individual item.  This is accordingly VERY RARE.  ''

name: Clothing
definition_en: This is the Clothing of which the target word is a part.  'His trouser pocket...'

name: Subpart
definition_en: This is a Subpart of the Clothing item.  'His trouser pocket...'

name: Material
definition_en: The Material from which the Subpart is made.  'He wore a jacket with a fur collar.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: A part of the Clothing item.  'a shirt with long sleeves'

name: Wearer
definition_en: The person who is wearing the clothes, or for whom the clothes are intended.  'He wore a filthy leather miniskirt.'

name: Body_location
definition_en: This is the part of the body were the garment is worn.  'He had a stocking over his head.' 'He put gloves on his hands.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE identifes any description of the clothing besides Material.  'He shoved his left hand into a deep pant pocket.'

name: Participant1
definition_en: The profiled member of a co-association relationship.

name: Participants
definition_en: The members of a Co-association relationship (collectively).

name: Participant2
definition_en: The backgrounded member(s) of a Co-association relationship.

name: Place
definition_en: The place at which the Co-association relationship exists.

name: Time
definition_en: The time during which the co-association relationship exists.

name: Institution
definition_en: The institution or organization that the Participants have in common.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: With a target verb, the Cognizer is usually expressed as an External Argument, with the Topic appearing as an Object NP, a gerundive verbal Complement, or a PP. 'Pat considered a career change.' 'The employees contemplated going on strike.' 'Everyone thought about the game.'  With a target noun, the Cognizer is typically expressed as the External Argument of a support verb, as a possessor, or in a PP. 'The teacher gave some thought to a career change.' 'Your thoughts about art are not relevant.' 'Your application was submitted for consideration by the committee.'

name: Topic
definition_en: With a target verb, the Topic is usually expressed as an Object NP, a gerundive verbal complement, or a PP. 'Pat considered a career change.' 'The employees contemplated going on strike.' 'Everyone thought about the game.'  With a target noun, the Topic is typically expressed in a PP. 'Your contemplation of a career change is understandable.' 'Your thoughts about art are not relevant.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The FE Degree indicates the degree to which the cognizing occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

name: Manner
definition_en: The FE Manner indicates the way in which the cognizing is being done.

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Cognizer that makes them able to cogitate.

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Medium
definition_en: The physical or abstract setting in which the Cognizer considers the Topic.  'Over the telephone, Frank pondered  telling Maria about the fire.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Cognizer is trying to bring about by thinking.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Cognizer considers the Topic.

name: Concept_1
definition_en: The concept which is linked to Concept_2.  Generally expressed as the external argument. 'Smoking is tied to cancer.'

name: Concept_2
definition_en: The concept which is tied to Concept_1.  Generally expressed as a PP complement. 'Smoking is tied to cancer.'

name: Point_of_view
definition_en: The point of view from which the connection exists. 'Smoking is linked to cancer in his mind.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the connection exists.  'In the lab, a person's weight and life expectancy are strongly connected.'

name: Concepts
definition_en: The two concepts expressed jointly. 'Smoking and weight gain are connected.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree of connection between the Concepts. 'These two incidents are closely linked.'

name: Specification
definition_en: A further specification on the linkage. 'These two concepts are innately connected.' 'Smoking and lung cancer are linked in some unknown way.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The Phenomenon is the entity that evokes a cognitive reaction for the Experiencer.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer in the entity who experiences the cognitive impact brought about by the Phenomenon.

name: Judgment
definition_en: The Judgment is the characterization of the cognitive impact or evaluation of the Phenomenon.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The physical or abstract Circumstances that determine the Judgment of the Phenomenon.

name: Manner
definition_en: The extent to which the cognitive impact of a Phenomenon affects the Judgment ascribed to it.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency with with the Experiencer experiences the Phenomenon.

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: A State_of_affairs (that is, an event or state) that holds independently of (potentially) causally-related States of affairs.  'Is it a coincidence that most of the planets fall within the Titius-Bode law's boundaries?'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the State_of_affairs holds.  'Last night's coincidences were too much for me to handle.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the State_of_affairs holds.  'Several strange coincidences at the airport got the attention of federal officials.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the target word not covered by a more specific FE.

name: Partner_1
definition_en: When the parties in a collaboration are expressed separately, this Frame Element marks constituents that express the one that is grammatically more prominent, i.e., the one that is the subject of an active clause.  ' Smithers collaborated with Chief Wiggum '

name: Partner_2
definition_en: This Frame element marks constituents expressing the grammatically  less prominent, typically oblique, party in a collaboration.  ' Britain is collaborating with France and West Germany in the development of anti-tank missiles'

name: Undertaking
definition_en: This frame element marks constituents that express the project in which the Partners are collaborating.   ' The two artists collaborated on a mosaic.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which Partner_1 collaborates with Partner_2 or in which the Partners collaborate.

name: Partners
definition_en: This frame element marks expressions that express the parties that work together in an Undertaking.  ' Smithers and Chief Wiggum collaborated well '

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Partners are engaged in their collaboration.  'Last year some of my colleagues collaborated in the design of a theme-park.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the collaboration occurs.  ' In New Braunfels Paul and John collaborated in the design of a new Guggenheim '

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the amount of time the Partners collaborate.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate to what extent the Partners are cooperating.  'The French government cooperated fully with the New Zealand police.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action taken by the Partners that lets them accomplish the collaboration.

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: A region of space located at a Ground.

name: Ground
definition_en: An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Profiled_region.

name: Colonists
definition_en: A group of people who move together to an area outside their Homeland for the purpose of settling.  'Spain settled the northern areas of Mexico through the use of missions, civil settlements, and presidios. '  Often the phrase expressing the Colonists will also encode the Homeland (e.g., French people, China), which we indicate with second-layer FE annotation.  'In the 7th century BC, Phoenicians colonized the eastern section of Libya.' 'In the 7th century BC, Phoenicians colonized the eastern section of Libya'

name: Homeland
definition_en: The Homeland is where the Colonists are originally from.

name: New_area
definition_en: The Colonists move to the New_area, inhabiting it and (in the case of nation-states) extending the control of the Homeland.  'Norse invaders in the 900s colonized the North Midlands more densely than any other part of England" '

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the colonizing takes place.  'The English colonized the islands in 1632.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the group of Colonists spreads across or inhabits the New_area.  'In the reign of Elizabeth, the English strove to thoroughly colonize Ireland, which they had originally invaded in the twelfth century.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the colonizing is done.  'Humans in the future may end up colonizing outer space in order to survive.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Colonists, Homeland, or New_area.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the colonization event logically follows.

name: Entity
definition_en: This FE identifies the Entity described by the Color. 'His jacket was absolutely green.'

name: Color
definition_en: A position in color-space, generally used to describe the quality of some Entity.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category of a Color is indicated. 'It is said that the eyes of the prophet will be of the deepest azure blue.'

name: Comparand
definition_en: A physical entity (or type of physical entity) whose color is similar to the designated color.  When this FE occurs with adjective targets, (a relatively rare circumstance) the Comparand also serves to specify a Type, which should be labeled on the second FE layer. 'Her lips looked sunset red in the light of the single lamp.' 'The ents stared out at us with eyes the deep green of the forest.'

name: Color_qualifier
definition_en: A phrase that indicates the direction in color-space from the center of the region designated by the Color. 'Its gill-flaps turn a sort of reddish orange when it has the disease.' 'I told him not to use the dark brown, but he didn't listen.' 'For a moment the whole sky turned bright pink.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Some characteristic or judgment of a Color implicitly imposed by a speaker. 'Her feathers were dyed a lovely purple for the occasion.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The state of affairs that the Color is dependent on. 'His face was red with anger.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The closeness of the Entity 's color to the center of a Color prototype.  'The plums are very red, and very ripe.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the Entity that has the indicated Color.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The aspect of the Entity which is under discussion, namely color.  ' The wine is bright red in color with aromas of red fruits, toasted almond, clove and orange peel. '

name: Color
definition_en: The color that is being described.  'I love really pale yellows.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The level to which the Color is representative of a specific quality.  'That's a very vivid red.'

name: Described_entity
definition_en: The entity whose Color is being described.  'Fornalutx is a jewel of warm stone. '

name: Source
definition_en: The individual or environmental reservoir of a Disease that the Protagonist was exposed to.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Protagonist contracts the Disease.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Protagonist contracts the Disease.  It is different from the Source (usually marked with "from") in that it does not necessarily mean that it was contact with the Place that actually led to infection.  'He caught a cold in Hawaii .'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event as a whole in comparison to other events ("the same way") or in terms of details of the event that affect the overall event ("rapidly").

name: Binding_principle
definition_en: This FE describes the Binding_principle which comes into effect.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner in which an action is performed.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the Event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Event occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time for which the Binding_principle is ongoing after it has come into effect.  'Curfew laws go into effect for the entire night.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result of the Event.

name: Initial_subevent
definition_en: The Initial_subevent of the Binding_principle.  'In the morning, the newly decided law came into effect as the Senate chambers opened. .'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that the specified type of Event begins.  'Parking restrictions on this street will come into effect at the beginning of every football season.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for why Event occurs.

name: Individuals
definition_en: The Individuals are self-movers who come together.

name: Configuration
definition_en: The Configuration describes the resulting formation of the individuals. 'The crowd gathered on the streets of Paris.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means descibes the way in which the Individuals accomplish the congregating.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the congregating occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the congregating occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Configuration plans to engage in upon assembly.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The position in a series of iterations that the current congregating event occupies .  'The group came together the first time in 1984.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Individuals come together to form an Configuration.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of congregating which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Individuals or Configuration that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Retired Sainsbury employees came together in grand style in March and April to reminisce and share afternoon tea in the sumptuous surroundings of the Royal Lancaster Hotel .'

name: Topic
definition_en: A Topic of a discussion that may occur between the Individuals.

name: Party_1
definition_en: Party_1 is the grammatically more prominent participant in the congregating event.  'Our group met with theirs in the plaza.'

name: Party_2
definition_en: A grammatically less prominent participant in the congregating event.  'Our group met with theirs in the plaza.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Entity
definition_en: Concrete or abstract entity that did not exist before the Time of the event.

name: Place
definition_en: This is the Place where the new Entity comes into being.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifes the Time when a new Entity comes into existence.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE labels the Explanation of the formation of the Entity. 'New clarity coalesced out of the hours spent simulating the climate.'

name: Components
definition_en: This FE identifies the components out of which the Entity forms. 'New plants form from cut veins in two weeks.'

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: This FE identifies the length of time that the Entity exists after coming to be.

name: Role
definition_en: The form in which the Entity comes to be. 'Vishnu materialized in the form of a half man, half beast.' 'The megacorps stranglehold on property emerged as a problem.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE identifies the Period_of_iterations during which habitual or iterative actions are performed.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Entity comes to be.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: Cognizer is the person who comes to believe something.   'Sue realized that Bob was lost.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: Words in this frame may occur with a PP headed by from which expresses the Evidence on which knowledge or belief is based:   'I have learned from experience that poison oak can be painful.'

name: Content
definition_en: With a target verb, the Content is usually expressed as a finite clausal Complement or an Object NP, and may sometimes be expressed by a PP:  'The President learned that the reporters were hungry.'  'The children determined the answer.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Some verbs in this frame may occur with postverbal Topic expressions: They found out about us! More generally verbs in this frame may occur with quantificational nouns followed by Topic expressions:   'The jury learned something terrible about the suspect.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The <fex name="">Degree to which the Cognizer comes to believe the Content.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Cognizer.  'We realized it eating dinner'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Cognizer which enables them to figure something out. 'A post-mortem examination was unable to ascertain the cause of death.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Cognizer discovers the Content.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the text created by the Cognizer to communicate that they came to believe a specified Content.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Cognizer realizes the Content.  'Back at the tailor's shop, I deduced that our murderer was not the owner of the kerchief.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: Cognizer is the person who comes up with or conceptualizes the Invention. It is normally expressed as an External Argument:   Kim devised a new recipe.

name: Idea
definition_en: Invention is the intellectual creation of the Cognizer. It is normally expressed as an NP Object, but sometimes as a PP Complement:   'Kim devised a new recipe. '  'Kim came up with a new recipe.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: Some of the words in this frame frequently occur with a constituent expressing the Purpose for which the Idea is intended. Normally this constituent is a PP Complement headed by for or a to-marked VP Complement:   'This car has been designed for quicker performance.' 'Kim created this plan to prevent a hostile takeover.'

name: Material
definition_en: Words in this frame sometimes occur with a constituent that expresses the intellectual material from which the Idea is created. This frame element is characteristic of physical creation verbs like make; its presence gives sentences in this frame an especially strong metaphorical quality. The Material FE is normally expressed by a PP Complement headed by from or out of:   'The composer created the symphony out of snippets of popular melodies.'

name: Amount_of_progress
definition_en: The extent to which the Cognizer succeeds in coming up with the idea.  'Before he could even half-way improvise a response, she moved on.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of a focal participant during the time the invention takes place. 'The Arvanids concocted a desperate plan to break the siege, unaware that the Ahurmids themselves were starving.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A state of the Cognizer that directly and palpably influences the overall action.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Cognizer that contributes to the creation of the Idea.

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Location_of_appearance
definition_en: (This FE belongs in Achieving_first, not here.)

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Cognizer comes up with the Idea.  'She had cooked up the story in Pisa, before she even left Italy.'  The following belongs in Achieving_first:  'Sandboarding was invented in Florianopolis, Brasil.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Idea is created.  'You had better hatch some plans before you get there.'  The following belongs in Achieving_first:  'Toilet paper was invented in 1857'

name: Honored_entity
definition_en: This FE identifies the person, subject, or event that is being honored.  'We have a picnic every year on Veterans' day.'

name: Dedicated_type
definition_en: This FE identifies the type of entity that had been dedicated to honor the Honored_entity.  'Is Armistice DAY a national holiday?'

name: Dedicated_entity
definition_en: The entity which has been dedicated to the Honored_entity.  'The Jimmy Hoffa Building hasn't opened yet.'

name: Buyer
definition_en: The Buyer wants the Goods and offers Money to a Seller in exchange for them. 'Jess bought a coat.' 'Lee bought a textbook from Abby.'

name: Goods
definition_en: The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction.  ' Only one winner purchased the paintings'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which a commercial transaction occurs. ' Will they allow you to purchase by check? '

name: Money
definition_en: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction. 'Sam bought the car for $12,000.'

name: Rate
definition_en: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. ' Jon bought some expensive apples at five dollars a pound! '

name: Seller
definition_en: The Seller has possession of the Goods and exchanges them for Money from a Buyer. 'Most of my audio equipment, I purchased from a department store near my apartment.'

name: Unit
definition_en: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by-PP.  'Lee buys potatoes by the pound. '

definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which an event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the purchasing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Buyer that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully). 'She gleefully bought the rock.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: The individual intended by the Buyer to receive the Goods. 'You bought me three pairs already!'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the commerce event began to be repeated to when it stopped. 'I have been buying from him for over 10 years.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The Buyer's intended purpose for the Goods. 'I purchased the calculatorfor easier calculation of my debts.'

name: Means

name: Rate

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.      'Worker 's compensation payments alone in cases involving falls , now average more than $8500 per incident in North America .'

name: Frequency

definition_en: Money is given in exchange for Goods in a transaction.  'The price of the sweater was  $50.'

name: Goods
definition_en: Goods is anything including labor or time, for example, which is exchanged for Money in a transaction.  'She was considered a purchaser of the finest things'

name: Rate
definition_en: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. ' The authorities cut tomato prices  to a dollar per pound. '

name: Unit
definition_en: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a 	by-PP.  'The price of Bob's peppers is determined by the pound.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs. 'It is efficient to engage in commerce by ship'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Purpose
definition_en: A state of affairs that the agent intends to bring about as a result of participating in the Commercial Transaction.

name: Buyer
definition_en: The Buyer has the Money and wants the Goods. 'Lee sold a textbook to Abby.'

name: Goods
definition_en: The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction.  'Kim sold the sweater.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which a commercial transaction occurs. 'Abby sold the car for cash.'

name: Money
definition_en: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction. 'Sam sold the car for $12,000.'

name: Rate
definition_en: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. ' The farmers' market sells apples  for one dollar a pound '

name: Seller
definition_en: The Seller has possession of the Goods and exchanges them for Money from a Buyer. 'So far, my company has sold more than three million copies.'

name: Unit
definition_en: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by-PP.  'Bob sells peppers by the pound. '

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which an event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the selling event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Seller that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully). 'Stuart reluctantly sold her his last rock.'

name: Result
definition_en: The state of the Seller after the sale has occurred. 'I sold the whole lot at a loss.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the commerce event began to be repeated to when it stopped. 'I have been selling materials to the factories for over 5 years.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The Buyer's intended purpose for the Goods. 'He sold the filing robot to me for filing all my legal documents.'

name: Back
definition_en: This FE indicates that the selling act reverses an earlier separate act in which the current Seller bought the Goods from the current Buyer.  ' There is a plan for Mercer to buy the ground and sell it back to the club for more money.'

name: Relay
definition_en: This FE indicates that the selling act constitues a re-selling by the current Seller of  Goods that they bought earlier from a third person who is not the Buyer of the current selling act.  'The Chambers villa has been sold on to a local construction company'

name: Buyer
definition_en: The Buyer wants the Goods and offers Money to a Seller in exchange for them.

name: Goods
definition_en: The FE Goods is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for Money in a transaction.

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs.

name: Money
definition_en: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction.

name: Rate
definition_en: Price or payment per unit of Goods.

name: Seller
definition_en: The Seller has possession of the Goods and exchanges them for Money from a Buyer.

name: Unit
definition_en: The Unit of measure of the Goods according to which the exchange value of the Goods (or services) is set. Generally, it occurs in a by-PP.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the person who commits him/herself to do something.  Speaker is usually the External Argument of predicative uses of the target or the Genitive modifier of a noun: Jo made a promise to me. Jo promised me she would cook dinner. Jo's promise to cook dinner came to nothing.

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Speaker's commitment can be made to an Addressee.  With those words which allow this frame element to be expressed, Addressee usually occurs as a PP Complement headed by to or the (Indirect) Object of verbs: Kim made a promise to me. Kim promised me that everything would be okay.

name: Message
definition_en: An expression of the commitment made by the Speaker expresses the frame element Message.  Message is expressed as a finite or non-finite clausal Complement or an NP Object: I swore that I would never make the same mistake again. The owner finally consented to sell the business. They threatened revenge.

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic expressions are not very frequent in this frame. They can occur with noun targets. Jo made endless promises about working harder at school.

name: Medium
definition_en: As with other frames in the Communication domain, the Medium of communication may be expressed. Medium is the physical entity or channel used to transmit the Message. Bob threatened the workers in Spanish.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the commitment is made.  '"I'll help you any way I can", he promised softly'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Speaker makes the commitment.  'The chancellor yesterday promised to increase defence spending in real terms next year.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Speaker makes the commitment.   'The july framework has reaffirmed what was promised at Doha.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by taking on the commitment.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE is used to indicate length of time from when Commitment event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Perpetrator
definition_en: The individual that commits a Crime.  'How can he commit treason against the King of England in a foreign country , if he is not English?'  'He perpetrated a crime against mother nature.'

name: Crime
definition_en: An act, generally intentional, that has been formally forbidden by law.  'How can he commit treason against the King of England in a foreign country , if he is not English?'  'He perpetrated a crime against mother nature.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The action that the Perpetrator was trying to accomplish in the Crime.  'People don't generally perpetrate a felony in order to go to jail.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Perpetrator that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'He committed each crime coldly and deliberately.'

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Perpetrator in order to accomplish the Crime.  'He perpetrated each heinous act by calculating what would do the most damage and then finding a patsy to do it.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Perpetrator is responding to in their Crime.  'Many of the poor commit petty crimes because they have no recourse.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the Crime was committed.  'A murder perpetrated at 1:08AM this morning was not investigated until noon today.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Crime occurs.  'We have jurisdiction over crimes committed in Woodside County.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument used in committing the crime. 'Most crimes are committed with a firearm.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The frequency with which a Crime is committed.  'The average serial killer commits a crime every five years.'

name: Entities
definition_en: This FE denotes the people in possession of the Commonality. This FE is usually genetive, the object of a postnominal PP, or null instantiated (INI), and null instantiaton often implies the public at large, as in "the common good".  'Their common enemy was Britain.'

name: Commonality
definition_en: This FE denotes an object or attribute which is jointly posessed by the Entities.  'Their shared parents were their only similarity.'

name: Entity_1
definition_en: One of the possesors of the Commonality. Can be singular or plural.  'He shares a home with us.'

name: Entity_2
definition_en: One of the possesors of the Commonality. Can be singular or plural.  'He shares a home with us.'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The individual that communicates the message concerning the Category of an Item.

name: Category
definition_en: The class of entities with characteristics that match those of the Item according to the portrayal of the Speaker.

name: Item
definition_en: The entity that the Speaker portrays as belonging to a Category.

name: Means
definition_en: An action taken by the Speaker through which they communicate that the Item fits into a particular Category.

name: Medium
definition_en: The piece of text in which a Speaker communicates their categorization of the Item.  'However, "A Brief History of Medicine" characterizes influenza as the most deadly plague, overall.'

name: Time
definition_en: The point in time at which the Speaker makes a characterization of the Item.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Speaker characterizes the Item

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the categorization is made.

name: Criteria
definition_en: The characteristics of an Item that fit the defining characteristics of a Category, and thus serve as the basis of the Speakers characterization of the Item .

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Speaker that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Communicator
definition_en: The sentient entity that uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to the Addressee.  'He finds it hard to communicate with people, not least his separated parents . '

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee receives a Message from the Communicator.  'The company must be able to communicate to potential customers the way in which its product would satisfy their needs, and provide competitive value. '

name: Message
definition_en: Message is a proposition or set of propositions that the Communicator wants the Addressee to believe or take for granted.  'How do you communicate to them that you really like them ?  '

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by "about", but in some cases it can appear as a direct object.   'Had someone communicated to the capital about the flagrant disregard of the religious law ? '

name: Medium
definition_en: The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.  'Opinions are usually communicated over the telephone and are often given within 24 hours. '

name: Amount_of_information
definition_en: The amount of information exchanged when communication occurs. 'He never really fully communicated his intentions.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Communicator communicates.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Communicator communicates.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the communication takes place.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration is the length of time during which the communication takes place.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE describes the number of times per unit of time that the Communicator conveys a Message.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the act of communication occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which a Communicator communicates.

name: Quote
definition_en: The Quote is the concrete record of a communication act.

name: Speaker
definition_en: Speaker is the sentient entity that produces a Message or communicates about a Topic. It is expressed as the External Argument of verbs:  'The boy mumbled an apology. '

name: Addressee
definition_en: Addressee is the person to whom the Speaker  is communicating.  When expressed, the Addressee occurs as a PP Complement:   'The taxi driver chattered away to me about gardening. '

name: Message
definition_en: Message is the content which is communicated by the Speaker. The Message may be a direct quote, a finite complement clause or an NP Object:  '"I- It was an accident," Jo stammered.' ' Jo stammered that it was an accident.' ' Jo stammered an apology. '

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic is the subject matter of the communicated Message.  It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by about and, in this frame, is frequently preceded by a quantificational noun which is treated as referring to the Message:  'The actor chattered about the difficulties of being famous.' 'The person next to me muttered something about pride coming before a fall. '

name: Medium
definition_en: This frame element expresses the medium of communication, such as the language used or the specific type of text in which the Message occurs. It is normally expressed as a PP-complement headed by on or in:  'The Beatles sang on the Ed Sullivan show.' 'The drunk man mumbled in French. '

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive is used for any phrase describing a participant in an action. 'Jo babbled in a tuxedo.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

name: Back
definition_en: This FE indicates that the communication act denoted by the target is in response to an earlier communication act in which the roles of Speaker and Addressee were reversed. This is conceptually akin to the Communication_response frame in which the targets themselves denote the responsive nature of the act.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that the communicative event lasts.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the communication event takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the communication event takes place.

name: Means
definition_en: The action that the Speaker performs in order to communicate in the particular way described by the target.  'She could only sing along by watching others singing.'

name: Communicator
definition_en: This FE is the person who uses the Means of communication to deliver the Message to the Addressee. The Speaker is normally expressed as the External Argument of target verbs, or as the Genitive modifier of  nouns. 'The President cabled his assistant to cancel all of his appointments.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: Addressee is the person to whom the Message is communicated. When this FE is expressed, it often appears in a prepositional phrase introduced by to, or as the direct object, or as the first object in a double object construction. 'The President cabled his assistant to cancel all other engagements.'

name: Message
definition_en: This FE identifies the content that the Communicator communicates to the Addressee. It can be expressed as a clause or as a noun phrase.

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It is typically expressed as a PP Complement headed by about.

name: Manner
definition_en: This Frame Element is for expressions that elaborate the manner in which an action is carried out.  'Jo faxed the document speedily. '

name: Means
definition_en: This Frame Element refers to the Instrument of Communication that is used by the Communicator (and Addressee). Each LU in this frame incorporates the Means frame element.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for using the means of communication. 'Pat phoned to talk about the party.' Note that this FE does not inheret from Intentional_act.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Communicator or Message during the communication. 'Worried about mail delays, Stephen faxed the agreement.' 'Since the general had died in the midst of writing them, the operator telegraphed Andrea's orders incomplete.'

name: Speaker
definition_en: Speaker is the sentient entity that delivers the Message.  'Kim whined that it wasn't fair.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee refers to the one toward whom the Communication_noise is directed.  Addressee generally occurs in to or at PPs.  'Kim whined to Jess that it wasn't fair.' 'Jess screamed at Kim to be quiet.'

name: Message
definition_en: Message has a number of different realizations in this frame, including that-clauses, direct quotes, infinitival complements, for-to phrases, and NP Objects. 'Kim whined that it wasn't fair.' '"Get moving!" Jess growled.' 'Jess growled at me to get moving.' 'Jess growled for me to get moving.' 'Jess growled an order.' Quoted Messages may either precede or follow the External Argument and verb, or may be discontinuous. '"Get moving!"Jess growled.' 'Jess growled angrily "Get moving!"' '"For goodness sake," Jess growled, "get moving!"'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic occurs in PP Complements, usually headed by about.  'Kim howled about the unfairness of it all.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is used for a physical entity or channel that transmits the Message. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by on or in.  'Pat screamed something in Spanish.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies the state of the Speaker during the communication.  '"Get outta here!" he barked unflinching.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner describes the manner or style in which the Communication_noise is delivered.  '"Huh!" he grunted disbelievingly.' '`"Long , dark hair" he murmured thoughtfully.'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The Communication_noise may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Speaker's mental or emotional state.  Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement.  'Kim growled at Tim in frustration.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Speaker communicates.

name: Voice
definition_en: The Voice describes the <fex name="">Speaker's utterance or other message-encoded production. 'John's voice bellowed for her to be quiet.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where an event occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Back
definition_en: This FE indicates that the communication act denoted by the target is in response to an earlier communication act in which the roles of Speaker and Addressee were reversed. This is conceptually akin to the Communication_response frame in which the targets themselves denote the responsive nature of the act.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time where the Communication noise event occurs.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the sentient entity that communicates the reply or response. It is expressed as the External Argument of predicative uses of a Target verb or as the Genitive modifier of a Target noun: 'Sue responded to the objection convincingly.' 'Sue gave a convincing response.' 'Sue's response was convincing.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: This is the person to whom the response is communicated.  When expressed, this FE occurs as the direct object of a Target verb, or in a prepositional phrase introduced by "to": 'Sue answered Bob immediately.' 'Sue responded to Bob immediately.'

name: Message
definition_en: The Message is the FE that identifies the content of what the Speaker is communicating to the Addressee. It can be expressed as a direct quote or a clause.'"I can't help you," Sue answered.''Sue replied that she couldn't help.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic occurs quite rarely in this frame and usually only as a PP Complement of a noun Target:'My boss still hasn't given me an answer about a promotion.'

name: Medium
definition_en: As with Medium in other Communication frames, the physical entity or channel used to communicate can be expressed, usually as a PP Complement headed by "on" or "in":'Sue responded to my question on the telephone.''Sue replied in writing.'

name: Trigger
definition_en: The Trigger is the prior communication or action to which a response is given. It can occur as an NP Object or a PP Complement.'Sue answered the question.''Sue responded to the questionnaire.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Speaker. 'Her husband responded to the police officer's query, smoldering.'

name: Means
