definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by the Speaker achieves the communication of the response Message .

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The response may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state.  Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement: 'Kim responded out of renewed hope.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Speaker  makes a verbal response.   'This was how Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Jayalalithaa responded in the Assembly on November 5, 2003.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which the Speaker makes their verbal response.  'A reminder letter was sent to all nonrespondents who had not replied after 28 days.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by making a verbal response.  ' We replied so as to shut you up and possibly, just possibly prevent this from happening again.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration of the communication response.  'He responded for five minutes before letting anyone else get a word in.'

name: Offender
definition_en: The individual who was convicted of a crime and given a sentence (the Original_punishment).  '  Some of the more interesting points to me include the description of Thomas More's original sentence before it was commuted to beheading' '  Some of the more interesting points to me include the description of Thomas More's original sentence before it was commuted to beheading'

name: Executive_authority
definition_en: The constitutionally specified authority who has the power to commute punishments.  'Hearst was sentenced to seven years in prison. 1979, President Jimmy Carter commuted Hearst's prison sentence after she served nearly two years. '

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Executive_authority  is responding to in commuting the Original_punishment.  ' His defence was a good one; but he was convicted and sentenced to death, commuted on account of his influence at court to having his sword broken over his head .'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Original_punishment  is commuted.  'Israel yesterday commuted the lengthy prison terms of seven Jews convicted of murdering or plotting to kill Arabs.'

name: Original_punishment
definition_en: The punishment the Offender was originally sentenced to.  'I had learned after all of this period of time has passed the court was about to let (Bush) pay a sum of money and commute her sentence to time served. '

name: New_punishment
definition_en: The new reduced form of punishment that the Executive_authority orders for the Offender.  'he bench comprising Justice Tariq Pervez and Justice Ijazul Hassan commuted his sentence to 10-year rigorous imprisonment.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the commutation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Executive_authority that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Executive_authority commutes the Original_punishment.

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Executive_authority that accomplishes the commutation.  'The governor may commute the sentence by committing the person who may benefit from programs offered at a youth correctional facility to the department of corrections until the youth is 18 years of age or until sooner placed or discharged.'

name: Term1
definition_en: The grammatically more prominent number involved in a commutative operation.

name: Term2
definition_en: The grammatically less prominent number involved in commutative operation.

name: Terms
definition_en: Two more or elements of a commutative arithmetic operation. This frame element may be represented as Term1 and Term2.

name: Calculator
definition_en: An entity that uses the arithmetic operation.

name: Result
definition_en: The number or role of a number that comes from the interaction of Term1 and Term2 via a commutative operation.

name: Term1
definition_en: The grammatically more prominent number involved in a commutative operation.

name: Term2
definition_en: The grammatically less prominent number involved in commutative operation.

name: Terms
definition_en: Two more or elements of a commutative arithmetic operation. This frame element may be represented as Term1 and Term2.

name: Item_1
definition_en: The Frame Element Item_1 marks the grammatically more prominent of the two entities, i.e.the subject in active clauses, when they are expressed separately.  'That technology turned out not to be compatible with the existing devices'

name: Item_2
definition_en: The Frame Element Item_2 marks the grammatically less prominent of the Items when they are expressed separately.  'My computer is not compatible with my new printer. '

name: Items
definition_en: This FE is used when the Items are expressed jointly in a phrase, either a plural or a coordinated NP.  'Your socks don't match.' ' Creationism and Evolutionary Theory  don't jibe.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This Frame Element is used for expressions that indicate the extent to which two Items are compatible. 'These devices are absolutely compatible.'

name: Parameter
definition_en: This Frame Element is used for expressions that indicate a Parameter or respect in which the Items are said to be compatible, not in conflict.  'The two applications are compatible in their essential features.'

name: Participant_1
definition_en: This FE identifies the first (or only) participant in a competition. 'Jo played the lottery every day.'

name: Participant_2
definition_en: This FE identifies the second participant in a competition. 'Jo played Leslie at tennis.'

name: Participants
definition_en: This FE is used for plural NP participants in a competition. 'Jo and Leslie played tennis.'

name: Competition
definition_en: This FE is used for the name of the competition. 'Jo played in the foosball tournament'

name: Score
definition_en: This FE is used for the score in a game. 'The Yankees won the game 2 to 0.' EX: The Yankees won the game by two points.

name: Rank
definition_en: This FE is used for the ranked results of a competition, and is translatable into a numerical value. 'Jo came in third.'

name: Prize
definition_en: This FE indicates a prize won in a competition. 'John was competing for a bronze medal.'

name: Venue
definition_en: This FE is for the named venue of a competition, particularly when the place has been built for the purpose of a competition. 'The Mets will play at the ball park on Sunday.' 'The Mets  will play at Shea Stadium tonight.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.  A constituent tagged as Place may require annotation on a secondary FE-layer.  'First layer: John's first competition  at Wimbledon astonished the crowd.' 'Second layer: John's first competition  at Wimbledon astonished the crowd.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way the Participants compete.

name: Means
definition_en: The action the Participants (or Participant_1) are involved in that constitutes a Competition.  'They played by seeing who could get the ball to the far side of the parking lot.'

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time when the Competition occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE is used to describe the length of time over which competition occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE is used to describe the intended outcome of the competition.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes the intensity of competition.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE expresses how often the Competition occurs.

name: Complainer
definition_en: The Complainer is the sentient entity that produces the Complaint (whether spoken or written).     'Peter has moaned about it on another thread but it sure must be nice for him to wallow again.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the person to whom the Complaint is communicated.   'Fresh out of prison, Martin whinged to Sonia about his life.'

name: Complaint
definition_en: The lamentable situation that the Complainer is communicating to the Addressee.    'One observer groused that Skagway was "little better than hell on earth."'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject matter to which the Complaint pertains.   'Ferdinand attended the reception at the city hall and complained vociferously about his reception at the city.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the complaining event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Complainer that affect the action (presumptuously, bitterly, vociferoursly ).   'The crowd complained vociferously when the other aldermen met Brewer?s proposal with silence.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: Frequency is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.    'Robert always complains to the neighbor whose children step on his flowers and ride bikes on his lawn.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Complainer makes a complaint.   'These people shouldn't be belly-aching about it by accusing the downfall of their candidate because it was all "whiteys" fault!'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotional or physical state of the Complainer that leads to their complaining.  ''Oooh,' he moaned in frustration.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Complainer to transmit the Complaint.   'I don't mean to discount any of what he has bitched about in his article, because most of his points are actually valid. '

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Complainer while making the Complaint.   'Pacing the floor at the American Club and getting increasingly drunk, he lamented, "I want to evacuate but my country won't let me leave." '

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the complaint is made.  'Now yesterday I pissed and moaned about Rolling Stone magazines choice for the number 1 song of all time. '

name: Place
definition_en: This FE specifies the location where the complaining takes place.   'Guest Relations actually refunded the full eighty-five dollar price of the event to many event attendees who complained at City Hall.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular complaining event referred to  is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.  'This is the third complaint of a similar nature filed by Naber against CN.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Occasion
definition_en: The Occasion is the reason a public statement is given.

name: Explanation
definition_en: Denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically followes. This often means that the Explanation causes the complaint, but not in all cases. In particular, there are cases when the connection is a bit weaker than normal for causation. In these instances,  cause is mediated by some actor responding in a complex way to the situation. Such cases are not paraphrasable in the language of direct causation.

name: Result
definition_en: An event or state which results from the complaining.

name: Degree
definition_en: An expression indicating a deviation of the actual level of completeness from the level indicated by the target.  'This course is very complete and addresses all aspects necessary to get a good understanding of hazardeous areas and the use of instrumentation. '

name: Whole
definition_en: The entity that is being assessed for having all its necessary parts or not.  'Our list of participants is still incomplete.'

name: Time
definition_en: The interval of time when the completeness of the entity is assessed.  'My journey to the dark side is now complete.'

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist's behavior is in or out of compliance with norms. 'Jo violated the no trespassing law.'

name: Act
definition_en: This FE identifies the Act that is judged to be in or out of compliance with the Norms.  'Jo's violation of the no trespassing law came as a surprise.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: A State_of_affairs may violate a law or rule. 'Their pricing policy violated inter-governmental agreements.'

name: Norm
definition_en: This FE identifies the rules or Norms that ought to guide a person's behavior.  'John violated the law by not paying taxes.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the compliance ocurrs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies any description of the Actor or Undergoer.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the compliance occurs. 'Jo complied with the law willingly.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the compliance is (or is not) accomplished. 'He complied with the decree by firing the employees.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of compliance.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time  when the act of compliance or non-compliance occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for complying with the Norm. 'He submitted to the will of the king because he had no other choice.'

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Conceded_state_of_affairs
definition_en: A proposition or set of propositions that the speaker wants the addressee to believe or take for granted. This statement is not asserted, but presupposed by the speaker of the sentence, and is mentioned to contrast with the Main_assertion. It would or could seem to predict a situation different than the Main_assertion, but, for reasons left implicit, this normal prediction is contradicted by the fact that the Main_assertion and the Conceded_state_of_affairs are both simultaneously true.

name: Topic
definition_en: An entity which metonymically stands in for an associated Statement.  'She got married in spite of him .' 'Despite her , they finished on time .'

name: Main_assertion
definition_en: The statement that the speaker wishes to assert or offer as their main contribution to the discourse, which is be modified or hedged in some way by the Conceded_state_of_affairs. The force of the contribution of the Main_assertion is presented as undiluted by the fact that something different from the Main_assertion would normally by predicted, based on the facts in the Conceded_state_of_affairs.

name: Patient
definition_en: The person who has a Medical_condition associated with Symptom.   'Premenopausal women often will present with atypical bleeding between typical menstrual cycles.'

name: Medical_condition
definition_en: A holistic description of the medical state of the Patient (or a part of the state of the Patient), which may or may not indicate the cause of a deviation from normal.

name: Symptom
definition_en: A deviation from normal function or feeling which is noticed by a Patient or physician, indicating the presence of a Medical_condition

name: Group
definition_en: Specific type of people in which a Medical_condition is normally found

name: Time
definition_en: When a Symptom or Medical_condition occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where a Medical_condition presents.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The commonality of a Medical_condition or Symptom

name: Extent
definition_en: The degree to which a Medical_condition is associated with a Symptom(s).

name: Explanation
definition_en: Explanation for why a Symptom(s) or Medical_condition(s) occur.

name: Influence
definition_en: Genetic, Biological, and Environmental Influences affect Medical_conditions

name: Profiled_possibility
definition_en: The situation presented explicitly as a possibility, contrasting with the implicit Negated_possibility.

name: Consequence
definition_en: The situation that follows from the Profiled_possibility.

name: Pragmatic_marker
definition_en: Pragmatically emphasizes a speaker's assumption of the truth of the Profiled_possibility for the conversation's duration. This FE does not occur for all LUs in the frame, and is closed-class, limited to the word 'always'.

name: Profiled_possibility
definition_en: The situation presented explicitly as a possibility, contrasting with the implicit Opposite_possibility.

name: Opposite_possibility
definition_en: The implicit situation that is mutually exclusive with the Profiled_possibility.

name: Consequence
definition_en: The situation that follows from the Profiled_possibility.

name: Anti_consequence
definition_en: The situation that follows as a result of the Opposite_possibility.

name: Agent
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that denote the person whose conduct is being evaluated.  'Douglas Hurd carried himself well '

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that characterize the way that the Agent behaves.  ' They stood together and posed for the pass, Alleyne relaxed and smiling , a tall , angular man who carried  himself with natural elegance .'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate a set of Circumstances under which the Agent acts in a particular way.  'But Garvey did not care what Gabriel believed , so long as he conducted  himself on stage like the Angel Gabriel .'

name: Affected_party
definition_en: A person to whom behavior is directed by the Agent.  'Smithers behaved himself shamefully towards me.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate why an Agent behaved in a certain way.  'People behave in the way they do because of their past learning experiences'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Agent behaves in a certain way.  ' She knew that she had behaved badly last night'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Agent exhibits their behavior.  'Sometimes an offender may be placed at a Probation hostel because they have committed a serious offence or have behaved badly at an independent hostel'

name: Means
definition_en: The way in which the Agent behaves in the specified manner.  'He behaved poorly by saying rude things.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain of human behavior in which the Agent acts in a certain Manner

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the (usually 'good' or 'bad') conduct of the Agent deviates from some standard or norm

name: Standard
definition_en: An explicit point to which the conduct of the Agent is compared.  'He carried himself admirably for a teenager.'

name: Benefactor
definition_en: The Benefactor is the person or thing that gives an advantage to the Beneficiary.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The Beneficiary is person or thing that receives an advantage from the Benefactor.

name: Beneficial_situation
definition_en: The Beneficial_situation is the item or action that is given to or done for the Beneficiary by the Benefactor.  A change of possession can, but does not have to occur.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Beneficiary gains an advantage from the Benefactor.

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain describes the type of advantage that is conferred.  'immigration BENEFITS' 'work BENEFITS'

name: Subset
definition_en: A Subset of beneficial situations is selected from the set of beneficial situations in a specific domain, though the domain need not be explicitly named.  'certain immigration BENEFITS' 'hardly any monetary BENEFITS' 'most BENEFITS'

name: Issue
definition_en: This FE identifies the Issue that the Agent deals with.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person who is acting to deal with the Issue.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the intentional act occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the reason why the Agent confronts the issue.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the way in which an Agent goes about facing the Issue.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain within which the Agent acts.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency with which the Agent does the Act in a given period of time.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result describes the resulting outcome of the confronting act.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Explanation
definition_en: Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE gives a description of the confronting event as a whole.

name: Part
definition_en: A  Part of a larger architectural unit, the  Whole.   'Could you open the door for me, please?'

name: Whole
definition_en: An architectural unit which includes the Part.   'The kitchen door came off its hinges'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A property relating to the  Part.   'People may give you weird looks as you struggle up the steps with your suitcase instead of using the slow escalator.'

name: Orientation
definition_en: This is a property of the  Part that situates  the  Part within the Whole.  'We can let you in through the  back door.'

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Part, including components, ingredients, etc.  'The house has an oak door'

name: Creator
definition_en: The Individual  who creates the Part.   'If a caprenter's door is shoddy, is it always his fault?'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is one of the Connected_locations treated as source.  'Does door from basement to living quarters have an adequate lock operated from living quarters side?'

name: Connected_locations
definition_en: Two or more named locations that are connected by the architectural  Part.  ' Security in the hallway between the jail and the Court Building needs to be improved.'

name: Direction
definition_en: The Direction is the direction or directions the Part of connecting architecture runs.  'Please take the <fex name="">east west stairs down to the lower floor'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is one of the Connected_locations treated as a goal  'Finally they corner us as we reach the escalator to the first floor.'

name: Connector
definition_en: Connector identifies the entity or substance that forms the bond that maintains the Item in a fixed position; it is usually expressed in a "with"-PP. 'The robber tied Harry to the chair with a rope.'

name: Connected_item
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity that is attached to the Connector in such a way as to stabilize their position or to immobilize them. 'The robber tied Harry 's bonds very tight.' 'Her rope was stuck between two rocks and she couldn't move far.'

name: Fixed_location
definition_en: This FE identifies the location to which the Connector is attached. 'The rope around his neck was like a noose, but it hung down as if it were a macabre necktie.'

name: Use
definition_en: The items that a Connector usually attaches or the type of activity the attaching is generally for. 'If the safety rope snaps, you're done for.'

name: Material
definition_en: Material identifies the material of which the Connector is made.  'Silk rope is surprisingly strong for its diameter.'

name: Type
definition_en: Type designates the type of Connector.  Often the Type labels part of a multi-word or compound word target.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to a Connector.  'Remove peg 3-B, if possible.'

name: Creator
definition_en: The individual or group that creates a Connector.  'I tried to find the DuPont adhesive , but they did n't have any .'

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which the Connector comes to be.  'The bolts of the 19th century had non-standardized thread widths.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Connector.

name: Conqueror
definition_en: The Conqueror is the entity that overtakes the Theme.  'The Achaemenid monarch Cambyses conquered Egypt in the year 525 BC'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the land, government, and its people that is seized by the Conqueror.  'Britain had an opportunity to conquer Europe.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes the intensity and extent of the conquering event.  'Britain had been ` completely conquered and immediately thrown away ''

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner in which the Conqueror takes over the Theme.  'He violently captured the castles of La Haye , Preuilly and Champigny'

name: Means
definition_en: The action by which the conquering event is made possible through the efforts of the Conqueror.  'They captured the haunted castle by bombarding it with low-energy x-rays.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Conqueror takes over the Theme.  'On Planet Earth, humans prefer to conquer those lands whose acquistion offers some economic benefit or advantage.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Conqueror seizes the Theme.  'China 's 1997 takeover would push over 10 per cent of the population out of the colony'.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason why the Conqueror seized the Theme.  'Rome initially conquered lands in order to enrich itself.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The tool used by the Conqueror to seize the Theme.  'The army will conquer the far-away lands with the most sophisticated weapons ever made.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Frequency
definition_en: Frequency is the number of times the Conquering event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: A region of space in contact with a Ground.

name: Ground
definition_en: An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Profiled_region.

name: Communicator
definition_en: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a message to another person.'He  wrote to John.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The physical or abstract setting in which the message is conveyed.'Opinions are usually called in over the telephone and are often given within 24 hours.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The person that receives the message from the Communicator.'The company must be able to call  potential customers.'

name: Address
definition_en: This FE is used for a (metaphorical) place in a system of communication where Communicators and Addressees can access the system. 'You can telephone your senator at 555-5555.'

name: Communication
definition_en: The information that the Communicator wishes to impart to the Addressee, often to get a particular response. In this frame the Communication is not necessarily received by the Addressee. 'Patients continually call in with questions.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for the Communicator contacting the Addressee. Often, this FE is used to identify a PP-for which indicates what the Communicator is attempting to obtain. 'Pat phoned to talk about the party.' 'For more information, call 1-EVANGELIST.'

name: Topic
definition_en: This is the subject matter to which the message pertains. It is typically expressed as a PP Complement headed by "about". 'Call John about the party.'

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: The location occupied by the Communicator.'Does anyone e-mail the office from a phone booth?'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the intentional act occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.

name: Intermediary
definition_en: The Intermediary is the person who facilitates the contact. ' We contacted her  through her employer  .'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive notes the state of one of the participants in the contacting event.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times a Communicator contacts the Addressee per unit of time.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the nature of the action (e.g. "the same way"), including especially internal states of the Communicator that also influence the way the action is carried out.

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Communicator that enables them to make contact.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the actor who instigates the filling.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the physical object or substance which changes location. 'Rev. Lovejoy carefully brushed the rolls with butter. '

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location where the Theme begins its motion. 'Josef filled his flask from the whiskey bottle.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is the trajectory of the motion.  'Jess filled the container through a small hole in the lid.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the area or container being filled. Goal is generally the NP Object in this frame.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the filling occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Agent of the filling action. 'Naked, Margeret filled the tub.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the filling occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the filling occurs.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result is the resultant state after the filling has occurred.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Agent fills or covers the Goal. 'Samantha covered the table with flowers because she was bored.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the filling occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the filling takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Agent fills the Goal. 'Samantha covered the table with flowers to please her mother.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which the filling occurs.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion is the smaller area of the Goal where the filling or covering occurs. 'Mrs. Bouvier anointed the children with oil on the forehead.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event which brings about the filling of the Goal.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the entity that does the emptying.  'Pat cleared the table of dishes.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme, when overtly expressed, invariably occurs in a PP Complement headed by "of". 'Pat cleared the table of dishes.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the region or container which is emptied of something.  In this frame, the Source occurs as an NP Object. 'Pat cleared the table.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal. 'Kim emptied the basin over the edge of the balcony.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is any expression which tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. 'The children emptied the toy box onto the floor.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Agent empties the Source.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depicitive phrase describing either the Agent or Theme of the emptying. 'Naked, Millhouse emptied the trash can.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Agent empties the Source.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Agent empties the Source.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of  the Agent emptying the Source.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This is the object with which the Agent empties the Source. 'I emptied the tub with a bucket.' 'I peeled the oranges with a knife.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is the non-sentient force which instigates the emptying. 'A basic washing can degrease your workclothes.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the emptying takes place.  'Don't eviscerate him in the house!'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the emptying takes place.  'The prisoners were deloused in June and August.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Container
definition_en: Container is an object which is conventionally used as a container.  Target words in this frame are tagged with this frame element.  'John carried a bucket.'

name: Contents
definition_en: Contents is the object(s)/stuff contained in the Container.

name: Material
definition_en: Material identifies the material of which the Container is made.  'straw basket'

name: Type
definition_en: Type designates the type of Container.  Often the Type labels part of a multi-word or compound word target.  'Erlenmeyer flask' 'TABLESPOON'

name: Relative_location
definition_en: Relative_location is the location of the Container.  'The wallet in his pocket was full of photos of his family.'

name: Construction
definition_en: Construction indicates the action (or causer) which creates the Container.  'fired urns.'

name: Owner
definition_en: Owner identifies the owner of the Container.  'Chuck's suitcase'

name: Use
definition_en: Use identifies the purpose for which an artifact is constructed and the activity with which it is associated, or the Contents protypically contained in the Container. 'watering can' 'wine  glass'

name: Part
definition_en: This FE identifies a Part of the Container.  'screw top bottle'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor describes some aspect of the Container.  'He put everything into a really really huge briefcase'

name: Container
definition_en: The Container is the physical object which holds within its boundaries the Contents  'The box holds three hundred pictures.'

name: Contents
definition_en: The Contents is the substance or objects contained within the physical bounds of the Container. 'The box holds three hundred pictures.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Container holds the Contents.

name: Container
definition_en: The non-point-like entity which has a Boundary which (largely or completely) separates the Interior region from the Exterior region.  It normally also has a Portal which links the Interior and Exterior regions.

name: Interior
definition_en: The (finite) region which is inside the Boundary of the Container, disjoint from the Exterior, and overall closer or included in the Container.

name: Portal
definition_en: A (relatively small) region which goes through the Boundary, connecting the Interior and Exterior of the Container.

name: Contents
definition_en: Thing or substance located within the Container.

name: Time
definition_en: The period or moment in which the Contents occupy the Interior of the Container.

name: Outcome
definition_en: An open question that is (to some degree) predictable from the Determinant.

name: Determinant
definition_en: An open question that determines the Outcome.  'Price, in such a case, depends only on the whim of the supplier.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount of predictive power supplied by the Determinant with respect to the Outcome.  'His decision was somewhat dependent on who won the game'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The conditions under which the Determinant dictates the Outcome.  Oftentimes it is expressed in a fashion similar to Time and Place in other frames, but such cases are actually metonymic for the prevailing conditions of the Time and/or Place.  'In London, how long it took to cross the city depended on how many state dinners were being served that night.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: A state which holds prior to and up through the Reference_occasion.  'How is your course going so far?'

name: Reference_occasion
definition_en: The time or event (normally speech time) with respect to which the State_of_affairs is located.  'She was loving and concerned about others up to her dying breath.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Event
definition_en: The Event that occurs despite an Adversity that would seem to contradict the possibility of its occurence.

name: Adversity
definition_en: The Adversity is a state of affairs or entity that hinders or negatively affects the Event.

name: Contrary_circumstances
definition_en: The Contrary_circumstances are the circumstances that would normally be expected to occur given the presence of the Adversity.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The FE Experiencer indicates the person who experiences the emotion about their prior action.  'Smithers was contrite about his wrongdoings.'

name: Action
definition_en: The FE Action marks expressions that indicate a prior action that the Experiencer has come to feel bad about.  'They confessed and repented their actions against the Soviet Union.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The FE Degree marks expressions that indicate how badly the Experiencer feels about their prior action.  'Smithers was very contrite.'

name: Expressor
definition_en: The FE Expressor marks expressions that indicate a gesture or body part which is displaying the Emotional_state of the Experiencer.  'Repentant tears welled to his eyes.'

name: Authenticity
definition_en: The FE Authenticity marks expressions that indicate whether the Experiencer genuinely feels contrite or just acts as if they did.  'The defendant showed no real remorse.'

name: Emotional_state
definition_en: The FE Emotional_state is modified by an adjective  that indicates the Experiencer is contrite.  'Martha had a guilty conscience after selling inferior merchandise.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Experiencer or the Expressor is contrite.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Experiencer or Expressor has contrition.

name: Controlling_entity
definition_en: A thing or person whose behavior controls a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.

name: Dependent_entity
definition_en: An entity, usually a thing, that is influenced in its behavior by a Controlling_entity or an Controlling_situation.

name: Controlling_variable
definition_en: A scalar variable (with unspecified value) which has an effect on the Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.

name: Dependent_situation
definition_en: A situation whose temporal or other characteristics are influenced by a Controlling_entity, Controlling_situation, or Controlling_variable.

name: Dependent_variable
definition_en: A scalar variable, whose value depends on the behavior of a Controlling_entity, a Controlling_situation, or a Controlling_variable.   'Move the slider on the SpeedBar while playing audio or video material to control playback speed.'

name: Controlling_situation
definition_en: A situation whose temporal or other characteristics control a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Controlling element affects the Dependent element.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the controlling occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the controlling occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Influencing_entity that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Control
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity or substance that is designed to have a particular Use. This is often an incorporated FE.

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which an control is intended. 'knob for volume control.'

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Control into existence.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which an Control comes into existence.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to an Control.

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Artifact.  'Flip the three-way switch.'

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Control, including components, ingredients, etc.

name: Controlled_entity
definition_en: The entity which the Control controls. 'The radio knob was broken.'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to another person.   'Juhl emphasized the importance of UPMC System investments, stating that their contribution to the school's funds had tripled in recent years.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the audience to which the Speaker communicates the Message.  'Pastor Host emphasized to him that as you study a passage, a theme develops from the text.'

name: Message
definition_en: The proposition whose denotation the Speaker presents as important.  'He emphasized to me that my words will go down in history and that this poem has made a difference in our world.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.   'The report emphasized that Iraq's unwillingness to cooperate represents a serious problem for the progress of this work.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs,  in particular secondary effects (loudly), general descriptions comparing events (the same way), and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).    'You will note above that I have deliberately stressed our ability as mental health professional to make a determination of current suicide risk.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Speaker communicates the importance of the state of affairs denoted by the Message.  'Mr. Rose stressed this by pointing out that the latest offender had been fined over $5000.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Speaker communicates a Message.   'However, Cockerill stressed last week that he had had many meetings about these obvious synergies and that he had pursued these aggressively.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times the Speaker conveys a Message whose denotation they present as an important fact to be aware of.  'During Chen's telephone call with Soong, Hsieh said at a press conference, Soong emphasized multiple times his commitment to the 10-point consensus.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree of importance that the Speaker conveys the Message's denotation as having.  'The need to understand design is often heavily stressed during conversations or articles about desktop publishing .'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Speaker delivers the Message.  'Putin stressed in Beijing that Russia does not favor independence for Taiwan.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE is minimally distinct from Duration and Duration_of final_state in that the clause described is conveyed to be iterative. Period_of_iterations can co-occur with either the peripheral FE Duration or the extra-thematic FE Duration_of_final_state (although these cannot occur together).

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Vehicles
definition_en: The constituent vehicles that make up the Convoy.  'Trained gunmen hijacked a 20-car convoy headed for the city.'

name: Convoy
definition_en: The group of vehicles transporting the Cargo.  'The southbound convoy of two vans and several armored vehicles arrived safely 10 hours after it had departed.'

name: Aggregate_property
definition_en: This FE describes a property of the Convoy rather than the Vehicles and is used to tag the adjective that modifies the aggregate noun when it is unambiguous.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to the Convoy.

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant Domain as it pertains to the Convoy.

name: Possessor
definition_en: The Possessor of the Convoy. Often a nation or organization that wants the Cargo transported.  'Recent attacks on NATO convoys have not helped the ongoing peace talks.'

name: Cargo
definition_en: The Cargo are the goods and/or individuals transported by the Convoy. This FE also covers the intended use of the transported goods.  'Trained gunmen hijacked a medical supply convoy headed for the city.'  'Aid convoys traveled through the city, mostly unharmed.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the beginning of the path along which the Convoy travels.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path along which the Convoy travels.

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the endpoint of path along which the Convoy travels.

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction in which the Convoy travels.  'All northbound convoys are to be redirected.'

name: Support
definition_en: People and possibly other elements of the convoy who support and defend the transport of the Cargo are the Support. In military contexts, this typically consists of soldiers and military vehicles who provide defense for the conveying Vehicles and Cargo.  'A military convoy of rebel gunmen stood between us and a large cache of weapons.'

name: Place
definition_en: The general Place where the Convoy is operating.  'Convoys in Afghanistan have been hardest hit.'

name: Cook
definition_en: The Cook  prepares the Produced_food. 'Drew cooked dinner for his friends.' 'Drew baked an apple pie.'

name: Produced_food
definition_en: The Produced_food is the result of a Cook's efforts. 'Drew prepared dinner for his friends.' 'Drew baked an apple pie for dessert.'

name: Heating_instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Heating_Instrument  with which the Cook prepares the Food. 'Drew  prepared vegetable soup in a crock pot.'

name: Container
definition_en: This FE identifes the Container that holds the food being produced. 'Bake the quiche in a pie tin.'  Things that apply the heat directly are Heating_Instruments, e.g. crock-pot,  electric griddle.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the cooking creation occurs.  'Drew prepared the soup  in the kitchen.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the cooking creation is performed. 'Drew prepared the soup  by throwing some vegetables into a pot of water.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the  Purpose for which the cooking creation is performed.  'Drew baked an apple pie to show Patty he was sorry.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: Recipient identifies the person for whom the food has been prepared.  'Drew baked an apple pie for Patty.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the cooking creation occurs. 'Drew baked an apple pie at six int he morning.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the cooking creation performed.  'Drew prepared dinner hastily.'

name: Ingredients
definition_en: This FE identifies the Ingredients which are altered by the Cook to create the Produced_food. 'Drew baked a pie with apples, nuts, and raisins.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

name: Means
definition_en: The action that is taken that results in punishement/reward. 'The emperor flogged her by taking one of the stays to her.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. 'John caned the criminal to set an example.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Evaluee
definition_en: Evaluee is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment is made. With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object:  'You will be flogged for your actions.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Reason
definition_en: Typically, there is a constituent expressing the Reason for the Judge's judgment. It is usually a for-PP, e.g.  'The Sheriff flogged him for his crimes.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Body_part
definition_en: This FE is the location on the body where the bodily injury takes place.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Severity
definition_en: This frame element marks a quantity related to the seriousness of the punished behavior. 'Mr. Devine could face up to 300 lashes for the offense.'

name: Information
definition_en: The Information matches or does not match the facts of the world.  'That statement is totally incorrect.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Information matches or does not match the facts of the world.  'Vague prophecies, interpreted with maximum latitude, are likely to appear at least somewhat accurate.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The aspect of reality which is accurately modeled by the Information.  'That claim may be factually accurate in terms of in vitro pharmacology but that may have no clinical relevance.'

name: Parameter
definition_en: The aspect of the Information which accurately models reality.  'Don't select an option just because it contains factually correct information about the clinical situation.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Information is correct.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the agent who holds the correct/incorrect information.   'He is correct'

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame, which typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Source is correct/incorrect.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Information or the Source is correct.

name: Medium
definition_en: The physcial context that the Information is found in.

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: Result
definition_en: The outcome of the correctness if the Source or Information.

name: Communicative_act
definition_en: The event which communicates the Information.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic about which the Source has accurate information.

name: Initial_state
definition_en: Initial_state is the original state of the Patient. 'The bikes RUSTED from their former beauty.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifes the Duration of time for which  the Patient corrodes.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Patient corrodes.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which  the Patient corrodes.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the change of phase. 'The metal corroded  into a mass of slime  . '

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Patient corrodes.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient undergoes a change.  'The bikes rusted from their former beauty.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Patient corrodes.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected. 'The metal  rusted around the edges .'

name: Speed
definition_en: This FE identifies the Speed at which  the Patient corrodes.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cause corrodes the Patient.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of  time for which the Cause corrodes the Patient.

name: Initial_state
definition_en: This FE identifies the Initial_state of the Patient. 'Acid rain corroded the metal from its former shininess.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Cause corrodes the Patient.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which the Patient is corroded.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the caused corrosion. 'The metal was corroded into a mass of slime.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Cause corrodes the Patient.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient  is corroded by the Cause. 'The metal was corroded by the water.'

name: Speed
definition_en: This FE identifies the Speed at which the Cause corrodes the Patient.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion identifies the part of a larger whole that is affected. 'Acid rain corroded the metal around the edges.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cause corrodes the Patient.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Cause corrodes the Patient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Patient is corroded.

name: Cause
definition_en: Cause identifies an animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that corrodes the Patient. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Cause.  'Acid rain corroded the metal.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that corrodes the Patient.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Agent may use an Instrument to cause the corrosion.

name: Theme
definition_en: This is the entity, frequently a living being, which moves in relation to the Cotheme. Normally the Theme frame element is expressed as an external argument.  'Pat accompanied me for five miles in a blue Toyota.'' The squirrel chased the nut across the road.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: This frame element is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique:   'Pat accompanied  me down the street.'  'The squirrel chased  after the nut . '

name: Source
definition_en: Source marks any expression which implies a definite starting-point of the motion of the Cotheme. In prepositional phrases, the  object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.  'The cat chased the mouse out of the house.'  'The cat chased the mouse out.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path marks phrases that describe the Theme and Cotheme's trajectory of motion and which are neither expressions of the  Source nor the Goal of motion. The notion Path also includes directional expressions. ' The bikers followed the truck west.'  'The bikers followed the truck through the desert. '

name: Goal
definition_en: Any expression which tells where the Cotheme ends up as a result of the motion expresses the frame element Goal. Note that if the Cotheme is animate, the Theme need not also end up in the same place. Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance.  'The children chased the ball into the park. (The children end up in the park.)' 'The children chased the dog into the park.  (The dog ends up in the park; the children may not have entered the park.) '

name: Manner
definition_en: Phrases marked with this frame element  describe a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Theme's motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.   'The bikers followed the truck furiously. '

name: Distance
definition_en: Any expression which characterizes the extent of the motion of the Theme and Cotheme expresses the frame element Distance.  'The police tailed the suspects for several miles. '

name: Area
definition_en: Area marks expressions which describe a general area in which the motion of Theme and Cotheme takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Locative setting adjuncts of motion expressions may also be assigned this frame element. 'The police followed the suspects all around town. '

name: Depictive
definition_en: This frame element marks a depictive phrase describing the Theme.  'John escorted his mother around naked'

name: Event
definition_en: An Event in which the Cotheme is involved. Usually this is some kind of travel.  'Paul Simon accompanied the President on his trip to Japan'

name: Means
definition_en: This frame element expresses the Means by which a (volitional) Theme moves in relation to the Cotheme. 'The policemen chased the suspect by running after him.'

name: Result
definition_en: Phrases marked with this frame element mark resultant states that the Cotheme can reach due to the motion event.'The dogs hounded their prey to death.'

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: This frame element denotes the means of conveyance on which the Theme is traveling. The Mode_of_Transportation can be the Theme's  own body or a vehicle. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium.  'The husband accompanied his wife to the hospital in the ambulance'  'Lily accompanied me to the store on foot'

name: Speed
definition_en: Phrases that describe the rate of motion of the Theme are marked Speed. 'The detective followed the suspect at a leisurely pace.'

name: Road
definition_en: Phrases that denote a physical path on which the motion of Theme and Cotheme takes place are marked Road.'The police followed the suspect on the interstate for several miles.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which motion occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the motion occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which a Theme moves. 'John stalked her every day to relieve his obsessions.'

name: Following_distance
definition_en: The Following_distance is the distance between the Theme and Cotheme. 'I followed him at a distance of 30 yards.'

name: Handle
definition_en: The Handle is active zone of the Cotheme. 'Mark led Sara by the hand.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location which provides a setting for a defined motion (that is one with Source, Path or Goal).

name: Explanation
definition_en: Some event or state of affairs that leads to the Theme following the Cotheme.

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction in which the Theme and Cotheme move.  'The tracking dogs chased their target towards the river, where they lost it.'

name: Victim
definition_en: This FE is the being or entity that is injured by the Assailant's attack.  'US troopscounterattacked the French the next day.'

name: Weapon
definition_en: An entity used by the Assailant to cause damage to the Victim.  'The mysterious fighter counterattacked with a sabre.'

name: Assailant
definition_en: The person (or other self-directed entity) that is responding to a prior attack by attempting physical harm to the Victim.  'The mysterious fighter counterattacked the guardsmen with a sabre.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Assailant that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Assailant that accomplishes the assault.   'Japanese counterattacked by invading coastal fortifications.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Assailant makes an assault on the Victim.  'Then they staged a counterattackon our left flank.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Assailant attacks the Victim.  'Hostile troops probably launched a counteroffensive to try to intimidate us.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Assailant is responding to that leads them to make an assault on the Victim.  'We counterattack because if we don't, we'll be an easier target next time.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Assailant attacks the Victim.  'The previous day's counterattack on French troops was deemed a success.'

name: Source
definition_en: The starting-point of the motion of the Assailant or projectiles of the Assailant as they move toward the the Place that the Victim is occupying in the attack.  In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion.  With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.  'We'll counterattack from our current position.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describeing the state of the Assailant or Victim while the Attack occurs.  'They counterattacked us in large numbers.'

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re-encoding, but not necessarily.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the attack on the Victim by the Assailant.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held. Examples include once, twice, [Cardinal expression] + times, a lot.

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Assailant travels.

name: Questioner
definition_en: The individual who asks a Witness questions.

name: Witness
definition_en: A person who is present in a courtroom in order to give some form of evidence, has been sworn in, and is being examined by a Questioner. 'You have leave to examine the witness.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The subject matter to which the examination pertains.

name: Time
definition_en: When the examination occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the examination takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Questioner examines the Witness. 'The defense attorneys cross-examined the prosecution's witnesses harshly.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose of the examination. 'The defense examined their own client in order to show the jury her compassionate side.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Questioner examines the Witness. 'Many attorneys cross-examine witnesses by asking misleading and often confrontational questions.'

name: Duration
definition_en: How long the examination takes place. 'The gruelling two-hour cross-examination revealed much new information regarding the murder.'

name: Activity
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the  Activity that is being performed habitually or conventionally.  ' Restrop was built at the very height of the great Elizabethan age, when the craft of building began to turn into an art.'

name: Practitioner
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate whose Activity is at issue.  'The development and the elaboration of metal armour for protection in warfare and jousting gave considerable impetus to the craft of the blacksmith'

name: Place
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the Place in which the Activity is performed.  'So, by application of the sacred northern art of fettling, here are a few tips on how to provide your steed with an almost Zen-like ride quality'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate attributes, traits, or evaluations of the Activity.  'Once upon a time people indulged in the ages-old craft of telling stories to each other'

name: Culture
definition_en: A Culture within which the Activity is performed.  'Origami is an ancient Japanese craft of paper folding'

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Representation into existence.  'Supposedly, the artist drew the picture from memory.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which a Representation is created.   'My brother took this picture in France almost 10 years ago, and has recently scanned it in.'

name: Representation
definition_en: The entity that is created to represent either iconically or abstractly.  'Most of us know where we took a photo but have a harder time remembering the time we took it.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Creator that also affect the action (deliberately, carefully).

name: Role
definition_en: This FE identifies a Role that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills in a background context, either generically or in some specific instance.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes the Creator as being in some state during the creation of the Representation.

name: Location_of_representation
definition_en: The physical location that holds the Representation.    'I drew him on a sheet of paper first.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Creator intends to accomplish by creating the Representation.   'Masha also took the picture to prove that you can find an Internet Cafe even here in Murmansk.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Creator produces the Representation.   'I took this picture in Italy a couple of weeks ago.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the creation of the Representation ogically follows.   'Well, I painted the picture because the quarry was visually exciting.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The entity which the Creator uses to create the work of art.

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Creator which brings about the creation of the Representation.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Creator or the Representation.

name: Reference
definition_en: A representation of the entity depicted which the Creator uses as a reference in the creation of the Representation. For instance, another piece of art, a photograph, or his/her memory.  'She sculpted this dragon from a painting of mine.'

name: Representation
definition_en: The entity produced by the Creator to evoke in an audience the idea of the Represented.   'The bell became famous after being painted by Jamie Wyeth in his painting Bronze Age.'

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Representation into existence.  'Since Frans photographed them ten years ago the population has increased.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which a Representation is created.

name: Represented
definition_en: The entity--which may be a thing, an action or a state--that is represented by the Representation.  'When Nadar photographed her, Desbordes-Valmore was sixty-eight.'

name: Depictive_of_represented
definition_en: A characterization of the state in which the Represented entity is presented.    'He carved St. Francis tumbling around, and St. Thomas banging his fist on a table.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Creator that also affect the action (deliberately, carefully).   'She set up her plywood on saw horses and carefully drew her mother.'

name: Role
definition_en: This FE identifies a Role that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills in a background context, either generically or in some specific instance.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes the Creator as being in some state during the creation of the Representation.   'As a young man he painted Philip IV as a fashionable equestrian.'

name: Material
definition_en: The physical Material that is used in the production of the Representation.    'I drew him on a sheet of paper first.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Creator intends to accomplish by creating the Representation.  'He also photographed them in order to form a composite girl for one end of the bench and a composite boy for the other end.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the artist produces the representation.  'I drew him at work a bunch of times, mainly for the amusement of the staff.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The entity used by the Creator to make a Representation of the Represented entity.

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Creator that allows them to make a Representation of the Represented entity.

name: Iterations
definition_en: Iterations is the number of times the Creator creates the representation.

name: Reference
definition_en: A representation of the Represented which the Creator uses as a reference in the creation of the artwork. For instance, another piece of art, a photograph, or his/her memory.  'She painted the portrait from a series of photographs.'

name: Components
definition_en: This FE identifies the Components that are attached together to form a Created_entity. 'The force of the rock above formed diamond out of the carbon.'

name: Created_entity
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity that the Agent intentionally creates. 'They were assembling grenades for export.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action. We wandered around naked. Cicadas screech unseen from within.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a Creator intentionally creates a new entity.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which a Creator intentionally creates a new entity.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place ehere the Agent intentionally creates the new entity.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifes the Time when an Agent intentionally creates a new entity.

name: Cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the instrument with which an Agent intentionally creates a Created_entitiy.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: A secondary agent with whom the Creator intentionally creates the Created_entity.

name: Creator
definition_en: The Creator creates a created entity.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Creator intentionally creates a new entity.

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The Creator's intended purpose for the Created_entity.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The Beneficiary benefits in some way from the creation of the Created_entity.

name: Role
definition_en: The Role that the Created_entity takes (or is intended to take, if there is a Creator).

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The individual who is intended to receive the Created_entity.  'She made me this hammock.'

name: Suspect
definition_en: The individual which is under suspicion of having committed the Crime.

name: Perpetrator
definition_en: The individual that commits a Crime.

name: Crime
definition_en: An act, generally intentional, that matches the description that belongs to an official Charge.

name: Charge
definition_en: A description of a type of act that is not permissable according to the law of society.

name: Authorities
definition_en: The group which is responsible for the maintenance of law and order, and as such have been given the power to investigate Crimes, find Suspects and determine if a Suspect should be submitted to the Criminal_process.

name: Investigator
definition_en: The Investigator is the person or agency that investigates the Suspect of a crime (Incident).

name: Incident
definition_en: The Investigator attempts to determine the exact circumstances surrounding the Incident, which is typically a criminal act (murder, robbery) or the result of such an act (death, loss of money).

name: Time
definition_en: When the Investigator investigates the Incident. 'Our guys are currently investigating her disappearance.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of the investigation. 'The police carried out a two-year investigation into terrorist kidnappings.'

name: Suspect
definition_en: This FE denotes the Suspect that is investigated by the Investigator. 'The police are investigating Dr. Phil.'

name: Court
definition_en: This FE identifies the Court involved in a trial.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

name: Defendant
definition_en: The Defendant is charged with an Offense.

name: Judge
definition_en: The Judge heads the Court where arraignment occurs and the case is tried.

name: Prosecution
definition_en: This FE identifies the attorney(s) prosecuting the Defendant.

name: Charges
definition_en: This FE identifies the Charges brought against the Defendant.

name: Defense
definition_en: The Defense represents the interests of the Defendant.

name: Jury
definition_en: This FE identifies the people who are charged by the Court to listen to the testimony, evidence, and arguments, and come to a consensus about the guilt or innocence of the Defendant.

name: Offense
definition_en: This FE identifies the Offense which the Defendant is accused of committing.

name: Authorities
definition_en: The Authorities charge the Suspect with commiting a crime, and take him/her into custody.

name: Suspect
definition_en: The Suspect is taken into custody by the Authorities, under suspicion of having committed a crime.

name: Witness
definition_en: A person who is present in a courtroom in order to give some form of evidence, has been sworn in, and is being examined by the Prosecution or Defense.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is the person (or other sentient being or group) that has in some way been harmed or wronged by the Defendant.

name: Healer
definition_en: The  Healer, anyone who treats or cures the Patient, occurs as the External Argument of verbs: 'Doctors alleviated his suffering. '

name: Patient
definition_en: This   is the sufferer of the injury, disease or pain and can occur as an NP Object in this frame. However, Patient may not be expressed as a separate Frame Element but frequently occurs as the possessor of the Affliction, an example of  FE Conflation:  (See section on Conflation.)   'Acupuncture cured Pat of his depression.' 'Acupunture cured Pat's depression.' The Patient may therefore not be tagged in a sentence although explicitly identified.

name: Affliction
definition_en: The Frame Element Affliction is generally the NP Object of a verb, frequently incorporating the Patient as a possessor, as described above:  'This potion heals a broken heart.' 'The potion healed Kim's broken heart. '

name: Treatment
definition_en: The FE Treatment is used for treatments and means, distinguished by separate FEs in FN-1.  'He emphasized treatment by surgical means. ' 'He will undergo radiation treatment.
