'  A  method used to treat the Affliction can be the External Argument of these verbs, or expressed in a  PP Complement:  'These herbs can cure insomnia.' 'Insomnia can be cured with herbs. '  Target nouns (e.g. therapy, treatment, etc.) will NOT be tagged with this FE.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Medication
definition_en: The injested, applied, injected, etc. substance designed to cure the Patient. 'He needs prolonged treatment with anibiotics. '                              Note the tight relationship between Treatment and Medicine.

name: Reciprocation
definition_en: The Reason for which an intentional act is performed. 'We treated the pigeon for the hell of it.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. 'John resuscitated her to receive a raise.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Body_part
definition_en: The Body_part is the specific area of the Patient's body which is treated.

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time that the Patient recieves the Treatment. 'The sailor was treated for venereal disease  for three months.'

name: Behavior
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the entrenched Behavior.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate whose entrenched Behavior is at issue.  ' His custom was to come here for the 10 o'clock service. '

name: Domain
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the area of human experience to which the Behavior belongs.  ' Witali tried to understand their religious customs. '

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate attributes, traits, or evaluations of the entrenched Behavior.  'In the year 2100, a historian will undertake a study of that  quaint custom of preserving public footpaths across private land .'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate a region where the Behavior is  entrenched.  'They found that a loca custom in the country was to walk around barefoot at all times of the year and in all weathers .'

name: Society
definition_en: 'We can help , you to meet Egyptian people and learn about  Egyptian customs.  '

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person cutting the Item into Pieces.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which the Item is being cut into Pieces.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the slicing takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Item is being sliced into Pieces.

name: Time
definition_en: When the slicing occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Agent that accomplishes the slicing. 'I sliced the cucumber in 1/8th inch slices by marking intervals with a ruler.'

name: Item
definition_en: The item which is being cut into Pieces. 'People back then had to chop firewood all day long.'

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the Item being sliced into Pieces.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner in which the Item is being cut into Pieces.

name: Pieces
definition_en: The Pieces are the parts of the original Item which are the result of the slicing.

name: Entity
definition_en: Concrete or abstract entity that did not exist, then came into existence, then (potentially) ceased to exist.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: Protagonist identifies the being or entity that is dead or alive. 'Frank was dead.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the damage to the Patient.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Patient is damaged. ''

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with a Patient to accomplish the damage.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the action of damaging which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the damage.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the location of the scene where a Agent damages a Patient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent causes the damage to the Patient. 'The dock workers keyed their manager's car to protest their working conditions.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action. 'He rent his garment out of the despair that only biblical character can feel.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the Patient which is directly affected by the damaging. 'The dog tore his pants just below the seat.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent damages the Patient.

name: Patient
definition_en: The entity which is affected by the Agent so that it is damaged. ''

name: Character_of_end_state
definition_en: A description of the state of the Patient after the damaging has taken place, including descriptions of the severity and the permanence of the damaged condition.  'To a all appearances, she had permanently damaged her right clavicle.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result of the Agent's action.  'She tore the sugar packet open'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event which leads to the damage of the Patient.  'The crash dented my car pretty bad.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that performs the Action, resulting in danger to themself.  'I do n't think you should hazard the ascent in the dark , that 's all .'

name: Action
definition_en: This FE denotes the Action taken by the Agent.  'I chanced a peek at myself.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Action is performed. 'He risked a look back to check for pursuit.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation the Agent takes the risk. 'She risked a disguise since they already had a photo of her.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Agent dares to perform the Action.  'At dawn, the Captain chanced opening the hatch.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent risks doing the Action.  'Back in his room, he risked peeking inside.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the risking action which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'If you carelessly chance going back there, you deserve what you get.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: Explanation identifies any object or event that brings about the death of the Protagonist.  'Within hours, Frank was dead of exposure.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which a Protagonist is dead or alive.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: Protagonist identifies the being or entity that is  dead or alive. 'Frank was dead.'

name: Figure
definition_en: This FE identifies the Figure or form being described by the target.  'Frank's dead body was apalling.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time in which the Protagonist is dead or alive.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The FE Protagonist is the being or entity that dies.  With verbs in this frame, the Protagonist is the External Argument.  'The goldfish died.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The FE Explanation expresses any object or eventuality that brings about the Protagonist's death.  'The cat died of old age.' 'The children perished from hunger.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Some measure of the event, generally frequency.  'You know, I wouldn't want to live in a Shakespearian play; people die in them a lot.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The FE Depictive denotes the state of the Protagonist as the death occurred.  'I think he died happy.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).   'He died horribly; I won't describe it.'

name: Result
definition_en: The FE Result indicates what occurs as the result of the death of the Protagonist.  'If we don't find something soon, we'll all starve to death.'

name: Place
definition_en: The FE Place indicates where the death takes place.  'Your father passed away in his hospital bed.'

name: Time
definition_en: The FE Time denotes when the dying or killing occurs.  'Your father passed  away about four minutes ago.' 'He sadly passed  away in 1962 because of severe cerebrovascular disease.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE identifies the larger event in which the Protagonist dies, i.e. changes from living to dead.  'The pilot died in the crash'

name: Maleficiary
definition_en: An individual negatively affected by the death of the Protagonist.  'Aww man, my dog died on me.'

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is the target of the deception.

name: Deceiver
definition_en: The Deceiver attempts to make the Victim unable to know about or detect the truth about a Phenomenon or Topic.

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The Phenomenon is presented to the Victim as a way to mislead about the Topic.

name: Topic
definition_en: The entity to which the misleading idea relates, what it is about.

name: Time
definition_en: When the deception fails or succeeds.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the deception fails or succeeds.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is the target of the deception.

name: Deceiver
definition_en: The Deceiver attempts to make the Victim unable to know about or detect the truth about a Phenomenon or Topic.

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The Phenomenon is presented to the Victim as a way to mislead about the Topic.

name: Topic
definition_en: The entity to which the misleading idea relates, what it is about.

name: Deceiver
definition_en: The person who acts so as to give the Victim an incorrect idea about a Topic.

name: Victim
definition_en: The person who receives an incorrect idea because of the Deceiver's actions.

name: Topic
definition_en: The entity to which the misleading idea relates, what it is about.

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by the Deceiver to fool the Victim.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the deception occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the deception occurs.

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The Phenomenon, as percieved by the Victim, causes the Victim to have an incorrect understanding about a Topic.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer decides on a course of action.  'Mo decided to quit the program.'

name: Decision
definition_en: Decision identifies the entity or course of action upon which the Cognizer decides. 'Mo decided to quit the program.'

name: Possibilities
definition_en: A Cognizer makes a Decision from among a set of Possibilities.  'Mo decided on the blue sweater from the pile on the counter.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time or time period over which the Cognizer makes the decision.  'The State Cabinet today decided to file an appeal in the Supreme Court seeking an extension of six months for implementation of its judgment'

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Cognizer makes the decision.  'At the first crossroad we decided to wait.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Cognizer makes a Decision

name: Inherent_purpose
definition_en: The Cognizer intends the Decision to fulfill an Inherent_purpose . 'Samson ruled out  Delilah as a wife.'

name: Circumstance
definition_en: The conditions under which the Cognizer makes a Decision.  'We have ruled out the effect of photosynthesis under the current conditions of the experiment.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Cognizer makes the Decision.  'Miss Patty opted for blue because it is her daughter's favorite color.'

name: Defender
definition_en: This FE is the being or entity that responds forcefully to the Assailant's attack.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity used by the Defender fend off the Assailant .

name: Assailant
definition_en: The person (or other self-directed entity) that is attempting physical harm to the Victim.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Defender that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Defender that accomplishes their defense of the Victim.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Defender defends the Victim from the Assailant.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Defender defends the Victim from the Assailant. 'John defended the bear to prove his manhood.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Defender is responding to that leads them to protect the Victim.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Defender takes forceful action against the Assailant.

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: The starting-point of the motion of the Defender or projectiles of the Defender as they move toward the the Place that the Assailant is occupying.  In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Defender or Victim during the Assailant's attack.

name: Victim
definition_en: The individual or entity that is under attack from the Assailant .

name: Location_of_assailant
definition_en: The location of the Assailant or the weapons of the Assailant.  'We have to take out their air defenses first.'

name: Alterant
definition_en: The Alterant causes a change in the Material.

name: Material
definition_en: The substance which is altered in some useful way.  ''

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount to which a Material has undergone processing.

name: Item
definition_en: The entity whose scalar property is specified.

name: Variable
definition_en: The scalar property that the Item possesses.

name: Limit1
definition_en: The first-mentioned possibility of the range of variation.

name: Limit2
definition_en: The second item of the range of variation.

name: Limits
definition_en: The range of positions on the scale that the Item occupies. 'Prices range between 10 and 20 dollars.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The deviation of the Upper_limit and the Lower_limit from each other (and thus from some single value).  'The weights range a lot .'

name: Duration
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the State's absolute duration.

name: State
definition_en: An ongoing state whose duration can be measured.

name: Deliverer
definition_en: This is the person who completes the movement of the Theme after having transported it.  'That afternoon, a staff courier delivered the box from St. Petersburg to Largo.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The end of the path and intended goal of the sending.  'I delivered the packages to the storage room.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The objects being delivered.  'I delivered the documents to the court house.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The vehicle employed by the Deliverer.  'I polished it until the last blemish had vanished, then delivered it by wheelbarrow.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Deliverer or Theme  'They delivered my cable box broken three times.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the delivery event  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously),  secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Deliverer that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  ' As was customary, she had eagerly delivered the morning paper to her parents' room'

name: Recipient
definition_en: This is the Recipient of the sent Theme.  'Tess delivered a package to Abby and her kitty.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose of the delivery.  'Rachel delivered the letter to her mother to see how she would react on getting it.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for the delivery.  'Letters are generally delivered in the morning because that's when most people are home.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the delivery takes place  'I delivered the letter to you last week, Sir.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: An additional theme delivered along with the main Theme.  ' I ordered a cappuccino and he delivered it along with a ricebubble sweet snack.'

name: Container
definition_en: A container in which the Theme is delivered.  'We delivered the roses in a beautiful vase as you requested.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the delivery takes place.  'Barney delivered the letter on Monday in Sheboygan'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed at which the Deliverer delivers the Theme.  'This service is for our clients who need speedy delivery of their goods.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The conditions under which the delivery takes place.  'Purchases over $400 are delivered for free.'

name: Source
definition_en: The location of the Theme before the delivery process begins.  'We offer direct delivery of all of your packages from anywhere in the UK.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means are intermediate actions performed by the Deliverer in order to move the package to the Goal.  'He always delivers the papers by tossing them through people's windows.'

name: Path
definition_en: The path along which the Theme moves while being delivered.  'He delivered it through the transom .'  'Oil deliveries were made along the interstate.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The person for whom the Delivery action occurs.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE applies to appraisals of the Delivery event.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the Delivery event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Authority
definition_en: The Authority orders the Protagonist to not engage in a particular Action.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist wants to engage in an Action, but is ordered not to by the Authority.

name: Action
definition_en: The Action is what the Protagonist seeks to do, but is ordered not to.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the denying of permission occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the denial of permission occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose is what the Authority hopes to accomplish by denying permission.

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.  First, it applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness. The notion of appraisal requires a factive portrayal of the event. The second subgroup consists of any descriptions of the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames. The state of affairs reported by the target is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier. What that role is depends only on the predicate heading the modifier phrase.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Allowed_category
definition_en: A category that the Action fits into, which dictates the Action's being permitted (in accord with some implicit Principle.)  'The transfer was sanctioned as a "necessary precaution".'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the event occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the Authority or the Protagonist while they are involved in the action.  'He granted permission fully aware of her crime .'

name: Manner
definition_en: A holistic description of the event (the same way), or a description of the Authority that also affects the overall event (carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by an Authority that brings about the Denying or Granting Permission.

name: Theme
definition_en: This is the object which moves. It may be an entity which moves under its own power, but it need not be. 'The officer left the house.'

name: Source
definition_en: All the verbs in this frame express some change of location, away from one place and to another. Any constituent that expresses the initial position of the Theme, before the change of location, is tagged with Source. Often the Source is understood from context. 'The woman left. DNI' 'The woman left the house.''We departed from New York on Friday.'

name: Path
definition_en: Any description of the trajectory of the departure which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path.  In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a sense meaning 'via'.  'Spiderman left through the window.'

name: Goal
definition_en: This FE labels any expression which tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of departing from the Source. 'Our visitors left for Los Angeles.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and many other things count as Manner expressions, though Speed and Means should be tagged using the more specific FE labels. 'The messenger left the room clumsily.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Theme which results in its departure. 'He retreated from his opponent by taking a quick leap backwards.'

name: Speed
definition_en: This frame element labels words or phrases that describe how quickly the Theme is moving. 'He quickly exited the crowded terminal.'

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Theme is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Theme. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium.   In this frame, Mode_of_transportation is often expressed obliquely in a prepositional phrase headed by 'in' or 'by'.  'We set out by boat for Nova Scotia. ''Wilbur departed on foot for London.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: The Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a prepositional phrase generally headed by 'with' or 'along with'.  'He left along with John.'

name: Distance
definition_en: The distance that the Theme has traveled. 'He withdrew a little from her. '

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the departure takes place.'We left in the morning.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency is the rate at which each Theme departs.

name: Journey
definition_en: The Journey is the trip or expedition on which the Theme embarks. 'Mr. Burns departed on a hunting expedition.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location in which the departing takes place.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies a phrase which describes the Theme at the time of departing.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the motivation or explanation for why the Theme departs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Theme departs from the Source.

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The length of time that the Theme stays away from the Source location.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE describes of the state of affairs denoted by the Departing event as role fillers in other frames; the state of affairs reported Departing event is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier.

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: An Eventuality or an Entity that is taken to constitute sufficient reason for taking another Action.  ' A heavy contact to the opponent 's face may not merit just a verbal warning '

name: Action
definition_en: An Action that is taken to be justifiable given the State_of_Affairs.  ' The end justifies the means.'

name: Degree
definition_en: How sufficiently State_of_affairs can be considered a reason for the Action.  'Your son's behavior completely justifies the punishment he received.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The general spectrum of reasoning along which the State_of_affairs is a justification.  'Not all bad behavior legally justifies eviction.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Deserving event and any of its participants.

name: Evaluee
definition_en: The Evaluee is being judged for its quality.  ' He gave me another lame excuse.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the  Degree to which the Evaluee is judged good or bad.  ' Smithers was doing an absolutely splendid job.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the quality of the Evaluee is being judged.  'It's a great game when it rains.'

name: Parameter
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that denote a scalar property of the Evaluee with respect to which the Evaluee is judged.  'The Beaujolais Nouveau is dazzling in freshness.'

name: Comparison_set
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate what class of things or events the Evaluee is being judged against.  'The standard of living is poor compared to other Western industrialized countries.'

name: Affected_party
definition_en: The Affected_party indicates entities that benefit or suffer from the good or bad quality of the Evaluee.  'The season was splendid for the team.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Frame Element Depictive encodes a state that the Evaluee is in and which does not represent a temporary or hypothetical set of Circumstances.  'The aerial view is superb with its view of the harbour.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The State_of_affairs that the speaker finds desirable.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the State_of_affairs has the specified assessment of desirability.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The event or state of affairs that is achieved by bringing about the desirable State_of_affairs.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the specified desirability of the State_of_affairs deviates from the expected desirability.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the person (or sentient being) who wishes for the Event to occur.

name: Event
definition_en: The change that the Experiencer would like to see.

name: Focal_participant
definition_en: This is the entity that the Experiencer wishes to be affected by some Event.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree is a the extent of the Experiencer's Desiring.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Experiencer desires something.  'I wanted more of her like a junkie wants his next fix.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: An aspect of the Experiencer that causes a desire. 'Do Italians have a genetic yearning for pizza?' 'Intellectually he longed for success, but really he just wanted love.'

name: Purpose_of_event
definition_en: The Purpose_of_event is the purpose pertaining to the desired Event.  'I want that book for my test tomorrow.'

name: Time_of_event
definition_en: The time that the Event would ideally occur. 'I want porridge tomorrow.'

name: Location_of_event
definition_en: The Location_of_event is the place involved in the desired Event.  'I want that box on top of the other one.' 'The prince wishes you here before matins.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Experiencer desires something. 'Oh, so now you want to go to the zoo!'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.  Note that this FE is of extremely rare occurrence in this frame. 'In the car I had desired nothing more than to get here, but now that I'm here...'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the Experiencer has desired something. 'His lifelong yearning for success had finally been fulfilled.' 'I've wanted them to fix the sidewalk for years!'

name: Role_of_focal_participant
definition_en: The Role is a role filled by a Focal_participant in the Event that the Experiencer desires.  'Michaels originally wanted Smith as the new Late Night producer.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The State_of_affairs that is destined to occur to the Protagonist.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist is the one for whom the future State_of_affairs is destined.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description of the sort of State_of_affairs that will occur.  'You are an important person with a glorious destiny and you have a wonderful biography written about you.'

name: Role
definition_en: The Role filled by the Protagonist in his/her destiny.  'Deciding that his true destiny is as a healer, Henderson returns home, planning to enter medical school.'  'His destiny as the disciple of Shri Krishna is to become the prototype of the perfect Yogi'

name: Time
definition_en: The time for which the Protagonist's future is determined.  'Their destiny over those years was to gradually take charge of most of the world's operations.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which State_of_affairs is destined to occur to the Protagonist.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the State_of_affairs is destined to occur to the Protagonist.

name: Destroyer
definition_en: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional action that results in the Patient's destruction.  'Who can unmake the ring?'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the destruction is completed. 'I destroyed all signs of our presence completely.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Destroyer that interacts with a Patient to accomplish the Patient's destruction.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the process of destruction which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Destroyer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Destroyer that accomplishes the destruction. 'Samptu obliterated the land of Abde with a great flood, leaving only the sea.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Destroyer destroys the Patient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which a Destroyer causes the destruction of the Patient. 'We laid waste to Hattusas to subjugate them, not to vex them.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Destroyer is responding to in destroying the Undergoer. 'He razed the goddess's temple out of sheer anger.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an event on the Patient.  This FE is very rare in this frame, and since the Patient is destroyed by this process, the Result is generally constrained to indicate the Patient 's resulting inexistence. 'All of the buildings had been razed to nothing.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the Patient which is directly affected by the destruction. 'The village was devastated from the north end to the banks of the Neva.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Destroyer destroys the Patient.

name: Patient
definition_en: The entity which is destroyed by the Destroyer.  'Who can unmake the ring?'

name: Cause
definition_en: The event or entity which is responsible for the destruction of the Patient. 'The subsequent explosions leveled most downtown office buildings.' 'Tornados vaporized this town a few decades back.'

name: Role
definition_en: The category in which the Patient is destroyed.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Cause or Destroyer destroys the Patient.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium expresses the Medium in which the Patient is destroyed by the Cause or Destroyer.  This FE is generally used in Metaphorical uses of this frame. 'West demolished Kraft's arguments in his most recent essay.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that causes the Item and Source to come apart by manipulating the connector.  'After a few minutes he got up and unchained me from the tree.'

name: Item
definition_en: This FE identifies the Item that the Agent detaches from the Source.  'Mercer's cell phone vibrated and he unhitched it from his belt to flip it open.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of a detaching event.

name: Source
definition_en: Source identifies the location to which an Item was attached before getting detached.   'Mercer's cell phone vibrated and he unhitched it from his belt to flip it open.'

name: Items
definition_en: This FE identifies the plural Items that are detached from each other, resulting in their separation.  'When, later, they untied his ankles, the ropes were left draped over the beam.'  Notice that when the FE Items occurs, neither Item nor Source can occur.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent detaches an Item or Items.   'I must have detached the macro lens by dragging my octopus hose over the camera as I was preparing to submerge.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the detaching event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously),  secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'I used a paper clip to pry it off slightly, then carefully detached it with a small screwdriver.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent detaches an Item or Items.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent intentionally detaches an Item or Items.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent detaches the Item from the Source.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Agent detaches an Item or Items.  Typically, it transmits the force applied by the Agent, and is not left behind as a participant in the resultant state.    'I detached it with my penknife.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Item ends up detached.  'Trypsin detached the rest of the basal lamina completely from the endothelium.'

name: Authorities
definition_en: The Authorities hold the Suspect in custody.

name: Charges
definition_en: This FE identifies the crime with which the Suspect is charged.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the detaining takes place.

name: Suspect
definition_en: This FE identifies the person who is taken into custody and held, under suspicion of having committed a crime.

name: Time
definition_en: When the detaining occurs.

name: Holding_location
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Suspect is confined. 'Marge was under arrest in the county jail.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the length of time that the Suspect spends in confinement.

name: Legal_basis
definition_en: This FE identifies the law, act, or precedent that allows the Authorities  to detain the Suspect. 'The government held him under the Why Not Act.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Authorities detain a Suspect.

name: Dependent_state
definition_en: This FE identifies the state of the Suspect being held. 'Snake was held in communicado.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent detonates the Explosive.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Agent detonates the Explosive.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent detonates the Explosive.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent detonates the Explosive.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent detonates the Explosive.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action ( deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Explosive
definition_en: The Explosive causes damage to surrounding objects when operated by the Agent.

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of the Agent's detonating the Explosive his or her Purpose.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event within which the Agent detonates the Explosive. Often, the Containing_event will also give an indication of the Agent's Purpose.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question "how often."

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE modifies a clause with an iterative interpretation, which may be signified by the simple present tense on the main verb.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute of the Explosive or the detonation act and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An implement used by the Agent to detonate the Explosive.  'The assailants seem to have detonated the bombs with a cellphone.'

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim (typically an individual or structure) is targeted by the explosion or inadvertantly damaged by the explosion. May be indicated explicitly with on or against, but is often implied by place expressions, in which case the FE is indicated on the second layer.  'Minutes later assailants detonated a bomb against the walls of police headquarters.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The cognizer is the person (or other sentient being) who potentially determines that two Phenomena are distinct from each other. It is normally expressed as an External Argument: ' The teacher couldn't distinguish one child from the other. '

name: Phenomenon_1
definition_en: The phenomena that are potentially judged to be different from one another can be expressed as separate constituents. When they are, one is typically expressed as an NP Object, and the other as a PP Complement headed by from: ' The teacher couldn't distinguish Pat from Kim.'  In this case, the phenomenon expressed more prominently as an NP Object is called Phenomenon_1:  'The teacher couldn't distinguish Pat from Kim. '

name: Phenomenon_2
definition_en: See Phenomenon_1, above. The phenomenon expressed less prominently as a PP complement is called Phenomenon_2: 'The teacher couldn't distinguish Pat from Kim. '

name: Phenomena
definition_en: Both phenomena that are potentially judged to be different from one another can be expressed jointly by the same constituent:  'The teacher couldn't distinguish the twins.'  Such constituents are assigned the FE Phenomena. They are always plural, as in the above example, or involve conjunction:  'The teacher couldn't distinguish Pat and Kim. '

name: Quality
definition_en: This is a property that is potentially used by the Cognizer to distinguish one phenomenon from another. It is normally expressed as a PP headed by a preposition such as from, by, or on the basis of:  'The coach could distinguish the twins by their hair.' General Grammatical Observations: Verbs in this domain often occur with the modal auxiliary can.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: State of a participant while the action is ongoing. 'We differentiated between the squid, certain that their characteristics put them in different species.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Cognizer that allows them to differentiate the Phenomena.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances describe the situation in which the Cognizer evaluates the Phenomena. 'It is difficult to distinguish contrasing figures from a distance.'

name: Activity
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions indicating the Activity that the Experiencer finds difficult or easy. In many cases, the relevant Activity has to be inferred from the context.  'The climb was difficult.' 'That question was difficult.' 'That question was difficult to answer.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the Degree of difficulty that the Experiencer has in carrying out the Activity.  ' Charlie is very tough for Lulu to please.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions in which the Activity is being experienced and which influence the Experiencer's perception of how easy or difficult the Activity is.  'In this weather the climb turned out to be very difficult.'

name: Experiencer
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate which person judges carrying out the Activity to be easy or difficult.  'The geology question on the exam was hard for me.'

name: Parameter
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate a respect in which the Activity is judged easy or difficult to carry out by the Experiencer.  'The problem involves a mathematically difficult Fourier transformation.'

name: Standard
definition_en: The experience of the Activity by the Experiencer may be compared to a Standard situation, which may be evoked either as an event or state, or by reference to a salient participant.  'Man, running on hilly bike paths of Calgary was tough compared to my routes in flat  southwestern Ontario.'  'Elsewhere, expert rider Kris Leeson was finding the going tough compared to the previous rounds.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Activity takes place.

name: Dimension
definition_en: This FE identifies the Dimension which is measured.  Most LUs in this frame incorporate the Dimension.  'The  new vase is 5 cm in circumference at the top.'

name: Object
definition_en: Object identifies the item which is measured along one of its Dimensions.  'The  new vase is 5 cm in circumference at the top.'

name: Measurement
definition_en: Measurement identifies the extent of the Object along the specified Dimension.  'The  new vase is 5 cm in circumference at the top.'

name: Locus
definition_en: Locus identifies the sub-region of the Object where the Dimension is measured. 'The  new vase is 5 cm in circumference at the top.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant dimension of development.

name: Degree
definition_en: FOR REFRAMING!

name: Landmark
definition_en: The point of reference from which the rest of the Path is reckoned.

name: Path
definition_en: The one-dimensional set of locations.

name: Domain
definition_en: The kind of space in which the set of points of the Path is defined. 'Let us progess a bit forward in time to the Napoleonic wars.'

name: Independent_variable
definition_en: The one-dimensional variable with respect to which the positions on the Path are reckoned.  For normal motion, the positions on the Path are with respect to time, while for directions of facing, the positions are merely reckoned with respect to another spatial dimension, the distance from the Landmark in the specified direction.  As these features are the default, literal interpretation of targets of this frame, this frame element is only to be used for metaphorical examples like the following:  'As public spending goes up in scale , this logic no longer makes sense .'

name: Distance
definition_en: How much movement in the stated direction along the Path from the Landmark there has been.

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure.  'The cat is above the mat.'

name: Figure
definition_en: The Figure is perceived as located relative to a certain Ground location in a certain direction specified by the particular LU. The Figure can be an entity or an event.  'The cat is above the mat.'

name: Accessibility
definition_en: An indication of how accessible the Figure is to some participant in the speech context (either the speaker or the addressee, or some other highly salient viewpoint in a narrative).  This FE normally describes availability for manipulation and use, but may simply describe how easily seen or difficult to see the Figure is. There is a closed class of items that can fill this slot, including only 'just' and 'right' indicating ease of access, and 'way' and 'all the way' indicating distance and difficulty of access.    'Oh yeah , the gas station is right west of here .'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure. This FE is filled by one of a closed class of adverbs: up, down, out (meaning 'beyond the boundary around the viewpoint'), off (meaning 'disconnect between landmark and figure'), back (meaning 'along a line from front to back of landmark, and relatively inaccessible'), and, more rarely, away, along, and dialectally, back down (meaning 'down and behind').   'The cat was hiding way out north of the house.'

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the locative relation between Figure and Ground obtains.  'He was north of the park on Friday.'

name: Distance
definition_en: This  FE identifies the  Distance between the Figure and the Ground.  This FE requires an image schema with a vector that extends from the Ground, or a subpart of the Ground, in some direction, and the Distance is measured along this vector from the Ground to the profiled region.    'Go 30 feet to the left of the pool.'  Note that a number of frequent adverbial targets identify the Ground, with the location of an implicit viewer, so Distance is effectively measured from the viewpoint location in these cases.  'We were already nearly 1000 meters ahead.'

name: Deixis
definition_en: An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder), or specifically separated from the speech context by distance or a barrier (over).  Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.  'It was lying there below the lightpole.'

name: Directness
definition_en: An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target.  This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, directly, and due (and some combinations of these), but also occurs with rarer items like 'smack dab'.  'I run in Ketchum, due east of the highschool .'

name: Temporal_profile
definition_en: A description of how the access path to the Ground interacts with time.  This FE is filled only by the closed class of adverbials back.adv (which indicates that the position was occupied by the Figure before) and on.adv (which indicates a continued path).  While this FE in its most basic use refers to cases of actual motion, it can be used with descriptions of static position, in which case it either refers to fictive, imagined motion, or it backgrounds motion entirely (as in the example below).  'They finally moved back east.'

name: Responder
definition_en: The individual or group that is responding to a disaster with directed action.  'The firefighters rushed toward the blaze.'

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim (typically a large group) which is affected by the disaster event.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Undesirable_event occurs.

name: Response
definition_en: Directed action leading to recovery, rescue, or general mitigation of distress due to an ensuing disaster.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the disaster scenario occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time between the instantiation of the Disaster and the conclusion of the Response.

name: Disaster
definition_en: An event of great proportional magnitude with evidence leaving blame to which only the stars might answer. A disaster is an indisputably ill-fated occurrence.

name: Interlocutor_1
definition_en: In cases where the Interlocutors involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, this FE identifies the conversational participant with greater semantic and syntactic prominence, as compared with Interlocutor_2. That is, Interlocutor_1 is generally encoded as Subject, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Interlocutor_1.  Thus a Purpose (or Means, Depictive, or Manner) is construed to be that of Interlocutor_1, not necessarily that of Interlocutor_2 or the group of Interlocutors as a whole. 'The President conferred with his top advisor.' 'I discussed evolution with Gould to prove he was wrong about it.'

name: Interlocutor_2
definition_en: In cases where the Interlocutors involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, Interlocutor_2 refers to the semantically and grammatically less prominent group.  It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with).  Note that it is possible for a single role to correspond to multiple referents. For example, if the prepositional object in the example below were plural, we would still assign it the single role Interlocutor_2. 'The President debated with his top advisor. '

name: Interlocutors
definition_en: In some sentences both participants are expressed by the Subject, and there is no 'with'-phrase (cf example 1). In sentences like this, the Subject is assigned the FE role Interlocutors. In such sentences, the Subject always denotes more than one person, and it is understood that the reciprocal communication takes place between these two (or more) people. The Subject may denote two or more people either through conjunction, as in example 1, or through plurality, as in example 2, or by denoting a group, as in example 3. In each of these cases the FE Interlocutors is assigned. Notice that for nouns in the Discussion frame, it is possible for the Interlocutors role to be expressed by a prepositional phrase as in example 4.   '(1) The President and his advisor discussed the Venezuelan situation briefly before the summit.'  '(2) The lawyers conferred before the trial.' '(3)The committee debated the bill for only a few minutes.' '(4) There was a brief exchange between the lawyers.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic expresses the subject that the Interlocutors are trying to come to some agreement about.  It may refer, for example, to an undesirable issue that the Interlocutors want to have the proper response to, or it may refer more directly to an unresolved question.  'The President and his top advisors discussed the scandal.' 'They had a discussion about the scandal.' 'The participants debated whether the US should soften its response.'

name: Language
definition_en: The linguistic system(s) used by the Interlocutors to discuss something.  'In our house everybody debated politics in three different languages at once.'

name: Amount_of_discussion
definition_en: Amount_of_discussion applies to phrases expressing how thoroughly a Topic has been discussed.  'This issue had been exhaustively discussed'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing Interlocutor_1 or the pair of Interlocutors.  'Jack and Jill discussed the issue unaware of its full import.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This frame element marks phrases that expresss the Manner in which one or both of the Interlocutors communicate.  'They debated amicably over who should pay the restaurant bill.'

name: Means
definition_en: This Frame Elememt marks constituents expressing the means the parties to the conversation use to talk to each other.  'Email allows people to communicate electronically' 'They briefly conferred with each other via a quick series of eyebrow twitches and a quirk of the mouth.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration of the conversation.  'They had a short conference off by the stable.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The goal that Interlocutor_1 or the Interlocutors jointly have, i.e. the state of affairs that they wish to bring about by the conversation.  'You engage in such idle debate just to see how long I'll let it go.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the discussion takes place.  'Last year the participants discussed taking down the last trade barriers without consensus.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which a discussion takes place.  'We just conferred for a couple of hours up in her room.'

name: Means_of_communication
definition_en: The device or system that facilitates a discussion.  'If we held a debate on the radio, noone would be listening -- you could say whatever you wanted!'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or a state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the discussion takes place and of which it is taken to be part.  'Did you catch that "Your Local News Now" discussion about rising crime in suburban areas?'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times the discussion happens in a given period of time.  'I came to enjoy our frequent discussions.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The general field or area in which the discussion takes place, or which shapes the discussion or its topic.  'This prompted a rather philosophical debate about the importance of having a purpose in life.'

name: Traveller
definition_en: The Traveller is the entity which disembarks from the Vehicle.  'We got off at the wrong bus stop.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The Vehicle is the means of conveyance that the Traveller disembarks from.    'The victim stopped the tractor and dismounted from it.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path describes the trajectory of the Traveller's motion off or out of the Vehicle.  'As we got off the plane via a set of steps we were immediately guided into a bus.'

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The amount of time the Traveller spends off or outside of the Vehicle after disembarking from it.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Traveller or Vehicle during the disembarking.

name: Time
definition_en: When the disembarking of the Vehicle takes place.  'Yesterday, we alighted onto this tiny hilly island, site of a Singaporean October festival.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: A theme that leaves the Vehicle together with the main Traveller. This may be an entity the Traveller transports or a co-traveller moving under their own power.  'Many people were waiting for him when he got off the ship with his wife, Estelita Villafane.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Traveller disembarks from the vehicle.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Traveller disembarks from the Vehicle.

name: Goal
definition_en: The location that the Traveller reaches by leaving the Vehicle.   'The driver and the majority of passengers dismounted onto the road as onlookers quickly formed an unruly squabbling mass.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The entity or event which brings disgrace upon the Protagonist.  'You will soon learn the penalty for your disgraceful conduct. '

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The person or organization responsible for the occurrence of the State_of_affairs.  'It is disgraceful to our Public Works Department.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the State_of_affairs diverges from the social norm for things of its kind.  '"This is absolutely disgraceful," she said .'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the judgment of disgrace logically follows.   'And Harvard's policy is shameful because it insults the memory and the principles of American patriotism at the very birthplace of American patriotism. '

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent disperses or scatters the Individuals.

name: Individuals
definition_en: The Individuals are scattered by the Agent.

name: Source
definition_en: Source is the relatively confined space from which an Agent scatters the Individuals.

name: Goal_area
definition_en: Goal_area identifies the broader space to which the Agent scatters the Individuals

name: Cause
definition_en: An event or force that causes that Individuals to disperse.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the dispersing event  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously),  secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). With agentive uses, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (eagerly, carefully).  ' He carefully scattered more mud around the rose bed'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Individuals are dispersed.

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the dispersal.

name: Result
definition_en: A state of the Individuals that results from the dispersal.

name: Path
definition_en: The trajectory along which the Individuals move.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the dispersing event happens.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in dispersing the Individuals

name: Distance
definition_en: The distance that the Individuals move from their original location, the Source.  'Firing four shots into the air scattered them only a short distance, but it was enough.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The rate of motion of the Individuals, usually in terms of how long it takes for them to leave the Source and end up in the Goal_area.  'We dispersed the smoke as rapidly as possible.'

name: Bomb
definition_en: The Bomb is set off by the Detonator at a distance, injuring or damaging a Target.  'These photographs were taken in the wake of a CWIED attack on the British.'

name: Use
definition_en: The type of activity that the Bomb is generally involved in.  Often this can be considered a kind of Type specification also.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Bomb belongs to.

name: Material
definition_en: The substance that makes up the Bomb.

name: Detonator
definition_en: The person that wishes to attack the Target and who activates the Bomb.

name: Part
definition_en: This FE identifies a part of the Bomb. This includes parts that aid in the detonation or damaging, or mere attachments.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to the Bomb.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which a Bomb comes into existence.

name: Creator
definition_en: The individual or group responsible for the creation of the Bomb.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description or characteristic of the Bomb not covered by more specific FEs.

name: Target
definition_en: The intended or actual target of the Bomb.

name: Feature
definition_en: The aspect of the Entity which makes it different from the other members of its class.  'That never depleting ammo in his arsenal - his signature smile - is contagious.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The item which differs from other members of its class in the Feature's value.  'These signatures may be distinctive of the entire Chlamydiales order.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the values of the Feature of the Entity and the Comparison_set are similar to each other.  'The twins have a very distinct walk.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme covers or fills the Location.

name: Location
definition_en: Location is the object or area that the Theme fills or covers.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree of abundance with which the Theme covers or fills the Location.

name: Time
definition_en: The time during which the Theme and the Location are positioned relative to each other.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme in this frame is the object which is described as standing in some spatial relation to a particular Location.  Theme typically occurs as the External Argument or, with passives, as a PP Complement headed by "with" or "by".'Ribbons festooned the car.''The table was covered by a purple velvet cloth.'

name: Location
definition_en: Location is the entity or area with respect to which the Theme's spatial arrangement is described.  This frame element generally occurs as an NP Object.'Thick varnish coated the beautiful wood.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the Location which contains or is covered by the Theme. 'Bulletholes covered the windshield on the right side.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Theme occupies the Location.  'By 1950, factories dotted the adjacent countryside.'

name: Deixis
definition_en: An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder). Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.  'The pens were there all over my desk.'

name: Region_quantification
definition_en: A description of how much of a potential profiled region actually has (or is expected to have) a Theme in it.  It is normally filled by closed-class items like 'all', 'somewhere', 'nowhere', etc.  'All around the town, people were dancing.'

name: Temporal_profile
definition_en: A description of how the access path to the Location interacts with time. This FE is filled only by the closed class adverbial back.adv (which indicates that the position was occupied by the Theme before).  While this FE in its most basic use refers to cases of actual motion, it can background motion entirely (as in the example below).   'The weeds were back around the garden.'

name: Group
definition_en: This FE marks constituents that express the set of objects or types whose diversity is at issue.

name: Dimension
definition_en: This FE marks constituents which express a property in respect to which the similarity of the Group is assessed.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the members of the Group are similar to each other, in general or with respect to some Dimension(s)  'The songs on the album are incredibly diverse .'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Group is diverse or homogenous.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the general area in which diversity occurs or exists.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which Dimension is similar or different

name: Explanation
definition_en: An inanimate entity or process that causes the diversity or homogeneity.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Group

name: Bearer
definition_en: The holder of the document. 'My  visa will expire next month.'

name: Issuer
definition_en: The authority that issues the document. 'US consulate issued a Visa to Ms. Yang to travel to San Francisco.'

name: Obligation
definition_en: Obligation is the obligation that is imposed on the Bearer of the Document. 'They were all under subpoena to appear in court.'

name: Right
definition_en: Right is the right of the Bearer of the Document  that is authorized by the Document.  'Raymond has a fishing licence.'

name: Status
definition_en: Status is the state of the Bearer of the Document indicated by the Document. 'The couple just got their marriage certificate.'

name: Specification
definition_en: A Specification is a condition that applies to the Rights and/or Obligations described in the Document. 'Before you get your driver's liscense, you need to carry your temporary driving permit when you drive. '

name: Document
definition_en: Document is the piece of paper that has the legal status. 'The police need a search warrant to enter his house.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The language the Document is written in, or a specification of the kind of object that instantiates it.  'We only need an electronic confirmation.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Descriptor covers any characterization or description of the target that is not covered by another more specific FE.

name: Dodger
definition_en: The Dodger acts to avoid an oncoming Bad_entity.  'Mo dodged the flower pot that Larry threw in disgust.'

name: Bad_entity
definition_en: The Bad_entity is  the oncoming entity to avoid.  'Mo dodged  the flower pot that Larry threw in disgust.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the dodging occurs.  'He sidestepped just enough to soften the blow.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the dodging occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the dodging occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time at which the dodging occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the dodging occurs.  'He sidestepped just enough to soften the blow.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the  Explanation for which the dodging occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the dodging occurs.

name: Predicate
definition_en: This Frame Element denotes the Predicate which is applied to the Domain.  'This policy is not economically sound.'

name: Domain
definition_en: This Frame Element applies to the Domain in which the Predicate is said to apply.  'Britain and France are close , not only geographically , but also strategically .'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent controls the Patient by being forceful and possibly aggressive.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is trying to gain control of a situation, but ends up being subject to the control and influence of the Agent.

name: Situation
definition_en: The Situation within which the Agent is able to gain control over the Patient (thus excluding them from controlling the Situation).

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time over which the domination occurs.  'For England and France, domination over their colonies during the colonial period was mainly a cultural obligation.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the event as a whole, or of any of the participants that does not fit any of the other more specific Frame Elements.  'He managed to be dominant over most of the rest of the staff, in a good way.'

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the domination occurs.  'Women tend to dominatemen at home and at Church.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the domination takes place.  'Their role models might have dominated women in the past; they may not have understood the concept of equality.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Agent dominates the Patient.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the most forceful and pivotal factor in the situation.

name: Situation
definition_en: The Situation is primarily affected by the Agent, in particular how it develops or concludes.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Agent is dominant.  'As discussed above, Ford dominated the market in the 1920s, then left the business to create production capacity for the Model A.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time over which the domination occurs.  'Dinosaurs were vertebrate animals that dominated the terrestrial ecosystem for over 160 million years.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the domination takes place.  'Indeed, in all Latin America, United States corporations dominated the key sectors of the economy.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the event as a whole, or of any of the participants that does not fit any of the other more specific Frame Elements.  'Most predict that the top teams from last year to ruthlessly dominate the league.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Agent dominates the Situation.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent has a controlling position in the Situation.

name: Situation
definition_en: The Situation is primarily affected by the Agent, in particular how it develops or concludes.

name: Competitor
definition_en: The Competitors are trying to gain control of a situation, but end up being subject to the control and influence of the Agent .

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the domination takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The location of the dominationw

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner of the domination.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time over which the domination takes place.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Agent dominates.

name: Dough
definition_en: The paste made out of any cereals (grains) or leguminous crops by grinding, with some water added, which expands in volume as a result of leavening before baking.   'While the dough was rising, they heated the oven.'

name: Duration_of_activity
definition_en: The length of the interval during which the Dough rises.  'The dough rose for about 2 hours.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the expansion of the Dough takes place.  ' The dough rose beautifully before it went into the fridge but afterwards it never really recovered.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed at which the Dough expands.   'The bread dough rose quickly.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the rising of the Dough  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).   'My dough rose nicely.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: A setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the event takes place. This FE also covers conditions that are causally connected to the event of the Dough rising.  'The dough rises higher if made by the bread machine than made by a standard mixer.'

name: Size_change
definition_en: The amount by which the volume of the Dough increases.  'While in the refrigerator, the dough rose by about 25%.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The entity or state of affairs that leads to the event of the Dough's rising.   'A slimmer approach relies on the bubbles of carbon dioxide created as the dough rises from the yeast.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent forces the Patient to come to the ground.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is the entity that is being forced to the ground.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of causing the Patient to come to the ground.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by an Agent that enables them to force the Patient to the ground.</def-root >

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the event takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the event takes place.

name: Cause
definition_en: An event which causes the Patient to come to the ground.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An object used by the Agent to facilitate bringing down the Patient.

name: Wearer
definition_en: The individual that puts Clothing on their body.

name: Clothing
definition_en: Clothing is used for the item of clothing that the Wearer ends up wearing.

name: Body_location
definition_en: The body part that the Clothing ends up covering.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of the donning event which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Clothing's motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Wearer or Clothing during the act.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is an act whereby the Wearer puts on the Clothing

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the Placing.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of the Wearing that results from putting on the Clothing.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place indicates where the Donning occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation indicates why the Wearer puts on the Clothing.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Wearer puts an item of Clothing on.  'She had put the dress on this morning expecting it to be sunny.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Wearer intends to accomplish by putting on Clothing.

name: Visitor
definition_en: The Visitor arrives at the Host_location to visit the Host for a Purpose.

name: Normal_location
definition_en: Normal_location is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Normal_location expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent.  If present, they often express a general direction from which a Visitor moves, rather than a landmark away from which it moves.

name: Path
definition_en: Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Normal_location nor the Host or Host_location.  In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.

name: Host
definition_en: The Host is the person highly associated with the goal location of the Visitor, and who allows the Visitor onto his/her territory, and possibly to make use of available resources. The Host and Visitor and in a host-guest relationship.

name: Manner
definition_en: A Manner expression  describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion.  Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Visitor arrives.

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Visitor is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Visitor.   Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when arriving occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Visitor arrives at a location associated with the Host.

name: Host_location
definition_en: The Host_location is a place primarily associated with the Host.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: The Containing_event denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the visiting takes place.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The frequency with whic hthe Visitor drops in on a Host.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Visitor remains with the Host.

name: Place
definition_en: The larger area within which the visiting takes place.

name: Particular_iteration
