definition_en: This FE indicates that the visiting is a particular instance in a series of repeated visiting events.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that explains why the Visitor is making a visit.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent places the Theme into a Substance.  'She dunked her sandwich into some tomato soup.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme temporarily goes partially or completely into the Substance.  'She dunked her sandwich into some tomato soup.'

name: Substance
definition_en: The Substance is the fluid into which the Theme is placed. This may be metonymically represented by the container of the fluid.  'She dunked her sandwich into some tomato soup.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Agent puts Theme in the Substance.  'He slowly dunked the biscuit into the coffee.'

name: Time
definition_en: The location in time when the dunking occurs.

name: Creator
definition_en: The Creator produces the Copy based on the Original.  It is normally expressed as an External Argument. 'Pat photocopied the article.'

name: Original
definition_en: The Original is the entity which is copied. With verbs it is frequently expressed as an NP Object:'Pat photocopied the article.'

name: Copy
definition_en: The Copy produced by the Creator is frequently not expressed. However, when Copy does occur, it is usually expressed as the External Argument of verbs: 'The results replicate those of an earlier study.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location from which material is copied, i.e. the location of the Original. Unlike the FE Source in other domains and frames, there is no actual movement of either Copy or Original from this location. Source is usually expressed by a PP Complement.  'I copied the design from a magazine. '

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the location to which material is copied.  Unlike the FE Goal in other frames, there is no actual movement of any entity to this location.  Goal is usually expressed as a PP Complement: 'Copy the file onto the hard drive.'

name: Characterization
definition_en: This FE designates the character of the medium in which a Copy is made. Usually, it is expressed as PP-in or AP. 'They sold a million copies in hardback.'  'Opposite is Pilinsky's wood-engraved copy.'  'The margins are covered in copies of the works of Shelley in Joan's handwriting.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Creator that lets them bring about the duplication.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase that describes a primary participant, either the Creator or the Copy/ Original.  'Such leaflets have to be duplicated en masse.' 'She did the copying unaware of the fact that John had already finished it.'</def-root >

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes Place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which an intentional act is performed.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Fidelity
definition_en: The way in which the Copy matches or does not match the Original. 'I made a half-size copy.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: The Iterations is the number of times the Original is copied. 'Jim copied the book 300 times.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency is the frequency with which the Original is copied. 'The scribes copied the scripture every 80 years.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: An entity that participates in much the same way as another participant (Creator, Copy, or Original), although it is characterized as being less focal to the action.  'Copy my list along with yours .'

name: Eventuality
definition_en: A situation, action or event whose duration is being described.  The Eventuality occurs as the External Argument if the adjective is used predicatively, or as the modified noun if the adjective is used attributively: The lecture was short. We had a lengthy conversation.

name: Period
definition_en: Sometimes these adjectives describe simply a period of time, rather than an event or state.  The Period almost invariably occurs as the modified noun with an attributive adjective: We waited for only a short time. Use of the drug over a lengthy period can cause memory loss.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Eventuality
definition_en: A situation, action or event whose duration is being described.  The Eventuality occurs as the External Argument if the adjective is used predicatively, or as the modified noun if the adjective is used attributively:   'The lecture did n't last long .'  'My unease persisted for some time .' 'Persisting decades past the end of the war , the economic disaster was to shape the fate of central Europe .'

name: Period
definition_en: Sometimes a period of time, rather than an event or state is described.    'This difficult period lasted only a short while .'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that the Eventuality, Period, or Entity lasts.  'If the film lasts more than one hour , I ca n't stay .'

name: Entity
definition_en: An item which is metonymically related to an Eventuality.  Some common eventualities that are metonymically entailed are the effect of the entity in its capacity as an instrument and the existence of the entity.  'The anesthesia lasted four hours .' 'You would n't last five minutes !'

name: User
definition_en: An individual that deploys a resource to receive a benefit.  The construction that introduces this FE is idiosyncratic, combining with last (in this frame), cost, and take--and more marginally see (in "saw me through the winter") and keep (in "It 'll keep me for a while .")  In this frame, the resource maps onto the Entity, and the benefit is the Eventuality.  'A gallon of water wo n't last us more than a few days .'

name: Period
definition_en: The Period whose the duration Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Period which is under discussion, namely the duration.

name: Duration
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the Period's absolute duration.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Duration from the norm.

name: Unit
definition_en: A standard measure, having a known duration.

name: Count
definition_en: The number of Units which are equivalent to the Duration of the Period .

name: Event
definition_en: An process whose duration is measured.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The FE  Protagonist is the being or entity that dies.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the dying event happens.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation why the dying event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the dying event occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: How long the Protagonist is dying.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the dying event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Entity
definition_en: Concrete or abstract entity

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Event
definition_en: Name of the event which occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Action
definition_en: The Action that exerts an energy of the level specified by the target.   'He was given a vigorous slap on the ear for his behavior.'

name: Exerter
definition_en: The Exerter which exerts an energy of the level specified by the target.   'More deadly and painful is the chemical weaponry of the camouflaged but lethargic stonefish.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describes the energy exertion of the Exerter, Action, or Force.  'I admired her incredible stamina throughout the marathon.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Exerter, Action, or Force exerts an energy.  'Uncle Dickie was exceedingly dynamic in the play that evening.' Where Degree is expressed by a comparative or superlative form of the target, the FE is marked on the target (as well as on the rest of the comparative/superlative expression, if present):  'Uncle John gave a much lazier performance than Unckle Dickie.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Exerter, Action, or Force exerts an energy.   'Charlie's workout was intense even first thing in the morning.'

name: Force
definition_en: The Force that exerts an energy of the level specified by the target.   ' They were trying to harness some of the lightening's intense power.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the Exerter, Action, or Force exerts an energy.   'Athletes gradually release energy in long-distance events.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Exerter, Action, or Force exerts its energy.  'Because of the added space, our ultimate frisbee game was more vigorous in Golden Gate Park.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain is the field in which the Exerter, Action, or Force exerts its energy.  'On the stage of New York's Felt Forum, Eddie Murphy glows with a kinetic dynamism that captivates the audience.'

name: Buyer
definition_en: The Buyer is the source of the Earnings of the Earner.

name: Earner
definition_en: The Earner is involved in a transaction or set of transactions as the party that receives payment.

name: Earnings
definition_en: Earnings are the money given to the Earner in a transaction, generally in exchange for Goods.

name: Goods
definition_en: Goods is anything including labor or time, for example, which is exchanged for Earnings in a transaction.

name: Rate
definition_en: In some cases, earning is described per unit of Goods.

name: Unit
definition_en: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a 	by-PP.

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the Earner gains money.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the action of earning which reveals correllated details, especially characterizations of the Earner which influence the event.

name: Purpose
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Earner intends to bring about as a result of participating in the Commercial Transaction.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Earner makes their Earnings.  'She made a lot of money in Africa .'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Earner makes their Earnings.  'Pfizer made billions in the 1990s .'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE identifies an event during which the Earner receives Earnings in a transaction.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE denotes a proposition from which the event of earning or losing logically follows.

name: Obstruction
definition_en: The entity which blocks the Eclipsed entity from view.  'Wispy clouds shrouded the treetops.'

name: Eclipsed
definition_en: The entity which is blocked from view.  'The mists obscured the top of the tower.'

name: Vantage_point
definition_en: The position from which an observer, if an observer were present, would have their view of the Eclipsed entity blocked by the Obstruction.  'The gate screened the house from the road.'  Phrases such as "from view" and "from sight" are assumed to indicate that the Eclipsed entity is not visible from any Vantage_point.  'The telescope is blocked from view by a big map of Europe.'  This frame element includes direct reference to observers.  'A fence screens the garden from passersby.'.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Eclipsed entity is blocked from view.  'The bungalow is completely obscured by thick foliage.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the Eclipsed entity which is blocked from view.  'The gazebo was screened by a hedge on one side.'

name: Political_region
definition_en: The Political_region is the nation, state, or other political body within which an economic system exists.

name: Economy
definition_en: The Economy is the state of the Political_region as defined by the production, consumption, etc. of goods and services.

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain of the state for which the Economy is being considered.  'In this way the agrarian economy of the mainland might have proceeded towards a further specialization in agricultural products and a more effective production of food.'

name: Market_type
definition_en: The type of economic market in which the Economy exists.  'For much of its post-1947 history, India ran a socialist economy.' 'China's free-market economy is generating unprecedented but not unlimited press freedoms, and there's momentum.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A further depction of the Economy.  'Hertfordshire enjoys a buoyant economy.'

name: Teacher
definition_en: One who instructs a Student in some area of knowledge or skill.

name: Student
definition_en: One who is instructed by a Teacher in skills or knowledge.

name: Institution
definition_en: An educational establishment, such as a school or college.

name: Subject
definition_en: The area of knowledge or skill which is taught by a Teacher or to a Student.  'She's a French Teacher'

name: Level
definition_en: This FE identifies the Level of a student in his/her education. This is  distinct from the goal or qualification towards which a student is working (Qualification ). 'a graduate student ' 'a fourth grade student ' The above are both Levels, in contrast to: 'a doctoral Student ' 'an MA Student '

name: Qualification
definition_en: A formal Qualification such as an academic degree or a certificate for which a student is aiming.   'She's Studying for a Master's degree' 'She's an MA Student'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the actor (Student or Teacher depending on the profiling of particular words) that lets them achieve the instruction or learning they are attempting.

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the teaching occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location within which the teaching takes place.  <!--Consider whether a possible Place phrase is really where the training took place or is rather part of a description of the Institution. -->

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Skill
definition_en: An action which the Student is able to perform as a result of instruction.   'Taut with worry, Dad taught us how to drive. '

name: Precept
definition_en: A guideline for correct behavior. In most cases, this concerns morally or socially desirable actions.  'My brother taught me not to be mean to guys when I'm not interested in them.'

name: Fact
definition_en: A piece of information that the Student is informed of by the Teacher.  'When I was two she taught me that a quarter was 25 cents and a dime was 10 cents.'

name: Material
definition_en: Educational Material, such as books, tapes, or videos, used by a Teacher or a Student to acquire skills or knowledge.  'All employees have received a booklet INSTRUCTING them on how to report ` anything from unwanted touching and uncalled-for blue jokes to overt demands for sexual favours . "'

name: Role
definition_en: A role, typically professional or vocational,  that the Student is meant to be able to fill as a result of their training.  ' When his father died he went to live with an uncle in Ka'u who trained him as a warrior during his teenage years'

name: Course
definition_en: FN: a program of lectures or other matter dealing with a subject

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Teacher hopes to bring about by teaching.  'I teach so that I can see the little light-bulb light up.'

name: Electricity
definition_en: Electricity is the physical force that is used as power.  'The Brunswick Electric Membership Corporation supplies electricity for sections of Brunswick and Columbus counties.'  'Power's out!'

name: Source

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate the Degree to which the Consideration is important to the Undertaking.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE  identifies the Explanation for which the Consideration is important to the Undertaking.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the individual who devotes time, concentration, or other resources to a Consideration that is important for the success of a larger Undertaking.  'Dell said Friday the company will put more emphasis on selling software'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by assigning the specified level of importance to the Consideration.  'Wilson said it is necessary to place less weight on SAT scores in order to maintain diversity.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that allows the Agent to respond to the importance of the Factor to the Undertaking.

name: Competing_consideration
definition_en: The Competing_consideration is another factor that is relevant to the Undertaking to which the Agent devotes less attention or effort.  'Monophysite Christians  emphasized Christ's divinity over his humanity.'

name: Time

name: Place

name: Manner

name: Artifact

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs-Iteration expressions answer the question how many times. definition_en: The person who enters an employment relationship with an Employer, thereby obligating themself  to perform assigned  Tasks in order to receive Compensation .

name: Employer
definition_en: The person (or institution) that enters an employment relationship with an Employee.

name: Compensation
definition_en: Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing assigned Tasks in the course of their employment.

name: Field
definition_en: This FE identifies the Field which the Employee enters as they take up employment with the Employer.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the employment relationship between an Employer and an Employee comes about.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Employer and  the Employee enter into the employment relationship.

name: Position
definition_en: The label given to a particular type of employment.

name: Task
definition_en: Task identifies the assignment that the Employee is obligated to do when she enters the employment relationship with the Employer.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when an Employer and an Employee establish an employment relationship.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the entity that does the emptying.  'Pat cleared the table of dishes.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme, when overtly expressed, invariably occurs in a PP Complement headed by "of". 'Pat cleared the table of dishes.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the region or container which is emptied of something.  In this frame, the Source occurs as an NP Object. 'Pat cleared the table.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal. 'Kim emptied the basin over the edge of the balcony.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is any expression which tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. 'The children emptied the toy box onto the floor.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Agent empties the Source.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depicitive phrase describing either the Agent or Theme of the emptying. 'Naked, Millhouse emptied the trash can.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Agent empties the Source.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Agent empties the Source.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of  the Agent emptying the Source.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This is the object with which the Agent empties the Source. 'I emptied the tub with a bucket.' 'I peeled the oranges with a knife.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is the non-sentient force which instigates the emptying. 'A basic washing can degrease your workclothes.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the emptying takes place.  'Don't eviscerate him in the house!'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the emptying takes place.  'The prisoners were deloused in June and August.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason why the Agent empties the Source of the Theme.

name: Speaker
definition_en: Speaker, the person who encodes the Message, occurs as the External Argument of all the verbs: 'The teacher phrased the question carefully.'

name: Message
definition_en: The Message is almost invariably expressed in an NP Object. (The only exceptions occur with the verb express, which is occasionally used with that-clause complements.) 'The Prime Minister expressed her sympathy for the victims.' BUT:'The Prime Minister expressed that she was worried about the victims.'

name: Manner
definition_en: For most of the words in this frame, some expression of Manner or Medium is obligatory. As in other frames, Manner expressions characterize the action (in this case, the speech act performed by the Speaker). However, a wide range of Manner expressions occurs in this frame, including the following types: 'True Manner: You should phrase it carefully.' 'Illocutionary Force: You should phrase it as a question.' 'Purpose: You should phrase it so that everyone understands. '

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium expresses the Medium of communication, such as the language used or the specific type of text in which the Message occurs:'Kim formulated her objections in French.' 'Kim formulated her objections in a letter.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the person to whom the communication is directed.

name: Means
definition_en: An act done by the Speaker whereby they achieve the phrasing of the Message. 'He worded his response with precision by consulting the relevant case law.'

name: Group
definition_en: The Group describes the resulting formation of the Individuals.

name: Individuals
definition_en: The Individuals are self-movers who unintentionally meet up.

name: Party_1
definition_en: Party_1 is the grammatically more prominent participant in the encountering event.  It can refer to either a single individual or a larger party separate from Party_2 previous to the by chance meeting.

name: Party_2
definition_en: A grammatically less prominent participant in the encountering event.  It can refer to either a single individual or a larger party separate from Party_1 previous to the by chance meeting.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the unintentional meeting which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects and general descriptions comparing events In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Individuals or Group that also affect the action.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means descibes the way in which the Individuals came together to form the Group.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the encountering event happens.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the encountering event happens.

name: Cause
definition_en: An (non-sentient) entity or state of affairs that leads to the peril to the Valued_entity.

name: Valued_entity
definition_en: The entity which may be negatively impacted as a result of the emperilment.

name: Agent
definition_en: The sentient entity which causes the risk to the Valued_entity.

name: Endangering_act
definition_en: The specific event or state of affairs brought about by the Agent or Cause which endangers the Valued_entity.  'The snow endangered not only the mission but also our lives by slowing us down.'  'His actions imperiled his immortal soul by exposing him to demonic influence.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes an aspect of the endangering act that is not directly related to the cause, intermediate action, or entity involved. 'Members of the underground club would frequently endanger the lives of others with reckless abandon.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Valued_entity is put in danger.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Valued_entity is put in danger.

name: Endeavor
definition_en: The Endeavor is rendered unable to continue its regular operations.  'His small business failed.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is named as one of the causes of failure.  'The local McDonalds shut down in 2008 because the owner died.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time of the failure.  'Her campaign failed in 2008 but found much more support in 2012.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place of the failing Endeavor.  'The hot dog stand on 4th avenue flopped.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances that caused failure. Compared to Explanation, this describes situations or environments that lead to failure, not a specific reason for failure.  'Shops often close down amid political or economic chaos.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes the way in which the Endeavor failed.  'Because of its lack of funding, the website quickly flopped.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: The Containing_event is an event within which the failure occurs.  'Businesses in the Congo failed during the civil war.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A Depictive describes something about the Endeavor.  'The business, unable to maintain appeal in the E.U., closed its doors in 2003.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Endeavor fails.

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the Endeavor fails.

name: Rule
definition_en: The Rule is the set of constrants on behavior that the Agent implements (i.e., forces others to obey or face consequences).  'Employers should strictly enforce a prohibition against use of any substance that may affect a worker's physical or mental ability.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time for which the Rule is or is not in effect.  'The coat-and-tie dress code for the Plimsoll Club in the World Trade Center was strictly enforced for years.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Agent enforces the Rule.  'That particular regulation was only enforced in 1920.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place at which the Rule is or is not enforced.  'For this reason they enforced the settlement system in America just as strictly as in Germany.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state-of-affairs under which the Agent puts the Rule into effect.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A cause, reason, or other explanation for the enforcing of the Rule.

name: Focal_participant
definition_en: The individual or group who is obligated to follow the Rule.  'Can a landlord <target>enforce</target> rules upon tenants?'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent, often an institution, governmental organization, or arm thereof, puts into effect (i.e., enforces) a Rule.  'Can a landlord <target>enforce</target> rules upon tenants?'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes some state of the Agent, or provides additional characterization of the event.  'The coat-and-tie dress code for the Plimsoll Club in the World Trade Center was strictly enforced for years.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is an intermediate action done by the Agent in order to enforce the Rule.  'Since 1961 the church has enforced it by "disfellowshipping" or expelling un-repentant members who wilfully accept prohibited blood components.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent enforces the Rule.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes how fully the Rule was enforced.

name: Medium
definition_en: This FE describes the medium through which the rule was enforced.  It may occur in the same syntactic position as the Agent. 'The rules will be enforced by a new computer system that tracks people's movements.'

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of enforcing the rule.

name: Judge
definition_en: The judge of the court in which the accused enters a plea.

name: Accused
definition_en: The person entering the plea in court. 'Joy Peterson pleaded innocent to the murder of his son.'

name: Charges
definition_en: The crime with which the Accused is charged 'Simpson pleaded not guilty to the murder of his wife.'

name: Plea
definition_en: The Plea that a defendant makes. 'The student pleaded guilty to stealing a bike.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Court
definition_en: The Court is the institution before which the plea is entered.

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Salient parts that make up the Entity.

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: Formational_cause indicates the action that brings about the features of an Entity.

name: Name
definition_en: This FE is used for the Name of an Entity.

name: Entity
definition_en: A thing (either abstract or physical) that exists with some degree of permanence.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Entity belongs to.

name: Individuals
definition_en: This FE identifies the people or things that form  the Entourage.  'Just before eleven o'clock, one of the consultants came to do a ward round, followed by his entourage of junior doctors and medical students.'

name: Entourage
definition_en: This FE identifies the collection of entities that follow the Attended.  'Most of the large entourage the president had brought with him quietly left him.'

name: Aggregate_property
definition_en: This FE describes a property of the Entourage rather than the Individuals and is used to tag the adjective that modifies the entourage noun when it is unambiguous.  'Most of the large entourage the president had brought with him quietly left him.'

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to the Entourage.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location or political locale that the Entourage exists within.

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant Domain as it pertains to the Entourage.

name: Attended_person
definition_en: The Attended_person is followed by the Entourage.  'The lord's train consisted of several dozen servants, cooks, and other attendants.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who removes the Information.

name: Information
definition_en: The thing that the Agent removes from the Document.

name: Cause
definition_en: A non-agentive entity that removes the Information.

name: Document
definition_en: The collection of pieces of information from which the specific Information is removed.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Agent or Cause removes the Information from the Document.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Agent or Cause removes the Information from the Document.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Agent or Cause removes the Information from the Document.

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the Agent or Cause removes the Information from the Document.

name: Escapee
definition_en: The Escapee manages to leave the Undesirable_location. 'Benjamin escaped from Germany.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal identifies any expression which tells where the Escapee ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.  'Benjamin escaped to the United States.'

name: Means
definition_en: covers any act performed by the Escapee brings about the escape.   'Benjamin escaped from Germany by bribing the border guards.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner is used for any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion, including descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, etc.  'Benjamin escaped from Germany with difficulty.'

name: Undesirable_location
definition_en: The Undesirable_location is where the Escapee begins.  'Benjamin escaped  from Germany.'

name: Speed
definition_en: Speed idenitifies the rate at which the escaping occurs.  'Benjmain speedily escaped  from Germany.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: Vehicle identifies the means of conveyance by which the Escapee leaves the Undesirable_location.  'Benjamin escaped in a lorrie.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the escaping occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the escaping takes place. 'Benjamin escaped from Germany to rsave his life.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Escaping occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies a word or  phrase describing a participant of an action. 'Benjamin escaped unscathed.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path describes the trajectory of motion of the Escapee.  'Benjmain escaped from Germany along the southern border.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the (abstract) nearness of the Escapee to being caught in the Undesirable_location.  'Benjamin's narrow escape from Germany left him fearful.'

name: Distance
definition_en: The distance along a path away from the Undesirable_location that the Escapee travels.  'She escaped a few feet away, then looked back at him coldly.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The situation that explains why the (instance of) the event occurred.  'We flew the coop 'cuz we knew pappy was coming home .'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The individual who has considered evidence or performed calculations to produce the approximation.  'Her estimation was that they had exported up to 180000 fish.'

name: Value
definition_en: The position or area  on the feature scale that the Cognizer has concluded the Item occupies.  'Sotheby 's estimate of its value was $10m-$14m.'

name: Item
definition_en: The entity that possesses a feature whose Value the Cognizer has approximated.  'He's an engineer and he is supposed to know the estimate of the house.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: Some fact perceived by the Cognizer which has contributed to their estimation of the Value.   'The habitat area based estimate is probably the more reliable projection of the two.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Cognizer formed the estimate.  'That is 30000 higher than last year's estimate of 2.65 million'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Cognizer has formed their estimate.

name: Estimation
definition_en: A proposition expressing the Cognizer's approximation of a feature's Value.  'One estimate was that eventually I had lost about 80% of my blood.'

name: Question
definition_en: An open proposition for which the Cognizer has approximated the Value of a variable.  'Galliard decided Rwanda was different, and he went public with his estimate of how many people had been killed in a matter of two weeks.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The individual who considers evidence or performs calculations to arrive at an approximation.  'The government estimated the cost of meeting EC water standards at £3-4 billion.'

name: Feature
definition_en: The feature is a scalar property of the Item.  'In one march from 42 Street down to Washington Square Park, the crowds were estimated in size from 125000 (NYPD estimate) to over 200000 (march organizers).'

name: Value
definition_en: The position or area  on the Feature scale that the Cognizer concludes the Item occupies.  'Sotheby 's have estimated its value at $10m-$14m.'

name: Item
definition_en: The entity that possesses the Feature whose Value the Cognizer seeks to approximate.  'I estimated the house at about 60-65% full.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: Some fact perceived by the Cognizer which contributes to their estimation of the Feature's Value.  'He then needs to estimate the desired shelf stock size on the basis of this record of use.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Cognizer forms the estimate of the Feature's Value.  'The US Forest Service estimated last year that 45 million piñons have died so far in north-central New Mexico.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Cognizer forms their estimate.  'At the London School of Economics they estimated that China would have to spend 2% of gross. domestic product on higher. education for 15 years'

name: Estimation
definition_en: A proposition expressing the Cognizer's approximation of a Feature's Value.  'At the time they estimated there to be as many as four million to the acre.'

name: Question
definition_en: An open proposition for which the Cognizer seeks to approximate the Value of a variable.  'Then Sandia estimated how many people would die and be injured within the first year due to their radiation exposure.'  ' He estimated the length of his nose at 6 inches but it was only 2 inches.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Cognizer enabling estimating.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner is used for any expression which describes a property of the activity of Estimating

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Cognizer estimates.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state-of-affairs enabling the estimating to occur.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE describes how the Estimation made by the Cognizer corresponds to reality. This FE can be represented by "correctly" or "wrong."

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Area
definition_en: This FE is used for phrases that describe a general Area in which motion occurs when it is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Locative setting adjuncts of motion expressions may also be assigned this frame element.  'Smithers fled and evaded them all over the ship.'</def-root >

name: Path
definition_en: Path is used for any description of a trajectory of the motion of the Evader, including directional phrases.  'Smithers fled northward.'  'Smithers evaded the police through the empty field.'

name: Evader
definition_en: The Evader moves under its own power to Capture or contact with the Pursuer. Normally the Evader frame element is expressed as an external argument.   'The mouse eluded the cats for only a few minutes.'

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: This  FE identifies  the Mode_of_transportation that the Evader uses to move.  It can either bea part of the Evader's own body or a vehicle. ' Smithers got away from us on foot .' ' Smithers got away from us on bike .'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Evader bringd about the evasion.   'Smithers evaded the police by ducking behind the dumpster.'

name: Pursuer
definition_en: The Pursuer is going after the Evader unless they act.  'The mouse eluded the cats for only a few minutes.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE is used for any expression that describes  the Degree to which the Evader avoids Capture or contact with the Pursuer.  'The mouse barely eluded the cats.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the evading occurs.  It is used for any expression that does not relate directly to the trajectory of motion, including speed, steadiness, and grace. 'Smithers evaded the police gracefully.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This  FE identifies the Purpose for which the Evading is done.  'Smithers evaded the police to prevent being captured.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which the Evading is. done. 'Smithers fled because he feared capture.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the Evader evades the Pursuer, or avoids Capture.  'Smithers evaded the police at all costs.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time at which the Evading occurs. 'Smithers got away at the stroke of midnight.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive is used to identify the state of any of the participants in the evading event.  'Smithers evaded the police barefoot.'

name: Speed
definition_en: This FE marks the Speed at which the Evader evades the Pursuer. 'Smithers got away from the police at lightning speed.'

name: Capture
definition_en: An actual or hypothetical  event in which the Pursuer takes physical control of the Evader.  'Rýmirez-Sýnchez , tried in absentia , had evaded capture since the murders in Paris on June 27 , 1975 '

name: Profiled_item
definition_en: In active sentences, the Profiled_item is the grammatically more prominent one of the items that are compared and realized as  the subject. .  'This PC stacks up well against its competitors '

name: Standard_item
definition_en: In active setnnces, the Standard_item is  the grammatically less prominent element, i.e. the object or an oblique.  ' This PC stacks up well against its competitors'

name: Attribute
definition_en: This Frame Elements marks constituents that indicate in which respect Item-1 and Item-2 are equal to each other.  ' The Tri-Cities stack up well against the competition in the area of innovation'

name: Degree
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate how close the Profiled_item and the  Standard_item are to each other on the scale evoked by the Attribute.  'A peanut butter and jelly sandwich stacks up well against other popular food items  '

name: Standard_attribute
definition_en: The Standard_attribute is used when the standard is a specific value on  a scale. '  We equalled <fex name = "Standard_attribute">father's skills . '

name: Profiled_attribute
definition_en: The Profiled_attribute is a particular value on a scale which is being compared to a Standard_item or Profiled_attribute.

name: Comparison_set
definition_en: The Comparison_set includes the Standard_item and is what the Profiled_item is judged with respect to.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Profiled_item rivals the Standard_item.  'In Africa, the level of drug resistance rivals even Noatirtin's vaunted efficacy.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Profiled_item rivals the Standard_item.  'American caviar now rivals Russia's in quality.'

name: Event
definition_en: Name of the event which occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which an event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: How long the Event takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Event occurs. 'Stuff like this happens every day at 3:00pm.'

name: Timespan
definition_en: The period within which an Event has occurred.  'It was the largest food fight to occur since the time Jimmy's mom packed him extra Sloppy Joes.'  'From 1992 to 2014, my amazing birthday celebration has happened 22 times.'

name: Entity
definition_en: Concrete or abstract entity

name: State
definition_en: State of an Entity.

name: Entity
definition_en: Concrete or abstract entity

name: State
definition_en: State of an Entity.

name: Instance
definition_en: The particular Instance of a given event. All LUs in this frame incorporate this Frame Element.  'He dumped trash for the last time.'  'He tapped me twice on the shoulder.'

name: Event
definition_en: The event that occurred in one or more instances.  'Listen to this song six times.'

name: Instance_prop
definition_en: A property of the particular Instance.  'This is the first time I've grown such delicious tea.'

name: Iteration_count
definition_en: The specific number of iterations.  'The last 3 times I did this, I lost the game.'  'This one time, at band camp, we went to the lake.'

name: Event
definition_en: This FE identifies the event which occurs and affects the Entity.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies where the event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the event occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which an event occurs.

name: Entity
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity, concrete or abstract.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Event happens to the Entity.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The person who perceives the Event and changes his or her mind.

name: Content
definition_en: The new idea that the Cognizer accepts as a result of experiencing the Event.

name: Event
definition_en: The Event which motivates the Cognizer to change his/her mind.  'The accident convinced him to drive slower.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Cognizer's mind is changed.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Cognizer is affected by an outside Event.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Cognizer accepts the Content.

name: Support
definition_en: Support is a fact that lends epistemic support to a claim, or that provides a reason for a course of action. Typically it is expressed as an External Argument. 'The fact that you lied to me shows that I shouldn't trust you.' 'The look on your face reveals that you are lying.'

name: Proposition
definition_en: This is a belief, claim, or proposed course of action to which the Support lends validity. Normally it is expressed as a Finite Clause Complement: 'The fact that you lied to me shows that I shouldn't trust you.' Some words in this frame require the proposition to be expressed as an NP Object: 'The fact that you lied substantiates the claim that you can't be trusted.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the degree to which a Proposition is supported.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the manner in which a Proposition is supported. 'The results of the experiments proved the hypothesis brilliantly.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intermediate logical step that justifies the relationship of the Support to the Proposition. 'Tiny patterns in fossil rocks can demonstrate that dinosaurs and pterosaurs were (at least potentially) warm blooded by showing that they had feathers or hair, today found only among endotherms.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the status of the Support within its relationship to the Proposition. This proves my conclusions all by itself.

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Domain_of_relevance
definition_en: This FE identifies the domain (usually, time or space) for which a given Proposition is true.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The person for whom the Proposition is supported by the Support.  'The behavior of the children indicated to the teacher that further action was required on his part.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person who remembers the Phenomenon .

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The Phenomenon is the mental content that a Cognizer remembers.  'You remind me of my uncle Jerry'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which Cognizer perceives the Stimulus to match the Phenomenon.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including speed (quickly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). Other expressions involving how the experience affects the Cognizer may also be expressed (painfully).

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration is the amount of time for which the Stimulus continues to remind the Cognizer of the Phenomenon.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Stimulus evokes the Phenomenon.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Cognizer remembers the Phenomenon.

name: Stimulus
definition_en: The entity or situation that causes the Cognizer to think of the Phenomenon.  ' Internationalization conjures up a world of diplomatic exchanges and international agencies in which the interests of ex-colonial and great powers still linger'

name: Feature
definition_en: A characteristic of the Stimulus that contributes to the perception of similarity to the Phenomenon.  'She reminds me of your mother with her darting beady eyes.'

name: Examiner
definition_en: One who administers a test of some kind.'The teacher tested the students.'

name: Examinee
definition_en: One who undergoes a test of some kind.'The students took a test.'

name: Knowledge
definition_en: The ability, practice, or command of information on which an Examinee is tested.  'I took my driving test.' 'Is there anything more odious than a History test strictly on dates ?'

name: Qualification
definition_en: A credential or status that one acquires by passing an Examination.'He took the college entrance exam.'

name: Examination
definition_en: The Examination that somebody takes.'The examination tests driving skills.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Examiner assesses the Examinee. 'The sarge tested him by having him take his rifle apart and put it back together.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Examiner wants to bring about by giving the Examinee the Examination.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the examination takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the examination occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Examiner that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Exchanger_1
definition_en: In cases where the Exchangers involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, this FE identifies the conversational participant with greater semantic and syntactic prominence, as compared with Exchanger_2. That is, Exchanger_1 is generally encoded as Subject, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Exchanger_1. Thus a Purpose (or Means, Depictive, or Manner) is construed to be that of Exchanger_1, not necessarily that of Exchanger_2 or the group of Exchangers as a whole.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the exchange occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which Exchanger_1 or the Exchangers make the trade.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the exchange takes place.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which Exchanger_1 or the Exchangers effect the trade.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the exchange act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of Exchanger_1 or Exchangers that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Theodosia and Felix carefully exchanged their bunches of flowers.'

name: Exchanger_2
definition_en: In cases where the Exchangers involved in a conversation are construed as two separate groups with different levels of volitionality or control, Exchanger_2 refers to the semantically and grammatically less prominent group. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with). Note that it is possible for a single role to correspond to multiple referents. For example, if the prepositional object in the example below were plural, we would still assign it the single role Exchanger_2.   'The trade with Cuba went exactly as planned. '

name: Exchangers
definition_en: In some sentences both participants are expressed by the Subject, and there is no 'with'-phrase (cf example 1). In sentences like this, the Subject is assigned the FE role Exchangers. In such sentences, the Subject always denotes more than one person, and it is understood that the reciprocal communication takes place between these two (or more) people. The Subject may denote two or more people either through conjunction, as in example 1, or through plurality, as in example 2, or by denoting a group, as in example 3. In each of these cases the FE Exchangers is assigned. Notice that for nouns in the Exchange frame, it is possible for the Exchangers role to be expressed by a prepositional phrase as in example 4.   'Smithers and Kornfeldt traded Pez dispensers.' 'My neighbors swappedlawn mowers .' 'The group exchanged phone numbers.' 'The prisoner exchange between North and South Dakota went bad somehow.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of Exchanger_1 or Exchangers during the exchange.  'Howell traded brooms with Susanne, uncertain of whether she would prefer his.  '

name: Theme_1
definition_en: The item that begins in the possession of Exchanger_1.   ' I tucked the pistol between my belt and tunic top (how I wish I had kept it, but I later swapped it with a Canadian for some cigarettes.'

name: Theme_2
definition_en: The item that begins in the possession of Exchanger_2.  ' The organization bought the property in 1999, then swapped it with the BLM for about 100 parcels in 10 counties ranging in size from one to 920 acres.'

name: Themes
definition_en: The items which change possession between the Exchangers.  'They swapped guitars.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element denotes how often the Exchangers trade Themes.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Money_owner
definition_en: The person who exchanges Sum_1 for Sum_2.  ' Kornfeldt hurried through customs, grabbed a city map at a tourist information desk, changed $40 USD into about 300 Hong Kong dollars before leaving the airport'

name: Sum_1
definition_en: An amount of money in the Source_currency that the Money_owner exchanges for an amount in the Target_currency.  'I said forget it and just exchanged $40 US cash into $47 and change in Canadian. '

name: Source_currency
definition_en: The kind of currency of the Money_owner has before the exchange.  'We stopped at a bank were we exchanged Euros for Danish money.'

name: Sum_2
definition_en: The amount of money in the Target_currency that the Money_owner receives in exchange for Sum_1.  'On the bus we exchanged $50 for 1410 rubles.'

name: Exchange_service
definition_en: The individual or institution which changes the Money_owner's money into the Target_currency.  'Bill exchanged $100 at a bank, before hitting the bike path for Krems.'

name: Target_currency
definition_en: The kind of currency that the Money_owner receives as part of the exchange.  ' We had exchanged $100 into francs in LAX to be able to pay for the cab ride upon arrival. '

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the money is exchanged.  'I exchanged $100 in Croatia because i needed a round trip bus ticket to sarajevo.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the currency is exchanged.  'We walked around Eyre Square and exchanged money before walking into Taaffes pub and grabbing my first draught pint of Guinness of the trip.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the exchange event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Money_owner that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  'He carefully exchanged his dollars for roubles.'

name: Exchange_rate
definition_en: 'I exchanged $100 in $20 bills at an exchange rate of 24.4 to 1.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Money_owner whereby the exchange is acheived.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The action that the Money_owner is attempting to accomplish with the exchange.

name: Money
definition_en: Currency that is being exchanged by the Money_owner.  ' I exchanged $1000 of my money at the bank. '

name: Member
definition_en: The person who used to belong to a Group.  'I 'm afraid that I was expelled from the Society after they found I endorsed him.'

name: Group
definition_en: A set of people standing in a semi-permanent relationship together.  'Giles bemoaned his expulsion from the Future Farmers of America'

name: Authority
definition_en: An empowered subset of the Group which decides to expel its former Member.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Member is excluded.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A cause, reason, or other explanation for the exclusion of the Member.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Member is excluded.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Authority excludes the Member.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive describes a participant in the exclusion event.

name: Excreta
definition_en: The Excreta is the waste expelled by the body. 'Dr. Nick vomited puke across the table.'

name: Excreter
definition_en: The Excreter is the agent who excretes the Excreta.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the starting point of the Excreta's motion.

name: Path
definition_en: Path identifies the trajectory of the Excreta.

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is where the Excreta finishes its motion.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Excreter engages in excretion.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Excreter engages in excretion.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifieis the Place where the excretion occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Excreter engages in excretion.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose is the motivation behind the Excreter's act. 'Rod Flanders vomited to get out of choir practice.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: TheFrequency is the number of times per time period that the Excreter is engaged in exctretion.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which all of the Excreta are removed from the body.  'Patients need to void their bladder completely before surgery'

name: Plan
definition_en: The Plan is a goal or purpose that the Agent carries out.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time for which the Plan is or is not in effect.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Agent puts the Plan into effect.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place at which the Plan is or is not operational.  [CHANGE: or, place where agent puts into effect? 2 fes?]

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state-of-affairs under which the Agent puts the Plan into effect.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A cause, reason, or other explanation for the implementation of the Plan

name: Focal_participant
definition_en: The individual or group who is obligated to follow the Plan.  [CHANGE: may only be relevant for "implemented the policy for residents of florida only"]

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent, often an institution or governmental organization, puts a Plan into effect. The Agent is generally a primary participant in the Plan, but a separate Focal_participant may be specified.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes some state of the Agent, or provides additional characterization of the event of executing the plan.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is an intermediate action done by the Agent in order to execute the Plan.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Agent executes the Plan.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes how fully the Plan was executed.

name: Medium
definition_en: This FE describes the medium through which a plan was executed.  It may occur in the same syntactic position as the Agent. 'The policy will be implemented by a new computer system.'

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of executing the plan.  'We implemented the new approach with astounding results'

name: Executioner
definition_en: The Executioner is the individual who performs the execution.  'The truth is, we have all put them to death.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which an Executioner performs an execution.

name: Means
definition_en: The action that is taken that accomplishes the execution 'Execution by lethal injection is certainly humane.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the execution takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the execution is carried out.

name: Execution
definition_en: The punishment of death given to the Executed by the Executioner.

name: Time
definition_en: When the execution occurs.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing a participant in the action.  'He was executed with only a loincloth on.'

name: Executed
definition_en: The Executed is the person who is killed by the Executioner in retribution for the crime that the Executed was convicted of.  'He was to be hanged in the morning.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the execution event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  Moreover, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Executioner that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Explanation
definition_en: Often, there is a constituent expressing the Explanation for the Judge's judgment which the Executioner is carrying out. It is usually a for-PP.  'He was hanged for his crimes.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Instance
definition_en: A thing or episode that is considered exemplary of a certain Type.

name: Type
definition_en: The category of things or events from which an Instance is picked out.

name: Domain
definition_en: The comparative terms along which the Instance is deemed an exemplar of the Type.

name: Instance_prop
definition_en: A property of the particular Instance.

name: Entity
definition_en: The thing being judged by its similarity to an ideal.

name: Comparison_set
definition_en: The group which the Entity is a member of.

name: Domain
definition_en: The domain along which the Entity is judged to be exemplary.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Entity is exemplary.

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who is trying to improve or maintain their physical fitness.  'The manager exercises before and after work.'

name: Body_part
definition_en: An area of the Agent's body that the activity is direct at.  'Is there a way to exercise the neck muscles?'

name: Means
definition_en: Something that the Agent uses to exercise.  'He trains with weight machines.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A general description of how the Agent acts while exercising.  'With only 2 weeks until the race, Joan was exercising frantically.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time that the Agent exercises.  'I like to exercise at 3 am.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location of the Agent while exercising.  'Some people only exercise in gyms.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Agent works on their fitness.  'He rarely works out.'

name: Subtype
definition_en: This frame element describes a subtype of the more general exercise category.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Agent exercises.  'The doctor told me I have to exercise to lose weight.'

name: Entity
definition_en: Some entity, abstract or concrete, which is stated to exist.

name: Time
definition_en: A time at which the entity is in existence.

name: Duration
definition_en: The period during which the Entity exists.

name: Inherent_purpose
definition_en: The reason why the Entity exists.  Generally, this is more specifically the reason why the Entity was made.

name: State
definition_en: The condition that the Entity exists in.  'Natural electricity exists in many forms:  in storms, solar wind, and nerve impulses.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A situation, force, or entity which brings about the existence of the Entity.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the Entity exists.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the Entity is declared to exist

name: Viewpoint
definition_en: The perspective of an individual who judges whether they consider the Entity (or further state of affairs) to exist or not.  'For him, there 's just too much drink in the world.'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Item
definition_en: This FE identifies the Item whose size changes. 'Joan's new sweater shrank to a size that might fit a doll.'

name: Dimension
definition_en: Change of size may be limited to or described in terms of a single Dimension.   'The wall grew in height.' 'The piglet had grown 6 inches in length.'

name: Group
definition_en: This FE identifies the Group in which an Item changes size.  'Tails lengthened 10% among rats more than 3 days old.'

name: Initial_size
definition_en: Initial_size is used for the size of the Item before any change occurs.  It is rarely expressed without Result_size also being explicit.  Initial_size generally occurs in a PP-from Complement.  'The glacier shrank from 1km square to 400 square meters.'

name: Result_size
definition_en: Result_size is the size that the Item has after the event.  It is typically expressed in a PP Complement headed by to.  'The trees grow to 25 feet.'

name: Size_change
definition_en: This FE identifies the Size_change of an Item.  'A 2-3cm expansion in width is required.'

name: Rate
definition_en: This FE identifies the Rate of change of the value.  'The balloon inflates about 2 cubic cm a minute.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time that the expansion takes.  'The piglet had grown 6 inches over two months.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the expansion occurs.

name: Co-variable
definition_en: Co_variable is the quantity that varies commensurately with the size of the Item, usually construed to be causally linked to the size.  'The snake's belly expanded with each mouse it ate.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE is used for any description of the Manner of the expansion including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the expansion occurs. 'Joan's new sweater had shrunk completely.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path is used for any expression that gives information about points on the scale of size that the Item traverses between the starting and ending point of its movement. 'The muscle tissue contracts down to less than half its original length.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Where the Iteam ends up due to Expansion.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: This is the person who believes some Phenomenon will take place in the future. It is normally expressed as an External Argument: Pat expects that the Yankees will win the World Series.

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: This is what the Cognizer believes will happen in the future. It can be expressed as a Finite Clause Complement, an NP Object, or a VP Complement with or without an NP Object (see General Grammatical Observations):  'Pat expects that the Yankees will win the World Series.' 'Pat expects a big win.' 'Pat expects the Yankees to win the World Series.'  General Grammatical Observations:  Many of the verbs in this frame allow Raising: Pat expects it to rain. In the example above, the word it is grammatically the Object of the target verb expect, but it does not express an FE. Rather, it is merely construed as the External Argument of the verb rain, which heads the VP Complement of the target. In this situation, both the raised consituent it and the VP Complement are marked with the Phenomenon FE, but are marked as separate constituents. That is because the Object can be passivized and therefore not appear adjacent to the VP Complement: It is expected to rain.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action 'We awaited the lunar eclipse sitting atop a hill.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Evidence
definition_en: Words in this frame may occur with a PP headed by from which expresses the Evidence on which knowledge or belief is based: I have learned from experience that poison oak can be painful.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Cognizer foresees the Phenomenon.  'Even at the far side of the house I could predict what was going on the kitchen.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Cognizer makes the prediction.  'She predicted the outcry several months ago.'

name: Topic
definition_en: An entity that serves as the focus of a predicted Phenomenon.  'Predictions about stock prices are notoriously undependable.'

name: Time_of_phenomenon
definition_en: The time that the Cognizer expects the Phenomenon to occur.  Note that it is distinct from simple Time, which is when the Cognizer is actually involved in thinking about the Phenomenon.  'Another arrival is expected this Tuesday .'

name: Location
definition_en: The Location  is the place of business or residence prototypically occupied by the Person.  'I couldn't access the details of prospective buyers and sellers and was uncontactable when I was out of the office.'

name: Person
definition_en: The Person is located in or at a place that they customarily occupy.   'The doctor is not in right now.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Person occupies the Location.  'Call work, tell them you'll be in in the afternoon.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of the time interval during which the Person occupies the Location.  'It's only nine o'clock, so he won't be in for another two hours.'

name: Resource
definition_en: The Resource is exhausted over time by being used.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent uses the Resource.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Agent uses the Resource for a Purpose.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action ( deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Agent exhausts the Resource.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent exhausts the Resource.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent exhausts the Resource.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Resource is depleted by the Agent.  'Their program used up very little processing power.'

name: Goods
definition_en: The FE Goods is the item(s) whose price is being assessed.  Goods is usually an External Argument:  'These paintings are very pricey. '

name: Payer
definition_en: The person whose Asset is given up in order to achieve an Intended_event.  This FE is often expressed as INI.   'A holiday in Europe is very expensive for me.' 'Europe is not cheap. INI'

name: Asset
definition_en: The price of or payment made for the Goods.  'The painting was cheap at $600.' '$600 is exorbitant for that painting!'

name: Origin
definition_en: The place where a transaction would take place, generally where Goods and services are created or sold. 'Shirts are cheap at K-Mart.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which Goods are cheap or expensive.</def-root >

name: Intended_event
definition_en: The event that the Payer brings about by deploying the Asset.  'Attending summer school is expensive.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when a transaction takes place.  'No, they've got a special on; it's really cheap there on Tuesdays'

name: Rate
definition_en: The amount of an Asset relative to some measure of the Goods

name: Body_part
definition_en: The location on the body of the Experiencer where the bodily injury takes place. 'I cut my finger on the envelope.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: The event in which the bodily injury takes place. 'I broke my arm in the accident.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner in which the injury takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the harming event occurs. 'She fell and hit her head out in the playground.'

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The being or entity that is injured. 'The squirrel abraded its tail as it twitched nervously in the confined space.' 'Then I cut myself on an envelope.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the harming event occurs. 'So you cut your leg on the window frame at six o'clock, correct?'

name: Injuring_entity
definition_en: The Experiencer injures him/herself on an Injuring_entity.  'He punched me, but he hurt his fist on my nose.'

name: Severity
definition_en: The extent to which the Experiencer is affected by the injury. 'The suspect injured his leg severely climbing the fence.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times that the injury happens to the Experiencer. 'I jammed my pinky on these juggling clubs three times in the last hour.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time during which the Experiencer repeatedly receives bodily injuries.  'Smithers stubbed his toe on the couch for several months before he got used to its new location.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that the Experiencer has an experience of bodily harm.  'Sue stubbed her toe three times today'

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer experiences the emotion or other internal state.

name: Content
definition_en: Content is what the Experiencer's feelings or experiences are directed towards or based upon.  The Content differs from a stimulus because the Content is not construed as being direcly responsible for causing the emotion. ' Everyone loves compliments.' ' Everyone loves being complimented.'  ' His parents despaired of him.' ' John likes that I cook him lunch.' ' I am afraid of spiders.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the explanation for why an Experiencer experiences the particular emotion. ' People love giant pandas because they look like teddy bears.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the experience occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Expressor
definition_en: The Frame Element Expressor marks expressions that indicate a body part, gesture or other expression of the Experiencer that reflect his or her emotional state.  They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.  ' The delight on her face was mixed with asonishment. ' ' The worshipper's apprehensive praise revealed his lacking devotion. '

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Content.  'Very few physical science students stressed the intellectual  enjoyment of the degree course. '

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the area about which the Experiencer has the particular experience. ' Mr. Whiskers was upset about his cat treats.'

name: State
definition_en: The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer. 'Tracy was in an irritated mood. '

name: Event
definition_en: The Event is the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in. ' It felt pretty awkward to partake in such a nervous ceremony.' Here we know that the ceremony was filled with nervous Experiencers.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances FE encodes the circumstances or conditions under which the Experiencer experiences the emotion. Unlike Content it does not give the specific content of the emotion, but the Content can often be inferred from the Circumstances.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Experiencer is in the specified emotional state.  'Last year, Bob was still interested in the young Republicans.'

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer reacts emotionally or psychologically to the Stimulus. 'Horror films terrify Edna.'

name: Stimulus
definition_en: The Stimulus is the event or entity which brings about the emotional or psychological state of the Experiencer. 'The news greatlyalarms all the women of the village.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree is the degree to which the Stimulus brings about an emotion in the Experiencer.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies a phrase which describes a state of the Experiencer.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Stimulus affects the Experiencer.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Stimulus affects the Experiencer.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the Stimulus affecting the Experiencer.

name: Circumstances
