definition_en: The Circumstances is the circumstances under which the Stimulus brings about the experience. 'Soft music calms the children when they're wound-up.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason why the Stimulus causes the emotion in the Experiencer.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Experiencer has an emotion as caused by the Stimulus.

name: Experimenter
definition_en: The Experimenter is the individual conducting the Experiment. 'Justin's experiment turned out to be rather successful.'  'The professor performed an interesting experiment for the class. '

name: Control_group
definition_en: The group of entities in the Experiment which have not been treated and are compared to the Treatment_group or Treated_individual. ''  'The control in George's experiment consisted of 17 mice.'

name: Control_group_member
definition_en: An individual entity of the Experiment which is left untreated and then compared with the Treatment_group or the Treated_individual.  ''

name: Treatment_group
definition_en: A group of subjects that receive Treatment and are compared to the Control_group or Controlled_individuals. '' 'The experiment's rats who received a dose of the drug every hour did not live to see the next day. DNI'

name: Treated_individual
definition_en: An individual subject that receives treatment and is then compared to the Control_group or Controlled_individual.  'One rat's treatment caused it to outlive the rats of the control group.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time the Experiment lasts.  'The six week long study was published in a prominent scientific journal.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place in which the Experiment is conducted.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Experimenter conducts the Experiment.

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: A property that belongs to either the Control_group or the Treatment_group.  Usually expressed by a PP. 'The control for the problem of imprecise sensing is currently being monitored. '

name: Result
definition_en: The Result depicts the outcome of the Experiment. 'The experiment proves the new drug is effective treating the disease.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A Descriptor identifies a characteristic or description of the Experiment or the Subjects not captured by any other frame element. 'Mica's clever study was conducted in 2011.'

name: Experiment
definition_en: The test or Experiment conducted by the Experimenter using a Control_group and a Treatment_group. '' 'Jeff's experimentshowed the drug to be harmful to human health.'

name: Hypothesis
definition_en: The Hypothesis is a conjecture as to the result of an Experiment.  The Experiment takes place in order to prove the Hypothesis as correct or incorrect.   'Katrina tested her hypothesis yesterday afternoon. '

name: Subjects
definition_en: In this frame Control_group and Treatment_group can be combined and expressed as Subjects.  This FE can also be used for a generic individual on whom the Experiment is being conducted (see second example). 'They were hoping to conduct an experiment on the albino rats.' 'The subject was asked to respond as quickly as possible to the stimuli in front of him.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: A tool used in conducting the Experiment.  Usually expressed by a with-PP. 'Silke experimented with chemical insecticides. '

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject that the Experiment is studying. 'Jimmy conducted an experiment on tropical plants in non-tropical environments.'

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The person whose expertise is assessed.

name: Skill
definition_en: Skill identifies the Protagonist's talent or ability to do things with one's hand or body.

name: Knowledge
definition_en: The area of knowledge (as opposed to a practical skill) in which the Protagonist 's experience is assessed.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Behavior_product
definition_en: A  product of behavior that shows the Protagonist's skill or lack of skill.  'A skillful advertising campaign persuaded voters that his opponent was soft on crime.'

name: Focal_participant
definition_en: This frame element can only occur in place of a skill expression. It refers to the prototypical patient in an action involving the Protagonist. For instance, in the following sentence  the children are experts at some (contextually given) action such as rolling the hoops.  Some children were quite expert with wooden hoops.

name: Role
definition_en: This frame element denotes a role in which the protagonist has developed his expertise.   'His prowess as a surgeon is impressive.'  In many cases, the Role noun secondarily evokes the Skill that is at issue.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner give further description of the way in which the Protagonist exhibits their skill or lack of skill.

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Protagonist has the expertise.

name: Fact
definition_en: A Fact which can be connected by a chain of reasoning to the State_of_affairs.  'This fact alone explains the Sun/climate anomaly.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: A Fact whose cause is under consideration.  'Do increased proinsulin concentrations explain the excess risk of coronary heart disease in diabetic and prediabetic subjects?'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies how much of the State_of_affairs is explained by the Fact.  'This, in my opinion, partially accounts for  why Anakin became a ghost.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE indicates salient characteristics of the Fact considered as an explanation.  'Current life-history theory would readily explain the small males in B if juvenile male mortality were higher than that of females , but adult mortality should not affect the timing of maturity or adult size .'

name: Means
definition_en: An intermediate logical step that justifies the relationship between  the Fact and the State_of_affairs.   'This gives an explanation for the observation by identifying it as an instance of general pattern'

name: Viewpoint
definition_en: The perspective of an individual who judges whether they consider the Fact an explanation for the State_of_affairs.  'To her, this explains things, and we therefore need not discuss it any longer. '

name: Question
definition_en: An open proposition concerning the cause of the State_of_affairs.  'The fact that this remained in Pandora's box explains why men have hope.'  ''

name: Concessive
definition_en: The state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the Concessive.

name: Explosive
definition_en: The Explosive releases a large amount of force, destroying itself and causing damage to the surrounding area.  'The bomb exploded in the middle of the plaza.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the explosion occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the explosion occurs.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is targeted by the explosion or inadvertantly damaged by the explosion. Typically expressed by an on-PP.  'The roadside bomb exploded on 20 civilians just outside the central plaza.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the explosion occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.  'Several of the rockets detonated in the blast.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the Explosive explodes.  'The device can detonate by remote control.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the explosion not specifically covered by other Frame Elements.  'The bomb detonated explosively in the middle of the square.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The strength of the explosion, or to what degree it damaged the affected areas or objects.  'That morning a powerful explosion rocked the city.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often an explosion occurs.  'The daily explosions are enough to drive anyone mad.'

name: Exporter
definition_en: The conscious entity, generally a person, that moves the Goods across a border out of the Exporting_area.    Very often, an Exporting_area will metonymically stand in for the person or persons directly responsible for the movement of the Goods.  In such cases the constituent should be labeled Exporter on the first layer and with the appropriate locational FE on the second layer. 'The U.S. exports most of its peanut products.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: A mobile entity directed by the Exporter that holds the Goods and moves them along from the Exporting_area to the Importing_area.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Exporter that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Exporter that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

name: Goods
definition_en: The items of value whose location is changing.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the state-of-affairs that the Exporter is attempting to bring about by exporting.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that explains why the Exporter moves the Goods across the border.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Exporter moves the Goods.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies the state of a participant during the action 'Kazakhstan exported the petroleum, gleeful at how much they were earning.'

name: Importing_area
definition_en: The FE Importing_area is the place that the Goods end up as a result of motion.

name: Path
definition_en: Path identifies the location of the Goods during transit, i.e. after leaving the Exporting_area and before reaching the Importing_area.  'The exportation of goods across state lines is strictly prohibited.'

name: Exporting_area
definition_en: The place where the Goods are initially, before the the Exporter moves them.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Exporting event belongs to.

name: Communicator
definition_en: The Communicator is the person who expresses the Content (whether spoken or written).    'Reagan gave voice to the innate patriotism of the American people.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the person to whom the Content is communicated.   'After waiting 2-hours for his appointment, Kiyosaki vented his frustration to his rich dad.'

name: Content
definition_en: The attitude or feeling that the Communicator had not previously expressed.  'Members aired their grievances and resented the way higher education was being dealt with.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Communicator that also affect the action (eagerly).   'The girl's grandfather's body was frail but his ideas were strong and his voice rose as he furiously expressed his ideas.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Communicator communicates the Content.    'The students expressed their gratitude by creating colorful hand-made cards for Annie and Renita.'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotional or physical state of the Communicator that leads to their communication.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the observable action or product of the Communicator.   'I do not especially espouse the ideas articulated by Diana Plesa in her article.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Communicator during the statement.  'Hermann considered her to be a tramp unworthy of the Kafka name, and vented his ire with full passion.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Content is communicated.  'Sometimes, children may later put into words a memory from early life, but not customarily.'

name: Place
definition_en: The FE specifies the place where the communication takes place.   'John Ryan voiced concerns in Parliament about the suggestion that somehow the inquiry was not independent.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular Statement event referred to  is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose is the desired result of public expression.  'Because of its spread of membership , it has retained value as a forum where a wide range of ideas and views can be aired for discussion .'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.   'An important policy matter which has been aired occasionally in recent years is the size of academic library collections , compared with the amount of use they receive .'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the communication and any of its participants.  Quite often, Circumstances secondarily provide an Explanation for the particular communication.  'With half the opposition in exile, hardly anyone dared give voice to their deep misgivings .'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the particular public expression logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the expression, but not in all cases.   'The mute had to voice the concerns of her community because there was no-one else to do so.'

name: Authorities
definition_en: The Authorities act on behalf of the Current_jurisdiction, giving up the Suspect to the Crime_jurisdiction.  'French officials extradited him back to Canada.'

name: Current_jurisdiction
definition_en: The jurisdiction (generally a nation) the Suspect starts off in.  'Jones was extradited from Mexico last Thursday to face criminal charges in the United States.'

name: Crime_jurisdiction
definition_en: The jurisdiction (generally a nation) to which the Suspect is sent.  'It was the third time a neo-Nazi was extradited from Denmark to Germany.'

name: Suspect
definition_en: The Suspect is forced to go to the jurisdiction where a crime he or she is suspected of took place or is being tried.  'A hearing on whether or not to extradite Johnson to Isreal will be held tomorrow.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Authorities extradite the Suspect.  'The authorities extradited him for trial in the US'.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Authorities extradite the Suspect.  'The authorities extradited him to the US for drug trafficking'.

name: Legal_basis
definition_en: This FE indicates the basis in law of an extradition. 'He was extradited under the long-standing treaty between the two nations.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which  the Suspect is moved.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the manner of the extradition.  'They are seeking rapid extradition.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the Authorities or Suspect during the extradition.  'It had been five years since his handcuffed extradition from France.'

name: Means
definition_en: The act of the Authorities which brings about the transfer from the Current_jurisdiction to the Crime_jurisdiction.  'The extradited him by continually badgering the French.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the extradition occurs.  'In Europe they extradite more freely than in North America.'

name: Entity
definition_en: An concrete or abstract entity that possesses characteristics that change over time.  'Midway was the ZENITH of Japanese military advancements.'

name: Marker
definition_en: A point or phase in time when, viewed across the actual or expected development, the Entity's powers have reached an extreme high or low point. The point or phase is often identified metonymically by reference to a product created by the Entity or an event involving the Entity.  'Watergate was the ZENITH of American investigative journalism.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity whose Value of a particular gradable Attribute is extreme.  'JetBlue's high of $55.15 was reached on May 6'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.  'East Harlem reached its historic population high of 210000 in 1950.'

name: Value
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the Attribute.  'The state of Michigan reported a new unemployment high of 7%.'

name: Period
definition_en: The period for which values of a particular Attribute of one or more entities are compared.  'Food stamp error rates are at an all-time low.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain for which there is a Value of an Attribute of an Entity.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of some property of the Extreme_value.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Extreme_value event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of Expression.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the Expression occurs.

name: Expression
definition_en: This is the Expression made.'He gave a wide grin.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: This is the person who exhibitis the Expression.'Ryan grinned.'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The Expression may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause - the Possessor's mental or emotional state.  Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement as in: 'Kim made a frown in concentration'.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the face saliently exhibiting the Expression.  'The smile on her face was repayment enough.'

name: Conveyed_emotion
definition_en: The emotion that is conveyed by a particular Expression. 'He had an angry expression.'

name: Intended_perceiver
definition_en: An entity toward which the Expression is directed.

name: External_cause
definition_en: The state of affairs perceived by the Possessor which leads to an Internal_cause (emotion, etc.) which then gives rise to the Expression.'I made a grimace at her clumsiness.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time for which the facial Expression is held.  'A brief smile appeared on his face'

name: Actor
definition_en: The Actor is the individual who performs the Action and can thus be characterized with repsect to how that Action affects the Affected_party.

name: Action
definition_en: The Action is judged based on how just and appopriate it is to the Affected_party in a particular situation.

name: Grounds
definition_en: The Grounds is the event or state that requires some decision or action in response to it for which the Actor is judged.

name: Affected_party
definition_en: The Affected_party's treatment is what determines the evaluation of the Actor's Action.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree is the extent to which the Action or Actor is evaluated as being fair or unfair.

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is the area in which the Action is judged.

name: Manner
definition_en: A holistic characterization of the description of the Actor, including depictions of the Actor's state in terms of how it affects the entire description.  'You have been cruelly unfair to me !'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.

name: Sleeper
definition_en: The Sleeper is the entity that falls asleep.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time where the event occurs.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim has false beliefs as a result of exposure to a Deception.  'Seventeen respected scientists fell for the lie before it was revealed as a hoax.'

name: Deception
definition_en: The Deception is perceived by the Victim, leading to false beliefs. The Deception, orchestrated by an agent or agents with the intention of deception, may be any misinformation, event, or situation perceived by the Victim.  'Even the smartest person can fall for a cleverly-designed scam.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Victim falls for the Deception.  'They fell for it immediately.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Victim falls for the Deception.  'Young children were found to accept ridiculous ideas in the classroom which they would fall for at home.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the way Victim is deceived which is not covered by more specific FEs.  'I can't believe she so gullibly fell for his lies and flattery.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Victim believes the Deception.  'He fell for it completely.' 'Thankfully I only partially fell for the scam.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity which is widely known and recognized.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the degree of fame of the Entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is famous.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity is considered famous.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that provides an explanation (via reasoning, causation, etc.) for the level of fame of the Entity.

name: Reason
definition_en: The behavior, attribute, or associated entities that provide the reason for the Entity being famous.  'This station is famous for the many ramen shacks surrounding it.'  'Google is well known for having attracted and kept some of the best minds in the industry.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time during which the Entity is famous.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity is famous.  'Certain people are well known only in North America.'

name: Role
definition_en: The Role underwhich the Entity become famous.

name: Means
definition_en: The way in which the Entity becomes famous.

name: Entity
definition_en: A concrete thing or abstract phenomenon or fact that is assessed in terms of how well recognizable it is to a Cognizer.  'He gave an address quite familiar to the chauffeur.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The (typically non-specific and backgrounded) sentient being for whom the Entity possesses a specified level of recognizability.  'The information used to illustrate the concept is familiar to the reader.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The deviation of the actual level of recognizability of the Entity from the level specified by the target.  'He gave an address quite familiar to the chauffeur.'

name: Role
definition_en: This FE identifies the role filled by a particular participant of the clause headed by the target. In so doing, it relates the specification of a level of familiarity to another background state of affairs by indicating that one of the role fillers of the current frame also fills a second kind of role in the background, either generically or in some specific instance.   'I wanted to go with what was familiar to me as an artist.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes the Cognizer as being in some state during the event.

name: Context
definition_en: A situation or source from which the Entity is made more recognizanble to the Cognizer.

name: Container
definition_en: This FE identifies the item that is closed with the Fastener.  'On Friday night, many men will simply elect to remove their tie and unbutton their top shirt button.'

name: Fastener
definition_en: The artifact created to close a Container.  'Man, I have just bought the exact same belt buckle and it won't open.'

name: Container_portal
definition_en: This FE identifies the active zone of the container where the Fastener is located.     'We couldn't close the tent flap zipper and a lot of flies came in .'

name: Material
definition_en: This FE identifes the material from which the Fastener is made.  'It has a matching fabric back strap with a metal buckle and grommet.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the Fastener.  'So, he?s standing there in the dirt road in his slacks and black dress shoes, gut over a big stupid buckle and his short sleeve shirt and his tie all messed  up.'

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Fastener into existence.  'We have 3 vintage Levi Strauss buckles for sale.'

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which the Fastener comes into existence.  'This is a 1960s buckle made by Diablo Silversmiths.'

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to the Fastener.  'Our popular Essex buckle is combined with this Laurel terminal to make an elegant set. '

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of the Fastener.  'A flap portion is foldable over the Ziploc seal, secured in the closed position by a snap closure.'

name: Use
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Fastener is made.  'The unit has an adjustable diagonal zipper for heat control.'

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs.  It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.

name: Stimulus
definition_en: The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.

name: Empathy_target
definition_en: The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The body part, gesture, or other expression of the Experiencer that reflects his or her emotional state.  They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response.  In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus.  Quite often in such cases, the Stimulus can be inferred from the Circumstances

name: State
definition_en: The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Experiencer, Expressor, or State can be described as having said emotion.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer experiences the Emotion or is in the Emotional_state. 'After two pints, he felt a bit better and Ted arrived.'

name: Emotion
definition_en: The Emotion is the feeling that the Experiencer experiences. 'Patients experience high anxiety levels at time of admission to hospital.'

name: Emotional_state
definition_en: The Emotional_state is the state the Experiencer is in. 'Her heart was galloping so fast that she felt quite giddy with happiness.'

name: Evaluation
definition_en: The Evaluation is a negative or positive assessment of the Experiencer regarding his or her Emotional_state. 'Max was feeling worse than he'd ever felt in his life.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The thing or state-of-affairs that leads to the Experiencer feeling the Emotion or Emotional_state.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person who acts in a misleading way to create the impression that a State_of_affairs holds.  'A year after Audrey Seiler faked her own kidnapping while at college in Wisconsin, her lawyer says she's getting help and paying restitution.'

name: Original
definition_en: This is the entity which is copied. With verbs it is frequently expressed as an NP Object: Pat falsified the papers.

name: Copy
definition_en: The Copy produced by the Creator most commonly occurs as the External Argument of a predicative use of an adjective or noun target: The painting is a fake.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the imitation. 'I feigned death by breaking a bag of pig's blood and falling to the floor.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The State_of_affairs is a an event, a state, or a property that the Agent wants others to believe have occurred or hold.  'A college student who staged her own disappearance last month will try to reach a plea agreement and avoid trial on charges she obstructed officers.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action or state that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the feigning of some State_of_affairs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the feigning event logically follows.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Agent engages in the Feigning event.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Agent feigns something.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that the Agent feigns something.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs as being in some state during the feigning action.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Place
definition_en: The place in which the Agent feigns something.

name: Activity
definition_en: An activity that defines a group of people in their professional capacity.  'One of the companies we are presently invested in is Boral, which is in the building sector.'

name: Practitioner
definition_en: The individual, group, or organization  that engages in the Activity as part of their profession.  'I am in biology (molecular immunology).'  'The manufacturing sector has complained to the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) about the country's private commercial banks.'

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: A physical or abstract entity that is characteristically associated with the Activity.  'These companies who have their roots in either the 19th or early 20th century have been in oil all their existence.'

name: Work
definition_en: A phase of a Practitioner's career that is spent engaged in an Activity.    'My most recent job was in the construction industry.'

name: Type
definition_en: The subfield of the Activity that the Practitioner is engaged in.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Practitioner engages in the Activity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Practitioner engages in the Activity.

name: Combatants
definition_en: The Combatants participate as fighters in the Fight. 'The football referee's controversial call led to a bloody free-for-all among the fans.'

name: Fight
definition_en: The violent activity. 'I couldn't help but watch as several bruised people reentered the melee.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the Fight takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the Fight takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner of the Fight. 'Officers said they were stunned upon arrival at the scene of the raucous fray.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This is the Degree of violence of the Fight. 'The townspeople engaged in a full-scale free-for-all.'

name: Salient_activity
definition_en: An activity that engaged in by the Combatants while fighting. 'stabbing affray'

name: Issue
definition_en: The Issue over which Fight happens.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the Fight takes place.

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the Combatants engage in the Fight.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The weapon or other instrument used by the Combatants.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state of affairs that (some of) he Combatants wish to acheive by fighting.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the actor who instigates the filling.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the physical object or substance which changes location. 'Rev. Lovejoy carefully brushed the rolls with butter. '

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location where the Theme begins its motion. 'Josef filled his flask from the whiskey bottle.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is the trajectory of the motion.  'Jess filled the container through a small hole in the lid.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the area or container being filled. Goal is generally the NP Object in this frame.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the filling occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Agent of the filling action. 'Naked, Margeret filled the tub.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the filling occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the filling occurs.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result is the resultant state after the filling has occurred.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Agent fills or covers the Goal. 'Samantha covered the table with flowers because she was bored.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the filling occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the filling takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Agent fills the Goal. 'Samantha covered the table with flowers to please her mother.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which the filling occurs.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion is the smaller area of the Goal where the filling or covering occurs. 'Mrs. Bouvier anointed the children with oil on the forehead.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event which brings about the filling of the Goal.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the person who imposes the Fine upon the Payer.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which the fining is performed.

name: Means
definition_en: The action that is taken that results in punishement/reward. 'His parents disciplined him by taking away his toys.' 'The Bar Association rewarded her by host a lunch in her honor.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which an intentional act is performed. 'John flattered her to receive a raise.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Payer
definition_en: The Payer is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment is made.  With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object:  'The mental control officer fined you for your lack of diligence.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the event (or state) not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Reason
definition_en: Typically, there is a constituent expressing the Reason for the Judge's judgment. It is usually a for-PP, e.g. I admire you for your intellect. For some words in this domain, the Reason frame element is obligatory. That is to say, the overt expression of this frame element may only be omitted when the reason for the judgment is understood from context. For example, the sentence 'I blame you!' can only be uttered when it is clear what the addressee is being blamed for.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of an event.

name: Fine
definition_en: The money given to expiate some debt for transgression. 'Pat paid 14 dollars in fines.'

name: Rate
definition_en: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. 'The manager pays the paper boys five dollars an hour.'

name: Unit
definition_en: This FE is any Unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by-PP.  'Bob sells peppers by weight.' 'Lee buys potatoes by the pound.'

name: Event
definition_en: The imposition of a debt due to culpable behavior.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Fine is punitive to the Payer.  'Employers that hire foreigners without work permits are punishable by law and may be fined considerably'

name: Competitor
definition_en: The individual involved in the Competition.

name: Opponent
definition_en: The individual that the Competitor has been competing against.

name: Competitors
definition_en: The individuals who compete against each other.

name: Score
definition_en: A quantity whereby progress is measured during the game, and Rank and Prizes are awarded to the Competitors afterward.

name: Margin
definition_en: The amount by which the Competitor 's and Opponent 's Scores differ.

name: Rank
definition_en: The rank (according to Score) that a Competitor acheives.

name: Prize
definition_en: A socially and/or monetarily significant entity which is given to a Competitor according to Score or Rank.

name: Competition
definition_en: The event in which the Competitors compete with each other.

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Competitor that results in the outcome of the Competition.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Competition which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Competitor that also affect their action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Competition takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Competition takes place.

name: Venue
definition_en: This FE is for the named venue of a competition, particularly when the place has been built for the purpose of a competition. 'The Mets won against the Yankees  at Shea Stadium.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Game
definition_en: An activity the Player participates in.

name: Player
definition_en: The individual participating in a Game.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Game which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Player that also affect their action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Player that results in the outcome of the Game.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Game takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Player finishes the Game.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Player wins or loses the Game.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Player wins or loses the Game.

name: Fire_break
definition_en: The constructed entity that is intended to prevent a fire from reaching a protected area.  'The firefighters' fire break directly outside of the schoolyard fence prevented the field from going up in flames.'

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Fire_break into existence.

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Fire_break, including components, ingredients, etc.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to a Fire_break.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which a Fire_break comes into existence.

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Fire_break.

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which a Fire_breakis intended.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Fire is burning.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Fire is burning.

name: Fire
definition_en: The total material currently involved in combustion, including both the parts of the Fuel currently undergoing chemical alteration and the partially ionized gas that results from this process.

name: Fuel
definition_en: The entity that is undergoing rapid chemical alteration leading to damage or destruction.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Fire event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Name
definition_en: Name given to the burning fire.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that the Fire burns.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Descriptive phrase describing the fire.

name: Result
definition_en: The state or category of the affected entity after the event.  'The house burned to ash.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the affected entity that undergoes the process evoked by the target.  'The walls burned to the ground .' 'The house was already on fire, in the kitchen and one bedroom .'

name: Fire
definition_en: The fire which causes an emergency response.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time between the declaration of a Fire as in an emergency state and the conclusion of the emergency.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the fire emergency scenario occurs.

name: Responder
definition_en: The individual or group that is responding to a fire emergency with directed action.

name: Response
definition_en: Directed action leading to recovery, rescue, or general mitigation of distress due to an ensuing fire emergency.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the fire emergency scenario occurs.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim(s) affected negatively by the fire emergency event.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Fire goes out.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Fire goes out.

name: Fire
definition_en: The combustion process that is coming to an end.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes the how near the Fire is to going out.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing an undergoer of an action during their participation in the event.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the state of the Fire that affects the nature of the event.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the event.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Fire goes out.  'The Forest Service said they will have dedicated employees in the woods day and night until the fire is quenched.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Fire goes out.

name: Fire
definition_en: The combustion process that comes to an end.  'The fire went out this morning .'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes the how near the Fire is to going out.     'The firefighters have nearlyextinguished the blaze.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent puts out the Fire.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Fire goes out.  'The fire went out last night.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual or group that causes the Fire to no longer burn.

name: Fire
definition_en: The combustion process that the Agent causes to end.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes the how near the Agent is to putting out the Fire.

name: Fire
definition_en: The fire that Firefighters target.

name: Firefighter
definition_en: The individual or group who respond(s) to the Fire.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Firefighter fights the Fire.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the location of the Firefighters as they attempt to fight the Fire.

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner in which the Firefighters are fighting the Fire.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The desired result of the firefight. It may either directly refer to the state of affairs that is desired, e.g. 'The firefighters tackled the blaze early to prevent the further spread of the flames.' or the state of affairs may be implicit in an (abstract or concrete) entity that is desired by the firefighters, e.g. 'The firefighters fought for ground as the flames approached.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An instrument with which an intentional fire-fighting act is performed.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs as being in some state during the firefighting action.

name: Employee
definition_en: The person who is let go by their Employer.    'I was just fired yesterday!'

name: Employer
definition_en: The person (or institution) that end an employment relationship with an Employee.  'Dominic Mallozzi claims United Trust Bank fired him from a job at the bank's Palmer Township branch because he's HIV positive.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employer fires an Employee.  'Five were hastily fired, and the federal government is investigating possible insider trading violations.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Employer fires the Employee.  'The phone in his small apartment in the town of Milan rang and he dreaded it. He was going to be fired right there.'

name: Position
definition_en: The label given to a particular type of employment.   'Doc Rivers was fired as coach of the Orlando Magic.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Employer fires the Employee.  'John fired her to make his the other employees nervous.'

name: Task
definition_en: The action that the Employee is relieved from doing for the Employer  .'I was fired from training the new actors.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when an Employer fires the Employee.  'Guess who just got fired today!'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Employee is terminated.   'North was dismissed for gross mismanagement of funds.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means whereby the Employer fires the Employee  'Pat fired Jan by leaving a letter of dismissal on his desk.'

name: Firing_point
definition_en: The location from which the Detonator activates an explosive device.  'Can you identify a firing point?'

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Firing_point is located with respect to.  'Any firing points outside this zone should not be approached.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Firing_point.  'The abandoned firing point yielded minimal forensic evidence.'

name: Name
definition_en: The name of the locale.

name: Detonator
definition_en: The Detonator is located at the Firing_point when he or she activates the explosive device.  'We could not identify their firing point.'

name: Experience
definition_en: An event happens for the first time within the Context.  'Made from flax, linen was first used by the ancient Egyptians.'  'The Cobra was first deployed to Vietnam in September 1967.'

name: Context
definition_en: A spatial, cultural, or personal delimitation within which the Experience occurs for the first time.   'In Germany the pamphlet was first used by the leaders of the Protestant Reformation to inflame popular opinion against the pope'

name: Item
definition_en: An Item is the foremost thing in the Contrast_set.

name: Limits_of_consideration
definition_en: This FE identifies the domain (usually temporally or spatially defined) within which the Item is primary among its kind. 'The foremost band in the world of the 1960's was clearly the Beatles.'

name: Contrast_set
definition_en: The Contrast_set is a group of entities similar to the Item out of which the Item is the most preeminent. 'Our discussion has raised a number of issues, foremost among them time.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The Attribute of the Item which is under consideration.  'The foremost ski lodge in size is Lassen.'

name: Self_mover
definition_en: Self_mover is the living (or self-directed) being which moves under its own power.

name: Source
definition_en: Source is used for any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion.

name: Path
definition_en: Path is used for any description of a trajectory of motion involving a landmark which is neither a Source nor a Goal.  This includes "middle of path'' expressions.

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is used for any expression which tells where the Self_mover ends up as a result of the motion.

name: Manner
definition_en: An expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory or rate of motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.   'They had to flee on foot through the desert.'

name: Distance
definition_en: Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the motion occurs.

name: Cotheme
definition_en: An entity whose motion is correlated with that of the Self_mover, following and tracking the Self_mover, being followed and tracked, or with both parties mutually matching Paths.

name: Speed
definition_en: The rate at which the location of the Self_mover changes with respect to time.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Self_mover achieves movement.

name: Result
definition_en: The state of the world which exists because of the motion of the Self_mover

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotional or mental state of the Self_mover which motivates them toward motion or the particular manner of motion.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the Self_mover moves.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which a Self_mover moves. 'John ran away with her to shelter her from disapproval.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location within which a defined motion takes place.  Any specified or implied  Source, Path or Goal should designate a location contained with the Place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The state of affairs that leads to the particular motion that the Self_mover adopts.

name: External_cause
definition_en: External_cause is something in the external environment that causes the Self_mover to move.   'They fled at the sound of her voice.'

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction that the Self_mover heads in during the motion.

name: Means_of_motion
definition_en: The entity used by the Self_mover in getting away from the undesirable Source.

name: Area
definition_en: Area is the setting in which the Fluid's movement takes place on an unspecified Path. 'The Thames River flows throughout England.'

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE describes the phsyical extent of the motion of the Fluid.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the Fluid moves.

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is the location the Fluid ends up.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is the trajectory along which the Fluid moves.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location the Fluid occupies initially.

name: Speed
definition_en: This is the rate at which the Fluid flows.

name: Fluid
definition_en: The Fluid is the entity that changes location and moves in a fluidic way.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Fluid flows.

name: Configuration
definition_en: The Configuration encodes information about the amount, arrangement, and unitization of the flow. 'The water cascaded in torrents' . 'The water cascades in large volumes.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Fluid flows.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the reason for the fluidic motion. 'It flowed from the sheer weight of water above it.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing the Fluid throughout the action.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the result of the Fluid moving.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place describes the location of the motion which has a specified Source, Path or Goal. 'At Oregon Caves, a stream runs through the dining room.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE indicates a characteristic or description of the food.  ' She drinks low-fat milk'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE identifies a particular Type of the food item. ' cooking apple' 'Granny Smith apple.'

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: A part of the Food.  'You'd be surprised, but it was hard to eat a banana with such a thick peel.'

name: Gatherer
definition_en: The Gatherer is the agent gathering the Crop.  'Small growers can harvest quality crops.'

name: Crop
definition_en: Crop is item being collected together by the Gatherer.  'Tubers harvested immediately after spraying developed gangrene.'

name: Duration
definition_en: For what length of time the Gatherer was gathering the Crop.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Gatherer gathers the Crop.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Crop is gathered.

name: Place
definition_en: The greater geographic location where the Gatherer gathers his Crop.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Crop gathering action occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Gatherer intends to accomplish by gathering his Crop.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Gatherer collects his Crop.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the ground where the Crop is gathered from.  'They picked the apples from the tallest trees.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes the amount of effort put into the food gathering event.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The person on who's behalf the Gatherer gathers the Crop.

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: The materials or Constituent_parts that make up the Current_country.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location that the Current_country is a part of.

name: Current_country
definition_en: The country or countries that the speaker is indicating in the current instance, which may match or be distinct from the Discourse_salient_country.  'AutoPartsPlace.com offers discount prices on millions of import auto parts, domestic car parts, and car accessories. '

name: Name
definition_en: ULTIMATELY TO BE REPLACED BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases).  This FE is used for the Names of Locales.

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that the Current_country is located with respect to.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description, characteristic, or property of the Current_country which is not covered by more specific FEs.

name: Population
definition_en: The people living in the jurisdiction of the locale.

name: Discourse_salient_country
definition_en: The country that has been featured in the discourse, or that the speaker/hearer identify with or are located in; it serves to identify the Current_country by specifying it as the same or different.  This FE is incorporated in the targets of this frame.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person that creates a Forgery with the intent of passing it off as (an instance of) the Standard.  'He even faked her signature. '

name: Forgery
definition_en: The Forgery is the product that the Agent creates with the intent of passing it off as (an instance of) the Standard.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the imitation.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the forging event logically follows.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action or state that the Agent intends to accomplish by producing the Forgery.

name: Standard
definition_en: The Standard is the actually existing or imagined (kind of) thing that the Agent wants to pass the Forgery off as.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity manipulated by the Agent in order to produce the Forgery.  'Fortunately, he forged it with a black pen, which couriers never use.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Agent makes a Forgery.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the forgery takes place.

name: Fidelity
definition_en: The way in which the Forgery does or does not match the Standard.  'What I don't know is why she tried to forge it half-size.'

name: Source
definition_en: An entity corresponding to the Standard which the Agent scrutinizes in order to copy.  'He faked his travel documents from the ones his sister used last year.'

name: Judge
definition_en: The Judge holds the Evaluee responsible for the Offense.

name: Evaluee
definition_en: The Evaluee is subject to the judgment of the Judge for having committed the Offense. 'God forgives repentant sinners.'

name: Offense
definition_en: The Offense is the illicit or unpleasant act committed by the Evaluee. 'Won't you forgive me for keeping it a secret?'

name: Forgoer
definition_en: The Forgoer decides not to partake in the desirable activity or event.   'Chuck often skips lunch.'</def-root >

name: Desirable
definition_en: Desirable identifies the event or activity in which is the Forgoer does not partake.  'Chuck often skips lunch.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the forgoing occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner the forgoing occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the forgoing occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the forgoing occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time at which the the forgoing occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the forgoing occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which the forgoing occurs.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the Forgoer does not partake in the Desirable.  'Chuck skips lunch even when he's hungry.'

name: Partner_1
definition_en: The individual who comes to form a relationship with Partner_2.

name: Partner_2
definition_en: The individual whose relationship with Partner_1 changes.

name: Partners
definition_en: The individuals whose relationship is changing.

name: Means
definition_en: The action that Partner_1 or the Partners take in order to bring about the change in the relationship.  'In the old days, a man could divorce his wife just by saying "I divorce you" three times.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the relationship changes.  'She married Stephen last summer.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Partner_1 or Partners that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Depictive
definition_en: A salient state of Partner_1, Partner_2, or Partners which affects the perception of the formation of relationship.  'I befriended her unaware of her past.'

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The length of time that the changed relationship status lasts.  'Ekaterina befriended him for a short while.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the relationship is formed. 'We married in a gazebo.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Partners or Partner_1 hope to bring about by changing their status.

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the Forming_relationship event operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Forming_relationship event occurs.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Whole
definition_en: The Whole is a single entity which breaks into Parts.

name: Parts
definition_en: This refers collectively to the Parts resulting from fragmentation of a Whole.

name: Part_1
definition_en: Part-1 is the first of two Parts mentioned. This is most often the external argument of a verb.

name: Part_2
definition_en: Part_2 is the second of two Parts mentioned. This is usually a PP Complement.

name: Criterion
definition_en: This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which correlates with the locations (e.g.) of fragmentation on the Whole.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing any of the undergoers of the fragmentation.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the fragmenting occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the breaking occurs.

name: Resistant_surface
definition_en: The hard surface against which the Whole (or Part_1) breaks.  'Too fragile a knife will shatter on the stone.'

name: Means
definition_en: An action or state that enables the fragmentation.  'As the energy of the string increases, it fragments by producing quark-antiquark (or diquark-antidiquark) pairs at the breakpoints.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent causes the confinement or captivity  of the Theme to end, against the intentions of the captor.  'Their buddies sprung them from prison.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the person or object which is released by the Agent.  'Unknown individuals freed the suspect.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the release which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Not truly allies, they freed the suspect carefully.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Agent which brings about the release.  'He freed a hundred prisoners by disabling the transport vehicle and gassing the guards.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation identifies the reason for which the Agent sets the Theme free.  'Enemy fighters freed those two captives because they had knowledge necessary to mount a larger assault against our position.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose identifies the purpose for which the Agent releases the Theme.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Theme ceases to be confined.  'They sprung us on the highway'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time identifies when the Agent frees the Theme .

name: Location_of_confinement
definition_en: The location to which the Theme's motion was formerly inhibited.  'Johnny sprung me from prison and I've never forgiven him since.'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world when the event of setting free occurs.

name: Event
definition_en: This FE is used for any (bounded) Event whose frequency or iteration is described.  'The country has been struck by frequent economic crises.' 'The symptoms were sporadic.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the actually observed rate of occurrence of the Event or Salient_entity differs from the expected rate.   'The Crested Lark (Galerida cristata) is  very frequent from the coastal plain to the mountains.'

name: Interval
definition_en: The Interval is a noun modified by the target word. The target word specifies the frequency of the Interval . 'The meetings occurred at fortnightly intervals.' 'The parties were held on a monthly basis.'

name: Time_span
definition_en: The Time_span is the length of time of the Interval. This FE is incorporated by most of the lexical units in this frame.  'You have to renew the license every year .'

name: Rate
definition_en: The number of times per unit of real or scanning time that an Event or Salient_entity is encountered.   'The state government spends its fiscal year 2006 budget of $23.4 billion at a rate of $742 per second.'

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: An entity which the implicit cognizer encounters with the specified frequency.  'It costs about US$2.50 to travel 200km (124 mi), but buses are infrequent and only one or two buses a day service most routes.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The frequency feature of the Event or Salient_entity that is under discussion. All the lexical units in this frame incorporate this frame element.  'These exposures were likely to be intermittent in frequency occurring only when workers were participating in activities at these specific areas.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Event has a particular frequency.

name: Group
definition_en: The Group in which the Event or Salient_entity is frequent. 'Obesity is common to Americans.' 'Obesity is common in America.' 'Behaviors common to small children include crying.'</def-root >

name: Theme
definition_en: The physical entity which moves over the suface of the Static_object  'His backpack grated against the wall'.

name: Static_object
definition_en: A non-moving physical object over a surface of which the Theme moves.  ' The spout grates against the tap'

name: Themes
definition_en: Two moving entities whose surfaces move against each other.  'He felt his teeth scrape against the plaster '

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Theme moves against the Static_object  'is steel helmet grated gently against the top of the door'

name: Place
definition_en: The setting in which the motion of the Theme happens  'In the hallway a key grated in the lock'

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount of friction produced in the Theme's motion.  'The steel helment grated faintly against the top of the '

name: Side_1
definition_en: Side_1 is the party or individual in a relationship with Side_2. Side_1 is the primary protagonist of the frame, and is denoted by noun and adjective targets.  'The hostiles had become adept at spotting men in the night desert.'  'So now you are my enemy?'

name: Side_2
definition_en: The party or individual with whom Side_1 bears an adversarial or friendly relationship.  'His enemies were no doubt waiting for just such a moment.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the relationship holds.  'They mistakenly thought that the soldiers and sailors were their greatest enemy.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Sides have the indicated relationship with each other.  'Last year they were our enemy, but things are different now. '

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is a proposition denoting a state of affairs from which the Sides having the relationship indicated logically follows.  'Could it be that they are enemies because of deep-seated prejudice?'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE indicates a property of Side_1 or the Sides.

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the two Sides have an adversarial relationship.  'In our daily lives we are friends, but here we are bitter enemies.'

name: Sides
definition_en: A joint expression of the two Sides with a friendly or hostile stance towards one another.  'Aren't you afraid to be here? We are enemies!'

name: Front
definition_en: The Front acts as a legitimate individual, organization, or enterprise, but is truly a cover for an illicit organization or activity.

name: Illicit_organization
definition_en: The existence and activities of the Illicit_organization are concealed by the Front.

name: Illicit_activity
definition_en: The Illicit_activity of the Illicit_organization is concealed by (the activities of) the Front .

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the deceptive activity occurs

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Front is attempting to bring about.  'He fronted for the mob to get out of paying protection.'

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the fronting occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: The action taken by the Front to ensure successful deceit of authorities.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the similarity of the event to some other event, particularly descriptions of the Front that also affect the details of the action.

name: Resource_controller
definition_en: The Resource_controller is the individual whose frugality or generosity is being described. Person typically occurs as the External Argument or, in some cases when Behavior is also expressed, in an of-PP:  'Jo is very frugal.' 'It was frugal of Jo not to pay for dinner.'

name: Behavior
definition_en: Some specific Behavior may be described as frugal or extravagant, rather than attributing the characteristic directly to the Resource_controller. 'It's thrifty of Jo to re-use teabags.'

name: Resource
definition_en: This FE is the resource which the Resource_controller expends. 'Pat is wasteful with her time.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which a Resource_controller is frugal or profligate.

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Fugitive
definition_en: The Fugitive has escaped and/or is evading capture by law enforcement Authorities.  'Only two years earlier she had been on the lam from charges of embezzlement.'

name: Prison
definition_en: The facility where the Fugitive was being held.  'Police are still searching for three fugitives from Colorado State Prison.'

name: Authorities
definition_en: The Authorities want to take (or retake) the Fugitive into custody on suspicion of having committed a Crime.  'Fugitives from the law will have the opportunity to present their cases.'

name: Crime
definition_en: The crime of which the Fugitive is wanted. This FE also covers expressions that indicate suspicion of crimes, convictions, and sentences.  'A local woman on the lam from a ten-year prison sentence.'  'US Officials recently arrested over a dozen drug fugitives in a bust that has been planned for months.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the general Place where the Fugitive is located.  'Sloan, on the lam in Michigan for the last five months, is due to appear in court this Monday.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Fugitive is evading law enforcement.  'He was a fugitive in the early 1990s.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the state of being imprisoned which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Fugitive is avoiding capture.  'I'm on the lam because that's the only way I'll be able to prove my innocense.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Fugitive is on the run.  'The 30-year fugitive was stunned when authorities knocked on his door last May.'

name: Container
definition_en: Container is used for the entity whose fullness is being described. 'John carried an empty bucket.'

name: Contents
definition_en: Contents is used for the stuff that is present/absent in the Container. 'The bucket is  full of water.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the amount of Contents in the Container diverges from the maximal expected amount for the Container.  'Be careful, because the glass is very full .'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Container is full.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The amount of times the Container is empty per unit of time.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Container's fullness to the end.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity is an object or person that performs the Activity or fulfills the Role.

name: Activity
definition_en: The Activity is the action that the Entity performs.

name: Role
definition_en: The Role is  the position or duty that is occupied by the Entity.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor provides additional information about the Entity .

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration that the Entity performs an Activity or fulfills a Role.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Entity functions.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which an Entity functions.

name: Supplier
definition_en: Supplier is the person or entity that funds the Recipient or Imposed_purpose.  'Investors bankrolled the software start-up early on.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: Recipient is the person, people, or organization funded by the Supplier.   'Some governments fund students so that they can obtain doctorates and enter public service.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: Imposed_purpose is the intended purpose of the funding.   'The board agreed to finance the research program.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the conditions under which the funding is supplied.   'Hank's parents continued to support him as long as he was actively looking for a job.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE is the Explanation for which the Supplier gives funding to the Recipient or Imposed_purpose.   'Western governments financed the undertaking because they desired access to new oil reserves.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the funding event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Supplier that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Paul unwittingly funded his brother's drinking habit.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE expresses the Means by which the Supplier funds the Recipient or Imposed_purpose.  'Marie funded her trip to Mexico by tutoring kids throughout the summer.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE designates the period over which the Supplier engages in (multiple) funding acts.   'Our company has backed the governor's election campaigns since 2000.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Supplier funds the Recipient or Imposed_purpose.   'The Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation funded public libraries in rural Kenya, providing them with free Internet access.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source of the funding.   'Hank's parents supported him by drawing from their retirement fund.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Supplier gives funds to the Recipient or Imposed_purpose.   'The project was officially funded at noon today.'

name: Money
definition_en: Money is the specified currency or amount of funding.   'Band manager Mohammed has financed their project to the tune of $5,000.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Supplier funds the Recipient.  'Banks financed the undertaking so that Western nations would have access to new oil reserves.'

name: Aggregate
definition_en: This FE identifies the aggregate that results from the gathering.  It may be expressed either as an adjunct result phrase or as a direct object of a target verb. 'The police gathered the suspects into a line-up.' 'He amassed a collection of shiny bits of tin foil.'

name: Agent
