definition_en: Agent is the person who gathers Individuals. 'The police gathered the suspects into a lineup.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the gathering event occurs, if specified. The crowd assembled at dawn.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the gathering.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the gathering event occurs. He assembled the children in the hall.

name: Individuals
definition_en: This FE identifies the entities that come together to form an Aggregate. 'The police gathered the suspects into a line-up.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Individuals are gathered up.  'Sue assembled the team  quickly'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An Instrument that the Agent uses to gather the Individuals together.  'Native Americans gathered these bulbs with specially whittled and fired digging sticks'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state of affairs that the Agent is attempting to bring about by gathering.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times the Gathering_up event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the Gathering_up event occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal designates the location where the Individuals might end up.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: The Co-participant participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is the trajectory of motion that the Individuals take.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location where the Individuals are at the beginning of the gathering event.

name: Communicator
definition_en: This is the sentient entity that communicates a Message non-verbally. It is normally expressed as an External Argument: The teacher gestured us into the room.

name: Addressee
definition_en: This is the person to whom a non-verbal Message is communicated. It may be expressed as an NP Object or as a PP Complement: The teacher gestured us into the room. The teacher gestured to us to enter the room.

name: Message
definition_en: This is the content of non-verbal communication. It may be expressed as a that-clause Complement, a to-marked infinitive VP Complement, or a directional PP Complement: The teacher gestured that it was time to leave. The teacher gestured to us to enter the room. The teacher gestured us into the room.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Communicator that results in the successful transfer of a Message. 'He signalled John to fold by touching his ear and leaning back.'

name: Body_part
definition_en: The Body_part is the specific body part of the Communicator which gestures.

name: Time
definition_en: When the gesturing occus.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the gesturing occurs.

name: Indicated_entity
definition_en: The Indicated_entity is the entity which the Communicator is pointing out to the Addressee as meaningful.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An Instrument that the Communicator uses to gesture to the Addressee together.

name: Compensation
definition_en: The Compensation is the payment that the Employee receives for performing a Task.  'He said he wanted to play for a contender, and then he signed on for a lot of money with a team that is not a contender.'

name: Employee
definition_en: The person who enters an employment relation with an Employer.  'In spring of 1983, Tom signed on at the historic Wawona Hotel in Yosemite National Park, and continues to perform there nightly in the hotel's piano parlor.'

name: Employer
definition_en: The person (or institution) that the Employee enters an employment relationship with.   'He later played for the Scottish Claymores of the NFL Europe League in the spring of 2001, then signed on with Baltimore in July of 2001.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employee enters an employment relationship with an Employer.   'Van Auken eagerly signed on with Pennsylvania.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Employee enteres an employment relationship with an Employer.  'I had signed on right there with the rest of the freaks. '

name: Position
definition_en: The label given to a particular type of employment.  ' In 1973 Franco Acerbis signed on as a mechanic for the Italian enduro team.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Employee enters an employment relationship.   'Aengaela signed on with the Company to learn the family business. '

name: Task
definition_en: The action that the Employee is obligated to do for the Employer.   'In the end, however, Gaskill opted to remain out West and signed on to play Oscar Marone on CBS's The Bold and the Beautiful.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when an Employee signs on with an Employer.    'Things have been very busy with the new job since I signed on in June, 2001.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action by which the Employee enters an employment relationship.  'After interviewing, he signed on with a handshake in 1988.'

name: Contract_basis
definition_en: The Contract_basis is the condition of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period or payment arrangements.   'In addition, Kellie Anngotell and Emil Fredette have hired on part-time. '

name: Recipient
definition_en: The Recipient indicates the entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the object that changes possession.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location that the Theme formerly occupied.  Persons that begin in possession of the Theme may metonymically stand in for the Source.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place denotes where the Getting takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation refers to the existing eventuality that the Recipient is responding to.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is the action of the Recipient which results in their possession of the Theme.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent intentionally acts.

name: Result
definition_en: The state that either the Recipient or the Theme end up in after the acquisition.  'You should acquire it without any publicity.'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The Beneficiary is an entity which the Recipient passes the Theme to, or shares the Theme with.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Any condition or situation that serves as a very general background, against which the further importance of the Getting is understood.  'With him out of the room , I got all the popcorn .'

name: Recipient
definition_en: The Recipient indicates the entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the object that changes possession.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location that the Theme formerly occupied.  Persons that begin in possession of the Theme may metonymically stand in for the Source.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation refers to the existing eventuality that the Recipient is responding to.

name: System
definition_en: The System interacts with the environment and activates.  'The device triggered as she walked through the arch.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any holistic description of the event, including overall depictions (the same way) and descriptions pertaining to the System (quietly).

name: Place
definition_en: Where the System goes off.  'Police came running downstairs when the metal detector went off at the county courthouse.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the System triggers.  'The alarm went off at three o'clock today.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times the triggerent event occurs in a particular time period.  'Around here bombs go off several times a day.'

name: Self_mover
definition_en: The Self_mover is the volitional agent that moves.   'Tom and I got under way in the wee hours of the morning, planning to get to the confluence area between the onsets of nautical and civil twilight.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source refers to the starting-point of the Self_mover's motion.   ' The vessel got under way from San Francisco on 14 June and completed two round-trips to Manila before the cessation of hostilies.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path is any description of the Self_mover's trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.  'We can get going via Fife'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is any expression that tells where the Self_mover ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.   'On the 17th, the vessel got under way for Tarawa, Gilbert Islands.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A Manner expression  describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion.  Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.   'She slipped the Dyna-Cruiser into gear and we slowly headed out for a drive.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a Self_mover begins the motion.  'We get under way by heading up through the alpine meadows of la Balme 2140m and then past some sparse pine forests.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Self_mover begins the motion away from the Source.  'We got going at 5 am in the rain, just to make the massive hike to Davenport Gap.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the state of the Self_mover when she begins the motion away from the Source.

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The length of time of the Self_mover's absence from the Source.

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: The Mode_of_transportation is the transportation device that a human Self_mover uses to travel.  'The traffic, when we finally got going in Jamaorn's car, was appalling.'

name: Journey
definition_en: The journey is the trip or expedition on which the Self_mover embarks.  'I'm heading out on a mission.'

name: Direction
definition_en: The Direction in which the Self_mover begins to move.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The person or animal that has slept in a particular place and now leaves it to engage in other activities.  ' Melony got up from bed and changed clothes getting ready to go to the doctor.'

name: Bed
definition_en: The place where the Protagonist has slept.  'She got up from bed lazily and stretched her body and yawned.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Protagonist leaves their place of sleeping.  'We got up at 6:30 in the morning.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Protagonist gets out of Bed.  'I rose from bed to rectify the situation.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously),  secondary effects (quietly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Protagonist that affect the action (eagerly, carefully).   ' I rose from bed with urgency early one morning because a light clicked on.'

name: New_situation
definition_en: The New_situation is the situation the Protagonist finds him or herself in upon getting up from Bed.  'Hannibal admitted defeat at around 5 am and rose to find Face and Ray already up making coffee.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the getting up event takes place.  'During spring break, we got up at 7:45 and waited for the donut truck.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Protagonist is responding to in getting up.  'I get up because I have things I can't wait to do.'

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The length of the interval for which the Protagonist is not in Bed after getting up.  'I was so tired yesterday that I went home and slept 3 hrs, got up for 2 hrs, then back to bed.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Protagonist's Bed is situated.  'We eventually ended up getting home about 5am and I ended up sleeping all day. I got up late at home, went to Steve's and slept at his house. INI'

name: Driver
definition_en: This is the being, typically human, that prepares the Vehicle for motion, and will control it once it is in motion.    'He shook his head in amazement and slowly pulled the car out of the parking lot.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The device--such as a car, boat, spaceship,. etc.--which is used for transport and is prepared for travel by the Driver.   'Lyle was feeling very pleased with himself as he pulled the BMW out of its parking space.'

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which describes the location that the Vehicle has been stationed at.  'The ship cast off from Pier 21.'

name: Intended_goal
definition_en: The location that the Vehicle is intended to travel to.  ' At 1500 65 Royal Air Force personnel came aboard and the LCI 35 cast off for England. '

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Driver that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).    'The Duchess of Northumberland slowly weighed anchor and pulled away from the wharf at London.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Driver or Vehicle during the preparations.   'We cast off from the dock in fear and headed for Pequaming.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by the Driver by which they prepare the Vehicle for travel.   'I weighed anchor by hand - an easy affair with a boat that weighs less than a ton - and headed south with the Class of '93-'94.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result of the Driver's action.  'Bill pulled his Maserati out right into a truck.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: An individual or vehicle that is also involved in the preparations.   'On 8 April the Admiral weighed anchor with three of his consorts, leaving the others to follow.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE indicates the Circumstances under which the preparation of the Vehicle takes place.  'At sunrise I weighed anchor in a light breeze and set off for Spain.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place describes the location where the Driver prepares the Vehicle for motion.  'At 0900 on 10 September 1945, DE 353 weighed anchor in Victoria Harbor, adjacent to Labuan Island, Borneo.'

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The length  of the time that the Vehicle remains in the state of readiness.  'We weighed anchor for only 2 hours before the storm became too intense.'

name: Time
definition_en: The  Time when the Driver prepares the Vehicle for motion.  'We weighed anchor in the afternoon of October 9th and got out of the harbour under all plain sail.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE marks a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The Phenomenon is typically the External Argument of the verbs in this frame.'The soup tasted very salty.'

name: Characterization
definition_en: Characterization is the subjective description (of the Perceiver_passive ) of the Phenomenon.'Kim's new furniture looks sort of bluish.''The violins sounded as if they were in pain.''The city smelled like rotting sewage.'

name: Appraisal
definition_en: Appraisal is the positive or negative judgement given to the Phenomenon.'Kim's hair feels nice.''That trumpet sounds dreadful.'

name: Inference
definition_en: Inference expresses some property of the Phenomenon that is not a direct  feature of the particular sensory modality (if any), but rather is based on perception within that modality.'Pat sounds devastated by the bad news.' Inference may superficially look like Appraisal, as in: 'That idea sounds dreadful.' However, it is not the perception of the "sound" of the idea that is "dreadful", it is the idea itself that is inferred to be dreadful based on what was heard. 'It looks like Johanna is going to the ball without me.' Note the dummy-it as subject in this sense of  "look"  and that  "appears that" could replace "looks like".  Here, it is _inferrable_ that Johanna will go to the ball without the speaker.

name: Perceiver_passive
definition_en: The Perceiver_passive experiences some perception without necessarily intending to, but makes a judgment about the Phenomenon.  The Perceiver_passive generally occurs in a PP Complement.'The milk smells bad to me.'

name: Body_part
definition_en: Body_part expressions are not common in this frame, but may occur with the verb "feel" (the only verb in this frame that does not lexically encode the Body_part involved in perception) or occasionally (and redundantly) with other verbs.'The fabric felt soft on my skin.''The music sounded beautiful to my ears.'

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: Location_of_protagonist identifies the position of the Perceiver_passive during the act of perception.  Typically it is expressed in a PP-from.'The house looks deceptively small from the outside.'

name: Path
definition_en: This frame element, usually expressed in a PP, is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the Location_of_perceiver (see above), that describe how the Perceiver_passive's attention is directed during the act of perception. 'His voice sounded muffled through the wall.'

name: State
definition_en: This FE identifies expressions that predicate something of the Phenomenon, providing some information about its State while the Perceiver_passive experiences it.'Pat looks great dressed in red.''The meat tastes delicious seasoned with garlic.'

name: Ground
definition_en: Ground is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced (or not experienced) by the Perceiver_passive.'The painting looks great against the new wallpaper.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which a Phenomenon gives the impression that a certain Characterization or Inference holds.  'John looks like his father a bit.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The physical or abstract Circumstances that determine the appearance of the Phenomenon.  'The people I work with seem to either hate their jobs, or like them, depending on my mood.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Phenomenon has the Appraisal, Characterization, or Phenomenon.

name: Donor
definition_en: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient .

name: Recipient
definition_en: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The object that changes ownership.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the manner in which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the conditions under which the Theme is given. 'I give my services free of charge.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The Recipient's intended purpose for the Theme. 'Please give this list to the secretary for entry into the client database.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the Donor, Recipient, or Theme given independently of the giving event per se.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Mother
definition_en: Mother is the female creature that produces the Child. 'Betty bore Gerry three intelligent daughters.'

name: Child
definition_en: Child identifies the new self-motile creature produced from the Mother and Father. 'Betty bore Gerry three intelligent daughters.'

name: Father
definition_en: Father is the male creature that copulates with the Mother, thus  leading to the birth of the Child.  'Betty bore Gerry three intelligent daughters.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies the phrase describing a participant of an action  ' Demons are spawned fully formed.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which a Mother and Father produce produce a Child.  'Star fish can be spawned under the right conditions.'

name: Egg
definition_en: Egg is an immobile object containing an organism that may hatch as a mobile, infant organism.  'Female clownfish lay their eggs around sea anemones'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the event occurs.

name: Parents
definition_en: The Mother and Father expressed together. 'We are going to be having twins!'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of  the birth. 'John's mother bore him into a wealthy family.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Parents (or a Father or Mother) that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'They eagerly spawned more of their kind until there was no room for more.'

name: Capitulator
definition_en: The individual that yields to the Force exerted by the Compeller.   'I sensed that if John caved in to her that it would hurt his game.'

name: Issue
definition_en: The matter, usually concerning a course of action, in which the Capitulator has disagreed with the Compeller.  'Historically, the Senate has yielded to the House on the issue.'

name: Compeller
definition_en: An individual that intentionally exerts Force on the Capitulator.  'Relatively new to business, poor Kellie had eventually caved in to him.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Capitulator yields to the Compeller on the Issue.  'Ms Marinkovic relented yesterday under intense international pressure.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is a proposition denoting a state of affairs from which the Capitulator's giving in on the Issue logically follows.   'I yielded to him because I wanted to be a team player.'

name: Force
definition_en: A state of affairs, typically brought about by a Compeller, that impinges on the Capitulator and eventually causes them to no longer pursue their own view on the Issue.   'In 1649, Descartes yielded to the request of Queen Christina of Sweden that he join her distinguished circle she was assembling in Stockholm.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Capitulator ceases to oppose the Force.  'John refused to heed the barons? early calls for reform, but in June 1215 he capitulated at Runnymede.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Capitulator intends to accomplish by ceasing their opposition.  ' Corfu in 229 BC, after several raids and suzerainties, was forced to ask the protection of the Romans and finally yielded to them in order to protect itself .'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Giving_in  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Capitulator that affect the action (reluctantly, meekly).  'Congress reluctantly capitulated to this final demand on Sept. 1.'

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing the deviation of how the Issue is resolved from the desires of the Compeller.   'She partially gave in, admitting her anti-urban bias was mostly in part to her parents brainwashing her from a young age.'

name: Resultant_action
definition_en: The action that the Capitulator engages in after giving in to the Force.  'After months of pressure by my staff, I have finally yielded to doing a commentary on advertising.'

name: Donor
definition_en: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient .

name: Recipient
definition_en: The individual that ends up in possession of the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The object that changes ownership.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the manner in which the Donor gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The Recipient's intended purpose for the Theme.  'Please give this list to the secretary for entry into the client database.'

name: Use
definition_en: This FE identifies the prototypical Use of a tool or device.  'coffee machine'  'device for making soap bubbles'

name: User
definition_en: User identifies the person who (typically) uses a particular tool. ' This drawer is used for storage of dentist's equipment'

name: Power_source
definition_en: The Frame Element Power_source marks expressions that indicate how a device is powered.  ' We use gas appliances in our kitchen'

name: Gizmo
definition_en: The complex artifact with a particular use.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Gizmo.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the shape-changing event takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the change into the shape occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the changing into a particular shape occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: How long the event takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the shape-changing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the shape changing occurs.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme goes into a particular shape.

name: Resultant_configuration
definition_en: The Result is the shape the Theme becomes.  'It folded into a ball.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The conditions under which the Theme is shaped.  'The leaf folded in the sun because the heat evaporated much of its water content.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The state of the Theme with respect to the change brought about by making the adjustment.  'The contraption folds to fit in the bag.'

name: Landmark
definition_en: The relatively locatable entity which serves as a basis for determining the location of the Trajector using the Profiled_region.

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: The location (located with respect to the Landmark) which is profiled by the particular image schema pertaining to the locative relation.

name: Trajector
definition_en: The entity which is construed to be in motion, whose location at the end of the construed motion event is in question.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Trajector is located in the Profiled_region.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist is the person who has committed themselves to do something and later does not follow through on it.   'The human rights situation is infinitely better now than under the Taliban, but the Bush administration has reneged on its pledge of a new Marshall Plan.'

name: Affected_party
definition_en: The individual or group to whom the Protagonist had made the Commitment and who is negatively affected by the Protagonist's not honoring the Commitment.  'Two people backed out on me a few days earlier.'

name: Commitment
definition_en: An expression of the commitment that the Protagonist has taken on earlier and which they fail to follow through on.   'It appears that Schwarzenegger will renege on an agreement he made with teachers.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs,  secondary effects (quietly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Protagonist that also affect the action (coldly).   'They deliberately backed out of Government last November because they knew that the 'hard men' were not ready for it.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Protagonist fails to honor their commitment.  'When a host city backed out at the last minute and Russellville, Ark., landed the opportunity to host the Babe Ruth 16-Year-Old World Series.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Protagonist  fails to honor the commitment they made.    'But his efforts came to nought when 18 of the 19 accused were bailed out as most witnesses backed out in court.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the Protagonist's failure to honor the Commitment logically follows.   'The buyer backed out because the seller asked for more money'

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the Protagonist's act of going back on their Commitment as a whole.   'When Roy Jones cowardly backed out of a fight with Heavyweight Buster Douglas, Toney again offered himself as a replacement.'

name: Degree
definition_en: How much the Protagonist goes back on their Commitment.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re_encoding, but not necessarily.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times the Protagonist backed out on a commitment.

name: Result
definition_en: The outcome of the Protagonist going back on a commitment.

name: Institution
definition_en: The Institution forms a part of a governmental body. It consists of individual Members and is dedicated to a Purpose.

name: Members
definition_en: A person belonging to an Organization.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason for which an Organization is formed or the purpose to which it is dedicated.

name: Period_of_existence
definition_en: The interval during which the Organization exists.

name: Name
definition_en: A name given to the Organization for identification.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE describes the general location where the Organization operates, but does not indicate the possessor of the Organization.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description of the Organization not covered by a more specific frame element.

name: Domain
definition_en: The concern of the Institution -- broadly speaking, the aspect of society that they affect.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which a particular gradable Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Entity or Attribute from the norm.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity or its Attribute is in the state of having the specified style.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity or its Attribute has a particular style.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity has the Attribute to a given Degree.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which a particular gradable Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Value from the norm or from the value for another Entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having  a particular Value for the Attribute.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Value for the Attribute.

name: Value
definition_en: The generally implicit Value of the Attribute.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity is has the Attribute to a given Degree.

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure.  'The cat is near the mat.'

name: Figure
definition_en: The Figure is perceived as located relative to a certain Ground location. The figure can be an entity or an event.  'The cat is near the mat.'

name: Accessibility
definition_en: This  FE identifies the  Accessibility between the Figure and some reference location (generally, the deictic center or the Ground). 'The cat is right near the table.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure. 'The cat was down near its food bowl .'

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the locative relation between Figure and Ground obtains.  'He was near Athens on Friday.'

name: Figures
definition_en: The Figures are items which mutually serve to identify the location of the other items.  'The two waffle houses are so close together they can throw ingredients across the road to each other .'

name: Degree
definition_en: An assessment of how the distance between the Figure and the Ground diverges from expectation.  'We 're very close to the treasure .'

name: Deixis
definition_en: An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder), or specifically separated from the speech context by distance or a barrier (over).  Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.  'She has a boyfriend way over in Springfield .' 'It is lying here on my desk .'

name: Directness
definition_en: An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target.  This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, directly, and due (and some combinations of these), but also occurs with rarer items like 'smack dab'.  'It landed right near the pole .'

name: Temporal_profile
definition_en: A description of how the access path to the Ground interacts with time.  This FE is filled only by the closed class of adverbials back.adv (which indicates that the position was occupied by the Figure before) and on.adv (which indicates a continued path).  While this FE in its most basic use refers to cases of actual motion, it can be used with descriptions of static position, in which case it either refers to fictive, imagined motion (as in the first example below), or it backgrounds motion entirely (as in the second example).  'You 'll find it straight on over near the closet.' 'He's already back near the house.'

name: Distance
definition_en: This  FE identifies the  Distance between the Figure and the Ground.  This FE requires an image schema with a vector that extends from the Ground, or a subpart of the Ground, in some direction, and the Distance is measured along this vector from the Ground to the profiled region.   'The island was 30 miles distant from the mainland.'

name: Shape
definition_en: A pattern that can be recognized when the Data is represented on a Graph.

name: Data
definition_en: A (usually quantitative) abstraction of information being represented in some Shape on a Graph.

name: Graph
definition_en: The visual representation of the information extracted from the Data.

name: Name
definition_en: An sequenced based naming system for individual members of a group.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Shape.

name: Location
definition_en: A specific region within the Graph which reveals a Shape or pattern.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The sentient animate being who acquires new knowledge.  'Sue grasped the essentials right away'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: A state of affairs or dynamic system whose internal make-up and working the Cognizer comes to assimilate into their knowledge structure.  'You must grasp the complex relationship of all these subjects to each other'

name: Completeness
definition_en: The extent to which the Cognizer has incorporated the workings and significance of a Phenomenon into their knowledge structure.  'To comprehend fully the distinction between task and process it is necessary to appreciate the evolutionary stages that groups go through.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously)  and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate the relative ease of the Cognizer in acquiring new knowledge (readily, easily).  'Its appeal rests on a simple logic that those inside and outside schools can readily comprehend'

name: Reference_point
definition_en: A mental concept or domain  to which the Cognizer relates their new knowledge.  'Unless one posits an inherent human tendency to comprehend the world in binary terms, one has to look for more sociological explanations.'

name: Category
definition_en: This frame element expresses a general type or class of which the Phenomenon is considered an instance by the Cognizer, allowing them to make predictions about the qualities, occurrence, or behavior of the Phenomenon.  'Dooling argued that if an individual sentence is comprehended as part of a larger semantic unit, part of the meaning of the sentence is likely to be redundant'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the when the Cognizer asssimilates the new knowledge.  'Yesterday the students finally grasped the meaning of the equation'

name: Faculty
definition_en: A part  of a person's cognitive-emotional faculties that is said to acquire knowledge.  'My heart grasped that reality immediately.' 'Man has understood something only when he has grasped it with his heart'

name: Evidence
definition_en: Evidence marks expressions that indicate the source of the Cognizer's  knowledge.  'The reason for this effect is easiest to understand from a picture.'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Grinding_cause
definition_en: An animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that grinds. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic. ' The wind ground the leaves into a fine powder. '

name: Grinder
definition_en: The Grinder breaks the Patient into smaller pieces.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Grinder grinds the Patient.

name: Locus
definition_en: The Locus is a description of the active zone of the Grinder, where the grinding most saliently takes place.  ' Russell ground the paper cups under his foot.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which  the Grinder grinds the Patient.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which  the Grinder grinds the Patient.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where  the Grinder grinds the Patient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which  the Grinder grinds the Patient.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result is the shape the Patient becomes.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when  the Grinder grinds the Patient.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is the entity which undergoes the change brought about by the Grinder or Grinding_cause.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time for which the Grinder grinds the Patient.

name: Goal
definition_en: This is where the Patient might end up, after undergoing the grinding process.

name: Result
definition_en: Result of the grooming event.

name: Agent
definition_en: The agent is the person who does the grooming.   'She washed the baby'

name: Patient
definition_en: The patient is the person who gets washed. 'She washed the baby.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This is an object that aids the washing process. 'She scrubbed her hands with soap.'

name: Body_part
definition_en: This is the region of the body that gets groomed. 'She scrubbed her hands with soap.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: This is a region of the object, body or the body part that gets groomed. 'I washed from the waist up.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the substance that is the grooming agent. 'Bobby washed his hair with shampoo'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The frequency with which the Agent groom himself/other.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Agent intentionally acts.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Duration
definition_en: How long the grooming takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Agent is trying to bring about by grooming.

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by the Agent to accomplish the grooming.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is the entity acted on and that undergoes a change.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result is the shape the Patient becomes.

name: Grower
definition_en: The Grower is the agent growing Food.

name: Food
definition_en: Food is the item grown by the Grower, which can include things not traditionally eaten, like flowers, etc., or items for other consumption-related uses, like medicines, smokables, etc.   'He grew flowers and potatoes.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument is used by the Grower as a tool grow Food. (This tool is not limited to typical artifacts and can be hands, arms, and other atypical hunting and fishing instruments.)  'Heavy-yielding crops are grown with chemical fertilizers'

name: Duration
definition_en: For what length of time the Grower is growing Food.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Grower grows Food.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Grower grows Food.

name: Place
definition_en: The greater geographic location where the Grower grows Food.

name: Time
definition_en: When the growing event occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Grower intends to accomplish by growing Food.  'He can grow flowers to beautify the garden'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Grower grows Food.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Ground
definition_en: This is the the physical background or context for the Food to which the Grower pays attention in his growing efforts.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Source
definition_en: The starting state of the Food, e.g., a seed.

name: Host
definition_en: The Host provides a location and/or resources for the Guest at the Host_location.  'Commander Silvers was the President's guest last week.' 'Would you please be the host for our visiting scholar this time around?'

name: Guest
definition_en: The Guest receives the hospitality of the Host.  'Commander Silvers was the President's guest last week.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Guest or Host.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby a focal participant achieves an action indicated by the target.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of the relationship.  'I was Manu's guest for few days in Allepey, in a very beautiful old house.'

name: Host_location
definition_en: The location associated with the Host, where the Guest is staying, working, etc.  'Edward VIII was a guest of my hotel in 1920.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the guest-and-host relationship holds.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A trait or characteristic of the Guest or Host.

name: Accused
definition_en: This is the person who is accused of a  Misdeed.  'Frank Quattrone is found guilty of obstructing federal investigations'

name: Misdeed
definition_en: The wrongful act which  the Accused was purportedly involved in.   'Cambridge woman says she's innocent of fraud. '

name: Viewpoint
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in connecting the Accused to the Misdeed.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Accused is involved in the Misdeed.   'Sammy Sosa was completely guilty of corking.' 'For his part, the writer is somewhat guilty of his usual charges: undue casual talk of nudity.'

name: Person
definition_en: The person who is evaluated for a level of enthusiasm.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Person's level of enthusiasm and participation.

name: Hair
definition_en: This FE is the hair itself 'Her tresses were golden.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: This FE is the Possessor of the body part.  'Michael's hair is long.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: A subregion of the body part referred to by the target, e.g.  'Her hair is dark at the roots'

name: Configuration
definition_en: Temporary Configurations of hair (eg braid, bun, ponytail).   Something done to the hair merely by movement.   'I pulled Michael's  ponytail. '

name: Hair_property
definition_en: A property of the hair (eg curly, fine, brown).  This acts much like "Descriptor" in the Observable_bodyparts Frame.  Colors, styles, natural properties are described by this frame element.

name: Location
definition_en: Where the salient part of the hair is. 'His hair was in his eyes.'

name: Accessory
definition_en: Items that are put in the hair as part of a Configuration or Style 'She braided ribbons into her hair.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which a Theme stops the motion.   'When the kitty was standing beside the slayer's pillow, she stopped to make sure everything was quiet'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Theme's motion stops.   ' She stopped on the threshold with a sinking heart'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Theme stops.  'John stopped suddenly, whirled around and spread out his arms'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE is used for a Depictive phrase describing the Theme.   'Once she reached the end she stopped with her nostrils flaring'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Theme stops motion.  'Martha stopped abruptly and stared at her only son'

name: Theme
definition_en: This FE identifies Theme whose motion ceases.   'When the kitty was standing beside the slayer's pillow, she stopped to make sure everything was quiet'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the length of Time during which the motion  is stopped.  'She stopped for a minute and listened, but the wind came back empty handed as she stared down the desolate road'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Theme stops motion.  'She weaved back and forth on her feet, then piroetted. She stopped by putting her hand to the ground and crouching'

name: Co-timed_event
definition_en: This FE identifies the last Co-timed_event of the stopped motion.  'The bus stopped with a shudder'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the halting event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: Containing event is an event that is occuring at a time during which the Theme ceases motion.

name: Dependent
definition_en: The state-of-affairs which cannot hold without the state of affairs of the Requirement or the presence of the Required_entity.

name: Requirement
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that must obtain in order for the Dependent to obtain.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Dependent depends on the presence of the Required_entity or the obtaining of the Requirement.  'A performance like this absolutely demands charm.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The state-of-affairs which militates that the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent to obtain.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent.

name: Condition
definition_en: The conditions under which the the Requirement is necessary.  'This Par 5 demands great shotmaking if the player is to equal or better par.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The field of endeavor whose nature imposes the Requirement.

name: Required_entity
definition_en: An entity that has to be present for the Dependent state of affairs to obtain.  'Believe it or not, but this cake requires a pound of mild sausage.'

name: Required_individual
definition_en: An individual that has to provide the Required_entity or to see to it that the Requirement state of affairs holds.  'It's a sport that demands everything of me.'

name: Place
definition_en: Place denotes a location in which the specified relation between Requirement and Dependent holds.  'In the US, putting this on the agenda requires the political weight and leadership of big city mayors.'

name: Source_symbol
definition_en: A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Source_representation format.  '"Hi, dude" translates into Spanish as Hola tío.'

name: Source_representation
definition_en: The representation system in which the Content pre-exists.  'The bands' name translates into English as Killer Bananas from their native French and they play metal and horror themed punk rock 'n' roll.'

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the translation equivalence holds.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the translation is made.  'In other contexts the word translates as 'function' or 'intention'.'

name: Target_symbol
definition_en: A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Target_representation format.  'The word giallo translates into English as 'yellow'.'

name: Target_representation
definition_en: The representation system within which the Target_symbol is equivalent in its signification to the Source_symbol within the Source_representation system .  'More sinister still is the fact that Homeland translates into German as Fatherland.'

name: Content
definition_en: The information that is meant to be represented by the Source_symbol and Target_symbol.  'The disclaimer in question translated as: "Yo, Gringo! This episode of The Twilight Zone was paid for by Robinson for Congress."'

name: Equivalence
definition_en: An assessment of how equivalent the Source_representation and the Target_representation are.  'The Swedish word, pepparkakor, literally translates as pepper cakes.'

name: Medium
definition_en: A text in which the Source_symbol is rendered by a Target_symbol to express a particular Content.  'In the New Testament the Greek word ekklesia translates 115 times as "church".'

name: Entity
definition_en: Some entity, abstract or concrete, which is stated to exist and be associated with the Topical_entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Entity exists and is associated with the Topical_entity

name: Duration
definition_en: The period during which the Entity exists in association with the Topical_entity.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A situation, force, or entity which brings about the existence of the Entity or its association with the Topical_entity.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Entity is associated with the Topical_entity.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the Entity is declared to exist in association with the Topical_entity.

name: Viewpoint
definition_en: The perspective of an individual who judges whether they consider the Entity to be associated with the Topical_entity.  'In the United States' eyes, the country doesn't have any real infrastructure.'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Topical_entity
definition_en: The entity under discussion, whose states and properties are impacted by its association with the Entity.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Host
definition_en: The Host allows the Visitor to enter his/her location (house, office, etc.) for a temporary period so that the Visitor can achieve a goal. The goal is often socially-motivated (e.g., socialization between the Visitor and the Host).

name: Visitor
definition_en: The Visitor is a guest of the Host at a location strongly associated with the Host.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose of the Host in hosting the Visitor.

name: Party_1
definition_en: The individual or individuals that form the more prominent (i.e. agentive) party of the commercial agreement, as compared with Party_2. That is, Party_1 is generally encoded as the External Argument of verbs, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Party_1. Thus manner expressions are construed to apply to Party_1, not necessarily to Party_2 or the group of Parties as a whole.

name: Party_2
definition_en: The semantically (and grammatically) less prominent participant (or group of participants) in the agreement. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with).

name: Obligation
definition_en: An expression of the commitment which the Parties have to engage in a commercial transaction.

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic is a description of the domain covered by the commercial agreement.

name: Medium
definition_en: As with other frames in the Communication domain, the Medium of communication may be expressed. Medium is the physical entity or channel used to record or negotiate the Obligation.    'The parties have a written agreement to arbitrate disputes arising in connection with the contract.'

name: Parties
definition_en: The group of individuals portrayed as equally involved in having a commercial agreement.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where an agreement was made.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the agreement was made.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme whose motion is blocked or free.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Theme exceeds or falls short of the ability to move to the Useful_location  'He has full access to the facilities.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the Theme meets or fails to meet the pre-conditions for getting to the Useful_location.

name: Explanation
definition_en: An Explanation for why the Barrier exists, or for why the Theme meets or fails to meet pre-conditions for entering the Useful_location.

name: Useful_location
definition_en: The place or thing that the Theme is headed towards, despite a potential or actual Barrier.

name: Barrier
definition_en: An entity, event, or state that (at least potentially) prevents the Theme from getting to the Useful_location.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist occurs as the External Argument of the targets in this frame. The Protagonist represents the one exhibiting the response to the Trigger.  'Pat's allergy to dairy products is severe.' 'Young children are very susceptible to infections. '

name: Trigger
definition_en: The Trigger most commonly occurs in a PP Complement headed by to. The Trigger is that substance or element which causes a health response in the Protagonist.  'Some people are very sensitive to chemicals in the environment.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner describes the way (or style) in which the Protagonist Health_response manifests itself.  'Different socio-economic groups , age-groups , ethnic groups , genders have different needs for medical services because of their differing susceptibility and experience of morbidity and accidents.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree describes the extent to which the health response occurs.  'Jake is extremely allergic to codeine.'  'Grass and clover seeds need fairly warm conditions for germination and are more sensitive to drought or excessive moisture than cereals.'.

name: Body_part
definition_en: The Body_part identifies the part of the body that is responding to the Trigger.  'Diabetics may have increased vascular sensitivity to angiotensin II'

name: Speaker
definition_en: This is the person who produces a Message. Typically, it is expressed in this frame as a PP-complement headed by from:   'The students heard from Pat that class was canceled.'

name: Hearer
definition_en: This FE is the person who receives a Message. It is expressed as an Exteranal Argument in this frame: 'The students heard from Pat that class was canceled.'

name: Message
definition_en: The Message is the content that is communicated from one person to another. It is normally expressed as an NP Object or a finite clause Complement: 'The students heard the news.''The students heard from Pat that class was canceled.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic is the subject matter about which the Message is communicated. It is normally expressed as a PP-complement headed by about, with or without a quantificational noun: 'The students heard about class.''The students heard something about today's class.' The quantificational noun, if present, is treated as the Message.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used to transmit the Message.  It is normally expressed as a PP-complement headed by on or in: 'The students heard the news on the radio.''The students read the news in the paper.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time the Hearer receives the Message. 'I heard in June that Pablo left, how sad!'

name: Insulator
definition_en: The object which provides warm. It does not have to radiate heat; it may provide warmth with heavy insulation.  'That is a warm bed.'

name: Activity
definition_en: The Activity the Experiencer engages in to feel heat.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world when the Experiencer feels warmth

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Experiencer feels a level of heat.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The sentient entity that utilizes the Insulator.

name: Hedged_content
definition_en: The idea or ideas that the speaker wishes to be careful about asserting.

name: Communicator
definition_en: The Communicator greets the arrival of an Individual or occurrence of an Event.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Communicator heralds.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which a Communicator  heralds.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Communicator  heralds.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a Communicator heralds.  'The town heralded his arrival with a peal of church bells.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Communicator that also affect the heralding ( eagerly, carefully).

name: Individual
definition_en: The person who is greeted at their arrival by the Communicator.

name: Event
definition_en: The occurrence which is greeted by the Communicator.  'Sheep scattered from the road as trumpets heralded his arrival at the castle gates'

name: Medium
definition_en: The symbol-containing artifact whereby a Communicator heralds.

name: Obstruction
definition_en: The entity that the Agent uses to block the Hidden_object from being perceptible.   'She shrouded the tub with fabric featuring birds and flowers. '

name: Hidden_object
definition_en: The Hidden_object is the entity which is blocked from view.  'Michael Jackson gave wine to the 13-year-old cancer patient at the center of the molestation charges he's battling but concealed it inside a Coke can.'

name: Potential_observer
definition_en: The Potential_observer denotes a person who might perceive the Hidden_object if it was not hidden.   'The wife claims she hid the gun from him but retrieved it after he became abusive.'   Phrases such as "from view" and "from sight" are assumed to indicate that the Hidden_object is not visible to any Potential_observer.   ''He hid the motorbike from view under a few nearby bushes.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Hidden_object becomes perceptually inaccessible.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person who causes the Hidden_entity to be not perceptually accessible to potential perceivers.  'The deputy concealed the bayonet under his coat.'

name: Hiding_place
definition_en: The location in which the Hidden_object is placed so as not to be perceptually accessible.   'He had concealed the necklace behind him.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the spatial setting in which the hiding event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: Time denotes the interval of time during which the Agent causes the Hidden_object to become hidden from perceptual access.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the occurrence of the hiding event logically follows.

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Agent that brings about the hiding of the Hidden_object.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Agent hopes to bring about by hiding the Hidden_object.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist is the entity that tends towards or plans some Action which the Hindrance causes to be more difficult.

name: Hindrance
definition_en: The Hindrance is the force which makes the Action more difficult or less likely to be successfully completed. The Hindrance may be a lack of enabling force: ' The project was hampered by a lack of funds. ' or the Hindrance may be an obstacle in the natural progression of the Protagonist or Action. ' Burns was hindered by Smither's violent attack. '

name: Action
definition_en: The Action is what the Protagonist desires to do, which is made more difficult by the Hindrance. It can also be a natural act or collective endeavor, not linked to an overt Protagonist.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Hindrance affects the Protagonist or Action.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location where  he Hindrance affects the Protagonist or Action.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree is the extent to which the Hindrance affects the Protagonist or Action.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE describes the means by which hindering occurs

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE label is used for the cause of the Hindrance

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner in which hindering occurs

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time over which the hindering takes place.  'The exporting of goods from the United States was impeded for several months while negotiations continued.'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause. In other words, given only the facts of the *Concessive, one would expect them to cause the world to be the opposite of what is protrayed in the main clause.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Employee
definition_en: The person whom the Employer takes on as an Employee, obligating them to perform some Task in order to receive Compensation.  'I was just hired yesterday!'

name: Employer
definition_en: The person (or institution) that takes on an Employee, giving them  Compensation in return for the performance of an assigned Task.  'Last month, IBM hired Mike Zisman to head up its storage software group.'

name: Compensation
definition_en: The Compensation is the payment that the Employee is set to receive  for performing an assigned Task.  'They fired our management, hired him for 20% more and gave him a free office to set up his own company.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employer hires an Employee.  'The three young men were given medals and hastily commissioned'.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Employer hires the Employee.  'Actually, he hired me in a bordello.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when an Employer hires the Employee.  'Guess who just got hired today!'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Employer hires the Employee.  'John hired her to make his wife jealous.'

name: Task
definition_en: The action that the Employee is taken on by the Employer to do.  'I was hired just to empty the trash cans.'

name: Position
definition_en: The label given to a particular type of employment.  'Look, I wasn't hired as your waitress!'

name: Field
definition_en: The Field that the Employee is going to work in for their Employer.  'It's not easy to get hired in academia.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity that the Employer uses to hire the Employee.   'The congressman hired him with personal funds as an aide. '

name: Means
definition_en: An action by the Employer whereby the hire is brought about.  'The manager hired me with a handshake.'

name: Contract_basis
definition_en: The Contract_basis is the condition of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period or payment arrangements.   'She couldn't figure it out but suggested that I'd be good for the job, so they hired me part time at first.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the hiring event began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Event
definition_en: This FE identifies the event which occurs to create history.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies where the event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the event occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for which an event occurs.

name: Entity
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity, concrete or abstract.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain is (a characterization of) the type of event that is part of the Event's history.  'Throughout the campaign activists have made financial history as one by one major corporations have yielded to protester power'

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject about which the history is given.  'The role of the Byzantine Empire in European history is not understood by all.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain is (a characterization of) the type of event that is to be included in consideration of the Topic's history.  'Elizabethan Stage remain classics of literary history.'

name: End_time
definition_en: The end of the span of time during which the Topic occurs.

name: Start_time
definition_en: The beginning of the time span over which the Topic occurs.

name: Time_span
definition_en: The span of time over which the events related to the Topic take place.

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration, often expressed in calendric units, of the history of the Topic.

name: Time
definition_en: When the events concerning the Topic occured.

name: Event
definition_en: This FE identifies the event which occurs to create history.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies where the event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the event occurs.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual who tries to interact with the Target.

name: Target
definition_en: The Target is the entity located in an indirectly accessible location relative to the Agent.

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt at interaction, incorporated in the LUs of the frame.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent achieves a Purpose.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the interaction takes place at the Target_location.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when something hits or misses.

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the Agent during the event.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Agent manages or fails to interact with the Target.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of how the details of the event compare to others, either generally (the same way), or in terms of a state of the Agent which influences the event (carelessly).

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason for which the Agent attempts to interact with the Target

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which contextualizes the hitting or missing of the Agent but is not conceived of as caused by it.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The object manipulated by the Agent in order to interact with the Target.

name: Target_location
definition_en: The location that the Agent is attempting to access using the Instrument.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times that the Agent hits or misses the Target.

name: Deviation
definition_en: The distance of the actual location from the Target_location.

name: Target
definition_en: The entity which is hit by a Projectile directed by the Agent.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that directs the Projectile such that it impacts the Target.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Agent hopes to bring about by hitting the Target

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Agent hits the Target.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the event happens.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the Target hit by the Agent.  'He shot me in the arm!'

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by the Agent that accomplishes hitting the Target.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The entity, most often ammunition or a firearm, which the Agent manipulates to hit the Target.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent decides not to engage in a Desirable_action for a while or not to interact with a Salient_entity.  'Instead, he held off on a public announcement of his decision for more than a year.'</def-root >

name: Desirable_action
definition_en: Desirable_action identifies the event or activity in which the Agent does not engage for a while.  'The board also waited with the appointment of seven members to the planning and zoning commission until a policy is set regarding requirements.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the temporary forgoing occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the temporary forgoing occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the temporary forgoing occurs.  'Portland General Electric, for example, has held off on retail rate increases by selling some excess power at high wholesale prices.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the temporary forgoing occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the interval of Time during which the the forgoing occurs.  'Saskatchewan teachers are not a happy lot as they had voted for a strike in June then held off on it to give negotiations a chance during the summer.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the temporary forgoing occurs.   'We held off on taking him out so as to not disrupt the plans for the invasion of Iraq?'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the Agent's decision to temporarily forgo a Desirable_action or to not interact with a Salient_entity logically follows.   'Yes yes I saw them, but I waited with a reply for sometime because I wanted first to show them to my guildmates.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the Agent does not engage in the Desirable_action.

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: An entity that evokes a contextually inferrable Desirable_action that the Agent is temporarily forgoing.  'I ordered the blackberry cobbler with ice cream for dessert and held off on another pint as the rain kept coming down.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the Agent's decision to forgo a Desirable_action to the point in time when the Agent engages in the action.  'The United Arab Emirates (UAE) waited with the deal for nearly five years because of a dispute with the Pentagon about the avionics.'

name: End_point
definition_en: The point in time, defined either as a clock time or in terms of an event that takes place, at which the Agent engages in the Desirable_action or interacts with the Salient_entity.  'We waited on technology development until we had made instructional plans.'

name: Host
definition_en: The Host is the person whose Behavior towards others as a (potential) host is evaluated.

name: Guest
definition_en: The Guest is the entity which is positively or negatively treated by the Host.

name: Behavior
definition_en: The Behavior is the action of the Host on which the evaluation of the Host's character is based.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree is the extent to which the Host exhibits the particular Behavior towards others.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the situation or person that the Host's Behavior responds to or is related to.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part which indicates the character of the Host.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the way in which the Host embodies the characters of a good or poor host.

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the evaluation.

name: Side_1
definition_en: One of two participants in a hostile encounter.  'While the U.S.'s battle with terrorist-harboring nations is far off ...'

name: Side_2
definition_en: One of two participants in a hostile encounter, usually the second mentioned. 'While the U.S.'s battle with terrorist-harboring nations is far off ...'

name: Sides
definition_en: The jointly expressed sides in a hostile encounter.  'They fought over the right to own land.'

name: Issue
definition_en: An unresolved question over which the two sides of a hostile encounter are in disagreement.   'They had a dust-up over who was prettier .'  Quite often it takes the form of a covert question of various sorts. So in an example like:  'They fought over the right to own land.'   among many other possibilities, the covert question might be more explicitly phrased as follows:  'They fought over what the right to own land means.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The desired result of the outcome of the hostile encounter for the Side_1 or for all the Sides collectively.  It may either directly refer to the state of affairs that is desired, e.g.  'He dueled with his former second to defend the honour of the man he had killed .'   or it the state of affairs may be implicit in an (abstract or concrete) entity that they desire, e.g.  'Rival Democratic presidential candidates Mr Bill Clinton and Mr Jerry Brown taunted each other at the weekend as mudslinging in the battle for votes in tomorrow's crucial New York primary reached a new low.'

name: Means
