definition_en: Means describes the way in which a side engages in a hostile encounter. 'President Corazon Aquino of the Philippines is bracing herself for a legal battle over her decision to allow the remains of the former president, Ferdinand Marcos, to be returned home from Hawaii for burial.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of the hostile encounter. Descriptions of the intensity count as Manner expressions. 'After Brundle's Jaguar took off like a scalded cat, it was Mass who hunted it down, an soon engaged it in a lurid battle.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the hostile encounter takes place.   'Following the battle of Naseby in 1645 ...'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the hostile encounter occurs.   'Following the battle of Naseby in 1645 he died.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which an event occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: A Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of an event.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which an event occurs.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The body movement may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal Cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state.  Internal Cause is expressed in a PP complement.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Hunter
definition_en: The Hunter is the agent hoping to obtain Food.

name: Food
definition_en: Food is the sought-out item by the Hunter.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument is used by the Hunter as a tool to help obtain Food. (This tool is not limited to typical artifacts and can be hands, arms, and other atypical hunting and fishing instruments.)  'Late Prehistoric peoples hunted with the bow and arrow.'

name: Duration
definition_en: For what length of time the Hunter attempted to obtain Food.   'We all fished for several hours.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Hunter makes the attempt for Food.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an attempt at achieving a Food obtainment.

name: Outcome
definition_en: The failure or success of an attempt.  'She successfully hunted and ate a porcupine.'

name: Place
definition_en: The greater geographic location where the Hunter attempts to obtain Food.  'Europe's billionaires hunt boars in Romania.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the Time seeking action occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Hunter intends to accomplish by seeking Food.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Hunter attempts to obtain Food.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the amount of effort the Hunter puts into his attempt to obtain Food.

name: Ground
definition_en: This is the entity to which the Hunter pays attention. It is referred to as Ground because it serves as the background or context for the Food.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist, regardless of whether the protagonist, and hence the Co-participant, is more agent- or more undergoer-like.

name: Hunter
definition_en: The Hunter is the agent hoping to obtain Food.

name: Food
definition_en: Food is the sought-out item by the Hunter.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument is used by the Hunter as a tool to help obtain Food. (This tool is not limited to typical artifacts and can be hands, arms, and other atypical hunting and fishing instruments.)

name: Duration
definition_en: For what length of time the Hunter attempted to obtain Food.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Hunter makes the attempt for Food.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an attempt at achieving a Food obtainment.

name: Outcome
definition_en: The failure or success of an attempt.

name: Place
definition_en: The greater geographic location where the Hunter attempts to obtain Food.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Food seeking action occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Hunter intends to accomplish by seeking Food.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Hunter attempts to obtain Food.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the amount of effort the Hunter puts into an attempt to obtain Food.

name: Ground
definition_en: This is the entity to which the Hunter pays attention. It is referred to as Ground because it serves as the background or context for the Food.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Hunter
definition_en: The Hunter is the agent that has successfully obtained Food.

name: Food
definition_en: Food is the item obtained by the Hunter.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument is used by the Hunter as a tool to obtain Food.   'He could easily catch fish with his hands.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Hunter obtains the Food.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Food is obtained.

name: Place
definition_en: The greater geographic location where the Hunter obtains Food.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Food seeking action occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Hunter intends to accomplish obtaining Food.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Hunter obtains Food.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the amount of effort the Hunter puts into an attempt to obtain Food.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Type
definition_en: The kind of thing of which instances are under discussion.   'Smithers works in a different office now'

name: Current_instance
definition_en: The instance of the Type that is currently under discussion.

name: Previous_instance
definition_en: An instance of the Type that was encountered previously and which is now compared for identity with the Current_instance.

name: Previous_context
definition_en: The situation in which another instance of the Type was encountered earlier.  'This is a different car than last week'

name: Set_of_instances
definition_en: The complete set of instances of the Type involved in the mentioned contexts.   'Kent Clark and Superman are the same person' 'Kent Clark and Superman are the same person'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Current_instance is the same or different.

name: Instance
definition_en: The instance of a type or out of a set that is currently under discussion.

name: Identity
definition_en: The feature of each Instance that distinguishes it from all others.  Notionally, each Instance has a separate Identity, although in practice many Instances cannot be distinguished from each other.

name: Type
definition_en: The kind of thing of which instances are under discussion.   'Smithers works in a different office now'

name: Instance
definition_en: The instance of the Type that is currently under discussion.

name: Identity
definition_en: The property of an Instance that is defined as unique for each separate Instance of a Type.

name: Idiosyncrasy
definition_en: An entity or characteristic  belonging to the Entity.  'Paul has an idiosyncratic tendency to go barefoot at all times.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity that has a certain distinguishing Idiosyncrasy.  'This bird is unique to England'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Idiosyncrasy differs from the norm.  'Was this behavior completely idiosyncratic?'

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: A region of space located relative to a Ground.

name: Ground
definition_en: An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Profiled_region.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person that borrows a Characteristic behavior from a Standard.  'Mimic Snotlings do n't really think for themselves, they merely mimic the actions of Orcs and Goblins around them.'

name: Characteristic
definition_en: The Characteristic is a behavior or property that the Standard possesses and which the Agent adopts in his or her own behavior.  'They were all mimicking my accent.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (eagerly, carefully).  'She mimicked him carefully as he moved, her movements naturally graceful.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the imitation.   'Alhough proud of their strong balance sheets , most European superbanks have yet to imitate the Japanese by lending aggressively abroad.'

name: Standard
definition_en: The Standard is the entity that exhibits a certain Characteristic that the Agent models their own behavior on.  'The singer says Gwen has copied her in many different ways.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the imitation.  'Kashi's soul remembered all the characteristics of Kashi, the boy, and therefore mimicked his hoarse voice in order to stir my recognition.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the imitation event logically follows.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the imitating event as being in some state. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the imitating event.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the imitation event occurs and of which the imitating event is taken to be a part.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Agent's way of behaving is similar to that of the Standard.   'Kurt Cobain aped him to perfection.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the imitation occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent imitates some entity which acts as a Standard.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent immobilizes the Patient. 'Lisa handcuffed Mike to the refridgerator.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is immobilized by the Agent, optionally to an Anchor.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Agent that accomplishes the immobilization.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent immobilizes a Patient.  'Lisa handcuffed Mike to the refridgerator to reduce the mess.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Anchor
definition_en: The Agent attaches the Patient to an Anchor, generally, an immobile object. Lisa handcuffed Mike to the refridgerator.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Patient is immobilized as a result.  'The policman tied up the burglar completely'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the immobilizing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). This FE also covers expressions that indicate salient characteristics of the Agent which also affect the action (carefully, eagerly).  'Brian grabbed Kim's arm and handcuffed him quickly.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which an Impact occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Impactor
definition_en: The entity that hits the Impactee. 'The rock hit the sand with a thump.'

name: Impactee
definition_en: The entity which is hit by the Impactor. 'The rock hit the sand with a thump.'

name: Impactors
definition_en: The multiple entities that collide. 'The car and truck collided at a combined speed of over 100MPH.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The speed at impact. 'The wrecking ball struck at 330 mph.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: Subregion identifies the affected part of the larger whole. 'The sparks hit the paper right on the edge.'

name: Force
definition_en: The amount of force in the course of the impact.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The Time throughout which the impact repeatedly takes place.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Impactors or the Impactor during the impact.

name: Agent
definition_en: The conscious entity, generally a person, that moves the Goods.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: An mobile entity directed by the Agent that holds the Goods and moves them along from the Exporting_area to the Importing_area.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

name: Goods
definition_en: The items of value whose location is changing.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Agent moves the Goods.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent moves the Goods.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies the state of a participant during the action

name: Importing_area
definition_en: The FE Importing_area is the place that the Goods end up as a result of motion.

name: Path
definition_en: Path identifies the location of the Goods during transit, i.e. after leaving the Exporting_area and before reaching the Importing_area.

name: Exporting_area
definition_en: The place where the Goods are initially, before the action.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This Frame Element is used for a characteristic or description of the Goods. Note that Descriptor is not an FE of the same character as other FEs.  Specifically, rather than filling a slot, it identifies a modifier of its head noun.

name: Factor
definition_en: Factor is used for the concrete or abstract entity whose importance is assessed. ' Being sure they are buying fresh food is important to most people.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate the Degree to which the Factor is important to the Undertaking. ' 1992 is of great importance to the business community. '

name: Undertaking
definition_en: The Undertaking is a process or state or field of activity in which the Interested_party has a stake. 'Temperature is the most critical factor in successful storage.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE  identifies the Explanation for which the Factor is important to the Undertaking. 'It 's critical to get it right because there are situations  where if you don't, they will withhold some commission..'

name: Interested_party
definition_en: Interested_party identifies the people who are affected by a particular Factor.  ' Being sure they are buying fresh food is important to most people.'

name: Field
definition_en: A Factor may be generally important to the people or the activities in a field of endeavour.  ' A successful GATT round is important for the world economy. '

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Factor is important to the Undertaking.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Factor is important.

name: Importer
definition_en: The conscious entity, generally a person, that brings the Goods into the Importing_area.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: A mobile entity directed by the Importer that holds the Goods and moves them along from the Exporting_area to the Importing_area.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Importer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Importer that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

name: Goods
definition_en: The items of value whose location is changing.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Importer moves the Goods.  'Some department stores import expensive items to please their higher-paying customers.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that explains the Importer's importation of the Goods.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Importer moves the Goods.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies the state of a participant during the action 'Kazakhstan imported the petroleum, unaware of its own reserves.'

name: Importing_area
definition_en: The FE Importing_area is the place that the Goods end up as a result of motion.

name: Path
definition_en: Path identifies the location of the Goods during transit, i.e. after leaving the Exporting_area and before reaching the Importing_area.

name: Exporting_area
definition_en: The place where the Goods are initially, before the being moved.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative instance of the importing event , and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar importing events.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result is the final state of the Goods when brought into the Importing_area.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: This FE applies to participants who derive a benefit from the occurrence of the act of importation.  'The United States imported protein bars for backpackers and hikers. '

name: Responsible_party
definition_en: The person who must perform the Duty.   'The winning bid committed her to paint an oil portrait for the high bidder.'

name: Duty
definition_en: The action that the Responsible_party is obligated to perform.  'Had she really said the word which pledged her to marry Horace Holmcroft in a fortnight?'

name: Condition
definition_en: This FE indicates the Conditions under which the Responsible_party is obligated to perform the Duty .

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which  the Duty is imposed on the Responsible_party  by the Obligator or the Situation.  'The City Council then obligated themselves to have the sewers made ready and the streets leveled off without any additional cost to the Sisters.'

name: Place
definition_en: A location in which the Responsible_party has a specified Duty .  'At Dayton, the parties obligated themselves to respect and promote fulfillment of the annexes.'

name: Obligator
definition_en: The Obligator is the person who imposes the Duty on the Responsible_party.   'She pledged him to pay her the money back.'

name: Situation
definition_en: A state of affairs that results in the Responsible_party being obligated to carry out the Duty in accordance with the Principle.   ' Admitting a genocide was occurring  would have obligated them, based on their signing the December 1948 Convention on the repression of genocide, to do something about it. '

name: Principle
definition_en: A regulating idea  (which may be instantiated as a document)  that the Responsible_party is subject to.  'And no law obligated him to talk to the police, let alone the media'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Obligator hopes to bring about by imposing the obligation.  'She pledged him to work on the project just to get him out of her hair .'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any holistic description of the details of the action, either comparing to another event or describing the action in terms of characteristics of the Obligator that affect the action holistically.  'You committed me to this maliciously !'

name: Means
definition_en: An event which brings about the obligation.  'She did n't understand that she obligated me to stay by always getting in trouble .'

name: Figure
definition_en: The entity (a person, organization, product, or event) for which the Audience has an Impression.  'He projects a mysterious persona.'

name: Audience
definition_en: A person or group of people who have an Impression of a Figure.  'His public image is flawless'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The effect of the Impression left on the Audience.

name: Degree
definition_en: The effectiveness of the Impression on the Audience.

name: Context
definition_en: A spatial, cultural, or personal delimitation within which a Figure leaves an Impression on an Audience.

name: Impression
definition_en: A generalized conception of a Figure presented to or shared by an Audience.

name: Prisoner
definition_en: The person who is confined in a penal institution.  'Man Falsely Imprisoned for 24 Years Seeks Damages'

name: Prison
definition_en: The Prison  within which the Prisoner comes to be confined.

name: Authorities
definition_en: The Authorities are the institution or actors carrying out the imprisonment.  ' When she returned, the Chaoyang Town government authorities imprisoned her for 5 days.'

name: Offense
definition_en: The action that the Prisoner is being punished for.  'After all, Dowdy was not imprisoned <fex  name="off">for taking a bribe or even thinking about taking a bribe, but rather for committing perjury against two government witnesses who themselves eventually were imprisoned for defrauding the government.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Prisoner is kept.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the imprisonment happens.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose of the imprisonment.   'City officials later release the blacks and say they imprisoned them in order to protect them from rioters.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Authorities that brings about the imprisonment.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the imprisoning event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Authorities that affect the action (ruthlessly).

name: Explanation
definition_en: The act or state of affairs that the Authorities respond to by imprisoning the Prisoner.   'Though both of my grandparents were born in Canada and grew up speaking English and never had been to Japan, during the Second World War, the Canadian government imprisoned them because of their Japanese genes.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Authorities maintains the confinement of the Prisoner.   'Enforcement officers caught up with Irma and imprisoned her for two weeks.'

name: Conviction
definition_en: The legal classification which characterizes the Offense.  'Alf leader is Imprisoned for Arson and Burglary.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: Iterations marks expressions that indicate the number of times the Prisoner was imprisoned.

name: Entity
definition_en: The object that undergoes change.  'Improvements in marketing techniques have since rendered it obsolete.'

name: Prior_state
definition_en: The former state of the Entity.  'The prognosis has improved from a few months of life to a median age of survival of over 20 years .'

name: Post_state
definition_en: The state of the Entity following the improvement.  'The prognosis has improved from a few months of life to a median age of survival of over 20 years .'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the improvement occurs.  'Her mood suddenly improved after sundown .'

name: Rate
definition_en: The rate at which the change happens.  'His leadership has slowly improved until he has made us forget the sulky Nasser Hussian era'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the improvement, generally a description comparing events (the same way).   'Our major overseas markets has improved tentatively and increased spending by consumers and government does not appear to be benefiting this .'

name: Duration
definition_en: The period over which the improvement occurs.  'Screwcap wine seals enable bottle maturation, one of many wine-making improvements over a long period of time.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount of improvement that the Entity has attained.  'Robert's music is declining further as his self-indulgence is encouraged by a small subset of fans .'

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant dimension of improvement.  'Why have n't we improved in our outlook ? '

name: Explanation
definition_en: An event or state of affairs that brings about the improvement of the Entity.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Improvement occurs.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE describes the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Improvement event occurs.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Bomb
definition_en: The Bomb explodes, injuring or damaging a Target.

name: Use
definition_en: The type of activity that the Bomb is generally involved in.  Often this can be considered a kind of Type specification also.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Bomb belongs to.

name: Material
definition_en: The substance that makes up the Bomb.

name: Wielder
definition_en: The person that wishes to attack the Target and who controls (directly or indirectly) the detonation of the Bomb.

name: Part
definition_en: This FE identifies a part of the Bomb. This includes parts that aid in the detonation or damaging, or mere attachments.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to an Bomb.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which a Bomb comes into existence.

name: Creator
definition_en: The individual or group responsible for the creation of the Bomb.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description or characteristic of the Bomb.

name: Target
definition_en: The intended or actual target of the Bomb.

name: Location
definition_en: The location of the Bomb.

name: Entity
definition_en: TheFrame Element Entity identifies the person or thing that has a tendency towards some Behaviour.   ' Lubomir was not inclined to believe me '

name: Behavior
definition_en: The FE Behavior marks expressions that indicate which state or action the Entity tends towards.  'Martha has a tendency to overdo the housekeeping.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate how great the inclination of an Entity towards a Behavior is.  'We're very inclined to doubt it. '

name: Basis
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate why the Entity has the propensity for some Behavior.  'Smurphs have a natural propensity to hide in caves'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Total
definition_en: A complex entity, either an aggregate or a unit, of which a Part,  a constituent or a component, is specified.   'His collection included two El Grecos'

name: Part
definition_en: A component or constituent that is specified to form part of the Total.  'The larger album includes designs for his house at Whitehall.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE indicates the purpose for which some implicit (non-expressed) agent causes the inclusion of the Part within the Total. 'This electronic transmission includes encryption protocols in order to prevent outside surveillance.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE identifies the frequency with which the Part is included int he Total. 'Software packages often contain promotional items.'

name: Contrast_set
definition_en: This FE indicates other elements that are included within the Total. 'This book includes among other things three chapters on macroeconomics.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: This FE indicates the sub-location of the Total in which the Part is included.  'This plan includes within the final stage three separate sub-stages.' 'My list contains four names in the final section.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Total includes the Part.  'Last year the recognized departments included the Russian and East European Institute, and the Office of International Programs.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Total includes the Part.  'In California, the category excludes minors and the mentally ill.'

name: Whole
definition_en: The Whole is the larger entity that includes the Part.

name: Part
definition_en: The Part is either a subset or a constituent part of the Whole.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the inclusion relation holds.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the inclusion relation holds.

name: Class
definition_en: The general category of entity which has been referred to.  'My Husband left me for another man!'

name: Added_set
definition_en: The instance of the Class that is added to the Initial_set of entities in the Class.   'There was another power outage today.'

name: Initial_set
definition_en: The previously mentioned group of entities of the Class.  'A further five incursions over and above those noted for 1995 took place in the first three months of 1996.'

name: Increment
definition_en: The number of entities within the Added_set.  'Four more years of misguided leadership appeared to be in the offing.'

name: Communicator
definition_en: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey the Unresolved_referent to another person.

name: Unresolved_referent
definition_en: The thing to which the Communicator or Medium refers for identification purposes.

name: Medium
definition_en: The physical or abstract setting in which the Unresolved_referent is conveyed.

name: Amount_of_information
definition_en: The amount of information exchanged when communication occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Communicator makes the indication.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Communicator makes the indication.

name: Time
definition_en: When the the Communicator is makes the indication.  'When this is resolved, I will name the winner.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration is the length of time during which the indicating takes place.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Communicator or Medium indicates the Unresolved_referent.  'Every month, new people name him in connection with these crimes.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason why the Communicator is indicating the Unresolved_referent.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Communicator or Medium indicates the Unresolved_referent.

name: Purpose
definition_en: To what end the Communicator or Medium makes the indication.

name: Entity
definition_en: The item whose Origin is under discussion.

name: Origin
definition_en: The discourse-salient place or culture where the Entity was produced.

name: Participant
definition_en: The Participant is either an active participant in all of the Events (e.g., Agent or Patient), or is more peripherally associated with the Events (e.g., Location or Topic).  'We've been worried about our recent hire's history of deceiving employers.'  'I was charmed, and also determined to learn more about the factory's history.'

name: Events
definition_en: The Events which the Participant is a part of. This FE is used to mark the frame-evoking element.  'We will focus on events in her recent history.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain is (a characterization of) the type of event that is to be included in consideration of the Participant's history.  'One of my colleagues is an expert on the economic history of the Hellenistic period'  'The Netherlands' long history of trade with China provides important information for modern political economies.'

name: End_time
definition_en: The end of the span of time during which the Events occur.  'This article discusses mainly the geography and the history of Palestine until the United Nations took up the Palestine problem in 1947.'

name: Start_time
definition_en: The beginning of the time span over which the Events occur.  'The introduction describes the history of geography from the eighteenth century onwards.'

name: Time_span
definition_en: The span of time over which the Events take place.  'We have traced the flag?s past between its original conception in the 14th century and its end a hundred years later.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration, often expressed in calendric units, of the history of the Participant.  'The following sections document the entire 25-year history of the company.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A characterization of the Participant or Events.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Events concerning the Participant occured.

name: Stimulus
definition_en: The entity which inspires a feeling of amazement at its exceptionality.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer experiences the emotion brought about by the Stimulus

name: Degree
definition_en: An expression of how unusual the ineffability of the Stimulus is.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the Stimulus is able to bring about the emotion.

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is the area in which the Stimulus brings about an effect on the Experiencer.

name: Comparison_set
definition_en: The Comparison_set is the set of individuals the Stimulus is compared to when determining the Degree of the emotional reaction.

name: Property
definition_en: A feature of the Stimulus which causes a particular experience.  'That night was magic in every way .'

name: Attribute
definition_en: An expression of the attribute of ineffability.  'She had a magical quality .'

name: Infection
definition_en: An invasion, typically undetected, of an entity's system. The infection most often compromises the entity's stability. Infections are a common pathology for diseases.

name: Infected_entity
definition_en: This FE labels the recipient of the Infection.

name: Infection_cause
definition_en: This FE labels the cause of the Infection which affects the Infected_entity.

name: Medium
definition_en: The medium through which the infection is transmitted.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Infecting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification, force, secondary effects, and general descriptions comparing events.

name: Place
definition_en: The place at which the Infecting event occurs; or, the location of the Infection_cause.

name: Time
definition_en: When the infection occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing a participant in the event.

name: Means
definition_en: An act by an Infection_cause that enables them to act upon the Infected_entity.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of an Infection.

name: Force
definition_en: Something which has the capability of affecting a Entity in some way.  'The power of love can do great things.'

name: Entity
definition_en: Something which is dependent on the influencing Force.  'Final quarter reports have great influence on stock prices.'

name: Domain
definition_en: A description of the areas in which the Force can affect the Entity.

name: Source
definition_en: A principle factor which gives the Force the capability to affect the Entity.

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: A situation which can be influenced or brought about by the Force.

name: Information
definition_en: The Information that the Cognizer possesses or comes to posess.  'Not long before Bill Marlin died, he shared with me his information that Mrs Wright was with her husband on the day Wright was born.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is aware of the Information.  'Our information shows that soon after the turn of the 1900's, John Dazey was making can openers in the Dallas Texas area at the time.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is what the Information is about in general.  'What happens to my information if I quit my membership?'

name: Source
definition_en: The Cognizer obtains the Information from the Source.  'How credible is the information from the Internet?'

name: Means_of_gathering
definition_en: An action or method used by the Cognizer that results in the acquisition of the Information.  'Who can see and use survey information?'

name: Display
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity or substance that is designed to have a particular Use.

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which a display is intended.

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Display into existence.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which an Display comes into existence.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to an Display.

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Display.

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Display, including components, code, etc.

name: Activity
definition_en: The Activity which is enabled or facilitated by the infrastructure.  'At present, you'll find that Belize has a travel infrastructure that's improving but still far from polished.' 'As a result , one of the central policy priorities of government has been to strengthen significantly the academic infrastructure.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location of the infrastructure.  'Much of the transportation infrastructure in the US was developed when there was no need for private money.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: The organization, institution, or individual who owns the infrastructure.  'Increase the value of  your company's technology infrastructure'

name: Resource
definition_en: The infrastructure may be conceived of as consisting of Resources that can be made use of by Users in performing an Activity.  'Members of the organization can use the service infrastructure to perform management tasks.' 'It is critical to point out that, while our highway infrastructure continues to deteriorate, highway use is on the rise.'

name: User
definition_en: The people for whom the infrastructure is designed to be used by.  In the cases where the constituent denoting the user also evokes the Activity, we annotate this on the second FE layer.  ' There are no specific barriers to investment in Bulgaria's tourist infrastructure or in the import of products to be used for tourist infrastructure development.' ' There are no specific barriers to investment in Bulgaria's tourist infrastructure or in the import of products to be used for tourist infrastructure development.' 'Our company makes constant use of the vast infrastructure for businesses offered by the government.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the infrastructure.

name: Infrastructure
definition_en: The collection of entities and/or institutions that help to promote an Activity of a public character.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Ingestor ingests the Substance.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Ingestor ingests the Substance.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Ingestor ingests the Substance.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Ingestor ingests the Substance.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Ingestor ingests the Substance.

name: Delivery_device
definition_en: The Delivery_device is the means by which the Substance is ingested. ' Tabitha smoked a pipe.' ' Simon  smoked  pot with a bong.'

name: Ingestor
definition_en: The Ingestor ingests the Substance.

name: Substance
definition_en: The Substance is the drug or other substance that is ingested by the Ingestor.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency with which the Ingestor ingests.

name: Entry_path
definition_en: The Entry_path is the path along which the Substance enters the Ingestor's body. ' Rick snorted cocaine up his nose.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration is the length of time for which the Ingestor ingests.

name: Ingestor
definition_en: The Ingestor is the person eating or drinking.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Ingestibles
definition_en: The Ingestibles are the entities that are being consumed by the Ingestor.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action.

name: Source
definition_en: Place from which the Ingestor takes the Ingestibles

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Ingestor that enables them to accomplishes the whole act of ingestion. 'The thing ate by snaking its long tongue out and grabbing with it.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Ingestibles are consumed by the Ingestor.  'The wolves devoured the carcass completely'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The action that the Ingestor hopes to bring about by ingesting.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time spent on the ingestion activity.  'They 've been eating for hours !'

name: Material
definition_en: The entity which is used to make a Product.  'Add all the ingredients, toss and chill.'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Material belongs to.

name: Origin
definition_en: The location that the Material comes from, including both extraction sites and emission/production sources.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Material.

name: Use
definition_en: The purpose for which the Material is intended.  'Supply and placing of building materials shall be incidental to installation of the paving stones.'

name: Product
definition_en: The entity or substance that is created out of the Material.

name: Name
definition_en: An sequenced based naming system for individual members of a group.

name: Apparatus
definition_en: An entity that was not created by a living thing that is conceptualized to exist to fulfill some Goal.

name: Goal
definition_en: The ultimate aim of the Apparatus.

name: Domain
definition_en: The sphere of activity in which the Apparatus operates.

name: Type
definition_en: A description of the Goal.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent prevents the Theme from moving.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme has a tendency or desire to move, but is prevented from doing so.

name: Holding_location
definition_en: The location where the Agent keeps the Theme.

name: Cause
definition_en: A non-volitional cause that inhibits the motion of the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity which is confined.  'He confined 340 mutineers in Burford Church for the next three days under general sentence of death.'

name: Holding_location
definition_en: The area within which the Theme comes to be confined.  'He confined 340 mutineers in Burford Church for the next three days under general sentence of death.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person intentionally restricting the movement of the Theme.   'He confined 340 mutineers in Burford Church for the next three days under general sentence of death.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which the confinement is carried out.

name: Reciprocation
definition_en: The reason for the confinement.  'He was locked in his room for disobeying his mother.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose of the confinement.  'John was locked in his room so he could think about what he had done wrong.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.  'The Lilliputians tied him down by catching him unconscious and traversing his body with their thickest ropes.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Agent maintains the confinement of the Theme.

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is the non-sentient entity which is responsible for restricting the movement or location of the Theme.

name: Inspector
definition_en: The person who inspects the Ground to see if it is intact or without blemish.  'Smithers proof-read my paper on phlogiston production.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The entity that the Inspector inspects with his senses to ascertain whether it is intact.  ' `Mister Thomas' said Holmes, `have you examined the lock to determine whether or not it has been forced or otherwise tampered with?''

name: Unwanted_entity
definition_en: An entity whose presence would impair the acceptability or usefulness of the Ground.  'Security guards frisked all the spectators for weapons as they entered the stadium.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE is used for the Means by which the Inspector examines  the Ground.  'As in the second step the baby went to the toy and examined it by placing it in his mouth.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: Some of the words in this frame occur with a constituent that expresses the desired outcome of the inspection.  Normally this constituent is a PP Complement headed by for, or a to-marked VP Complement.  'Check all gutter brackets and clips to ensure no water will drip on to the walls.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Inspector scrutinizes the Ground.  'Leather is carefully inspected for softness, elasticity and texture'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the extent  to which the Inspector examines the Ground.  ' This section was partially inspected by the commissioner of Metro rail safety on Thursday'

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: This FE is the position of the Perceiver during the act of perception.  Typically, it is expressed in a from-PP. 'He moved toward the control panel and inspected it from a distance, without touching it.'

name: Desired_state_of_affairs
definition_en: The desirable state of affairs which the Inspector hopes to find to obtain when inspecting the Ground.  'Check that the light is out before you leave.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Inspector examines the Ground.  'Yesterday we inspected all the taps and water pipes at animal enclosures being utilized'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The circumstances under which the Inspector examines the Ground.  'Under pressure to find something, the team leader examined the site for signs of illicit activity.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity used by the Inspector to scrutinize the Ground.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person (or other force) that installs the Component.   'John installed it last night on my Gentoo system and everything is going fine so far.'

name: Component
definition_en: The Component is the object that is placed in a Fixed_location.   'My plumber installed the shower pan.'

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: This frame element specifies the location of the Agent (or of parts of their body) in cases where the Agent cannot manipulate the Component in straightforward fashion during the installation.  'The front was easy for me to install, I held the bar and bolt in place from below and installed the nut from the top around the control arm bushing.'

name: Fixed_location
definition_en: The Fixed_location is the location where the Component is placed and to which it is attached so as to be useful.   'I assembled the fuel tank using a vent line and a supply line, and then I installed the tank in the fuselage.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the installation event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree indicates the degree to which the installation is completed.  'Is the riser complete at the point the stab fittings are complete or when the fittings are complete and the riser is completely installed in the bracket with the bolts tightened?'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Component that is installed.   'We delivered and installed it unfinished because the customers wanted to finish it themselves.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is an act whereby the Agent achieves the installation of the Component.   'We installed the spindle assembly by starting with the lower-ball joint, followed by the upper.'

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The Duration_of_final_state is the amount of time for which the Component is to  remain part of the System.   'Per the suggestion of A. Briggs Geddis, Mr. McChord informed the Commission that a curtain drain could be installed and monitored for two months to try to lower the groundwater level in the proposed septic area.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place indicates where the installation occurs.  'When I installed the server there last winter they only had two rows of racks, mostly empty.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation indicates why the installation occurs.  'I installed a new HDD because it had numerous bad sectors.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period in which the Component is installed.   'When we installed our hood last month, the folks at Dallas Auto Body painted our roll pan at the same time.'

name: Area
definition_en: The Area is the setting into which multiple Components or a  complex Component is installed.    'I installed  tongue and groove pine flooring through my entire house.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: This is a second component that is installed alongside the primary Component or an individual performing the installation together with the Agent.  'The Hewlett Packard 5989A MS Engine was installed in 1991 together with the Hewlett Packard 5890 Series II Gas Chromatography (GC/MS).'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by perform the installation.   'North Johnston High School installed many technologies in order to dramatically improve the energy efficiency of our building.'

name: Instance
definition_en: A thing or episode of a certain Type.

name: Type
definition_en: The category of thing or event of which an Instance is picked out.'I collected two specimens of this rare species.'

name: Instance_prop
definition_en: A property of the Instance:'This is a clear example of the problem.'

name: Patient
definition_en: The person who is committed to a facility with a view towards helping them mentally or physically.    'Buffy's got this hospital phobia because her caring parents institutionalized her for a while before she moved to Sunnydale.'

name: Facility
definition_en: The facility where the Patient is taken for treatment.   'Unfortunately for Mrs. Lincoln, her son, Robert, institutionalized her in the Batavia Asylum shortly after the visit to St. Charles.'

name: Authority
definition_en: The Authority is the actor carrying out the institutionalization with proper legal authorization, either invested into them in general by the government or granted due to power of attorney over the Patient.  'Goodrum then went to see a private doctor who hospitalized him.'

name: Affliction
definition_en: The condition exhibited by the Patient, which is deemed to merit institutionalization by the Authority.   'Her parents institutionalized her for what was essentially typical bad adolescent behavior.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which the institutionalization happens.  'Later her mother became depressed and was institutionalized.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose of the institutionalization.  'His squabbling parents would rather institutionalize him to rid themselves of their problem.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Authority that brings about the institutionalization of the Patient.  'Without informing Volkobraun or her attorney of the court's decision, police forcibly committed her to a psychiatric hospital.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the institutionalization event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Authority that affect the action (ruthlessly).    'St Remy, of course, is most noted for being the place where Van Gogh committed himself voluntarily to an asylum.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the occurrence of the  institutionalization event logically follows.

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: This FE identifies the length of the time period for which the Authority has placed  the Patient in the Facility.  'This time, physicians hospitalized him for more than a month.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Facility is situated.  'The widow of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. suffered a stroke on Wednesday, and was hospitalized in Atlanta.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the institutionalization as being in some state during the action.   'A man was hospitalized in stable condition after he was mauled by a ?pet? bear.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE marks the amount of times the Patient is committed to the Facility per unit of time.

name: Institution
definition_en: A permanent organization with a socially important purpose.

name: Domain
definition_en: The concern of the Institution-- broadly speaking, the aspect of society that they affect.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The goal of the Institution.  'We're trying to figure out the quality indicators of an institution for addiction care.'

name: Members
definition_en: The individuals that make up an Institution.  'We are an institution of primarily academic personnel.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Institution is located.

name: Deceiver
definition_en: The person who acts so as to give the Victim an incorrect idea about a Topic. 'Politicians do nothing but deceive us about money.'

name: Victim
definition_en: The person who receives an incorrect idea because of the Deceiver's actions.  'Practicing deception upon them , ' 'Sometimes it may be the case that the press itself stands as a monolith practicing deception upon the people .'

name: Topic
definition_en: The entity to which the misleading idea relates, what it is about.  'You deceived me about the location of the diamonds.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by the Deceiver to fool the Victim.  'Chris misled me with her powers of persuasion.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the deception occurs.  'Some, looking for decent employment, said they were deceived soon after getting off the train.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the deception occurs.  'It's hard to fool someone in their own home.'

name: Self_mover
definition_en: This is a sentient being or a vehicle steered by a sentient being which moves.   'We drive down dusty roads, forded through a stream, and tried to get up a mountainside on a rocky road.'

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source.   'We forded from the island to the mainland.'

name: Path
definition_en: Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path, excluding directional expressions:    'We decided to cut through the forest. '

name: Goal
definition_en: Any expression which indicates where the Self_mover ends up as a result of the motion expresses the frame element Goal.   'I'll cut across the Sahara desert up to Algeria and Morocco.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of a Self_mover that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Immediately, the monk invited her to sit on his shoulders and he carefully forded the river, depositing her on the opposite bank.'

name: Distance
definition_en: Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.   'He followed the coast as far as Fronteras, then cut 160 miles across the Gulf of Mexico to the Yucatán Peninsula.'

name: Means
definition_en: An event involving the Self_mover that results in their moving in the specified way.  'The enemy had forded the river by piling up the bodies of their fallen comrades in the river bed.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the Self_mover moves.   'Motorists once again must quickly cut across three lanes of traffic to get from Exit 7 to Exit 8.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: This is a second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique, relative to which the Self_mover moves.   'They cut across the bushes after him and watched him Go into a small shrine-like building at the very center of the compound'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Self_mover.  'I actually forded the river in my ski boots.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.  'The common brook is best forded south of the hut.'

name: Path_shape
definition_en: The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Self_mover, taken simultaneously.

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction in which the Self_mover goes.  'We followed the trail (which is well marked with cairns) and then cut west across a grassy meadow for about 1000 feet to the crest of  the nearby saddle lying below North Peak.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the motion takes place.    'The Federal Army of the Potomac forded the river in August 1862.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Self_mover wishes to bring about.   'I cut through the alley in order to escape my pursuers.'

name: Means_of_motion
definition_en: The device or bodypart that serves to move the Self_mover.  'The General was received by Colonel Thayer, and ascended the hill in a landau, escorted by the officers of the post.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Self_mover spends in motion.   'We forded Cooper Cr. for several hours then built a fire to dry out gear.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Self_mover.  'Streams were forded because there were no bridges over meandering Back Creek.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time the Intentional_traversing occurs and which the Intentional_traversing is taken to be a part of.  'He had comfortably forded it on his trip to Beatrice'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.  'Early in the morning, Chapman had twice forded the river a short distance north of the footbridge.'

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: A larger conceptualization that includes the Intentional_traversing as an integral part. The Intentional_traversing expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.   'The 133rd Infantry hurriedly forded the river in an attempt to capture a bridge intact.'

name: New_situation
definition_en: An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Self_mover), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the Intentional_traversing.  'I cut across Arnold's new backyard only to find literally hundreds of squirrels everywhere.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Traversing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.  'These waterways can be forded by infantry at low water, but at other times a six-foot tide makes them difficult to cross.'

name: Endpoints
definition_en: The Source and Goal of either a single or a repeated motion taken together as Endpoints of the Path.   'It is located at the place where explorers Marquette and Jolliet forded between the Chicago and Des Plaines Rivers.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the same event as the primary protagonist, regardless of whether the protagonist, and hence the Co-participant, is more agent- or more undergoer-like.  'John forded the river with his cousin.'

name: Act
definition_en: This FE identifies the Act that the Agent performs intentionally.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent performs the intentional act.  'We have not yet acted .'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the intentional act occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent performs an intentional act. John flattered her to receive a raise.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent acts intentionally.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  ''Twould be best it were done quietly.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain within which the Agent acts.  'No doubt he has begun to engage in political activity of late'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency with which the Agent does the Act in a given period of time.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of an act.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE gives a description of the Intentionally_act event.

name: Apparent_conclusion
definition_en: This FE describes an additional situation or modification that would seem to hold given the rest of the situation. In some cases, it marks a completely separate conclusion than one would draw from the manner of the event in the main clause.  As far as we know, this idea is only explicitly marked in English with "as if".  'We have to do our duty as if it matters .'  Usually, the Apparent_conclusion contains another FE, either peripheral or extra-thematic, which is non-factive (i.e., it may, but does not necessarily, hold). For these cases, we annotate the other frame-element on the second layer; thus the following should be annotated with Purpose on the second layer.   'As if to guarantee failure , they conducted the study without consulting experts .' 'As if to guarantee failure , they conducted the study without consulting experts .'  We do not annotate this FE in cases where we merely infer that a part of the sentence is meant sarcastically, as in the following minimal modification of the above sentence:  'To guarantee failure , they conducted the study without consulting experts .'  In this case, we simply annotate the Purpose FE.

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

name: Event
definition_en: This FE identifies the act that the Agent performs intentionally.

name: Agent
definition_en: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs the intentional act that affects the Patient.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with an Patient to accomplish the action indicated by the target.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Agent performs the intentional act.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent intentionally affects a Patient.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent intentionally affects the Patient.

name: Patient
definition_en: Patient is the entity acted on and that may, but need not, undergo a change.  'A professional dishwasher does dishes one at a time.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Patient is affected by the Event.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE describes the event.

name: Creator
definition_en: The Creator creates a created entity.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place ehere the Agent intentionally creates the new entity.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifes the Time when an Agent intentionally creates a new entity.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent intentionally creates a new entity.

name: Components
definition_en: This FE identifies the Components that are attached together to form a Created_entity. 'He made a jungle gym out of iron bars.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action.

name: Created_entity
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity that the Agent intentionally creates. 'They were generating grenades for export.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the creation event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Creator that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a Creator intentionally creates a new entity.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the instrument with which an Agent intentionally creates a Created_entitiy.

name: Role
definition_en: The role of Created_entity.  'This particular book was created as an introductory text.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: A secondary agent with whom the Creator intentionally creates the Created_entity.  'Emily set up the business with the former president of Intersoft, Inc.'

name: Interceptor
definition_en: The volitional agent who without authorization of sender or recipient takes control of a Theme that is en route to a destination.  ' Two days later, an aerial patrol intercepted an enemy trying the same thing.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity, physical or abstract, construed as traveling from a sender to a goal location, which is taken hold of by the Interceptor without permission.  'They could either sail west down the Channel or north-east to intercept an enemy making for the Thames estuary.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Interceptor takes control of the Theme.  'She had been intercepted outside Guy 's room and would be severely punished.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Interceptor takes control of the Theme.  'The five had been intercepted after a DFLP attack on March 5.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the intercepting event as being in some state during the action.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Intercepting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously),  and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate also salient characteristics of the Interceptor that also affect the action (carefully).  'With the help of John Poindexter, I've carefully intercepted communications from cycling's best and brightest.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The circumstances under which the interception takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state of affairs that the Interceptor hopes to bring about by intercepting.

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by the Interceptor that results in success.

name: Figure
definition_en: The Figure is the entity located with respect to the Ground.  'Ben is in the hallway.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground is the area that the Figure is located in.

name: Time
definition_en: The time during which the Figure was located in the Ground.

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure.  'The book is  way back in the Paleontology area.'

name: Accessibility
definition_en: This  FE identifies the Accessibility between the Figure and some reference location (generally, the deictic center or the Ground). 'The cat is just in there.'

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: The area or zone interior to the Ground.  This FE excludes Figure and is only used in particular constructions such as the following:  'Inside the cupboard was a good place to hide .' 'We looked between the trees .' 'I found the ring in there , in among the old moldy rugs .'

name: Directness
definition_en: An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target.  This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, directly, and due (and some combinations of these), but also occurs with rarer items like 'smack dab'.  'I was standing right inside the entrance of the church.'

name: Temporal_profile
definition_en: A description of how the access path to the Ground interacts with time.  This FE is filled only by the closed class of adverbials back.adv (which indicates that the position was occupied by the Figure before) and on.adv (which indicates a continued path).  While this FE in its most basic use refers to cases of actual motion, it can be used with descriptions of static position, in which case it either refers to fictive, imagined motion (as in the first example below), or it backgrounds motion entirely (as in the second example).  'You 'll find it straight on over inside the closet.' 'He's already back in the house.'

name: Deixis
definition_en: An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder), or specifically separated from the speech context by distance or a barrier (over).  Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.  'It is lying here among the flowers.'

name: Region_quantification
definition_en: A description of how much of a potential profiled region actually has (or is expected to have) a Figure in it.  It is normally filled by closed-class items like 'all', 'somewhere', 'nowhere', etc.  'I think he's somewhere within the building.'

name: Cause
definition_en: A force, process, or event that produces the interruption.  'Leaving the page after you've clicked "Download" will interrupt the transfer.'

name: Process
definition_en: The Process goes into a paused state due to the Cause or Actor.  'Leaving the page after you've clicked "Download" will interrupt the transfer.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the interruption takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the interruption occurs.

name: Actor
definition_en: An entity which participates in a Cause, perhaps volitionally and perhaps not, but effectively causing the interruption.  'In such cases the server will automatically interrupt the process.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any holistic description of the event, including overall depictions (the same way) and descriptions pertaining to the Actor or Cause's influence on the character of the event.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Means
definition_en: An action or sub-event through which the Actor or Cause interrupts the Process.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the interruption occurs.

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Intoxicant
definition_en: The Intoxicant is ingested. ' We smoke  <fex name = "Intoxicant">marijuana every day.'

name: Type
definition_en: Type identifies the kind or sort of Intoxicant. 'They smoked freebase cocaine.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Descriptor describes a quality of the Intoxicant. ' We smoked some fine <fex name = "Intoxicant">marijuana.'

name: Country_of_origin
definition_en: Country_of_origin identifies where the Intoxicant is grown or originates.   ' The British enjoy Afghanistan's opium.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The mental state of the Cognizer is changed by an Intoxicant .

name: Intoxicant
definition_en: The Intoxicant alters the Cognizer's mental experience.

name: Degree
definition_en: This Fe identifies the Degree to which the Cognizer is altered by the Intoxicant.

name: Evaluation
definition_en: Evaluation indicates the Cognizer's reaction to the intoxicatoin. ' Jim had a bad trip. '

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the intoxication holds. ' Bill has been sober for 7 months.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer is intoxicated.  ' Michael was <fex name = "Manner">aggressively drunk.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Cognizer becomes intoxicated.

name: Land
definition_en: The political area that is being crippled by the Invader's entry.  'Henry II had made no attempt to invade France.'

name: Weapon
definition_en: An entity used by the Invader to assist in the invasion of the Land.

name: Invader
definition_en: The army or other self-directed entity that is entering the Land in a hostile manner.  'Indeed , three months later Hitler invaded Austria.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).
