It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Invader that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Invader that accomplishes the assault.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the location where the Invader invades the Land.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Invader attacks the Land.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Invader is responding to that leads them to make an assault on the Land.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Invader invades Land.

name: Source
definition_en: The starting-point of the motion of the Invader or projectiles of the Invader as they move toward the the Place that the Land is occupying in the attack.  In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Invader or Land while the Invasion occurs.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re-encoding, but not necessarily.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the invasion on the Land by the Invader.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held. Form: once, twice, Cardinal expression + /it times, /it lots/a lot

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole and describes and describes the event more generally.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Invader travels.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Invader invades the Land.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates the subtype of invasion into the Land.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes how intense the invation of the Land is.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Duration
definition_en: For how long the Land is invaded by the Invader.

name: Invader
definition_en: The  Invader is the entity that overtakes the Attacked.

name: Attacked
definition_en: The Attacked is the land, government, and its people that is seized by the Invader.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes the intensity and extent of the invasion event.

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner in which the Invader takes over the Attacked.

name: Means
definition_en: The action by which the conquering event is made possible through the efforts of the Invader.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Invader takes over the Attacked.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Invader seizes the Attacked.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason why the Invader seized the Attacked.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The tool used by the Invader to seize the Attacked.

name: Origin
definition_en: The Origin is the place where the Combatant was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

name: Combatant
definition_en: The Combatant is the human being involved in combat.

name: Persistent_characteristic
definition_en: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Combatant which is concieved of as persisting over time.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Combatant.

name: Age
definition_en: The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.

name: Ethnicity
definition_en: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Combatant belongs.

name: Context_of_acquaintance
definition_en: An expression indicating the context with which the Combatant is associated.

name: Side_1
definition_en: The side of the conflict for which the Combatant fights.

name: Side_2
definition_en: A (or the) side of the conflict to which the Combatant is opposed.

name: Conflict
definition_en: The Conflict in which the Combatants are fighting.  'Some call him a holy war fighter and martyr.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The desired result of the outcome of the hostile encounter for Side_1. It may either directly refer to the state of affairs that is desired, or the state of affairs may be implicit in an (abstract or concrete) entity that they desire.  'We are not just soldiers - we are fighters for a cause.'

name: Group
definition_en: The larger military group of which the Combatant is a part.  'A number of militia fighters were arrested during the raid.'

name: Place
definition_en: The town or area that is in a remote location.  'He lives in the backwoods of Canada.'

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place with respect to which the Place is located.  'I live in Bumblefuck, Kansas.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer makes the judgment. This role is typically expressed as the External Argument (or in a by-PP in passives). 'The boss appreciates you for your diligence.' 'The boss is very appreciative of my work.'

name: Evaluee
definition_en: Evaluee is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment is made. With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object:  'The boss appreciates you for your diligence. '

name: Reason
definition_en: Typically, there is a constituent expressing the Reason for the Judge's judgment. It is usually a for-PP, e.g. 'I admire you for your intellect.'

name: Role
definition_en: Role is used for the capacity in which the Evaluee is judged, and is expressed in as-PPs. 'I admire you as a composer.'</def-root >

name: Expressor
definition_en: Expressor is the body part or action by a body part that conveys the judgment made by the Cognizer.  'She viewed him with an appreciative gaze.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the judging occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies any expression describing the state of a participant in the event. 'We admire him , certain that he is a great leader.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner of judging.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Cognizer judges the Evaluee.

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic identifies the entity to which the proposition or propositions conveyed relate.  'Jon was disapproving  about Madie's managerial style.'

name: Extent_of_acclaim
definition_en: The Extent_of_acclaim is a description of the number or locales of the Cognizers. 'The proposal gainedwidespread approbation.'

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the judgement event.

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee hears the judgement from the Communicator.   ' Jon belittled Madie to her colleagues.'

name: Communicator
definition_en: The Communicator uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey his or her evaluation of the Evaluee to another person.  'Jon belittled Madie to her colleagues.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium identifies the physical or abstract setting in which the evaluation is conveyed.   'Jon belittled Madie over the telephone.' 'The party denounced the General in vehement terms.' 'Mayor Quimby criticized the townspeople in his annual speech.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic identifies the entity to which the proposition or propositions conveyed relate.  'Jon criticized Madie about her managerial style.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Communicator judges the Evaluee to be good or bad.

name: Evaluee
definition_en: A judgment is made about the Evaluee  With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object:  'Jon belittled Madie to her colleagues.'

name: Expressor
definition_en: Expressor is the body part or action by a body part that conveys the judgment made by the Communicator.  'She viewed him with a critical gaze.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the judgmental communication occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a judgmental communication is accomplished.

name: Reason
definition_en: Typically, there is a constituent expressing the Reason for the Communicator's judgment. It is usually a for-PP.  'Jon extolled Madie for her efforts.' It can also sometimes be expressed as an as-phrase, when that phrase picks out the reason for the praise or critique. 'The book was ridiculed as an example of all the worst of post-modernism.' For some words, Reason is an obligatory FE. In other words, the FE may be ommitted only when the Reason for the judgment is understood from context, as when it is clear why an Evaluee is being blamed. 'I blame you.DNI '

name: Role
definition_en: Role is used for the capacity in which the Evaluee is judged, and is expressed in as-PPs. ' Jon belittled Madie as a nurse.' </def-root >

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies any expression describing the state of a participant in the event.

name: Grounds
definition_en: The Grounds is the standard by which the Evaluee is judged. 'The proposal was critiqued on this basis.'

name: Extent_of_acclaim
definition_en: The Extent_of_acclaim provides a description of the number or whereabouts of the Communicator.  'The movie met with international acclaim.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the communication of the judgment takes place. 'He received critical acclaim last week.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the communication of the judgment takes place. 'He was belittled by his long-time friend in front of his family.'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotional or physical state of the Communicator that leads to their communication of a judgment. 'He criticized his compatriots out of a deep hatred for all who are better than him.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE describes the frequency with which the specified communication occurs

name: Communicator
definition_en: The Communicator communicates a judgment to the Addressee.

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is jduged by the Communicator and receives the message of approval or disapproval.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject on which the Addressee is being judged. 'The teacher scolded the children about their meessy cookie eating.'

name: Reason
definition_en: The Reason is why the Communicator forms the type of judgment they form. 'The principal rebuked the student for cheating on the exam.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The Medium identifies the physical or abstract entity in which the judgment is conveyed.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree is the severity of the judgment.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator or Addressee.

name: Grounds
definition_en: The Grounds describes the basis for the judgment.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the way in which the judgment is communicated.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is the method employed to communicate the judgment.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Communicator admonishes the Addressee.  'We were scolded in the kitchen by the biggest cook you've ever seen.'

name: Time
definition_en: The point in time at which the Communicator berates or compliments the Addressee.  'She complimented me almost every morning on my smart starched shirts.'

name: Role
definition_en: The laudable or reprimandable status held by the Addressee.  'He rebuked them as heathens and blasphemers.'

name: Expressor
definition_en: An action or entity under the control of the Communicator that expresses the criticism or praise directed towards the Addressee.  'Though she had killed him so long ago, she could still see his jeering smile.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which a particular gradable Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the intensity of the Attribute from the norm or from the value for another Entity. This FE is incorporated for each LU in this frame.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having  a particular Value for the Attribute.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Value for the Attribute.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity is has the Attribute to a given Degree.

name: Judicial_body
definition_en: A permanent organization with the socially important purpose of administering justice.  'The International Monetary Fund Administrative Tribunal (IMFAT) adjudicates employment disputes between staff members and the IMF.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The concern of the Judicial_body-- broadly speaking, the aspect of society that they affect.  'Anything you say or write can and will be held against you in a court of law.'

name: Task
definition_en: The responsibility that a Judicial_body has, either defined in terms of the type of cases that they can hear, or more specifically by reference to an action that the authority constituting them wishes the Judicial_body  to achieve.  'The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda sentenced Mikaeli Muhimana on April 28 to life imprisonment.'

name: Rank
definition_en: The degree of authority invested in a Judicial_body relative to other courts in the same system.  'The High Court of Calcutta had all Bengal jurisdiction even after the partition of Bengal in 1905.'

name: Seat
definition_en: The location (typically a city) in which the Judicial_body hears cases.,  'Ante Gotovina, was charged with war crimes by the International Criminal Tribunal in Den Hague and is currently hiding from the authorities.'

name: Jurisdiction
definition_en: The geographical area within which the Judicial_body has authority and responsibility.  'On February 18, 1983, the Supreme Court of Alabama denied this motion.'

name: Source_of_authority
definition_en: The political entity under whose laws the Judicial_body is constituted and whose laws are applied.  'A jury in the US District Court of Central California told Microsoft to pay a large award to Carlos Armando Amado.'

name: Judges
definition_en: The individuals that make up the Judicial_body.  'I will not be heard before a court of 50-year-old white men!'

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Judicial_body is located.

name: Jury
definition_en: The group that debates the case.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the deliberation is ongoing.

name: Charges
definition_en: The legal label for the crime that the defendant is accused of.

name: Case
definition_en: The Case which a trial is convened to decide.

name: Time
definition_en: When the deliberation takes place. 'The jury deliberated for three hours last Tuesday..'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the deliberation takes place. 'The jury deliberated for several hours in the Oakland courthouse.'

name: Possible_sentence
definition_en: A sentence that the jury considers during deliberation. 'The jury deliberated his guilt.'

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs.  It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.

name: Stimulus
definition_en: The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.

name: Empathy_target
definition_en: The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The body part, gesture, or other expression of the Experiencer that reflects his or her emotional state.  They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response.  In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus.  Quite often in such cases, the Stimulus can be inferred from the Circumstances

name: State
definition_en: The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Experiencer, Expressor, or State can be described as having said emotion.

name: Type
definition_en: Type describes the kind of response the Stimulus or Topic invoke in the Experiencer.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used to transmit the experience invoked by the Stimulus.

name: Agent
definition_en: The person or organization that  is held responsible for a prior Act or for a State_of_affairs.  'Smithers  defended his decision by insisting that he had used his best judgment'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The set of facts or circumstances that the Agent offers in explanation of their earlier Act or of the State_of_affairs  'Mr De Klerk justified his decision on the curious grounds that an inquiry would take too long'

name: Act
definition_en: An action  for which the Agent is held responsible, frequently one that the Agent has taken themself.  'Kim failed  to fully justify his decision.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: A State_of_affairs that the Agent is held responsible for.  ' The lawyers tried  to justify enormous punitive damages being paid to victims on a first-past-the-post system .'

name: Judge
definition_en: The person or institution that holds the Agent responsible for an Act or State_of_affairs.  ' Any decision that preparation and presentation should be separate would have to be justified to the public and be open in the last resort to judicial review'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action, typically an act of speaking, which the Agent performs in order to justify an Act or State_of_affairs.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE denotes the number of times the Act or State_of_affairs are justified.

name: Domain
definition_en: The general spectrum of reasoning that the Agent uses to explain the Act or State_of_affairs.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time of the justifying event.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the justification was adequate.  'He barely justified his actions.'

name: Key
definition_en: This FE identifies the object that is designed to grant access to a location or function. This is the target LU, and this frame element is incorporated into each of this frame's LUs.

name: Function
definition_en: The function that the Key grants access to.  'Hand me the key that opens the garage.'  'This password allows access to the website.'

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Key into existence.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which an Key comes into existence.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to an Key.

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Key, often denoting the kind of device that the key operates on.  'Is that a skeleton key?'

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Key, including components, ingredients, etc.

name: Location
definition_en: The location that the Key grants access to.  'These are the keys to the house.'  'I lost my office keycard.'

name: Object
definition_en: The artifact that the key operates on.  'My car keys are locked inside.'

name: Perpetrator
definition_en: The Perpetrator is the person (or other agent) who carries off and holds the Victim against his or her will.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is the person who is carried off and held against his/her will.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the kidnapping takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the kidnapping occurs.

name: Source
definition_en: Source is the initial location of the Victim before it changes location.

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is the place in which the Victim ends up.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner in which the kidnapping takes place.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Perpetrator that helps them accomplish the kidnapping.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose is what the Perpetrator hopes to accomplish by kidnapping.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation expresses why the Perpetrator commits the kidnapping.

name: Event
definition_en: The abduction of a Victim by a Perpetrator.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: An additional abductee taken along with the Victim. 'She was abducted with her brother.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time for which the Victim is held by the Perpetrator  'Two young man abducted her for about two hours'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that the Victim is kidnapped.  ' The prelate was kidnapped twice in the last two years'

name: Killer
definition_en: The person or sentient entity that causes the death of the Victim.</def-root >

name: Victim
definition_en: The living entity that dies as a result of the killing.

name: Cause
definition_en: An inanimate entity or process that causes the death of the Victim.  'The rockslide killed nearly half of the climbers.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state of affairs that the Killer is trying to bring about by killing.  'It's simple:  he killed her to get the inheritance.'

name: Means
definition_en: The method or action that the Killer or Cause performs resulting in the death of the Victim.  'The flood exterminated the rats by cutting off access to food.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The preexisting state of affairs that the Killer is responding to.  'She drowned him for lying.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the death took place.  'Apparently there were two murders in Atherton in one week.'

name: Time
definition_en: The point or period of time within which the Victim is killed.  'There is no evidence that the royal family was killed during the destruction at this site.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Killer or Victim during the killing.

name: Result
definition_en: The state of the Victim that results from being killed.  (Normally this is somewhat redundant.)  'Two men ... smothered her to death.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The device used by the Killer to bring about the death of the Victim. 'It's difficult to suicide with only a pocketknife.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of a Killer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully). 'Kill them quietly.' 'A true professional , he beheaded his victims with unhurried expertise, a credit to his calling.' 'A gunman slaughtered six people in cold blood because he had been evicted.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree appears with adjectives to describe the killing potential of an object or with nouns to describe how widespread the killing is. 'The Nazis engaged in mass genocide.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: This extra-thematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Alter
definition_en: The person who fills the role named by the Kinship term with respect to the Ego.'John is my cousin.''I met his brother last year.'

name: Ego
definition_en: The person from whose perspective the Kinship relationship is defined.'Bill is Sue's son.'

name: Relatives
definition_en: The combination of Alter and Ego together.'John and I are brothers.'

name: Degree
definition_en: An expression of the closeness or distance of the relation.  We do not go into full anthropological detail in measuring the distance of the relation, but simply annotate all such expressions as Degree

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describe some characteristic of the Alter or the Ego.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which a Knot is produced..

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. John flattered her to receive a raise.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Agent by which the creation of the Knot is accomplished.

name: Knot
definition_en: The stable configuration of a String which results from tying.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action. We wandered around naked. Cicadas screech unseen from within.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the sentient being who manipulates the Rope.  'Melissa braided Jessica's hair.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which the Rope is manipulated.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the manipulation of the Rope takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.   'Prof. Frink braided my hair to make me look beautiful.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the manipulation of the Rope takes place.  'Terri tied the rope around her waist before scrambling up the side of the mountain.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.  'Kelly tied her laces around the back of her heel to combat loose shoes.'

name: Rope
definition_en: The basically linear object which is manipulated by the Agent to produce a Knot.  'He tied an electrical cable around the trunk and his neck before hanging himself .'

name: Knot
definition_en: The stable configuration of a Rope which results from tying.  'Jake tied the cravat into an acceptable knot.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner in which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.  'John knotted the tie tightly around his neck.'

name: Locus
definition_en: Where the manipulation of the Rope takes place.  'Kelly tied her laces around the back of her heel to combat loose shoes.'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the person who conventionally uses a linguistic sign to refer to an Entity.  'They call it a Mutt Mitt.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The concrete or abstract thing with which the Speaker has associated a particular linguistic sign.  'He termed it "a pretty incredible discovery" on par with two other 10,000- to 11,000-year-old specimens'

name: Label
definition_en: The linguistic sign that the Speaker uses to designate the Entity.   'In Texas, we call it walking".' 'Americans call it a faucet. What do the British call it ?'

name: Time
definition_en: A time period in which a Speaker uses the Label.  'Back in the olden days, they called it "Bohemian people."'

name: Place
definition_en: A physical space whose occupants use the Label to refer to the Entity.   'I really loved this movie. In France, they called it "Turbo Interceptor".'

name: Medium
definition_en: A text whose author applies a particular Label to an Entity.  'Your article labels him "Republican Senator Jim Exon".'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: Duration_of_final_state denotes the length of time from the beginning of a state resulting from the activity denoted by the target until the state no longer holds.

name: Agent
definition_en: A sentient entity whose physical and mental faculties are directly expended on the Input to create the Output.

name: Cause
definition_en: A non-sentient entity whose physical faculties are directly expended on the Input to create the Output.

name: Input
definition_en: The mental or physical faculties onto which the Agent or Cause expends energy.

name: Output
definition_en: The end product, either a concept or physical object onto which the Agent or Cause has exerted its mental or physical faculties from the rudimentary state of Input.

name: Depictive
definition_en: A word or phrase that characterizes the target.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Output was committed into reality.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Output was birthed.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The entity for whom the Output is created.

name: Presentation
definition_en: The place where the target or Output is presented.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A Descriptor is a chracterization or description of the Output that is not covered by any more-specific FE.

name: Process
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the process that the Agent initiates.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Process is initiated.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is the way in which the Agent initiates the Process.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE is for the Time when the Agent initiates the Process.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical or abstract setting in which the Agent initiates the Process.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the actor responsible for starting the Process.

name: Purpose
definition_en: To what end the Agent initiates the Process.

name: Co-timed_event
definition_en: This FE identifies the first Co-timed_event of the started Process.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Agent initiates the Process.

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason why or the way in which the Agent initiates the Process.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world at the time when the Agent produces the Process.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: New_situation
definition_en: A consecutive event to the starting of the Process of the Agent.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies the  Depictive phrase describing the actor or undergoer of an action.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The party for who's benefit the Process is launched.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re-encoding, but not necessarily

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Process is launched.

name: Law
definition_en: This FE identifies the rule designed to guide activity, deprecating some types of activity and/or requiring other types of activity. This FE is incorporated into each LU in this frame.

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which a law is intended.  'We brought back a law to forbid the use of profanity.'

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Law into existence.  'But this was forbidden by the King's Law of 1665.'

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which a Law comes into existence.  'The 1996 welfare reform act was a sham.'

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to a Law.  'Well, they're still in violation of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.'

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Law.  'According to Canon Law, priests may not marry.'

name: Part
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Law.  'We don't need another law with 300 subsections.'

name: Forbidden
definition_en: The state-of-affairs which is disallowed by the Law.  'I think we need a law against all firearms within city limits.'

name: Required
definition_en: A state-of-affairs which the Law declares must be maintained.  'The law that all minors must be accompanied by an adult is a laughingstock.'

name: Jurisdiction
definition_en: The location where a given Law is in force.  'According to Fijian law, no-one may enter the park after sunset.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description of the Law not covered by a more specific frame element.

name: Agency
definition_en: The Agency is a part of the government dedicated to enforcing the laws of the government's jurisdiction.

name: Members
definition_en: A person belonging to the Agency.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason for which the Agency is formed or the purpose to which it is dedicated. This FE is for expressions that indicate more specific purposes than the general one(s) indicated by the target itself.

name: Period_of_existence
definition_en: The interval during which the Agency exists.

name: Name
definition_en: A name given to the Agency for identification.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE describes the general location where the Agency operates, but does not indicate the jurisdiction of the Agency.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description of the Agency not covered by a more specific frame element.

name: Jurisdiction
definition_en: The Agency is charged with enforcing the laws of and within a particular Jurisdiction.

name: Leader
definition_en: The Leader is the one who has the role of leading.  With verbs, and with predicate nominals linking an individual to a Role, the Leader is usually the External Argument:  'King Hussein ruled Jordan.'  'Hussein was King of Jordan.'  With leadership nouns, the frame element Leader is most frequently instantiated by the target itself. 'The queen announced her upcoming visit to Belgium.'

name: Role
definition_en: The role played by the Leader in a given situation, often an official title; incorporated in most noun LUsin this frame. When expressed separately from the target, Role usually occurs in a PP Complement headed by as.  'Hussein reigned as King of Jordan'

name: Duration
definition_en: Leadership by any particular individual is frequently limited in time, which is noted here as Duration.   Duration usually occurs in a PP Complement. 'She reigned for 3 years.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive refers to that which describes one of the participants in the leadership relationship.  'He led them for a thousand years, strong, bold, and deathless.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner refers to the style/way in which the leadership is asserted.  'Alternative and orthodox practitioners reign harmoniously side by side.'

name: Means
definition_en: Means identifies act(s) performed by the Leader through which leadership is maintained. 'He ruled by sheer brutality and intimidation.' 'Napolean reigned by the grace of God and the will of the people.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which leadership is asserted.

name: Time
definition_en: Time refers to the point in time that the leadership took place.  'The general led his troops into battle on June 22, 1883.'

name: Governed
definition_en: The entity whose actions or beliefs the Leader directs in the context of a joint activity or movement.  This entity can be a political body, a person, or a group of people.  'Cyprus Turks turn against their leader' 'Naoto Kan is the new leader of the Democratic Party of Japan.' 'King Hussein ruled Jordan.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Leader.  'A nervous governor stepped up to the lectern to give his speech.'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Leader belongs to.

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant Domain within which the Leader rules.  This includes a specification of a country that the Leader serves (Iranian officials) or any other organizations that the Leader acts as part of (congressional representative; several directors from UNHCR).

name: Activity
definition_en: The Leader directs the Activity.  'The captain's cousin led the mutiny.' 'John Cage is one of the leaders of the minimalist music movement.'

name: Place
definition_en: The locale from which the Leader leads the Governed or the Activity.  'He ruled the west from his palace in Milan.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: The thing that indicates an Entity was in a Location.  He found traces of the burglar in the hallway.

name: Entity
definition_en: The thing whose former existence in a Location can be deduced from the Evidence.  Traces of the former inhabitants can still be found in the abandoned manor.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This frame element describes characteristics and properties of the Evidence not covered by other frame elements.

name: Location
definition_en: The place or context in which the <fex name="">Evidence of an is discovered, showing that an <fex name="">Event occured there or an <fex name="">Entity existed there.

name: Event
definition_en: An event whose details are revealed through the discovery of Evidence.

name: Time
definition_en: A description of the time that an Event occurs or an Entity exists at a place.

name: Reliability
definition_en: Any description of how clearly the Evidence indicates the former Event.

name: Process
definition_en: The activity that is being applied to the mass or the set of entities.   'An additional eighty-three invitations remain to be sent'

name: Remainder
definition_en: The mass or group that has not yet been processed.  'In this case everyone should be informed by word of mouth to contact the person holding the list to find out which gifts still remain to be bought.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Remainder is assessed.  'Now only three more items remain to be sold'

name: Agent
definition_en: The individuals who are scheduled to apply the Process to the Remainder.  The Agent may be the same or a different individual who applied the process to the part that has already undergone the Process.  'To insure my appointment, much will remain for you to do'

name: Authority
definition_en: The Authority (which may be the jury, judge, magistrate or court) decides on the Finding.  'The US International Trade Commission ruled that a 1987 anti-dumping tariff against frozen concentrated orange juice from Brazil could be revoked DNI.'

name: Finding
definition_en: This FE identifies the outcome of the Authority's deliberation or consideration.  'Miss Mahmod's father ruled that she would never marry him.'

name: Case
definition_en: This FE describes the question on which the Authority gives a Finding.  'US Supreme Court ruled on flag salutes in public schools today.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the Authority gives his Finding.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the Finding takes place.

name: Legal_basis
definition_en: This FE indicates the basis in law of a Finding.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the ruling was reached.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Authority acts.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose why the Authority returns a particular Finding.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies an action that the Authority performs in order to return the verdict.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for the Finding.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re-encoding, but not necessarily

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the ruling event operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that a Finding holds.

name: Defendant
definition_en: The person about whom the Authority passes a judgment or Finding.  'They held judgment upon me as a convicted traitress.'

name: Action
definition_en: The Action is the behavior which complies with or violates the Code.' Illegal drug use is on the rise. '

name: Code
definition_en: The Code is the set of rules, laws or regulations that determine whether the Action is allowed or prohibited.

name: Object
definition_en: The Object complies with or violates the Code by virtue of its existence, location or possession.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Borrower
definition_en: The person or institution who receives the Theme from the Lender for a Duration. 'I lent the book to him for a whole month, and he still hasn't read it.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amout of time in which the Borrower has possession of the Theme.  'I lent the book to him for a whole month, and he still hasn't read it.'

name: Lender
definition_en: The person or institution who gives the Theme to the Borrower for a Duration.  'I lent the book to him for a whole month, and he still hasn't read it.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The object that is transferred from the Lender to the Borrower for a Duration. 'I lent the book to him for a whole month, and he still hasn't read it.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The aim of the Lender which they believe will be accomplished by lending the Theme to the Borrower.  'His parents lent him money to pay off his student loans.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the lending event occurs.  'I lent him my car on Friday.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Lender lends the Theme.  'Juan lent me the car reluctantly.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Lender lends the Theme to the Borrower.  'I lent him my book in Dubai.'

name: Exerter
definition_en: The Exerter that can or does exert a force of the level specified by the target.   'Salesmen touted the power of the engine's motor.'

name: Force
definition_en: The Force that can or does exert a force of the level specified by the target.   'No one should underestimate the mighty strength of the dung beetle.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Exerter, Action, or Force can or does exert its force.   'My quads feel particularly weak after 100 squats.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the Exerter, Action, or Force can or does exert a force.   'The winds were strongest during the hurricane.'

name: Action
definition_en: The Action that can or does exert a force of the level specified by the target.   'She gave him a playful, weak punch in the arm.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Exerter, Action, or Force can or does exert a force.   'After being in space for six months, his muscles were extremely weak.'  Where Degree is expressed by a comparative or superlative form of the target, the FE is marked on the target (as well as on the rest of the comparative/superlative expression, if present): 'Years of lifting had made him a stronger man.' 'Years of lifting had made him stronger than any of his peers.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Exerter, Action, or Force can or does exert its force.  'Muhammad Ali's force in the ring was indisputable.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describes the force exertion of the Exerter, Action, or Force.  'Henry's longstanding powerlessness against the school bully made him fearful and withdrawn.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain is the field in which the Exerter, Action, or Force can or does exert its force.   'The U.S. possesses great military strength.'

name: Resisting_entity
definition_en: The Resisting_entity is the item that resists the Opposing_force to the level specified by the target.   'These are made from a tough plastic foam and are very light to wear.'  'A great number of hardy plants usually succeed in blooming even in the severest season.'   'The fragile canoe did not capsize!'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Resisting_entity resists.  'Their colonial structures turned out to be very durable.'  Where Degree is expressed by a comparative or superlative form of the target, the FE is marked on the target (as well as on the rest of the comparative/superlative expression, if present): 'On the whole, triticale is hardier than wheat.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Resisting_entity resists an external force.  'They decided the tree-house would be sturdiest in the big old backyard oak.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Resisting_entity resists an external force.   'The retaining wall was even weaker yesterday, and had begun to crumble.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the Resisting_entity resists an external force.   'Wexford thought the yellow chair felt flimsy as he lowered his heavy body into it.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describes the force resistance of the Resisting_entity.   'Scottish ancestors had given her an amazing toughness which enabled her to endure the hardships of life.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain is the field in which the Resisting_entity resists an external force.   'Factors that determine the choice of materials include physical robustness.'

name: Opposing_force
definition_en: The Opposing_force is the item placed in opposition to the Resisting_entity. Opposing_force hinders, blocks, helps, or allows (lets) the Resisting_entity to resist at the level specified by the target. Sometimes this Core FE is incorporated in the target; otherwise, it is often null instantiated in example sentences.   'The fortress was impregnable to attack by hostile invaders.'   'Its best-known feature is its soft and pliable duck-like beak. INI '

name: Location
definition_en: The place whose amout of light is being described.  The Location can also be a location in time, as seen in the second example below:  'She hid from the man in a dark corner.'  'We set off on our journey on a dark night.'

name: Source
definition_en: The entity from which the light eminates.  'A dim lamp swung over the entrance to the castle.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree of the amount of light.  'The room was totally dark.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the level of light not covered by a more specific frame element.  'The hall was unusually dark when she stepped out of the apartment.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the light movement occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the external argument. 'Their swords glowed red in the setting sun.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Emitter
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity at the Source from which the Beam originates.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location the Beam occupies initially before its change of location.

name: Beam
definition_en: The light that travels from a Source along a Path to a Goal.  'Sunlight gleamed from the water of the bay.' 'Lamplight flickered through the foggy air.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path refers to where the Beam travels over or to a landmark the Beam travels by.

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is the location the Beam ends up in.

name: Hypothetical_event
definition_en: The state of affairs or occurrence whose likelihood is assessed. 'Rain is fairly unlikely today, I think.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE expresses a reason the speaker has for making  judgment about the likelihood of an event.  'There is a high chance of rain because of the stormfront.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs  'There is a high probability that it will rain today.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.  'There is a high chance of rain in Seattle.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.  'There is a high chance of rain today.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the Hypothetical_event is likely.  'A positive placebo effect is more likely when both patient and physician believe that therapeutic benefit will result.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity would normally be expected to have a set of possibilites, but instead exhibits only certain possibilites, or exhibits them on fewer situations than expected.  'Our technology  has limits we didn't expect.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Entity is limited.  'There are strong limits on its usefulness.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent consciously places limits upon the Range_of_options.  'The military limited building access to key personnel.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is a natural occurrence or state-of-affairs that limits the Range_of_options.  'Ongoing rains have limited drivers to a small number of roads.'

name: Range_of_options
definition_en: The Range_of_options would normally be expected to have a set of possibilites, but is limited by an Agent or Cause to particular subtypes, situations or characteristics.  'The military limited building access to key personnel.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Range_of_options has been limited.  'Our choices have now been severely limited.'

name: Characteristic
definition_en: The Characteristic indicates the subtypes or situations to which the Range_of_options is limited.  'The military limited access to key personnel only.'  'You should limit your meals to three per day at most.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the limiting takes place.  'Banks are currently limiting customers to two cash transactions per day.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time over which the Range_of_options is limited.  'If you limit your caloric intake for too long, it could damage your health.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Agent of Cause limits the Range_of_options.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Agent or Cause limits the Range_of_options.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Agent or Cause that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Agent or Cause limits the Range_of_options.

name: Form
definition_en: Form is the formal pole of a linguistic sign.

name: Meaning
definition_en: Meaning is the sense of a linguistic Form.

name: Textual_location
definition_en: The FE Textual_location is used for expressions that indicate under which semantic, collocational, pragmatic or other circumstances a Form has a particular Meaning.

name: Referent
definition_en: Referent identifies an object in the real (or a hypothetical) world that a linguistic expression is used to talk about.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute of the Form and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Location
definition_en: The Location where a lot of activity is taking place, or prototypically takes place.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation in amount of activity from the norm or from the amount for another Location.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Location is characterized by a lot of activity.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Location has some degree of activity or liveliness.

name: Place
definition_en: The larger or general area where the Location is lively.  'On this side of town the streets are livelier.'

name: Activity
definition_en: The Activity that is conceptually filling the Location.

name: Individuals
definition_en: The Individuals are engaged in the Activity, creating a lively Location.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Individuals or Location is engaging in the Activity.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: A person who experiences the effects of some situation or Condition for a long period of time.

name: Condition
definition_en: This FE describes the situation that the Experiencer must cope with over a long period of time.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the Experiencer is located when he or she faces the Condition.

name: Time
definition_en: A general description of the temporal location of the Experiencer while coping with the Condition.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Experiencer must cope with the Condition.

name: Locale
definition_en: A stable bounded area.  It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.  'There used to be a forest in that area.'

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Salient parts that make up a Locale.   'This is the largest live oak area in the forest.'

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Locale is located with respect to.  'For some reason, the place next to the lamp was damp.'

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Locale about.  This FE should also include words that indicate that there was no salient formation.  'In an official "Defense of the Pedestrian Act" zone, all forms of wheeled transport (excluding wheelchairs) are prohibited.'

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location that the Locale is a part of. 'John spent several years wandering the northern regions of Europe.'

name: Name
definition_en: ULTIMATELY TO BE REPLACED BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases).  This FE is used for the Names of Locales.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Locale.  'The day after the hurricane, the prime minister visited the devastated area.'

name: Related_event
definition_en: An event related to the locale in some way other than (1) Formational_cause (which is a separate FE) or an intended use (which would place the instance in Locale_by_use), or (3) a defining event (which would place the instance in Locale_by_event).

name: Inherent_purpose
definition_en: The activity that is carried out in the Locale.

name: Locale
definition_en: A stable bounded area characterized by properties of the entities who are typically located there (e.g., work and/or live there).  'A twenty-minute walk will take you to the Dutch-speaking quarter of the city.'

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Salient parts that make up a Locale.

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Locale is located with respect to.  'Residents of the suburban enclave near downtown have started their own little rebellion.'

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Locale about.  This FE should also include words that indicate that there was no salient formation.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The larger area within which the Locale is located.  'A twenty-minute walk will take you to the Dutch-speaking quarter of the city.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Locale.

name: Related_event
definition_en: An event related to the locale in some way other than (1) Formational_cause (which is a separate FE) or an intended use (which would place the instance in Locale_by_use), or (3) a defining event (which would place the instance in Locale_by_event).

name: Inherent_purpose
definition_en: The activity that is carried out in the Locale.

name: Characteristic
definition_en: A property or characteristic of the entities in the Locale.  'A twenty-minute walk will take you to the Dutch-speaking quarter of the city.'

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: The region where the Entity is located.  'If you sign up for this new service, we can get a fix on your phone's location if you lose it or it is stolen.'

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Salient parts that make up a Profiled_region.

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Profiled_region is located with respect to.  'Once you have indicated your location next to a shopping mall, you can access the full array of our services on your mobile device.'

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: This FE indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Profiled_region about.  This FE should also include words that indicate that there was no salient formation.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location that the Profiled_region is a part of.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Profiled_region.

name: Related_event
definition_en: An event related to the Profiled_region in some way other than (1) Formational_cause (which is a separate FE) or an intended use (which would place the instance in Locale_by_use), or (3) a defining event (which would place the instance in Locale_by_event).

name: Inherent_purpose
definition_en: The activity that is carried out in the Profiled_region.

name: Entity
definition_en: The entity is located at the Profiled_region.  'If you sign up for this new service, we can get a fix on your phone's location if you lose it or it is stolen.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Entity is at the Profiled_region.  'Any updates on his current location?'

name: Locale
definition_en: A stable bounded area.  It is typically the denotation of the nouns in Locale_by_event, which will be annotated on the target word.  'We need to find a suitable venue for such a large wedding.' 'Tours was the site of the defeat of the Turks by the French.'

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Salient parts that make up a Locale.    'We need a meeting site with more computers .'

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Locale is located with respect to.  'The site of their first meeting, west of the Mississippi, has never been disclosed.'

name: Defining_event
definition_en: The event for which the locale is known or is named 'The driver died at the scene of the accident.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Locale.  'The next day, the governor visited the still-smoldering site of the fire.'

name: Name
definition_en: The name of the locale. 'The Bonneville site has been a favorite of drivers for many years.'

name: Locale
definition_en: A stable bounded area.  It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Locale is located with respect to.

name: Owner
definition_en: The individual or group of individuals who hold posses the Locale.

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Salient parts that make up a Locale.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any feature or characteristic of the Locale not covered by more specific FEs.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location that the Locale is a part of.

name: Name
definition_en: The name of the Locale.

name: Inherent_purpose
definition_en: The activity that is carried out in the Locale.

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: FN: Salient parts that make up a Locale.   'This is the oldest apartment complex in Florida.'

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location that the Locale is a part of. 'John spent several years wandering the villages of Romania'.

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Locale about.

name: Locale
definition_en: A stable bounded area.  It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.  'There used to be a carnival every summer in that city.'

name: Name
definition_en: ULTIMATELY TO BE REPLACED BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases).  This FE is used for the Names of Locales. 'The city of Paris'

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Locale is located with respect to. ' The corn field across from the highway has been there for many years.'

name: Use
definition_en: The activity that is carried out in the Locale.  'The Campus Microscopy and Imaging Facility (CMIF) serves a wide range of faculty staff and students of The Ohio State University .'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any feature or characteristic of the Locale not covered by more specific FEs.  'We made our way to a quiet farm on the outskirts of Surrey, hoping to be isolated from the goings-on in London.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent Locale itself and any of its participants.

name: Locale
definition_en: The Locale is the entity that ceases to be available for use.  'The other post office closed so they could build a new one.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for the closure, if any.  'The oldpost office closed so they could build a new one.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: The Containing_event describes some event in which the closure occurs.  'Yosemite swiftly closed when the wildfires were sweeping through.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A Depictive describes something about the Locale.  'The police department, suffering from 100 years of wear and tear, closed its doors in 2003.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time of the closure.  'The fire department closed in 2008  after the city ceased to be incorporated.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes the way in which the Locale closed.  'Yosemite swiftly closed when the wildfires swept through.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances that caused closure. Compared to Explanation, this describes situations or environments that lead to failure, not a specific reason for failure.  'Public spaces often close amid political or economic chaos.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place of the failing locale.  'Every park closed in New York City last week for the fireworks.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Locale remains closed.  'The shop closed for three hours while police did their investigation.'

name: Perceiver
definition_en: The individual that determines the Location of the Sought_entity.  'I finally found the peanut underneath the couch cusion.'

name: Sought_entity
definition_en: The entity that the Perceiver succeeds in finding.

name: Location
definition_en: The position of the Sought_entity.  'I found him under the bed.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The general set of entities that the Perceiver examined in order to find the Sought_entity.  'Sam located the Imperial regal among the coins in his pocket and passed it to the boy.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Sought_entity is located.  'We found it last night.'

name: Relative_time
definition_en: Relative_time denotes words that locate the time with respect to an identifiable reference point. '' 'The last day of June, market crashed.'

name: Name
definition_en: Name denotes the name of the particular point in time. '' 'Make sure you lock the doors at closing time.'

name: Whole
definition_en: The Whole describes the larger unit of which the target word describes one part. If there is an appositive that is necessarily larger, it's the Whole. '' 'What time of day is it?'  ' On that day, 1449, a battle raged.'

name: Focal_time
definition_en: The particular, salient point in time. If a specified time is present, it is the focal time. Otherwise, the unit is the focal time. If there is an appositive that specifies an entity that it not necessarily larger than the target, both the unit and the specification are the FE. '' 'I didn't see it at that time.'  'The time is 10:00.'  'That day, Dec. 7th, will live in infamy.'

name: Salient_event
definition_en: Salient_event is an event that is associated with the given point in time. '' 'It is time to go.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A Descriptor is any characterization or description of the point in time that is not covered by a more specific FE. '' ' WWII was a strange time to be an American.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the Light is emitted, usually indicating the brightness.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of a focal participant during the emission of Light . 'The moonlight shone cold over the Scottish moor.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of Light emission. 'In the dim light the gold and strong colours glittered and glowed intensely.'

name: Figure
definition_en: The percept which is perceived at a certain Ground location. 'Candlelight sparkled on the silverware.''Her face glistened with sweat.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The location of the phenomenon.'Hot coals glowed behind the fire grate.'

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the emission of the Light . 'The screen glowed into life.'

name: Cause_of_shine
definition_en: This is the cause of the shininess of the phenomenon, generally introduced by 'with'.'Her face glistened with sweat.''His eyes gleamed with amusement.'

name: Light
definition_en: The Light which is emitted.  In this frame, it is usually incorporated in verbs and adjectives, and is the denotation of many of the nouns. 'The fire glowed.' 'The glint of gold made me blind with greed.'  Occasionally this FE shows up as a full argument:'The chamber glowed with brilliant light.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The period for which the Figure shows up against the Ground due to Light falling on it.  'For a few minutes the walls glowed in the sun'

name: Place
definition_en: The spatial setting in which the Figure shows up against a Ground location.  'Outside something was shimmering on the shore.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Figure is observed against the Ground location due to Light shining on it.  'In the morning the grass glistened with dew'

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure somewhere in the midst of their motion or during the entirety of the motion event.

name: Figure
definition_en: The Figure is perceived as in motion relative to a certain Ground location.

name: Distance
definition_en: This  FE identifies the Distance traveled by the Figure after the point where they were in the Profiled_region of the Ground.  'The party had climbed 2000 feet past the base camp.' 'She tunneled deep under the earth.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE identifies the Direction traveled by the Figure.  This FE is filled by one of a closed class of adverbs:  up, down, out (meaning 'beyond the boundary around the viewpoint'), off (meaning 'disconnect between landmark and figure'), back (meaning 'along a line from front to back of landmark, and relatively inaccessible'), and, more rarely, away, along, and dialectally, back down (meaning 'down and behind').

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the locative relation between Figure and Ground obtains.

name: Figures
definition_en: The Figures are items conceived of as moving with respect to each other.

name: Deixis
definition_en: An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder), or specifically separated from the speech context by distance or a barrier (over).  Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.  'She has a boyfriend way over in Springfield.' 'It is lying here on my desk.'

name: Accessibility
definition_en: An indication of how accessible the Figure is to some participant in the speech context (either the speaker or the addressee, or some other highly salient viewpoint in a narrative).  This FE normally describes availability for manipulation and use, but may simply describe how easily seen or difficult to see the Figure is. There is a closed class of items that can fill this slot, including only 'just' and 'right' indicating ease of access, and 'way', 'all the way', or (dialectally) 'clear' indicating distance and difficulty of access.    'Oh yeah , the flashlight 's right in my handbag.' ' I had an uncle that lived clear over in Kenmore , and I tried to ride my bike there.'  While ease of access correlates with proximal deixis (e.g. 'right here') and difficulty correlates with distal deixis (e.g. 'all the way over there'), these notions are separable as shown in the following examples:  'I have two officers right over in the next room.' 'You ca n't come way out here to my mom 's!'

name: Directness
definition_en: An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target.  This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, directly, and due (and some combinations of these), but also occurs with rarer items like 'smack dab'.  Some general adverbs that indicate exact and non-exact match to an idea can also express this FE:

name: Temporal_profile
definition_en: A description of how the access path to the Ground interacts with time.  This FE is filled only by the closed class of adverbials back.adv (which indicates that the position was occupied by the Figure before) and on.adv (which indicates a continued path).  While this FE in its most basic use refers to cases of actual motion, it can be used with descriptions of static position, in which case it either refers to fictive, imagined motion (as in the first example below), or it backgrounds motion entirely (as in the second example).  'You 'll find it straight on around behind the door.' 'I do n't know why my kids are back out of the crib.'

name: Region_quantification
definition_en: A description of how much of a potential profiled region actually has (or is expected to have) a Figure in it.  It is normally filled by closed-class items like 'all', 'somewhere', 'nowhere', etc.

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: The region within which a Figure might be found.  This FE is exclusive of Figure, and is a reconstrual that is not possible with verb lexical units.  'Past the kitchen is the path she chose .'

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure.  'The cat is on the mat.'

name: Figure
definition_en: The Figure is perceived as located relative to a certain Ground location. The figure can be an entity or an event.  'The cat is on the mat.'

name: Distance
definition_en: This  FE identifies the  Distance between the Figure and the Ground.  This FE requires an image schema with a vector that extends from the Ground, or a subpart of the Ground, in some direction, and the Distance is measured along this vector from the Ground to the profiled region.    'The climbers are now 2000 feet above the base camp.' 'Deep under the earth lurk dark things.'  In cases where the target does not introduce such an image schema, Distance should be annotated as part of the Direction FE that introduces such a vector.  'She found a phone 200 feet up on the radio tower.'  Note that a number of frequent adverbial targets, e.g. up.adv and down.adv, identify the Ground, with the location of an implicit viewer, so Distance is effectively measured from the viewpoint location in these cases.  'We were already nearly 1000 meters down.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure.  This FE is filled by one of a closed class of adverbs:  up, down, out (meaning 'beyond the boundary around the viewpoint'), off (meaning 'disconnect between landmark and figure'), back (meaning 'along a line from front to back of landmark, and relatively inaccessible'), and, more rarely, away, along, and dialectally, back down (meaning 'down and behind'). 'The cat is down on the mat.'

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the locative relation between Figure and Ground obtains.  'He was in Athens on Friday.'

name: Figures
definition_en: The Figures are items which mutually serve to identify the location of the other items.
