name: Profiled_region
definition_en: The region within which a Figure might be found.  This FE is exclusive of Figure, and is a reconstrual that is not possible with verb lexical units.  'Next to the kitchen is the best place to locate your garage .'

name: Figure
definition_en: The entity that is located with respect to the Ground.

name: Ground
definition_en: The entity with respect to which the Figure is located.

name: Figures
definition_en: The entities that are located with respect to each other.

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: The area with respect to the Ground or Figures in which the Figure or Figures reside.

name: Host
definition_en: The Host is the individual (or group of individuals) that own or control the Residence and allow the  Lodger to temporarily stay there.

name: Lodger
definition_en: The Lodger is the individual who is given permission to lodge in the Residence.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Host provides a Residence to the Lodger

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the Host provides a temporary Residence.

name: Residence
definition_en: The location controlled by the Host which the Lodger stays at temporarily.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the Relinquishing occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation indicates what the Donor is trying to accomplish by the Relinquishing.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time indicates when the Relinquishing occurs.

name: Donor
definition_en: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the object that changes ownership due to the Relinquishing.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose indicates the purpose for which the intentional Relinquishing takes place.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The Recipient is the entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

name: Donor
definition_en: The entity that began by owning the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The thing which was originally owned by the Donor. (This does not include bodyparts or medical conditions, but does include intellectual property, etc.)

name: Owner
definition_en: The original Owner of the Possession.

name: Possession
definition_en: The object that is possessed by the Owner.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Possession is lost.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Possession is lost.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE describes how the Owner loses the Possession.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the event of losing a Possession logically follows.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: This is the person (or people) whose mental state changes.  'Kim went ballistic.'

name: Action
definition_en: Something done by the Protagonist as a result of losing mental equilibrium.  'You totally lost it with that speech you just gave to the Principal.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree marks the extent to which the Protagonist's mental state changes.  'John totally lost it'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, especially general descriptions comparing events.  'He flipped out like my dad did last year.'

name: Affected_party
definition_en: A person (or persons) who is saliently affected by the Protagonist 's Actions.  'I'm sorry, but every time I try to sneak out she goes apeshit on me.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The cause for the Protagonist to go crazy.  'She went ballistic because of the pizzas, man.'

name: Sufferer
definition_en: The being or entity that emotionally experiences the death of the Deceased.

name: Deceased
definition_en: The entity that has died.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Deceased passed away.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Deceased passed away.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE describes how the Deceased passed away.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Timespan
definition_en: The period over which a loss has occurred.

name: Duration
definition_en: How long the event takes place.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the loss occurs.

name: Perceiver
definition_en: The Perceiver is the entity who fails to keep the Theme in sight.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the object that becomes unperceivable.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Perceiver loses perception of the Theme.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Perceiver loses perception of the Theme.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE denotes a proposition from which the loss of perception logically follows.

name: Explanation

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The State of affairs that is evaluated.  'That was a lucky catch.'

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist is the one for whom the destiny is evaluated.  'He is lucky.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description of the sort of State_of_affairs. This occurs with nominal LUs which are both the target and the State_of_affairs.  'My good fortune has run out.'

name: Role
definition_en: The Role filled by the Protagonist.  'He is a lucky gambler.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time for which the Protagonist's destiny is good.  'I was rather fortunate in the late 90s, making much of my fortune at that time.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the State_of_affairs is lucky (either a degree of goodness or a degree of unexpectedness, or both).  'He is very lucky.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Protagonist has luck.  'I'm only lucky in casinos.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Individuals make each other's acquaintance.  'I met my wife 2 yrs ago.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Individuals make each others acquaintance.  'Bill met his  wife in Poltava, Ukraine.'

name: Individuals
definition_en: The persons (or in rare cases animals) that make each other's acquaintance.  'My wife and I met in college working in the theatre and we will have been married for 30 years in June 2000.'

name: Context
definition_en: The Event, frequently a social occasion, during which the Individuals make each other's acquaintance.  'The two first met at a lecture in 1851.'

name: Individual_1
definition_en: The semantically more prominent one of the two parties when the Individuals are realized separately.  'Melissa Hurley had never met her neighbor, Richard Congdon ? the dog owner ? until recently, when she and a reporter knocked on his door.'

name: Individual_2
definition_en: The semantically less prominent of the two parties when the Individuals are expressed separately.  ' Gossip reports say she either met Kennedy while helping him shop for suits at Calvin Klein, or was contacted by him after he saw her jogging in a New York park '

name: Intermediary
definition_en: A person or social group that connects both of the Individuals, with a group member typically introducing the Individuals to each other.   'Let's call her Gretchen. I "met" her through a mutual friend (the same fellow who has wanted me to write this column for the past couple years).'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The state of affairs that leads to the Individuals' making each other's acquaintance.   'No, I met him because he was also the teacher for the special science fiction class.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Party_1
definition_en: The individual or individuals that form the more prominent (i.e. agentive) party of the agreement, as compared with Party_2. That is, Party_1 is generally encoded as the External Argument of verbs, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Party_1. Thus Manner is construed to be that of Party_1, not necessarily that of Party_2 or the group of Parties as a whole.    'On Monday, the airline reached a deal with the Canadian Auto Workers.'

name: Party_2
definition_en: The semantically (and grammatically) less prominent participant (or group of participants) in the agreement. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with).  'Mozilla Foundation has finally reached an agreement with America Online.'

name: Obligation
definition_en: An expression of the commitment made by the Parties .    'The US and Russia have agreed to share early warning data on missile launches.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic is a description of the domain covered.  'Some types of alloy steel have been covered in the expiring trade agreement.'

name: Medium
definition_en: As with other frames in the Communication domain, the Medium of communication may be expressed. Medium is the physical entity or channel used to record or negotiate the Obligation.    'The parties made a written agreement to arbitrate disputes arising in connection with the contract.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the act of making an agreement which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of either Party_1 or Parties that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'I readily agreed with her to end our wrestling match.'

name: Parties
definition_en: The group of individuals portrayed as equally involved in making an agreement.  'The US and Russia have agreed to cooperate in destroying surplus portable anti-aircraft missiles.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Agreement occurs.'The town coucil members reached an agreement at the City Hall plenary session.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time where the Agreement occurs.'The town coucil members finally reached an agreement at midnight.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describes a characteristic of the Obligation.

name: Concept_1
definition_en: Concept1 is the phenomenon which is believed to be related to Concept2.

name: Concept_2
definition_en: The phenomenon which is believed to be linked to Concept1.

name: Evidence
definition_en: The phenomenon which proves the causal connection.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The sentient entity that recognizes the causal connection.

name: Concepts
definition_en: The phenomena which are believed to be related.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE describes how often the connection is made  'People often link  brand names with Hollywood celebrities'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Cognizer make the connection.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Cognizer makes the connection.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Party_1
definition_en: The individual or individuals that form the more prominent (i.e., agentive) party to the compromise, as compared with Party_2. That is, Party_1 is generally encoded as the External Argument of verbs, and peripheral FEs that do not make reference to the event itself generally make reference to Party_1. Thus Manner is construed to be that of Party_1, not necessarily that of Party_2 or the group of Parties as a whole.  'On Monday, the airline compromised with the Canadian Auto Workers. on a contract for salary and benefits.'

name: Party_2
definition_en: The semantically (and grammatically) less prominent participant (or group of participants) in the compromise. It is generally encoded within a prepositional phrase (e.g. headed by with).  'Parenthetical Foundation has finally reached a compromise with The Bracket Fund.'

name: Obligation
definition_en: An expression of the commitment made by the Parties .  'The US and Russia have compromised to share a portion of early warning data on missile launches.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic is a description of the domain covered by the compromise.  'They'll never compromise on salary.'

name: Medium
definition_en: As with other frames in the Communication domain, the Medium of communication may be expressed. Medium is the physical entity or channel used to record or negotiate the Obligation.   'The parties entered into an oral compromise to arbitrate disputes arising in connection with the contract.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the act of making an agreement which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of either Party_1 or Parties that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'I readily compromised with her to end our wrestling match.'

name: Parties
definition_en: The group of individuals portrayed as equally involved in reaching a compromise.  'The US and Russia have compromised on a plan to destroy surplus portable anti-aircraft missiles.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the compromise occurs.  'The town coucil members reached a compromise at the City Hall plenary session.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the compromise occurs.  'The town coucil members finally reached a compromise at midnight.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describes a characteristic of the Obligation, Party_1, or Parties.  'They compromised, unaware that we would have given in to any of their demands had the simply kept at it for another week.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Parties make the compromise.\  'We're making compromises to head off potentially larger conflicts down the road.'

name: Sound_source
definition_en: The frame element Sound_source is assigned to a constituent referring to a physical entity which emits a sound. Such an entity must have an appropriately complex internal structure such that it can create a sound. For example, a machine or some other thing with moving parts can create sound by itself.    'The wind howled.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for the Sound_source producing the sound.  Generally, this is some external stimulus that prompts the Sound_source to make noise.  'The planks above him creaked  as Simon hoisted himself inside'

name: Sound
definition_en: The frame element Sound is incorporated in the meaning of the verbs of this frame. Otherwise, this FE is assigned to NPs which actually refer to a sound in the presence of the target. This typically occurs when the target is a verb used as a modifier in its -ing form, e.g.:   'The branches made a rattling sound.'  In this example, the frame element Sound is actually expressed by the word sound.   Sometimes, Sound just occurs as an NP argument of a tensed verb form. 'Heavy music thundered from leather-curtained basements'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner expressions may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of a sounds as such: loudly, shrilly, etc.   'Jocelyn sobbed loudly. '

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: The location of the Sound_source by which the Sound is emitted.  ' A radio blasted music from the balcony.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: State of the Sound_source during the action. 'Cicadas screech unseen from within'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The noise-making may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the mental or emotional state of an animate Sound_source.  Internal_cause is expressed in a PP Complement:   'Kim hmmmed and haaed in concentration.' 'Kim wailed in despair.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion is the sulocation of the Sound_source from which the sound is emitting.  'Manville whistled through his teeth'

name: Addressee
definition_en: Addressee identifies the intended audience of an event of making a noise as a communicative signal.   ' Our new puppy has taken to growling at other dogs'

name: Noisy_event
definition_en: An event in which one or more Sound_sources participate and which is accompanied by Sound.   'The conversations droned on'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path along which the Sound travels away from the Sound_source.  'The radio blared across the room'

name: Place
definition_en: The location of the Sound_source. This FE differs from Location_of_source only in terms of point of view; the latter FE implies a point of view that is not on the Sound_source.   'A bat squeaked over our heads. '

name: Circumstances
definition_en: A state or  location of the Sound_source which contributes to the Sound_source's making noise.  'Leaves crunched underfoot'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Noisy_event occurs.  'It's going to beep again in two minutes.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times the noise-making event takes place.  'The raven cawed twice and flew on a short distance, then sat down again in front of her and cawed again twice. '

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: This FE indicates that the noise-making event is embedded within a series of similar events.

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who makes arrangements for the Event to take place at a Time and Place.  'Lucy organized a playdate for little Michael and Marcy.'

name: Event
definition_en: The incident for which the Agent has made arrangements.  'I've already made vacation arrangements.'  'Josie organized the conference last year.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The person for whom the Event was arranged.  'Ms. Moneypenny will arrange that for you, Mr. Bond.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The frequency with which the Agent organizes the Event.  'Silvia made the travel arrangements for the conference every year.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Agent makes the arrangements for the Event.  'Max hastily made arrangements to go see the therapist tomorrow.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means used by the Agent to make arrangements for the Event to take place.  'Lily made arrangements via email to see the venue.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Agent has made arrangements for the Event to take place.  'Lionel organized a meeting at the local pub to discuss the bleak future of our organization.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Agent's motivation for arranging the Event.  'Lionel organized a meeting at the local pub to discuss the bleak future of our organization.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The cause for arranging the Event.  'Marcy made the arrangements this time because Millie was out of town.'

name: Scheduled_time
definition_en: The time for which the Agent has arranged the Event.  'I've put together a luncheon for 12:30.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE describes the time at which the arrangements are made.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual that assumes a particular facial expression.

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotion or other mental state that leads the Agent to assume a facial expression.

name: Body_part
definition_en: The particular part of the face that the Agent moves into a facial expression.

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount to which the expression on the face of the Agent matches the prototypical image for the indicated facial expression.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Intended_perceiver
definition_en: The individual that the Agent intends to see the facial expression; often the Intended_perceiver is also the focus of the emotional Internal_cause of the Agent.  'Why don't you smile at me more often?'

name: Time
definition_en: The point in time at which the change in facial_expression takes place.

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: The location relative to some viewer (often the Intended_perceiver) at which the Agent makes an expression.  'He smiled up at me from the bottom of the well.'

name: Path_of_gaze
definition_en: A path expression that describes a line from the Agent to the Intended_perceiver.

name: Cognate_event
definition_en: The facial expression of the Agent.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Agent during the event.

name: External_cause
definition_en: An event experienced by the Agent that leads them to make an expression.

name: Manipulator
definition_en: The person who gets the Victim to act against their interest.

name: Victim
definition_en: The person who the Manipulator gets to do something they would not have done had no pressure or deception been applied.

name: Resulting_action
definition_en: What the Manipulator intends to make the Victim do and the Victim actually does.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Manipulator that enables them to alter the action of the Victim. 'I badgered her into coming by calling her every five minutes.'

name: Goods
definition_en: The FE goods is anything (including labor, time, or legal rights) that can be taken away.  'Leslie blackmailed the watch out of John.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity that the Manipulator uses to get the Victim to perform the Resulting_action.

name: Purpose
definition_en: A state-of-affairs that the Manipulator is hoping to bring about by manipulating the Victim.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the manipulation occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Manipulator manipulates the Victim.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including metaphorical force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Manipulator that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the volitional actor who manipulates the Theme.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which the Theme is manipulated.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the manipulation of the Theme takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the manipulation of the Theme takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the manipulation of the Theme takes place.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the manipulation of the Theme takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the manipulation of the Theme takes place.

name: Theme
definition_en: The object which is manipulated by the Agent into a particular shape.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the manipulation of the Theme takes place.  'John coiled the wire tightly around the spool.'

name: Locus
definition_en: Where the manipulation of the Theme takes place.  'Kelly wound the laces around the back of her heel to combat loose shoes.'

name: Resultant_configuration
definition_en: The shape or configuration of the Theme after being manipulated by the Agent.  'He twisted the wire into a hook.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent manipulates an object. Agent typically refers to animate beings, but is also extended to mechanical and other inanimate objects.  Agent is most frequently expressed as the external argument of verbs:   'A robot arm grasps the box on the conveyor belt and seals it.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity being manipulated often occurs as the direct object of verbs:   'Squeeze the ball as many times as you can.' 'Pat squeezed Jo's hand.'

name: Locus
definition_en: The Agent's manipulation of an Entity may be further specified as being localized to some part of the Entity, a Locus.  The Locus is usually expressed as a PP Complement.  'Pat squeezed Jo by the hand.'

name: Bodypart_of_agent
definition_en: The part of the Agent's body being used to manipulate the Entity may also be expressed. While the default is for an Agent to use his/her hands, other body parts may be specified. This frame element usually occurs as a PP-complement.  'Kim grasped the needle between finger and thumb.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of the manipulation.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner of performing an action.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of manipulation.

name: Time
definition_en: When the manipulation takes place 'I seized the letter before he did.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Agent's purpose in performing the manipulation. 'The President grabbed hold of the handle of the helicopter to avoid being blown away.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with the Entity to accomplish the action indicated by the target.  'Smithers nudged the insect with a paper towel.'

name: Means
definition_en: An action by the Agent to accomplish the desired manipulation.  'Martin clutched it by pulling a rope attached to a pully which tightened the belt to the PVC'

name: Place
definition_en: The spatial setting in which the manipulation takes place.  'In the hallway he managed to grabthe monarch by the ankles'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies a depictive phrase describing the Agent or Bodypart_of_agent that holds throughout the action.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs leading to the manipulation.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Comparison_event
definition_en: The Comparison_event is the principal event being characteriszed by the Manner. The Manner of this Comparison_event is often used in comparison with the Foreground_event.

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: The Salient_entity that is associated with or directly responsible for the Comparison_activity.

name: Manner
definition_en: The description of the Comparison_event or Comparison_activity.

name: Manner_descriptor
definition_en: A description of the Manner.

name: Foreground_event
definition_en: The Manner of Foreground_event is compared with the Manner of the Comparison_event (i.e. the principal event of the clause).

name: Comparison_activity
definition_en: The Salient_entity conducts or engages in the Comparison_activity that is being described.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The person who actualizes a pattern of behavior.  'John was living the dream.'

name: Lifestyle
definition_en: A pattern of behavior which the actions of the Experiencer matches for a significant period of time.  'He lived the life of a beggar.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Lifestyle may be characterized by a Manner, which is often expressed adverbially.  'He lived dangerously.'

name: Time
definition_en: A temporal description of when the Experiencer adopts a Lifestyle.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Experiencer is carrying out the expected patterns of behavior of the Lifestyle.  'Jeremy is living very adventurously these days.'

name: Place
definition_en: The spatial location where the Experiencer carries out a Lifestyle.

name: Domain
definition_en: The general category under which the Lifestyle can be categorized.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE covers characterizations of the Lifestyle that are not covered by other frame elements.

name: Producer
definition_en: The person or company that produces the Product. 'General Electric manufactures electronic appliances.'

name: Product
definition_en: The Product is produced by the Producer. 'The company manufactured T-shirts.'

name: Resource
definition_en: Resource is the material that the product is made from. 'Copal varnishes are manufactured from fossilised resins.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Product is manufactured. 'Those leather shoes were made in Italy.'

name: Time
definition_en: This Fe identifies the Time when the product was produced. 'Those cars were produced in 1997.'

name: Factory
definition_en: Factory identifies the particular plant where the Product is manufactured. 'Those machines were manufactured in the Miami plant.'

name: Consumer
definition_en: The Producer produces the Product for the Consumer. 'The toys are made for children.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A phrase that describes the state of the Producer or the Product during the manufacturing process. 'They manufactured the goods naked.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which a Producer  produces a Product. 'Those lamps were made by machines.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which a Producer creates a Product. 'Fine furniture is  usually made slowly.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a Producer  creates a Product. 'Cars are manufactured by mass production.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Producer produces a Product. 'The company will produce more high-tech  gadgets to meet the demand of the market.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE identifies the Circumstances under which the the product was produced. 'They produced only half of the units after an injunction to follow the environmental policy.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of manufacturing events in a given time period.  'We produce 90 million units every month.'

name: Locus
definition_en: The Locus is a description of the active zone of the Producer, where the manufacturing most saliently takes place.

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome of a contest whose Margin is under consideration.

name: Margin
definition_en: The difference between the minimum required for victory and the actual Outcome.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Value from what is expected given the Outcome and the Value indicated by the target.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Outcome has a particular Value for the Margin.

name: Value
definition_en: The generally implicit Value of the Margin.

name: Mass_theme
definition_en: The mass of entities which moves.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree of abundance.

name: Area
definition_en: The place where the overall motion event takes place, thus including Source, Path, and Goal locations.  'Letters streamed in all over the country.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which motion occurs.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location the Theme occupies initially before its change of location.   'Afterwards, the crowd flooded away from the ceremony. '

name: Path
definition_en: Path refers to (a part of the) ground the Mass_theme travels over or to a landmark the Mass_theme travels by.   'The door opened , and a crowd of people flooded past me, into the hall.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is the location the Mass_theme ends up in.    'Eager spectators crowded into the auditorium'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE is any expression which characterizes the extent of motion.  This frame element occurs throughout the motion domain but is very infrequent in Motion.Noise. The engine 	spluttered forward a short way and stopped.

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Mass_theme is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Mass_theme. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.  ' Fans poured in by boat and train.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the motion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Mass_theme that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully)  'Children crowded eagerly around us'

name: Place
definition_en: The spatial setting in which the Mass_motion takes place.  'In the main auditorium people crowded around Orange's newest computer'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE is used for expressions that indicate motion along a line from the deitic center towards a reference point (which may be implicit) that is neither the Goal of the posture change nor a landmark along the way of the moving part of the body.  Often Direction is defined with reference to the canonical orientation of the Mass_theme, or the orientation imposed by an implicit observer.

name: Purpose
definition_en: In cases wherein the Mass_theme is construed as a sentient entities, this FE denotes the state of affairs that the entities wish to bring about by mass movement.  'The ducks flocked south to mate.'

name: Expression_1
definition_en: In an equation that has more terms on one side than the other, Expression_1 is the side of the equation with fewer terms.  'Force EQUALS mass * acceleration'

name: Expression_2
definition_en: In an equation that has more terms on one side than the other, Expression_2 is the side of the equation that has more terms.  'Force EQUALS mass * acceleration'

name: Type
definition_en: The value or type of object that is computed by the equation.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent uses the Means to acheive a Purpose.

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by the Agent.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The goal or purpose of the Agent.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Means.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Agent uses the Means.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which a particular gradable Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

name: Value
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the Attribute.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Value from the norm.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having  a particular Value for the Attribute.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Value for the Attribute.

name: Unit
definition_en: The Unit of measurement.'Apollo grows 34 acres of strawberries.''Otto owns 43 hectares of land.'

name: Area
definition_en: The region whose surface is being measured. 'Klaas has  a 10 acre peach orchard '

name: Count
definition_en: The number of Units.'Smiley owns fifteen hectares of prime real estate.'

name: Occupant
definition_en: Things that occupy the Area that is being measured.'Swanson grows 1,000 Acres of vegetables.'

name: Entity
definition_en: An abstract or concrete undelimited entity that is measured by the Event.

name: Event
definition_en: The event that a delimitable quantity or duration of an Entity participates in.

name: Count
definition_en: The number of iterations of the Event.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Count
definition_en: The number of Units of the measured entity.'The ads had been absorbed into her brain during many hours of television watching.'

name: Unit
definition_en: The standardized quantity in terms of which other quantities are measured.'Seven hours of torrential rain reduced the pitch to a lake.'

name: Process
definition_en: The activity or state that takes place during the period of time under discussion.'He had to listen to almost two hours of complaints.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent either brings about or is the most involved in the Process.

name: Count
definition_en: The number of Units of the linear extent.'Five miles of pipework were necessary.'

name: Stuff
definition_en: The Stuff whose linear extent is being measured.'Miles of wiring were necessary.'

name: Unit
definition_en: The standardized quantity in terms of which other quantities of the same kind are  measured.'Miles of telephone cables had to be replaced.'

name: Dimension
definition_en: This FE marks constituents which express what property is being measured.

name: Count
definition_en: The number of Units of the measured mass.'Serena found two pounds of sugar in the freezer.'

name: Unit
definition_en: The standardized quantity in terms of which other quantities of the same kind are  measured.'Take two grams DNI every day before and after dinner.'

name: Stuff
definition_en: The Stuff whose weight is being measured.'Sue bought three kilos of cat food on sale.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which a particular gradable Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

name: Value
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the Attribute.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Value from the norm.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having  a particular Value for the Attribute.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Value for the Attribute.

name: Unit
definition_en: A standard measure, having a known value for the Attribute.

name: Count
definition_en: The number of Units which are equivalent to the Value of the Entity .

name: Count
definition_en: The number of Units of the measured volume.'Serena found two cups of sugar in the freezer.'

name: Stuff
definition_en: The Stuff whose volume is being measured.'Sue bought three bottles of milk on sale.'

name: Unit
definition_en: The standardized quantity in terms of which other quantities of the same kind are  measured.'Drink two glasses of wine every day.'

name: Size
definition_en: A specification of the volume of the container.'Michell bought a 2 liter bottle of Sangria.'

name: Count
definition_en: The number of Units of the measured Entity . 'The ads had been absorbed into her brain during many hours of television watching.'

name: Unit
definition_en: The known quantity with respect to an Attribute.

name: Entity
definition_en: The item which is quantified in terms of the Attribute.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The aspect of the Entity which is being described and quantified.

name: Patient
definition_en: This FE is used for the patient, entity, or population (originally) affected by the condition or illness.  'juvenile diabetes' 'Dutch Elm disease' 'Legionnaire's disease'

name: Body_part
definition_en: Body_Part is used for the part or area of the body affected by the condition or disease. 'cardiovascular disease' 'liver disease'

name: Cause
definition_en: This FE is used for the cause of a condition or disease. 'bacterial meningitis'

name: Symptom
definition_en: This FE is used for a prominent symptom of the condition or disease.  'asymptomatic stenosis' 'I have a cold with a really bad cough.'

name: Name
definition_en: This FE is used for the Name that identifies the condition or disease.  'Munchausen Syndrome'

name: Ailment
definition_en: FN: Any medical problem.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Ailment diverges from the norm.  'I am very sick.'  Since the degree of involvement with an Ailment is equivalent to how negative the experience of the Patient is, in many cases, Degree is expressed by a negative descriptor.  'It seems that he does have very severe eczema.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Ailment is effecting the Patients.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time over which a medical condition persists.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Instrument is used.  'Use the stethoscope to check his lungs'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the medical Instrument. 'Use the stethoscope to check his lungs.'

name: Medic
definition_en: The medical professional who has responsibility for the care of the Patient

name: Affliction
definition_en: The particular disorder that the Patient is suffering from and the the Medic treats.

name: Body_system
definition_en: The part of the Patient's body that is being treated.    ''

name: Medical_center
definition_en: The place visited by the Patient and where the Medic works.

name: Patient
definition_en: The person who is under the care of a Medic or other form of medical professional.

name: Intervention
definition_en: A drug or procedure is administered or performed in order to treat a Medical_condition.

name: Result
definition_en: The consequence of the Intervention.

name: Medical_condition
definition_en: A holistic description of the medical state of the patient (or a part of the state of the patient), which may or may not indicate the cause of a deviation from normal.

name: Patient
definition_en: Individuals that receive medical Intervention because of their Medical_condition.

name: Side_effects
definition_en: Effects of the Intervention that are unintended or undesirable.

name: Extent
definition_en: The degree to which an Intervention has affected the Medical_condition or Symptoms.

name: Frequency_of_success
definition_en: The regularity with which an Intervention is effective for treating a Medical_condition or Symptom(s).

name: Medical_professional
definition_en: The individual or team that attempts to improve the medical condition of the Patient.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE identifies the Type of medical professional. 'Paediatric oncologists treat children with leukemia.'

name: Professional
definition_en: This FE identifies the medical Professional. 'Paediatric oncologists treat children with leukemia.'

name: Affliction
definition_en: The particular disorder that the medical Professional treats.  Most words in the frame inherently indicate this information.  'Cardiac gerontologists can make more money in a year than I 'll see in my life !'

name: Body_system
definition_en: The part of the body that the medical Professional treats.  This is usually indicated by the Lexical Unit itself.  ''

name: Age
definition_en: The length of time the Professional has been alive.

name: Compensation
definition_en: The payment that the Professional recieves for working.

name: Contract_basis
definition_en: The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.

name: Employer
definition_en: The Employer gives compensation to the Professional for working.

name: Ethnicity
definition_en: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Professional belongs.

name: Place_of_employment
definition_en: The place where the Professional works.

name: Rank
definition_en: Rank is the position in a hierarchy that the Professional occupies within an organization.

name: Origin
definition_en: The Origin is the place where the Professional was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

name: Specialty
definition_en: This FE identifies the medical Specialty that someone practices.  'Ralph practices paediatric oncology.'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE identifies the Type of medical Specialty . 'Ralph practices paediatric oncology.'

name: Body_system
definition_en: The sub-part or sub-system of the body which is studied.  This is normally incorporated in the LUs of the frame.  'Dr. Steppenhame was a specialist in intestinal epidemiology.'

name: Affliction
definition_en: The disease or disorder that a specialist attempts to treat.  This concept is normally incorporated in the name of the Specialty.  'She briefly worked as diabetic endocrinology intern.'

name: Text
definition_en: The written source, body of work, or linguistic utterance in which the Item is found/expressed.

name: Item
definition_en: The piece of information or expression that is contained within the Text.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Item appears in the Text.   'Everyday in the newspaper there are articles relating to science and technology.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the Item appears in the Text.

name: Agent
definition_en: The intentional Agent acts to meet to a Standard.

name: Entity
definition_en: The non-intentional Entity becomes sufficient enough to meet a Standard.

name: Event
definition_en: An act or occurence that changes circumstances sufficiently so as to meet a Standard.

name: Standard
definition_en: A condition or requirement that the Agent, Entity, or Event attempt to meet.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Agent or Entity become sufficient in regards to the Standard.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Agent or Entity become sufficient in regards in to the Standard.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Agent, Entity, or Event becomes sufficient in regards to the Standard.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Standard is exceeded or not by Agent, Entity or Event.

name: Party_1
definition_en: Party_1 is the grammatically more prominent participant in the meeting event.  It can refer to either a single individual or a larger party separate from Party_2 before the meeting.

name: Party_2
definition_en: A grammatically less prominent participant in the meeting event.  It can refer to either a single individual or a larger party separate from Party_1 before the meeting.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that Party_1 and Party_2 plan to engage in upon meeting.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the meeting happens.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the meeting happens.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means descibes the way in which Party_1 and Party_2 convene.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the meeting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of Party_1 or Party_2.

name: Trigger
definition_en: The event that elicits a Response.

name: Response
definition_en: The means action or judgement in response to the Trigger.

name: Manner
definition_en: A characterization of the Response action.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Response action takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: The point in time when Response is made to the Trigger.

name: Origin
definition_en: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

name: Person
definition_en: The Person is the member of the military.

name: Persistent_characteristic
definition_en: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.

name: Age
definition_en: The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.

name: Ethnicity
definition_en: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.

name: Context_of_acquaintance
definition_en: An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.  'Is she the marine from the movie we saw last night?'

name: Rank
definition_en: Rank is the position in the military hierarchy that the Person occupies.  	 'Robin is the highest-ranking soldier at the facility.'

name: Place_of_employment
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Person is stationed.

name: Loyal_side
definition_en: The Person belongs to the military of the Loyal_side.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE identifies a more specific Type of military function or specialty that the Person has.

name: Compensation
definition_en: The Compensation is the payment that the Person receives for performing military service.

name: Contract_basis
definition_en: The Contract_basis describes the conditions of military membership with respect to permanency, time or duration of duty, payment basis, and so on.

name: Military_organization
definition_en: The military organization to which the Person belongs.  'Hundreds of US Navy sailors will be returning home soon.'

name: Member
definition_en: The person who belongs to a Group.  'Two members of the Red Cross were here about a donation '

name: Group
definition_en: A set of people standing in a semi-permanent relationship together.

name: Standing
definition_en: An indication of the Member's status within the Group.   'Bill is a full member of the Elks.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Member is a member of the Group.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the membership relationship holds.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The sentient being that focuses on a Pattern so that it will remain in the memory.  ' I have memorized two kinds of knowledge from Allah's Apostle '

name: Pattern
definition_en: The phenomenon that the Cognizer observes and commits to memory.  'Impress your friends by memorizing your phone numbers and throwing away your PDA! '

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Cognizer memorizes the Pattern.  'Barney memorized the poem yesterday.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location wherein the Cognizer memorizes the Pattern.  'Herbert Kornfeldt memorized his speech in the mailroom.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the memorization event  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously),  secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of a Cognizer that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Hurriedly, the bus-driver memorized the new route.'

name: Completeness
definition_en: The exactness of the match between the Cognizer's memory and the Pattern.  'Whomever you emulate, internalize the sound of the soloist and memorize it exactly.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Cognizer by which they achieve memorization.   'Don't memorize Morse code  by counting dots and dashes.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The goal that the Cognizer has in mind, which they believe will be accomplished by memorization.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person whose mental Content is at issue.

name: Content
definition_en: The Content is the mental content that a Cognizer retains or forgets.  'Each student must be able to recall the whole paragraph  .'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject the Cognizer mental Content is about.  'John  forgot everything about his uncle.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Cognizer manages to remember or forget the Content.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result represents the consequences of the remembering or forgetting of the mental Content.

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration is the amount of time for which the mental Content is remembered or forgotten.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the remembering or forgetting takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the remembering or forgetting occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the remembering or forgetting of mental Content occurs.

name: Experience
definition_en: An event (or period of time standing in for events) that the Cognizer has experienced that leads to the Cognizer remembering the Content. 'Then I remembered from our summer together that he frowned on smoking.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The situation which surrounds a Cognizer remembering a Content or Topic.  'With the lights off, people can remember better.'

name: Sentient_entity
definition_en: The individual whose mind has a particular piece of Content in it, or, more generically portrayed, whose mind is focussed on a particular Topic.

name: Content
definition_en: The situation or state-of-affairs that the Sentient_entity's attention is focussed on.

name: Evidence
definition_en: The source of awareness or knowledge of the Content.

name: Topic
definition_en: A description of the kind of Content in the Sentient_entity's attention in terms of an idea which is salient throughout the Content.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the cognitive act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Sentient_entity that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Expressor
definition_en: Expressor is the body part that reveals the Sentient_entity's state to the observer.

name: Role
definition_en: The category that an element of the Content is considered to belong to.

name: Paradigm
definition_en: The system of knowledge which serves as the basis for the Sentient_entity's awareness.  'The formation of black holes should be understood in astrophysic terms.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which the Sentient_entity has the Content in their attention.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: This is the person (or people) to whom a mental property is attributed. The FE may be expressed as External Argument of a predicative use of the adjective, as a PP Complement, or as the head noun modified by an attributive use of the adjective:  'You were smart to save all your receipts.' 'It was smart of you to save all your receipts.' 'You are a smart person to save your receipts.'

name: Behavior
definition_en: The Behavior refers to any action, utterance, belief, or artifact thereof on the basis of which a mental property is attributed to the Protagonist. The meaning of the English word behavior should not be taken to constrain the identity of this frame element too much---conceptually, this frame element includes things that would not normally be described using the word behavior.  Note the following examples: 'That was a stupid mistake.' 'The manager made a few stupid remarks and then sat down.' 'What a stupid book!' 'It's stupid to think that everything will improve.'

name: Practice
definition_en: Some of the words in this frame have a slightly different use in that they evaluate someone only with respect to their mental performance in some particular domain or capacity.  We call this domain or capacity Practice. E.g., She is astute at math. Note that this does not mean she is considered to be astute in general for doing math. Rather, she is astute with respect to math, but may be dumb with respect to other things. These uses probably belong in a different frame with words such as skilled, but for the time being they are marked with the FE Practice. General Grammatical Observations:  The adjectives in this frame may exhibit Extraposition of a to-marked infinitive VP, with an optional Protagonist expressed in an of-PP: It was brilliant (of you) to invite the clowns to the party.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree marks the extent to which the Behavior or Practice is exhibited or attributed.  'Jenkins is far too astute to fall for that' 'She was a bit careless at adding drops.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner refers to the method or way in which the Mental_property is attributed to the Protagonist.  'It was not licence he wanted -- his goal was the forcible enlightenment of mankind.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The domain in which the Behavior or Protagonist has a given mental property. 'It was politically astute to decline the offer.'

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.  'To my mind, his dialogues with his Vietnamese counterpart were the most trenchant, astute and screamingly funny things Trudeau has ever done'

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the general area in which the emotion occurs.  It indicates a range of possible Stimulus.

name: Stimulus
definition_en: The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.

name: Empathy_target
definition_en: The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response.  In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus.  Quite often in such cases, the Stimulus can be inferred from the Circumstances

name: State
definition_en: The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Experiencer is has a feeling about the Stimulus.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The body part, gesture, or other expression of the Experiencer that reflects his or her emotional state.  They describe a presentation of the experience or emotion denoted by the adjective or noun.

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration is the amount of time for which the Experiencer is affected by the Stimulus, Topic, or State.</def-root >

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.

name: Stimulus
definition_en: The Stimulus is the person, event, or state of affairs that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.

name: Empathy_target
definition_en: The Empathy_target is the individual or individuals with which the Experiencer identifies emotionally and thus shares their emotional response.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the explanation for why the Stimulus evokes a certain emotional response.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Stimulus evokes its response.  In some cases it may appear without an explicit Stimulus.  Quite often in such cases, the Stimulus can be inferred from the Circumstances

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the Stimulus which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Experiencer  can be described as having said emotion.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Stimulus Stimulus affects the Experiencer.

name: Communicator
definition_en: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to another person.   'Her father never mentioned it.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee receives a Message from the Communicator.   'I mentioned it to him in direct terms.'

name: Message
definition_en: A proposition or set of propositions that the Communicator wants the Addressee to believe or take for granted.   'A CBS report did mention that the First Lady was required to wear a flak jacket for her safety.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.   'The report also mentioned contamination problems during the manufacture.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Communicator communicates.  'Her mother mentioned casually that Parr had gone to Belfast.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Communicator communicates.

name: Time
definition_en: When the the Message is mentioned.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration is the length of time during which the communication takes place.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times the Message is mentioned by the Communicator.  'I mentioned it fourteen times and it still wasn't enough.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Communicator mentions the Message.

name: Specified_content
definition_en: The relevant entity or state-of-affairs that the Communicator mentions.  'If someone mentions things like ration books , my stomach turns.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world when the Communicator mentions the Message or Specified_content.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Communicator communicates the Message.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Communicator mentions the Specified_content.

name: Force
definition_en: The Force is the body of soldiers that acts in military capacity for the Possessor. This FE is incorporated in each word in this frame.

name: Possessor
definition_en: The Possessor is the nation, institution, or individual who possesses and/or controls the Force.  'The American invasion, which drew 26000 American troops against General Noriega's army, was the largest US military operation since Vietnam.' 'Unfortunately, They don't have a very strong army.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Force.  'And while Serbia is keen to invest in its dilapidated armed forces, Montenegro wants to introduce a 4000-strong professional army.'

name: Members
definition_en: The consituent members of the Force.  'The US has an entirely citizen army.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain in which the Force operates.  'The Persians originally planned to rely solely on their land army to advance beyond Athens.' 'You seem to think that our intelligence and covert ops forces and our military are only able to conduct one mission at a time.'

name: Goal
definition_en: A (permanent or temporary) Goal of the Force.  'Right at this time of emergency, the revolutionary army made one attack after another in their rear, thus adding to their confusion.'

name: Period_of_existence
definition_en: The length of time that the particular military organization has existed.

name: Force
definition_en: The Force carries out the operation. Depending on the size of the operation, this may be as few as one individual or as large as the armed forces of a nation.  'He died while carrying out counter-IED operations.'  'US forces currently operating in Iraq are due to be recalled within the next several months.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: The Possessor controls the army and ultimately directs its goals and methods.

name: Area
definition_en: The Area in which the Military is conducting operations.

name: Opponent
definition_en: The nation, group, or situation which the operation opposes.  'Operations against Afghanistan continue to be carried out.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the operations are carried out.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time over which the operation is carried out.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the operation or participants that are not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Military that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the Military carries out its operation.

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain of the operation, e.g., military, intelligence.  'NATO forces are conducting military operations in highly volatile regions.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal of the operation.  'He was captured in a covert arrest operation carried out by an elite group of highly-trained Marines.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location of the operation.  'This sort of operation should only be conducted in open areas.'

name: Miner
definition_en: The Miner searches for mineral Resources.

name: Resource
definition_en: The Resource is usually buried in the ground, and is searched for by the Miner.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Miner searches for the Resource

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the Miner uses to obtain the Resource.

name: Outcome
definition_en: The success or failure of the attempt to obtain the Resource by the Miner.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Miner obtains the Resource.

name: Wrongdoer
definition_en: This is the person whose Misdeed is being judged with respect to its morality.

name: Misdeed
definition_en: The assessment of the Wrongdoer is based on his or her Misdeed.

name: Severity
definition_en: The Severity is the degree to which the Misdeed offends the moral sense of the Viewpoint.  'Such a grievous sin was not likely to go unpunished.'

name: Viewpoint
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which a Misdeed is performed.  'The misdeeds of the previous evening were all forgotten now.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where a Misdeed occurs.  'Sexual peccadilloes in the White House are one thing, lying before Congress quite another.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Wrongdoer is hoping to accomplish through their Misdeed.  'You sin merely to spit in the eye of your own creator!'

name: Means
definition_en: An action taken by the Wrongdoer which accomplishes the Misdeed.  'If they sin by ignoring the warnings of their elders, they are to blame for the consequences.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Misdeed which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Wrongdoer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).          'Many years of quiet transgressions later, he found he no longer knew if it was truly wrong.'

name: Injured_party
definition_en: An individual who is harmed by the Misdeed of the Wrongdoer.  'Sins against one's fellow man are the most egregious, though.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Wrongdoer commits the Misdeed.

name: Money
definition_en: Money is used as a medium of exchange.

name: Inherent_purpose
definition_en: The use for which the Money is intended or designed.

name: Creator
definition_en: The government (or possibly other organization) that mints, issues and guarantees the legal use of the Money.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which an Money comes into existence or begins to be circulated.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to the Money.

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Money.

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Money, including components, ingredients, etc.

name: Origin
definition_en: The process or means by which the Money comes to be possessed.  'It turns out that the company used drug money to develop this regionv'

name: Possessor
definition_en: The Possessor has control over the use the Money.  'They managed to scam him out of most of his cash.'

name: Evaluee
definition_en: This is the person whose Behavior is being judged with respect to its morality.  'It was honorable of Jackie to give up the position.'

name: Behavior
definition_en: The assessment of the Evaluee is based on his or her Behavior.  'Accepting that money was immoral of Lindsay.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the evaluation holds.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part which is the basis of the evaluation of morality. 'His face twisted into an evil grin'

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.   'Timothy McVeigh was, in my opinion, an evil and horrible man.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the entity that changes location. Note that it is not necessarily a self-mover. 'The explosion made me move in a hurry.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location the Theme occupies initially before its change of location.  'The policeman moved away from the door.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Theme travels  or to a landmark by which the Theme travels.  'Jo moved past Dad into the hall.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the location the Theme ends up in.  'The car moved into the slow lane.'

name: Area
definition_en: Area identifies the setting in which the Theme's movement takes place without a specified Path.  'Emily moved restlessly around the room.'

name: Distance
definition_en: Distance is any expression which characterizes the extent of the Motion.  'The twig floated atop the water for about 100 yards.'

name: Speed
definition_en: This FE is used for the Speed at which the Theme moves.  'The ash cloud drifted at twenty-five kilometres per hour.'

name: Carrier
definition_en: The Carrier is the means of conveyance of the Theme.  'The nest blew from its tree in a gale.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of  time for which the Motion takes place.  'The balloon floated for  hours.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Motion occurs.  'A radioactive cloud drifted across Britain after the fire at the Windscale nuclear factory.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Motion takes place. 'A naval airship drifted wildy in the stormy sea.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result identifies the ultimate effect of the Motion. 'The feathers floated together on the water's surface.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Theme while the motion is occuring.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the general area in which a specific motion (with Source, Path, or Goal) occurs.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Theme cross a boundary as it moves away from a Source region or into a Goal region.  'Pluto has moved fullyinto Sagittarius'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE is used for expressions that indicate motion along a line from the deitic center towards a reference point (which may be implicit) that is neither the Goal of the posture change nor a landmark along the way of the moving part of the body.  Often Direction is defined with reference to the canonical orientation of the Protagonist, or the orientation imposed by an implicit observer.

name: Purpose
definition_en: In cases wherein the Theme is construed as a sentient entity, this FE denotes the state of affairs that the entity wishes to bring about by moving.  'Johnny went to Langley  to turn himself in.'

name: Path_shape
definition_en: The shape of the overall Path travelled by the Theme.  'They drifted in circles for weeks before rescue .'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event that the described motion forms an integral part of.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Area
definition_en: This FE identifies the general Area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path.  'Soot-contaminated snow falls in Slovakia's mountainous regions.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the the state of the Theme during the motion.

name: Distance
definition_en: Distance identifies a phrase that characterizes the extent of motion of the Theme.  'The student plunged from a road bridge more than 100 feet to his death.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration is  used for the length of time for which the Motion takes place.  'In one storm , 46 inches of rain fell in 24 hours .'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the location the Theme ends up in (often unintentionally).  'The rivals both fell backwards into empty space.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Motion takes place.  'A few heavy spots of rain fell on the pavement like coins.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Theme travels  or to a landmark past which the Theme travels.  'The boys plummeted down the stairs into the basement.'

name: Speed
definition_en: This FE identifies the Speed at which the motion occurs.  'Michelle toppled slowly to the floor.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Motion occurs.  'In 1977 Nigel plunged to his death in his car on a mountain road in southern France.'

name: Carrier
definition_en: The Carrier is the means of conveyance of the Theme.  'Nigel plunged to his death in his car on a mountain road in southern France.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the entity that changes location.  'In 1977,  Nigel plunged to his death in his car on a mountain road in southern France.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location the Theme occupies before the Motion occurs.  'The man toppled from the passenger seat into the road.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the motion.   'Marie shoved Simon, and he toppled over.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where motion specified by Source, Path or Goal occurs. 'In the kitchen, the towel dropped onto the floor.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Theme crosses boundary as it enters a Goal region or exits a Source region.  'Sucking in a deep breath, he plunged fully into the cold water'

name: Point_of_contact
definition_en: This FE is used for expressing some part of the Theme participant that makes contact with a horizontal surface.   'With a loud thump, the monster fell on its back, the earth trembling as he hit the ground.'

name: Path_shape
definition_en: The shape formed by the path followed by the Theme.

name: Means
definition_en: An event whereby the motion of the Theme comes about.

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction of motion of the Theme.  Direction characterizes the Path of motion according to some system of orientation, most often that imposed by gravity.  'I hope your egg does n't fall down .'

name: Explanation
definition_en: Any state of affairs or event from which the particular direction motion logically follows.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state of affairs that the agentive Theme hopes to bring about by moving in a particular direction.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world as the action occurs.

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause describes the reason for the motion. 'The glasses clinked across the table during the tornado.'</def-root >

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the entity that changes location.  In sentences containing a Cause, the Theme is typically the NP Object.  In other sentences, the Theme is normally the External Argument.   'Pat crunched over the fresh snow.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of Motion.  'The train rumbled out of the station.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.  'The truck roared through the tunnel.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is any expression which tells where the Theme ends up as a result of the Motion.  'The plates clattered to the floor.'

name: Area
definition_en: This FE identifies the general Area in which motion takes place, used particularly if the motion is understood as following a complex or non-linear path.  'The fly buzzed about the room.'

name: Distance
