definition_en: The Distance is any expression which characterizes the extent of Motion.  This frame element occurs very infrequently with Motion_noise verbs.  'The car wheezed the two miles into town.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the motion occurs.  'My Saab purrs along easily at 80 miles an hour.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive indicates the state of the Theme during Motion.  'The car chugged across the ruts, unstoppable.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the way in which the Motion takes place.  'The drone buzzed curiously across the room and vanished behind the table.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Theme moves in the specified way.  'The autochopper whirred along by supplementing its onboard power with solar generators.'

name: Result
definition_en: The Result is the ultimate effect of the Motion.  'The door of the empty box creaked open in the wind.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Motion occurs.  'Suddenly , the pole thumped really hard into an unseen object.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place describes the location of a more specific motion (which has Source, Path, Goal, or Area).

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time for which the Theme moves under accompaniment of noise.  'From there they roared northward for about 10 minutes before turning up the beach approach onto A1.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the motion event takes place.  'The train screeched into the station at half past seven'</def-root >

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for the movement is ongoing.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the motion occurs.  'The truck moved at 10 o'clock.'

name: Area
definition_en: The Area is the setting in which the Theme's movement takes place.   'Emily rose to her feet and moved restlessly around the room.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: The Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.  'Pat accompanied me down the street.' 'The squirrel chased after the nut.'

name: Distance
definition_en: The Distance is any expression which characterizes the extent of motion.

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the location the Theme ends up in.  'The car accelerated and moved into the slow lane, as he passed.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path refers to (a part of the) ground that the Theme travels over or to a landmark the Theme travels past.  'The door opened , and he moved past Dad, into the hall.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location the Theme initially occupies before its change of location.  'The policeman moved away from the door.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which motion occurs.  'The car moved along at 55 miles per hour.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the entity that changes location.   'The explosion made me move in a hurry.'

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Theme is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Theme. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.

name: Theme
definition_en: A physical entity that is participating in non-translational motion.

name: Fixed_location
definition_en: The point or set of points that define the limits of motion for the Theme.  For spinning motions, it is the axis, for vibrating it is a boundary, for swinging it is a point. 'Balls spin on their axes .' 'The window vibrated in the frame.'

name: Periodicity
definition_en: The number of times the Theme returns to a state in a given duration. 'They spun it at 1000 rpms.'

name: Angle
definition_en: The amount of rotation that the Theme undergoes.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Theme is in bounded motion.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the bounded motion happens.

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction of rotation of the Theme. 'The dial rotated clockwise one revolution, then the vault opened.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes the way in which the Theme moves in place.</def-root >

name: Result
definition_en: The Result describes the end state brought about by the motion in place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Cause_external describes the force which sets into motion the motion. 'The strings vibrated with the impact of the wind.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the Theme during the action.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state of affairs that the agentive Theme hopes to bring about by moving.

name: Path_shape
definition_en: The shape formed by the path that the Theme follows.

name: Entity
definition_en: The entity that Speakers refer to by using the Name.

name: Name
definition_en: The linguistic expression by which Speakers refer to the Entity.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The person who uses the linguistic expression (Name) to refer to the Referent.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation of the intentional act. We did it for the hell of it.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. John flattered her to receive a raise.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Name_source
definition_en: This frame element is the person or thing whose name was chosen by the Speaker to give to the Entity.  They named their daughter Carol after Paul's grandmother.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An action the Speaker takes in order to accomplish the name conferral.  'When he was born they christened him by smashing a bottle of champagne against his arse'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity about whom it is asserted that they share a name with a Namesake.   ' Homer's mythical enchantress was a weaver, and so is her namesake'

name: Namesake
definition_en: The person or thing that has the same name as the Entity.  'Claire is her namesake'

name: Anchor
definition_en: A domain, often a place or time, in which the Namesake of the Entity is located.   'Karam is a member of the Parti Socialiste Guyanais (PSG), which has long been the strongest political party and is allied to its French namesake.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any temporary or permanent property  of the Namesake.  'Adalvard the younger  had visited and buried his elder namesake in 1060.'

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Salient parts of the  Locale.  'We drove through a mossy dell.'

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location that the Locale is a part of. 'John spent several years wandering the mountains of Romania.'

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Locale about. ' There is a glacial valley near here.'' There is a impact valley near here.'

name: Locale
definition_en: A stable bounded area.  It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.

name: Name
definition_en: This FE is used for the Names of Locales.  'Lake Constance' 'Pike's Peak' 'The Indonesian archipelago'

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Locale is located with respect to.  'All the mountains in America are small.'

name: Type
definition_en: The Type is the subtype of natural feature.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description, characteristic, or property of the Locale which is not covered by more specific FEs.  'That 's a long way down on such a steep cliff.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer requires or believes he/she requires the Requirement to hold so that the Dependent will occur.

name: Requirement
definition_en: The entity or state-of-affairs that must be present or obtain in order for the Dependent to obtain.

name: Dependent
definition_en: The state-of-affairs which cannot hold without the Requirement.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the conditions under which the Requirement is likely to be needed.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Dependent depends on the presence of the Requirement.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Cognizer requires the Requirement.  'I need that book now!'

name: Place
definition_en: The location of the Cognizer when he/she requires the Requirement.  'Over at Merv's house they need three more cement trucks to finish the job.'

name: Consequences
definition_en: An undesirable state-of-affairs that results if the Requirement is not met.  'He needs to focus on his schoolwork, or he's not going to pass the third grade.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times the Cognizer has a need per some unit of time.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason why the Cognizer needs the Requirement.

name: Negated_proposition
definition_en: The situation which is presented as false overall. The particular focus of negation which contrasts with the Factual_situation is not separately marked.  'She didn't know, rather she suspected.'  'She had not one, but two books on transcendentalism .'  'I did n't say anything , but rather paced all the more nervously .'

name: Factual_situation
definition_en: The situation or part of situation that actually pertains, in contradistinction to the profiled situation in the Negated_proposition that is asserted not to pertain.  In spoken language and casual written language, but not in normatively edited written texts, the Factual_situation may be expressed as an unmarked clause immediately preceding or following the Negated_proposition.  'She did n't know, rather she suspected .' 'She had not one, but two books on transcendentalism .' 'I did n't say anything , but rather paced all the more nervously .'

name: Profiled_possibility
definition_en: The situation presented explicitly as a possibility, contrasting with the implicit Negated_possibility.

name: Anti_consequence
definition_en: The situation that follows as a result of the Negated_possibility, and is not expected to occur if the Profiled_possibility holds.

name: Network
definition_en: The system functioning as a unit that is constituted by the Nodes and Connections.  'Efforts are underway to improve the road network in the state.'

name: Nodes
definition_en: The entities that are connected into a Network.  'The National Network of Libraries of Medicine is dedicated to making the world's biomedical information available throughout the US.'

name: Connections
definition_en: The relationships or physical entities that connect the Nodes.   'Every computer has its own cable to be connected straight to the server or by the network of cables and T-connectors. '

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any characterization or evaluation of the Network.  'But its ability to deliver these programs was severely compromised by its outdated computer network.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: A person or organization that possesses or owns the Network  or a larger entity of which the Network itself is a part.  'This file-swapping activity on a company's computer network exposes a company to legal risk.'

name: Noise_maker
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity or substance that is designed to produce sound.

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which an Noise_maker  is intended.

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Noise_maker into existence.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which a Noise_maker comes into existence.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to an Noise_maker.

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Noise_maker.

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Noise_maker, including components, etc.

name: Ground
definition_en: The location with which the Noise_maker is associated.

name: Term_1
definition_en: Term_1 is the first operand in the non-commutative arithmetic that is modified by Term_2 (e.g. subtracted by or divided by Term_2).

name: Term_2
definition_en: Term_2 is the second operand of the non-commutative arithmetic which modifies Term_1 (e.g. subtracts from or divides Term_1).

name: Calculator
definition_en: The Calculator is the agentive entity that combines Term_1 and Term_2.

name: Term_1
definition_en: Term_1 is the first operand in the non-commutative arithmetic that is modified by Term_2 (e.g. subtracted by or divided by Term_2).

name: Term_2
definition_en: Term_2 is the second operand of the non-commutative arithmetic which modifies Term_1 (e.g. subtracts from or divides Term_1).

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the non-commutative process combining Term_1 and Term_2.

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure.  'The cat is next to the mat.'

name: Figure
definition_en: The Figure is perceived as located relative to a certain Ground location. The figure can be an entity or an event.  'The cat is next to the mat.'

name: Accessibility
definition_en: An indication of how accessible the Figure is to some participant in the speech context (either the speaker or the addressee, or some other highly salient viewpoint in a narrative).  This FE normally describes availability for manipulation and use, but may simply describe how easily seen or difficult to see the Figure is. There is a closed class of items that can fill this slot, including only 'just' and 'right' indicating ease of access, and 'way' and 'all the way' indicating distance and difficulty of access.    'Oh yeah , the flashlight 's right by my handbag .'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure. This FE is filled by one of a closed class of adverbs: up, down, out (meaning 'beyond the boundary around the viewpoint'), off (meaning 'disconnect between landmark and figure'), back (meaning 'along a line from front to back of landmark, and relatively inaccessible'), and, more rarely, away, along, and dialectally, back down (meaning 'down and behind').   'The cat is hiding down under the porch.'

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the locative relation between Figure and Ground obtains.  'He was by the park on Friday.'

name: Distance
definition_en: This  FE identifies the  Distance between the Figure and the Ground.  This FE requires an image schema with a vector that extends from the Ground, or a subpart of the Ground, in some direction, and the Distance is measured along this vector from the Ground to the profiled region.    'Go 30 feet to the left of the pool.'  Note that a number of frequent adverbial targets identify the Ground, with the location of an implicit viewer, so Distance is effectively measured from the viewpoint location in these cases.  'We were already nearly 1000 meters ahead.'

name: Deixis
definition_en: An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder), or specifically separated from the speech context by distance or a barrier (over).  Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.  'It is lying here beside the chair.'

name: Directness
definition_en: An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target.  This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, directly, and due (and some combinations of these), but also occurs with rarer items like 'smack dab'.  'I ran right along the edge .'

name: Temporal_profile
definition_en: A description of how the access path to the Ground interacts with time.  This FE is filled only by the closed class of adverbials back.adv (which indicates that the position was occupied by the Figure before) and on.adv (which indicates a continued path).  While this FE in its most basic use refers to cases of actual motion, it can be used with descriptions of static position, in which case it either refers to fictive, imagined motion, or it backgrounds motion entirely (as in the example below).  'They finally moved back east.'

name: Origin
definition_en: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

name: Person
definition_en: The Person is a non-participant in a Conflict.  'Don't shoot -- I'm just a civilian!'

name: Persistent_characteristic
definition_en: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.

name: Age
definition_en: The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.

name: Ethnicity
definition_en: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.

name: Context_of_acquaintance
definition_en: An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.

name: Conflict
definition_en: The Conflict in which the Person is not fighting.  'Jones was a noncombatant in WWII.'

name: Type
definition_en: The kind of thing which is notable. This may be an event, place, item, or role and is plural.  'Shakespeare is one of the great poets.'  'The Four Seasons is a notable hotel.'  '"Green Eggs and Ham" is one of the great children's books.'  'The US civil war is perhaps the most notable of the US's wars.'

name: Name
definition_en: The name of the notable entity.  'Shakespeare is one of the great poets.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time during which the entity is considered notable.  'Bob Dylan is among the most notable musicians of the 20th century.'

name: Place
definition_en: The geographic area in which the entity is considered notable.  'Dumas is one of the most notable authors in France.'

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing the deviation of the individual of a certain Type from the norm of that Type.

name: Arraign_authority
definition_en: The judge or other authority of the court in which the accused person is arraigned.

name: Accused
definition_en: The person being charged with an offense against the law.

name: Charges
definition_en: The crime with which the Accused is charged

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: The larger event which contains the Notification of Charges event. 'Seven people have been indicted in the seven-year investigation.'

name: Element
definition_en: A substance definable in terms of the kind(s) of atoms that make it up.

name: Final_element
definition_en: The type of Element that results from the process.

name: Initial_element
definition_en: The type of Element that begins the process.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Element undergoes the transformation.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Change event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Element's substance is converted to the Final_element.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The physical or abstract Circumstances under which the change takes place.

name: Cause
definition_en: An event or state that causes the change to take place.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the nuclear process occurs.

name: Influencing_entity
definition_en: A thing or person whose behavior has an effect on an Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.   ' Much of the acreage in this round is closer to the coastline, and as such has many implications in terms of how it could impact upon fish spawning, local bird life, and even the Ministry of Defence in some cases'

name: Dependent_entity
definition_en: An entity, usually a thing, that is influenced in its behavior by an Influencing_entity or an Influencing_situation.  'The Committee is responsible for making recommendations to the Board regarding the group's activities as they impact on the environment.'

name: Influencing_variable
definition_en: A scalar variable (with unspecified value) which has  an effect on the Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.  ' Factors which influence the stability of the combination include the softness of the car and the trailer's suspension, plus the balance of the trailer.'

name: Dependent_situation
definition_en: A situation that whose temporal or other characteristics are influenced by an Influencing_entity, Influencing_situation, or Influencing_variable.  'The new network file system server line supports database or backup applications running alongside NFS input/output operations without one activity impacting another.'

name: Dependent_variable
definition_en: A scalar variable, whose value depends on the behavior of an Influencing_entity, a Influencing_situation, or an Influencing_variable.  'This kind of elementary boo-boo would certainly impact video speed.'

name: Influencing_situation
definition_en: A situation whose temporal or other characteristics have an effect on a Dependent_entity, Dependent_situation, or Dependent_variable.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Influencing_entity effects the Dependent_entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the influence occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the influencing occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Influencing_entity that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A Descriptor gives additional information about the influence. It may be affecting, as with 'positive impact on GDP'; or not, as in 'potential (or possible) influence of SSRIs on metabolism'. Descriptors are typically adjective phrases. 'Many illicit substances can have a strong, negative impact on the body.'

name: Responsible_party
definition_en: The person who must perform the Duty.

name: Duty
definition_en: The action that the Responsible_party is obligated to perform.

name: Condition
definition_en: This FE indicates the Conditions under which the Responsible_party is obligated to perform the Duty .

name: Consequence
definition_en: The undesirable Consequence that will result if the Duty is not performed.

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which the Responsible_party is obligated to fulfill the Duty.

name: Place
definition_en: A location in which the Responsible_party has a specified Duty .  'I almost forgot to tell you that in Sweden we are obligated to spend atleast 7.5 months in the army for training.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The deviation of the requirement from the norm.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The desirable situation which can be brought about by fulfilling the Duty.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity which is not widely known and rather obscure.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the degree of fame of the Entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is not well known.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity is considered not to be famous.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason that the Entity is not famous.  'Some tech companies are little known because they mostly operate behond the scenes.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time during which the Entity is not famous.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity is not famous.  'Certain academic works are obscure only in North America.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The entity or facts that are undeniable given the Evidence.  'It is obvious for example that 9/10 is not the same as 1.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The gradable aspect of a Phenomenon which concerns how likely it is that the Phenomenon be known. This frame element is incorporated by the lexical units in this frame.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Phenomenon from the norm or from the value for another Phenomenon in terms of how likely the Phenomenon would be known.  'It is abundantly obvious you have not a clue how the Retro Program works.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Phenomenon is obvious  'It is obvious now that Senator O. T. Tawa has no plan.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the conditions under which the Phenomenon is likely to be known.

name: Perceiver
definition_en: The sentient entity for whom perception or cognition of the Phenomenon is judged to be more or less likely.  'It was obvious to Peter he had made a wise choice.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: A state-of-affairs  that has a bearing on whether the Phenomenon will be perceived or apprehended cognitively. Evidence is often metonymically indicated by the mention of an entity whose existence or whose properties are relevant.   'It is usually obvious from the context which meaning is appropriate.'  Some lexical units such as visible, audible etc. which refer directly to perception in a particular modality incorporate the Evidence frame element.

name: Group
definition_en: The likelihood of a Phenomenon to be observed perceptually or cognitively in a particular Group of comparable background items may be contrasted, implicitly or explicitly,  with different groups.  'This correlation was obvious in patients classified as acute myeloid leukemia (AML)as well as in the monocytic varieties of ANLL.'

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: The physical location of a Perceiver of the Phenomenon or a metaphorical point-of-view location of a cognizer relative to the Phenomenon.  'It is obvious from here  that the crux of the climb is the ascent up to the southern peak. '

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Direction
definition_en: This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver (see above), that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception.   'The top of the mountain showed through the mist'

name: Rank
definition_en: The Rank which the Item occupies.

name: Item
definition_en: The Item which occupies the Rank in the hierarchy.

name: Dimension
definition_en: The dimension along which the ranking is defined.   'He ranks second in his class in mathematics.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which/period over which the Item occupies the Rank 'Jim ranked as thirty-second degree Mason in 1970.'

name: Comparison_set
definition_en: The Comparison_set is the set of entities ranked in a hierarchy.  The Item is a member of the set.  'He ranks highest among his peers in the field of basket weaving.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE broadly picks out the degree of offense. 'She faces conviction on three counts of first-degree murder.' 'Aggravated assault is usually considered a felony.'

name: Specification
definition_en: The Specification is an additional aspect of the main crime being commited. 'He was charged with assault causing actual bodily harm.' 'The prosecutors decided to go with arson with intent to harm.'

name: Offense
definition_en: The illegal act. 'He was charged with assault.'

name: Victim
definition_en: This FE denotes the person or entity that is badly affected by the Offense. 'The police is investigating the homicide of Dr. Johnson.'

name: Punishment
definition_en: This FE denotes the Punishment that is specified by the statute in which the offense is defined. 'Suicide is a felony punishable by four years in prison.'

name: Perpetrator
definition_en: The individual who commits the Offense

name: Offerer
definition_en: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and offers it to the Potential_recipient .

name: Potential_recipient
definition_en: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The object which is offered for transfer.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Offerer offers the Theme to the Potential_recipient.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Offerer offers the Theme to the Potential_recipient.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Offerer offers the Theme to the Potential_recipient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Offerer offers the Theme to the Potential_recipient.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Offerer offers the Theme to the Potential_recipient.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the manner in which the Offerer offers the Theme to the Potential_recipient.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the conditions under which the Theme is offered.   'I offer my services free of charge.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The Potential_recipient's intended purpose for the Theme.  'Plesae offer a list of people for potential promotion.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the Offerer, Potential_recipient, or Theme given independently of the giving event per se.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the offer began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Original_body
definition_en: The body from which the Offshoot is derived.

name: Branch
definition_en: The offshoot or branch of the original body which differs from it in some important respect.

name: Place
definition_en: The place in which the Branch is locate or where it first forms.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Branch forms or thrives.

name: Predictive_phenomenon
definition_en: Predictive_phenomenon provides evidence for the existence or the nature of the Outcome of Future_phenomenon.  'To achieve so much this year augurs well for the future.'

name: Future_phenomenon
definition_en: Future_phenomenon is that phenomenon that is predicted to occur or have a particular quality.  'This move presages a freeze on the granting of new concessions.'

name: Outcome
definition_en: The FE Outcome identifies those expressions that indicate how the Future_phenomenon is expected to turn out based on the evidence of the Predictive_phenomenon.  'It all bodes well for the future.'

name: Interested_party
definition_en: Interested_party marks expressions that indicate people who are interested in the Outcome of the Future_phenomenon.  'That Meisel speaks so highly of Kate bodes well  for her.'

name: Strength
definition_en: The degree to which the Predictive_phenomenon predicts the occurrence of the Future_phenomenon.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the omen is occuring.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Predictive_phenomenon is an omen for the Future_phenomenon or the Outcome.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Predictive_phenomenon indicates a particular Future_phenomenon or Outcome.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where something good or bad might occur.  'The storm bodes ill for you here .'

name: Entity
definition_en: The part of the Organism which is undergoing biological development.    'The development of a human embryo is fascinating to study.'

name: Organism
definition_en: The living thing whose Entity is undergoing development.  'Rachel studies nervous system development in apes.'

name: Prior_state
definition_en: The stage from which the Entity develops.  'She grew from a child to a teenager in what seemed like minutes.'

name: Post_state
definition_en: The state into which the Entity develops.  'She watched her baby grow into an adult.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Entity develops.  'Someday this bud will grow into a rose.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Entity develops.  'You can see the partial development of the fingers on the ultrasound.. '

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant dimension of development.  Usually expressed by an entity-denoting adjective.  ' Embryonic development had been stunted by the disease. '

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the development occurs.  'The cells are developing normally.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity develops.  'The cells were developing rapidly in the Petri dish.'

name: Rate
definition_en: The Rate at which the Entity develops.  'The cells were developing rapidly. '

name: Duration
definition_en: The period over which the Entity develops.  'The tissue grew rapidly throughout the evening.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme whose motion is blocked or free.

name: Useful_location
definition_en: The place or thing that the Theme is headed towards, despite a potential or actual Barrier.

name: Barrier
definition_en: An entity that (at least potentially) prevents the Theme from getting to the Useful_location.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which a Theme can easily access the Useful_location

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Useful_location is or is not accessible.  'This door is closed every Monday.'

name: Driver
definition_en: This is the being, typically human, that controls the Vehicle as it moves.  'Kim drove my old car cross-country.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: This is the means of conveyance controlled by the Driver.  It may move in any way or medium.  With verbs, Vehicle is usually expressed as Object:  'I drove my car to Canada.'

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion.  With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.  'Kim drove out of town.'  'Kim drove away.'

name: Path
definition_en: Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. This includes directional expressions and "middle of path'' expressions, e.g.: 'The bikers rode through the desert.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Any expression which tells where the moving object(s) ends up as a result of the motion expresses the frame element Goal. Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance.  'Kim drove into the parking lot.' 'Kim drove in.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.   'The bikers rode recklessly through the desert.' 'The bikers rode haltingly over the rough terrain.'

name: Distance
definition_en: Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance. 'The bikers rode hundreds of miles.'

name: Area
definition_en: This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Locative setting adjuncts of motion expressions may also be assigned this frame element. 'The bikers rode all over the place.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Driver or Vehicle during the Transportation. 'I was flying blind.' 'Murray drove the car, still unpainted, right through the store front.'

name: Event
definition_en: An event that the Driver is also participating in while directing the Vehicle. 'How long have you flown combat missions?'

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by the Driver by which the Driver achieves directed Transportation. 'I managed to bike home by holding the left handlebar in my teeth!'

name: Result
definition_en: Result of the Driver's action.

name: Cotheme
definition_en: This is a second moving object, expressed as a PP headed by with.

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the Vehicle moves.

name: Route
definition_en: The Route is the road or path that the Vehicle regularly travels on. 'United Airlines flies the London-New York route.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE indicates the Circumstances under which the operation of the Vehicle takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place describes the location of a more specific motion (which has Source, Path or Goal).

name: Duration
definition_en: The length  of the time interval during which the Driver operates the Vehicle.  'Henry would bike through  the woodsfor hours in all kinds of weather'

name: Time
definition_en: The  Time when the Driver operates the Vehicle  'Yesterday, Smithers paddled his boat across the lake and back'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Vehicle crosses a boundary or the extent to which the Vehicle completes a course.  'Sylvie paddled completely around the breakwater' 'Eugenedrove completely off the highway and turned the engine off'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Driver tries to bring about by the way that they direct the Vehicle.  'I bike to work to save money.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Operate_vehicle event occurs.

name: Frequency
definition_en: "How often" the Operate_vehicle event occurs.

name: Operator
definition_en: The Operator maneuvers the Vehicle.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The Vehicle is directed to move by the Operator

name: Source
definition_en: The starting-point of motion.

name: Path
definition_en: Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. This includes directional expressions and "middle of path'' expressions, e.g.:

name: Goal
definition_en: Where the Vehicle ends up as a result of motion.

name: Area
definition_en: This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path. Locative setting adjuncts of motion expressions may also be assigned this frame element.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the operation takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the operation takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the vehicle operation  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Operator that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An action which enables the Operator to operate the Vehicle, or which more directly causes the Vehicle to operate.

name: System
definition_en: The entity that  the Operator gets to perform its intended function.   'Robert Faye, who has run the organization since its inception in 1991, said all the money the group has raised has been properly distributed.'

name: Operator
definition_en: The invididual who manipulates the substructure of the System.  'WELS Kingdom Workers operates this program for students interested in doing ministry for a summer job.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Operator runs the System.  'North Korea Operates a Restaurant in Vietnam.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Operator runs the System.  'The City operates the system to ensure high quality water at competitive rates.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Operator runs the System.  'This guaranteed donation to the charity was begun by Eric Von Stroh, Mike Cioli and Andrew Seligson, the three men who ran the business last year.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Operator runs the System.   'By the end of the film you'll be marveling at Buster's dexterity while he operates the steamboat by climbing up and over or jumping down and around the ship.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the running of the System  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Operator that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'The farm is owned and carefully operated by John and Janice Maloney in Newberry Springs, California.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of the time interval in which the Operator runs the System.  'The vendor has operated this business for the last 7 years.'

name: Tester
definition_en: The person who uses  the Product to see if it is intact or to ascertain its characteristics during operation.   'I just wish we could have tested the car with a manual gearbox, instead of the five-speed automatic'

name: Product
definition_en: The entity that the Tester uses  to ascertain whether it is intact.

name: Unwanted_characteristics
definition_en: An entity or property whose presence would impair the acceptability or usefulness of the Product.  'To ensure that the remedy is complete, nCipher have fully reviewed the software and tested it for similar errors.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE is used for a Means action which the Tester   carries out in testing the Product.   'How we tested the Radeon 9700 Pro video-card.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Tester intends to accomplish subjecting the Product to a test of its functioning.   'Once you have copied your site and have tested it to make sure it works normally, you're ready to pull out the scalpel and start hacking away.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Tester uses the Product in order to evaluate its functioning.  'Engineers carefully tested the fields of view to make sure that security personnel would be able to view all critical areas.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the extent  to which the Tester examines the Product.

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: This FE is the position of the Tester during the act of testing.  Typically, it is expressed in a from-PP.

name: Desired_state_of_affairs
definition_en: The desirable state of affairs which the Tester hopes to find to obtain when using the Product.   'Test-Driven Development requires you to set an expectation of a result and then test that the result is achieved.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Tester uses  the Product to evaluate its functioning.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The FE Circumstances is used for circumstances that obtain during the test procedure. These are typically relevant to how the Product functions.  'We tested the drive using the generic drivers of the OS.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of the time period during which the Tester continuously or repeatedly operates the Product to determine its operational characteristics.   'Before launching BioCheck, we  tested the system for a year in Washington DC in response to more than 50 actual 9-1-1 calls.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the test is carried out.  'We tested the product in California first.'

name: Function
definition_en: A  use to which the Product is put .  'If you have HTML files from another source and you can't first read them into Microsoft Word, you can try the process, but I haven't tested it for that use. '

name: Tested_property
definition_en: A variable of behavior of the Product which is specifically evaluated.  ' ILCSO staff have tested the behavior of the ILCSO-standard version of WebVoyage with several browsers.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the testing event began to be repeated to when it stopped.  'This approach has been tested since 2001.'

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the Operational_testing.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person whose Opinion is in question.   'My take is that Johnson will not actually make it to the last round .' 'Everyone is entitled to their opinion .'

name: Opinion
definition_en: The Cognizer's way of thinking, which is not necessarily generally accepted, and which is generally dependent on the Cognizer's point of view.  'My take is that it is a version of the Macbeth story - what happens when people become violent but cannot quite handle it.' 'Svetlana knew that it was Sergei's view that the Berlin crises were merely a charade which it was necessary for both sides to enact and re-enact every few years.' 'Her child-like portrayal only manages to live up to the other characters' view of her as the deranged little sister.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: The events or states-of-affairs that form the basis for the Cognizer's Opinion.  'From what I've seen so far, my opinion is that it won't really matter.'

name: Topic
definition_en: A phenomenon that the Cognizer is considering with respect to their Opinion.  Note that this extra-thematic frame element occurs freely with nouns, but only in very restricted contexts with verbs.  'My opinion about that Tigers' win is that it was completely bogus.'

name: Constancy
definition_en: The level of firmness with which the Cognizer holds an opinion.  It refers to the amount of convincing that they would need to change their mind.  'I really think that you should reconsider.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of how the Cognizer holds an opinion which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quiet(ly)), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Cognizer that also affect their thinking (presumptuous(ly), cold(ly)).   'She quietly held the belief that it was he that had betrayed the rebellion.'

name: Role
definition_en: Role describes the presuppositional terms of the Opinion by placing the Topic or the Cognizer of the Opinion into a category.  'My opinion of her as a brother isn't important anymore.' 'Your take on it as a political event is not in question at this time.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The aspects of the Opinion (and its Topic, if any) which are under consideration.  'We seemed to have two quite different moral views about this situation.' 'Noone could take seriously Dr. Furst's ill-advised medical opinion that Terry was still alive.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Cognizer has the Opinion.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Opportunity
definition_en: The situation during which the Desirable_situation is possible. For nominal LUs, this is generally in the second layer and contains the target.

name: Agent
definition_en: The sentient agent that may or may not participate in the Desirable_situation.

name: Desirable_situation
definition_en: A situation or event that the Agent can participating in during the period of the Opportunity.

name: Image
definition_en: The optical representation of the Source.

name: Source
definition_en: The entity from which the Image's form is based on.

name: Type
definition_en: The kind of entity that the Item belongs to.  'Capitalizes the first letter of the first word in each sentence'

name: Starting_point
definition_en: A usually spatial reference point from which the implicit cognizer scans across the members of the Comparison_set.  'Yes, I covered the cycle issue in  the second paragraph from the top.'

name: Basis_of_order
definition_en: A kind of event in which the members of the Comparison_set, including the Item, participate in a certain order.  'Lorna was the third student to be expelled from the Academy.'

name: Item
definition_en: The entity picked out by the implicit cognizer as occupying a certain place in the ordered Comparison_set.   'Bennett is the fifth woman to be showcased.' 'Bennett is the fifth woman to be showcased.'

name: Comparison_set
definition_en: A set of entites of which the Item is a member and which are ordered either by the Basis_of_order or by the order in which the implicit cognizer focuses attention on them.  'The first student of the college to cross the ramp will present the name-card reader with a card having the name of the college printed on it. .'

name: Organization
definition_en: The entity of which the individuals are Members.

name: Members
definition_en: A person belonging to an Organization.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason for which an Organization is formed.

name: Period_of_existence
definition_en: The interval during which the Organization exists.

name: Name
definition_en: A name given to the Organization for identification.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location or political locale that the Organization is contained within.  'Or, if you want to work on women's human rights issues, work for a Canadian organization that advocates on behalf of women.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE describes the general location where the Organization operates, but does not indicate the possessor of the Organization.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description of the Organization not covered by a more specific frame element.

name: Entity
definition_en: The item whose Origin is under discussion.

name: Origin
definition_en: The place or culture where the Entity was produced.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the person or sentient entity that experiences or feels the emotions.

name: Other
definition_en: The Other is the person that evokes the emotional response in the Experiencer.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Experiencer's emotion deviates from the norm for the emotion.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the explanation for why the Other evokes a certain emotional response.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances is the condition(s) under which the Other evokes its response.

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer experiences the feelings of the Other.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the way in which the Experiencer experiences the feelings of the Other which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  Manner may also describe a state of the Experiencer that affects the details of the emotional experience.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Experiencer feels for the Other.

name: Situation
definition_en: The  Situation is the circumstances or topic about which the Experiencer feels an emotion.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Other gets sympathy from the Experiencer.

name: Entity
definition_en: Concrete or abstract entity that does not exist after the event.

name: Place
definition_en: This is the Place where the Entity (saliently) does not exist.

name: Time
definition_en: A point at which the Entity (saliently) does not exist.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE labels the Explanation of the destruction or disappearance of the Entity.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the length of time before the Entity comes into existence again.

name: Role
definition_en: The aspect of the Entity which no longer exists.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Entity disappears.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Offender
definition_en: This FE denotes the offender that seeks or gets the pardon.  'Defense minister Ivanov rules out pardon for Chechen rebel leader Maskhadov.'

name: Authority
definition_en: Authority is the organization or person taht grants the pardon.  'The governement issued a pardon to the two convicts.'

name: Offense
definition_en: This FE denotes the the illegal act that the Offender is pardoned for.  'They demanded a pardon to John for inadverdent manslaughter.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: Explanation is the cause for pardoning an Offender. 'He appealed for a pardon on the grounds such as ill-health.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE denotes the time when the pardon is given  'The families demanded a posthumous pardon for the executed soldiers.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Authority  that accomplishes the pardon.   'But Queen Mary, pitied his youth and pardoned him by a bill addressed to her chancellor, Stephen Gardener from St.James's, on 18th March 1554.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the act of pardon which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of an Authority that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the pardoning takes place.  'On 1 March 2002, Andreyev was found guilty of libel and conditionally sentenced to two years in prison and then pardoned in the courtroom.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Authority intends to accomplish by pardoning  'U.S. research on biologicals started in World War II and was greatly augmented by captured Japanese research and scientists, who were pardoned to help the U.S. efforts.'

name: Orientation
definition_en: This is a property of the Part that determines the portion of the Part.

name: Whole
definition_en: An undivided entity having all its Parts.'The show takes place on the western edge of town.'

name: Part_prop
definition_en: A property relating to the Part of a Whole.'Sue painted the longer edges of the dollhouse.'

name: Part
definition_en: Part is that which forms a boundary between the Whole and what is not the object.

name: Part
definition_en: This element describes the Part of the larger Whole.'She only ate the skin of the apple.'

name: Whole
definition_en: An undivided entity having all its Parts.'She eats only the thick skin of the banana.'

name: Part_prop
definition_en: A property relating to the Part of a Whole.'Sue ate the thick shell of the pistachio.'

name: Ordinality
definition_en: This is the number of the sequence of Parts.' I sat through the first interminable act of the play . '

name: Part_prop
definition_en: A property relating to the Part of a Whole. ' I sat through the first interminable act of the play . '

name: Part
definition_en: A part of a larger Whole. ' I sat through the first interminable act of the play . '

name: Whole
definition_en: An undivided entity having all its Parts. ' I sat through the first interminable act of the play . '

name: Part
definition_en: A piece of a larger Whole.'The top shelf of the bookcase was lying on the floor.'

name: Part_prop
definition_en: A property relating to the Part of a Whole.'The white-painted front of the house had 2 black doors.'

name: Whole
definition_en: An undivided entity having all its Parts.'The show takes place in the West wing of the White House.'

name: Piece
definition_en: A Piece made of a substance.'Sergey had a few morsels of bread for breakfast.' The specific whole entity from which the Piece comes is not specified. Thus, the following sentence is not in frame: A piece of the TV fell of the floor.

name: Piece_prop
definition_en: A property relating to the Piece.'Sue had a big piece of cake.'

name: Substance
definition_en: The Substance is what the Piece is made of and may describe the type of larger whole from which it came.'Sue ate a big piece of cake.'

name: Part
definition_en: A Part of a larger Whole.'Sergey had  half of the pizza for breakfast.'

name: Whole
definition_en: An undivided entity having all its Parts. 'Sergey had  half of the pizza for breakfast.'

name: Part_prop
definition_en: A property relating to the Part of a Whole.'Sue painted a big section of the room.'

name: Orientation
definition_en: This is a property of the Part that determines the portion of the Part.  'Abby ate only the top half of the cake . '

name: System
definition_en: A system of organization of the Parts within the Whole, of which a Part is identified with a Name .

name: Name
definition_en: A label applied to a Part of a Whole in order to identify the Part within some System.

name: Decision_maker
definition_en: This Frame Element marks the person whose objectivity in making assesment is being evaluated.  'The referee was totally biased against our team. '

name: Side_1
definition_en: This Frame Element marks one of the Sides in a dispute or one of the alternatives in a situation of choice.'The umpire was partial to the home team.'

name: Sides
definition_en: This Frame Element marks phrases jointly expressing both Sides in a dispute or all of the alternatives in a situation of choice.'The judge was neutral between the parties.'

name: Side_2
definition_en: The second-mentioned of the Sides to a dispute or alternatives in a situation of choice.'The judge favored the defendant over the plaintiff.'

name: Domain
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions of a Domain or parameter with respect to which the Judge exhibits bias or lack thereof.'The judge was politically biased against the defendant.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that tell to what extent the Judge exhibited or lacked bias.'The referee was totally biased against the Giants.'

name: Manifestation_of_bias
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate how the bias of the Judge expresses itself in their behavior or actions.'The judge made a biased decision.''The referee was partial when he called all those fouls.'

name: Dispute
definition_en: The Dispute is the situation in which there is some conflict between two sides. ' My sister remained neutral in our disputes.'

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for the partiality.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE denotes the time when the partiality occurs.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part which indicates the character of the Decision_maker.  'He had a neutral smile on his face.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the way in which the Decision_maker embodies the bias associated with him or her.  'He was cooly impartial towards the matter.'

name: Participants
definition_en: The individuals or entities that have been participants in an Event.  'Thereafter, everybody participated in the 17 May parade ending in the Nordic Club.'

name: Participant_1
definition_en: Participant_1 is the grammatically more prominent participant in an Event with multiple Participants.  'Last year, Bill participated in the Montana State University Earth Systems Science distance learning course in the Atmosphere Unit.'

name: Participant_2
definition_en: A grammatically less prominent participant of an Event with multiple Participants.  'The Second Amended Complaint alleges that Andrew S. Pitt ("Pitt"), Conectisys Corporation ("Conectisys" or the "Company"), and BM Capital Corp. participated with Zaman and Smith Benton in a fraudulent and manipulative trading scheme.'

name: Event
definition_en: An Event with multiple Participants, who may or may not be involved intentionally.  'Some who participated in D-Day are finally ready to talk about it'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the multiple-participant Event occurs.  'A survey of students who participated last year showed that 61 percent would be the first in their family to attend college.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Event involving multiple Participants occurs.  'The most exciting tours for Mr. Osako were when he participated  in France, Belgium, Holland, Cuba and Japan.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). When the Participants are understood agentively frames, it may indicate salient characteristics of them that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).   'He had performed well on the varsity wrestling team and participated eagerly in student government'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Participants or Participant_1 intend to accomplish by performing the action indicated by the Event.  'Mahoney participated in order to protest racism in the United States in general.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by Participant_1 or the Participants that contributes to bringing off the Event.   'WICS-TV participated by handing out pamphlets, corporate job opening lists and other information regarding employment opportunities within the broadcasting field. '

name: Degree_of_involvement
definition_en: The extent to which Participant_1 contributes to the Event's coming off.   'We built a new hospital here in 1991, but I was on the board then and only peripherally involved.'

name: Institution
definition_en: A group, location, or institution conventionally associated with an Event.  'Several of the countries were unable to participate in the market .'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE describes the length of time for which participation occurs (usually appears as a for-PP)

name: Subset
definition_en: A Subset belonging to  the Group.

name: Group
definition_en: The Group of entities which includes the Subset.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the one who passes the Theme.  The Agent is generally realized as the External Argument.  'Pat passed me the ball.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The FE Theme is generally an NP Object that is passed to the Recipient.  'Pat passed the ball to the goalie.'

name: Source
definition_en: The FE Source is the starting point of the passing action  'Pat passed the ball from behind the defensemen.'

name: Path
definition_en: The FE Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal.  'I passed him the ball over the wall.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: The FE Recipient is the entity which possesses the Theme as a result of the passing.  'Kim passed the salt to her mother.'

name: Distance
definition_en: The FE Distance is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme.  'Pat passed the ball 50 meters to me.'

name: Area
definition_en: The FE Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which passing takes place when the passing is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element.  'The team passed the ball around the court.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of a participant during the passing action. 'We passed the ball around, gleeful.'

name: Means
definition_en: The FE Means indicates the action that is taken that results in the motion of the Theme

name: Manner
definition_en: The FE Manner is any expression which describes a property of the motion of the Theme which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, and other things count as Manner expressions.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity saliently involved in the transmission of force from an Agent to a Theme.  It may be the Agent's bodypart, or some kind of device.  'When playing basketball, you should pass with both hands.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the general area that provides a setting for a specific motion (with Source, Path, or Goal).  'The players passed the ball to each other at the park.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the passing of the Theme occurs.

name: Result
definition_en: A resultant state that the Theme is in at the end of its motion.   'The center passed the ball clear of the double-team.'

name: Initial_state
definition_en: A previous state that the Theme was in before the beginning of its motion.  'Paul passed the ball away from the danger of the double-team.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person who acts in a misleading way to create the impression that the Item is a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.  'Most recently, Grant Palmer has palmed himself off as a high-placed "insider" in the Church.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the passing off event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that contributes to the Item being perceived as a (particular kind of) Simulated_entity.

name: Item
definition_en: The Item is the concrete or abstract entity that the Agent misleadingly represents as a particular (kind of) Entity.  'From all reports Muhammad passed the child off as his son and behaved accordingly.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by passing the Item off as a (particular kind of) Simulated_entity.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the passing-off event logically follows.

name: Simulated_entity
definition_en: The Simulated_entity is a particular individual or a token of a particular type that the Item is represented as.  'The colleague who stole your idea and passed it off as her own? '

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location that is the setting for the passing off event.  'In London she passed herself off as a rich American heiress.'

name: Audience
definition_en: The Audience denotes the people that the Agent intends to mislead into thinking that the Item is a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.  'Ritchie passed it off to them as his own original thinking.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Agent gives the impression that the Item is the Simulated_entity.

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of the Road. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.   'The Way descends from the City of the Peak through a dense forest.'

name: Path
definition_en: The trajectory that would be followed by one moving on the Road.  'Valencia angles across the number streets.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Any expression which tells where the fictive mover travelling along a Road would end up.   'Where does Interstate 80 enter the city ?'

name: Road
definition_en: A physical path that a virtual moving entity can be imagined to travel along. The bike trail zigzagged through the woods.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of the kind of motion a hypothetical mover would have (including steadiness, grace, and general comparisons) count as Manner expressions.    'Drifting clouds lent a mystical touch while the narrow road twisted crazily through ancient stone villages on the valley floor.'

name: Distance
definition_en: Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.   'The thin line of dirt and gravel wound another ten miles and on into the Ozarks before it petered out completely.'

name: Area
definition_en: This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path.    'The paths crisscrossed the desert.'  Note that this FE should not be used for any locational modifier which would occur just as naturally with a non-motion predicate, like speech.

name: Degree
definition_en: Extent to which the described configuration deviates from the norm for a Road.  'The road bent slightly before resuming its long, straight march to the sea .'

name: Means
definition_en: An state of affairs involving the Road that allows the Road to be in the specified configuration.  'As the Condell Road the route skirts the northside of Limerick by passing through Westfield's bird sanctuary on the north bank of the River Shannon.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which an imaginary traveler on the Road would move.  'The road quickly drops after passing the final turn.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the character of the Road.  'The trail snaked down the mountainside, arduous and nearly impassable.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.  'In the mountains, Highway 60 winds and swerves a lot, so we lost a couple of hours from my estimate.'

name: Path_shape
definition_en: The configuration formed by the entire Path along the Road. 'The cavern descended in a spiral.'

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction in which a "fictive" mover would travel along a Road.  'The pass dips down about 2000 feet, and then back up again.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the fictive motion takes place.  This may describe the time when the Road or a particular piece of the Road existed, or it may implicitly describe the time when an actual motion event occurred on the Road.  'Thousands of years ago, the Roman roads criss-crossed this landscape.' 'After it reached the edge of the forest, the road slanted upwards and grew rough.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Road brings about by being in a particular configuration.  'The roadwound around in order to circumvent the house..'

name: Path
definition_en: The series of interconnected locations that the Theme traverses.  'In insects, blood is confined to vessels during only a portion of its circuit through the body.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is one of the Endpoints treated as a source.  'The Cassini spacecraft will travel 3.5 billion kilometers (2.175 billion miles) along its path from Earth to Saturn.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the endpoint of the Path.  'The Cassini spacecraft will travel 3.5 billion kilometers (2.175 billion miles) along its path from Earth to Saturn.'

name: Endpoints
definition_en: The Endpoints are two (or more) named endpoints of the Path.  'This Pacific typhoon traveled far inland, knocking down everything in its path between Los Angeles and Denver.'

name: Characteristic
definition_en: The Characteristic is a characteristic(s) of the Path.  'Unlike Hubble, Compton was not designed to be serviced by astronauts in its 270 mile orbit.'

name: Landmark
definition_en: An entity relative to which the Theme moves on its Path .   'Lenny killed at least nine people and caused millions of dollars in damage on its course past 16 Caribbean islands.'

name: Direction
definition_en: The Direction is the direction or directions the Path runs.  'There was huge relief that Hurricane Emily's projected westward path across the Caribbean is likely to track to the south of oil and gas fields.'

name: Ground
definition_en: A setting location through which the Path goes.  'Hurrican Dennis was blamed for five deaths in Florida and Georgia -- but was much more brutal in its path across the Caribbean.'

name: Length
definition_en: The Length is the distance the Path extends.  'The bolt traveled smoothly in its short path through the air to Santa.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The moving object whose motion describes the Path.  'The thick white line shows the army's path from Uzbekistan through Iran, Iraq, Palestine, and into Italy.'

name: Patrol
definition_en: The person (or group) who inspects the Ground to see that it is safe.  'Detective Jones patrolled the northern half of the building.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The area that the Patrol inspects with to ensure its safety.  'Four soldiers with submachine guns patrolled the room, and an officer made his rounds at frequent intervals.'

name: Unwanted_entity
definition_en: An entity whose presence would impair the desirability or safety of the Ground.  'Security guards patrolled for intruders while the game was in progress.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE is used for the Means by which the Patrol examines  the Ground.  'Policing your neighborhood by walking your block and asking about new or unusual things can significantly improve your and your neighbors' safety.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The desired outcome of the patrolling. Normally this constituent is a PP Complement headed by for, or a to-marked VP Complement.  'Patrol all unlit areas to ensure no one is hiding there.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Patrol inspects the Ground.  'My officers have been bravely patrolling that estate, on behalf of the community which we serve, and will continue to do so.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the extent  to which the Patrol examines the Ground.  ' This section is thoroughly policed by the correctional officers every morning and evening.'

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: This FE is the position of the Patrol during the act of perception.  Typically, it is expressed in a from-PP.  'We'll have to patrol the roof from a distance, avoiding the snipers' notice.'

name: Desired_state_of_affairs
definition_en: The desirable state of affairs which the Patrol hopes to ensure by visiting Ground.  'All our grounds are regularly patrolled for safety.'

name: Time
definition_en: >The Time when the Patrol examines the Ground.  'Officerspoliced the parade grounds during the Memorial day events. .'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The circumstances under which the Patrol examines the Ground.  'Under pressure to find something, the team patrolled the site for signs of illicit activity.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity used by the Patrol to scrutinize the Ground.  'Scouts patrolled the beaches with binoculars, looking for aircraft.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description of one of the participants in the patrolling event.  'They patrolled the parade grounds, unaware of the lurking danger.'  'An American patrol encounted resistance in the area.'

name: Members
definition_en: An indication of the members of the patrol.  'We patrolled the area with thirty soldiers.'  'Our patrol was ambushed just outside the village.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time of the patrol.  'We've been patrolling for hours and haven't even seen anyone.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: The Co-participant patrols along with the Patrol.  'US troops patrolled the area with Iraqi soldiers.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The Patrol may move around in a Vehicle.  'We typically patrolled this area in heavily armored cars.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: The Possessor is the organization (usually a nation or group of nations) that orchestrates the patrol.  'The bombmaker was found by a NATO patrol.'

name: Entities
definition_en: The entities whose interrelations form the pattern.

name: Name
definition_en: The name of the pattern, such as "wing-T".

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A descriptor of the pattern, such as "regular".

name: Origin
definition_en: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

name: Person
definition_en: The Person is the human being.

name: Persistent_characteristic
definition_en: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is concieved of as persisting over time.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.

name: Age
definition_en: The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.

name: Ethnicity
definition_en: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.

name: Context_of_acquaintance
definition_en: An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.  'Hey, where'd that museum guy go?' 'Is that the woman from the rally?'

name: Individual
definition_en: The Individual who is referred to in terms of their place along the political spectrum.  'Why the Left has lost credibility.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Individual resides.  'We need to reshape the agenda of the left in Hungary.'

name: Domain
definition_en: A set of issues that is used to identify a sub-set of the group members.   'So where, oh where, can Democrats find a candidate who is a fiscal conservative, a social moderate and well-liked in the West?'

name: Origin
definition_en: The Origin is the place where the Individual was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.  'We won the cold war and a lot of the French left has never gotten over that little fact of life.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Individual.  'I'm another one of those angry conservatives that everyone hates!'
