name: Context_of_acquaintance
definition_en: An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.  'Is she the actress from the movie we saw last night?'

name: Rank
definition_en: Rank is the position in a hierarchy that a Person occupies within an organization.  	 'Robin is the head waitress at La Notte.'

name: Place_of_employment
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Person works.

name: Employer
definition_en: The Employer gives compensation to an Person for their work.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE identifies the Type of the vocation that the Person practices.

name: Compensation
definition_en: The Compensation is the payment that the Person receives for performing a task.

name: Contract_basis
definition_en: The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.  'Smithers is a half-time clerk for Procteur et Gamble '

name: Perceiver
definition_en: The FE Perceiver refers to someone whose cognitive state or experience (e.g. knowledge, beliefs, ideas judgments or classifications) is being described.

name: Sought_phenomenon
definition_en: The Perceiver is the entity or event which causes the perceptual experience of the Perceiver.   'So do our domestic dogs perceive smells with the same range  of subtle `hues'  as we perceive colour?'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: Phenomenon is experienced by the Perceiver.   'Kim perceived  a flaw.'

name: Perceiver_agentive
definition_en: The Perceiver_agentive performs some action in order to have a perceptual experience. It is expressed as an External Argument:  'The waiter smelled the milk to see if it was fresh.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: Phenomenon indicates the entity or phenomenon to which the Perceiver_agentive directs his or her attention in order to have a perceptual experience. Typically, it is expressed as an Object with verbs.  'The waiter smelled the milk to see if it was fresh.' 'The policeman watched him run out the door'

name: Body_part
definition_en: Body_part identifies the part of the body used as a sensory organ of the Perceiver_agentive, typically expressed in a with-PP. 'You should feel the water with your toes before jumping in.' This frame element occurs infrequently in this frame, because most of the target words intrinsically imply what part of the body is used (e.g. smelling must be done with the nose). However, the verb feel does take  this frame element, because touch is not localized on the body the same way as other modalities .  Body_part may be expressed in other modalities when it adds specificity to what is implied by the target word in question.  'I was now able to breathe properly and started to feel over my body with both hands.' 'I looked at the wreckage with my good eye.'

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: This FE is the position of the Perceiver during the act of perception.  Typically, it is expressed in a from-PP. 'We watched the parade from the roof.'

name: Direction
definition_en: Direction is used for all path-like expressions that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception, with the exception of those indicating the location of the Perceiver_agentive (which would be marked Location_of_perceiver)  'The detective looked across the street at the suspect.' 'The detective listened through the wall to their conversation.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: State is used for predicate expressions that apply to the Phenomenon, providing some information about the state it is in while the perceiver's attention is directed to it: 'The detective watched the suspect fleeing.' 'Pat tasted the cookie dough raw.'

name: State
definition_en: State is the location, activity, or other characteristic of the Phenomenon.  'I tasted the soup in the fridge.'  'I stared at the man running out the door.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner expressions may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of active perception as such: closely, carefully, etc.  'Dan looked at the inscription carefully.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means indicates the tool or method the Perceiver_agentive is using to actively perceive the Phenomenon.  May be confused with Direction in cases with through-PP, but is referring more to the instrument used than the path used.  'Joann peeked at John through the binoculars' 'You can observe distant galaxies with a good telescope. ' 'He observed babies using ultrasound and discovered that each showed a preference for one or the other thumb.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the activity of attempting to perceive occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: Some action that the Perceiver_agentive is trying to accomplish by directing their own attention.  'She listened to the music to find out if it was actually written by Satan.'

name: Place
definition_en: The general location within which the act of perception takes place.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of  time for which the Perception takes place.  'I  WATCH them for quite a while .'

name: Expected_entity
definition_en: An entity or state-of-affairs that the Perceiver_agentive hopes, fears, or expects to find within the Phenomenon.  'Watch for little errors with hand position.' 'While Bertha was n't looking, he carefully smelt the soup for any trace of the poison.'

name: Ground
definition_en: Ground is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced by the Perceiver_agentive.    'Kim looked at the cloud against the blue sky.'

name: Obscuring_medium
definition_en: The Obscuring_medium is the medium through which the Phenomenon makes itself perceivable to the Perceiver_agentive.  This is similar to the Direction, but occurs in the opposite direction and implies a movement of the Phenomenon.  'I eavesdropped on them through the wall'.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the being who has a physical experience on some part of his  or her body, or internally. Often information about this frame element is incorporated as a possessive determiner into the constituent expressing the Body Part, in which case it is not tagged separately (from Body Part), as shown below: My legs hurt! Sometimes, however, this frame element is expressed as an External Argument in its own right:  I hurt all over! Here, the phrase all over can be considered a kind of generalized Body Part expression, and the pronoun I expresses the Experiencer independently. With nouns and adjectives in this frame, the separate expression of the Experiencer is more common: I have a pain in my leg.

name: Body_part
definition_en: This FE is the location on the body where the physical experience takes place, typically expressed as External Argument, often as PP complement: My legs are a little sore. I'm a little sore in my legs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation describes the cause of the perception the body is experiencing.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion is the specific area of the Body_part which experiences the sensation. 'My leg aches under the bandage. '

name: Perceiver_passive
definition_en: This FE is the being who has a perceptual experience, not necessarily on purpose. It is typically expressed as an External Argument.  'The waiter smelled something foul in the kitchen.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: This FE is the entity or phenomenon that the perceiver experiences with his or her senses. It is typically expressed as Object with verbs.  'The waiter smelled something foul in the kitchen.'  'I saw the baker prepare his special peanut butter pie'.

name: Body_part
definition_en: The Body_part is the location on the Perceiver_passive's body where the perceptual experience  takes place.  It is typically expressed in a PP. 'Marlow felt something cold and hard against the back of his neck.' This Frame Element occurs less frequently than others, because many target words imply that a particular part of the body is involved (e.g. smelling must be done with the nose). However, the verb feel does take this Frame Element, because touch is not localized on the body the same way other modalities are.  Body_part may be expressed in other modalities when it adds specificity to what is implied by the target word in question. 'I heard a ringing in my right ear. '

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: This FE identifies the Location_of_protagonist during the perceptual experience. It is typically expressed in a from-PP. 'The witnesses saw the robbery from the their car.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver (see above), that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception. 'The detective could easily see into the house.' 'The detective heard their conversation through the wall.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The State indicates predicate expressions that apply to the Phenomenon, providing some information about the state it is in while the Perceiver_passive experiences it.  'The detective saw the suspect fleeing.' 'Pat saw Kim naked.'

name: State
definition_en: State is the location, activity, or other characteristic of the Phenomenon.  'I saw the baker baking his special peanut butter pie'.  'I overheard the cat in the cupboard'.  'I heard fear in his voice'.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner expressions may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of perception as such: clearly, loudly, etc.  'Pat heard the shot clearly.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree indicates the degree to which the Perception is experienced.  'A nightmare creature, barely perceived in the swirling dense smoke, was beating at the flames coming from its own body.' 'Older people perceive less well.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action whereby the Perceiver perceives.  'He saw it by looking out the window.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Perceiver_passive or the Body_part perceives the Phenomenon.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

name: Contrastive_context
definition_en: An element of the discourse that serves to contextualize the Phenomenon, with which it is directly related (i.e. filling a frame-element role of the Phenomenon or vice-versa).  It contrasts with other contextually relevant elements that potentially (but do not actually) fill the same role.  'Such a difference in note-taking accuracy can also be seen for second-year pupils .'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state-of-affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state-of-affairs would be expected given the state-of-affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: A situation which pertains during the event.  This frame element is primarily used to highlight the event denoted by the target against a (potentially partially) causal or concessive background state-of-affairs.

name: Frequency
definition_en: An expression of how often the event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The general location within which the act of perception takes place.

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is  experienced (or not experienced) by the Perceiver_passive.  It can be distinguished from locative postnominal modifiers of the Phenomenon in negative contexts. 'Pat didn't see Kim  behind the bar.' In this example, it is implied that Pat looked behind the bar and did not find Kim there.

name: Obscuring_medium
definition_en: The Obscuring_medium is the medium through which the Phenomenon makes itself perceivable to the Perceiver_passive.  This is similar to the Direction, but occurs in the opposite direction and implies a movement of the Phenomenon.  'My mother heard the scream through the attic window'.

name: Origin
definition_en: The Origin is the place where the Person was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.  'Sir Alec Guiness was a British actor until his death.'

name: Person
definition_en: The Person is the human being.  'Smithers is a brilliant actor.'   'That actor was terrible.'  (Note that the Person FE is incorporated in the LU actor.n, so the FE need not be explicitly marked unless an overy Person is named.)

name: Persistent_characteristic
definition_en: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Person which is conceived of as persisting over time.  'Billy Throb is a  swarthy actor who frequently plays in scary movies.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Person.  'Hundreds of angry actors were protesting against the new contract'

name: Age
definition_en: The Age is the length of time the Person has been alive.  'I need help with the name of an old actor'

name: Ethnicity
definition_en: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Person belongs.  'She's one of the most famous black actresses around today'

name: Context_of_acquaintance
definition_en: An expression indicating the context with which the Person is associated.  'Is she the actress from the movie we saw last night?'

name: Rank
definition_en: Rank is the position in a hierarchy that a Person occupies within a performance.  	 'Robin is the lead actress in La Notte.'

name: Place_of_employment
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Person works.  'Actors at the Theater on the Square went on strike'

name: Employer
definition_en: The Employer gives compensation to an Person for their work.  'Margaret's fortunes improved in 1949 when she joined a host of young MGM actresses'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE identifies the Type of performer the Person is.   'Smithers is a stage actor'

name: Compensation
definition_en: The Compensation is the payment that the Person receives for performing a task.  'Barney Smith is a highly-paid actor'

name: Contract_basis
definition_en: The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.  'Smithers is a part-time actor at the National Theater '

name: Audience
definition_en: The Audience experiences the Performance.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Performer to transmit the Performance to the Audience.

name: Performance
definition_en: The Performers generates the Performance which  the Audience perceives.

name: Performer
definition_en: The Performer provides an experience for the Audience.

name: Score
definition_en: The music which may be performed in the Performance, either in isolation or accompanying actions and speech.

name: Script
definition_en: The (usually written) directions which instruct the Performers on what actions to perform, when, and how.  It has many different names depending on the Type of Performance including script, screenplay, libretto, book, and choreography.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates the subtype of Performance, including dance, theater, film, etc.

name: Role
definition_en: Role identifies one of the possible relations that the Performer can have to the Performance.  The Role (s) a Performer has in the Performance will determine which parts of the Script should be performed by the Performer, as the Script is written in terms of which Role (s) each set of instructions applies to.  In the fields of theater, movies, ballet, and opera, a Role generally corresponds to a character in the story of the Script, while other types of performance may use more general Roles like lead violinist.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when an event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place an event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing.

name: Performer1
definition_en: The person that performs alongside Performer2. 'He co-starred with Matt Perry in Tool 3.'

name: Performer2
definition_en: The person that is also in the Performance, alongside Performer1. 'Who co-starred with Glen Close in that space opera thingy?'

name: Duration
definition_en: How long the Performer is in the Performance. 'She starred in Cats for several years.'

name: Event_description
definition_en: This is an appraisal or description of the performance event.

name: Performer
definition_en: The Performer provides an experience for the Audience.

name: Personnel
definition_en: The Personnel, including writers, producers, stage hands, key grips, etc., contribute to the Performance without actually being directly perceived by the Audience.

name: Audience
definition_en: The Audience experiences the Performance.

name: Performance
definition_en: The experience generated by the Performers and perceived by the Audience .

name: Script
definition_en: The (usually written) directions which instruct the Performers on what actions to perform, when, and how.  It has many different names depending on the Type of Performance including script, screenplay, libretto, book, and choreography.

name: Score
definition_en: The Score may be performed in the Performance, either in isolation or accompanying actions and speech.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates the Type of Performance, including dance, theater, film, etc.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Performer to transmit the Performance to the Audience.

name: Partner_1
definition_en: That partner in the Relationship who is realized as the subject of verbs in active form sentences, or of adjectives in predicative uses. 'John is married to Sue.' 'John is Sue's husband.' When the target word is a noun (e.g. mistress, lover, bachelor), that noun is annotated  as Partner_1 and, if there is one, the other member of the Relationship is Partner_2. 'George is a bachelor.' 'George's mistress left the party.' 'George has  a  mistress.' When there is a word other than the target that refers to Partner_1, that word is tagged rather than the target. 'George is Laura's lover.'

name: Partner_2
definition_en: That partner in the Relationship who is not expressed as the external argument. 'John is Sue's husband.' 'John is engaged to Joan.'

name: Partners
definition_en: The joint construal of both Partners in the Relationship. 'John and Sue are married.' 'They are engaged.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Partners.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby a focal participant achieves an action indicated by the target. 'He befriended her by staying after to talk every day.'

name: Relationship
definition_en: The Relationship between Partners. 'His wanderings caused the break-up of their marriage.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of the relationship. 'I'd like you to meet my long-time friend.'

name: Source_of_relationship
definition_en: The source of the relationship. 'Have you seen my old High School buddy Johnathan Rich lately?'

name: Person
definition_en: A sentient being or group of beings that is prosperous or well known after being involved in some Endeavor.  'He became a success at the age of 25.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Entity is determined to be successful.  'After 20 years of hard work, he finally made it as an artist in '84.'

name: Degree
definition_en: A qualification of the level of success that the Entity achieves.  'He had an extremely successful career.'

name: Endeavor
definition_en: An event that the Person is involved in which leads to their state of prosperity or renown.  'Looking back, I had a very successful career.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: An explanation of why the Person or Endeavor achieves its goal of prosperity or renown.  'Apple's iPad is wildly successful because Apple actually thinks about its customers.'

name: Field
definition_en: The area in which the <fex name="">Person achieves success.  'Winfried became successful in business.'

name: Artifact
definition_en: This FE identifies the entity or substance that is designed to have a particular Use.  'The first of the two drawings by Parmigianino recently acquired for the National Gallery is a study for the Madonna dal collo lungo.'

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which the Artifact is intended.  'The author's lucid text and instructional drawings provide a strong foundation in the basic and functional anatomy of the pain's region.'

name: Creator
definition_en: An individual or individuals that bring the Artifact into existence.  'Italian paintings include an allegorical work by Garofalo which was mentioned in Vasari 's ` Vite ' .'

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which an Artifact comes into existence.  'Here's a 1987 photo of how the Union School building had deteriorated after many years of neglect.'

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to an Artifact.  'In his painting The Fall of Man Albrecht went through a hard time trying to achieve a geometrical figure of two beings known as man and woman.'

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of the subtype of Artifact.  'The Impressionist style paintings of 1896-7 are rare but of great interest'

name: Material
definition_en: Any indication of what makes up the Artifact, including components, ingredients, etc.  'The exhibition also features a marble statue of a naked Aphrodite crouching at her bath'

name: Represented
definition_en: The entity--which may be a thing, an action or a state--that is represented by the Artifact.  'I was able to take a fine photo of his arrival.'

name: State_of_represented
definition_en: A characterization of the state in which the Represented entity is portrayed.  'Within the church is the painting of Virgin Mary sitting on the throne holding a child among various saints.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE identifies a characteristic, description, or evaluation of the Artifact.  'The cover features a horrible photo of the man.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Artifact is presently located.

name: Constituents
definition_en: Salient parts or substances that make up an Entity.  At this level of abstraction, not every Entity is conceived of as having parts, though any normal entity has them.   'A bronze sword is nearly as strong as the steel ones .'

name: Entity
definition_en: A thing (either abstract or physical) that exists with some degree of permanence.

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: Indicates the action (or causer) which made or makes the Entity what it is. 'glacial valley'

name: Name
definition_en: A label applied to a specific Entity.  Not usual for general words inheriting from this frame, but common for Locales.  'Keyboard 1 has all the right features .'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Entity belongs to. When a subtype is signified by some more specific FE, like Formational_cause, we use that more specific FE instead of Type, so this FE is most often needed when there is a vague or unknown relation between a name that indicates the Type and the Type of Entity in question.  This FE is normally found as a pre-nominal modifier.  'We use only d'Arbin pottery .'

name: Place
definition_en: A place that a physical Entity is located with respect to.  'All the stuff on the bureau is small.'

name: Perpetrator
definition_en: This is the person (or other agent) who forcibly seizes control over a vehicle to gain some end.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: This is the means of transportation which gets under the control of the perpetrator. Example: The terrorists hijacked the plane.

name: Victim
definition_en: This FE describes the people that are suffering as a result of the Perpetrator's action.  'The rebels skyjacked a plane with 89 passangers.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Event
definition_en: The unlawful seizure of a Vehicle by a Perpetrator.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Perpetrator by which the seizure of the Vehicle is accomplished.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Goal
definition_en: This is the place to which the vehicle is directed.

name: Source
definition_en: This is the place from which the vehicle is taken away.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The action that the Perpetrator is trying to accomplish by piracy.  'We have hijacked this plane just to show how easy it is.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The situation that the Perpetrator had in mind which lead to the decision to perpetrate the particular act of piracy.  'He carjacked the Lincoln Towncar instead because it looked ritzier.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An object that the Perpetrator uses in taking control of the Vehicle.  'The plane was hijacked with knives'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that the Vehicle is seized in acts of piracy.  'The ferry that Kenneth was on was hijacked twice in three days'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person (or other force) that causes the Theme to move.  'The waiter placed the food on the table.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the object that changes location during the Placing.  'The waiter placed the food on the table.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the initial location of the Theme, before it changes location.  'Her mother shelved the cans from the countertop.'

name: Path
definition_en: Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.  'The mail carrier stuck the letters through the slot.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The FE Goal is the location where the Theme ends up. This FE is profiled by words in this frame.   'The waiter placed the food on the table.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of the placing action which is not directly related to the trajectory of the Theme's motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.  'The chef packaged the food carefully into take-out containers.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree indicates the degree to which the placing occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Theme of the placing.   'I put the dishes into the cabinet unwashed.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is an act whereby the Agent achieves the placing of the Theme.  'The Egyptians set it in place by simple levering.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the Placing.

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration is the amount of time for which the Theme is to stay in the Goal location.  'If you place it there for extended periods, your monitor may suffer permanent damage.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place indicates where the Placing occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation indicates why the Placing occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: Time is when the Placing occurs  'Smithers had placed the table there the night before.'

name: Area
definition_en: The Area is the setting into which the Theme is placed.   'She emptied a wash basket full of towels and deposited them around the house.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: This is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.  'Pat lay the trophy on the mantle along with her portrait. '

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE is any expression which characterizes the extent of motion.    'I plunged my hands wrist deep in the fragrant herbs and rubbed the dry fragments between the fingertips'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which Placing occurs.  'Smithers put his book down quickly and turned around.'

name: Cause
definition_en: 'Grass , which is sown with clover , provides rich pasture for cattle in summer and the clover is another plant which puts nitrogen into the soil .'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by perform the placing action.  'They put the vase in a box to protect it during transportation.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: This extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the actor who instigates the filling.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the physical object or substance which changes location. 'Rev. Lovejoy carefully brushed the rolls with butter. '

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location where the Theme begins its motion. 'Josef filled his flask from the whiskey bottle.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is the trajectory of the motion.  'Jess filled the container through a small hole in the lid.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the area or container being filled. Goal is generally the NP Object in this frame.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the filling occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Agent of the filling action. 'Naked, Margeret filled the tub.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the filling occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the filling occurs.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result is the resultant state after the filling has occurred.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Agent fills or covers the Goal. 'Samantha covered the table with flowers because she was bored.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the filling occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the filling takes place.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which the filling occurs.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion is the smaller area of the Goal where the filling or covering occurs. 'Mrs. Bouvier anointed the children with oil on the forehead.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event which brings about the filling of the Goal.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the entity that traverses the trajectory.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source profiles the region where the Theme has travelled from (i.e. the region where the Theme's movement began).

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is the region upon which the Theme travels. It is any region in between the Source (where the Theme departed from) and the Goal (where the theme will eventually arrive).

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal profiles the region at the end of the Theme's Path. This is the region where the Theme movement stops.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor provides additional information that characterizes one or more of the aspects of the trajectory: the Source, the Path, or the Goal.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent plants the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: Theme is the item planted by the Agent.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument is used by the Agent as a tool to help obtain the Theme. (This tool is not limited to typical artifacts and can be hands, arms, and other atypical hunting and fishing instruments.)

name: Duration
definition_en: For what length of time the Agent plants the Theme.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Agent plants the Theme.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Agent plants the Theme.

name: Outcome
definition_en: The failure or success of an attempt.

name: Place
definition_en: The greater geographic location where the Agent plants the Theme.

name: Time
definition_en: When the planting event occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by planting the Theme.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Agent cultivates the Theme.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground is the background or context to which the Agent pays attention in his agricultural efforts.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive describes a participant in the Planting action.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: The Co-participant is an entity that participates in the planting event in a coordinated way with another participant.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the planting event logically follows.

name: Plant
definition_en: The living organism belonging to the kingdom Plantae.

name: Characteristic
definition_en: A quality of the Plant.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Plant not covered by another frame element.

name: Origin
definition_en: The location from which the Plant originated.

name: Question
definition_en: The Question is an open proposition the answer to which is under dispute.  'The issue is who will have control of Iraq's rich oil resources.'

name: Group
definition_en: The Group are the persons or organizations who have different points of view on the Question.

name: Status
definition_en: The Frame Element Status is used for expressions that indicate the relative importance of a Question with respect to the other topics that are disputed.   'The main issue is where the revenue is coming in from.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Question, often with regard to its complexity or whether it has been resolved or not.  'Two unresolved issues fuel speculation that he might not receive a fair trial.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The area of human experience which the Question concerns.  'The third sector of the Master Plan explores the important economic issue of tourism.'

name: Context
definition_en: A state or event within which the Question arises as a problem for the Group.  'The question in Argentina's case is what exchange rate is appropriate now.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which the Question exists as a problem for the Group.  'The issue at the time was whether or not to relocate the Rennes-based part of the team to California.'

name: Viewpoint
definition_en: An individual or individuals from whose point of view the Question is a point of dispute within the Group.  'For Elijah, the issue was between two altars: worship of God and worship of BaaI.'

name: Activists
definition_en: The person or group of people that act out against the Institution in an attempt to have their Demands fullfilled.

name: Institution
definition_en: The Institution is the company, factory, political party / institution, or entity that yields authority over the Activists.

name: Demands
definition_en: The Demands are the guarantee(s) given by the Institution to the Activists that act to correct or address the issues or state of affairs that were grievous to the Activists.

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration is the length of time that the political action takes to be resolved.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the political action is carried out.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Activists carry out the political action.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location where the political action occurs.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE is the subtype of the general category of action taken by the Activists against the Institution.    'The hunger strike lasted for three weeks.'

name: Result
definition_en: The result of the event in which the Activists act against the Institution.

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: The materials or Constituent_parts that make up a Locale.   'New York is a city of glass and steel'

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location that the Locale is a part of. 'John spent several years wandering the villages of Romania.'

name: Locale
definition_en: A stable bounded area.  It is typically the designation of the nouns of Locale-derived frames.  'There used to be a forest in that city'

name: Name
definition_en: ULTIMATELY TO BE REPLACED BY MULTIWORD TARGETS (in almost all cases).  This FE is used for the Names of Locales.   'The city of Paris' 'The town of Smithersville'

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Locale is located with respect to.  'All the cities near the San Francisco bay are large.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description, characteristic, or property of the Locale which is not covered by more specific FEs.  'He ruled the largest kingdom that ever existed.'

name: Population
definition_en: The people living in the jurisdiction of the locale.  'Stawiski was a city of laborers, of whom can be said ?You shall eat your bread by the sweat of your brow? '

name: Evaluee
definition_en: The person or object that is being evaluated for its desirability.  'I heard he's a cool guy.'

name: Degree
definition_en: A description of how desirable the Evaluee is.  'Hanna Montana is really cool.'

name: Judge
definition_en: The person who decides how desirable the Evaluee is.  'Knitting is cool to your grandma.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Evaluee is judged to be desirable.  'Go-go boots were popular in the 60s.'

name: Place
definition_en: The geographic area where an Evaluee is considered desirable.  'Electronica is all the rage in Europe.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person who acts in a misleading way to create the impression that they are a particular individual or type of Simulated_entity.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the posing event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that contributes to the his or her being perceived as a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.  'Some activists posed as delegates by wearing suits.'

name: Simulated_entity
definition_en: The type or individual that the Agent gives the impression of being.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by posing as a particular (kind of) Simulated_entity.  'He posed as a Hurricane Katrina evacuee in order to get food, clothing and money from Good Samaritans in Shreveport.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the posing event logically follows.   'They posed as patients because the paper's previous attempt at a formal survey met strong resistance.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent gives the impression that they are the Simulated_entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Agent impersonates the Simulated_entity.

name: Item
definition_en: Item identifies the entity whose scalar property is specified. 'Bacon is high in fat.'

name: Variable
definition_en: Variable is the scalar property that the Item possesses.  Soda is high in sugar.

name: Value
definition_en: The Value is the position or range of positions on the scale that the Item occupies.  This is normally implicit in the LU.  'This car is high in price.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the scalar property of an Item holds with respect to some Variable. 'Bacon is very high in fat.'

name: Domain
definition_en: Domain describes the set of Items for which the Variable 's position is determined.  'Interest rates are high in West Germany.'

name: Owner
definition_en: The entity that owns a posession.

name: Possession
definition_en: The thing which is owned by the Owner. Ex.:  I have twenty bucks. (This does not include bodyparts or medical conditions, but does include intellectual property, etc.)

name: Depictive
definition_en: State of the Owner or Possession.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Owner possesses the Possession.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time interval during which the Owner has a possession.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Owner has the Possession.

name: Possible_event
definition_en: The Possible_event has met its preconditions, and will occur if some further Condition holds.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the preconditions of the Possible_event are met.  'In this weather, an experienced pilot can still manage to fly 500 miles.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: An entity, event, or state that brings about the possibility of the Possible_event.

name: Condition
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that does not hold, but if it did, the Possible_event would occur.  'If he wants , he can have all the fishsticks .'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Possible_event can occur.  'You can come in now.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: The individual that has just come into possession of the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity which has just come into the possession of the Recipient.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Recipient has the Theme

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time interval during which the Post_getting event occurs.

name: Donor
definition_en: The individual that has just given the Theme to the Recipient and no longer has the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity that the Donor has just given to the Recipient.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Donor lacks the Theme.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The individual that has just come into possession of the Theme.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_giving event occurs.

name: Owner
definition_en: The entity that no longer owns the posession.

name: Possession
definition_en: The thing which was owned by the Owner. (This does not include bodyparts or medical conditions, but does include intellectual property, etc.)

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the possession state which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_lose_possession event occurs.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The person who has just acted to come into possession of the Theme.

name: Donor
definition_en: The person who has just given the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity that changes possession, beginning in the possession of the Donor and ending up with the Recipient.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Recipient has the Theme

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_giving event occurs.

name: Donor
definition_en: The individual that has just given the Theme away.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity which has ended up in the possession of the Recipient

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Donor possesses the Theme.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The individual that has ended up with the Theme.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_transfer event occurs.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the individual whose body is in a particular posture.  The Agent FE is generally expressed as the external argument of verbs:  'Kim was kneeling by the window.'

name: Location
definition_en: A description of the position of the Agent.  The Location of the Agent is frequently expressed and generally occurs as a PP Complement:  'Kim was kneeling by the window.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Agent's state throughout the time they are in a particular posture.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Dependent_state
definition_en: A state of the Agent which crucially depends on their posture. 'She sat upright'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time interval during which the Agent held a certain posture.  ' Yesterday evening he was sitting in his armchair as usual'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Agent holds the posture.  ' Joel sat on the porch to watch the traffic go by'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time for which the Agent holds the posture.  ' I could have stood there all afternoon'

name: Point_of_contact
definition_en: The part of the body that provides support to the Agent's body in the posture.  'I stood on my heels and looked out the window'

name: Action
definition_en: This FE identifies the Action that the Agent performs intentionally in order to prepare for a later Occasion.  'Little Dieter practiced playing the piano all day.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent performs the Action in preparation for later performances of the same type.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the practicing occurs.  'Our band practices on the football field.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent performs an intentional act. 'John practiced typing to receive a raise.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent practices.  'We practiced the play on Tuesday.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent  practices.  'We practiced the slam dunk by bouncing on a trampoline.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the practicing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the Action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'We ran through the song at quarter speed.'

name: Occasion
definition_en: The later enactment or enactments that the Agent expects to perform. Note that the Agent does not have to have specific Occasions in mind.  'For our brother's wedding we had to rehearse the dinner twenty times.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time during which an Action is repeatedly practiced.  'The troupe rehearsed the ballet for 4 months before going on tour.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times that the Action is practiced.  'We practice this scene daily'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: A person who participates in a practice event along with the Agent.  ' Then I went back to rehearsing with the band while she sat around listening '

name: Evaluee
definition_en: The Behavior of the Evaluee is being judged as worthy of a particular reaction. 'It was commendable of Lisa to give so much to charity.'

name: Behavior
definition_en: This FE indicates the Behavior on which the assessment of praiseworthiness is based. 'Your behavior is commendable' 'The children made a commendable effort.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the judgement or reaction is deserved. 'Your actions were very commendable'

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Prank
definition_en: The Prank is a device, strategy, or system designed to mislead and cause harm and amusement to a Victim (and possibly others observing the prank).

name: Joker
definition_en: The Prank is orchestrated by a Joker.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Joker intends to mislead and cause harm to the Victim by means of the Prank.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description of the Prank.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The individual that is about to gain a possession.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity which is about to be acquired by the Recipient.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the way that the Recipient has the Theme

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_getting event occurs.

name: Donor
definition_en: The individual that has possession of the Theme and is about to transfer possession to the Recipient.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity which is in the possession of the Donor, which later ends up in the possession of the Recipient.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Donor possesses the Theme.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The individual who is about to come into possession of the Theme.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time when the Pre_giving event occurs.

name: Owner
definition_en: The Owner is the entity that owns the Possession.

name: Possession
definition_en: The Possession is the thing which is owned by the Owner.  'I have twenty bucks.' (This does not include bodyparts or medical conditions, but does include intellectual property, etc.)

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the possession state which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time when the Post_lose_posession event occurs.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The person who acts to come into possession of the Theme.

name: Donor
definition_en: The person who has the Theme and is about to give it to the Recipient.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity that changes possession, beginning in the possession of the Donor and ending up with the Recipient.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the way that the Recipient has the Theme.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time when the Pre_receiving event occurs.

name: Donor
definition_en: The individual that is about to transfer the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity which is in the possession of the Donor.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Recipient or Donor possesses the Theme.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The individual who is about to receive the Theme.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time when the Pre_transfer event occurs.

name: Theme
definition_en: A valuable entity which might fall and be damaged.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of precariousness from the expected value given the Theme and the state indicated by the target itself.

name: Falling_event
definition_en: The event of falling, incorporated in the LUs of this frame.

name: Dangerous_entity
definition_en: An entity which may cause the Theme to fall.

name: Place
definition_en: A particular location in which the Theme is at risk of falling. Frequently, it is to be inferred that the characteristics of the location put the Theme in danger.

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Theme is in danger of falling.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the state of precariousness of the Theme logically follows.

name: Situation
definition_en: The Situation under which the Theme is safe or unsafe from falling.  Most expressions of Time and Place also express the Situation and should be labeled as such on the 2nd FE layer.

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain in which the Theme has a degree of precariousness. Usable only in metaphorical sentences.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes the Theme as being in some state during the action.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the holistic properties of the balancing situation.

name: Location
definition_en: The location where the Theme is supported.

name: Result
definition_en: An event or state that results from the instability of the Theme.

name: Precipitation
definition_en: The water in liquid or solid form that falls from the sky is the Precipitation. This FE is incorporated in many LUs in this frame.

name: Rate
definition_en: The Quantity of Precipitation that falls within a certain Duration. 'It rains only half an inch per year around here.'

name: Quantity
definition_en: The Quantity is the amount of Precipitation that has fallen in a precipitation event or events.  It is usually measured as the height that the Precipitation attains if prevented from further movement. 'It rained six inches last night.'

name: Place
definition_en: The area which experiences precipitation.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the precipitation event lasts.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs. 'It will probably be raining at five o'clock.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the reason for the precipitation event. 'It rains because of high humidity.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the precipitation falls. 'It drizzled softly.'

name: Temperature
definition_en: This FE identifies the temperature of the precipitation. 'I was standing in the cool drizzle.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is in an undesirable Situation.  'The insurers ended up in a bind.'

name: Situation
definition_en: This FE identifies the undesirable Situation the Experiencer is in. 'They found themselves in a quite a fix.' 'The company was definitely in dire straits from the dollar's inflation.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation of  the Situation.  'We 're in this mess from paying too little attention to quality control.'

name: Time
definition_en: Thiis FE identifies the Time when the Situation is in effect.  'Yesterday's predicament was a little too exciting.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Situation occurs.  'The trouble in America is only going to get worse.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain in which the Experiencer has the problem.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker makes a prediction.  'The institute forecast an increase in leisure spending of 15 per cent.'

name: Eventuality
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate an event or state that is predicted to occur or hold at a future time. A single Eventuality may be expressed discontinuously in a raising construction. This FE is also used for expressions that denote entities with variable attributes about which the Speaker makes predictions.   ' Predicting the weather is risky business.' 'Predicting the numbers of disabled elderly into the future is problematic as it depends upon the projection forward of current patterns of disability .' ' Wangforecasts a 9 per cent increase in state revenue' ' The European market is  forecast to grow 18.1%.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: Evidence marks expressions that denote a set of facts on the basis of which the Speaker makes the prediction.  'Violence was  predicted on the basis of disorder at demonstrations in Paris.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the prediction is made.  'John predicted last year that he would be finished by October.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Speaker makes the prediction.  ' Greenman predicted at a small dinner party that the market would rise again.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner marks any description of the Speaker's prediction making  that is not covered by more specific FEs.   'Smeagol confidently predicted that he would win the race.' 'One commentator rashly predicted that the fad for adaptions wouldn't last much longer'  Note that this FE does not cover modifiers such as 'correctly' or 'accurately'.

name: Time_of_eventuality
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate for what future time an Eventuality is predicted.  ' Cocoa stocks reached a record 1.2m tonnes and a seventh year of surplus is forecast for the year to September 1991.'

name: Accuracy
definition_en: This FE indicates the Accuracy of the prediction. 'Compary president Randall Johnson predicted correctly that a major reworking of infrastructure would be necessary.' 'It is hard to forecast with a high degree of certainty what the weather will be like past two or three days.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Descriptor describes a characteristic of the Eventuality.

name: Medium
definition_en: The Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the prediction.  'The events that would occur over the next several years had been predicted in the Bible.'  'Her texts predict the future.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject matter to which the prediction pertains. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by about.

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Speaker makes a prediction.  'My regular psychic fortells my future by examining the configuration of spent coffee grounds.'

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer is the person (or sentient being) who wishes for the Event to occur.

name: Event
definition_en: The change that the Experiencer would like to see.

name: Focal_participant
definition_en: This is the entity that the Experiencer wishes to be affected by some Event.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree is the extent of the Experiencer's Desiring.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Experiencer desires something.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation shows why the Experiencer wants the Event to occur.  This FE occurs frequently as a PP complement headed by for.

name: Purpose_of_event
definition_en: The Purpose_of_event is the purpose pertaining to the desired Event.

name: Time_of_event
definition_en: The time that the Event would ideally occur.

name: Location_of_event
definition_en: The Location_of_event is the place involved in the desired Event.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Experiencer desires something.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.  Note that this FE is of extremely rare occurrence in this frame.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the Experiencer has desired something.

name: Contrast
definition_en: An alternative Event or Focal_participant that is less desirable for the Experiencer.  'I always preferred trackballs over mouses.'

name: Profiled_possibility
definition_en: The situation presented explicitly as a possible for agents to influence that leads to a better situation, contrasting with the implicit Opposite_possibility that leads to a worse situation.

name: Opposite_possibility
definition_en: The implicit situation that is mutually exclusive with the Profiled_possibility.  It is presented as leading to a less desirable situation, the Undesirable_consequence.

name: Positive_consequence
definition_en: The preferable situation that follows from the Profiled_possibility.

name: Undesirable_consequence
definition_en: The less desirable situation that follows as a result of the Opposite_possibility.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent uses the Preparatory_act to acheive a Purpose.

name: Preparatory_act
definition_en: The action performed by the Agent that is a preliminary to the achievement of the Purpose. The Preparatory_act may also be expressed by a result of such an act.  'The company's actions at that stage were simply preliminary to the takeover.' 'Nothing remarkable could be found, as it was almost certainly a preliminary book to the final publication of results.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The ultimate goal or purpose of the Agent, which the Preparatory_act enables.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Preparatory_act, Agent, or other participant.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Preparatory_act is distant from the achievement of the Purpose.

name: Domain_of_relevance
definition_en: The area, field, or domain for which the preliminary action is relevant.  'This laid the political groundwork for his victory in May.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Preparatory_act takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Preparatory_act takes place.

name: Preparatory_phase
definition_en: The part of the larger process that is preliminary to the achievement of the Purpose.  'We are still in the preliminary phases.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity whose existence at the Location is confirmed.

name: Location
definition_en: The Location of the Entity. The Location is conceived as a ground for an event of inspection to determine the presense of the Entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Entity is present at the Location.

name: Depictive
definition_en: A separate description of the state of the Entity when it is present.

name: Duration
definition_en: The time period during which the Entity is present. In this frame, Duration may be expressed with for preceding an event which stands for the duration of the event. In cases where the Entity is sentient, there may be an inference that the Entity's intent is to be present so as to participate in the event.  'I can be present for the first half of the ceremony and the last part of the reception, but I'll have to leave in the middle.'  'A catalyst should typically be present for the thermal and/or photochemically induced curing of the coating composition applied onto a suitable substrate.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose of the Entity.  'Mr. Jones will be present to answer your questions.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the presence or absence of the Entity.  'Because of the mills and their conspicuous absence, hundreds of people were uprooted.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Entity is present.  'The CDH gene exhibited a complete absence of expression in one cell line.'

name: Mitigating_situation
definition_en: The Mitigating_situation is the situation that actually occurs. It is presented in a discourse to mitigate the fact that a better situation did not occur - since the FE is still preferable to an even worse situation.    'We didn't win $7 million, but at least I only lost $2 on lottery tickets.'   'She didn't have time to exercise, but at least she had time to get groceries.'   'Their hunger pains, in any event, seemed to be diminishing.'   'He, at any rate, seemed to enjoy the party.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act that leads to the preservation.'Arlene pickled the cucumbers.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the substance in which the Patient might be  submerged to be preserved. 'Tess pickled the beets in vinegar.'

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is organic matter that undergoes the preservation.'Tess pickled the beets in vinegar.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which an an Agent performs the Preserving.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Agent preserves the Patient.'Hannah cured the shrimp by injecting them with brine.''This salami was cured naturally in salt.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Agent preserves the Patient.'Jake painstakingly embalmed the next body.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the preserving occurs.'Mr. Amber embalmed the woman's body in Turkey in 1922.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Agent preserves the Patient.'Mr. Amber embalmed the woman in Turkey in 1922.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Agent preserves the Patient.'Jude pickled the onions to increase their potency.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an action.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of Time for which the process of Preserving is ongoing.'...oak cured for eight years.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive phrase describing one of the participants.'The herring was cured with its innards still inside it.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Patient is preserved from decaying.  ' The corpse had been mummified completely.'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a deceptive Message to the Addressee. 'Politicians do nothing but tell lies about money.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The person that receives a Message from the Speaker.  'You're kidding me!' 'Satan lies to everyone, including himself.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic is the entity to which the proposition or propositions  relate, that they are about.  'You deceived me about the location of the diamonds.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the deception occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the deception occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: The (communicative) action performed by the Speaker in order to deceive the Addressee.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of Time that the Speaker spends on the Topic.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The goal of the Speaker's deceit of the Addressee

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Speaker deceives the Addressee about the Topic.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE describes how often the Speaker discusses the Topic with the Addressee.

name: Potential_hindrance
definition_en: The Potential_hindrance is the force which keeps the Event from happening, or does not prevent it.  'Israeli law effectively deprived the owners of their homes and lands.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The  is the situation, state-of-affairs, or state of having a possession that the Protagonist is kept from having.  'Their parents denied them a brand new car upon their sweet 16.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Potential_hindrance keeps the Event from taking place.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the Potential_hindrance keeps the Event from taking place.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the  person who keeps the Event from happening.  'The uncaring King Frank often starves his citizens of tax relief.'

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist is the person who is kept from having the State_of_affairs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason why the Agent keeps the Protagonist from having the State_of_affairs.  'I have suggested depriving children of TV-viewing time as a sanction.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time for which the Protagonist is denied the State_of_affairs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: How it is possible that the deprivation event occurs.  'By acting as his own agent, Joe deprived himself of this valuable information.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE marks the frequency with which the Protagonist is prevented from having the State_of_affairs.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time of prevention and which the prevention is taken to be a part of.

name: Potential_hindrance
definition_en: The Potential_hindrance is the force which keeps the Event from happening, or does not.

name: Event
definition_en: The Event is prevented from occurring by the Preventing_cause or the Agent.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Potential_hindrance or Agent keeps the Event from taking place.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the Potential_hindrance or Agent keeps the Event from taking place.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the sentient being which keeps the Event from happening.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: A situation that accompanies the preventing or allowing.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of details of the event that influence the overall understanding and impression, such as the attitude of an Agent (casually) or the overall nature of the event (the same way).

name: Means
definition_en: The action performed by an Agent that brings about the prevention or allowing.

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.  First, it applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness. The notion of appraisal requires a factive portrayal of the event. The second subgroup consists of any descriptions of the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames. The state of affairs reported by the target is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier. What that role is depends only on the predicate heading the modifier phrase.

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the Agent or an entity of the Event while they are involved in the action.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Allowed_category
definition_en: A category that the Event fits into, which dictates the Event's being permitted or prevented (in accord with some implicit Principle.)  'The transfer was sanctioned as a "necessary precaution".'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the event occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The situation that the Agent hopes to bring about with their action.

name: Product
definition_en: A commodity, item, or service being sold by the Seller at a certain Price.  'The rate for second hand products is just too high.'

name: Price
definition_en: The amount of money that the Seller charges the Buyer for a Product.  'She sells seashells at a rate of $20 per pound.'

name: Seller
definition_en: The entity that offers a Product at a certain Price.  'Their rates are really low.'

name: Buyer
definition_en: The person who purchases the Product at a particular Price. 'The ratefor you is going to be $15/month.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description of the Price, usually characterizing its position on a scale of expensiveness.  'That company charges ridiculous rates.'

name: Operator
definition_en: The Frame Element Operator marks expressions that indicate which level of government operates the Penal Institution.  'Smithers had to serve time in federal prison.'

name: Inmates
definition_en: Inmates marks expressions that indicate the group of people a Penal Institution is intended to hold.  'Monica served time in the Tennessee Prison for Women.'

name: Name
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that are the Name of a Penal Institution.  'Kolimov visited the Willy C. Peterson State Prison.'

name: Location
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate the Location of the Penal Institution.  'Carruthers spent three years in Fort Pulaski State Prison.'

name: Security
definition_en: The level of security maintained at the prison. 'He was held in a maximum security Prison.'

name: Penal_institution
definition_en: The locale which serves to confine individuals, generally for the purpose of punishment. This FE is incorporated in each LU in this frame.

name: Part
definition_en: A subpart of the Penal_institution.  'You really expect me to run a prison with only ten cells?'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE is used to describe a salent characteristic of the Penal_institution not otherwise specified. 'They held him for years in an isolated prison.'

name: Odds
definition_en: A numerical representation of the probability that a Hypothetical_event will occur.  'There's a 95 % chance of rain today.'

name: Position
definition_en: A metaphorical representation of the position on the scale of likelihood that the Hypothetical_event will occur.  'Chances are slim that he'll pull through.'

name: Hypothetical_event
definition_en: The event that is expected to happen with a certain likelihood.  'He's got a small chance of making it out alive.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Reason for which an event occurs.

name: Process

name: Process

name: Time

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase about the state of a focal participant. 'The rain continued unabated.'

name: Manner

name: Duration

name: Event

name: Place

name: Explanation

name: Next_subevent

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Process
definition_en: Name of the event which occurs.'Let the carnage end.'

name: Final_subevent

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Explanation

name: Time

name: Degree

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of the event.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing the event.

name: Result

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that the event is repeated.  'Twice the peace march ended with a prayer.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time it takes for the Process to end.

name: Process
definition_en: The overall process which is about to begin.

name: Time
definition_en: The point at which the Process begins.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Process remains ready to begin.

name: Process
definition_en: The Process which is halting.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the pause takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the pause in the Process occurs.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the event occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the pause.

name: Final_subevent
definition_en: The Final_subevent of an event.  'The peace march stopped with a prayer.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation of the pause.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that a Process remains stopped.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times that the Process stops.,  'Mining activities on the opal fields ceased twice in the last two weeks due to heavy rain storms'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of Time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Process
definition_en: The Process which is being resumed.'The meeting resumed after the bomb threat passed.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which an event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that the Process resumes.  'The tenth emergency special session resumed twice more to address ongoing violations against the security council resolution '

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  'Trading resumed in an orderly fashion on Monday'

name: Event
definition_en: Name of the Event which occurs. ' The crying began after sunset.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the Event takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which an Event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Event occurs.

name: Initial_subevent
definition_en: The Initial_subevent of the Event.'The service began with a prayer.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action.

name: Manner

name: Result
definition_en: Result of the Event.

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time for which the Process is ongoing after it has started.  'In three instances, violence erupted for brief periods.'

name: Frequency

name: Process

name: Degree

name: Depictive

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of an event.

name: Final_subevent
definition_en: The Final_subevent of an event.  'The peace march stopped with a prayer.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that a process remains stopped.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that the Process stops.,  'Mining activities on the opal fields ceased twice in the last two weeks due to heavy rain storms'

name: Process
definition_en: The overall event which is stopped.

name: Time
definition_en: The point at which the Process is not continuing.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Process does not resume.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the state takes place.

name: Process
definition_en: This FE identifies the name of the Process that occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is a person who applies the Process to the Material.

name: Alterant
definition_en: The Alterant causes a change in the Material.

name: Material
definition_en: The Material is altered by the Agent in some useful way. 'Stu treated the lumber with magical waterproofing fairydust.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Agent processes the Material. 'He treated the exterior of the house with waterproofing to protect his valuable peanut butter collection..'

name: Result
definition_en: The result of the processing action, whether intended or not.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time during which the application of the Alterant is applied to the Material

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Materials are processed, often a purpose-built facility such as a tannery or water treatment plant.

name: Time
definition_en: The point in time or period during which the treatment of the Material takes place.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the Material which is affected by the process.  'You have to galvanize the pipes only in the interior.'

name: Explanation
