definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in processing the Material.

name: Dimension
definition_en: The dimension or aspect of the Material that is processed.  'This supernatant was used for neasurement of isotopic enrichment of free leucine.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A holistic description encompassing all the details of an act of processing, often indicated by giving a characteristic of the Agent that affects the action.  'Botulinum can not be weaponized the same way .'

name: Participants
definition_en: The set of entities engaged in or subjected to procreative sexual contact.

name: Participant_1
definition_en: One party present for procreative sex.

name: Participant_2
definition_en: Another party present for procreative sex.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE describes the length of time that an entire sexual encounter can last, including but not necessarily implying the length of all stages of the encounter.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the sex act which is not covered by more specific FEs. In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of one or more Participants that also affect the action.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which Participants accomplish a sexual act.

name: Place
definition_en: To be clear: the place FE describes the overall location of the Participants of the sexual activity and nothing else.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE relates the relative time of occurrence of the sexual activity.

name: Domain
definition_en: For a sexual act, the Domain describes the specific realm of the contact between Participants; for example, phone sex.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the justification of a sexual act, for at least one of the Participants.

name: Deliverer
definition_en: This is the person who completes the movement of the Goods after having transported it.

name: Goal
definition_en: The end of the path and intended goal of the sending.

name: Goods
definition_en: The objects being delivered.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The vehicle employed by the Deliverer.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Goods or the Deliverer during the action.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the delivery event  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Deliverer that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Purchaser
definition_en: The individual who purchases and receives the Goods.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Deliverer hopes to bring about by delivering to the Purchaser.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state-of-affairs that explains why the Goods were delivered.

name: Time
definition_en: When the delivery takes place

name: Cotheme
definition_en: An additional theme delivered along with the main Goods.

name: Container
definition_en: A container in which the Goods is delivered.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the delivery takes place.

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed at which the Deliverer delivers the Goods.  'This service is for our clients who need speedy delivery of their goods.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The conditions under which the delivery takes place.  'Purchases over $400 are delivered for free.'

name: Source
definition_en: The location of the Goods before the delivery process begins.

name: Means
definition_en: The intermediate actions performed by the Deliverer in order to move the Goods to the Goal.

name: Path
definition_en: The path along which the Goods move while being delivered.

name: Developer
definition_en: The person who develops the Product.  'Elsa developed a new line of facial products.'

name: Product
definition_en: The entity which is developed by the Developer.  'Dr. Pepper was developed in Texas.'

name: Company
definition_en: The organization for which the Developer develops the Product.  'Wilhelm developed the software for Microsoft, but they rejected it.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Product is developed by the Developer.  'Gabriela developed her new line of fashion in Milan.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Product is developed by the Developer.    'The development of unique, high-quality writing instruments in the late 1990s saved the company from going bankrupt. '

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner in which the Product is developed.  'High-quality products must be developed quickly by employees.'

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which the Product is intended.  'This product was developed for underwater photography.'

name: Developer
definition_en: The Developer is the person who develops the Entity.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity is the item developed by the Developer.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Entity is developed by the Developer.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity is developed.

name: Company
definition_en: The organization for which the Entity is developed by the Developer.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Developer develops the Entity.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for why the Developer developed the Entity.

name: Brand
definition_en: The company that produces the Collection of Products.  'Did you see the new Kate Spade line?'

name: Collection
definition_en: The set of Products produced by the Brand.  'They're so damn rich, they could buy this whole line without batting an eyelash.'

name: Products
definition_en: The individual items produced by the Brand.  'Jaques just showed us his Fall line of cocktail dresses.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Collection or individual Products.  'His debut collection had brilliant crisp white shirts, beautiful eveningwear, and denim that was a little suspect.'

name: Collection_name
definition_en: The name of the Collection of Products produced by the Brand.  'The Greenwich armchair from Barnsley House's Winterthur collection is a must for those looking for sturdy yet stylish garden furniture.'

name: Designer
definition_en: The person who designs the Collection.   'Did you see Louis' new line?'

name: Entity
definition_en: The object that undergoes change.  'Advances in marketing techniques have since rendered it obsolete.'

name: Prior_state
definition_en: The former state of the Entity.  'I think we have advanced somewhat from that way of thinking .'

name: Post_state
definition_en: The state of the Entity following an advance.  'The roads have now advanced to a level of perfection not seen since Rome .'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the progress occurs.  'When did the X-wing progress beyond the drawing board?'

name: Rate
definition_en: The rate at which the change happens.  'His captaincy has slowly matured until he has made us forget the sulky Nasser Hussian era'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the progress, generally a description comparing events (the same way).   'Recovery in our major overseas markets has progressed tentatively and increased spending by consumers and government does not appear to be benefiting this .'

name: Duration
definition_en: The period over which the progress occurs.  'Screwcap wine seals enable bottle maturation, and provide ideal conditions for maturation of wines over a long period of time.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount of advancement that the Entity has attained.  'Robert's music is developing further as he hones his live set to bring in the diverse elements of pan-African music.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant dimension of development.  'Why have we developed economically as we have? '

name: Explanation
definition_en: An event or state of affairs that brings about the development of the Entity.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Progress occurs.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE describes the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Progress event occurs.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Principle
definition_en: A moral, legal, or social norm which rules a State_of_affairs to be inadmissible behavior or an outcome of behavior.  'The Establishment Clause of the First Amendment plainly prohibits the establishment of a national religion by Congress.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the prohibiting occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the prohibiting occurs.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the conditions under which the State_of_affairs is prohibited.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the State_of_affairs is prohibited.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual or organization that carries out the project.  'The DOE Human Genome Program also has developed high-throughput approaches to identifying is-regulatory sequences in the human and other genomes'

name: Field
definition_en: An area of human endeavor, typically scientifc in nature, in which the Agent's Activity falls.   'Several projects in computational linguistics have recently stalled due to lack of funding .'

name: Activity
definition_en: What the Agent (an individual or the members of an organization) are dedicated to doing.  'The New Car Assessment Program (NCAP) is dedicated to helping the public buy a safer car. '

name: Name
definition_en: A name given to the project for identification.  'Our agency is responsible for administering the WIC Program'

name: Goal
definition_en: The larger aim that the Agent is pursuing by carrying out certain coordinated measures.  'The program to analyze the composition of Titan's sludge is nearly complete.'

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: An entity (abstract or concrete) which is involved in an implicit Activity.  'Iran has vowed to continue its nuclear program and is demanding that sanctions against it should be lifted .' 'The DOE Human Genome Program also has developed high-throughput approaches to identify cis-regulatory sequences in the human and other genomes, based on shared '

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the manner in which the Agent performs the Activity associated with the program.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time over which the project is lasts or is slated to last.  'The government has initiated yet another seven-year program.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the Activity of the project as the Agent.  'It turned out that the company was doing a program with a local Arab-American communal group.'

name: Project
definition_en: The ongoing plan of action which allows the Agent to pursue the Activity.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Project is ongoing.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where a Project is pursued.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE is used to describe a characteristic of the Project.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The Attribute is the number of entities that make up the Set.

name: Set
definition_en: The group of entities, possibly construed as a collective, whose number changes.  'The union's membership has dwindled from 1.5 million in 1979 to a little more than 600000 today.'

name: Difference
definition_en: The number of entities by which the Set increases or decreases.  'Jaffna's student population has dwindled by more than a hundred.'

name: Path
definition_en: Any expression that gives information about points on the number scale that the Set traverses between the starting and ending point of its movement.  'The top three pulled away from the pack as the laps dwindled down.'

name: Final_number
definition_en: The number of entities in the Set afterwards.  'Church of England baptisms have dwindled from 365000 in 1940 to 150000 in 1995.'

name: Initial_number
definition_en: The initial number of entities in the Set.  'The number of Medline searches has greatly proliferated from 7 million to 120 million.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The rate of change of the value.   'Those systems proved popular, and they quickly proliferated.'

name: Correlated_variable
definition_en: The Correlated_variable is an ordered progression of positions or values (most often a sequence of spatial locations) that the (dependent) Attribute is measured against. The Correlated_variable is metaphorically mapped onto the progression of time, and in the absence of this FE, changes in the number in the Setare simply measured against (forward-directional) time.  'Mushrooms and deep moss proliferate as you get deeper into the trail.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs,  secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs.  'Our supply had completely dwindled with our war fatalities and we needed a small supply on hand.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the proliferation takes place.  'Referrals multiply when patients know you care. '

name: Group
definition_en: The Group within which the number of entities in the Set changes in the specified way.  'During the last third of the nineteenth century, fraternal orders, featuring reform and ritual, proliferated among the urban middle classes.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is the time-frame in which the change in number occurs.  'Oh, my aching software: Worms and viruses proliferated in 2003.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time over which the change takes place.   'Cellular phone and paging device ownership by adolescents has proliferated over the past years.'

name: Initial_correlate
definition_en: The value, location, or state-of-affairs that corresponds to the Initial_number of entities in the Set.  'From California to Massachusetts, these predators proliferate uncontrollably and unsustainably.'

name: Final_correlate
definition_en: The value, location, or state-of-affairs that corresponds to the Final_number in the Set.  'From California to Massachusetts, these predators proliferate uncontrollably and unsustainably.'

name: Place
definition_en: A location where the Set changes in number.

name: Initial_state
definition_en: A description that presents the Set's state before the change in the number of entities making it up as an independent predication.   'The human population has dwindled from being world dominators to simple survivors.'

name: Final_state
definition_en: A description that presents the Set's state after  the change in the Attribute's value as an independent predication.   ''

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which the saliency Attribute is appropriate and under consideration.  ' If you are asked to search for the plus sign with red-vertical and green-horizontal elements, all the red and green plus signs may seem to become salient.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of the Entity which is under discussion, namely perceptual salience.  'The diagram, (a frequency distribution chart) shows a prominently conspicuous region of stars that extend from the extremely bright and hot stars to the faint and cool variety. '

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the prominence from the norm or from the value for another Entity.  'The gobies (the family Gobiidae) are not a very conspicuous part of the fish fauna in most of. the Mekong Basin.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having  a particular salience.  'The affection for American culture seemed more prominent last year.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular degree of prominence.  'Europa is also prominent at a distance of 25000 km and Io is visible in the distance.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE refers to the location where the Entity has a prominence of some Attribute.

name: Entity
definition_en: The name of a particular entity that otherwise might be interpreted as having a broader reference.  'Private quarters are in the tower proper with a chapel at the very top'

name: Intended_referent
definition_en: The entity that the speaker intends to refer to using the Entity in a more restricted sense. The Intended_referent is typically a part of the referent that the hearer might have identified based on the broader use of the Entity.  'The gatehouse providing entry from the outer defences to the Castle PROPER was erected by King James III and originally formed part of a splendid fore-front .'

name: Criteria
definition_en: A representation of the conditions upon which membership to a Subset of a Group is determined. 'This drug can reduce the rate of heart disease significantly in people over 50.'

name: Subset
definition_en: The members of a Group that fulfill particular Criteria to belong to a Subset of the Group. 'California has a high divorce rate compared to other states.'

name: Group
definition_en: A general collection of entities which are judged against the Criteria to determine membership in a Subset. 'Georgia's literacy rate is the highest in the world.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description of how the Ratio compares to expectations. 'We see similar crime rates in the two areas.'

name: Ratio
definition_en: The numerical representation of the size of the Subset relative to the size of the Group. 'New laws have raised crime rates by 5%'

name: Denoted_quantity
definition_en: The quantity denoted by phrases headed by the Target.

name: Mass
definition_en: A substance that is being quantified.

name: Individuals
definition_en: A collection of entities, either quantifiable physical beings (e.g. toads) or quantifiable units whether physical or not (e.g. dollars).

name: Q_prop
definition_en: A property of the Denoted_quantity.

name: Reference_quantity
definition_en: A relatively precise quantity in some oft-used form that is used as the basis for defining the Denoted_quantity.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Protection
definition_en: The person, entity, or action that prevents harm to an Asset.  'The tabloid's deal with the woman shielded Schwarzenegger.'

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Danger threatened the Asset.    'To make his way on a foreign soil, he needed different guardians from those that protected him in his own birthplace .'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Danger threatens.  'Regardless of the distribution media, USPTO information is safeguarded before, during, and after dissemination from improper access and modification.'

name: Danger
definition_en: A situation that could damage the Asset.   'Other nations tended to muffle or modulate their occasional annoyance with the country that was their shield against the Soviet threat.'

name: Asset
definition_en: Something desirable possessed by or directly associated with the Protection which might be lost or damaged.  'Almost 10 years later, that agreement insulated Microsoft from liability on copyright claims over the graphical user interface (GUI).'

name: Means
definition_en: An event involving the Protection that removes the Asset from potential harm through the Danger.  'Jackson secured the flank by timely charging the enemy and driving him back.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by a volitional agent acting as a Protection which interacts with an undergoer to accomplish the security of the Asset from harm by the Danger.  'Your Brake Pads Parts order is encrypted and safeguarded with the latest SSL technology for a protected and secure shopping experience!'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the protecting event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In cases of agentive Protection, it may indicate salient characteristics of an agent that also affect the action (carefully).  'Finally, I thank all of the curators of all of the museums around the world who have carefully protected the Ivory-billed specimens in their care.'

name: Event_description
definition_en: Tthis FE is used for phrases that describe the protecting event as a whole.  It applies to appraisals of the event, typically a judgment of its expectedness. The notion of appraisal requires a factive portrayal of the event.  It also applies to descriptions of the protecting event as a role filler in another frame.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description or characteristic of the Protection.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the act of protecting logically follows.

name: Duration
definition_en: FN: This FE denotes the length of time in which the Asset is protected.

name: Depictive
definition_en: FN: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: FN: This extra-thematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the protecting event.

name: Protester
definition_en: The individual (or individuals) who holds an opinion on an Issue or Side.  'On 8 May a student demonstration was attended by a large number of workers.'

name: Issue
definition_en: The matter, usually concerning a course of action, which the Protester has an positive or negative opinion about.  'Hundreds gathered this afternoon to demonsrate for women's rights.'

name: Side
definition_en: The party or individual (generally associated with a particular position on an Issue) that the Protester sides with.  'Violent protests against the government are sure to break out.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Protester supports or opposes something, or expresses views on the Issue.

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Protesters express their opinions.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is a proposition denoting a state of affairs from which the Protester's expressing his or her views on the Issue logically follows.

name: Action
definition_en: An action taken by a Side or a view that the Side takes on an issue which the Protester either supports or opposes.  'Several hundred Tibetans, already worried by inflation, took to the streets to protest at the new measures.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describes the person or element that is protesting.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the a Protest which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Protester that affect the action (reluctantly, meekly).

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Protester takes Sides on an Issue .

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time of the protest.  'The month-long protest is slowly losing momentum.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The frequency with which the protest occurs.  'Police have grown increasingly frustrated at the nightly demonstrations.'

name: Host
definition_en: The Host is the individual (or group of individuals) that own or control the Residence and allow the  Lodger to temporarily stay there.

name: Lodger
definition_en: The Lodger is the individual who is given permission to lodge in the Residence.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the conditions under which the Host provides lodging.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Host provides a Residence to the Lodger

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the Host provides a temporary Residence.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose is the goal of the Host in allowing the Lodger to stay.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the cognitive cause of the Host's granting of permission.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the provision of lodging which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Host that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Host whereby they communicate or enact the granting of permission to stay in the Residence.  ''

name: Residence
definition_en: The location controlled by the Host which the Lodger stays at temporarily.

name: Near_profiled_region
definition_en: A region of space located relative to a Ground that is maximally relevant near the Ground, with decreasing applicability away from the Ground.

name: Ground
definition_en: An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Profiled_region.

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount of deviation from an idealized expected distance of the Profiled_region from the Ground.

name: Distant_profiled_region
definition_en: A region of space located relative to a Ground that is not relevant near the Ground, with increasing applicability away from the Ground.

name: Institution
definition_en: A permanent organization with a socially important purpose.

name: Domain
definition_en: The concern of the Institution-- broadly speaking, the aspect of society that they affect.  'At one emergency financial service, I double-checked people's math to make sure they weren't blowing the budget.'

name: Target_group
definition_en: The members of the public whom the Institution is intended to serve.  'PG & E was the electric service for much of the West Coast.'

name: Service_action
definition_en: The action performed or enabled by the Institution for the Target_group.  'Reach Out ! is a service for helping young Australians through tough times.'

name: Publisher
definition_en: The entity that acts on behalf of the Author to release the Work to the public.

name: Medium
definition_en: The format utilized by the Author to create the Work.

name: Work
definition_en: The creation of the Author that is made public by the Publisher.

name: Time
definition_en: The date when the Work is available or is expected to be available.

name: Audience
definition_en: The subset of the population that the Work is targeted towards or released to.

name: Author
definition_en: The person or entity that is responsible for the detailed construction of the content of the Work.  It is normally expressed in place of the Publisher FE, but the Publisher may cooccur with Author, appearing as an adjunct.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The situation that the Author or Publisher hopes to bring about by publishing.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Publisher releases the work.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the action that clarifies, in a holistic way, the details of how the publication event unfolded, including comparisons to other events ('the same way') and states of performers of the action that influence the act itself ('peevishly').

name: Means
definition_en: The action taken by the Author or Publisher that makes the Work publicly available.

name: Perceiver
definition_en: The being who has a perceptual experience, generally construed to be not on purpose.   'When she looked back, Maria glimpsed an arm clawing around the corner.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The entity or phenomenon that the perceiver experiences with his or her senses. It is typically expressed as Object with verbs.  'The waiter glimpsed a fly disappearing under the surface of the soup.'

name: Body_part
definition_en: The Body_part is the location on the body where the perceptual experience  takes place.  It is typically expressed in a PP.  'Mata Hari turned to her lawyer as her eyes glimpsed the blindfold.'

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: The Location_of_protagonist during the perceptual experience. It is typically expressed in a from-PP.  'She had only glimpsed him briefly from behind a veil.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This frame element is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver (see above), that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception.  'Hard to be certain what I glimpsed through the crack of the door.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Perceiver during the event of perception.

name: Ground
definition_en: The perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is  experienced (or not experienced) by the Perceiver.   'Had he caught a glimpse of her face among the crowd?'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of properties of perception, such as: clearly, loudly, etc.  'Pat secretly glimpsed the designs for a new headquarters.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree indicates the degree to which the Perception is experienced.  'A nightmare creature, barely glimpsed in the swirling dense smoke, was beating at the flames coming from its own body.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action whereby the Perceiver perceives.  'He just glimpsed the car by craning his neck.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time, generally construed as punctual, at which the Perceiver or the Body_part perceives the Phenomenon.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end.

name: Agent
definition_en: The volitional actor who intends to achieve a goal. ' Microsoft 's goal of delivering a million copies in the first year is trifling compared to the 25 million copies of Windows it has shipped since May 1990.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The action or state of affairs that the Agent wants to achieve.  'The company missed its goal of getting a thousand third-party software packages shipped.'

name: Means
definition_en: A Means is an object or action that is used or designed to achieve a particular Goal.  ' The goal of treatment was to lower diastolic blood pressure below 85 mm  Hg .'

name: Domain
definition_en: This frame element expresses a sphere of activity within which an Agent has a Goal.  'His political goal is the restoration of the monarchy'

name: Time
definition_en: This Frame Element expresses a time period during which an Agent had a particular Goal.  'But the main goal of the 1990s could be to transform a big , heavily armed standing army into a more flexible force '

name: Restrictor
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate a spatial or temporal or individual framework relative to  which the Goal is said to hold. More than one Restrictor can be mentioned.  'Our goal for Japan for next yearis to sell 2000 units' 'Our sales target for that week was 200 units'

name: Attribute
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate an Attribute for which it is the Agent's goal that it have or reach a particular Value .  'We exceeded our production target of 2000 units'

name: Value
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate which Value the Agent wants the Attribute to reach.  'GM has a production target of 2,000,000 units'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies the Depictive phrase describing an actor or an undergoer of an action during their participation in the event.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the state of an Agent that affects the nature of the event as the Agent brings about the end of the Fire.  'The firefighters heroically extinguished the flames.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the event.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Agent puts out the Fire.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Fire goes out.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual or group that causes the Fire to no longer burn.  'The firefighters extinguished the wildfire.'

name: Fire
definition_en: The combustion process that the Agent causes to end.  'It took four days before the firewas extinguished.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent puts out a Fire

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which an Agent puts out the Fire.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes the how near the Agent is to puting out the Fire.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Quantity
definition_en: The Quantity-denoting Target word. 'I had a heap of troubles.'

name: Mass
definition_en: A substance that is being quantified. 'A modicum of seepage on the floor is to be expected.'

name: Individuals
definition_en: A collection of entities. 'A number of concerned citizens have raised objections.'

name: Q_prop
definition_en: A property of the Quantity.  'John bought a large heap of old National Geograhics at the flea market.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Entity
definition_en: Entity identifies the concept or substance being quantified by a Quantity. 'My blood-sugar level is high.' 'The patients were sorted by level of radiation exposure.'

name: Quantity
definition_en: Identifies the Quantity-denoting target word. 'Their level of productivity decreased with each hour of overtime worked.'

name: Value
definition_en: Value identifies the numerical amount of the Entity. 'He wrote me a check in the amount of $500.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Quantity. 'He received an appropriate amount of replies to his online survey.'

name: Arguers
definition_en: A group of people in an argument.

name: Arguer1
definition_en: A person who is arguing with Arguer2.

name: Arguer2
definition_en: The person who is being argued with by Arguer1.  'Why are you arguing with us.'

name: Issue
definition_en: The the thing the the Arguers are arguing over or about.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The frequency with which the Arguers have a disagreement.

name: Depictive
definition_en: A state of the Arguers, Arguer1, or Arguer2 which saliently affects the perception of the action.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that the Arguers spend in the altercation.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the dispute which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Arguers that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully). 'They squabbled heatedly long into the night.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action that the Arguers perform in order to quarrel with each other.

name: Medium
definition_en: The equipment, language, or other entity that the Arguers use to pursue their argument.  'When they couldn't get together, they bickered over the phone.'  'Having them squabble in french is better than if I understood it.'

name: Amount_of_discussion
definition_en: The degree to which the argument has been finished.  'If you don't believe me now, we'll just have to argue it out.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Arguers or Arguer1 hope to bring about.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Arguers quarrel

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the argument takes place.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The person asking a question generally occurs as the External Argument of verb and noun targets:  'Pat quizzed me about where I had been.' 'Pat's question surprised me. '

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is most frequently the NP Object of a target verb.  However, with the verb inquire, Addressee can only occur as an of-PP and with a noun target, Addressee occurs in a PP Complement or as a possessive : 'Pat questioned me about where I had been.' '"Do you often come here?" Kim inquired of the person sitting next to her.'  'My question to you is straightforward.' 'Kim's interrogation by the police was long.'

name: Message
definition_en: The Message, or content of the question, usually takes the form of a direct quote or an embedded question with a verb target:  '"What are you doing?" Kim inquired.' 'Kim inquired what I was doing.' With noun targets, Message is not common (as Topic occurs more  frequently).  However, Message does occur in a PP Complement with the noun question:  'The answer to your question of how the company makes money is simply that it doesn't. '

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic occurs very frequently in this frame with both noun and verb targets. It generally occurs as a PP Complement: 'Pat inquired about train times.' 'Pat's inquiry about train times fell on deaf ears.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the question:  'Kim questioned me over the phone.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing the request.  'I slowly asked the question again.'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The body movement may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal Cause, the Agent's mental or emotional state.  Internal Cause is expressed in a PP Complement:  'Kim asked me several questions in frustration.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the questioning occurs.  'I inquired yesterday.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.  'I asked twice.'

name: Employee
definition_en: The person who is obligated to perform some task in order to receive compensation.  'I just quit yesterday!'

name: Employer
definition_en: The person (or institution) in whose employ  the Employee stood.  'He replaces Michael Lawrie, 50, who quit IBM to run Siebel.'

name: Field
definition_en: The Field that one works in. 'He might quit showbusiness for years.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which an Employee leaves the job.   ' Los Angeles junior high school teacher named Patricia Ann Carruthers quit her job in a huff.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Employee quits the employment of the Employer.  'Actually Iquit  in the lobby before I got to my office.'

name: Position
definition_en: The label given to a particular type of service that the employer quits. ' I  quit as a professional player!'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Employee quits the employment of the Employer. 'John resigned  to join the private sector.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when an Employee quits the employment of the Employer.  'Guess who just quit today!'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Employee quits.  'North quit over the mismanagement scandal.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means whereby the act of quitting is accomplished 'Lately, many workers have been quitting by simply not showing up for work.'

name: Self_mover
definition_en: This is the entity which moves under its own power.

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

name: Path
definition_en: A relation to a landmark that describes the trajectory in the midst of the motion.  (It is thus neither a Source nor the Intended_goal.)

name: Intended_goal
definition_en: Any expression which tells where the Self_mover intends to end up as a result of the motion.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

name: Means
definition_en: An event involving the Self_mover that results in the Self_mover moving in the specified way.

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the Self_mover moves.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: A second moving object that moves in coordination with the Self_mover.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Self_mover during the action.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.

name: Path_shape
definition_en: The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Self_mover, taken simultaneously.

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction in which the Self_mover goes.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the motion takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Self_mover wishes to bring about.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The device or bodypart that serves to move the Self_mover.

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The length of time that the Self_mover spends away from the Source.

name: Result
definition_en: The state of the Self_mover at the end of the event.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Self_mover.

name: Reciprocation
definition_en: An event paired with the motion, which explains why the motion is expected. In particular, Reciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished by the motion, and/or is paired with the motion as the other side of an agreement.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time of departure and which the departure is taken to be a part of.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: A larger conceptualization that includes the departing as an integral part. The departure expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.

name: New_situation
definition_en: An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Self_mover), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the departing.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the departing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.

name: Coordinated_event
definition_en: The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event (it does not allow states) that the departing is rhythmically aligned with. (This would then further require that the departing be iterated.)  The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.

name: Distance
definition_en: The distance from the Source that the Self_mover ends up.

name: Person
definition_en: The Person whose race is being described.

name: Event
definition_en: A type of occurrence whose effects extend a certain distance.

name: Participant
definition_en: An entity that is conceived as driving the Event.  'Their missile range has decreased, since we have degraded their sensors.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity which is deployable by the Participant to interact with things within a certain distance.  'Their laser range is four times ours .'

name: Distance
definition_en: The spatial extent over which the Participant can interact in an Event.  'Our range is smaller than theirs.' 'Normal people have a reach of around one meter.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The conditions under which the description of a Participant's range holds.  'The patient has a lesser range of motion in cold weather.'

name: Rank
definition_en: The Rank itself, usually denoted by the noun.

name: Item
definition_en: An entity which holds a particular Rank.

name: Entity
definition_en: The item which is described in terms of its expectedness in the context.  'The entire day was spent on the project .'

name: Perpetrator
definition_en: This is the person who forces another person to have sexual intercourse with him or her against the other person's will.

name: Victim
definition_en: This is the person who is forced to engage in sexual intercourse against his or her will.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Event
definition_en: The rape of a Victim by the Perpetrator.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Perpetrator by which the sexual crime is accomplished.

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the event occurs.  'The lawyer said the woman was raped on a night of madness '

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE is any object used to commit the crime.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that a rape event takes place.  ' The eleven year old told the court that she was raped three times.'

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist acts or is apt to act with some degree of consideration regarding the circumstances and possible consequences of an Action he or she may perform.  'I feel that most do, but typically people are rash, and often reach anger and hostility quickly.' 'I think it was patient of me to wait another month.'

name: Action
definition_en: The Action is carried out by the Protagonist with or without regard for the circumstances under which it is performed or consideration of possible consequences.  'What he did was impetuous and quite irrational - some might say ill-considered.' 'Caryn thinks Tom made a rash choice by electing to move to the new camp.'

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time when the Protagonist acts with (or without) consideration regarding an Action.  'Were n't you impetuous when you were young?'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Action of the Protagonist deviates from the expected in its rashness.

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Event
definition_en: The Event whose Rate is being described.   'He was rapidly losing his patience.'

name: Rate
definition_en: The Rate at which something happens during an Event.  'Anthony marveled at the rapid rate of production.'

name: Degree
definition_en: How much the Rate deviates from a neutral or expected standard.  'It was followed by an extremely rapid deterioration of order.'

name: Agent
definition_en: A participant in an Event that is responsible for its unexpected Rate.  'She was really fast at shorthand.'

name: Event
definition_en: The Event that occurs at a certain Rate.   'Production rates have risen in the last year.'

name: Rate
definition_en: How much a particular salient quantity involved in an Event changes over time. 'His heart rate quickened.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any characterization of the Rate that is not covered by another more specific FE.  'This camera is capable of shooting at high speeds.'

name: Entity
definition_en: A participant in the Event who is responsible for the indicated Rate. 'The mating rate of cats has dropped dramatically.'

name: Type
definition_en: A name of the Rate of or description of the particular category the Rate belongs to.  'His heart rate was unusually fast.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree compares the given rate for the standard or familiar rate for a given Event.

name: Ratifier
definition_en: The individual or body that confirms a Proposal negotiated or created by another party, causing it to become binding in a jurisdiction represented by the Ratifier.  In the case of direct democratic ratification, the jurisdiction and the Ratifier are the same.  'If we ratify Management 's plan , we 'll have to take a drug test every week !'

name: Proposal
definition_en: The idea or course of action proposed by another individual or body which the Ratifier endorses and makes binding.  'President Aleksander Kwasniewski ratified protocols to the Europol Convention.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Ratifier makes the Proposal binding.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the Ratifier ratifies the Proposal.  ''

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose is the goal of the Ratifier when they ratify the Proposal.  'The South had to ratify these amendments to be readmitted to the Union'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the cognitive cause of the Ratifier's ratification.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the allowing which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Ratifier that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'It is no coincidence that the EU, on behalf of its 25 member states, has eagerly ratified Rotterdam and other treaties, no doubt seeing it as the perfect opportunity.'

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Ratifier whereby they make binding the Proposal.  'After Inuit approve the Labrador Inuit Land Claim Agreement, the province will ratify it by submitting it to the provincial cabinet for approval, and then signing it.'

name: Reader
definition_en: The one who examines a Text to understand it.

name: Text
definition_en: The entity that contains linguistic symbols.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Sought_phenomenon
definition_en: A particular characteristic or thing that the Reader intends to process. Read Chapter 7 only for the major concepts..

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the reading event that implicates details of how the event unfolds or is carried out (e.g. "the same way"); additionally used for descriptions of the Reader that also affect the event (e.g. "eagerly").

name: Means
definition_en: An act that allows the Reader to read in the specified manner. 'I skimmed the book by reading just the section headings and the first sentences after.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose is the reason for which the Reader reads the Text.

name: Time
definition_en: When the reading event takes place. 'Charlie often reads the newspaper at night.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the reading event takes place. 'Surprisingly, few of the students read much at all in the designated reading rooms.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Textual_location
definition_en: The context wherein the Reader reads.

name: Topic
definition_en: The idea that an implicit Text or texts focuses on.  'I love reading about history .'

name: Frequency
definition_en: An assessment of how many iterations of (the specified kind of) reading occur per time.  'I do n't read often ; but when I do ...'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The person or people to whom the Speaker is directing the reading of the Text.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The person who reads the Text aloud.

name: Text
definition_en: The source from which the Speaker reads.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Speaker reads the Text aloud.

name: Source
definition_en: The medium from which the Text is read.

name: Time
definition_en: When the reading takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The result that the Speaker is trying to achieve by reading aloud.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the reading takes place.

name: Means
definition_en: The method by which the Text is read aloud by the Speaker. 'My mother always read to me by candle light.'

name: Reader
definition_en: The one who examines a Text to understand it.

name: Text
definition_en: The entity that contains linguistic symbols.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Sought_phenomenon
definition_en: A particular characteristic or thing that the Reader intends to process. Read Chapter 7 only for the major concepts..

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act that allows the Reader to read in the specified manner. 'I skimmed the book by reading just the section headings and the first sentences after.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose is the reason for which the Reader reads the Text.

name: Time
definition_en: When the reading event takes place. 'Charlie often reads the newspaper at night.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the reading event takes place. 'Surprisingly, few of the students read much at all in the designated reading rooms.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Context
definition_en: The context wherein the Reader reads a particular Text.

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who responds to a State_of_Affairs by performing some Action.  'Those are my reasons , " said Toby . '

name: Action
definition_en: The action that the Agent performs in response to a State_of_Affairs.  ' I find that all my reasons for postponing giving birth still apply '

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The eventuality  that motivates the Agent"s performing a particular Action in response to it.  '  My reason is that our cities are now designed round the motor car'

name: Content
definition_en: The Arguer wants the Addressee to entertain the Content, which can be a proposition to be believed or a course of action to be taken, based on the Support presented.'Jan argued that the evidence was inadmissable.'

name: Medium
definition_en: This FE identifies the physical or abstract setting in which the Content is conveyed.'Jan argued in writing that the evidence was inadmissable.'

name: Arguer
definition_en: The Arguer presents the Content before the Addressee.'Jan argued that the evidence was inadmissable.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: Addressee is the entity before whom the Arguer presents a Content. 'Jan argued to the court that the evidence was inadmissable.'

name: Support
definition_en: Support lends epistemic support to a claim, or provides a reason for a course of action.'Jan argued that gun was inadmissable as evidence because the police didn't have a search warrant.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifes the Manner in which an Arguer argues.'Jan argued convincingly that the evidence was inadmissable. '

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Arguer presents Content to an Addressee.'Jan argued the evidence was admissable by waving the warrant in the air.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies a phrase describing a participant in an action.'Jan argued that the evidence was inadmissable in a tuxedo.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an arguing event.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an arguing event occurs.'Jan argued the defendant's innocence beyond a shadow of a doubt.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which an Arguer makes an argument for the Content.  ' The government argued in August that the prisoners should not be released'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the location where an argument is made by an Arguer.  'The young men will be arguing their policies in the school auditorium.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The period of time for which the Arguer presents his or her reasoning to the Addressee.  'He argued for hours that chess is a sport '

name: Group
definition_en: An entity related to the Content.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The sentient entity that uses language in the written or spoken modality to reassure another person.  'He reassured her that she was his favorite ice-skating star. '

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer receives reassurance from the Speaker.  'He tried to reassure his potential customers that his company not only offered the best service, but also the most competitive prices. '

name: Message
definition_en: The Message is a proposition or set of propositions that the Speaker wants the Experiencer to believe in order to feel reassured.   'How do you reassure them that you really like them?  '

name: Situation
definition_en: The Situation is the problem plaguing the Experiencer, about which the Speaker  reassures them.  'The policeman reassured him about the safety of the neighborhood. '

name: Medium
definition_en: The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.

name: Amount_of_reassurance
definition_en: The amount of reassurance given. 'He never really fully reassured me about the situation.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive describes the state of the Speaker.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Speaker reassures the Experiencer.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Speaker reassures the Experiencer.  'Him mother reassured him with a pat on the back.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the reassurance takes place.

name: Rebel
definition_en: The individual or group within a society that attempts to overturn the Current_leadership, and possibly also the Current_order of governance.  'In 1641 there was a Catholic rebellion against the Protestants of Ulster, and English authority over the island was shaken.'  'In the summer he crushed Geoffrey's rebellion and compelled him to renounce his claim.'

name: Current_leadership
definition_en: The people currently in power, whom the Rebels attempt to overthrow.  'It was the first time that a man of such high rank had been put to death for rebellion against the king.'

name: Current_order
definition_en: The currently-existing system of authority or government.  'At the time they were in rebellion against the Catholic government.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location of the rebellion.  'It seems probably that rebellion in East Anglia was as rigorously suppressed as in Kent.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the rebellion takes place.  'Did you support the insurrection of 1854?'

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the Rebel rebels against the authorities.  'Those actions virtually guarantee that she will be facing an armed revolt within the week.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Rebel opposes and fights against the Current_leadership.  'He was wary of entering into complete and utter rebellion.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the Rebel or the rebellion not covered by more specific FEs.  'We face an increasingly violent insurgency with no end in sight.'

name: New_order
definition_en: The rebellion aims to install a New_order as their leader. This FE is more frequent with noun targets.

name: Result
definition_en: A result of the rebellion.  'The old guard is trying furiously to put an end to what has been an extremely headly rebellion.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time of the rebellion.  'The months-long insurgency has taken its toll on an already-reeling nation.'

name: Host
definition_en: The Host allows the Visitor to remain with him/her to acheive a goal.

name: Visitor
definition_en: The Visitor temporarily remains with the Host in order to achieve his/her purpose.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The goal of the Host in allowing the Visitor to enter the Host's location.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The person who acts to come into possession of the Theme.

name: Donor
definition_en: The person who gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity that changes possession, beginning in the possession of the Donor and ending up with the Recipient.

name: Purpose_of_donor
definition_en: The aim of the Donor, which they believe will be accomplished by giving  the Theme.  'Rural communities  received government subsidiesto ensure their continued viability..'

name: Means
definition_en: The act that the Recipient performs which brings about their reception of the Theme.  'She received the package by signing her name on the delivery certification.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Recipient comes into possession of the Theme.  'She received the package before the month was out.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Recipient comes into possession of the Theme.

name: Mode_of_transfer
definition_en: The system whereby the Theme travels (literally or metaphorically) so that the Recipient comes into possession of the Theme.  'I received it by e-mail.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Recipient or Theme during the action.  'I didn't expect to receive this steak absolutely raw!'

name: Manner
definition_en: The character of the Recipient which saliently affects the action, or a general description of the action itself.  'He slyly received the package without signing for it.'

name: Countertransfer
definition_en: A good given or a service rendered by the Recipient, in return for wich the Theme is given to the Recipient by the Donor.  'Shelley Walker of Washoe County?s Information Technology Department received $100 for her suggestion to create an electronic employee evaluation form. '

name: Path
definition_en: When the Theme is received physically by the Recipient from the Donor, the Path of motion of the Theme  may be specified.

name: Purpose_of_theme
definition_en: What the Recipient intends to do with the Theme.  'James Madison Memorial High School received $1,000 to purchase instruments for school orchestra and band programs. '

name: Role
definition_en: A role that the Theme is intended to fill by the Donor.  'He received the book as a gift from his uncle.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: The person who acts to come into possession of the Theme.

name: Donor
definition_en: The person who gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity that changes possession, beginning in the possession of the Donor and ending up with the Recipient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The aim of the Recipient, which they believe will be accomplished by accepting the Theme.  'She accepted the ring so that his suspicions would not be aroused.'

name: Means
definition_en: The act that the Recipient performs which brings about their reception of the Theme.  'She received the package by signing her name on the delivery certification.'

name: Mode_of_transfer
definition_en: The system whereby the Theme travels (literally or metaphorically) so that the Recipient comes into possession of the Theme.  'I received it by e-mail.'

name: Protagonist_1
definition_en: The particpant in a reciprocal event that is encoded as the subject of an active-form sentence or as a by-PP in a passive. `'You can't argue politics with foreigners,' sighed the policeman.'

name: Protagonist_2
definition_en: The participant in a reciprocal event that is coded in a with-PP. 'We have been arguing the point with the inspector at claims branch for many many months and we just seem to go round in circles. '

name: Protagonists
definition_en: The jointly expressed participants in a reciprocal activity. 'They were gossiping about the weather and American football.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the sentient entity that creates a permanent record of the Phenomenon.  'Police informed Mr Wong that they recorded the attack as a racial incident.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The Phenomenon is the entity or situation in the world of which a Agent becomes aware.   'Adams took some very good advice and meticulously recorded the events that ensued.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Agent  that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifes the action whereby the Agent creates a record of the Phenomenon.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent creates the record of the Phenomenon.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The goal that the Agent has in mind in creating a record of the Phenomenon.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Agent uses an Instrument in order to create a record of the Phenomenon or to measure an Entity's Value for a specified Attribute.

name: Attribute
definition_en: That feature of the Entity which is under discussion.   'When Mohammed was sentenced to death in the Anti-Terrorism Court in Rawalpindi the court recorded his age as  17 or 18.'

name: Value
definition_en: The Value of the Entity that is recorded for the specified Attribute.  'In the fiscal year 2000, Nepal's imports from China and Tibet were recorded at 166.6 million dollars.'

name: Entity
definition_en: An Entity for which the Agent records the Value of an Attribute.  'At the time the Army recorded him as a married resident of the Town of Two Creeks.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity in which the Agent creates a record of their impression of the Phenomenon.  'In fact, Pepys recorded everything in his diary.'

name: Language
definition_en: The symbolic system used by the Agent.  ' I recorded my notes in English, usually translating from French.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent sets down the facts.  'From what the book says, these events were recorded in the Chamber of Mazarbul .'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Phenomenon has been documented.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The amount of times the Agent records something per unit of time.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE denotes a duration in which the recording event occurred iteratively.

name: Record
definition_en: The Record is the entity in which events or accounts are permanently recorded. 'She kept a record of how many times he asked to borrow money.'

name: Data
definition_en: The Data is the information which is recorded in the Record.  It is often expressed as a prepositional phrase. 'Andy kept a log of the girls he had dated.' 'His assistant maintained the records of customer payments.'

name: Recorder
definition_en: The Recorder is the person who records the Data in the Record. 'Shirley's log of her favorite eateries grew every day.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity is the person or institution for which the Record is maintained. 'She keeps the books for the advertising firm.' 'The bank's records were not ready for the unexpected audit.'

name: Type
definition_en: The Type refers to the kind of Record being kept. 'Molly was in charge of the finacial records at the small law firm.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Record.  'Moria's bank kept detailed books.'

name: Material
definition_en: What a Record is made of (if applicable).

name: Medium
definition_en: The Medium is the language in which a Record is composed, or the physical medium (radio, ink) in which it is distributed.

name: Place
definition_en: The region where the Record is sold, circulated, or otherwise popular

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The Time at which the Record was created.

name: Title
definition_en: The Title of a Record.

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic is what the Record is about.

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which the Record was produced; its purpose.

name: Patient
definition_en: The    Patient may either be expressed as the External Argument or, as in Health.Cure, may occur as the possessor of the Affliction (an example of FE conflation):  'Pat is convalescing from surgery.' 'Pat's wound is healing.' In the second example, Pat's wound is the Body_part, but Pat's is also an instantiation of the Patient.

name: Affliction
definition_en: This FE is the injury, pain or disease experienced by the Patient.  Affliction occurs either as an External Argument of verbs or as a PP Complement of nouns or verbs:  'The wound is healing well.' 'Pat's wound is healing well.' 'Pat is recovering from scarlet fever.' 'Pat's recovery from scarlet fever was very rapid. '

name: Body_part
definition_en: Where Body Part is expressed as a separate constituent (rather than in phrases such as the wound on Pat's arm), it occurs as an External Argument:  'Pat's arm healed up quickly.'  Body Part is treated as a separate Frame Element although it may be viewed as metonymic for Affliction.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Patient's state diverges from their former illness.

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Patient that results in their recovery. 'You will recover more quickly by getting simple bed-rest.'

name: Company
definition_en: An individual or group of individuals that the Patient is generally in the presence of during convalescence.  'She had confidently expected to convalesce with her brother and his wife.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the recovery takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the recovery takes place.

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity that is in motion, and changes path due to the action of an Agent or due to a Cause.

name: Original_path
definition_en: The route that the Theme was originally headed for.  In cases when the Theme is an intentional actor or is controlled by an intentional actor, the Original_path correlates with the (former) plan of the actor.  In other cases, the Original_path corresponds to what would be expected for the path of the Theme from general principles or physics.  (In some cases, the Original_path may indicate the intended destination, and not just the path, of the Theme.)  'VTA detoured motorists from southbound I-880 onto Airport Boulevard to access Coleman Avenue.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Theme ends up travelling after being diverted.   'Traffic was redirected Tuesday along Melrose Avenue to make way for the scoreboard columns, Mellecker said.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The location the Theme ends up in after being redirected.   'Not knowing any better, he redirected people to the city center.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the redirection of motion occurs.  'Last Tuesday they were detouring everybody down onto 5th avenue .'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the redirection which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Anything flagged as suspect by this system would be carefully diverted to another nearby area, remote from public access. and well shielded, for a second screening .'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Theme or Agent during the redirection.  'The emergency personnel redirected the cars back towards the border, unaware of the recent conflagration.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location at which the redirection occurs.  'They redirected us <fex name="">at the corner of Alstone and Bokchoy Avenue.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE is used for expressions that indicate motion along a line from the current deitic center towards a reference point (which may be implicit) that does not necessarily correspond to the Goal.  Often Direction is defined with reference to the canonical orientation of the Theme, the orientation imposed by an implicit observer, or the inherent orientation of the scene.  'Flight 93 left Newark, NJ, earlier that day, bound for San Francisco, but it was hijacked by four terrorists who diverted it back toward Washington, DC . '

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Agent intends to bring about by redirecting the Theme.  'She was talking about how the passengers diverted the plane in order to protect the nation's capital.'

name: Agent
definition_en: An individual that determines the change in course of the Theme.  'When we ended up over in Marrakech, or Dakar, they diverted us up to Tobruk.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event that brings about the change in the Path of the Theme.  'We even got a bonus morning in Tokyo's international airport when a bad storm diverted us on the way to Asia.'

name: Means
definition_en: The method by which the Agent redirects the Theme.

name: Source_of_information
definition_en: The Source_of_information is referred to as a source of information related to the current text.  'The accreting matter forms a disc whose instabilities trigger outbursts (see Lasota 2001 for a review of the instability model).'

name: Information
definition_en: The Source_of_information contains Information that the reader is directed to.  'The accreting matter forms a disc whose instabilities trigger outbursts (see Lasota 2001 for a review of the instability model). '

name: Speaker
definition_en: The person who uses the Name  to refer to the Entity.   'The Lord, who was charmed by her beauty, addressed her as 'than kaadhali!' (My darling) and hence the name.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The entity that is designated by the Speaker with the Name used.  'And that's the reason why we called him 'Tom' when his real name was actually John. '

name: Name
definition_en: The linguistic form used by the Speaker to refer to the Entity.   'A male voice answered the call, and Jones addressed the man as "Johnny."'

name: Time
definition_en: The point of time or interval when the Speaker uses the Name.  'No one had ever called her "my lady".'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Describes the Name.  'Our new name for Jack is Jill.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The sentient entity that effects a change in the Entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the change of the Entity is caused.  'The House of Representatives, on a bipartisan basis, sought to reform the program this year.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Entity differs from its former state at the end of the reform.  'I am trying to completely overhaul my diet, and i need help.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the  event causing the change of the Entity which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly), general descriptions comparing events (the same way), and salient characteristics of the Agent that also affect the action (carefully).

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which reform event logically follows. In many cases, the state of affairs denoted is specifically one that the Agent takes as a reason for reforming the entity.  'But his great-grandson, Aurangzeb (1618-1707), reformed the policy due to religious conflicts. '

name: Entity
definition_en: This FE denotes a complex, abstract, human-created entity with interdependent parts which has either deteriorated or is no longer adequate for its purpose given a change in circumstances and which the Agent therefore wants to modify.  'Particular attention will be devoted to recent proposals to reform UK competition policy.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by effecting a change in the Entity.  'Indeed, as the world becomes increasingly paperless, it would be prudent to consider overhauling the rules in order to adapt them to a digitalized society.'

name: Initial_category
definition_en: The category of which the Entity is a member before the Agent causes a change in its makeup.  'Since 1986, the Vietnamese Government has performed a 'doi moi' (renovation) policy that reformed the economy from central planning economy to market.'

name: Final_category
definition_en: The category that the Entity belongs to after it has undergone the change.  'We have also reformed the office managing system from a "proprietorship" to a "partnership".'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the steps or actions directly enabling reform.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: An alternative description of expressed action

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE is used for phrases that describe the event of reforming as a whole .

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE describes the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the reform process.

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time over which reforming takes place

name: Cause
definition_en: This FE is for non-human causes, such as a processes or institutions, responsible for reform.    'Thus , radical reform restructures rape offences in ways that it is hoped will facilitate the prosecution process without jeopardising the interests of the accused .'

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the reformation occurs.

name: Cognizer
