definition_en: The Cognizer is the one that makes a Judgment. This role is typically expressed as the External Argument (or in a by-PP in passives).  'The boss appreciates you for your diligence.' 'The boss is very appreciative of my work.'

name: Evaluee
definition_en: Evaluee is the person or thing that a judgment is made with respect to. With verbs this FE is typically expressed as Object:  'He regarded her poorly.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: There may be a constituent expressing the Explanation for the Cognizer's judgment. It is usually a for-PP.  'I think highly of you for your honesty.'

name: Role
definition_en: Role is used for the capacity in which the Evaluee is judged, and is expressed in as-PPs.  'My high regard for you as a composer is due strictly to political concerns. '</def-root >

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies any expression describing the state of a participant in the event.  'We hold him in low esteem, certain that he will never redeem himself.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Cognizer's judgment which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions of events (the same way, presumptuously, secretly).

name: Extent_of_acclaim
definition_en: The Extent_of_acclaim is a description of the number or locales of the Cognizers.  'He is widely held in high regard.'

name: Judgment
definition_en: A description (from the point of view of the Cognizer) of the position of the Evaluee on a scale of approval.  'I hold him in the highest esteem.'

name: Interior
definition_en: A region of space located inside a Ground.

name: Ground
definition_en: An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Interior, Surface, or Boundary.

name: Surface
definition_en: The region located outside of, but in contact with, the Ground.

name: Boundary
definition_en: The region associated with the boundary of the Ground.

name: Exterior
definition_en: The region which is not located inside or in contact with the Ground.

name: Entity
definition_en: The concrete or abstract thing that is brought into an earlier state in which it was more effective and powerful.  'The reinvigoration of the tourism economy is recognised by many as an ambitious but necessary objective.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent puts the Entity into a state of renewed vigor.  'We revitalized the Golden Mountaineer Card, and we gave seniors a prescription drug benefit.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Agent brings about the change in the Entity's state.   'New York's distinction as America's tax cut leader has revitalized the economy in every corner of the state.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent brings about the revitalization of the Entity.  'Older neighborhoods throughout the area should be revitalized in order to be retained as neighborhoods having unique identities.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent causes the renewal of the Entity.  'Production was revitalized last June.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the action that the Agent performs in order so as to bring about the reinvigoration of the Entity.  'Natalie Cole resuscitated her career by recording a posthumous duet with her father on his old hit "Unforgettable".'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'They assessed the effectiveness of four different species of native trees for rapid rejuvenation of the mined land.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain within which the Entity is affected.  'Course wares and websites should be changed and renewed creatively often.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times that an Entity is caused to return to a more effective state.  'Ancient Egypt twice fell into a similar state of decrepitude, and was twice rejuvenated and suffused with energy and artistic creativeness.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event or state whose occurrence brings about the Entity's return to a vigorous state.  'Rock has been rejuvenated creatively and commercially by hip-hop-inspired rock acts.'

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole, either appraisals of the event, or descriptions of the rejuvenation event as role fillers in other frames.   'Blair's career was miraculously revitalized, personal liberties were compromised, and the global neocon war-agenda moved forward.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The device used by the Agent to help accomplish the action indicated by the target.

name: Role
definition_en: Role is used for the capacity in which the Entity is Rejuvinated, and is expressed in as-PPs.

name: Result
definition_en: The end state of the Rejuvination action.

name: Concept_1
definition_en: The concept which is linked to Concept_2.    'High death rates among smokers connect cigarettes with disease.'

name: Concept_2
definition_en: The concept which is tied to Concept_1.    'Skid marks on the street connects my neighbor's car to my broken mailbox.'

name: Point_of_view
definition_en: The point of view from which the connection exists.  'As far as we are concerned this evidence ties the secretary to the case of the missing apple fritters.'

name: Evidence
definition_en: The phenomenon that points to or proves the connection between Concept_1 and Concept_2. Generally expressed as an external.  'Footprints connect her to the crime.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the connection exists.  'If we get the protocal right the study will link leprosy to too much stress-inducing homework.'

name: Concepts
definition_en: The two concepts expressed jointly.  'Ample evidence is able to connect the two.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree of connection between the Concepts.  'This definitively connects our water shortage problems to the ascendance of a new governor.'

name: Specification
definition_en: A further specification on the linkage.  'The evidence causally links these two.'

name: Entity_1
definition_en: An entity with a relationship to Entity_2.  'This topic has no relation to the matter at hand.'

name: Entity_2
definition_en: The entity with a relationship to Entity_1.  'This topic has no relation to the matter at hand.'

name: Entities
definition_en: The things that are related to each other. Collective expression of the FEs Entity_1 and Entity_2.  'The relation between these data sets is not clear to me.'

name: Relation_type
definition_en: A characterization of the relation that determines what model is active for further reasoning.  'There is a kinship relation between them .'

name: Individual_1
definition_en: The individual being described in terms of Individual_2.

name: Individual_2
definition_en: The individual whose identity serves to identify Individual_2.

name: Relation
definition_en: The type of connection between the Individuals.

name: Individuals
definition_en: The individuals in a (symmetrically construed) Relation to each other.

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: The region which is located relative to the Ground and which is shaped according to an image schema.

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Salient parts that make up a Profiled_region.

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Profiled_region is located with respect to.

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Profiled_region about.  This FE should also include words that indicate that there was no salient formation.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location that the Profiled_region is a part of.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Profiled_region.

name: Related_event
definition_en: An event related to the Profiled_region in some way other than (1) Formational_cause (which is a separate FE) or an intended use (which would place the instance in Locale_by_use), or (3) a defining event (which would place the instance in Locale_by_event).

name: Inherent_purpose
definition_en: The activity that is carried out in the Profiled_region.

name: Ground
definition_en: An entity whose location is relatively well-known and which, thus, can serve as a land-mark to identify the Profiled_region.

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: Salient parts of the Focal_feature.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location that the Focal_feature is a part of.

name: Formational_cause
definition_en: Indicates the action (or causer) which brings the features of the Focal_feature about.

name: Focal_feature
definition_en: A stable bounded area defined by its relation to another landform. This FE is incorporated in each LU in this frame.

name: Name
definition_en: This FE is used for the Names of Focal_features.

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that a Focal_feature is located with respect to.

name: Type
definition_en: The Type is the subtype of natural feature.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description, characteristic, or property of the Focal_feature which is not covered by more specific FEs.

name: Landmark_feature
definition_en: The landform with respect to which the Focal_feature is defined.

name: Constituent_parts
definition_en: The materials or Constituent_parts that make up a Locale.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The political locale that the Locale is a the head of. 'People come from all over the nation to work in and visit the capital of the United States.'

name: Locale
definition_en: The politically or administratively-defined locale that functions as the head of state for the containing entity.  'Most of the major government buildings are in the center of the capital'

name: Name
definition_en: This FE is used for the Names of Locales.   'Gyeonggi Province is located in the west-central area of the Korean Peninsula, and surrounds the Korean capital of Seoul.'

name: Relative_location
definition_en: A place that the Locale is located with respect to.  'All the capitals in Canada are clean.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description, characteristic, or property of the Locale which is not covered by more specific FEs.  'He essentially was the head of the largest county seat in northern California.'

name: Population
definition_en: The people living in the jurisdiction of the locale, typically expressed with a PP-of.

name: Rate
definition_en: The number which represents the relative quantities of the Numerator and the Denominator.

name: Numerator
definition_en: Identifies the quantity whose magnitude is determined relative to the Denominator.

name: Focal_entity
definition_en: The set of things to which the Rate pertains.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any characteristic of the Rate that is not covered by another more specific FE.

name: Type
definition_en: A name of the Rate of or description of the particular category the Rate belongs to.

name: Denominator
definition_en: The quantity whose magnitude is determined relative to the Numerator.

name: Focal_occasion
definition_en: The Focal_occasion is the event which is  being located in time with respect to some other event: The Focal_occasion is profiled, in contrast to the Landmark_occasion, which is backgrounded.  'Hours of eating and drinking followed the wedding ceremony.' 'Her belated party was still a success.' 'During the previous week, he had eaten 5 mangoes.'

name: Landmark_occasion
definition_en: The Landmark_occasion is the event  with respect to which the Focal_occasion is located.  'Hours of eating and drinking followed the wedding ceremony.'

name: Interval
definition_en: Frequently, the Interval between the Reference and Focal Occasions is expressed: The article in the Times closely followed the singer's announcement that he was retiring.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE is used for the Explanation or explanation for the Focal_occasion being early or late.

name: Focal_participant
definition_en: The Focal_participant is the participant in the Focal_occasion which is profiled as being in a relation of relative time to the Landmark_occasion.  'We were late for dinner.'

name: Captor
definition_en: The Captor is the individual who ends the confinement or captivity of the Theme. The release of the Theme is in accord with the plans of the Captor.  'The police released the suspect.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the person or object in motion released by the Captor.  'The police released the suspect.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the release which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Captor that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'The police released the suspect carefully.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Captor which brings about the release.  'He released a hundred prisoners by signing a single document..'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation identifies the reason for which the Captor are releasing the Theme.  'The police released the suspect  because he had a good alibi.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose identifies the purpose for which the Captor release the Theme.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Theme ceases to be confined.  '"Aren't you going to release us here?" she asked.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time identifies when the Captor release the Theme .

name: Location_of_confinement
definition_en: The location to which the Theme's motion was formerly inhibited.  'She petitioned unsuccessfully for their release from Chateau D'If.'

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world when the Releasing event occurs.

name: Authorities
definition_en: The Authorities are those who have the official authority to release a Suspect.  'The police released the suspect.'

name: Suspect
definition_en: The Suspect is the person released by the Authorities, having been held under suspicion of having committed a crime.  'The police released the suspect.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the way in which the Authorities release the Suspect.  'The police released the suspect carefully.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means identifies the means by which the Authorities release the Suspect.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation identifies the reason for which the Authorities are releasing the Suspect.  'The police released the suspect  because he had a good alibi.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose identifies the purpose for which the Authorities release the Suspect.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place identifies the place where the Authorities release the Suspect .

name: Time
definition_en: The Time identifies when the Authorities release the Suspect .

name: Holding_location
definition_en: The place that the Suspect is no longer confined to.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The person or thing whose needs are served by the Means action.  ' I rely on this walking stick to get me around'

name: Benefit
definition_en: An action or state that the Means action brings about and from which the Protagonist profits.  'He still relies on me to do the head work'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the achievement of the Benefit depends on the Means action.  ' He knows I rely entirely on him to point out all my blunders and spelling mistakes.'

name: Intermediary
definition_en: The person or thing that performs a Means action to the Benefit of the Protagonist.  'We rely  on you for feedback and input'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An object that the Protagonist uses to realize a Benefit.  'I hate having to rely on my car to get where I want to go'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action or state that the Protagonist wants to bring about.  It is more or less the Benefit viewed in relation to the Protagonist rather than the Means.  'The user will quickly begin to rely on the pills to cope with life pressures.'

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed either by the Protagonist or an Intermediary that has a Benefit for  the Protagonist attached to it.   'We rely on your response'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The conditions when the Protagonist needs to rely on an Instrument or Intermediary.  'We have to fully rely on him when times get a little rough'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: An individual that considers the Expectation certain.

name: Expectation
definition_en: The fact which the Cognizer depends on in planning for the future.  'I think you should count on getting a paycut.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The situation in which the Cognizer can count on the Expectation.  'When investing in such a volatile area, you can bank on getting burned a few times.'

name: Believer
definition_en: The Believer is the person whose religious beliefs are in question.

name: Content
definition_en: The Content is the object of the Believer's religious conviction. Content can be expressed as a finite clause or in a in-PP Complement.   ' A Christian believes that Jesus of Nazareth was a prophet. '

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Believer is convinced of the usefulness and validity of their religious beliefs .  'Christ the King Presbyterian Church therefore believes fervently in Christian civilization'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Believer knows or thinks something.  'All we have to do is believe in Jesus like a child and confess him'

name: Role
definition_en: Role is a  function that an Element of the faith is believed to serve.  'If a person believes in Jesus as his Saviour, he can he baptized.'

name: Element
definition_en: A predefined, fixed idea to which reference is made throughout the belief system.    'I believe in Jesus' 'To Clark, who infinitely believes in angels and celebrating the holidays with loved ones, Christmas means kids and family.'

name: Remainder
definition_en: The part of the Resource that the Process has not yet applied to.

name: Resource
definition_en: The original set of items to which the Depletive_process applies one after the other.

name: Location
definition_en: The place where the Resource is found.  'How much is left in the treasury?'

name: Original_owner
definition_en: The individual who owned the Resource that is being depleted.  'Only two poems are left from Virgil Smithers'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the amount of the Resource that is let is assessed.  'In 1910, only two of the Renaissance buildings remained'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: An individual who may use the Remainder for his benefit.  'Is there any food left for me?'

name: Original_context
definition_en: A temporal setting or event which metonymically stands for the entities that were in existence then. The Remainder is part of the Original_context. This FE occurs especially when abstract entities such as social institutions are seen as Resources.  'Only the Beaux Arts cinema is left from the golden era of the 1940s'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: A person who recalls memories of past experience or impressions.   'I will truly miss Delmar and I will always remember when his eyes lit up everytime he got ice-cream.'

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: A person or thing that the Cognizer remembers as being involved in some state or event or as having some property.  'today I saw a sister's exclassmate, and didn't recognise him, I remember him taller.'

name: Experience
definition_en: A past event or state that the Cognizer witnessed and is now recalling. The Experience may be a specific event or state or a vaguer period that is treated as a unit.  ' I can still remember saying the pledge every morning before class in elementary school, a rare occurrence among elementary school kids nowadays. '

name: Impression
definition_en: A property that the Cognizer attributes to the Salient_entity based on their past experience of the Salient_entity or a category to which the Salient_entity is assigned.  'I remember Peter as immensely kind in those first three weeks before I was packed off to boarding school.'

name: State
definition_en: A property or role that a Salient_entity actually held and which frames the memories that the Cognizer has of the Salient_entity.  'Atulprasad is principally remembered as a musician and composer. '

name: Vividness
definition_en: The degree of detail and/or immediacy of  a remembered Experience.  'Brian Wooley only dimly remembered the hand falling on his shoulder'

name: Context
definition_en: A situation in which the Cognizer encountered the Salient_entity.  'She was just how I remember her from school .'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Cognizer remembers the experience.  'I 'll never forget being in hospital'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Cognizer that affect the action (fondly).   'Bill will be fondly remembered by all.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the Cognizer remembers the experience.  ' Your generosity and kindness will be long remembered for years to come. '

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The person who retains and retrieves information.  'I bet Johno can remember the name of the Ramones' drummer.'

name: Mental_content
definition_en: Mental_content stored by and accessible to the Cognizer. It may derive from experience or activity or simply from being informed of it.  'Do you remember how to spell cupboard ?'

name: Accuracy
definition_en: The extent to which the remembered Mental_content matches the information or experience that it is based on.  'If I remember correctly the pre-War price for hanging a wall up, a roll of wallpaper was about sixpence a roll , and that included preparing as well.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Cognizer retrieves Mental_content or forgets it.  ' Afterwards, I forgot what I was pissed off about, but I was. '

name: Topic
definition_en: An entity, concrete or abstract, or an event that the remembered Mental_content is about.   'The boy who suffered brain damage when he was hit by a vehicle while walking into school testified Friday he remembers nothing about being hit. '

name: Context
definition_en: A situation or a text from which the Mental_content was acquired.  'You will remember from grade school that you do not want to make the nuns impatient.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The person who thinks of or fails to think of an obligatory or desireable Action.  '.Alex and Zach Swindle, Centre, visited their brother in San Francisco in June and remembered to take along a copy of The Post>. '

name: Action
definition_en: An Action that the Cognizer is supposed to carry out. This may be a Task imposed specifically on the Cognizer or it may be self- or socially imposed.  'This time we remembered to turn the gas off before leaving.'

name: Time
definition_en: A Time when the Cognizer remembers or fails to carry out an Action.   'He remembered afterwards to kiss her fingers.'

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: The Salient_entity is a person or thing that the Cognizer needs to affect or effect when carrying out the Action.  'We piled into the taxi and right when we were about to leave, I realized we forgot the video camera'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE describes how often the Action is performed by the Cognizer.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person (or other force) that causes the Theme to move.   'The waiter removed the dishes from the table.'

name: Theme
definition_en: Theme is the object that changes location.   'The waiter removed the dishes from the table. '

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the initial location of the Theme, before it changes location.  'The waiter removed the dishes from the table.'  A few of the words in this frame participate in an alternation between a Theme object and a Source object.  'The waiter cleared the dishes from the table.' 'The waiter cleared the table of dishes.' 'The plumber drained the water from the sink.' 'The plumber drained  the sink of water.' 'The gardener emptied the soil from the bucket.' 'The gardener emptied the bucket of soil.' 'The army evacuated the people from the town.' 'The army evacuated the town.'  Sentences with a Source object belong in the frame Motion_Emptying. The frames Motion_Emptying and Motion_Removing differ in terms of which frame element, the Source or the Theme, is construed as being more highly affected.

name: Path
definition_en: Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal expresses the frame element Path. In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.   'The army evacuated the townspeople through the tunnel. '

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the location where the Theme ends up. This Frame Element is not profiled by words in this frame, though it may occasionally be expressed, as with the word remove.  'Grandmother removed the fine china to a safe place.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.  'The army evacuated the townspeople efficiently'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is an act whereby the Agent achieves the removal.  'You'll have to eject it by sticking an unfolded paperclip into that little hole.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Cause
definition_en: The non-Agentive cause of the removing event.  'The raging fire quickly emptied the square of all people.' 'Magnetic storms on the sun sometimes eject hot gas from beneath the surface.'

name: Distance
definition_en: The Distance is any expression which characterizes the extent of motion.  This frame element occurs throughout the motion domain but is very infrequent in Motion_Noise.   'John withdrew the gun a few feet.'

name: Means_of_motion
definition_en: The Means_of_motion expresses the conveyance with which the Agent effects the motion of the Theme. The Means_of_motion holds and conveys the Theme. Means_of_motions can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.  'Weevacuated the population by helicopter.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: The Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.  'Pat removed the jam from the fridge along with the cheese.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the removal takes place.  'That year they drained the swamp-water out of Higgs' bottomland.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the removal takes place.  'You just take the dishes and rinse them in the kitchen, okay?'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The tool the Agent uses to remove the Theme from its Source.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Co-timed_event
definition_en: An event the punctuates the larger Removing event.  'With a laugh, she tore a page from his diary.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world when the Agent or Cause removes the Theme from the Source.

name: Purpose
definition_en: To what end the Agent or Cause removes the Theme.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE is used to indicate the Direction that the Theme travels when it is removed.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the entity that does the emptying.  'Pat cleared the table of dishes.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme, when overtly expressed, invariably occurs in a PP Complement headed by "of". 'Pat cleared the table of dishes.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the region or container which is emptied of something.  In this frame, the Source occurs as an NP Object. 'Pat cleared the table.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal. 'Kim emptied the basin over the edge of the balcony.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is any expression which tells where the Theme ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion. 'The children emptied the toy box onto the floor.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Agent empties the Source.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depicitive phrase describing either the Agent or Theme of the emptying. 'Naked, Millhouse emptied the trash can.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Agent empties the Source.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Agent empties the Source.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of  the Agent emptying the Source.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This is the object with which the Agent empties the Source. 'I emptied the tub with a bucket.' 'I peeled the oranges with a knife.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is the non-sentient force which instigates the emptying. 'A basic washing can degrease your workclothes.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the emptying takes place.  'Don't eviscerate him in the house!'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the emptying takes place.  'The prisoners were deloused in June and August.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Agent
definition_en: The sentient entity causes the Artifact to not function.

name: Artifact
definition_en: The device that no longer works.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An event that the Agent hopes to bring about by breaking an Artifact. 'I totaled my car so I wouldn't have to renew the tags.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action that the Agent performs which results in the Artifact being inoperable.  'I guess I broke the doorknob by twisting it too hard.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An inanimate entity or force that renders the Artifact non-functional.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the event takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The place at which the event takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: A holistic description of the event (e.g. the same way), including depictions of the Agent in terms of how the state of the Agent affects the overall action (e.g maliciously).

name: Frequency
definition_en: Meaning: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs--Iteration expressions answer the question how many times.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Artifact is (or has been) rendered nonfunctional.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of particpant while lack of functionality is being rendered.

name: Lessee
definition_en: The individual that gains temporary use of the Goods by paying the Lessor  'We 've been renting from him for years .'

name: Goods
definition_en: The FE Goods is an item which is temporarily exchanged for Money in a transaction.  'I tried to hire a bicycle .'

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs. ' Will they allow you to lease the airfield by check? '

name: Money
definition_en: Money is the thing given in exchange for tempory use of the Goods. 'Sam chartered the ship for only $12,000.'

name: Rate
definition_en: In isome cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. ' Jon rented a car for twenty dollars a day . '

name: Lessor
definition_en: The individual who has permanent ownership of the Goods and allows them to be used by the Lessee temporarily.  'Kim and Pat rent the apartment from Jess. '

name: Unit
definition_en: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by-PP.  'Lee rents rooms by the hour. '

name: Place
definition_en: The location the renting takes place.  'I rented the car right next to the airport .'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the renting is performed.  'Though he was already wanted , he rented a car to make a getaway .'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state-of-affairs from which the renting logically follows.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the purchasing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Lessee that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully). 'She quit her old job and gleefully leased a cheap, Upper East Side apartment.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: The individual intended by the Lessee to receive the Goods. 'She rented him a cadillac from the lot next door and they hit the road .'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Goods are (or have been) in the Lessee's possession.    'Our neighbors have been renting their house for the last ten years.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The Lessee's intended purpose for the Goods. 'I rented a computerto sit in my office.'

name: Lessee
definition_en: The Lessee has Money and wants the Goods. 'Lee rented a textbook to Abby.'

name: Goods
definition_en: The FE Goods is the item which is temporarily exchanged for Money.  'Kim rented the shed out .'

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which a commercial transaction occurs. 'Abby rented her room by putting an ad in the Examiner.'

name: Money
definition_en: Money is the thing given in exchange for Goods in a transaction. 'The x-ray machine was leased for $12,000 to a small firm in Menlo Park .'

name: Rate
definition_en: In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of Goods. ' The hostel rents a bunk for about 20 dollars a night .'

name: Lessor
definition_en: The Lessor has possession of the Goods and temporarily exchanges them for Money from a Lessee. 'So far, my company has rented the video more than three million times .'

name: Unit
definition_en: This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured. Generally, it occurs in a by-PP.  'Bob rents rooms by the hour. '

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the leasing takes place.  'U-haul rents almost everywhere.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state-of-affairs from which the renting logically follows.  'I rented it out because since Ned died, nobody's been using it for anything.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the renting takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the renting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Lessor that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully). 'Stuart reluctantly rented her his last apartment .'

name: Result
definition_en: The state of the Lessor after the sale has occurred. 'I leased the whole lot at a loss.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Goods are (or have been) in the Lessee's possession.     'Our neighbors have rented their house out for the last ten years.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The Lessee's intended purpose for the Goods. 'He leased the filing robot to me to organize all my legal documents.'

name: Back
definition_en: This FE indicates that the selling act reverses an earlier separate act in which the current Lessor rented or bought the Goods from the current Lessee.  ' There is a plan for Mercer to buy the ground and lease it back to the club'

name: Relay
definition_en: This FE indicates that the current leasing constitues a re-lease by the current Lessor of  Goods that they bought or rented earlier from a third person (not the Lessee of the current leasing act).  'My housemates rented my room on to an English student .'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the person who communicates their cessation of association with the Content.

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the person to whom the Speaker is communicating. When this FE is expressed, it often appears in a prepositional phrase introduced by "to", or as a direct object.

name: Content
definition_en: The idea that the Speaker no longer associates with, whether it be an activity, a propostion, or a group.  'Bonnie Charlie then renounced his aspirations to the throne.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the renunciation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Speaker that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'Your government then coldly and completely renounced you.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Speaker makes a statement of renunciation.

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to their renunciation.  'That 's when he finally renounced their friendship in despair.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement of renunciation.  'Castro renounced all involvement with the group over the radio.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Speaker during the statement.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the statement is made.

name: Place
definition_en: The FE specifies the place where the statement takes place.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Injured_party
definition_en: The Injured_party was affected by some previous wrongful act of the Wrongdoer and who should benefit from the reparations. 'You can never make amends to Susan for standing her up.'

name: Injury
definition_en: The Injury is the injurious action that  the Wrongdoer committed against the Injured_party.  Although conceptually present, this FE need not always be realized.  'Wyelander sought reparations for the brutal murder of his nephew.'

name: Wrongdoer
definition_en: The Wrongdoer makes amends to the Injured_party for the Injury. 'How  can I make it up to you?'

name: Benefiting_action
definition_en: The Benefiting_action is performed by the Wrongdoer to make amends. 'Between friends, amends can be made by apologizing.'

name: Gift
definition_en: Gift identifies the entity that the Wrongdoer gives to the Injured_party. 'He made it up to her with a bouquet of flowers.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner marks any description of the Wrongdoer's making of reparations not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification, (e.g. probably), and general descriptions comparing events (e.g. the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of a Wrongdoer that also affect the action ( e.g. presumptuously).  'Smeagol humbly made amends for his earlier bad behavior.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Wrongdoer makes amends. 'Restitution was given in Milan with the Treaty of Abiselle.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when amends are made. 'He made amends to her that very afternoon.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Wrongdoer makes restitution to the Injured_party. 'He thinks that Japan made restitution for the incident to lull Americans into complacency.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Wrongdoer makes amends for the Injury .  'Of course, they won't be able to make it up to you completely.'

name: Loaner
definition_en: The person who is owed Money by the Debtor.  'If you borrow, you'll have to repay the bank'

name: Debtor
definition_en: The person who is giving Money to the Loaner to return an earlier borrowed amount.  'I paid Johnson back for the movie ticket.'

name: Money
definition_en: The amount of Money that the Debtor gives to the Loaner, which may or may not be the full amount of the Loan.  'Pay me back my 20 dollars!'

name: Loan
definition_en: A situation or a representative of a situation prior to repayment in which the Debtor uses the Loaner's money.  'You must repay the mortgage in full.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The level to which the Loan can be considered repaid in its entirety.  'He wishes to completely repay the loan.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the Debtor gives the Loaner money.  'Don't worry, I'll pay you back later.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world when the Money is transfered.

name: Manner
definition_en: How the Debtor gives Money to the Loaner.  'Paul quietly repaid all of his debts and skipped town.'

name: Place
definition_en: The physical location where the repayment takes place.  'They repaid Lenny in a dark alleyway.'

name: Means
definition_en: What the <fex name="">Debtor does in order to repay the <fex name="">Loaner.  'I repaid my loan by mowing their lawn once a week.'

name: Enemy
definition_en: The  Enemy is the entity that fails to overtake the Defender.  'General Monk would repel Jacobite invaders.'

name: Defender
definition_en: The Defender is the land, government, and its people that the Enemy fails to seize.  'General Winter repelled invaders from Napoleon to Hitler.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes the intensity and extent of the repelling event.

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner in which the Defender repels the Enemy.

name: Means
definition_en: The action by which the repelling event is made possible through the efforts of the Defender.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Defender repels the Enemy.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Defender succeeds to repel the Enemy.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason why the Defender repels the Enemy.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The tool used by the Defender to repel the Enemy.

name: Invasion_act
definition_en: This FE refers to the Invasion_act perpetrated by the Enemy.  'Spain pledged to repel any Allied invasion.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE describes the outcome of the repelling event.

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the replacement.

name: Agent
definition_en: The conscious entity, generally a person, that performs actions resulting in the New entity occupying the position.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Agent that interacts with an New entity so that it ends up in the position.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies where the Agent installs the New entity.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent places the New entity in a position.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent installs the New entity.

name: New
definition_en: The New entity is the person or thing that the Agent sets to fill a Role.  'I don't know; perhaps you could substitute regular sugar.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification  secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics or states of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in placing the New filler in a position.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the New entity is affected by the Agent.  Degrees of replacement are generally only possible when there are multiple New and Old entities.  'He replaced the 6761 models entirely with about half as many 6800s.'

name: Old
definition_en: The entity that formerly occupied the position.  'If you substitute a 15" arm for the 50cm one, it works pretty well.' 'Please replace the broken fixture as soon as possible.'

name: Role
definition_en: The category that the New and Old entities fit into as a result of the function they serve.  'AN AUSTRALIAN state has proposed the country adopt a bill of rights and replace the Queen as head of state with an Australian president .'

name: Informer
definition_en: The Informer reports the activities of the Wrongdoer to the Authorities.

name: Wrongdoer
definition_en: The Wrongdoer has his or her activities reported to the Authorities.

name: Authorities
definition_en: The Authorities are the officials, government or otherwise, who handle misbehavior.

name: Behavior
definition_en: The Behavior is the action or actions for which the Wrongdoer is reported.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Informer reports the Behavior of the Wrongdoer.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location where the reporting occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose is the purpose for which the Informer reports the Wrongdoer.

name: Origin
definition_en: The Origin is the place where the Representative was born or lived a salient part of her or his life.

name: Representative
definition_en: The Representative speaks for another.

name: Persistent_characteristic
definition_en: The Persistent_characteristic is a physiological characteristic or personality trait of the Representative which is concieved of as persisting over time.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor is a temporary condition of the Representative.

name: Age
definition_en: The Age is the length of time the Representative has been alive.

name: Ethnicity
definition_en: The Ethnicity is the religious, racial, national, socio-economic or cultural group to which the Representative belongs.

name: Context_of_acquaintance
definition_en: An expression indicating the context with which the Representative is associated.

name: Rank
definition_en: Rank is the position in a hierarchy that a Representative occupies within an organization.

name: Place_of_employment
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Representative works.

name: Represented
definition_en: The Represented authorizes the Representative to communicate on its behalf.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE identifies the Type of Representative.

name: Compensation
definition_en: The Compensation is the payment that the Representative receives for performing a task.

name: Contract_basis
definition_en: The Contract_basis describes the conditions of employment with respect to permanency, hours per time period, or payment basis.  'Smithers is a half-time spokesperson for Procteur et Gamble '

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The event, idea, or emotion evoked by the Entity.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes the Degree to which the Entity represents the Phenomenon.  'That mural is hardly a symbol of what we're all about!'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period in which the representing occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE describes the means through which the representing occurs. 'What does a black and white snake symbolize in a dream?'

name: Entity
definition_en: An object that has some association with a Phenomenon.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person or group of people who believe in the representation.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency denotes how often the Entity is associated with the Phenomenon.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the represenation logically follows.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the representing event occurs.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker, as in other communication frames, is generally an External Argument.   'The judge ordered the plaintiff to return the money.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: In this frame the Addressee can either occur as an NP Object (usually with a following complement clause) or as a PP Complement of verbs or nouns.  'The child implored her parents to let her stay up late.' 'I pleaded with the bus driver to let me on without paying.' 'I made an appeal to the passers-by to help me.'

name: Message
definition_en: The Message is the content of the request that can be expressed as a quote, in a finite or non-finite clausal Complement, an NP Object or PP Complement. '"I'd like an extension," begged Pat.' 'The directors requested that Pat resign.' 'Pat begged them to reconsider.' 'The students requested an extension of the deadline.' 'The offender begged for clemency.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is rarely expressed in this frame but can occur as a PP Complement headed by about.  'Can I make a request about the content of the lessons?.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The Medium is the physical entity or channel used to transmit the Message. The Medium is frequently expressed as a PP Complement headed by on or in.  'The parents of the missing child made an appeal on television.' 'The parents of the missing child made an appeal in the papers.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner indicates the manner in which the Message is delivered.  'Don't stop, " he commanded huskily.' '"Maybe that was the basic problem," she told him wearily.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Speaker that results in a request being made and received.  'He asked for food by holding his hand out with a doleful expression.'

name: Time
definition_en: The interval during which the Speaker makes the request.  'I urged him to concede yesterday.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: This extra-thematic FE applies to participants that are expected to derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate.  'I asked him to get that for you.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs, or a state of affairs that holds, at a time that includes some time that the request was occuring. This often makes us of "as" and "while".  'I asked him for directions while we waited.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.  'I asked twice.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.  'Glancing out the window, she asked me to hand her the cane and assist her down the stairs.'

name: Customer
definition_en: The Customer is the person or business ordering the Entity from the Supplier.  'Simone ordered a hamburger and fries.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The object ordered by the Customer.  'Liz ordered a new espresso maker for the office.'  'His order did not arrive on time.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The channel used by the Customer to transmit the request.  'Harold ordered the material via email.'

name: Supplier
definition_en: The person or organization from whom the Customer orders the Entity.  'Mrs. Apfelbaum ordered a coffee from the barista.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Customer requested the Entity.  'Sara placed the order three days ago. '

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The person or organization which benefits from the Entity.  'Rose ordered a new computer for Mr. Cooper.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the request is placed.  'Mr. Shaw hastily ordered the first thing he saw on the menu.'

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Customer that results in a request being made.  'Cheri accidently ordered the jacket by clicking on the link.'

name: Required_situation
definition_en: The state-of-affairs which prevents Negative_consequences.

name: Negative_consequences
definition_en: An event or state of affairs that results if the required Required_situation does not occur and which impacts some deprofiled entity in a way that the speaker finds undesirable.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the requirement holds.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The event or state of affairs that is achieved by bringing about the Required_situation and which entails the non-occurrance of Negative_consequences.

name: Time
definition_en: The period during which the Required_situation is necessary to prevent negative consequences.  'He was told that when he got back , his column needed a serious rethink .'

name: Place
definition_en: The location within which the Required_situation is required.  'In California , seatbelts must be fastened at all times .'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason why the Required_situation is necessary.  ' I do realize his pitch needed to be wide-ranging because of the differences between folks in the room .'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Required_situation is necessary.  The Degree may either imply a modification of the direness of the Negative_consequences, the probability of the Negative_consequences (if the Required_situation is not made to hold), or both.  'He absolutely must be replaced .'

name: Dependent
definition_en: The state-of-affairs which cannot hold without the Requirement.

name: Requirement
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that must be present or obtain in order for the Dependent to obtain.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Dependent depends on the presence of the Requirement.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The state-of-affairs which militates that the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent to obtain.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Requirement is necessary for the Dependent.

name: Condition
definition_en: The conditions under which the the Requirement is necessary.  'Such care is necessary when under martial law.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The field of endeavor whose nature imposes the Requirement.

name: Place
definition_en: Place denotes a location in which the specified relation between Requirement and Dependent holds.

name: Dependent_individual
definition_en: The individual in whose interest it is to have the Required_entity or for the Requirement state of affairs to obtain.

name: Required_entity
definition_en: An entity that has to be present for the Dependent state of affairs to obtain

name: Required_individual
definition_en: An individual that has to provide the Required_entity or see to it that the Requirement state of affairs holds.

name: Agent
definition_en: The sentient being who rescues the Patient or Asset from the Harmful_situation.  'He rescued the innocent girl from a fate worse than death. '

name: Patient
definition_en: The living being who is rescued by the Agent.  'Three foxes were saved from being savagely ripped apart.'

name: Asset
definition_en: The entity that is judged to be valueable which might be lost or damaged by the Harmful_situation.  'She saved countless lives during her short stay on the plantation.'

name: Harmful_situation
definition_en: An event that occurs which could result in injury or harm to the Patient or Asset.  'Three foxes were saved from being savagely ripped apart.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Agent rescues the Patient or Asset.  'She saved my life on the bridge yesterday.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Agent rescues the Patient or Asset.  'Kevin informed her that he would happily save her, given the opportunity.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Agent rescues the Patient or Asset.  'She saved my life on the bridge yesterday.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The setting in which the rescuing act takes place.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The tool with which the Agent saves the Patient or Asset.  'She saved my life with her words.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the Agent rescues the Patient or Asset.  'The nurse saved my life by performing CPR.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Agent rescues the Patient or Asset.  'You know he only saved the dog to get close to Miranda.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in performing the action.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Patient or Asset is actually saved.  'He wholly saved the town from hunger.'

name: Researcher
definition_en: The people engaged in a research endeavor.  'Before he became an astronaut, Grunsfeld did research in physics. '

name: Field
definition_en: An area of inquiry.  ''

name: Question
definition_en: A significant unanswered open proposition which the Researcher is attempting to resolve.  'When we have researched why Brazilian mothers have stopped breastfeeding, principal reasons given are 'poor milk' and 'insufficient milk' .'

name: Topic
definition_en: A phenomenon or idea involved in a Question.  'Would you take part in research on the best place to have a baby? '

name: Time
definition_en: The time when  the research is carried out.  'During summer of 1999, I did research using a technique called "Path Integral Monte Carlo", to simulate quantum particles.'

name: Means
definition_en: The experimentations, observations, or other procedures performed by the Researcher in order to find an answer to the Question.  'The workgroup has researched this issue by reviewing the basin plans of other regions and other various sources.'

name: Population
definition_en: A group of entities that are studied by the Researcher to answer the Question. The studied group need not be the only kind of entity that provides evidence for answering the research Question.  'Prior researchers have investigated senile dementia in relatively small populations.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously),  general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Researcher that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'The West Chicago Park District carefully researched how much of an increase was needed to accomplish all of our goals.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: Purpose indicates an action that the Researcher intends to accomplish by performing research.  'We research this fungus to fight ailments in tobacco and tomato fields.'

name: Duration_of_state
definition_en: The Duration_of_state is the period of time over which the research takes place.  'That particular think tank researched population change for over three decades.'

name: Place
definition_en: The physical place where the research is carried out.  'Johnson and Randall's research in Africa has proven extremely valuable.'

name: Type
definition_en: The Type, or subclass of research.  'His lab conducts a lot of mainstream research.' 'Several institutes exist only for theoretical research.'

name: Client
definition_en: The entity that is intended to receive the Services of the Organization.   'Phil Collins booked his cockatoo into a $350-a-night pet hotel.'

name: Services
definition_en: The goods or labor that the Client requests the Organization preserve for future consumption or rendering.

name: Organization
definition_en: The entity that enters into its records the request of the Client to retain Services in the future.

name: Scheduled_time
definition_en: The future point in time when the Client arranges for the Organization to provide Services.  'She reserved the room for the meeting for Tuesday .'

name: Booker
definition_en: The entity that contacts the Organization directly.  In many if not most cases, a Booker is also a Client, but the roles may also be separated, e.g. a travel agent.  'The hotel reserved two rooms for me . '

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event as a whole ("the same way") or a characteristic of the Booker during the action that holistically affects the event ("sloppily").

name: Place
definition_en: The location the Booker performs the action.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The situation that the Booker intends to bring about by reserving.

name: Means
definition_en: An action or methodology used by the Booker to bring the reservation about.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the reserving event takes place.  'I booked the room for Monday only on Tuesday .'

name: Payment
definition_en: The amount paid to the Organization in exchange for the Services.

name: Deformer
definition_en: The Deformer is the one who does the reshaping.  'The lieutenant crushed it angrily with his boot before looking back at Hencke.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the Deformer affects the Patient.  'The lieutenant crushed it angrily with his boot before looking back at Hencke.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The FE Manner identifies the manner in which an Deformer intentionally affects the Patient.  'The lieutenant crushed it angrily with his boot before looking back at Hencke.'

name: Means
definition_en: The FE Means identifies the means by which the Deformer intentionally affects the Patient.

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is the entity acted on and that undergoes a change.  'Jack plucked the flower out of his morning coat and closed his fist slowly over it , crushing it into a pulp.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place indicates where the Deformer intentionally affects the Patient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Deformer intentionally affects the Patient.  'What 's more , when you 've finished with it simply wipe it clean and then fold it flat for easy storage.'

name: Time
definition_en: The FE Time identifies when the Deformer intentionally affects the Patient.  'The lieutenant crushed it angrily with his boot before looking back at Hencke.'

name: Result
definition_en: The Result is the shape the Patient becomes.  'Jack plucked the flower out of his morning coat and closed his fist slowly over it , crushing it into a pulp.'

name: Resistant_surface
definition_en: The Resistant_surface is the surface against which a Deformer presses the Patient.  'Michael flattened the can against his head . ' 'She crushed her cigarette in the ashtray and stood up to go.'

name: Locus
definition_en: The Locus is the locus of the reshaping action; it is essentially a simultaneous Instrument and Resistant_surface.  'Russell crumpled the paper cups in his fist.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is an animate or inanimate entity, a force, or event that produces an effect. Volitionality is not a necessary characteristic of Causes.  'The strong winds deformed the structure of the outhouse.' 'The rockslide squashed our summer villa.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: The FE Iterations indicates the number of times the reshaping has occurred.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation indicates a state of affairs that the Deformer is responding to in performing the reshaping.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Patient is reshaped. 'The steamroller flattened my shoes completely.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the Patient which is directly affected by the reshaping. 'He warped the steering rack on the left side.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The location that the Patient ends up in.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The conditions under which the Patient is shaped.  'The machine crushed rocks in the baking heat.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The state of the Patient with respect to the change that the Deformer brings about by making the adjustment.  'You should fold the contraption to fit in the bag.'

name: Configuration
definition_en: A state that holds of the Patient or a relation that holds among the constituent parts of the Patient as a result of the arranging action.

name: Resident
definition_en: The individual(s) that reside at the Location.  'Hannah lives in San Francisco.'

name: Location
definition_en: The place in which somebody resides.  'Sue  lives in Berkeley.'

name: Co_resident
definition_en: A person or group of people that the resident is staying with or among.  'Boris still lives with his parents.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: Frequency at which event occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of a Resident during their residence.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Resident that enables them to reside in the Location.  'He dwelt in the wild for years by foraging nuts and berries and occasionally stealing.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE refers to the Time when the Resident resides.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent finds the solution or explanation to the outstanding mystery or Problem.  'If we have not been able to resolve a problem to your satisfaction, please email us.'

name: Problem
definition_en: The Problem is the predicament or mystery that is resolved.  'Likewise, once the students worked through the problem and obtained their results, their next assignment would be to publish these to the web.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is the non-Agentive event or state of affairs that brings about the resolution of the Problem.  'First, the Tripartite Agreement of 1979 actually solved the only significant friction between the two countries.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is an intermediate action taken by the Agent in order to resolve the Problem.  'I fixed the floorplate issue by shaving off the excess stock around the floorplate that was keeping it from closing'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time at which the Problem is resolved.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE indicates the location at which the Problem is resolved.  'A group of international scientists solved the fundamental particle hierarchy question at an underground accelerator.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Agent or Cause resolves the problem.  'Our plan, I believe, wil completely resolve all outstanding questions.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the resolution, such as secondary effects ( quietly ) or comparisons of events ( the same way ).  In agentive cases,  Manner may also describe salient characteristics of the Agent which affect the action.  ( carefully, dilligently, deliberately etc. )

name: Resultant_situation
definition_en: The Resultant_situation is any situation which arises as a result of resolving a Problem .    'The question was : could the situation be resolved by improving the integration of the thought and design processes , so that what was built better achieved what was intended ?'

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of resolving a Problem .  'This issue must have been raised before and BSM would presumably be gratified to see the situation successfully resolved , once and for all .'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: The Containing_event denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the resolution of the Problem occurs.   'There are tricky design and methodological issues which would need to be worked out , as foreshadowed earlier in this paper and by no means fully resolved in the preliminary study .'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Problem is resolved.  'Such issues can only be resolved at local level .'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument is an entity used for resolving the Problem .    'Using modern computers , many practical elastic and other problems may be solved by manipulation of this matrix .'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: This FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the resolution of a Problem .    'I wanted you to believe that I was as grateful as you that the baby had died and solved the problem for us of concealing the birth .'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the length of time taken to resolve a Problem .  The government resolved the beach ball crisis in just 22 hours.

name: Role
definition_en: Role is used for the capacity in which the Agent resolves a Problem or the role of the Problem in being resolved, and is expressed in as-PPs.

name: Frequency
definition_en: Frequency describes how often the Agent or Cause resolves this problem.   'Unfortunately , when such influences are considered as explanations of the results of free-running experiments , the following problems have never been satisfactorily dealt with.'

name: Medium
definition_en: This FE identifies the physical or abstract setting in which the Problem is resolved.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: A person who participates in resolving a Problem along with the Agent.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state of affairs that the Agent is trying to bring about by solving the Problem in the specified way.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the person who communicates the reply or response.   'Iran on Saturday rejected Europe's proposal for ending the standoff over Tehran's nuclear program.'

name: Interlocutor
definition_en: This is the person who made the Proposal to the Speaker and to whom the Speaker communicates  their response. This frame element stands in for the Proposal and is only licensed when the Proposal  can be understood from the context.  'But senior SLN officials had rebuffed the man who is ever so willing to please the guerrillas.'

name: Medium
definition_en: As with Medium in other Communication frames, the physical entity or channel used to communicate can be expressed, usually as a PP Complement headed by "on" or "in".

name: Proposal
definition_en: The Proposal is the prior communication or action to which a response is given.  'Dr. Carolyn Herrington has accepted our offer to become Dean of the College of Education .'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including  secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly).  'Moreover, as with Surrey, myths have proliferated, such as that Oxford cruelly rejected his wife in 1576.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Speaker.   'She turned it down, unaware she would some day become a member.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by the Speaker responds to the Proposal .  'Others, I would say have actually turned me down by not replying and not responding.'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The response may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause, the Speaker mental or emotional state.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Speaker  makes a verbal response.   'Legislation that would have required smaller school districts to share administrators has been rebuffed repeatedly in the Oklahoma House of Representatives.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time interval during which the Speaker makes their verbal response.  'This must make yesterday's Taliban rebuff all the more wounding.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Speaker intends to accomplish by making a verbal response.  'He was asked to join the National Assembly ruling party, but repeatedly turned them down in order to continue his work as a journalist.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of response events.

name: Role
definition_en: Role denotes the capacity in which the Interlocutor is judged.  'The Policy Committee had rejected her as a candidate for chronic dialysis because of her young age. .'

name: Group
definition_en: The Group is the set of people within which the Respond_to_proposal is occuring.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or  failure, but not in all cases.

name: Response
definition_en: The means action whereby the Agent responds to the Trigger.  'The diocese responded by taking the property'

name: Responding_entity
definition_en: A non-agentive entity that is impinged upon by a Trigger event to which they respond.  'This plastic responds well to pressure.'

name: Trigger
definition_en: An event that impinges upon the Agent or Responding_entity and produces a Response from it.  ' How has the modern welfare state responded to the needs of working class women, and why? '

name: Time
definition_en: The point in time when the Agent or Responding_entity manifests its Response to the Trigger .  'Israel responded yesterday to the killing of 22 people by Palestinian suicide bombers with a helicopter attack'

name: Manner
definition_en: A characterization of the Responding_entity, Agent, or their Response action.  'The government agencies responded slowly and without much effort.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Response action takes place.  'The auto industry has responded in the U.S., but particularly in Asian and European markets by manufacturing an entry-level segment of cars that is more appealing, better looking, and safer than in the past.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the Response action.

name: Agent
definition_en: The intentional Agent that is impinged upon by a Trigger event to which they respond.  'Once again the Government is responding to a crisis with measures that will only harm patients'

name: Dimension
definition_en: A particular feature of the Responding_entity or Agent that is involved in the Response action.  'Don't respond emotionally, respond rationally.'  'The body's immune response to this agent is particularly extreme.'

name: Role
definition_en: The capacity of of the Agent is their Response act.  'His response as an official was quite off-putting.'

name: Responding_entity
definition_en: A non-agentive entity that is impinged upon by a Trigger event to which they respond.

name: Trigger
definition_en: An event that impinges upon the Agent or Responding_entity and produces a Response from it.

name: Response
definition_en: The means action whereby the Agent responds to the Trigger.

name: Agent
definition_en: The intentional Agent that is impinged upon by a Trigger event to which they respond.

name: Manner
definition_en: A characterization of the Responding_entity, Agent, or their Response action.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Response action takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by performing the Response action.

name: Time
definition_en: The point in time when the Agent or Responding_entity manifests its Response to the Trigger .

name: Act
definition_en: This FE identifies the Act that the Agent performs intentionally.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent performs the intentional act.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the intentional act occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent acts intentionally.

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain within which the Agent acts.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency with which the Agent does the Act in a given period of time.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time over which an Act was committed multiple times.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the Agent performing the Act.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Explanation
