definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the state of affairs expressed by the target, but not in all cases.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE gives a description of the Intentionally_act event.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Agent bears responsibility for performing the Act.  'She was entirely responsible for the prank.'

name: Part
definition_en: A Part of a larger Whole that has been mentioned in prior discourse or is available in the discourse setting.   'the GP had stipulated counselling as a complement to medication'

name: Rest
definition_en: The previously unmentioned part of the Whole.   'You should try to persuade the rest of the family to do so whatever their personal opinions'

name: Whole
definition_en: The larger entitiy or group that is fully made up of the Part and the Rest.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a Goal.

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is what the Agent attempts to achieve.

name: Action
definition_en: This FE identifies the means by which the Goal is achieved (or not).

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt succeeds or fails.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent during the Action.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where an attempt succeeds or fails..

name: Role
definition_en: A participant function in a particular event or in events of a particular kind.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE is applied to expressions which indicate the prevailing physical conditions for the event, or some concurrent states of affairs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or  failure, but not in all cases.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the success or failure reported by the target occurs and of which the success or failure is taken to be a part.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Action succeeds or fails.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The being or entity that becomes living again.  'If the Lord resurrected in three days, surely he could relieve my back pain in, say, a week.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the resurrection occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: An explanation of how the state-of-affairs came to pass.

name: Prior_state
definition_en: The state of the Protagonist before resurrection.  'If he comes back from the dead, we'll need this spell to ward him off.'

name: Result
definition_en: The state of the Protagonist which results from resurrection.  'I just hope he doesn't come back to life again.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Protagonist during the resurrection.  'The trouble is they always come back to life angry.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Protagonist returns from the dead.

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who has possession of the Theme.  'At all times the Saxon government held on to its insistently practiced political tradition. '

name: Theme
definition_en: The entity which the Agent possesses for a Duration.  'Once you've got a War Bond, hang on to it for the full ten years of its life.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the Agent is in possession of the Theme.  'The man who hates his life will keep it for eternal life.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent keeps the Theme.  'He will retain in his heart the memory of the vast Holocaust.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way the Agent retains possession of the Theme.  'I knew these gifts were not meant to be kept selfishly.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Agent has possession of the Theme.  'Margerite held on to the key on Wednesday until I returned to pick it up.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the Agent retains the Theme.  'If Britian had focused on India, could it have retained it by force?'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the sentient entity that reveals  the Information (whether spoken or written).   'Kornfeldt revealed that he had embezzled more than twice the amount his company owned.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the person to whom the Information is revealed.   'Evelyn confessed to Barney Holesum about what had happened.' 'An unknown intern in the White House leaked the "lunch menu" to the press.'

name: Information
definition_en: Information identifies the content that the Speaker reveals to the Addressee.  It can be expressed as a clause or as a noun phrase.  'You shouldn't reveal any murders you've been involved in, if you know what I mean.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject matter about which the Speaker is speaking. It normally only appears with noun targets, or in special constructions.  'Revelations about the coming of the Christ surfaced in early Mediaeval times.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner is any description of the revelation which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Speaker that also affect the revelation (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully, maliciously).

name: Completeness
definition_en: The degree to which Information is revealed.  'When she confessed, she confessed completely.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Speaker makes a revelation. 'He revealed his true feelings about the matter by giving her the thumbs-up behind his back.'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to the revelation.  'Out of spite Spuddmeier revealed his boss's affair.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement. 'Kim confided in me over the phone.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Speaker during the statement.  'He let slip his involvement in the coverup in a drunken stupor at an embassy party.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the revelation is made.

name: Place
definition_en: The FE specifies the Place where the Information is revealed.  'According to the report, he confessed to eating onions and gargling with generic mouthwash at the station.'

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: An alternative description of expressed action.

name: Location_of_protagonist
definition_en: This FE is used to indicate the location of a participant in cases where the multiple participants of an event are not co-located in the typical fashion. In Release 1.2, this FE has various frame-specific names including Location of perceiver, or Location of participant; it was even (incorrectly) labelled Place in some frames.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE identifies an event during which the Speaker reveals Information.

name: Source_material
definition_en: The medium in which the secret Information origninally resided.

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole especially any descriptions of the state of affairs denoted by the target as role fillers in other frames.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE describes the length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Frequency
definition_en: Frequency is defined as the number of times the Reveal_secret event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question "how often."

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the revealed secret.

name: Avenger
definition_en: The Avenger exacts revenge from the Offender for the Injury.  ' We want to avenge her. '

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an event occurs. 'Marie took terrible revenge on Trevor.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive identifies a phrase describing the actor of an action.

name: Offender
definition_en: The Offender has committed the earlier Injury for which the Avenger seeks revenge.  'Jo had the affair as a kind of revenge against Pat.' 'Marie took terrible revenge on Trevor.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument with which the revenge is performed.

name: Manner
definition_en: This frame element refers to the Manner in which the Avenger exacts their revenge from the Offender.  'They took brutal revenge on the criminal.'

name: Punishment
definition_en: The Avenger carries out a Punishment in order to exact revenge on the Offender.  'The team took revenge with a resounding victory.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the revenge occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the revenge is performed.

name: Injury
definition_en: The Injury is the injurious action committed by the Offender against the Injured_Party. This Frame Element need not always be realized, although it is conceptually necessary.   'The team sought revenge for their 4-1 defeat last month.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of  inflicting punishment for a wrong suffered.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the revenge occurs.

name: Injured_party
definition_en: This frame element identifies the constituent that encodes who or what suffered the Injury at the hands of the Offender. Sometimes, an abstract concept such a person's honour or their blood is presented as the element that has suffered the Injury. These also constitute instances of  Injured_party   'Sam's brothers avenged him.' 'We will decide later how to avenge the blood of the fallen.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Avenger seeks revenge for the Injury.

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual or group within a society that overturns the Current_leadership.

name: Current_leadership
definition_en: The people currently in power, whom the Agent attempts to overthrow.  'She fomented revolution against the Romans.'

name: Current_order
definition_en: The currently-existing system of authority or government.  'Toppling the capitalist government was their first goal.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location of the revolution.  'A series of revolutions in the eastern part of the continent made long-distance travel all but impossible.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the revolution takes place.  'China's 20th-century revolutions have yet to have their full impact on global politics.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means by which the revolution is carried out.  'The infantry launched an armed mutiny over low pay and poor living conditions.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Agent defeats and removes the Current_leadership or removes the Current_order.  'After years of back-and-forth fighting it seems unlikely that they will ever decisively overthrow the current regime.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the Agent or revolution not covered by more specific FEs.  'Ten years later, after another jail sentence, he led the Civil Forum movement to victory in Czechoslovakia's peaceful revolution.'

name: Evaluee
definition_en: Evaluee is the person or thing about whom/which a judgment has made and to whom reward/punishment is dealt. With verbs, the Evaluee is typically expressed as Object. 'The boss rewarded you for your diligence.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing the reward or punishment.

name: Means
definition_en: The action that is taken that results in punishement/reward. 'His parents disciplined him by taking away his toys.' 'The Bar Association rewarded her by hosting a lunch in her honor.'

name: Reason
definition_en: Typically, there is a constituent expressing the Reason for the Agent's judgment. It is usually a 'for'-PP, e.g. 'I punished him for his impudence.'</def-root >

name: Result
definition_en: Result of the reward or punishment.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person doing the rewarding or punishing. 'Jake's rewards to his best workers were very generous.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which the reward or punishment is carried out.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose of the reward or punishment.

name: Response_action
definition_en: The reward or punishment given to the Evaluee by the Agent. 'If a person be guilty of impiety let him be punished with death.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree of reward or punishment.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Agent of the reward or punishment.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the entity which moves by means of the Vehicle. 'Margeret flew to Cabo San Lucas.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The Vehicle is the means of conveyance of the Theme. It is usually expressed in a PP-complement or the direct object. 'Professor Frink sailed to Italy on an oceanliner.'

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. 'We flew from Atlanta.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory. 'Samantha always rode gracefully on the back of a motorcycle.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path describes the trajectory of the motion. 'The caravan rode through the desert.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the endpoint of the trajectory of motion. 'We sailed to Morocco.'

name: Distance
definition_en: The Distance is the extent of the motion. 'We flew 300 miles in 40 minutes.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration is the amount of time the motion takes. 'We rode in the van for 45 minutes.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the motion occurs. 'Weflewat nearly 600 miles per hour.'

name: Area
definition_en: The Area is the location where the motion takes place. 'We rode around the state.'

name: Road
definition_en: The Road is the thoroughfare on which the Vehicle travels. 'We ride the bus on highway 580.'

name: Route
definition_en: The Route is the usual path that the Vehicle travles. 'I ride the London-Birmingham route almost everyday.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Theme or Vehicle during the motion. 'We flew to New Orleans naked.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the riding takes place. 'We will fly back to New York in September.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: A theme that rides in the same Vehicle as the main Theme. 'My family always flies to New York with our good friends, the Jacksons.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Theme rides a vehicle. 'Jennifer hitchhiked to the island to see her long lost friend, Mr. Moreau.'

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist who is exerting effort to meet the pre-conditions for participating in the Activity.  'How a small hospital rose to the challenge of a legionella outbreak.'

name: Activity
definition_en: The Activity that the Protagonist expends efforts towards.  'She rose to the occasion of bringing up her children single-handed even as a woman who was not educated except a few years in Primary school.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Protagonist exceeds or falls short of the minimum requirements for participating in the Activity as a result of expending effort to get themselves ready.  'I'm used to second books not living up the promise of the first, but Nero Blanc fully rose to the challenge.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the Protagonist exerts effort to meet the pre-conditions necessary for engaging in the Activity.  ' I recalled how she rose to the occasion in mishaps, avalanches, oxygen shortage, lack of food, loss of comrades.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: An entity, event, or state of affairs that causes the Protagonist to expend the effort necessary to meet the pre-conditions for participating in the Activity.   'The installation was anything but a routine project from the beginning and everyone involved rose to the challenge because it was gratifying to be contributing in some way to the tsunami relief effort.'

name: Relevant_feature
definition_en: A characteristic or behavior of the Protagonist that is considered when judging whether the Protagonist might participate in the Activity.  'You are able to adapt quickly to important shifts in the world around you, and rise to the challenge where career is concerned.'

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Protagonist which enables them to overcome the difficulties and engage in the Activity.  'Learn how one small shop rose to the challenge through the use of gift tables.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Protagonist through expenditure of effort becomes capable of engaging in the Activity.    'A president for whom the jury was still out for many Americans first appeared shaken, but then rose to the' crisis.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Protagonist expends effort to become capable of engaging in the Activity.  'Students from a number of Metropolitan schools rose to the challenge at DMIT's Panorama Campus on Friday 22nd August and spent the day  participating in an annual 'Taste of Engineering' activity.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Protagonist that also affect the action (eagerly).  'Despite all odds the brave Macedonian people heroically rose to the task with valour.'

name: Asset
definition_en: Something judged to be desirable or valuable which might be lost or damaged.

name: Harmful_event
definition_en: An event that may occur or a state which may hold which could result in the loss of or damage to the Asset.

name: Situation
definition_en: The Situation under which the Asset is safe or unsafe.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of security from the expected value given the Asset, the Situation, and state indicated by the target itself.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the degree of safeness holds.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place at which the degree of safeness holds.

name: Situation
definition_en: The Situation which may lead to a harmful event.  'Most people agree, going over 100mph is unsafe.'

name: Asset
definition_en: Something judged to be desirable or valuable which might be lost or damaged.  'Honey is not safe for babies.'

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing the deviation of the actual level of security from the expected value given the Situation and the state indicated by the target itself.  'Rogue nations are our greatest threat.'

name: Place
definition_en: A particular location for which the Situation is safe. Frequently, it is to be inferred that the characteristics of the location make various Situations safe or unsafe.

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Situation has the specified level of safety.

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain in which the Situation is safe.  'All of our websites are educationally safe.'

name: Dangerous_entity
definition_en: A concrete or abstract entity which may come to cause the loss of, or damage to the Asset.  'That man is a risk!'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Asset encounters the Risky_situation.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances in which an Asset is at risk.

name: Leader
definition_en: This is the religious or cultural leader who performs and/or leads the rite.  'The medicine man performs this ritual'

name: Member
definition_en: The FE Member describes the member of the religious or cultural group who participates in/undergoes the rite.  'Joe received communion.'

name: Organization
definition_en: Organization identifies the institution in which the rite is prescribed.  'His baptism into the Catholic Church is scheduled for next Sunday.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action that is taken to perform the ritual.  'A building is consecrated by anointing the doorposts with special oil and saying certain prayers'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing the rite

name: Time
definition_en: When the rite is performed

name: Place
definition_en: Where the rite takes place.

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE identifies the Instrument used to perform a particular rite.  'We baptise children with holy water'

name: Desired_state_of_affairs
definition_en: This FE identifies the state which the rite is hoped or intended to bring about. 'They performed a fertility ritual.'

name: Type
definition_en: The type of ritual or ceremony being performed.  'We performed the traditional marriage rites'

name: Object
definition_en: This FE indicates an object on which a rite is performed.  'The priest blessed the wine'

name: New_status
definition_en: Rites may confer a New_status on a participant (e.g. rank, membership).  'Elliott was almost ordained as a priest'

name: Guardian
definition_en: The Guardian is the member of the Organization who instigates the rite for someone of which they are a guardian.  '<fex name = "Guardian">Mr. and Mrs. Wilson baptized their son.'

name: Roadway
definition_en: The Roadway is the roadway that connects locations.  'The road runs between London and Manchester.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is one of the Endpoints treated as a source.  'The road from london to Glastonberry...'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is one of the Endpoints of the Roadway treated as a goal.  'The road from London to Glastonberry...'

name: Endpoints
definition_en: The Endpoints are two (or more) named endpoints of the Roadway.  'The road between London and Glastonberry...'

name: Characteristic
definition_en: The Characteristic is a characteristic(s) of the Roadway.  'It was a long, winding, bumpy road.'

name: Name
definition_en: The Name is the name of the Roadway.  'We went down Abbey road.'

name: Path
definition_en: This is the setting through which the Roadway goes.  'The tunnel through the mountains...'

name: Use
definition_en: The Use is the purpose of the Roadway.  'This is the main traffic artery out of Berkeley.'

name: Direction
definition_en: The Direction is the direction or directions the Roadway runs.  ' I-80 is an east-west highway.'

name: Relative_location
definition_en: The Relative_location is where the Roadway is located.  ' The highways in California are the second-worst in the nation.'

name: Material
definition_en: The Material is what the Roadway is constructed from.

name: Frequency_of_use
definition_en: The Frequency_of_use is the state of the Roadway with regard to the number of people who are using the Roadway or typically use it.

name: Abundant_entities
definition_en: The Abundant_entities are the entities which occupy the space denoted by the Roadway.  ' We passed an avenue of boutiques and restaurants.'

name: Length
definition_en: The Length is the distance the Roadway extends.

name: Part
definition_en: A subpart of the Roadway.  'It was a road with too many twists and turns to count.'

name: Perpetrator
definition_en: The Perpetrator is the person (or other agent) that takes the Goods away by force or threats.  'Leslie robbed Kim of her watch.'

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is the person (or other sentient being or group) that owns the Goods before they are taken away by the Perpetrator.  'Leslie robbed Kim of her watch.'

name: Goods
definition_en: The Goods are anything (including labor, time, or legal rights) that can be taken away.  'Leslie robbed John of his watch.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source is the initial location of the goods, before they change location. 'Leslie and Kim robbed a bank' This FE is realized in compound nouns as follows: 'bank robbery'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means indicates the means by which the Robbery takes place.  'John mugged his victim by holding a toy gun to his head.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes the way in which the Robbery took place.  'He was known for committing violent muggings on schoolchildren'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the Robbery occurs.  'They robbed a bank in North Berkeley.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time indicates when the Robbery occurs.  'They ROBBED a bank in North Berkeley last May.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The action that the Perpetrator is trying to accomplish by the robbery.  'They used to rob folks just to see the expression on their faces.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The state of affairs that the Perpetrator has in mind which leads to the decision to commit the robbery.  'Listen, I just mug people 'cause I got mouths to feed -- nothing personal.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times a robbery event occurs.  ' An Agoura Jills cigar store was robbed twice last week'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: Co-participant denotes a person that participates in a coordinated way in robbery event as the primary protagonist, the Perpetrator.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the sentient being who manipulates the Rope.  'Melissa braided Jessica's hair.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument with which the Rope is manipulated.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the manipulation of the Rope takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.   'Prof. Frink braided my hair to make me look beautiful.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the manipulation of the Rope takes place.  'Terri tied the rope around her waist before scrambling up the side of the mountain.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.  'Kelly tied her laces around the back of her heel to combat loose shoes.'

name: Rope
definition_en: The basically linear object which is manipulated by the Agent to produce a Knot.  'He tied an electrical cable around the trunk and his neck before hanging himself .'

name: Knot
definition_en: The stable configuration of a Rope which results from tying.  'Jake tied the cravat into an acceptable knot.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner in which the manipulation of the Rope takes place.  'John knotted the tie tightly around his neck.'

name: Locus
definition_en: Where the manipulation of the Rope takes place.  'Kelly tied her laces around the back of her heel to combat loose shoes.'

name: Patient
definition_en: The Patient is the entity that undergoes a change.  'The leaves rotted into a mass of slime.' 'The dresses decayed from their former beauty.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the rotting occurs.  'Any traces of uneaten food will decompose in your tank and foul the water.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time indicates when the rotting occurs.  'Before he could get to the specimen , its entrails had decomposed so badly that they had to be thrown away.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation indicates the reason for which the Patient rots.  'Typically, the front top six teeth will decay because of the way the child has sucked on its bottle.'

name: Result
definition_en: The Result is the result of the change of phase of the Patient.  'The leaves rotted into a mass of slime.' 'A dead snail decomposes very rapidly, fouling the water badly.'

name: Initial_state
definition_en: The Initial_state is the original state of the Patient.  'The dresses decayed from their former beauty.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration indicates the amount of time for which the Patient rots.  'That thorn had been there , festering, for months.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the Patient changes.  'A dead snail decomposes very rapidly, fouling the water badly.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: The Subregion describes which part of a larger whole is being affected.  'The cloth was rotting around the edges.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree expressions that indicate to what degree the Patient has changed.  ' Its entrails had totally decomposed.' 'Before he could get to the specimen , its entrails had decomposed so badly that they had to be thrown away.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that a rotting event takes place.  'Often, the food would perish because there was no refrigeration.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Rotting event  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously),  secondary effects (horribly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  'The soldiers' wounds festered slowly'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: A state of affairs that entails the Patient decaying.  'And I've got a piece of ham that 'll spoil if we don't eat it tonight.'

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The person who is at risk of some Bad_outcome

name: Place
definition_en: The place where there is risk. 'There is always some danger to rich men in a bar like this.'

name: Severity
definition_en: The probability of something bad happening to the Protagonist. 'If he is uncertain of right and wrong, he is in dire peril of losing his immortal soul.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the risk pertains. 'Even after the end of Apartheit we still run the risk of letting racism continue forever.'

name: Bad_outcome
definition_en: A situation that the Protagonist would like to avoid. 'There was no risk of his returning.'

name: Asset
definition_en: Something desirable possessed by or directly associated with the Protagonist which might be lost or damaged. 'The risk to his reputation was significant.'

name: Action
definition_en: The Action that creates the risk. 'Implementing this program <supp>runs</supp> the risk of offending our core constituents.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency with which the Protagonist runs risks.  'Some people have no problem with risking their hides every day.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The desired action or goal that the Protagonist hopes to bring about.  'They all risked being caught in order to come to the United States.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: An Explanation for why the Protagonist has put the Asset is in a dangerous situation.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times that the Protagonist risks an Asset.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances indicates the state of affairs under which the risky situation holds.  'Putting forward new ideas risks sparking controversy if you don't frame your argument properly.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The Protagonist intends for his/her actions to benefit Beneficiary in some way.  'They would risk all for their closest friends.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent gives up the Asset in hopes of receiving a greater Benefit.  'We never sacrifice quality for price.'

name: Asset
definition_en: The item which is sacrificed by the Agent.  'We never sacrifice quality for price.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: State of the Agent or Asset.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Agent sacrifices the Asset.  'So many people gladly compromise comfort to look more attractive.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation (the one denoted by the target) to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time when the Agent gives up the Asset.  'In wartime much was compromised in favor of security'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Agent gives up the Asset.

name: Benefit
definition_en: The Agent hopes to receive or gain advantage from the Benefit as a result of giving up the Asset.  'We never sacrifice quality for price.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The volitional Agent who is in line with a Standard.

name: Entity
definition_en: The non-agentive Entity that is in line with a Standard.

name: Event
definition_en: An occurrence or action that brings about the satisfaction or nonsatisfaction of a Standard.

name: Standard
definition_en: The condition or requirement that the Agent, Entity, or Event satisfy (or not).

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Standard is satisfied.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Standard is satisfied.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time in which satisfaction of the Standard occurs.

name: Collection
definition_en: The Collection whose Quantity is under consideration.  'Relax, oil supplies are plentiful.'

name: Quantity
definition_en: The feature of an Collection which is under discussion. This FE is incorporated by all the lexical units in this frame.  'The majority of specimens were poorly represented, as judged by the small size of mature plants, the immaturity of thalli or scarceness in occurrence.'

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Measure from the norm or from the value for another Collection.  'Iron is very scarce inside the human body, so pneumococcal bacteria have mechanisms to obtain iron more easily.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Collection is in the state of having  a particular Measure for the Quantity.  'These days food is plentiful and easy to get and physical activity is no longer a part of daily life.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Collection has a particular Measure for the Quantity.

name: Measure
definition_en: The measure of the Quantity, which is incorporated by the lexical units.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Collection occurs.  'Northern Pike are plentiful in Perrault Lake.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The sentient being who schedules an Event to take place at a Time and Place.  'I set up a meeting with Carlos on Monday.'

name: Event
definition_en: The incident that the Agent has scheduled to take place at a Time and Place.  'I'd like to set up a meeting with Mr. Hofmann.'

name: Scheduled_time
definition_en: The time at which the Event is scheduled to take place.  'Maria scheduled the appointment for Monday.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent has scheduled the Event to take place.  'Gina scheduled a dentist appointment for Monday in Berkeley.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The person for whom the Event was scheduled by the Agent.  'My mom scheduled a dentist appointment for me tomorrow morning.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The frequency with which the Agent schedules and Event.  'Every Monday morning my assistant schedules the weekly meeting according to employee availability.'

name: Means
definition_en: The means used by the Agent in order to schedule the Event.  'Chad always schedules his appointments via email.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Agent's motivation for scheduling the Event.  'My boss scheduled a meeting to let us know how great we were doing.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The cause for the scheduling of the Event.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Agent schedules the Event.   'Jackie hastily scheduled an appointment with a psychologist this evening.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE describes the time at which the scheduling occurs.

name: Event
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that affects a set of entities.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Salient_entity which is under discussion.

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: The entity which enables or causes the Event being judged.

name: Searcher
definition_en: The person who is looking all over the Ground for the Sought_entity.  'They first gained entry into the house of Raja Rao, who resides on the ground floor and ransacked the house for valuables.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The location that the Searcher covers in looking for the Sought_entity.  'I had never really seen much on the bigfoot subject or I would have scoured the area for signs and looked for droppings'

name: Sought_entity
definition_en: The entity that the Searcher wants to find.  'Coast Guard and Navy ships and aircraft combed the area for the six aircraft'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Searcher scrutinizes the Ground.  'We carefully scoured the road for what damaged all of those tires and we finally found it- a piece of nasty, barbed wire, laying across the road.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE specifies the length of the interval during which the scouring activtiy takes place.  'He combed the area for hours that night looking for the dogs and has been searching ever since.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Searcher scrutinizes the Ground.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity manipulated by the Searcher to examine the Ground.  'They scoured the entire beach with a metal detector, but found nothing.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Searcher that allows them to search the Ground.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Searcher hopes to bring about by searching a Ground.  'We scoured the entire book to find this supposed evidence.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Searcher scoures the Ground.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer pays attention to an entity in order to discover something about it.   'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground, so named because it serves as the background or context for the Phenomenon.   'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.' 'Kim searched the woods for mushrooms.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The entity that the Cognizer is alert for in the Ground.  'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.' 'Kim searched the woods for mushrooms.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Cognizer which allows them to scrutinize the Ground.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The event that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by looking for the Phenomenon.  'You should inspect your mail to determine the outcome of the module transfer.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Cognizer  that interacts with the Ground to accomplish the scrutiny.  'The temperature controller monitored the temperature with a calibrated silicon diode.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer pays attention to an entity in order to discover something about it. The FE is normally expressed as an External Argument:  'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground, so named because it serves as the background or context for the Phenomenon. This FE can be expressed as an NP Object or as a PP Complement. 'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.' 'Kim searched the woods for mushrooms.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: Phenomenon identifies the property that belongs to an entity or that the entity contains. Typically, it is expressed as a for-PP. 'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.' 'Kim searched the woods for mushrooms.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE is used for the Means by which the Cognizer to scrutinize the Ground. 'We analysed the sediment by putting it through the mass spec.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

name: Direction
definition_en: Direction is used for all path-like expressions, except those indicating the location of the perceiver, that describe how the perceiver's attention is directed during the act of perception.  'The detective looked across the street at the suspect.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: Some of the words in this frame occur with a constituent that expresses the desired outcome of the Scrutiny.  Normally this constituent is a PP Complement headed by for or a to-marked VP Complement.  'You should inspect your mail to determine the outcome of the module transfer.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The Medium is the piece of text or work in which the Cognizer pays attention to an entity in order to discover something about it. The FE is normally expressed as an External Argument:  'Chapter four examined the case for free speech.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Cognizer  that interacts with the Ground to accomplish the scrutiny.  'The temperature controller monitored the temperature with a calibrated silicon diode.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Cognizer is scrutinizing the Ground.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground in order to find instances of a type of Phenomenon.  'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The Cognizer pays attention to the Ground, so named because it serves as the background or context for the Phenomenon.   'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.' 'Kim searched the woods for mushrooms.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The entity that the Cognizer is alert for in the Ground.  'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.' 'Kim searched the woods for mushrooms.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Cognizer which allows them to scrutinize the Ground.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Cognizer scrutinizes the Ground.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The event that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by looking for the Phenomenon.  'You should inspect your mail to determine the outcome of the module transfer.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Cognizer  that interacts with the Ground to accomplish the scrutiny.  'The temperature controller monitored the temperature with a calibrated silicon diode.'

name: Phenomenon
definition_en: The Phenomenon is the activity, state or object that is purposefully hidden from the awareness of a potential cognizer.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Phenomenon is hidden from cognizers.

name: Time
definition_en: A period of Time during which the Phenomenon is hidden from the awareness of potential cognizers.  'There was stuff in there that was 'secret' in the 1980s, but has since become pretty common knowledge.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person who might become aware of the Phenomenon if it was not concealed.   'Moreover, the blood and decorations were sacred and could only be removed in a procedure which was secret from women'

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer realizes the existence of a deception and is not misled by it.

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The State_of_affairs is intended to be perceived and taken to be true even though it is not.

name: Focal_entity
definition_en: The Focal_entity is a part of the deception (possibly also the agent behind it) which is perceived by the Cognizer to be misleading.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by the Cognizer which enables them to figure something out.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the text created by the Cognizer to communicate that they came to believe a specified State_of_affairs.

name: Topic
definition_en: Some verbs in this frame may occur with postverbal Topic expressions

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Cognizer comes to understand the State_of_affairs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Cognizer.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Cognizer realizes the State_of_affairs.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Cognizer discovers the State_of_affairs.

name: Cognizer_agent
definition_en: The person who attempts to find the Sought_entity. 'John  looked for his pencil.'

name: Ground
definition_en: This is the entity to which the Cognizer_agent pays attention. It is referred to as Ground because it serves as the background or context for the Sought_entity. This FE can be expressed as an NP Object (first example) or as a PP Complement (second example).  'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.'  'Kim searched in the woods for mushrooms.'

name: Sought_entity
definition_en: This is the entity that the Ground may contain. Typically, it is expressed as a for-PP.   'Leslie examined the glass for cracks.'  'Kim searched in the woods for mushrooms.'  Some words in this frame allow alternate expressions of the Ground and the Sought_entity.  'We searched the yard for my contact lens.'   'We searched for my contact lens in the yard.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner of performing an action.

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Cognizer_agent that allows them to look for the Sought_entity. 'They foraged for clams by visiting the pools at low tide.'

name: Outcome
definition_en: The failure or success of an attempt.

name: Place
definition_en: A spatial setting larger than the Ground in which the Seeking event occurs.  'In Paris police were hunting for suspects in two of the city's southerns suburbs today'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Seeking occurs.  'The police were hunting for evidence in my house yesterday'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Cognizer_agent intends to accomplish by performing the search.  'Police were hunting for evidence in my house to mislead their real suspect about the state of the investigation'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the amount of effort put into an attempt.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a State_of_affairs or to  obtain a Sought_entity.  'Those states sought a remedy that would substantially change the company's business practices.'

name: Sought_entity
definition_en: The entity that the Agent attempts to acquire.  'Or the monstrous Saddam, who filled mass graves to bursting, invaded two neighboring countries, and avidly sought weapons of mass destruction.'

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of an attempt to acquire a Sought_entity.  'WWDA also successfully sought funding from Office of the Status of Women'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an attempt at achieving a State_of_affairs or at acquiring the Sought_entity is made.  'Agassi sought relief by taking Advil.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the amount of effort put into an attempt.  'He also sought intensely to know more of Christ.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt occurs.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the Agent is seeking to achieve a particular State_of_affairs or to acquire a Sought_entity.  'The disclosure came as prosecutors successfully sought in federal court to keep Luise Garofalo behind bars.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Agent makes the attempt.

name: Duration
definition_en: The time period over which the attempts at achieving a State_of_affairs or acquiring the Sought_entity take place.  'Finally the peace I've sought for years!'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by bringing about a particular State_of_affairs or acquiring the Sought_entity.

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: A state or event that the Agent wants to bring about. The Agent may but need not be a participant in that State_of_affairs.  ' His enemies sought his destruction.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A proposition from which the occurrence of the seeking event follows.  'About 6% of all abortions are sought because either the woman or fetus has medical reasons.'

name: Source
definition_en: An individual or organization that helps the Agent bring about the State_of_affairs or delivers the Sought_entity to the Agent.  'He has lain that way ever since and has given power to all who sought it from him.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE introduces the underlying situation(s) in which seeking occurs.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: This FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the Sought_entity or State_of_affairs .   'Jed sought the world's largest diamond for his Jeda .'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent who tries to keep an Event from taking place.

name: Event
definition_en: The Event is the action or state of affairs that the Agent wishes to prevent.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place  is where the Agent attempts to prevent the Event from taking place.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Agent prevents the Event from taking place.

name: Self_mover
definition_en: Self_mover is the living being which moves under its own power. Normally it is expressed as an external argument. 'Fred crawled the narrow passage.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source is used for any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion.  With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context. 'The cat ran out of the house.' 'The cat ran out.' 'The cat ran away.' 'The cat ran off.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path is used for any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.  This includes "middle of path'' expressions.  'The scouts hiked through the desert.' 'The scouts hiked along the river.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is used for any expression which tells where the Self_mover ends up as a result of the motion.  'The children skipped into the park.' Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance. 'The principal walked over and sat down.' 'A dog ran up and licked our hands.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory or rate of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.  'We slithered smoothly through the crowd.' 'They had to trek on foot through the desert.'

name: Distance
definition_en: Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.  'I barely hobbled six feet before collapsing.' 'We hiked a short distance into the forest and sat down.'

name: Area
definition_en: Area is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path.  Note that this FE should not be used for cases when the same phrase could be used with the same meaning with a non-motion target, since these should be annotated with the Place FE.  'The mouse scurried about.' 'Stop running around the room and sit down!'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the motion occurs.

name: Cotheme
definition_en: An entity whose motion is correlated with that of the Self_mover, following and tracking the Self_mover, being followed and tracked, or with both parties mutually matching Paths.  'We clomped down to the shore with a whole troop of younglings.' 'I had little hope of catching up, but I crawled after her as fast as I could.' 'The troops marching in front of him paid no attention to the beggar by the roadside.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The rate at which the location of the Self_mover changes with respect to time.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action 'We wandered around naked.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Self_mover achieves movement. 'He walked back to the village by dragging his mangled foot behind.'

name: Result
definition_en: Result of an event

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotional or mental state of the Self_mover which motivates them toward motion or the particular manner of motion.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which a Self_mover moves. 'John walked with her every day to relieve the boredom.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location within which a defined motion takes place.  Any specified or implied  Source, Path or Goal should designate a location contained with the Place.  This FE can be differentiated from Area by the fact that the annotated phrase can be used in the same meaning with non-motion targets.  'The hitchhikers walked in the middle of the road.'  ''

name: Explanation
definition_en: The state of affairs that leads to the particular motion that the Self_mover adopts.

name: External_cause
definition_en: External_cause is something in the external environment that causes the Self_mover  to move.   'They danced at the sound of her voice.'

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction that the Self_mover heads in during the motion.  'You should walk south about a block .'

name: Coordinated_event
definition_en: The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event-it does not allow states-that the Traversing is rhythmically aligned with. The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.

name: Path_shape
definition_en: The shape of the overall Path travelled by the Self_mover.

name: Concessive
definition_en: An event or circumstance that would not be expected given the nature of the particular Self_motion event.

name: Sender
definition_en: This is the person who initiates the movement of the Theme and, unlike Carrying, does not accompany it.

name: Path
definition_en: Path along which movement occurs. I  shipped the books along Interstate 65.

name: Goal
definition_en: The end of the path and intended goal of the sending. I sent the logs to the shed.

name: Source
definition_en: The beginning of the path, similar to source except that it serves to define the path. I sent wood from Illinois to California.

name: Theme
definition_en: The objects being sent. I mailed the books to Alaska. Note that Theme may be multiply instantiated. They maileda questionnaire with a return envelope.

name: Transport_means
definition_en: The mode of sending employed. I shipped the crops by bigrig .

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the Sender or Theme 'He faxed his order while brushing his teeth'

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme. Pat threw the Javelin 50 meters.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Recipient
definition_en: This is the recipient of the sent Theme. Tess mailed a letter  to Abby

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose of the sending. 'Rachel sent the letter to her mother to let her know about the marriage.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for the sending. 'Letters are generally forwarded for several months because people are lazy about telling people their new location.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the sending takes place 'I sent the letter to you last week.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: An additional theme sent along with the main Theme.

name: Container
definition_en: A container in which the Theme is sent. 'Please send in the request in a self-addressed stamped envelope.'

name: Place
definition_en: A spatial setting encomnpassing the Source location, where the Sending event takes place.  'Barney posted the letter on Monday in Athens'

name: Perceiver_passive
definition_en: This FE is only expressed with certain nouns in this frame, and then only with the help of a support verb, such as have:  'I have a tingling sensation in my hands.'  With most nouns in this frame, a perceiver can only be expressed as the subject of a perception verb such as detect or sense:  'The dog detected the scent of explosives.' In sentences like these the perceiver-denoting expression is not annotated because it is introduced by another perception word, which is treated independently in a different frame.

name: Source
definition_en: This is the entity or phenomenon which gives rise to the sensation. In cases of veridical sensation, this FE is not typically distinguished from Percept. Most of the phrases that express this FE can be paraphrased as from-phrases, e.g.  'The smell of the garlic made me hungry.' 'The smell from the garlic made me hungry.' 'The smell of garlic made me hungry.' '*The smell from garlic made me hungry.' The first sentence, in which the object of the prepostion of is a definite NP, can be roughly paraphrased by the second sentence, which replaces the of-PP with a from-PP. This shows that the phrase of the garlic in the first sentence expresses Source. On the other hand, the third sentence, in which the object of the preposition of is a bare noun, cannot be so paraphrased. The bare-noun of-PPs express Percept rather than Source. Source can be expressed as the External Argument of a support verb, e.g. 'This herb emits a strong odour. '

name: Percept
definition_en: The FE Percept is used for phrases that express the characteristic property of a sensation. Typically this characteristic property is described with reference to the entity or phenomenon that produces the sensation---that  is why this FE can be difficult to distinguish from Source. It is possible for Source and Percept to be expressed separately, however:  'This herb gives off a smell of garlic.'  In cases in which it is impossible to distinguish between Source and Percept, Percept is used as the default FE.

name: Body_part
definition_en: This FE is assigned to phrases expressing the body part in which a sensation is located. Since touch is the least localized of sense modalities, words relating to haptic sensations are the ones most likely to occur with this FE:  'I have a tingling feeling in my hands.'  Words for other sense modalities can occasionally express this FE as well: 'There is a bitter taste on the back of my tongue.' 'The ringing sound in my left ear distracted me during class. '

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the sensation not covered by a more specific FE.

name: Ground
definition_en: This FE is the perceptual background against which the Phenomenon is experienced by the Perceiver.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the sensation is perceived.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE describes how strong the sensation is.

name: Sender
definition_en: This is the person or organization who initiates the movement of the Sent_item and, unlike in the case of Carrying, does not accompany it.  'Today's mail from eBay brought me a copy of this book.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The end of the path and intended goal of the sending.  'My shipment to Australia was received in 10 days.'

name: Source
definition_en: The beginning of the path, similar to source except that it serves to define the path.  'Mail from England to our office is sent registered mail.'

name: Sent_item
definition_en: The objects being sent.   'Today the post contained a pair of brand new tyres from Continental.'

name: Transport_means
definition_en: The mode of sending employed.  'We promise to expedite your air mail as agreed.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: This is the recipient of the sent Sent_item  'He went to the study and examined his mail'

name: Time
definition_en: When an interaction with the Sent_item occurs.  'Finally, today's mail contained yet another book by the same author.'

name: Place
definition_en: The  place in which the Sent_item is located.  'After that, I notice the mail on the table.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any characterizations or evaluations of the the Sent_item that introduce another frame, in which the Sent_item figures.  'A cat could have kittens before the stupid shipment rolled in.'

name: Convict
definition_en: The Convict is given a Sentence by the Court. 'Judge Duncan sentenced Marty to five years under house detention.'

name: Court
definition_en: The Court imposes a Sentence on a Convict. 'Judge Duncan sentenced Marty to five years under house detention.'

name: Sentence
definition_en: The Sentence is imposed on the Convict by the Court. 'Judge Duncan sentenced Marty to five years under house detention.'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE denotes the type of sentence. 'He will receive a prison sentence if convicted.'

name: Term_of_sentence
definition_en: This FE denotes the duration of the sentence. 'Tom will recieve a sentence of five years.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Convict is sentenced.  'He will be sentenced at a later date.'

name: Offense
definition_en: The illegal action of which the Convict has been found guilty and for which they are punished.  'A pet store owner was sentenced for illegaly smuggling protected reptiles.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location of the sentencing Court.  'Biancaniello will be sentenced in San Francisco later this summer.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state that the Convict is  in at the time of their sentencing.  'He was sentenced in absentia during the mass trials.'

name: Whole
definition_en: The Whole is a single entity or an aggregate of entities which is separated into Parts.  It is usually the NP Object of a target verb.  'The directors split the company in two.' ' The teacher divided the children into groups. '

name: Parts
definition_en: This refers collectively to the Parts resulting from separation of a Whole: 'The directors split the company in two.' 'The teacher divided the children into groups.'  'The teacher separated the children from each other. '

name: Part_1
definition_en: Part-1 is the first of two Parts mentioned. This is most often the Object of a verb.  'First, separate the yolks from the whites. '

name: Part_2
definition_en: Part_2 is the second of two Parts mentioned. This is usually a PP Complement. First, 'separate the yolks from the whites. '

name: Agent
definition_en: With causative uses of these verbs, an Agent separates or divides something.  The Agent is usually expressed as the External Argument:  'The researcher divided subjects into groups. '

name: Criterion
definition_en: This frame element expresses a property of the Parts or components of the Whole which is used as the basis for separation. Criterion is typically expressed as a PP headed by by, or as a complex PP of the form on the basis of....  'The researcher divided subjects into groups on the basis of eye color.' As with the frame General.Joining (above), words in this frame can be used statively, as in The rooms are separated by a partition, inchoatively, as in The group separated or causatively, as in I separated the laundry.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent who separates or the undergoers of the separation. 'Naked, Selma Bouvier separated the yolks from the whites.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Agent that accomplishes the separation. 'You can bisect an angle by drawing three circles.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an event.

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is the non-agent that brings about the separation.

name: Recipients
definition_en: The Recipients are the groups who come into possession of the Parts of the Whole.  'Mrs. Simpson divided the candy between her children.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the separation occurs. 'I divided the prize money among the winners that night.'.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the separation occurs. 'You should separate the yolks from the whites over the sink.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument used to cause the separation. 'I sectioned the block with a knife.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Agent's intent for separating the Whole.

name: Entity_1
definition_en: This entity occurs in some sequence with Entity_2.

name: Entity_2
definition_en: This entity occurs in some sequence with respect to Entity_1.

name: Entities
definition_en: Entities that occur in some temporal order.

name: Relation_type
definition_en: A characterization of the sequence in which the entities occur.  'The study consisted of a chronologically varied SERIES of grotesque heads.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the sequence.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the entity that occpuies the Role.

name: Role
definition_en: The Role that the Agent occupies.

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration of time that the Agent occupies the Role.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: The Descriptor modifies the Agent .

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Agent served in the Role.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Agent served in the Role.

name: Component_entities
definition_en: The entities that function together as a unit.   'How could consciousness arise in a system of matter?'

name: Complex
definition_en: The unit formed by the Component_entities.  'An open system is any distinct entity -- a cell, a person, a forest, or an orchestra organization -- that takes in resources from its environment, processes them in some way, and produces output.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any characterization or evaluation of the Complex.  'Because the earth is a closed system, disposing of products at the end of their useful life can waste usable materials.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: A person or organization that possesses or owns the Complex or a larger entity of which the Complex itself is a part.

name: Superset
definition_en: The Superset is the larger collection of entities that includes the Subset.

name: Subset
definition_en: The Subset comprises a part of the Superset.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the inclusion event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the set relation holds.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the set relation holds.

name: Firefighter
definition_en: The Firefighter is the person making the firebreak.

name: Flame
definition_en: The Flame is what is created by the Firefighter.

name: Flammables
definition_en: The Flammables is the the object that is burned in the back fire.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the event takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Firefighter that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An event brought about by the Firefighter that actually makes the Flammables catch fire.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes the Firefighter as being in some state during the action.

name: Kindler
definition_en: The Kindler is the person performing the intentional act. ' Mark started the fire with a magnifying glass. '

name: Flame
definition_en: The Flame is what is created by the Kindler. 'Oscar started the fire.'

name: Flammables
definition_en: The Flamables is the the object that is set on fire by the Kindler. 'Tracy set the couch on fire.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The cause of the fire. 'A spark ignited the curtains.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the event takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Kindler that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An event brought about by the Cause or the Kindler that actually makes the Flammables catch fire.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes the Kindler as being in some state during the action.

name: Self_mover
definition_en: This is the entity which moves under its own power.

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

name: Path
definition_en: A relation to a landmark that describes the trajectory in the midst of the motion.  (It is thus neither a Source nor the Intended_goal.)

name: Intended_goal
definition_en: Any expression which tells where the Self_mover intends to end up as a result of the motion.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.

name: Means
definition_en: An event involving the Self_mover that results in the Self_mover moving in the specified way.

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the Self_mover moves.

name: Cotheme
definition_en: A second moving object which the Self_mover moves to follow.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Self_mover during the action.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.

name: Path_shape
definition_en: The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Self_mover, taken simultaneously.

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction in which the Self_mover goes.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the motion takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Self_mover wishes to bring about.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The device or bodypart that serves to move the Self_mover.

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The length of time that the Self_mover spends away from the Source.

name: Result
definition_en: The state of the Self_mover at the end of the event.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Self_mover.

name: Reciprocation
definition_en: An event paired with the motion, which explains why the motion is expected. In particular, Reciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished by the motion, and/or is paired with the motion as the other side of an agreement.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time of departure and which the departure is taken to be a part of.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: A larger conceptualization that includes the departing as an integral part. The departure expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.

name: New_situation
definition_en: An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Self_mover), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the departing.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the departing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.

name: Coordinated_event
definition_en: The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event (it does not allow states) that the departing is rhythmically aligned with. (This would then further require that the departing be iterated.)  The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.

name: Distance
definition_en: The distance from the Source that the Self_mover ends up.

name: Offense
definition_en: The Offense is the action, crime, or event which is described in terms of what legal or punishing action can be taken against the offender.

name: Code
definition_en: The legal Code under which the severity of the offense is determined. 'That crime is indictable under British law.'

name: Participants
definition_en: The set of entities engaged in or subjected to sexual contact.

name: Participant_1
definition_en: One party present for sex.

name: Participant_2
definition_en: Another party present for sex.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE describes the length of time that an entire sexual encounter can last, including but not necessarily implying the length of all stages of the encounter.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the sex act which is not covered by more specific FEs. In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of one or more Participants that also affect the action.

name: Place
definition_en: To be clear: the place FE describes the overall location of the Participants of the sexual activity and nothing else.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE relates the relative time of occurrence of the sexual activity.

name: Domain
definition_en: For a sexual act, the Domain describes the specific realm of the contact between Participants; for example, phone sex.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the justification of a sexual act, for at least one of the Participants.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which Participants accomplish a sexual act.

name: Parents
definition_en: The parents who will receive offspring.

name: Father
definition_en: The participant in a sexual relationship who fertilizes an egg.

name: Mother
definition_en: The participant in a sexual relation whose egg is fertilized.

name: Offspring
definition_en: The zygote, in some stage of development.

name: Part
definition_en: A shaped Part of a larger Whole.  'Sergey put his arm on the arm of his armchair.'

name: Whole
definition_en: A Whole which has a shaped Part.  'The leg of the table came off when we moved it.'

name: Part_prop
definition_en: A property relating to the shaped Part of a Whole.   'Sue fixed the broken leg of the table.'

name: Orientation
definition_en: This is a property of the shaped Part that situates  the  Part within the Whole.  'Abby broke  the top handle of the suitcase . '

name: Substance
definition_en: A Substance of which pieces can be extracted.'Sue ate a big square of cake.'

name: Shape
definition_en: This is the Shape that the Substance is in.'I ate a stick of butter.'

name: Shape_prop
definition_en: This describes a property of the Shape, e.g. it's size.'Sue ate a big square of cake.'

name: Count
definition_en: The number of units of the measured Substance. 'Serena found two squares of coth in the cabinet.'

name: Protagonists
definition_en: The jointly expressed participants in the use of the Entity.  'It was a small house so they had to share the bed.'

name: Protagonist_1
definition_en: The participant that is encoded as the subject of an active-form sentence or as a by-PP in a passive, who partakes in the joint usage of the Entity.  'I shared my breakfast with the woman on my right, because she had forgotten hers.'

name: Protagonist_2
definition_en: The participant in the reciprocal event that is coded in a with-PP, who partakes in the usage of the Entity along with Protagonist_1.  'When I looked back, Henry was sharing his juice with his classmate.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The object that is shared by the Protagonists.  'Prices are based on two people sharing a twin room.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Protagonists share the Entity.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Protagonists partake jointly in the use of the Entity.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity to which the Sharpness attribute is related.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The sharpness feature of the Entity.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Sharpness from the norm or from the value for another Entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having  a particular value for Sharpness.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Entity has a particular value for the Sharpness.

name: Sharpness
definition_en: The Sharpness value of the Entity.  This FE is denoted by the adjectives of the frame.

name: Firearm
definition_en: The device used by the Agent to cause the motion of the Projectile.

name: Projectile
definition_en: The entity whose rapid, dangerous motion is caused by the Agent and/or Firearm.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act causing the motion of the Projectile.

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Theme. Pat threw the Javelin 50 meters.

name: Goal
definition_en: This FE is the point at which the Theme ends up as a result of the motion. Kim threw the cat into the garden.

name: Manner
