definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Agent whereby the rapid motion of the Projectile is achieved.

name: Path
definition_en: This FE is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal. I pushed the trolley along the street.

name: Source
definition_en: This FE is the starting point of motion. Pat dragged the box out of the cupboard.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the state of the Agent or Projectile during the event.  'He shot three arrows at the target, all unsuspecting as to why Harold had done so well.'

name: Area
definition_en: This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element. Kim pushed the lawnmower around the garden.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the shooting event takes place.  'The bankrobbers were crazy enough to shoot at the clerks with an AK-47 inside the bank'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the shooting event takes place.  'The robbers shot at the clerks as they ran out of the bank'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Agent's purpose in launching the Projectile  'We mistook a satellite launched to study earthquakes to be a missile, so we shot it down over the Pacific.'

name: Firearm
definition_en: The device used by the Agent to cause the motion of the Projectile.

name: Projectile
definition_en: The entity whose rapid, dangerous motion is caused by the Agent and/or Firearm.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act causing the motion of the Projectile.

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE is any expression characterizing the extent of motion of the Projectile.  'Pat threw the Javelin 50 meters.'

name: Goal
definition_en: This FE is the point at which the Theme ends up as a result of the motion. Kim threw the cat into the garden.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Agent whereby the rapid motion of the Projectile is achieved.

name: Path
definition_en: This FE is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor Goal. I pushed the trolley along the street.

name: Source
definition_en: This FE is the starting point of motion. Pat dragged the box out of the cupboard.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Depictive
definition_en: A description of the state of the Agent or Projectile during the event.  'He shot three arrows at the target, all unsuspecting as to why Harold had done so well.'

name: Area
definition_en: This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular or not to consist of a single, linear path. Locative setting adjuncts may also be assigned this frame element. Kim pushed the lawnmower around the garden.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the shooting event takes place.  'The bankrobbers were crazy enough to shoot at the clerks with an AK-47 inside the bank'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the shooting event takes place.  'The robbers shot at the clerks as they ran out of the bank'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Agent's purpose in launching the Projectile  'We mistook a satellite launched to study earthquakes to be a missile, so we shot it down over the Pacific.'

name: Shopper
definition_en: The person who attempts to find the Goods. 'John shopped for a pencil.'

name: Ground
definition_en: This is the entity to which the Cognizer pays attention. It is referred to as the Ground because it serves as the background or context for the Goods. This FE is usually expressed as a preposition phrase.

name: Goods
definition_en: This is the entity that the Ground may contain. Typically, it is expressed as afor-PP.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the shopping action is done.

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Shopper that allows them to look for (and perhaps purchase) the Goods.  'They shopped for hot items by camping out overnight at shopping malls.'

name: Outcome
definition_en: The failure or success of an attempt.

name: Place
definition_en: A spatial setting larger than the Ground in which the Shopping event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the shopping occurs.  'The children were shopping for gifts for their parents before Christmas.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Shopper intends to accomplish by performing the search.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the amount of effort put into shopping.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of shopping scenario as being in some state during the action.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: The Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the shopping event with the Shopper.

name: Lender
definition_en: The original owner and soon to be Lender of the Assets.

name: Assets
definition_en: The financial Assets being traded.

name: Intermediary
definition_en: The entity that is the borrower to the Lender and the seller and later repurchaser to the Market.

name: Market
definition_en: The aggregate selling place of many types of financial stocks, bond, securities, etc. The Market is also a metonym for the people who buy the Assets.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The situation that the Intermediary wishes to bring about by short selling.  Because this concept is associated with finance, the Purpose is normally to earn a profit.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time at which the Intermediary engages in short selling.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place at which the short selling occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Intermediary that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Intermediary acts intentionally.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the the state of the Astronomical_entity during the motion.  'That morning the sun rose blood red in the east.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the location above the horizon that the Astronomical_entity ends up in.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the motion of the  Astronomical_entity takes place. It covers any description of the appearance  which is not covered by more specific FEs such as Speed,  including general descriptions comparing events (the same way), and aesthetic judgements of the event .  'The sun rose beautifully, but the air was cold.'

name: Path
definition_en: The sequence of locations that the Astronomical_entity traverses as it comes over the horizon.  'A pale copper sun rose through a sea of muted cloud layers, and now there is no afterglow at all.'

name: Speed
definition_en: This FE identifies the Speed at which the Astronomical_entity comes into view.   'In the summer, the sun comes up quickly, and you?ll need to work fast. '

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Astronomical_entity appears.  'As the sun came up at 5:15 am, it made the red rocks almost glow.'

name: Astronomical_entity
definition_en: An entity which is periodically visible from the earth's surface.   'Heku left one morning as the sun rose along the plain.'

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location the Astronomical_entity is construed to occupy before coming above the horizon.   'The night passed away, and the sun rose from the ocean.'

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of the Astronomical_entity's motion.   ' As we continued moving east, the sun rose high.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place from which the motion of the Astronomical_entity is viewed.  'The very end of the eclipse will be visible as the sun rises in some locations in Africa and northeastern North America.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Astronomical_entity comes into view above the horizon.  'When the sun rose fully, painting the area a beautiful red gold his father would turn to him and smile.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: A setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the appearance of the Astronomical_entity takes place  'The Sun rose with just a few clouds along the eastern horizon as we eagerly unpacked our gear.'

name: Correlated_event
definition_en: An event that takes place simultaneously with the Astronomical_entity's appearance.  'The moon rose with the early onset of dusk.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: FN: The amount of times the Astronomical_entity appears per unit of time.

name: Indicator
definition_en: The phenomenon that signifies the Indicated.  'He was unable to display any sign of pain.'

name: Indicated
definition_en: The phenomenon that is signified by the Indicator.  'We now exhibt the same symptoms of the same disease.'

name: Reliability
definition_en: This FE indicates the Reliability of the Indicator as a sign of the Indicated.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description of the Indicator not covered by a more specific FE.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE depicts how often the Indicated manifests itself.  'A 24-hour Holter moniter should be considered only for patients with daily symptoms.'

name: Signatory
definition_en: The signatory of the Agreement.  'Eisenhower signed a treaty  with aliens.'

name: Signature
definition_en: The entity signifying the identity of the Signatory, resulting from the act of writing on the Agreement document.  'The Attorney General seemingly never put his signature on the agreement.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: An expression of the state of the Signatory at the time of signing.  'Jean signed the contract naked.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Signatory that interacts with the Agreement document so as to produce the Signature.  'He signed the contract with a mixture of his own blood and spit.'

name: Place
definition_en: The place where the signing occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Signatory that also affect the action (happily, eagerly).   'Bob eagerly signed the contract.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the action whereby the Signatory achieves the signing of the Agreement.   'He signed the contract by writing his name, Cornelis Wynkoop.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Signatory commits to the Agreement.  'In order to become a Party Australia will need to sign the Protocol by 31 March 1998 and then take the binding step of ratification.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time at which signature is given.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for putting signature to paper.

name: Agreement
definition_en: The document which encodes the commitment of the Signatory.  'I signed the contract and now the dealership claims they made a mistake, quoted the price too low and now I have to pay them more money. '

name: Co-participant
definition_en: The Co-participant signs the Agreement along with the Signatory.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: his extrathematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of Agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

name: Role
definition_en: The category of the Signatory in the Sign_agreement event.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person performing the intentional act.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed. 'John quieted the crowd to reassert his authority.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Agent silences the Speaker.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The sentient entity that is not communicating.

name: Topic
definition_en: This is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It is typically expressed as a PP Complement headed by about.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which an intentional act is performed. 'I hushed him because quiet hours were in effect.'

name: Result
definition_en: The Result is the final state of the Speaker.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The Expressor is the Speaker's voice or other communicative noise emitted by the Speaker. </def-root >

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the silencing event  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).   'Kim shushed Pat rather haughtily.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Agent succeeds in creating silence.  'Valois silenced the crowd completely with one commanding gesture'

name: Entities
definition_en: This FE marks constituents that express the set of objects or types whose similarity is at issue.   ' The two painters  were alike in being unable to draw acceptably . ' 'Agbenugba confirms the resemblances between his own experience and that of his protagonist.'

name: Entity_1
definition_en: When there is an asymmetry, Entity_1 is the entity characterized by its similarity to Entity_2, whose characteristics are assumed to be known.  Entity_1 is often an external argument.  'In the first phase Barthes's approach has similarities to that of Levi-Strauss.' 'Our economy is like a healthy plant after a long drought' 'I found a similar passage in Tolkien.'

name: Entity_2
definition_en: When the Entities are expressed separately, Entity_2 is the one whose characteristics are assumed to be known; it serves as a basis for establishing characteristics of Entity_1.  'The results of Method 2 show remarkable similarity to those obtained by Method 1' 'Leadbelly's recordings are not dissimilar to those of Jimmie Rodgers.' 'This is a problem different from meltdown only in degree.' 'Here we see a similar case. DNI'

name: Dimension
definition_en: This FE marks constituents which express a property in respect to which the similarity of the entities is assessed.  'The disc announced Friday is physically similar to current music CDs '

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which entities are similar to each other, in general or with respect to some Dimension(s)  'The twins are very similar.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the similarity occurs or exists.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the general area in which similarity occurs or exists

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which Dimension is similar or different

name: Explanation
definition_en: An inanimate entity or process that causes the similarity.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describing the state of the Entities

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Differentiating_fact
definition_en: A fact about Entity_1 or the Entities that reveals how Entity_1 is the same or different from other entities.  (Note the contrast with 'as to'.)  'His presidency was different in that it offered a way forward for the common man .' 'Banks primarily differ in offering different rates for different risks .' 'We are all similar in having two arms , two legs , a mind , and a heart to feel with .'

name: Term
definition_en: The linguistic sign that is used for referring to a type of Entity.  'The French term for this is rime pauvre or rime faible.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The type of Entity that is conventionally referred to by a Term.  'Jews are still waiting for the "annointed one" to come; their word for this is Messiah.'

name: Speaker
definition_en: A speaker or speech community that uses a Term to refer to a particular Entity.  ' An antigen is biologists? term for an invading organism, such as the influenza virus.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The type of Entity that is conventionally referred to by a Term.  'Because of that shift, physicists call this effect the "gravitational red shift."'

name: Term
definition_en: The linguistic sign that is used for referring to a type of Entity.  'The French term this plant Petit Chêne, from the shape of the leaves.'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The speaker or speech community that uses a Term to refer to a particular Entity.  'Mathematicians call this subject "arithmetic," reserving the word "algebra" for the more advanced aspects of the subject.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A reason for why the Term used for the Entity is the one chosen.  'They call their chip the C-Most because it is a CMOS chip.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Speaker uses the Term referring to the Entity.

name: Profiled_event
definition_en: The event which is asserted to occur at the same time as the Landmark_event.

name: Landmark_event
definition_en: The event or time period whose timing the Profiled_event is judged against.

name: Events
definition_en: The states-of-affairs which are asserted to be co-timed.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Profiled_event and Landmark_event coincide.  'The attacks on the palace nearly coincided with the beginning of peace talks.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The thing whose size is being considered.  'I had a big dinner.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the size of the Entity deviates from the norm.  'I had a really big dinner.'

name: Standard
definition_en: The size of the Entity may be compared to the size of a Standard.  'You 're tall for a Swede.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: This FE denotes a specific subregion being sized.

name: Dimension
definition_en: The feature of an (actual or possible) Entity that is measured. In literal examples, it essentially must be size, or a word equivalent to size such as bulk.  'The particles were smaller in size than expected .' 'Her <fex name="">huge girth interfered with normal daily activities .' 'Chickens hardly have an immense intellect .'

name: Sleeper
definition_en: The entity that is sleeping.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the sleep occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Sleeper is asleep.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the sleeping event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, noisily), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  'Fitzhume slept soundly'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.

name: Sleeper
definition_en: The Sleeper is the entity that is sleeping.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the event occurs.

name: Perpetrator
definition_en: This is the person (or other agent) that illegally takes the goods into or out of a country.

name: Goods
definition_en: The FE Goods is anything (including labor, time, or legal rights) that can be illegally taken into our out of a country.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which a state holds or a process is ongoing.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Source
definition_en: The source is the location the goods occupy initially before change of location.

name: Path
definition_en: The path refers to (a part of the) ground the Goods travel over or to a landmark the Goods travel by.

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is the location the Goods end up in.

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Perpetrator which allows them to smuggle the Goods.

name: Event
definition_en: The unlawful movement of Goods.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the Event not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In most cases, it indicates salient characteristics of a Perpetrator that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully). 'The rebels had secretly smuggled in several tonnes of explosives.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The action that the Perpetrator is trying to accomplish by the act of smuggling.  'We smuggled you in here to try to help but ...'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that a smuggling event occurs.  'Inmates frequently smuggle marijuana into the prison'

name: Constant_location
definition_en: The container, vehicle, or other entity that the Goods move with and remain stationary with respect to.  'She 'll smuggle them in suit cases.'

name: Distance
definition_en: The distance travelled by the Goods.

name: Speed
definition_en: The amount of time per distance travelled by the Goods.  'They smuggled the bomb swiftly through customs.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person performing the soaking.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the entity that changes location.  ' Ellen soaked the beans in the water  for 30 seconds .'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the Theme is soaked.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Agent soaks the Theme.

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the substance in which the Theme is submerged.'Bobby soaked the potatoes in water overnight.'

name: Container
definition_en: This FE identifies the Container that holds the Theme which is submerged and the Medium that it is in.  'soak the potatoes in a medium-sized pan.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the submerging occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Agent soaks the Theme.

name: Means
definition_en: The action of the Agent that brings about the soaking.  'Soak the beans by placing the entire package, unopened, in the water.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The situation that the Agent hopes to bring about by soaking the Theme.

name: Item
definition_en: The Item is the absorbant friendly thing that takes in the Substance.

name: Substance
definition_en: The Substance is the material that is taken in by the Item.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Item takes in Substance.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Item takes in Substance.

name: Duration
definition_en: For what length of time the Item is imbued with Substance.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Item soaks in the Substance.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree describes the extent to which a particular absorption event deviates from the norm.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist is the person whose sociability is being described.  'Pat is sociable.' 'Pat was a very shy child.' 'Pat is a loner.' 'Everyone had heard about the recluse SLF who lived on the hill. '

name: Company
definition_en: The Protagonist may be sociable, shy, outgoing, etc. when with particular Company (specific people or types of people).  Company usually occurs in a PP Complement with a target adjective: 'Kim is shy of strangers.'  'The children are friendly to everyone they meet. '

name: Content
definition_en: The Protagonist may be sociable, shy, outgoing, etc. when in a particular situation, or about performing some action.  'Kim is outgoing when traveling alone.' 'Kim is timid about meeting new people. '

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.  'Pongo is very shy, In my opinion.'

name: Behavior
definition_en: The Behavior is the action of the Individual on which the evaluation of the Individual's character is based.

name: Individual
definition_en: The Individual is the person whose Behavior is being evaluated.

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the described Behavior deviates from the norm.

name: Individuals
definition_en: Individuals have a Connection with each other.

name: Individual_1
definition_en: Individual1 has a social Connection to Individual_2.

name: Individual_2
definition_en: Individual2 has a relationship to Individual_1.

name: Connection
definition_en: Connection is the personal relationship between Individuals that keeps them involved in each other's lives.

name: Type
definition_en: Type is the sub-category to which the Connection belongs.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree (strength or closeness) of the Connection.

name: Evaluee
definition_en: The Evaluee is being judged for its quality.   ' His shirt seems very common compared to their modern fashions.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the  Degree to which the Evaluee is judged good or bad.  ' His shirt seems very common compared to their modern fashions.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the quality of the Evaluee is being judged.

name: Comparison_set
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate what class of things or events the Evaluee is being judged against.  ' His shirt seems very common compared to their modern fashions.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Frame Element Depictive encodes a state that the Evaluee is in and which does not represent a temporary or hypothetical set of Circumstances.   ' His shirt seems very common with its generic logo.'

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the Social_event is ongoing.

name: Social_event
definition_en: This FE identifies the Social_event itself.  'The department picnic was lots of fun.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the Social_event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Social_event occurs.

name: Host
definition_en: The Host is the person or organization that hosts the Social_event.  In cases where an individual stands in for an organization, the host may be marked twice.  'Ron threw a party.' 'President Reagan hosted a state banquet.' The FE Host is also used in ambiguous cases, such as: 'church picnic.'

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The person for whom the Social_event is held.  'I threw a party for Josef.'

name: Occasion
definition_en: The Occasion for which the Social_event is held.

name: Attendee
definition_en: Attendee is used for the people who come to the Social_event.  'The whole group attended the party.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Social_event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Social_event occurs.

name: Refreshment
definition_en: Refreshment is used for the meal, food or drinks that are served at the Social_event.  'I enjoy a tasteful dinner party.' 'I attended a cocktail party and drank myself silly.' 'First layer: I attended a banquet on Saturday. ' 'Second layer: I attended a banquet on Saturday. '

name: Style
definition_en: This FE identifies the Style of  the Social_event and its level of formality, indicating appropriate dress for participants and/or  the kind of activities in which they engage.  'Lee hosted a formal party.' 'Abby's garden party was successful.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: COD: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the social_event.

name: Name
definition_en: The Name of the Social_event.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE describes how often the Social_event occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason the Social_event is being held.  'We threw a banquet to raise awareness to our cause.'

name: Attendees
definition_en: The Attendees are the collectively construed participants of the social event.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the social event occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the social event is ongoing.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the social event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the social event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the social event occurs.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with Particular_iteration modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Party_1
definition_en: Party_1 is the grammatically more prominent participant in the social event.  Party_1 can be one or more individuals.

name: Party_2
definition_en: Party_2 is the grammatically less prominent participant in the social event.  Party_2 can be one or more individuals.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the social event occurs.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of time for which the social event is ongoing.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the social event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the social event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the social event occurs.

name: Evaluee
definition_en: The Evaluee is the person whose Behavior towards other human beings is being evaluated.

name: Affected_party
definition_en: The Affected_party is the entity which is positively or negatively treated by the Evaluee.

name: Behavior
definition_en: The Behavior is the action of the Evaluee on which the evaluation of the Evaluee's character is based.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree is the extent to which the Evaluee exhibits the particular Behavior towards others.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the situation or person that the Evaluee's Behavior responds to or is related to.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part which indicates the character of the Evaluee.  'She flashed me a kind smile.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the way in which the Evaluee embodies the characteristic ascribed to her or him.  '<fex name = "Evaluee">Lester was <fex name = "Manner">coldly polite.'

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the evaluation denoted by the target.  'In my book, that wasn't very gracious.'

name: Event
definition_en: This FE identifies the event which occurs to create history.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies where the event takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the event occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain is (a characterization of) the type of event that is part of the Event's history.

name: Item
definition_en: An Item is alone in its category.

name: Type
definition_en: Type specifies a category which in principle could apply to multiple items, but which is limited to the Item.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which the sound level Attribute is under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is under consideration. This FE is incorporated in each LU in the frame.

name: Volume
definition_en: A quantity or characterization of the Entity's sound output with repspect to its Attribute.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing the deviation of the Volume from the norm.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Volume for the Attribute.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having  a particular Volume for the Attribute.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where an Entity is located.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Sound
definition_en: A percept produced  in hearing organs by  vibrations which travel through the air or another medium.  'Laughter echoed through the halls'

name: Location_of_sound_source
definition_en: The location of the Sound_source from which the Sound travels  'The Prince 's laugh echoed from the corridor.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path of the Sound's movement is any description of its trajectory of motion which is neither a Location_of_sound_source or a Goal.  'A loud bang echoed through the valley.'

name: Place
definition_en: A setting in which Sound movement happens.  'I heard their footsteps echo in the hollow cavern.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when  the Sound movement occurs.  ' In the mornings the harsh , squawking voices of the gulls echo between the channel walls'

name: Sound_source
definition_en: The point-like entity which produces the Sound.  'There was muzak echoing from cheap speakers.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Sound moves.  'The scream reverberated around the house like the scream of a soul in pain'

name: Goal
definition_en: A description of the location where the Sound ends up.

name: Noisy_event
definition_en: An event during which sound is produced.

name: Sound_source
definition_en: An entity that is construed as a single point source emitting sound.  'He woke up because of the blare of a car horn.'

name: Theme
definition_en: One of  two entities which is construed as moving relative to the other, resulting in either friction or impact. This entity is given greater syntactic prominence--it is either a possessor or an of-complement of the noun phrase head.  'He heard the clang of metal on metal , and a ricochet whined viciously past his head '

name: Ground
definition_en: An entity construed as stationary on or against which the Theme moves, resulting in either friction or impact. This entity is given less grammatical prominence compared to the Theme and is usually encoded in a spatial prepositional phrase.  'He heard the clang of metal on metal , and a ricochet whined viciously past his head .'

name: Themes
definition_en: Two entities that are both moving against each other, resulting in either friction or impact.  'The sound of voices and the clink of glasses was like music to her ears '

name: Location_of_sound_source
definition_en: The place from which the sound emanates.  'There followed a small silence that was interrupted by a distant clatterof metal from the ward.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which sound is produced. This FE differs from Location_of_sound_source in that it does not highlight the sound's spreading from its source to the perceiver's location, which is usually indicated by the preposition "from".  'There was a clatter of running feet in the street outside.'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The noise-making may be prompted by either some outside phenomenon or occurrence, or by an Internal_cause,  that is the mental or emotional state of an animate Sound_source.  'She checked a giggle of hysteria'

name: Manner
definition_en: Certain properties of the sound relating to its production, loudness, etc  may be of lexicographic interest if they describe properties of a sounds as such: loudly, shrilly, etc.  'The Brigadier had heard the faint tinkle of sheepbells'

name: Component_sound
definition_en: The sound percept may be characterized in terms of Component_sounds.  'The lunch itself was held in a huge room and there was a constant babble of noise'

name: Degree
definition_en: Expressions that indicate the loudness of the sound.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE idntifies the Explanation that the Sound_source produces the sound. Generally, this is some external stimulus that prompts the Sound_source to make noise.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path along which the sound travels away from the Sound_source.  'As he opened the throttle, the roar of the BMW's engine bit into the moan and  howl of the wind  across the culvert's mouth'

name: Theme
definition_en: The abstact or concrete thing acquired by the Goal from the Source.  'The sun doesn't burn up because its source of power is nuclear energy.'

name: Source
definition_en: A concrete or abstract entity from which the Goal has gotten the Theme.  'Dr Kelly is his source for the specific information relating to phlogiston production.'

name: Goal
definition_en: An entity or individual that has acquired a Theme from the Source.   'The beetles thereby cut off the tree's source of nourishment and it dies.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any evaluative or descriptive characterization of the Source, pertaining either to temporary or permanent properties.    'In fact , the amount of electricity produced by renewable sources in the UK has steadily declined over the past five years.'

name: Trajector
definition_en: The entity that moves (or is conceived of as moving) from the Source, along the Path to the Goal.

name: Source
definition_en: A description of the initial location of the Trajector, before a motion event begins.

name: Path
definition_en: A description of the intermediate position of the Trajector, after departing the Source and before arriving at the Goal.

name: Goal
definition_en: A description of the location that the Trajector ends up.

name: Means
definition_en: The action or state-of-affairs that causes the Trajector to change location.

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure.

name: Figure
definition_en: The Figure is perceived as located relative to a certain Ground location. The Figure can be an entity or an event.

name: Accessibility
definition_en: An indication of how accessible the Figure is to some participant in the speech context (either the speaker or the addressee, or some other highly salient viewpoint in a narrative).  This FE normally describes availability for manipulation and use, but may simply describe how easily seen or difficult to see the Figure is. There is a closed class of items that can fill this slot, including only 'right' indicating ease of access, and 'way', 'all the way', or (dialectally) 'clear' indicating distance and difficulty of access.    'It's the door all the way at the back of the room.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure.  This FE is filled by one of a closed class of adverbs:  up, down, out (meaning 'beyond the boundary around the viewpoint'), off (meaning 'disconnect between landmark and figure'), back (meaning 'along a line from front to back of landmark, and relatively inaccessible'), and, more rarely, away, along, and dialectally, back down (meaning 'down and behind').  'The dog was waiting up at the top of the hill.'

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the locative relation between Figure and Ground obtains.  'He was at my shop on Friday.'

name: Deixis
definition_en: An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder), or specifically separated from the speech context by distance or a barrier (over). Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.   'She stood there at the fountain .'

name: Directness
definition_en: An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target.  This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, directly, and due (and some combinations of these), but also occurs with rarer items like 'smack dab'.  'I was sitting right at the edge of the chair .'

name: Temporal_profile
definition_en: A description of how the access path to the Ground interacts with time.  This FE is filled only by the closed class of adverbials back.adv (which indicates that the position was occupied by the Figure before) and on.adv (which indicates a continued path).  While this FE in its most basic use refers to cases of actual motion, it can be used with descriptions of static position, in which case it either refers to fictive, imagined motion (as in the first example below), or it backgrounds motion entirely (as in the second example).  'You 'll find it straight on over there.' 'He's already back at the house.'

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground serves as a basis for describing the location of the Figure.  'The cat is on the mat.'

name: Figure
definition_en: The Figure is perceived as located relative to a certain Ground location. The figure can be an entity or an event.  'The cat is on the mat.'

name: Accessibility
definition_en: An indication of how accessible the Figure is to some participant in the speech context (either the speaker or the addressee, or some other highly salient viewpoint in a narrative).  This FE normally describes availability for manipulation and use, but may simply describe how easily seen or difficult to see the Figure is. There is a closed class of items that can fill this slot, including only 'right' indicating ease of access, and 'way', 'all the way', or (dialectally) 'clear' indicating distance and difficulty of access.   'My bag sat right on the table.'

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure.  This FE is filled by one of a closed class of adverbs:  up, down, out (meaning 'beyond the boundary around the viewpoint'), back (meaning 'along a line from front to back of landmark, and relatively inaccessible'), and, more rarely, away, along, and dialectally, back down (meaning 'down and behind').  'The cat is up on top of the table .'

name: Time
definition_en: The period of time during which the locative relation between Figure and Ground obtains.  'He was against the wall on Friday.'

name: Figures
definition_en: The Figures are items which mutually serve to identify the location of each other.

name: Deixis
definition_en: An indication of how the locative phrase relates to the grounding of the speech situation, either locating it near (here) or far (there, yonder), or specifically separated from the speech context by distance or a barrier (over).  Fillers of this FE are restricted to this closed class of items.  'It is lying here on my desk .'

name: Directness
definition_en: An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target.  This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, directly, and due (and some combinations of these), but also occurs with rarer items like 'smack dab'.  'I stood right on the edge .'

name: Temporal_profile
definition_en: A description of how the access path to the Ground interacts with time.  This FE is filled only by the closed class adverbial back.adv (which indicates that the position was occupied by the Figure before). While this FE in its most basic use refers to cases of actual motion, it can be used with descriptions of static position, where motion is backgrounded.   'Put the book back upon the shelf.'

name: Audience
definition_en: The person or persons to whom the Speaker delivers their text.  'He lectured to the officers of the Scots Guard  in  1929.'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The person who orally delivers a text about a Topic to a passive Audience.  'You have to sermonize about the good times'

name: Topic
definition_en: What the text that the Speaker produces is about.  'He was the Director: he could lecture on whomever he liked.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is a description of the Speaker's speech.

name: Medium
definition_en: This frame element is the Medium through which the Speaker communicates.

name: Occasion
definition_en: The Occasion is the reason a public statement is given. 'The New Year address was well received.' 'Professor Frinkgave the Macarthur lecture in 1978.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time describes when the speaking occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place describes the location where the speaking occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: Denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically followes. This often means that the Explanation causes the complaint, but not in all cases. In particular, there are cases when the connection is a bit weaker than normal for causation. In these instances,  cause is mediated by some actor responding in a complex way to the situation. Such cases are not paraphrasable in the language of direct causation.

name: Type
definition_en: The class of items within which the Instance is made salient.

name: Instance
definition_en: The notable case of the Type.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity whose Speed is under consideration.

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is a function of the distance that the Entity moves in a given duration. With the adjectives of this frame this Frame Element is generally incorporated.

name: Speed
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's speed.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Speed from the norm.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having  a particular Speed.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Speed.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason why the Entity or Attribute is ata certain speed.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The language user who produces a Sign in some modality.  'He insists on mispronouncing my name every time, the bastard!'

name: Sign
definition_en: An abstract form-meaning pairing.  'My little nephew can't say prestidigitation'

name: Judgment
definition_en: An evaluation of whether the Formal_realization that the Speaker produced matches the standard or standard range.   'Finally, I would pay more attention to your "oppinion" if you spelled it correctly.'

name: Formal_realization
definition_en: The written string, gesture, or vocalized sound sequence that the Speaker produces.  'The old uncensored editions of the Talmud referred to Jesus as Yeshua censored versions spelled it as Yeshu '

name: Part_of_form
definition_en: A constituent part of the Formal_realization.   'You spelled it with a "t".'

name: Manner
definition_en: The way that the Speaker produces the Formal_realization.  'You spelled it the way it sounds.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the Speaker produces the Formal_realization.  'Today you spelled it "pjuok". '

name: Textual_location
definition_en: The context wherein the Speaker produces a particular Formal_realization.  'On page 1223, you spelled her name wrong. '

name: Addressee
definition_en: The person that the Speaker is producing the Formal_realization for.  'So I asked the ladies down in the kitchen if they could maybe pronounce your name for me.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: Denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically followes.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The amount of times the Sign is spelled or pronounced per some unit of time.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE marks any state that the Speaker is in while spelling or pronouncing.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Competition
definition_en: This FE is used for the name of the competition.

name: Agent
definition_en: This FE is used for plural NP participants in a competition.

name: Entity
definition_en: The object that has reached a particular stage of its development.  'We offer advice for very advanced learners of English on the different EFL/ESL exams.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the progress occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of the stage of progress, frequently an evaluation.  'The new version is wonderfully advanced.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount of advancement that the Entity has attained.  ' The province, which is very developed economically, is at the same time a center of brassworking.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant dimension of development.  ' The Soviet Union was more highly developed militarily than China.'

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The sentient being who delays action until an Expected_request has been received.  'He was on call every night this week.'

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: A concrete or abstract entity that the Protagonist expects to participate in an Expected_request, typically the party that makes the request of the Protagonist.  'Riot officers are standing by for protesters.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Protagonist is waiting for the request.  'At least 17 ships were standing by yesterday to commence the attack.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which the Protagonist is waiting.  'Guards are standing by outside the State Guesthouse for new orders.'

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of the waiting to its end.  'She was on standby for three hours last night, but no one showed up.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the waiting event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of the Protagonist that also affect the action (patiently, anxiously).  'Troops were silently standing by for the order to arrive.'

name: Expected_request
definition_en: The Expected_request is what triggers the Protagonist to proceed with an appropriate action.  'She did n't stand by for them to supply her with orders; she just rushed right in.'

name: End_point
definition_en: The point in time, defined either as a clock time or in terms of an event that takes place, at which the Protagonist ends the waiting.   ' I'll be on call until 4am.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the occurrence of the waiting event logically follows.  'Senior employees are on call over the weekend because it was discovered that it was difficult, if not disasterous, to rely entirely on new hires.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes the Protagonist as being in some state during the waiting.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Protagonist intends to accomplish by standing by.  'Our experienced technitions are standing by to assist you in order to get you back up and running as soon as possible.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the waiting event with the Protagonist.  'I was on call with several other doctors so at least it wasn't too boring.'

name: Activity
definition_en: The Protagonist is prepared to conduct an Activity in response to the Expected_request.  'We're on call to answer all of your questions.'

name: Entity
definition_en: Concrete or abstract entity

name: State
definition_en: State of an Entity.

name: Entity
definition_en: A concrete or abstract Entity.

name: State
definition_en: The State of an Entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the State is found to still persist.  'Financial recovery remains elusive in 2002.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Entity is in the State.   'Martial law remains in effect in Absurdistan.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The state of affairs that explains why the State persists.  'Simandle ruled that the contract remains in force because the GTMUA accepted $400,000 in connection fees from the trust.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The time period over which the State continues to hold of the Entity.  'Our commitment to high-quality, distinctively Canadian programming has remained constant for more than six decades.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the State continues.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Entity
definition_en: The entity whose State is specified and/or evaluated.  'It was stressed that no diagnosis of my state of health would be made, so all she was doing was describing how she felt my 'aura' to be. '

name: Evaluation
definition_en: An assessment or characterization of the Entity's State.  'I read a lot about the sorry state of music and agree that it is often hard to find good music.'

name: State
definition_en: A relation in which the Entity participates or a property that the Entity possesses.   'Despite being in a state of considerable disrepair, the building is surprisingly roomy inside and has a pleasant feel to it. '

name: Parameter
definition_en: A subpart or characteristic of the Entity that is in a specified State.  'Our state of mind can be the most determining factor in the achievement of our goals.'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the sentient entity that produces the Message (whether spoken or written).  It is normally expressed as the External Argument of predicative uses of the target	 word, or as the Genitive modifier of the noun. 'Evelyn spoke feelingly about what happened.' 'Evelyn made a persuasive statement.' 'Evelyn's statement was quite persuasive.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee is the person to whom the Message is communicated. When this FE is expressed, it often appears in a prepositional phrase introduced by "to", or as a direct object. 'Evelyn reported to me about what happened.' 'Evelyn spoke to me about what happened.'

name: Message
definition_en: The Message is the FE that identifies the content of what the Speaker is communicating to the Addressee.  It can be expressed as a clause or as a noun phrase. 'Evelyn said that she was not ready to leave.' 'Evelyn explained that she had seen him before.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the subject matter to which the Message pertains. It is normally expressed as a PP Complement headed by "about", but in some cases it can appear as a direct object. 'Evelyn spoke candidly about her past.' 'The teacher mentioned the recent campus incidents.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner of performing an action.

name: Means
definition_en: An act whereby the Speaker makes a Message. 'Bilio commented on the paper by scrawling innumerable post-its in a range of colors and sticking them all over it.'

name: Internal_cause
definition_en: The emotional or physical state of the Speaker that leads to their speaking. 'He wrote in bitterness of the treatment the Malloreans had given him.'

name: Medium
definition_en: Medium is the physical entity or channel used by the Speaker to transmit the statement. 'Kim preached to me over the phone.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Speaker during the Message. 'Let's see if you say that sober!'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Message is made.

name: Place
definition_en: The FE specifies the location where the Message takes place. 'In some remarks at the National Press Club, Mr. Keating said he would make a better prime minister tha nMr. Hawke.'

name: Occasion
definition_en: The Occasion is the reason a public Message is given. 'The New Year address was well received.'

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE indicate that the particular Message event referred to is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. Most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.  'A further biography Shadowland by William Arnold, published in 1978, asserted for the first time that Farmer had been the subject of a transorbital lobotomy'

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the Message is expressed (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Group
definition_en: The Group of Speakers or Mediums within which the Message is made.   'Much would be achieved if these were more widely acknowledged.'

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE describes the Message event.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The FE Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE identifies an event during which the Speaker produces the Message.

name: Stimulus
definition_en: The Stimulus is the object or event which brings about the emotion in the Experiencer.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer experiences the emotion brought about by the Stimulus

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which the Stimulus evokes the emotion in the Experiencer

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate a set of conditions under which the Stimulus is able to bring about the emotion.  ' When sunny the view is impressive. '

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is the area in which the Stimulus brings about an effect on the Experiencer.  ' This art work is aesthetically pleasing.'  'The book is emotionally disturbing. '

name: Comparison_set
definition_en: The Comparison_set is the set of individuals the Stimulus is compared to when determining the Degree of the emotional reaction. 'Randy is very stimulating for a curator. '

name: Property
definition_en: This FE indicates a Property of the Stimulus which causes a particular experience. 'The movie is terrifying in its realism' 'The movie is terrifying in its use of violence' 'The move was disappointing in every respect . '

name: Resource_controller
definition_en: The Resource_Controller is the individual who controls access to the Resource. 'Stampy was stingy with his peanuts.'

name: Resource
definition_en: The Resource_controller controls the Recipient's access to the Resource. 'Surprising, Dad was stingy with his inheritance.' 'Dragons often hoard gold.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: The Recipient is the individual or individuals who receive or should receive the Resource from the Resource_controller. 'Mr. Burns is extremely miserly towards his employees.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree is how generous or stingy the Resource_controller is judged to be. 'John is very generous.'

name: Behavior
definition_en: The Behavior is an action of the Resource_controller which is judged to be generous or stingy. 'It was generous of Jim to have us over for dinner.' 'Jim's dinner invitation was very generous.'

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The Expressor is the body part or action by a body part which indicates the character of the Resource_controller.

name: Manner
definition_en: A characterization of the way in which the Resource_controller exhibits stinginess.  'She was always sensitively generous to me.'

name: Supply
definition_en: This FE denotes the Supply of Resources. It is incorporated into each LU in this frame.

name: Resource
definition_en: The goods or commodity that is being stored in a Supply.  ' India has made great strides in agriculture and now not only meets it own grain needs but has a sizeable reserve of basic grains, mainly rice and wheat.'

name: Use
definition_en: The future Use for the Resource.  'Due to restrictions imposed by our export control, the Japanese have begun to use a portion of their war reserve of petroleum.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: The entity that possesses the Supply.  'In 1997, France's stock of unirradiated civil plutonium increased to 72 tons.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Supply itself, rather than the Resource.  'Institutions have focused on Broward County?s dwindling supply of land, continued population growth and elevated income levels.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person who has placed the Theme in the Location.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the object that is kept in a Location by the Agent

name: Location
definition_en: The location where the Theme is kept. Some, though not all, LUs in this frame incorporate this FE.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the storing state which is not covered by more specific FEs, including general descriptions comparing events (the same way) and salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (deliberately, carefully).

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE identifies any Depictive phrase describing the Agent or Theme of the storing event.

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration is the amount of time for which the Theme remains in the Location.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place indicates where the Storing occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the storing event logically follows.

name: Time
definition_en: Time is the time period during which the Theme is stored.

name: Area
definition_en: The Area is the setting into which a mass Theme is placed.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the storing event either as a co-agent or a co-theme.

name: Purpose
definition_en: An action that the Agent intends to accomplish by perform the storing action.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the person who is strict or liberal in his/her control over another. This FE is usually the External Argument with predicate adjectives, or the head noun if the adjective is used attributively: The school is very liberal in approach and curriculum. I attended a very liberal school.

name: Controlled_entity
definition_en: The Agent's strictness may be directed towards or limited to some particular person or group over whom he/she has control.  The Controlled_entity generally occurs in a PP Complement. Grandparents are often indulgent with their grandchildren.

name: Controlling_act
definition_en: The Agent's strictness may be manifested in particular behavior: The judge was lenient in dealing with the offender.

name: Issue
definition_en: The Agent may be strict or lenient with respect to a particular matter or situation.  Issue occurs in PP Complements, usually headed by about: The city council is strict about pollution control.

name: Medium
definition_en: A Medium of control, such as rules, may also be described as strict or lenient.  Medium may occur with or without the Agent who ultimately has control (i.e. the one who implements or enforces the rules). The club has strict rules about who can become a member. Immigration law is very strict.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Area
definition_en: The Area is the arena in which the Agent is or is not strict.

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment denoted by the target.

name: Expressor
definition_en: The body part or expression of the Agent that indicates their strictness.  'I like to think he quaked under my authoritarian glare.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the way in which the Agent embodies the strictness associated with him or her.  'These could perhaps be tied to the sometimes cruelly authoritarian structures of the peasant household.'

name: Teacher
definition_en: One who instructs a Student in some area of knowledge or skill.  'She studied from him for years.'

name: Student
definition_en: One who receives instruction from a Teacher or Institution.

name: Institution
definition_en: An educational establishment, such as a school or college.

name: Subject
definition_en: The area of knowledge or skill which is taught  to a Student.  'She studies astrophysics.'

name: Level
definition_en: This FE identifies the Level of a <fen name="Student">student in his/her education.  'a graduate student' 'a fourth grade student'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A state which describes the Student during the process of study.

name: Manner
definition_en: The manner of studying that the Student has.

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the student is studying.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location within which the studying takes place.  NOTE: Consider whether a possible Place phrase is really where the training took place or is rather part of a description of the Institution.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time for which the process of study is ongoing.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Student studies the Subject.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: Co_participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the Studying event.

name: Intended_academic_credit
definition_en: The Student's motivation for studying.    'He is studying for his Master's .'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The person that the Speaker seeks to influence to act.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The person who intends through the use of language to get another person to act.

name: Content
definition_en: The wish for action on the Addressee's part that the Speaker expresses.

name: Text
definition_en: A piece of written or spoken material that changes the mind of the Addressee. 'His speech convinced me to join the Peace Corps.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The general item or items that are the focus of the Content of the Speaker's message. 'You haven't convinced me about that yet.'

name: Means
definition_en: An act of the Speaker that accomplishes the persuasion. 'I persuaded the committee by giving each member a grand.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Speaker suades the Addressee.  'The car salesman expertly persuaded the customer to spend more than he could afford.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the Speaker suades the Addressee.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Speaker suades the Addressee.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The person who is influenced by the Situation or Entity.   'George Gilder would run with this idea later in writing the New Testament of supply-side economics that influenced Reagan. '

name: Situation
definition_en: A state of affairs--- which can be an event, state or conditions---that has an influence on the Cognizer.   'The balmy temperatures inspired me to write a poem on the advent of spring.' 'Hecker said that although the sheer age of the building inspired him to preserve its heritage aspects he also designed its interiors around the ·clean and fresh· mood of Queensland.'

name: Entity
definition_en: A person or thing that has an influence on the Cognizer.  'The painting inspired me to take a risk and use the intense green for the sky.'

name: Action
definition_en: An Action that the Cognizer decides to carry out as a consequence of the influence of a Situation or Entity.   'What factors influenced Nixon to issue the doctrine?'

name: Behavior
definition_en: A Behavior that the Cognizer is engaged in independently but whose execution is subsequently influenced by the Situation or Entity.  'Attention will also be paid to St. Paul , what influenced him in his thinking and what he wrote in his letters about sex, sexuality, men and women'

name: Product
definition_en: An entity that stands metonymically for the actions and considerations that produced it.  'Does anyone know what inspired this song? '

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Subjective_influencing event occurs.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE applies to appraisals of the Subjective_influence event.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent acts to influence a Cognizer.

name: Place
definition_en: The location in which one has influence.  'Chavez has much influence in South America.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The field in which one maintains influence.  'Chavez has much influence in South American politics.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This is typically an adjective describing a nominal target.

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The entity which perceives a level of warmth.

name: Degree
definition_en: How much the actual feeling of temperature deviates from a certain level of warmth.

name: Body_part
definition_en: A part of the body of the Experiencer in which the sensation of a temperature is located.  'My hands are freezing.'

name: Submittor
definition_en: The person that begins in possession of the Documents and gives them over into the possession of the Authority for processing.  'The Human Services financial worker cannot decide if you will get food support benefits until you turn in the form and needed verifications.'

name: Authority
definition_en: The individual or organization that ends up in possession of the Documents and processes them.  'If an application is late, whether you submitted it late to us or it was held up at your Command, NMETC will not be able to fund registration fees.'

name: Documents
definition_en: The artifacts containing content, typically in the form of text and images, that the Submittor gives to the Authority.  'Once you have submitted the form, a request to make an oral statement will be generated based on the information you supplied.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Submittor gives the Documents to the Authority.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which event of the Submittor's giving the Documents to the Authority logically follows.  'Two of the establishments submitted the application because they were producing a new product.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Submittor gives the Documents to the Authority.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Submittor gives the Documents to the Authority.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Submittor gives the Documents to the Authority.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the manner in which the Submittor gives the Documents to the Authority.  'The company hastily submitted the manuscript to three additional reviewers.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The Authority's intended purpose for the Documents.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: This extra-thematic FE applies to participants that derive a benefit from the occurrence of the event specified by the target predicate. Further, the target predicate should involve some sort of agent that intends that the benefit go to the Beneficiary.

name: Superior
definition_en: The individual in charge of the Subordinate.

name: Subordinate
definition_en: The individual under the command of the Superior.

name: Entity
definition_en: The living organism which requires the Support to survive.  'He lived on peanuts until she came along.'

name: Support
definition_en: The resource that the Entity relies on to survive through a situation.  'Harry managed to subsist on ramen and cheap beer through college.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time that the Entity survives with the help of the Support.  'John lived on whatever he could find in dumpsters for three years.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree to which the Support is responsible for the survival of the Entity.  'She was barely subsisting on the allowance her parents sent her every month.'

name: Constituents
definition_en: The frame element expresses substances/ingredients that make up the Substance.  'Argon gas is added into the station's air mixture.'

name: Substance
definition_en: The undifferentiated entity which is presented as having a permanent existence.   'Liquid flowed over the rocks but it was not water.'

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype of the general category the Substance belongs to.  'Greenhouse gases trap heat and prevent its escape from the atmosphere.'

name: Origin
definition_en: The location that the Substance comes from, including both extraction sites and emission/production sources.   'It retrieves most of the expensively generated heat from flue gases and puts this heat back into the system.' ' The transport of Iraqi petroleum and petroleum products through the  Kirkuk- Yumurtalik pipeline in Turkey is authorized by paragraph 1 a.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Substance.  'The new Chrysler minivans will run on compressed natural gas.'

name: Inherent_purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Substance is intended.  'Supply and placing of filler sand shall be incidental to installation of the paving stones.'

name: Substance
definition_en: The Substance is the entity which has had its phase altered.

name: Subregion
definition_en: The part of the Patient that is in an altered state. 'The turkey was only defrosted on the top.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event or state_of_Affairs that successfully impedes an Agent or a State_of_affairs.  'This failure undermines governmental authority'

name: Counter_actor
definition_en: A person who intentionally or not acts in such a way that an Agent or State_of_affairs is impeded.  'Tory rebels queued to warn that they wouldsabotage efforts to put the treaty through Parliament .'

name: Agent
definition_en: A person who is intentionally engaged in some Activity and who is impeded in that Activity.  'If he is really undermining me, then he is a fine friend.'

name: Activity
definition_en: An Activity that is being impeded.  'The Dominican Republic was widely held to have undermined its own efforts to become a full member of CARICOM'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: A state or event that is ongoing and whose continuance or unfolding is impeded.   'Whenever I try to quit they all try to sabotage my efforts.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Cause or Counter_actor impede the Agent or the State_of_affairs.  'The so-called advantage of a Premier being able to determine an election date is totally undermined by speculation surrounding the date for the next election.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Counter_actor hopes will result from his undermining.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Counter_actor subverts an Activity.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Counter_actor or Cause works agains the Agent.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Counter_actor that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE denotes the number of times the Counter_actor or Cause subverts the Agent per unit of time.

name: Iterations
definition_en: This FE denotes the number of times the subversion event has occurred.

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Counter_actor or an event related to the Cause that enables the subversion.  'They sabotaged our plans by cutting off communications between the island and the mainland.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent makes an attempt to achieve a Goal. 'John managed a feeble smile.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is what the Agent attempts to achieve.  'If you don't succeed in your subterfuge, then report back for further orders.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which the Goal is achieved (or not).

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an attempt occurs.  'Your attempt at convincing me has utterly failed.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt succeeds or fails.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the Agent.

name: Place
definition_en: The place where an attempt succeeds or fails.  'On the bridge he succeeded in putting the wig on the corpse.'

name: Role
definition_en: A participant function in a particular event or in events of a particular kind.  'Benedikt was successful as a master brewer of beer.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE is applied to expressions which indicate the prevailing physical conditions for the event, or some concurrent states of affairs.  'And could anybody have succeeded under those conditions, using other methods?'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or  failure, but not in all cases.   ' Kerry failed because of his inability to tell his own story.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE identifies an event during which the Agent attempts to achieve a Goal.   'He was successful in the Smithers v Burns case. '

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: Re-encoding presents the success or failure event as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

name: Means
