definition_en: The action that the agent undertakes to achieve the Goal.  'His daring, almost reckless, move succeeded and he lived to fight another day.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is what the agent attempts to achieve by performing the Means action.  'This move succeeded in securing trade concessions and the release of imprisoned American sailors.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the agent as part of the Means action in order to accomplish the Goal.  ' All of my usual source books seemed incomplete, but your website did the trick!'

name: Place
definition_en: The place where Means action succeeds or fails.  'A similar strategy, perhaps even bloodier, did the trick in El Salvador.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the attempt succeeds or fails  ' But it did the trick at the time.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The FE Circumstances encodes a setting, often temporal or spatial, within which the successful action expressed by the target takes place.  'The installation failed under FreeBSD 5.2.1.'

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist is the deprofiled individual who makes an attempt to achieve a Goal by performing the Means action, which may involve using an Instrument.  'Download also failed for me on both March and May issues. '

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which an attempt involving a particular Means or Instrument succeeds.  ' A 1000 pf cap almost completely did the trick so I went bigger with what happened to be handy'

name: Role
definition_en: A participant function of an Instrument or Means in a particular event or in events of a particular kind.  'The machine was successful as a reconnaissance vehicle.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the success or failure logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the success or  failure, but not in all cases.   ' The attempt failed because of John's repeated interference..'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event or state of affairs that occurs or holds at a time that includes the time during which the success or failure reported by the target occurs and of which the success or failure is taken to be a part  'This argument succeeded in Waltons-Morse v Dorrington where a non-smoking secretary claimed she was forced to work in a smoke-filled office. '

name: Communicator
definition_en: The person who uses language in the written or spoken modality to convey a Message to another person.   'Nobody seems to be able to get the idea through to her that she needs a job!!!!'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee receives a Message from the Communicator.     'According to Masztalics, a good teacher uses experiments to get the point across to the class.'

name: Message
definition_en: Message A proposition or set of propositions that the Communicator wants the Addressee to believe or take for granted.    'He tried to get through to his wife that the debt he's taken on buying stocks poses no risk.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The physical or abstract setting in which the Message is conveyed.   'The article conveys Mr. Handley's disrespect for those who disagree with him.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive describes the state of the Communicator.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Communicator communicates.  'Rais carefully conveys his own personal faith journey while respecting those who may have distinctly different views or experiences.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Communicator communicates.  'She finally got her point across by miming a shark's fin with her hands over her head. '

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the communication takes place.  'Greenspan got his point across yesterday that a measured pace of rate hikes is still the plan.'

name: Adequacy
definition_en: The degree to which the Communicator's efforts are effective at making the Addressee understand and appreciate the Message.  'The ads clearly got across the need to respect the health of non-smokers.'

name: Item
definition_en: The entity whose scalar property is specified.'The light is probably bright enough.''I have sufficient paper for the purpose.'

name: Scale
definition_en: The Scale is the attribute of the Item that is being described.'It was hot enough to ignite the iron.''The workforce is sufficient in number and proficiency to finish the building in minimum time.'</def-root >

name: Enabled_situation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Enabled_situation by which the critical value is judged. 'Can He make a rock too heavy for Him to lift?' 'There's almost enough for thirty people.' 'That information sufficed to convince me.' 'Finding a parking spot is sufficiently difficult that you'd do better to walk.' 'This legislation was inadequate in that it allowed many obvious delinquents to escape prosecution.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree frame element indicates a modification of the value indicated by the target.'The spell was almost powerful enough to destroy the demonic pumpkin.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Victim
definition_en: This Victim is the being or entity that is injured by the Assailant's suicide attack.  'Her suicide attack on the guardsmen was the third such attack in the last month.'

name: Weapon
definition_en: An entity used by the Assailant to cause damage to the Victim.  'The suicide attack with a car killed over a dozen people.'

name: Assailant
definition_en: The person (or other self-directed entity) that is attempting physical harm to the Victim.  'The group's suicide attacks continue to affect troop morale.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Assailant that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Assailant that accomplishes the assault.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Assailant makes an assault on the Victim.  'Last week's suicide bombing outside the city was the first in weeks.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Assailant attacks the Victim.  'They continue to suicide-attack throughout the city to intimidate and terrorize the population.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Assailant attacks the Victim.  'Last Tuesday's suicide attack killed seven and wounded 20.'

name: Source
definition_en: The starting-point of the motion of the Assailant or projectiles of the Assailant as they move toward the the Place that the Victim is occupying in the attack.  In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion.  With particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE is used for any Depictive phrase describeing the state of the Assailant or Victim while the Attack occurs.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action within the frame expressed by the Re-encoding, but not necessarily.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the attack on the Victim by the Assailant.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Path
definition_en: The Path refers to (a part of) the ground over which the Assailant travels.

name: Evaluee
definition_en: This Frame Element marks constituents expressing the entity that is judged to be more or less suitable for some Purpose or User.  'Being a project leader is not a job for which everybody is suited.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This Frame Element marks constituents that express the Degree to which the Evaluee is suitable for the Context.  'Please advise on the most suitable design '

name: Purpose
definition_en: This Frame Element marks constituents that express the Purpose for which the Evaluee is judged to be suitable or unsuitable.  'We need to plan more buildings suitable for disabled people.'

name: User
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate a User to whom

name: Communicator
definition_en: The Communicator creates and communicates the summary of the Information.

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Communicator communicates the summary to the Addressee.

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The State_of_affairs is summarized by the Communicator.

name: Medium
definition_en: The textual or other Medium through which the Communicator summarizes.

name: Summary
definition_en: The content that results from the summarization.  'She summarized our involvement as a "qualified success".' 'Aston boiledthe situation down to one word: FUBAR.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Communicator makes the Summary.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Communicator communicates.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the details of the action beyond the identity of the participants and the setting, especially descriptions of the Communicator that affect the action.

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Communicator that brings about the communication.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Communicator is attempting to bring about by communicating.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time taken by the Communicator in creating and conveying the Summary.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Supplier
definition_en: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.  'I approve of your having supplied him with a file of soldiers.'

name: Recipient
definition_en: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.  'VESID also supplied him with an all zone bus pass to help him travel to interviews.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The object that is given to the Recipient .   'Cromwell merged men from multiple regiments into a single one and provisioned them with red uniforms to replace their former regiment colors. '

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.  'The Harpley was launched in Launceston on the 2nd February, 1847, and with the exception of her chain cables, was there supplied with all her materials and stores.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.  'Jesus equipped them because if they tried to do it in their own strength they would have understood defeat in a whole new way.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.  'In Breidbach, water tankers were yesterday supplied to the community as the main water supply pipe had been washed away.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Supplier gives the Theme to the Recipient.  'Some financial support can be provided in order to help you and MPI with the product approval process in an efficient and effective way.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Supplier acquires or gives the Theme to the Recipient.  'Euell provisioned them by foraging, hunting, and trapping whenever his father was away.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the supplying event  which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously),  secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Supplier that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).  ' PandG secretly provided Schwartz with several boxes of documents.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the conditions under which the Theme is supplied.    'I supplied the food free of charge.'

name: Imposed_purpose
definition_en: The Recipient's intended purpose for the Theme.  'God gave them the promise of victory and equipped them for the battle.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The period over which the Supplier engages in (multiple) supplying acts.  'Our company has supplied nations with voting machines since 2000.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: An additional theme which is supplied along with the main Theme.  'Several cables were provided with the printer, but I'm not sure which ones to use.'

name: Source
definition_en: The source of the Theme.  'We equipped them from our own supply of equipment.'

name: Supporter
definition_en: The Supporter acts to benefit the Supported by providing additional strength or stability.

name: Supported
definition_en: The Supported is given strength through the assistance of the Supporter.

name: Degree
definition_en: The measure to which the Supporter's assistance brings the Supported added strength and support.  'The physical therapist must totally support tthe patient during the exercises.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The time period during which the Supporter supports the Supported.  'For some seventy years, this judicial fabrication buttressed racial segregation.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity used by the Supporter in service of the Supported's strength by support.  'The troops used their shoulders to support the doors of the keep, as the enemy forces tried to break through.'  'For years, patrons of the organization have supported our bi-weekly tea-times with their generous donations.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which a Supporter supports the Supported.   'The British Government happily buttressed Saddam's appalling oppression of his people'.

name: Means
definition_en: An action that the Supporter undertakes in service of the Supported's strengthening.  'The foundation supports the building by distributing the load to the ground below.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the support occurs.  'In England, economic incentives are buttressed by closing certain overdoctored areas from new practices.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies when the support occurs.  'Early in the twentieth century, such economic arguments buttressed the creation of a National Park Service.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The situation that the Supporter wishes to bring about by supporting the Supported.   'The porch tower of Saint-Germain-des-Prés is sturdily buttressed to support the weight of its massive bells'.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state-of-affairs from which the accomplishment would be predicted.

name: Event_description
definition_en: A clause describing the event as a whole.

name: Standard_item
definition_en: The FE Standard_item denotes the entities that are exceeded by the Item with regard to the Attribute.  'In her time, she outstripped most politician in the country.'

name: Profiled_item
definition_en: The Profiled_item is the entity that is located closest to the end of the scale evoked by some Attribute.  'The buildings were outstripped in beauty and grace many years ago.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The Attribute is a property that evokes a scale along which the Item is located closer to one extreme in  comparison to the Standard_item.

name: Extent
definition_en: The Extent is the degree to which the Item surpasses the Standard.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Item is higher on the scale than the Standard.

name: Standard_attribute
definition_en: The Standard_attribute is used when the standard is a specific value on  a scale. ' We  surpassed our father's skills . '

name: Profiled_attribute
definition_en: The Profiled_attribute is a particular value on a scale which is being compared to an Attribute or Standard_item.

name: Comparison_set
definition_en: The Comparison_set includes the Standard and is what the Item is judged with respect to.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Fugitive
definition_en: The Fugitive is wanted by the Authorities and turns himself or herself in to the Authorities.

name: Authorities
definition_en: The Authorities are the officials, government or otherwise, who are in charge of initiating the criminal process.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location where the surrendering occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Fugitive surrenders.

name: Charges
definition_en: The Charges is the offense for which the Fugitive is wanted.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Fugitive surrenders to the Authorities.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE denotes a proposition from which the surrendering event logically follows.

name: Surrenderer
definition_en: The person compelled to transfer the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The object that changes possession.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE denotes a proposition from which the surrendering event logically follows.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means by which the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner is the manner in which the Surrenderer gives the Theme to the Recipient.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Surrendering event itself and any of its participants.    'John surrendered the gun with everybody looking on in stunned silence.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE modifies a clause with an iterative interpretation, which may be signified by the simple present tense on the main verb.

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame.

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time during which the event or state of affairs reported by the target occurs and of which it is taken to be a part.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. It is to be distinguished from Iteration, which pertains simply to the number of times an event occurs-Iteration expressions answer the question how many times.

name: Result
definition_en: This FE identifies the Result of an surrendering event.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Figure
definition_en: The Figure is the entity located with respect to the Ground.  'He had both hands wrapped around her arm .'

name: Ground
definition_en: The Ground is the area that the Figure surrounds.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Figure is located around the Ground.

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE identifies the Direction from a reference location (generally, the deictic center) of a path to the Figure.  'Up around the bolt she saw a frayed noose .'

name: Distance
definition_en: This  FE identifies the Distance between the Figure and some reference location (generally, the deictic center or the Ground).  WARNING: Probably not relevant for this frame.

name: Profiled_region
definition_en: The area or zone immediately external to the Ground.  This FE excludes Figure and is only used in particular constructions such as the following:  'We looked around the trees .'

name: Directness
definition_en: An indication of how closely the position of Figure matches the prototype expected from the image schema associated with the target.  This FE is normally filled by closed-class, dedicated adverbs like right, straight, and directly.  'A single membrane directly surrounds the cytoplasm.'

name: Accessibility
definition_en: An indication of how accessible the Figure is to some participant in the speech context (either the speaker or the addressee, or some other highly salient viewpoint in a narrative). This FE normally describes availability for manipulation and use, but may simply describe how easily seen the Figure is. There is a closed class of items that can fill this slot, including only 'just' and 'right' indicating ease of access.   'The skittles lie just around their empty package.'

name: Survivor
definition_en: The Survivor lives through a Dangerous_situation.

name: Dangerous_situation
definition_en: The Dangerous_situation is one in which people are likely or expected to be negatively affected.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Survivor (primarily) lives during the Dangerous_situation.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the surviving takes place.  'Last year, Florida residents survived the devastating triple punch of Hurricanes Frances, Ivan and Jeanne,'

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Survivor that enables them to live throug hthe Dangerous_situation.  'They survived the devastation by using age-old early warning systems.'

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE identifies the Degree to which the Survivor survives.  'Growing up in a rough section of the Bronx, New York, Bobby barely survived several serious bouts of rheumatic fever that left him with a damaged heart.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive is a description of the Survivor, during or after the Dangerous_situation.  'He survived the crash with minor injuries.'

name: Authority
definition_en: The Authority is the group or person who suspects the Suspect of criminal activity.

name: Suspect
definition_en: The Suspect is the target of the Authority's suspicion.

name: Incident
definition_en: The (typically criminal) Incident in which the Suspect is suspected of being involved.

name: Time
definition_en: When the suspecting takes place. 'Jakobson was placed under suspicion last week .' 'At that time, the police suspected no one.'

name: Protagonists
definition_en: All the participants in an event or situation, viewed as symmetrically contributing or participating in the situation.  'We are alike .'

name: Component_entities
definition_en: The entities that function together as a unit.  'The people of Bangkok had the opportunity to experience the long awaited underground train system.'

name: Complex
definition_en: The unit formed by the Component_entities.  'The DeKalb County School System cordially invites you to attend the Ground Breaking Ceremony for Peachtree Middle School.'

name: Function
definition_en: The activity that the Complex entity performs by virtue of its Component_entities interacting.  'These cells form part of the immune system and help to prevent the body from getting diseases .'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any characterization or evaluation of the Complex.  'Kwame Kilpatrick is taking a hard look at Detroit's highly inefficient bus system.'

name: Possessor
definition_en: A person or organization that possesses or owns the Complex or a larger entity of which the Complex itself is a part.  'China's transportation system has undergone profound changes in recent years.'

name: Salient_entity
definition_en: The kind of entity that the Complex operates on as part of its Function.  'The lifespan of a central sewage system is about 80 years.'

name: System
definition_en: The complete entity or system whose complexity is under consideration.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Dimension provides domain specific information about the System.

name: Dimension
definition_en: This frame element situates the System within a certain domain.

name: New
definition_en: The new filler of the Role that was previously occupied by the Old filler.   'The traditional thatched roof has often been replaced by corrugated galvanized iron.'

name: Role
definition_en: The category that the New and Old entities fit into as a result of the Function they serve.  'What gas replaced Hydrogen as a safer medium for use in balloons on account it does not burn? '

name: Function
definition_en: The (generally desirable) state of affairs that the New and Old entities are involved in bringing about.  'Oil and gas replaced coal in heating homes, in industry, and in transportation.'

name: Old
definition_en: The entity that occupied the Role or served the Function before the New filler.  'The electron was discovered and electricity replaced gas lamps.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the New takes up the Role previously occupied by the Old.   'When electricity replaced oil in the early 1930's, the steady beam was replaced by a flashing light.'

name: Degree
definition_en: A Degree of replacement is generally only possible when New entities replace Old entities in multiple contexts.  'In the case of Cyprus, all of the former non-flying terrestrial species were exterminated, and have been entirely replaced by species introduced deliberately or accidentally by man.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).  The rapidity of replacement is also indicated as Manner.  'On land the angiosperms rapidly replaced the gymnosperms as the dominant plants'

name: Textual_location
definition_en: The domain in which the New and Old entities function.  'Machines have replacedmen in the work force'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows.

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who takes possession of the Theme.  'Milton took the can of beer out of the refrigerator.'

name: Theme
definition_en: The Agent takes possession of the Theme. 'Milton took the can of beer out of the refrigerator.'

name: Source
definition_en: The location of the Theme prior to the taking. 'Milton took the can of beer out of the refrigerator.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the taking takes place. 'Police seized several tons of marijuana in Berkeley last weekend.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the taking takes place. 'The government seizure of a suspected dissident's computer last November has increased the tension between citizens and law enforcement.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner of the taking. 'Milton stealthily took the can of beer out of the refrigerator.'

name: Means
definition_en: The intermediate action taken by the Agent to take the Theme. 'Milton took the can of beer from John by distracting him with a shiny nickel'.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for the taking. 'Milton took the can of beer out of the refrigerator to make sure no one else took it.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for the taking. 'Milton took the champagne out of the ice because it was getting too cold.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: The larger event which contains the Taking event. 'These weapons were seized in a police raid'.

name: Captive
definition_en: The entity which is captured.  'Police have captured three of the suspected bombers after a week-long search.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent brings the Captive into custody.  'Authorities recently captured several suspects who were hiding in a remote mountain area.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The instrument with which the capturing is carried out.

name: Reciprocation
definition_en: The reason for the confinement.  'He was captured for treason.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the event occurs.  'Authorities secured the target in a private residence.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Agent takes the Captive into custody.  'These targets were secured to ensure that they would pose no danger during the trial.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Agent that accomplishes the action indicated by the target.   'Troops secured the target by entering his compound in small numbers and under the cover of darkness.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event (or state) which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Agent that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that the Agent is responding to in capturing the Captive.  'She was captured quickly beacuse she was on the department's high priority targets list.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause is the non-sentient entity which is responsible for restricting the movement or location of the Captive.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The description of one of the participants in the capturing event.  'Make sure they're taken alive!'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: The larger event which contains or during which occurs the event of taking the Captive captive.  'The suspects were secured in a large raid conducted by both nations' police forces.'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The individual that holds an opinion on an Issue or Side.

name: Issue
definition_en: The matter, usually concerning a course of action, which the Cognizer has a positive or negative opinion about.

name: Side
definition_en: The party or individual (generally associated with a particular position on an Issue) that the Cognizer has an opinion about.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Cognizer supports or opposes something.

name: Time
definition_en: The time period during which the Cognizer has the indicated point of view towards the Issue.  'Last year she opposed the bill, but changed her mind after she received correspondence supporting the bill. '

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is a proposition denoting a state of affairs from which the Cognizer's taking the indicated view on the Issue logically follows.  'Could it be that he sided with them because it was the constitutionaly correct thing to do?'

name: Action
definition_en: An action taken by a Side or a view that the Side takes on an issue which the Cognizer either supports or opposes.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describes the person or element that is taking a side.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states. In addition, most expressions of Particular_iteration indicate which instance of the series is being referred to.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Taking_sides which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Cognizer that affect the action (reluctantly, meekly).

name: Concessive
definition_en: This FE signifies that the state of affairs expressed by the main clause (containing the target) occurs or holds, and something other than that state of affairs would be expected given the state of affairs in the concessive clause.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Cognizer takes Sides on an Issue .

name: Activity
definition_en: The event which requires some Time_length for completion.  'Mona had a speedy recovery.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The durational feature of the Activity.  'In actual experiential time, sorting the beads takes an extremely long time.'

name: Time_length
definition_en: The amount of time required for the Activity.  'It'll only take 20 seconds.'

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Time_length from the norm.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Activity takes place.  'That took an hour  last week.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Activity takes a particular amount of time.  'In the rain, biking to work takes me a lot longer'

name: Agent
definition_en: The individual who performs the Activity.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration is the length of time from the beginning of the Activity to its end.

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker intends through the use of language to get another person to act.

name: Content
definition_en: The wish for action on the Addressee's part  that the Speaker expresses.

name: Addressee
definition_en: The person that the Speaker seeks to influence to act.

name: Means
definition_en: Act of the Speaker that enables them to persuade the Addressee. 'Mr. Mortiarty talked me into it by claiming it was the last job.'

name: Goods
definition_en: An entity that the Speaker gets the Addressee to give to them.  'He talked me out of five dollars.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state of affairs that the Speaker hopes to bring about.

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity that the Speaker manipulates to get the Addressee to perform the Content.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Speaker talks the Addressee into performing the Content.

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who eats or drinks the Food.  'Patty tried the sausage before serving it.'

name: Food
definition_en: The entity being tasted or ingested by the Agent.  'He tasted the soup and then added a tablespoon of salt.'

name: Means
definition_en: The method in which the Food is eaten or drunk if not covered by the FE Instrument.  'You should taste the wine by rolling it around your tongue a few times before spitting it.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The object that the Agent uses to try the Food.  'John tried the soup with his stirring spoon.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: A more specific description of what the Agent hopes to determine by trying the Food.  'Try the cabbage to see if it has enough salt!'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Agent tries the Food.  'Try each dish before you serve it.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the scene of an Agent trying Food occurs.\  'Patty tried the sausage in the kitchen.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A characterization of the Agent as they try the Food.  'I carefully tasted the piping hot casserole.'

name: Members
definition_en: This FE identifies the people or things that form  the Aggregate.

name: Team
definition_en: This FE identifies the collection of entities that are the Team.

name: Aggregate_property
definition_en: This FE describes a property of the Aggregate rather than the Members and is used to tag the adjective that modifies the aggregate noun when it is unambiguous.  'A large crowd of hoodlums filled the plaza.'

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to the Aggregate.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location or political locale that the Organization is contained within.

name: Domain
definition_en: The relevant Domain as it pertains to the Aggregate.

name: Activity
definition_en: The job, obligation, or goal worked towards jointly by the Members of the Team.

name: Parent_organization
definition_en: The broader organization (if any) that members of a team belong to.  'A team from the American Nutrition Council issued their report today .'

name: Speaker
definition_en: The Speaker is the sentient entity that produces the Message. 'Bill told me that he would come to the party.'

name: Addressee
definition_en: The Addressee receives the Message from the Speaker.

name: Message
definition_en: The Message is the communication produced by the Speaker. 'The authorities informed me that my brother had been arrested.' 'I told him a bedtime story.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is a general description of the content of the Message. 'Leroy told his mother about his arrest.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes the way in which the Speaker delivers the Message.

name: Means
definition_en: The Means describes the way the Speaker accomplishes the task of giving the Addressee the Message.

name: Medium
definition_en: This FE is the Medium in which the Message is expressed.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Speaker informs the Addressee of the Message.  'Even when we had a size problem they informed me right away and everything worked out great.'

name: Place
definition_en: Place is the location in which the Speaker informs  the Addressee of the Message.  'She looked at it for a few moments, thinking of Mark Smeaton and what he had told her on the steps of City Hall.'

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the Message is expressed. This FE is often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.  'She has yet to receive official notification.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the telling event.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The FE Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity for which the temperature Attribute is under consideration.   'The soup's too hot.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: The feature of an Entity which is under discussion.

name: Temperature
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the Entity's state with respect to the temperature Attribute.  'The skillet had a temperature of 230 F'

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Temperature from the norm.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity is in the state of having  a particular Degree for the temperature Attribute.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the Circumstances under which the Entity has a particular Temperature.

name: Subregion
definition_en: A part of the Entity that has the specified Temperature value.   'The pan is hot on the handle'

name: Trajector_entity
definition_en: The entity that occurs at some time.  'The current President of Georgia was born in Tbilisi.'  'Books in the early 19th century had fewer pictures.'

name: Landmark_event
definition_en: The event which designates the time at which a trajector occurs.  'During last night's walk , I stubbed my toe.'

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE describes the state of affairs reported by the target is understood to play a role in the state of affairs of the modifier.

name: Trajector_period
definition_en: The period that occurs with respect to some other time.  'Future eras will be vastly changed from today.'

name: Landmark_period
definition_en: The period in which a trajector takes place.  This period can be cyclical and, in that case, is interpreted contextually.  'I went to the store on Tuesday.' 'In the Triassic Era, the first flying vertebrates appeared.'

name: Trajector_event
definition_en: The event that occurs at some time.  'Currently, researchers are making new discoveries very quickly.'

name: Landmark_entity
definition_en: The entity which designates the time of some trajector.  Note: this FE is infrequent or non-existent in English and is included for completeness.

name: Process
definition_en: The larger event that is characterized by the recurring Subevents.  'The rhythm of the rain falling on the roof kept me awake'

name: Subevent
definition_en: The salient, punctual event that is construed as part of a Process.  'His rhythmic tapping irritated her'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Pattern in which the Subevents recur.  'I could feel the steady rhythm of his breathing'

name: Pattern
definition_en: The Pattern that can be detected in the recurrence of  the Subevents of the Process .   'The music had a driving rhythm' 'The music had a driving rhythm'

name: Type
definition_en: An indication of a conventionally recognized subtype that the Pattern belongs to.   'Herminio illustrated a rhumba rhythm on the congas'

name: Subpart
definition_en: The part of the Time_period which is profiled.  'The findings mark the beginning of a new age of planetary science, in which "extrasolar" planets can be directly measured and compared.'

name: Subpart_property
definition_en: Some description which pertains specifically to the Subpart (rather than the Time_period).  'Indeed, the sorry end of the HCI period, with Korea in recession and. in the throes of rampant political turmoil, has led some analysts to conclude that the prior period had been underlyingly unstable despite its appearance of promise.'

name: Time_period
definition_en: A temporal span conceived of as a whole.  'A zillion copies and clones have been made of this Russian game since it first was released in the mid 80's.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE indicates the Time that is being referred to.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Temporary_group
definition_en: The group formed temporarily from a larger group for a particular purpose.  'The Americans posted a small detachment to guard the facilities.'

name: Members
definition_en: The people belonging to the Temporary_group.  'We were provided with a security detail of several soldiers.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The reason for which an Temporary_group is formed.  'We've requested a large guard detachment.'

name: Period_of_existence
definition_en: The interval during which the Temporary_group exists.

name: Name
definition_en: A name given to the Temporary_group for identification.

name: Container_possessor
definition_en: The location or political locale that the Temporary_group is contained within or is responsible to.  'The American detachment left at around midnight to begin the next round of patrols.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE describes the general location where the Temporary_group operates, but does not indicate the possessor of the Temporary_group.  'A Marine detail in southern Greenland suddenly stopped communications.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any description of the Temporary_group not covered by a more specific frame element.  'Smith was part of a small security detail tasked with the patients' safety.'

name: Parent_organization
definition_en: The Parent_organization is the larger group from which members are selected to be part of the Temporary_group.  'A detachment from the US military forces is due to arrive soon.'

name: Person
definition_en: The person who is absent from his or her Activity for a Duration of time.  'During his wife's absence, Linkworth and his mother had another violent argument.'  'Lemaire took a sabbatical from the club.'

name: Activity
definition_en: This FE describes the activity or responsiblilities from which the Person is taking a temporary leave.  'Such conditions would be likely to lead to absence from work.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time the Person is absent from his or her Activity.  This can also be expressed as a description of a duration, as shown below:  'Dissuaded from resigning, Macmillan took extended leave rather than restrain his public utterances.'  'During her two-year absence Eliza suffered great pangs of homesickness and longing for her children.'

name: Location
definition_en: The place in which the Person spends his or her leave.  'Chris read many books while on sabbatical in Spain.'

name: Type
definition_en: The kind of leave being taken by the Person.  'She's been on maternity leave for a while.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: A characterization of the absence.  'After a mysterious five-year absence from his tribe, Smohalla had returned.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the absences occur.  'Laura's frequent absences in London meant that her baby, Emma, was often left behind with Gwenny. '

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for the Person's absence.  'Ukraine's absence from the negotiations because of the forthcoming referendum on independence, had made the signing of a Union Treaty unlikely.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Person's intended purpose for the temporary leave.  'Mark Morrow will replace Ben Bradlee Jr., who is taking a leave to write a book.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the leave occurs.  'Columbus took leave of the known world on 6 September 1492.'

name: Guest
definition_en: The Guest remains for a relatively short period of time in the Location.  'Originally, we planned on rooming with our relatives in Reno.'

name: Location
definition_en: The Location where the Guest spends a short amount of time.  'Originally we planned on staying at the Hilton.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Guest remains at the Location.  'My wife and have just returned from a two day stay at Ocean Key.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: Another person who, along with the Guest, is temporarily living at the Location.  'I will stay at my parents' home, along with my wife and cats.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the temporary stay takes place.  'He'll be lodging here next month.'

name: Host
definition_en: The Host is living at the Location on a permanent basis, and is allowing the Guest to stay there.  'You should avoid staying with old college buddies when on business trips.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The activity that the Guest hopes to achieve by the stay.

name: Means
definition_en: An action of the Guest that brings about their ability to stay at the Location.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the type of event by comparison to other events (the same way) or by characterizing a state of the Guest that affects the action.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The average number of times the event occurs over a period.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times that the event occurs.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description of one of the participants in the temporary stay, or of the staying state-of-affairs in general.  'I hope you have a pleasant stay at our lodge.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place indicates the larger physical setting of the temporary stay.  'In London, I stayed at a hotel.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A state of affairs that provides an explanation for the temporary stay.

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE denotes an event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at a time that includes the time of the temporary stay, and which is taken to be a part of the stay.

name: Theme
definition_en: The object that is transferred from the Lender to the Borrower for a Duration.

name: Lender
definition_en: The person or institution who gives the Theme to the Borrower for a Duration.

name: Borrower
definition_en: The person or institution who receives the Theme from the Lender for a Duration.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of time in which the Borrower has possession of the Theme.

name: Agreement
definition_en: A mutual commitment to an obligation made by two or more parties.  'The right to remove tenants ' fixtures may be given by the terms of the lease. '

name: Regulated_entity
definition_en: A salient entity, an activity or behavior by the parties to the agreement to which a particular stipulation pertains.  'Many believed that the military terms of the armistice made the resumption of hostilities virtually impossible for Germany.'

name: Requirements
definition_en: The Requirements that a particular stipulation of the Agreement imposes on one or both of the parties.  'Each time you use the site, a condition of use is that you comply with the above terms.'

name: Desired_state_of_affairs
definition_en: An event or state of affairs that is desirable to some or all of the parties to the Agreement and which is conditional on the Requirements being met.  'What are your conditions of Sale?'

name: Party
definition_en: A party who demands that certain Requirements be met before they will enter into an Agreement or allow a Desired_state_of_affairs to be realized.  'Our political and military terms of peace will be designed to prevent a repetition of Germany's misdeeds'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description of the Requirements that are imposed by the Agreement.  'No reason why SU would have to impose harsh terms, the lease payments would pay the bank loan used to buy the stadium.'

name: Terrorist
definition_en: The Terrorist commits the Act of terror for political or ideological gains.  'Several domestic terrorists were operating from the site during the mid 1990s.'

name: Act
definition_en: The Act is the harmful action performed by the Terrorist or terrorist organization.  'Many have suffered due to their acts of terrorism.'

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is most directly affected or harmed by the Act of terrorism.  'Cowardly acts of terrorism upon innocent men, women, and children is not a doorway to Heaven, but a gateway to Hell.'  'Never have I seen such terrorism on Christians in Pakistan before.'

name: Organization
definition_en: A Terrorist may be part of a larger group or Organization of such people.  'Several Pioneer Liberation terrorists were arrested earlier today.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any characterization or evaluation of the Terrorist or Act.  'The armed terrorists were caught on tape.'  'terrorism'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Terrorist commits the Act.

name: Means
definition_en: The intermediate action performed by the Terrorist in order to comit the Act.

name: Time
definition_en: The location in time when the Act takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Act takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The action or state-of-affairs that the Terrorist is trying to accomplish by commiting the Act.

name: Instrument
definition_en: The Instrument is used by the Terrorist in order to inflict harm or commit the Act.  'The most recent threat to our security is biological terrorism.'  'Large-scale CBW terrorism is a constant worry to those in power.'

name: Author
definition_en: The Author is the person who produced a particular Text.  'I'm glad I bought and read Robbins's book.'

name: Text
definition_en: The Text is the entity that contains linguistic information. This an incorporated FE for each LU in this frame.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: The person for whom the Text is produced. 'The poem   for Caitlin was included in an anthology .'

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The Time at which the Text was created.  'Jackson's new story is based on a 1980 novel by his father.' 'Poems from the end of that dynasty are known to contain many novel metric structures.'

name: Material
definition_en: What a Text is made of (if applicable). 'The library was so old, it was filled with vellum tomes, not a paperback in sight.'

name: Containing_text
definition_en: This is a text in which the Text is located. 'The last poem in the anthology was horrid.'

name: Genre
definition_en: The Genre or sub-Genre of the Text.  'She writes only historical fiction.'  'I've got three comedic screenplays on my desk right now!'

name: Use
definition_en: The use for which the text was produced; its purpose.   'She read through the bicycle's construction manual.'

name: Subpart
definition_en: The smaller texts that make up the Text. 'He found it in a book of spells.'

name: Topic
definition_en: Topic is what the Text is about.'I read a book about knitting.'

name: Title
definition_en: The Title of a Text.  'She read Sassy magazine.' 'Current NOW President Kim Gandy said Friedan's Feminine Mystique book opened women's eyes.'  NOTE: when the Title is expressed in an appositive clause, it is labeled as Text on the first layer and Title on the second.  'She read the magazine Sassy.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The Medium is the language in which a text is composed, or the physical medium (radio, ink) in which it is distributed.  'Science articles in Greek are difficult to understand for me.'  'It's prudent to pay attention to radio bulletins.'

name: Place
definition_en: The region where the Text is sold, circulated, or otherwise popular.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characteristic of the Text

name: Author
definition_en: The Author produces a particular Text.

name: Components
definition_en: The Components are the parts that the Author uses to construct the Text. ' Caitlin wrote the book from memoirs she collected.'

name: Text
definition_en: The entity which results from the act of writing or speaking. 'Michael wrote a frame description.' ' Cybil wanted to speak those three words.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action 'I wrote everything in that decade on drugs.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: The instrument with which an intentional act is performed.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action.  This frame includes some peculiar examples of manner phrases. Write it in pen.   Write it in ink.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a Text is created.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which an intentional act is performed.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time at which the text is created.

name: Addressee
definition_en: This is the person to whom the Message is communicated. When this FE is expressed, it often appears in a prepositional phrase introduced by to, or as the direct object, or as the first object in a double object construction.

name: Beneficiary
definition_en: Beneficiary identifies the person in whose honor or for whose benefit the Text is created.

name: Form
definition_en: This FE describes the form in which the text is presented.  'Yeats wrote out his poems in prose.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for creating the text. 'I wrote the article because I would have lost my teaching post otherwise.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The language in which the Text is represented or the physical materials upon which the Text is recorded.  'I wrote the code on the back of the envelope.'

name: Perpetrator
definition_en: Perpetrator is the person (or other agent) that takes the goods away.   'Leslie stole the watch from Kim.'

name: Victim
definition_en: Victim is the person (or other sentient being or group) that owns the goods before they are taken away by the perpetrator. 'Leslie stole the watch from Kim. '

name: Goods
definition_en: Goods is anything (including labor, time, or legal rights) that can be taken away.   'Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source is the initial location of the goods, before they change location.  'Leslie stole the watch from the table.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the theft occurs.  'Leslie swiftly STOLE the watch from Kim.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a Perpetrator takes the Victim's Goods.  'Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim by following her home after work.'

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the theft occurs. 'Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim in the park.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which a theft occurs. 'Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim in order to sell it on Ebay.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE identifies the Explanation for why a theft occurs.  'Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim because she'd always wanted a Gucci.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the theft occurs.  'Leslie STOLE the watch from Kim at dusk.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: An object used by the Perpetrator in taking possession of the Goods.  'Chis stole it with a long bamboo pole through the fence'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that a theft occurs.  'Thieves twice stole my Dodge Dart in the last two weeks'

name: Matter
definition_en: The Matter is the physical substance or entity being described in terms of a Phase.

name: Phase
definition_en: The state of the Matter being described.

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity is experiencing a period of desirable events or states.  'In the 1920s the peach industry thrived in Upson County.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.   'In those nations, the economy languishes under repressive regimes which do not govern for their people but rather against them.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Entity thrives.  'In the 1920s the peach industry thrived in Upson County.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place where the thriving takes place.  'Why was it that democracy flourished in America?'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Role
definition_en: The category in which the Entity thrives.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for why or how the Entity thrives.

name: Desirability
definition_en: This FE describes the state of the Entity. It is often incorporated into the LUs of this frame.  'He was living well after his promotion.'

name: Preventing_cause
definition_en: The Preventing_cause is the agent or force who keeps the Protagonist from completing her or his planned Action.

name: Protagonist
definition_en: The Protagonist is the individual or group of individuals who have a planned Action which is prevented by the Preventing_cause

name: Action
definition_en: The Action is the action or event certain individuals desire to bring about which is prevented by the Preventing_cause.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time is when the thwarting occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the thwarting occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Preventing_cause thwarts the Action of the Protagonist. 'He easily thwarted my plans.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the Action is thwarted.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for why or how the Protagonist and/or Action was thwarted by the Preventing_cause.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This FE is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often.

name: Enabled_action
definition_en: The action that becomes possible through the existence of the period of time.

name: Duration
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the period of the time in which an Enabled_action is allowed.  In this frame, the duration may be exact or inexact.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent is the one who performs the Enabled_action.

name: Whole
definition_en: The Whole is the larger time period to which target is a part of.

name: Landmark_event
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate the reference point in which the Event  is anchored.  ' Sue is going to pick me up again two days from tomorrow. '

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate the amount of time that lies between the Target and the Landmark_event.  'Peter will meet me a week from today '

name: Direction
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate whether the Target is prior or subsequent to the Landmark_event on the time line.  ' Mom last called me a week ago. '

name: Event
definition_en: This FE indicates the Event temporally located with respect to the Landmark_event. 'The incident was several years ago.'

name: Duration
definition_en: A quantity or other characterization of the State's duration.  In this frame, the duration can be inexact.

name: State
definition_en: An ongoing state whose duration can be measured.  'He was a great actor in his time.'

name: Whole
definition_en: The Whole is the larger moment in time of which the target is a part.  'What time of year do you suggest we visit Tbilisi?'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: Any characterization or evaluation of the timespan not covered by a more specific FE.

name: Timetable
definition_en: The mental schedule of times at which the Events are set to take place.  'My idiot friend forgot his class schedule again.'

name: Events
definition_en: The events which are to take place at specified times acording to the Timetable.  'What's your class schedule like this spring?'

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The sentient entity who keeps the Timetable.  'John's schedule is packed this afternoon.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The time period within which the Timetable repeats.  'Depending on the camper's age group, his or her daily schedule will vary.'

name: Time_of_implementation
definition_en: The time at which the Events on the Timetable transpire.  'What's on the agenda today?'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose for which the Cognizer keeps the Timetable.  'You need to develop a weekly timetable to manage your goals.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterization of the Timetable.  'University students have very full schedules.'

name: Experiencer
definition_en: The Experiencer experiences tolerance with respect to the Content.

name: Content
definition_en: Content is what the Experiencer's feeling of tolerance is directed towards..  The Content differs from a stimulus because the Content is not construed as being direcly responsible for causing the emotion.  ' Everyone must endure some disappointments in life.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is the explanation for why an Experiencer tolerates the Content.  ' Spouses often tolerate their partner's vices because they love the overall person.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the toleration occurs.

name: Manner
definition_en: Manner of performing an action

name: Parameter
definition_en: The Parameter is a domain in which the Experiencer tolerates the Content.  'Intellectual tolerance is a very important trait to have in this field.'

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the area about which the Experiencer has the  tolerated experience(s). ' They 're very tolerant about boys' mess in the home and untidiness generally.'

name: State
definition_en: The State is the abstract noun that describes a more lasting experience by the Experiencer.  'Tracy was in a surprisngly tolerant mood today.'

name: Event
definition_en: The Event is the occasion or happening that Experiencers in a certain emotional state participate in.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances FE encodes the circumstances or conditions under which the Experiencer experiences the emotion. Unlike Content it does not give the specific content of the emotion, but the Content can often be inferred from the Circumstances.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Experiencer is in the state of toleration.  'When they are young,, they  cannot stand extremes of temperature. '

name: Purpose
definition_en: A Purpose is a generic goal associated with the Tool.

name: Tool
definition_en: A Tool is the object or process that has been designed specifically to achieve a Purpose.

name: Type
definition_en: A description of the Purpose.

name: Domain
definition_en: The sphere of activity in which the Tool is typically used.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is what a Text is about.

name: Text
definition_en: A set of propositions that is coherent in being about a Topic  'Sue bought a book about Pennsylvania'

name: Communicator
definition_en: The Communicator is the person who has produced a Text on a Topic.  'In his book, Smithers discusses cotton production. '

name: Degree
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate to which Degree the Text is about the Topic   'The article is mostly about yoga techniques'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE marks expressions in which Manner the Topic is treated.  'The book carefully discusses the events leading up to the war'

name: Status
definition_en: The Frame Element Status is used for expressions that indicate the relative importance of a Topic with respect to the other topics that a Text is about.  'The book is mainly about 19th century sewage systems' ' A peripheral topic of Chapter 3 is Appalachian coal-mining. '

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Communicator produces Text on a Topic.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which the Text or Communicator presents the Topic.

name: Tourist
definition_en: The individual that is seeking an experience at an Attraction.

name: Attraction
definition_en: The societally-recognized unique location that the Tourist experiences.

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Tourist or the Attraction during the tour.

name: Ground
definition_en: The perceptual background against which the Attraction is experienced by the Tourist.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the details of the event in terms of how they compare to other events (the same way) or in terms of how the state of the Tourist affects them (happily, obliviously).

name: Means
definition_en: The Means indicates a method the Tourist is using to participate in a tour.

name: Time
definition_en: The time that the touring takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: Some action that the Tourist is trying to accomplish with touring.  This is generally (at a minimum) for the purposes of entertainment and learning.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the touring takes place.

name: Duration
definition_en: The amount of  time the touring activity lasts.

name: Particular_iteration
definition_en: Expressions marked with this extra-thematic FE modify a non-iterative use of the target, and indicate that it is conceived as embedded within an iterated series of similar events or states.

name: Co-participant
definition_en: The Co-participant is an entity that participates in a coordinated way in the touring event with the Tourist.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is the being or entity that is capable of being harmed by the Toxic_substance.  'Chocolate can be poisonous for some types of pets.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree is the degree to which the Toxic_substance is harmful to the Victim.

name: Body_part
definition_en: The Body_part defines the part of the Victim's body that is harmed.  'This vitamin taken in excess could be poisonous for the liver'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A fact or action that explains why the Toxic_substance has a harmful effect on the Victim .

name: Toxic_substance
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate the substance which potentially causes harm to a Victim.   'Highly toxic pollutants could be safely disposed of by burning them'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: A set of circumstances, often the relative amount of the Toxic_substance that is present, under which the Toxic_substance is specified to have or lack a toxic effect.  'Some metals, such as copper and selenium, are essential to normal metabolic function as trace elements but are toxic at high levels of exposure'

name: Toxin_source
definition_en: A living organism, object or process that produces a Toxic_substance.  'A young man was bitten by a poisonous snake and lives to tell about it.'

name: Type
definition_en: Type identifies the kind or sort of Toxic_substance.

name: Duration
definition_en: Temporal period for which the substance or source remains toxic to the victim.

name: Recipient
definition_en: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The object that changes ownership.

name: Donor
definition_en: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which an event occurs.

name: Time
definition_en: When the transfer occurs.

name: Transferors
definition_en: The Donor and Recipient conceived of as a unit.

name: Means
definition_en: The action whereby the transfer of the Theme from the Donor to the Recipient is effected.  'The South State delivery system provides for courier transfer of documents and interlibrary loans among member libraries and the South State Office. '

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the transfer which is not covered by more specific FEs

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which a Theme is transferred

name: Recipient
definition_en: The entity that ends up in possession of the Theme.

name: Theme
definition_en: The object that changes ownership.

name: Donor
definition_en: The person that begins in possession of the Theme and causes it to be in the possession of the Recipient.

name: Transferors
definition_en: The Donor and Recipient conceived of as a unit.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the change takes place.  'I went nuts in Berlin .'

name: Time
definition_en: When the change occurs.  'By 1945 he had gone bad .'

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The length of time that the Entity retains the Final_quality.   'He went nuts for three years . '

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In cases where the Entity is intentional, Manner may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Entity that also affect the event (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'The majority slowly went silent .'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity which undergoes a change so that it possesses the Final_quality.  'I went limp .'

name: Final_quality
definition_en: The quality that the Entity has at the end of the event.  'Everything 's going wrong!'

name: Transitional_period
definition_en: The period during which the Entity is in transition.  'Over the last 5 years, I've gone crazy.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE marks the set of conditions under which the Entity adopts Final_quality.

name: Group
definition_en: A characterization of the kind of Group members that the Entity pertains to, and which are saliently affected by its change.

name: Explanation
definition_en: Any eventuality or entity which brings about the change of the Entity.  'Smithers went numb from all the work he'd been doing.'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the change takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the change occurs.  'By 1945 he had come to doubt the advisability of anyone having such a weapon.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In cases where the Entity is intentional, Manner may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Entity that also affect the event (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'The majority slowly came to understand him.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity which undergoes a change, ending up in the Final_situation.  'I am coming to loathe your insolence.'

name: Transitional_period
definition_en: The period during which the Entity is in transition.  'Over the next three years she came to represent the hope of latinos everywhere .'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE marks the set of conditions under which the Entity enters the Final_situation.

name: Group
definition_en: The type of individual things that have an instance of the Entity and which are saliently affected by its change.

name: Explanation
definition_en: Any eventuality or entity which brings about the change of the Entity.  'Smithers came to hate her because of all the work he'd been doing.'

name: Final_situation
definition_en: The Entity's situation after the change.  'My father came to wonder why he 'd worked so hard .'

name: Place
definition_en: Where the change takes place.

name: Time
definition_en: When the change occurs.  'By 1945 he had become uncertain of the advisability of anyone having such a weapon.'

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: For how long the Entity remains in the Final_category, Final_situation, or Final_quality.   'He became for the next three years the prophetic voice of the Salvadoran people until his assassination on March 24, 1980'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In cases where the Entity is intentional, Manner may indicate salient characteristics of an intentional Entity that also affect the event (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'The majority slowly became more and more disenchanted with him.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The Entity which undergoes a change, ending up in the Final_category, Final_situation, or Final_quality.  'I grow impatient with your insolence.'

name: Final_quality
definition_en: The quality of the Entity after the change.  'Everything 's going wrong!'

name: Final_category
definition_en: The category that the Entity ends up in after the change.  'He never could understand how she ended up an evangelist.'

name: Transitional_period
definition_en: The period during which the Entity is in transition.  'Over the last 5 years, I've become sick and tired of your tomfoolery.'

name: Initial_state
definition_en: This FE describes the state of the Entity before becoming occurs.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE marks the set of conditions under which the Entity enters the Final_category, Final_situation, or Final_quality.

name: Initial_category
definition_en: This FE describes the category of the Entity before becoming occurs.

name: Group
definition_en: The individual entities related to the Entity which are saliently affected by its change.

name: Explanation
definition_en: Any eventuality or entity which brings about the change of the Entity.  'Smithers became tired from all the work he'd been doing.'

name: Final_situation
definition_en: The Entity's situation after the change.  'My father got to where he did in the business through instinct and entrepreneurialism.'

name: Agent
definition_en: Agent is the entity that acts on another entity.

name: Patient
definition_en: Patient is the entity that is being acted on and that may but need not undergo a change.

name: Event
definition_en: An Event in which an Agent acts on an entity.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing a participant in the event.

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of a transitive action.

name: Means
definition_en: An act performed by an Agent that enables them to act upon the Patient.</def-root >

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the event takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the event takes place.

name: Cause
definition_en: An event which causes the Patient to be affected in some way.

name: Cognizer
