definition_en: This is the person who carries out the translation.   'The text was published in Lescarbot's Les Muses de la Nouvelle-France (Paris 1609) and later translated by HT Richardson.'

name: Source_symbol
definition_en: A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Source_representation format.  'Biblical scholars typically translate kenosis as self-emptying or self-offering.'

name: Source_representation
definition_en: The representation system in which the Content pre-exists.  'More books were translated from other languages into Russian in the 1980s , including record numbers from English , German and French.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the translation event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may indicate salient characteristics of the Cognizer that also affect the action (deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'His book, carefully translated by Teresa Lavender Fagan, is a fascinating account for the layman, of the cuisine of the Mesopotamia. '

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Cognizer which accomplishes the translation of the Content.  'We also translated the queries into Chinese by looking up each English word in the bilingual dictionary.'

name: Time
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions that indicate when a certain Categorization was made.  'Last year I translated a short book on the artist Anne Ratkowski (of the pre-war November Group in Berlin) from German into English.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances are the set of conditions in which the translation is made.  'With everybody waiting for him, he simply translated the word as ?son? or ?child?.'

name: Target_symbol
definition_en: A symbol or set of symbols representing the Content in the Target_representation format.  ' Together with the French Prime Minister, Guizot, he translated it into French as entente cordiale for King Louis Philippe to use in his speech.'

name: Target_representation
definition_en: The representation system into which the Content is rendered by the Cognizer.  'Well they translated it into Spanish as "Uno-Dos-Tres Meneha Meneha!"'

name: Content
definition_en: The information that is meant to be represented by the Source_symbol and Target_symbol.  'She guided me through the dishes available that afternoon and translated my order into Spanish for the older woman in the kitchen.'

name: Equivalence
definition_en: An assessment of how equivalent the Source_representation and the Target_representation are.  'The Japanese term hai is literally translated as yes.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The Medium is a text produced by the Cognizer in which she uses a Target_symbol to express Content from a Source_representation system.  'Gearóid Ó Cairealláin translates Texas as Teicseas in an article in Lá.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the translation takes place.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Cognizer hopes to bring about by translating.

name: Rider
definition_en: The Rider is being transported by a Vehicle.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The Vehicle carries the Rider.

name: Trap
definition_en: The Trap is a device, strategy, or system designed to mislead and cause harm to a Victim.

name: Deceiver
definition_en: The Trap is orchestrated by a Deceiver.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Deceiver intends to mislead and cause harm to the Victim by means of the Trap.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description of the Trap.

name: Area
definition_en: This is the Area in which the traveling takes place. This frame element describes the enclosed area inside which travelling, of unspecified Source, Path or Goal takes place. 'We travelled in Europe.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: The Co-participant is the person or persons who accompany the Traveler on the journey.

name: Distance
definition_en: This FE dientifies the Distance traveled.

name: Duration
definition_en: This FE identifies the Duration of  time during which the trip occurs.

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the location where the travelers end up.

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the traveling takes place. 'The Brownie troop travelled hurriedly.'

name: Means
definition_en: The action done by the Traveler by which the traveling is accomplished. 'I traveled to London by hitchhiking and walking.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path is the route along which the travel takes place.

name: Traveler
definition_en: This is the living being which travels. Normally, the Traveler is expressed as an external argument.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the starting point of the trip.

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the travel takes place. 'The Simpsons travelled at 60 km per hour.'

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Traveler is effected, by their body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Traveler. Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.  'Barney used to travel by bus  a lot' 'Strom  travelled on foot  to see the Pope'

name: Time
definition_en: When the traveling occurs.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the travel is undertaken.

name: Baggage
definition_en: The Baggage are the items necessary for travel that accompany the Traveler. 'Ellen journeyed to Europe with five suitcases.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: The Frequency with which the Traveler makes the journey.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Traveler travels, i.e. the future state of affairs that will hopefully come about.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The number of times the trip is traveled by the Travelers.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The Time throughout which the traveling repeatedly takes place.

name: Travel_means
definition_en: This FE applies to expressions that indicate documents, money, tickets, etc. which allow people to engage in travel. 'He traveled to San Diego on a standby ticket.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Traveler during the journey. 'We traveled around unencumbered.'

name: Result
definition_en: The affect of travel on a Traveler. 'We journeyed to exhaustion.'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is the location of the motion. It describes the area in which motion (with a specified Source, Path or Goal) takes place.

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction in which the Traveler goes.  'They began their odyssey north.'

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A characterisitic of the traveling event.

name: Theme
definition_en: This is the object which moves. In many sentences this FE will be expressed as something which moves under its own power. However, this FE is not required to be an animate mover, so it is different from Self_mover.  'Kim crossed through the woods.'

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. In prepositional phrases, the prepositional object expresses the starting point of motion. In particles, the starting point of motion is understood from context.   'The cat crossed the street from her yard.'

name: Path
definition_en: Any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal (see below) expresses the frame element Path, including directional expressions:   'The bikers crisscrossed through the desert.'  'The cyclist ascended towards the gate.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Any expression which tells where the Theme ends up as a result of the motion expresses the frame element Goal.   'The children hopped into the neighbor's yard.'  Some particles imply the existence of a Goal which is understood in the context of utterance:  'The children hopped over and sat down.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any expression which describes a property of motion which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion expresses the frame element Manner. Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.   'The bikers crossed furiously through the desert.'

name: Distance
definition_en: Any expression which characterizes the extent of motion expresses the frame element Distance.  'I leaped twenty feet before slipping and falling.'

name: Area
definition_en: This frame element is used for expressions which describe a general area in which motion takes place when the motion is understood to be irregular and not to consist of a single linear path.   'The bikers crisscrossed the desert.' Note that this FE should not be used for any locational modifier which would occur just as naturally with a non-motion predicate, like speech.

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree to which event occurs

name: Means
definition_en: An event involving the Theme that results in the Theme moving in the specified way. 'The less experienced mountaneers ascended by crawling.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the Theme moves.

name: Cotheme
definition_en: This is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique:   'The squirrel leaped after it.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depictive phrase describing the actor of an action  'We crisscrossed the country naked'

name: Place
definition_en: The Place is where the motion (which is specified by a Source, Path or Goal) is located.

name: Path_shape
definition_en: The configuration formed by the entire Path of the Theme, taken simultaneously. 'He circled downward in a spiral.'

name: Direction
definition_en: The direction in which the Theme goes.  'The frogs jumped down through the meadow.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the motion takes place.  'They crisscrossed the country in April.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state-of-affairs that the Theme wishes to bring about.  'The participants circled around in order to avoid the house..'

name: Means_of_motion
definition_en: The device or bodypart that serves to move the Theme.  'We crossed the river by boat.' 'Bravo company broke an axle while trying to jump a ditch in a Humvee.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The length of time that the Theme spends in motion.

name: Result
definition_en: The state of the Theme at the end of the event.

name: Explanation
definition_en: A factor which explains the particular motion or manner of motion of the Theme.

name: Reciprocation
definition_en: An event paired with the motion, which explains why the motion is expected. In particular,  or an action that Reciprocation is used to indicate an action that is being rewarded or punished by the motion, is paired with the motion as the other side of an agreement.</def-root >

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event that occurs or state of affairs that holds at the time the Traversing occurs and which the Traversing is taken to be a part of.

name: Frequency
definition_en: The number of times that an action occurs in a given time.

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: A larger conceptualization that includes the Traversing as an integral part. The Traversing expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action in this larger conceptualization.

name: New_situation
definition_en: An unexpected event that affects some agent (usually the Theme), which is enabled by, and occurs after, the Traversing.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the Traversing event itself and any of its participants, and is merely peripherally related to the event as a whole.

name: Endpoints
definition_en: The Source and Goal of either a single or a repeated motion taken together as Endpoints of the Path.  'A large plastic "football" wildly passed between goal posts.'

name: Coordinated_event
definition_en: The label Coordinated_event is to be used for phrases denoting an event-it does not allow states-that the Traversing is rhythmically aligned with. The Coordinated_event is conceived of as independent: it would occur regardless of the event expressed by the target, which is not even an incidental or optional sub-part of the Coordinated_event.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The time period within which the motion event occurs repeatedly.

name: Event_description
definition_en: In general, this FE is used for phrases that describe the clause of the target as a whole. There are two somewhat distinct subgroups of sentence modifiers that cover this function.

name: Iterations
definition_en: The frame element Iterations is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.

name: Agent
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that denote the person whose conduct is being evaluated.  'Douglas always treated Mary well.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that characterize the way that the Agent behaves toward the Affected_Party. In the case of mistreat.v, this FE is incorporated.  'Douglas always treated Mary well.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate a set of Circumstances under which the Agent acts in a particular way.  'When Douglas was in a good mood he would never mistreat us.'

name: Affected_party
definition_en: The person to whom behavior is directed by the Agent.  'Douglas always treated Mary well.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: This FE marks expressions that indicate why an Agent behaved in a certain way.  'Douglas treats his wife well because he loves her.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Agent behaves in a certain way.  'Douglas ill-uses us every week after his son visits.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Agent exhibits their behavior.  'Douglas mistreated me in the office.'

name: Means
definition_en: The way in which the treating or mistreating is done.  'Douglas mistreats waiters by yelling at them.'

name: Domain
definition_en: The Domain of human behavior in which the Agent acts in a certain Manner.  'Douglas rarely economically mistreated us but often verbally mistreated us instead.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the (usually 'good' or 'bad') conduct of the Agent deviates from some standard or norm.  'Douglas always treated me very well.'

name: Standard
definition_en: An explicit point to which the conduct of the Agent is compared.  'He treated us well for a teenager.'

name: Behavior
definition_en: The Behavior which is trendy.

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the degree of trendiness from the norm or from the value for another Behavior.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which the Behavior is trendy or fashionable.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Some specification of the circumstances under which the Behavior is trendy or not.

name: Evaluee
definition_en: The Evaluee is judged to conform to some degree with popular fashion with respect to his or her behavior.

name: Judge
definition_en: The individual whose point of view is taken in assigning the judgment of trendiness.

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Behavior is trendy..

name: Charges
definition_en: The legal label for the crime that the Defendant is accused of.

name: Court
definition_en: The specific room where the participants in a Trial meet.

name: Defense
definition_en: The individual or group which is responsible for promoting the welfare of the  Defendant during a Trial, usually involving the contention that the Defendant is innocent of the Charges.

name: Jury
definition_en: The group of individuals who observe the Trial and ultimately attempt to come to a verdict.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the trial occurs.

name: Prosecution
definition_en: The individual or group responsible for promoting the interests of the state in the Trial, prototypically including presenting arguments for the guilt of the Defendant.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the trial occurs.

name: Defendant
definition_en: The person charged with an offence.

name: Judge
definition_en: The official who directs and presides over the Trial.

name: Case
definition_en: The Case which a Trial is convened to decide.

name: Manner
definition_en: The way in which the Trial is conducted.

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause interacts with the System such that conditions are met for the System to operate.  'His presence set off the motion alarms.'

name: System
definition_en: The System interacts with or detects the Cause and activates.  'They let him through even though something triggered the metal detector?'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is a subevent which the Cause or Actor participates in which results in triggering the System .  'You must have set off the alarm by stepping near this sensor.'

name: Actor
definition_en: An entity which participates in a Cause, perhaps volitionally and perhaps not.  'She set off the silent alarm before being shoved into the middle of the lobby.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any holistic description of the event, including overall depictions (the same way) and descriptions pertaining to the Actor's or Cause's influence on the character of the event (eagerly, quietly).

name: Place
definition_en: Where the triggering takes place.  'Police came running downstairs when someone set off the metal detector at the county courthouse.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time when the triggering takes place.  'Three bombs were set off at three o'clock today.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The purpose of the Actor in setting off the System.

name: Cognizer
definition_en: The Cognizer is the person who has an opinion about the reliability of a Information_source or the Information from the Information_source.

name: Topic
definition_en: The Topic is the entity that a Cognizer trusts information about.

name: Content
definition_en: The Content denotes the mental content that the Cognizer is certain or uncertain about.

name: Degree
definition_en: This FE indicates the Degree to which the Cognizer trusts the Source.

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of an aspect of the Cognizer that also affects the nature of the trusting, or a general comparison of the state-of-affairs to others.  'She foolishly believed him .'

name: Expressor
definition_en: An object or action associated with the Cognizer which is so affected by the Cognizer's belief that it reveals the Cognizer's state.  'Her trustworthy eyes revealed that I was in no danger.'

name: Information_source
definition_en: The individual that gives Information to the Cognizer.  'Why should we believe him ?'

name: Information
definition_en: The text or speech which the Cognizer has heard and evaluates the truth of.  'America trusted his declaration , to their detriment .'

name: Judge
definition_en: The Judge heads the Court where the case is tried.  An expression referring to the Court may also stand in for the Judge. 'Judge Murphy will try the defendant for murder.' 'The court is currently trying several South American militants on charges of vehicular manslaughter.'

name: Court
definition_en: This FE identifies the Court in which a case is tried.

name: Defendant
definition_en: The Defendant is being tried for the Charges in Court.

name: Jury
definition_en: This FE identifies the people who are charged by the Court to listen to the testimony, evidence, and arguments, and come to a consensus about the guilt or innocence of the Defendant.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the case is tried.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the case is tried.

name: Charges
definition_en: This FE identifies the Charges brought against the Defendant.

name: Governing_authority
definition_en: The Defendant is tried under the laws of the Governing_authority. 'The United States will try the accused bomber in a federal courthouse.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner of the trial of the Defendant. 'Thomas Klein was tried in absentia.'

name: Evaluator
definition_en: The person (or metonymic manifestation thereof) that participates in the Experience.  'She tested out six cars before finding the one she liked.'

name: Experience
definition_en: The activity or event that the Evaluator participates in.  'Have you ever tried working out with kettlebells?'

name: Entity
definition_en: Entity is something that the Evaluator uses to try an Experience, and metonymically stands in for the Experience.  'We tried out the games, and they're fun.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A description of how the Evaluator acts in having the Experience.  'We cautiously tried the new system.'

name: Means
definition_en: A description of what the Evaluator does in order to participate in the Experience.  'We tried out the trampoline by letting our 2 year old jump on it'

name: Purpose
definition_en: A more explicit description of what the Evaluator seeks to learn by having the Experience.  'I tried out my neighbors vacuums to see if they met my needs'

name: Time
definition_en: The temporal location during which the Experience occurs.  'Try it out at midnight.'

name: Place
definition_en: The physical location in which the Experience occurs.  'I tried it for the first time at home.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The state of affairs that a cognizer realizes.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the State_of_affairs is realized.

name: Subtype
definition_en: The entity which denotes a subtype of the more general Category. 'I don't like this kind of fish.'

name: Category
definition_en: The more general type that the target denotes a subtype of. This FE is obligatory and should be labeled DNI when not present.   'They created a new breed of dog.'

name: Type_property
definition_en: A property of the Subtype itself rather than the members of the Category.   'I tried a new type of hair gel yesterday.'   Many Type_property adjectives (e.g. new, rare, traditional, modern, strange) make explicit that the type under discussion is just one of the types in the more general Category. Adjectives that denote properties of items in the category should be tagged Item_property.

name: Item_property
definition_en: A property of the members of the Category that helps identify (directly or indirectly) the particular set of members that are referred to by the Subtype.  'He had a Bon Jovi kind of guitar.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the Entity varies from other members of the Comparison_set.  'That is a very unusual bear.'

name: State_of_affairs
definition_en: The state of affairs which is evaluated with regard to whether it exhibits the essential characteristics of a Comparison_set.  ' However I have always loved having an unusual name and I think it's a beautiful name. .'

name: Comparison_set
definition_en: The set of indviduals, which are of similar kind to the Entity, and to which the Entity is compared.  'It's not unusual for interviewers to look beyond a resume and face-to-face meeting to find the unspoken clues about your personality.'

name: Feature
definition_en: A property of the State_of_affairs wherein it differs or is similar to members of a Comparison_set.  'David Hasselhoff's daughters are normal in every way. '

name: Reported_fact
definition_en: An assertion of a state, event, property or existence or the assignment to a category that the speaker attributes to unnamed others.  'Lester Hayes was purportedly joined in this suit by his wife.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Reported_fact was reported.

name: Duration
definition_en: The span of time for which the Reported_fact has been circulating.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for which or the apparant cause of the Reported_fact.

name: Entity
definition_en: The concrete or abstract entity that undergoes a change.   'How pleasing to see that Martha has changed now.'

name: Final_category
definition_en: The type of Entity that results from the change.

name: Initial_category
definition_en: The category that the Entity belongs to before it undergoes the change.  'The viccar changed from a professional clergyman into an anti-ecclesiastical activist.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Entity undergoes the transformation.  'Then she turned into a lizard.'

name: Initial_quality
definition_en: The value of the Attribute before the change takes place.  'At that time, my asthma changed from very mild to severe.'

name: Final_quality
definition_en: The quality of the Attribute that results from the change.   'Its color changed from red to blue.'

name: Attribute
definition_en: A characteristic of the Entity for which a quality can be assigned or determined by calculation, measurement, or observation.    'Test to check if the color changes when you place your mouse over the JavaScript image'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Change event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).   'He also identified all of the places where cancer rates or pollution levels changed quickly over short periods of time.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the initial and final categories, situations, or qualities differ from each other.  'Industrial economics has changed a lot during the last two decades'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The physical or abstract Circumstances under which the change takes place.  'Information may change whenever the US Department of Education issues additional guidance or regulations.'

name: Cause
definition_en: An event or state that causes the change to take place.  'Doctors' practices have changed due to concerns over medical litigation.'

name: Intermediate_value
definition_en: A value that the Attribute assumes before the Final_value obtains.  'The slurry was stirred until the color of the suspension changed from red via orange to yellow over a period of two hours.'

name: Value_range
definition_en: The Initial_value and Final_value taken together as the range through which the Entity changes.  The main faith of the church has changed between Orthodox, Protestant and Greek Catholic several times.

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Place
definition_en: The location that the change takes place.

name: Final_situation
definition_en: The Entity's situation that results from the change.   'Tests went from taking three hours to needing less than one .'

name: Initial_situation
definition_en: The situation that the Entity began in.  'She slowly shifted from giving him makework to actually finding he had some skills .'

name: Entity
definition_en: The concrete or abstract entity that undergoes a change.  'How pleasing to see that Scranton has metamorphosed .'

name: Final_category
definition_en: The type of Entity that results from the change.  'His smile transformed into a frown .'

name: Initial_category
definition_en: The category that the Entity belongs to before it undergoes the change.  'The viccar converted from a professional clergyman into an anti-ecclesiastical activist.'

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Entity undergoes the transformation.    'Then she turned into a lizard.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the Transformation event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).   'Dublin is experiencing the same transformation .'

name: Degree
definition_en: The extent to which the initial and final categories differ from each other.  'The formula had not yet transformed completely .'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The physical or abstract Circumstances under which the change takes place.

name: Cause
definition_en: An event or state that causes the change to take place.  'Doctors' practices have undergone a metamorphosis due to concerns over medical litigation.'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time.

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The length of time from when the event denoted by the target began to be repeated to when it stopped.

name: Place
definition_en: The location that the change takes place.

name: Entity
definition_en: The thing which is affected by the Event.

name: Event
definition_en: A change in the world which affects the Entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Entity undergoes the Event.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Entity undergoes the Event.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Entity undergoes the Event. The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Entity undergoes the Event.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly) and general descriptions comparing events (the same way).

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Entity
definition_en: The thing which is affected by the Event.

name: Event
definition_en: A change in the world which affects the Entity.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which the Entity undergoes the Event.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Entity undergoes the Event.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for which the Entity undergoes the Event. The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which the Entity undergoes the Event.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Wearer
definition_en: The individual who begins the action wearing the Clothing and ends the action without it.  'The suspects had to strip publically and endure several blasts from a firehose.'

name: Clothing
definition_en: The item that the Wearer is initially wearing but then removes.

name: Body_location
definition_en: The initial location of the Clothing on the body, before it changes location.  Quite often, the location is not overtly specified and is implicitly supplied by the location on the body that the Clothing is prototypically associated with.  'He doffed his hat from his bald head.' 'Take off your shoes and just set 'em over there. INI'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the clothing removal which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of a Wearer that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'He slowly and deliberately took off each shoe and placed it on the rack.'

name: Means
definition_en: The Means is an act whereby the Wearer achieves the removal.  'With her burned hands, she could only take off her jacket by sort of vigorously shrugging.'

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the event.

name: Degree
definition_en: The Degree to which the event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: The location at which the Wearer undresses an item of Clothing.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time at which a Wearer undresses.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The Purpose for which a Wearer undresses.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Individuals
definition_en: The group of people whose employment status is considered.   'The high unemployment of the Romany population is one of the key issues, which need addressing.'

name: Employment
definition_en: The property of a group of Individuals describing how many of them are employed or unemployed.  'The statistics are shocking: unemployment is 57 per cent.'

name: Value
definition_en: The count or percentage of people among the group of Individuals that are of the specified employment status.  'While current unemployment of about 6% isn't high by historical standards, there's no denying this trend toward job exportation.'

name: Degree
definition_en: A modifier expressing  the deviation of the Value from the norm.  'This leads to high joblessness in some pockets.'

name: Time
definition_en: The Time during which Employment level of the Individuals has a specified Value.  'Last month's unemployment was 5.17 percent on a seasonally-adjusted basis.'

name: Group
definition_en: The number or rate of individuals that are either employed or unemployment may be contrasted, implicitly or explicitly, with different groups.  'Ministers believe youth unemployment among Canada's Aboriginal population requires special and immediate attention.'

name: Place
definition_en: The location where the Individuals under consideration reside.  'A stadium is expected to cost $350 million, and financial woes caused by recession and high joblessness in Oregon all but rule out public financing.'

name: Agent
definition_en: The self-directed entity that uses and activates the Firearm.

name: Firearm
definition_en: This FE identifies the Firearm that an Agent activates so that it rapidly propels a projectile.

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the means by which an Agent uses the Firearm.

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the manner in which an Agent uses the Firearm.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Agent intentionally affects the Patient.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent uses the firearm. 'Firing cannons to have a good time is not my idea of prudence!'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the Agent fires the Firearm.

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is the location the Theme ends up in, or is intended to end up in. 'Who fired a pistol at my client?'

name: Path
definition_en: This is the path along which the projectiles travel.

name: Source
definition_en: The Source is the location of the Firearm from which projectiles originate.

name: Area
definition_en: Area is the setting in which the projectile's movement takes place.  'Sometimes they got together and fired off M-16 in the park.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: This FE identifies the number of times a firearm is used.

name: Depictive
definition_en: Depicitive phrase describing the state of a participant in the action.

name: Theme
definition_en: The Theme is the entity which moves by means of the Vehicle. 'Margeret flew to Cabo San Lucas.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The Vehicle is the means of conveyance of the Theme. It is usually expressed in a PP-complement or the direct object. 'Professor Frink sailed to Italy on an oceanliner.'

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion expresses the frame element Source. 'We flew from Atlanta.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner describes a property of the motion not related to its trajectory. 'Samantha always rode gracefully on the back of a motorcycle.'

name: Path
definition_en: The Path describes the trajectory of the motion. 'The caravan rode through the desert.'

name: Goal
definition_en: The Goal is the endpoint of the trajectory of motion. 'We sailed to Morocco.'

name: Distance
definition_en: The Distance is the extent of the motion. 'We flew 300 miles in 40 minutes.'

name: Duration
definition_en: The Duration is the amount of time the motion takes. 'We rode in the van for 45 minutes.'

name: Speed
definition_en: The Speed is the rate at which the motion occurs. 'We flew  at nearly 600 miles per hour.'

name: Area
definition_en: The Area is the location where the motion takes place. 'We rode around the state.'

name: Road
definition_en: The Road is the thoroughfare on which the Vehicle travels. 'We ride the bus on highway 580.'

name: Route
definition_en: The Route is the usual path that the Vehicle travles. 'I ride the London-Birmingham route almost everyday.'

name: Time
definition_en: When the riding takes place. 'We will fly back to New York in September.'

name: Cotheme
definition_en: A theme that rides in the same Vehicle as the main Theme. 'My family always flies to New York with our good friends, the Jacksons.'

name: Driver
definition_en: The individual that directs the motion of the Vehicle

name: Resource
definition_en: The Resource is a physical entity or an ability to perform work that was used in an earlier process, typically in pursuit of a goal.  'The battery is slightly worn out'

name: Degree
definition_en: A measure of the amount of the Resource that is gone, or of the degree to which its quality is reduced.  'Don't put the battery on a charger until it is totally spent.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes an event or state from whose occurrence the Resource's being used up logically follows.  'Others say that the Canadian marketing talent pool is depleted because fewer young people are being attracted to the business.'

name: Excess
definition_en: This FE indicates that the presence of an overwhelming amount of a kind of entity or the high intensity of an event is sufficient to bring about the used up state of the Resource.  'Rent it for nostalgia, but I don't recommend buying it unless you own the video and it is worn out with so much use.'

name: Subregion
definition_en: Subregion denotes a sub-part of the Resource in which the it is specifically exhausted or worn out.  'Sometimes if you have a shoe and it is worn out on one side you'll see that if you put your foot in it, it leans in that direction.'

name: Entity
definition_en: The item which is useful for some purpose.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The kind of task which is promoted by the use or presence of the Entity.

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount that the presence of the Entity aids in the completion of the (desirable) Purpose.

name: Domain
definition_en: This Frame Element marks expressions of a Domain or parameter with respect to which the Entity is useful.

name: Time
definition_en: When the Entity is useful for a Purpose.

name: Agent
definition_en: The Agent uses the Instrument to achieve their Purpose.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the place where the Agent uses the Instrument.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which an Agent uses the Instrument.

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the time when the Agent uses the Instrument.  'I went and used that ball yesterday and i bowled 5 games and i left about 14 ten pins with it.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which an Agent uses the Instrument.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action ( deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Instrument
definition_en: An entity directed by the Agent that serves to bring about the Purpose of the Agent.  'For cold conditions, we recommend using a heat gun or a hair dryer to make the adhesive work better. '

name: Role
definition_en: An Instrument that has a function associated with it.  'Mirabella shared the mischievous vision of childlike exuberance and used the chair as a pseudo jungle gym.'

name: Outcome
definition_en: The Outcome is the failure or success of the Agent's using the Instrument to achieve their Purpose.  'It has been used successfully in physician offices, schools, and in sensory function laboratories for over 35 years.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: An event within which the Agent uses the Instrument. Often, the Containing_event will also give an indication of the Agent's Purpose.  ' In the 1950s, the titanium metal industry was established primarily in response to the emerging aerospace industry which used it in the manufacture of airframe .'

name: Frequency
definition_en: This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question "how often."

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: This FE modifies a clause with an iterative interpretation, which may be signified by the simple present tense on the main verb.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the event itself and any of its participants.

name: Depictive
definition_en: This FE describes a participant of the state of affairs introduced by the target as being in some state during the action. The depicted state does not necessarily or usually facilitate or cause the state of affairs reported by the target.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation denotes a proposition from which the main clause (headed by the target) logically follows. This often means that the Explanation causes the target's proposition, but not in all cases.

name: Group
definition_en: This FE identifies the population within which the Using event occurs.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute of the Instrument or the Using act and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Duration
definition_en: Duration denotes the length of time from the beginning of a continuous situation to its end. In many cases, the continuous situation is a dynamic action which is ongoing, while in others it is simply an undifferentiated state.

name: Agent
definition_en: The person who depletes a Resource to achieve some Goal

name: Resource
definition_en: The exhaustible commodity that the Agent has access to.

name: Purpose
definition_en: What the Agent is attempting to achieve by using the Resource.

name: Portion
definition_en: The amount of the Resource that the Agent uses to achieve the Purpose.

name: Means
definition_en: A more specific description of how the Purpose is achieved by spending the Resource.

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the intentional act which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). In addition, it may indicate salient characteristics of an Agent that also affect the action ( deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Place
definition_en: The physical location where the Resource is used.

name: Time
definition_en: The time at which the Resource is used.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE identifies a characteristic or description of the Vehicle.  'Kim drove a  used car.'

name: Vehicle
definition_en: Vehicle is the transportation device that the human beings use to travel.This FE is incorporated into each LU in this frame.

name: Possessor
definition_en: This Frame Element denotes the Possessor of the Vehicle. 'His car crashed into a tree'.

name: Itinerary
definition_en: The frame element tells about the time and route of the service of the transportation device. 'You must take the midnight train to get there by tomorrow noon.'

name: Means_of_propulsion
definition_en: The Means_of_propulsion designates how the vehicle is moved. ' They rode in a horse-drawn carriage. '

name: Use
definition_en: The task which the Vehicle is put to.  Normally, this includes the transportation of some kind.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The vehicle which moves into position for typical operation.

name: Source
definition_en: Any expression which describes the location that the Vehicle has been stationed at.  'The ship cast off from Pier 21.'

name: Intended_goal
definition_en: The location that the Vehicle is bound for.  'At 3:15 the airplane took off to England. '

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the preparation for motion which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the Vehicle that affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).   'The airship slowly lifted off and rotated to face the center of the city.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The state of the Vehicle during the preparations.

name: Means
definition_en: An event in which the Vehicle participates which causes or enables it to travel.  'This experimental aircraft lifts off by rearranging its wings and thrusters to achieve maximal elevation in as short a time as possible.'

name: Result
definition_en: The Result of the Vehicle's motion.  'The plane lifted off right into some trees.'

name: Co-participant
definition_en: An individual or vehicle that is also involved in the preparations.  'A representative of the department said that the helicopter took off with three other aircraft, arriving at the hospital in just under an hour.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: This FE indicates the Circumstances under which the preparation of the Vehicle takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: The Place describes the location where the Vehicle prepares for motion.

name: Duration_of_final_state
definition_en: The length  of the time that the Vehicle remains in the state of readiness.

name: Time
definition_en: The Time when the Vehicle gets ready for motion.  'The helicopter took off in the afternoon of October 9th.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation is a proposition from which the main clause logically follows.

name: Vehicle
definition_en: The Vehicle comes to the ground, usually (but not necessarily) under the control of an operator.   'The plane landed on the airstrip.'

name: Source
definition_en: Source is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of motion. While Source expressions are possible in this frame, they are relatively infrequent.  'The plane landed from the east, a completely different part of the city than we were expecting.'

name: Path
definition_en: Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Source nor a Goal.  In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.  'The airplane landed through lightning and rain.'

name: Goal
definition_en: Goal is any expression that tells where the Vehicle ends up, or would end up, as a result of the motion.   'Most of the planes set down on the strip before midnight.'

name: Manner
definition_en: A Manner expression describes a property of landing which is not directly related to the trajectory of motion.  Descriptions of speed, steadiness, grace, means of motion, and other things count as Manner expressions.  'The aircraft landed noisily.'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies the Means by which a Vehicle lands.

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Vehicle is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Vehicle.

name: Cotheme
definition_en: Cotheme is the second moving object, expressed as a direct object or an oblique.   'Our airplane landed with the others in formation.'

name: Time
definition_en: This FE identifies the Time when the aircraft lands.

name: New_situation
definition_en: The New_situation are the state of the Goal when the Vehicle arrives.   'The troop carrier landed to a standing ovation.'

name: Depictive
definition_en: The Depictive is a phrase which describes the state of the Vehicle upon arrival.   'It landed, on fire and about to explode.'

name: Period_of_iterations
definition_en: The time period within which the landing event repeats multiple times.

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the landing event itself and any of its participants.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the purpose for which the Vehicle lands at the Goal.

name: Degree
definition_en: This frame element selects some gradable attribute and modifies the expected value for it.

name: Event_description
definition_en: This FE marks the state of affairs reported by the landing event as understood to play a role in the state of affairs of Event_description

name: Re-encoding
definition_en: This FE presents the current frame as an integral part of a larger conceptualization expressed by another frame. The frame expressed by the target typically corresponds to a Means action.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the Vehicle lands at the Goal.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE identifies the Place where the landing occurs.

name: Part
definition_en: Some Part of the larger vehicle, the Whole.

name: Whole
definition_en: A vehicle (the Whole)  which includes the Part.

name: Function
definition_en: The function of the part within the vehicule as a whole.

name: Orientation
definition_en: This property of the part that situates the part within the whole.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A property relating to the part.

name: Judge
definition_en: The Judge (which may be the jury, judge, magistrate or court) decides on the Finding.

name: Finding
definition_en: This FE identifies the outcome of the Judge's deliberation or consideration. Many LUs in this frame incorporate this FE.

name: Defendant
definition_en: The person who stands accused of a crime and is subject to the verdict.

name: Charges
definition_en: This FE refers to the Charges with respect to which the verdict is being given.

name: Case
definition_en: The Case on which the verdict is being given.

name: Time
definition_en: When the event occurs.

name: Place
definition_en: Where the event takes place.

name: Legal_basis
definition_en: This FE indicates the basis in law of a verdict. 'He was found guilty under section 28 article 5.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: The Circumstances under which the verdict was reached. 'He was convicted on a four to three vote.'

name: Manner
definition_en: This FE identifies the Manner in which the Judge acts.

name: Purpose
definition_en: This FE identifies the Purpose for which the Judge returns a particular verdict. 'Did you acquit him just to get the publicity?'

name: Means
definition_en: This FE identifies an action that the Judge performs in order to return the verdict.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The Explanation for the verdict given. 'The jury convicted him on all charges because of the overwhelming evidence against him.'

name: Inspector
definition_en: The individual or individuals that ascertain that the Unconfirmed_content is true.  'His later verification of the facts is certainly beyond reproach.'

name: Unconfirmed_content
definition_en: An open proposition that the Inspector decides by examining evidence.  It is usually a propostion put forward which some parties would disbelieve or contest.  'It is extremely difficult to confirm the absence of something.'

name: Manner
definition_en: Any description of the verification which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (probably, presumably, mysteriously), force (hard, softly), secondary effects (quietly, loudly), and general descriptions comparing events (the same way). It may also indicate salient characteristics of an Inspector that also affect the action (presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully).

name: Means
definition_en: An action performed by the Inspector by which the Inspector manages to establish the truth of the Unconfirmed_content.  'We confirmed our results by repeating the experiment and measuring the output with a mass spec.'

name: Degree
definition_en: The amount of certainty which the Inspector achieves after the process of verification.  'His involvement in the action has subsequently been completely confirmed.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: The state of affairs that the Inspector hopes to bring about by going through the verification.  'I spent a few minutes confirming his visa number just to make him sweat.'

name: Medium
definition_en: The Medium is the piece of text or work in which the Inspector verifies the Unconfirmed_content:  'Chapter four confirms the reader 's suspicions completely.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: A tool or instrument used by the Inspector in the verification process.

name: Condition
definition_en: The conditions under which the the verification will occur.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: This FE describes a characteristic of the verification event.

name: Communicative_force
definition_en: This FE indicates the Communicative_force or authority with which the target operates (often denoted by words such as "officially," "formally," "technically," etc.).

name: Time
definition_en: This FE describes the Time at which the verification event takes place.

name: Place
definition_en: This FE describes where the verificiation event takes place.

name: Explanation
definition_en: The reason for the state of the verification event.

name: Item
definition_en: The Item is one version among several versions (which may or may not yet exist), progressively getting closer to a final version.

name: Degree
definition_en: The degree of the distance the Item is from the final version.  'I warn you, this is a very rough draft.'

name: Bomb
definition_en: The explosive device which activates when set off by the victim.

name: Use
definition_en: The type of activity that the Bomb is generally involved in.  Often this can be considered a kind of Type specification also.

name: Type
definition_en: This FE indicates what subtype the Bomb belongs to.

name: Material
definition_en: The substance that makes up the Bomb.

name: Bomber
definition_en: The person who sets the bomb.

name: Part
definition_en: This FE identifies a part of the Bomb.  This includes permanent, obligatory parts and mere attachments.

name: Name
definition_en: The term used to refer to a Bomb.

name: Time_of_creation
definition_en: The time at which the Bomb comes into existence.

name: Creator
definition_en: The individual or group responsible for the creation of the Bomb.

name: Descriptor
definition_en: A description or characteristic of the Bomb.

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim inadvertantly causes the Bomb to denotate.

name: Aggressor
definition_en: The Aggressor is the person causing the Victim's injury.  'Your brutality on your enemies seems to know no boundaries.'

name: Victim
definition_en: The Victim is the being or entity that is injured.  'Increasing violence against supporters of government reform have attracted international attention.'

name: Degree
definition_en: Degree is the degree to which violence is done.  'Our troops are working in conditions of extreme violence.'

name: Manner
definition_en: The Manner in which the Aggressor acts upon the Victim.  'Acts of wanton violence unconditionally deserve condemnation.'

name: Means
definition_en: An intentional action performed by the Aggressor that results in the committing of a violent act.

name: Place
definition_en: Place identifies the place where the violence occurs.  'City leaders are troubled by recent surges in local violence'

name: Time
definition_en: Time identifies the time when the harm-causing event occurs.  'Last week's violence resulted in over three hundred injuries.'

name: Instrument
definition_en: This FE is any object used to cause the injury.  'Instances of gun violence will receive top priority from the police.'

name: Purpose
definition_en: Purpose identifies the purpose for which a harm-causing action is carried out.  'I  would only commit violence to protect myself.'

name: Containing_event
definition_en: This FE identifies the event in which the harm is caused.  'Violence in the standoff was unfortunate, but not unexpected.'

name: Explanation
definition_en: A fact or action related to one of the participants in the volient act that the Aggressor responds to in doing violence.  'They are quick to violence for petty reasons.'

name: Iterations
definition_en: Iterations refers to the number of times the violent act occurs.  'He committed brutality a dozen times over the past years.'

name: Cause
definition_en: The Cause marks expressions that indicate some non-intentional, typically non-human, force that inflicts harm on the Victim  'The storm's violence left many lives in shambles.'

name: Circumstances
definition_en: Circumstances describe the state of the world (at a particular time and place) which is specifically independent of the violent event and any of its participants.

name: Frequency
definition_en: How often the violence occurs.  'Residents by now are used to the daily violence that plays out on their streets.'

name: Aggressors
definition_en: The Aggressors commit acts of violence upon each other.  'Hope for a peaceful resoliton is gone as violence between the two sides reignites.'

name: Visitor
definition_en: The sentient entity that heads toward and is temporarily with the Host in order to fulfil some Purpose.

name: Host
definition_en: An individual that allows the use of his or her resources for the benefit of the Visitor.

name: Purpose
definition_en: The activity that is enabled by the hospitality of the Host and that the Visitor wishes to achieve.

name: Normal_location
definition_en: The location that the Visitor normally resides in or is (permanently) associated with.

name: Host_location
definition_en: The location associated with the Host, where the Visitor arrives at and remains during the visit.

name: Path
definition_en: Path is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a Normal_location nor a Host_location.  In this frame, Path expressions almost always have a via-sense.

name: Mode_of_transportation
definition_en: The Mode_of_transportation expresses how the motion of the Visitor is effected, by its body or by a vehicle which holds and conveys the Visitor.   Vehicles can move in any way and in any medium. They are usually expressed obliquely with 'in' or 'by'.

name: Time

name: Purpose

name: Host_location

name: Place
